Overall, Scooby-Doo and the Alien Invaders is a lighthearted, entertaining film that balances humor and adventure with deeper themes about friendship, self-discovery, and the power of believing in oneself.

overview: When the eternally optimistic Poppy, queen of the Trolls, learns that the Bergens no longer have any holidays on their calendar, she enlists the help of Branch and the rest of the gang on a delightfully quirky mission to fix something that the Bergens don't think is broken.
tagline: Prepare to be merry and bright
title: Trolls Holiday
plot:
Trolls Holiday is a 2017 animated television special produced by DreamWorks Animation. It serves as a spin-off to the 2016 film Trolls, which was also produced by DreamWorks Animation.

The story begins with Poppy (voiced by Anna Kendrick), the optimistic and cheerful princess of the Trolls, who is excited for the annual "Trollmas" celebration. Trollmas is a holiday where the Trolls come together to celebrate their unique qualities and express themselves freely. However, this year's celebration is threatened when Bergens (the main antagonists from the first film) discover that Trollmas is being held on the same day as their own holiday, "Bergenmas."

The Bergens, led by Prince Gristle (voiced by Justin Timberlake), plan to steal all of the Trolls' happiness and use it to fuel their own miserable existence. Poppy and her friends, including Branch (voiced by Christopher Mintz-Plasse) and Guy Diamond (voiced by Kunal Nayyar), must find a way to stop the Bergens and save Trollmas.

As the story unfolds, Poppy and Branch embark on a journey to gather all of the Trolls' happiness and bring it back to their village. Along the way, they meet new friends, including a group of "Happiest" Trolls who possess unique qualities that make them particularly happy. The group also encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain and Bergen soldiers.

Meanwhile, Prince Gristle becomes increasingly desperate to get his hands on the Trolls' happiness, leading him to make a deal with a mysterious figure known as "The Happiest Troll of All." This twist adds an element of surprise to the story, as Poppy and Branch begin to suspect that something is not quite right.

In the end, Poppy and her friends successfully gather all of the Trolls' happiness and return it to their village. The Bergens are thwarted in their plans, and Trollmas is saved. The special ends with a heartwarming celebration, where the Trolls come together to express themselves freely and celebrate their unique qualities.

Throughout the story, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the world of the Trolls to life. The characters are well-developed and relatable, with Poppy's optimism and Branch's sarcasm providing comedic relief. The special also features catchy musical numbers, including "Trollmas" and "Happiest Troll of All."

Overall, Trolls Holiday is a fun and festive animated special that celebrates the importance of self-expression and individuality. With its colorful animation, catchy music, and lovable characters, it's a great addition to any holiday viewing lineup.

overview: Three young women vacationing in Paris find themselves whisked away to Monte Carlo after one of the girls is mistaken for a British heiress.
tagline: She's having the time of someone else's life.
title: Monte Carlo
plot:
"Monte Carlo" is a 2011 American teen comedy film directed by Deborah Kaplan. The movie follows the story of two sisters, Emily (Leighton Meester) and Maddy (Selena Gomez), who are on the run from their wealthy but troubled father after he tries to kill them.

The main themes of "Monte Carlo" include:

*   Family dynamics: The film explores the complex relationships between the three sisters, particularly the bond between Emily and Maddy as they navigate their difficult home life.
*   Identity: As the sisters try to escape their past, they must also figure out who they are outside of their family's influence. This theme is reflected in their experiences with new friends and romantic interests.
*   Self-discovery: Through their adventures, Emily and Maddy learn more about themselves and what they want from life.

The movie features a mix of humor, drama, and romance, making it an entertaining watch for audiences.

overview: When a devoted husband and father is left home alone for the weekend, two stranded young women unexpectedly knock on his door for help. What starts out as a kind gesture results in a dangerous seduction and a deadly game of cat and mouse.
tagline: One night can cost you everything.
title: Knock Knock
plot:
Knock Knock is a 2015 erotic thriller directed by Eli Roth, who co-wrote the screenplay with Guillermo Amoedo and Nicolás López. It stars Keanu Reeves as Evan Webber, Lorenza Izzo as Genesis and Ana de Armas as Bel, with Aaron Burns and Ignacia Allamand. The film is a remake of Death Game, made in 1974 and released in 1977, whose director Peter S. Traynor and stars Sondra Locke and Colleen Camp were involved in the new production; Camp also appears in a cameo.

Evan Webber, an architect and devoted family man, stays home alone over Father's Day weekend to finish a work project and attend physical therapy while his wife Karen, an artist, and their children go on vacation. During a rainstorm, two young women, Genesis and Bel, knock on his door, soaked and lost, saying they are looking for a party. Evan lets them in to dry off and call a car, but as the evening goes on the women flirt with him and repeatedly push his boundaries. Despite his attempts to resist, he ends up sleeping with both of them.

The next morning, the women refuse to leave. Their behavior becomes increasingly erratic and destructive, and when Evan threatens to call the police, they claim to be underage and threaten to accuse him of statutory rape. After Evan finally appears to be rid of them, the pair return, tie him up and subject him to a night of psychological and physical torment, mocking his infidelity and filming his humiliation. Turning his home into a scene of chaos, they ruin Karen's artwork and threaten to expose him, while Evan struggles to escape their twisted game before his family returns.

The film presents a satirical take on temptation, morality and the consequences of infidelity, mixing thriller with dark humor.

Knock Knock premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 23, 2015, and was released by Lionsgate on October 9, 2015. Reviews were mixed, with 37 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus found its campy tone and repetitive story ineffective, and a Metacritic score of 53.

overview: Following a terrible car crash, a woman awakes to find an enigmatic mortician preparing her for burial.
tagline: Life is the symptom. Death is the cure.
title: After.Life
plot:
After.Life is a 2009 American psychological horror thriller film written and directed by Agnieszka Wójtowicz-Vosloo. Liam Neeson stars as a mysterious funeral director, with Christina Ricci as a young woman in his care and Justin Long as her boyfriend. It premiered in November 2009.

Eliot Deacon, a softly spoken funeral director in a small town, talks gently to the bodies he prepares for burial. Anna Taylor, an unhappy middle school teacher, meets him at the funeral of her old piano teacher. That night, after a bitter argument with her boyfriend, Paul, at a restaurant, she drives off in distress and crashes her car. She wakes on a table in Eliot's mortuary as he cuts away her clothes. He tells her that she is dead and that he has a gift that allows him to hear the dead and help them make the transition to the afterlife, and he injects her with a drug that he says will relax her muscles and prevent rigor mortis.

Over the following days, Anna veers between disbelief and despair. She tries repeatedly to escape and at one point reaches Paul by telephone, but he hangs up, believing it a prank. Eliot tells her that she was never truly living anyway and must let go of life, and when he shows her reflection, her pale, corpse-like appearance convinces her that she has died. Meanwhile, Paul, denied permission to see her body, grows suspicious, especially after one of Anna's students, Jack, claims to have seen her alive at the funeral home. At the police station, Paul learns of a drug that can mimic death by causing paralysis. Eliot tells Jack that they share a special gift.

Before her funeral, Anna asks to see herself once more and notices her breath fogging the mirror, realizing that Eliot has lied to her, but he sedates her again. At the funeral, Paul places on her finger the engagement ring he had planned to give her on the night of the accident. Afterward, as Anna wakes inside her coffin while it is being buried, Eliot goads the drunken Paul into going to the cemetery. Paul appears to reach her and they embrace, but he is suddenly back on Eliot's table. Eliot tells him he died in a car crash on the way, and as Paul insists that he is alive, Eliot begins to embalm him.

After.Life was poorly received by critics, who found its premise intriguing but felt it lacked thrills and tension; Rotten Tomatoes reported 24% approval.

overview: During a handover to the head of counter-terrorism of MI5, Harry Pearce, a terrorist escapes custody. When Harry disappears soon after, his protégé is tasked with finding out what happened as an impending attack on London looms, and eventually uncovers a deadly conspiracy.
title: Spooks: The Greater Good
plot:
Spooks: The Greater Good is a 2015 British spy thriller film directed by David Wilmot, based on the BBC television series Spooks. The movie follows the story of Harry Pearce (played by Richard Armitage), a former head of MI5's counter-intelligence unit, who is forced back into action when a mole within his organization threatens to destroy everything he has worked for.

The main themes of Spooks: The Greater Good include:

1. Loyalty and Betrayal: The movie explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal, as Harry Pearce navigates a complex web of allegiances and rivalries within his own organization. As he delves deeper into the mystery of the mole, he is forced to confront the possibility that those closest to him may be working against him.
2. Morality in War: The film raises questions about morality in the context of war and espionage. Harry Pearce's actions are guided by a strong sense of duty and loyalty, but as the stakes grow higher, he must confront the moral implications of his decisions.
3. Trauma and Redemption: The movie also explores the theme of trauma and redemption, as Harry Pearce grapples with the consequences of his past mistakes and seeks to make amends. His journey is marked by a sense of regret and longing for a lost love, which serves as a catalyst for his actions.

Overall, Spooks: The Greater Good is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities in the world of espionage.

overview: Get ready for a howling good time as an all new assortment of irresistible animal heroes are unleashed in this great family tail! In an unlikely alliance, the outrageous Waddlesworth - a parrot who thinks he's a Rottweiler - teams up with Oddball - an un-marked Dalmatian puppy eager to earn her spots! Together they embark on a laugh-packed quest to outwit the ever-scheming Cruella De Vil.
tagline: Meet Two Unlikely Heroes With A Bone To Pick.
title: 102 Dalmatians
plot:
102 Dalmatians is a 2000 American family adventure comedy directed by Kevin Lima and written by Kristen Buckley, Brian Regan, Bob Tzudiker and Noni White. A sequel to the live-action 101 Dalmatians (1996), itself drawn from the 1961 animated film and Dodie Smith's novel, it brings back Glenn Close as Cruella de Vil, with Gérard Depardieu as the furrier Jean-Pierre LePelt, Ioan Gruffudd as Kevin Shepherd, Alice Evans as Chloe Simon and Tim McInnerny as Alonzo.

After three years in prison, Cruella appears to have been cured of her passion for fur by the behavioural therapy of Dr. Pavlov. She is paroled on condition that any violation will send her back to prison and force her to hand her remaining fortune of eight million pounds to the dog shelters of Westminster. Reformed, she makes peace with her long-suffering valet Alonzo and rescues Kevin Shepherd's struggling Second Chance dog shelter from bankruptcy. Her probation officer, Chloe, remains suspicious; she owns Dipstick, one of the Dalmatians Cruella once stole, whose mate Dottie has just had three puppies, among them the spotless Oddball, who grows up self-conscious about her plain coat.

Pavlov has discovered, and kept quiet, that the chimes of Big Ben undo his treatment, and when Cruella hears them she reverts to her old self. She enlists LePelt to design a coat made from Dalmatian puppies, with a hood from Dipstick's litter. Knowing that her fortune would go to Kevin's shelter, the only one in Westminster, she frames him for the theft of dozens of puppies, exploiting an old conviction, and lures Chloe to a dinner party while LePelt steals Dottie and the puppies; Dipstick is captured too.

Kevin breaks out of jail with the help of his talking macaw Waddlesworth and explains that his earlier offence was freeing animals from a laboratory. He and Chloe chase Cruella onto the Orient Express but miss the train, while Waddlesworth and Oddball follow the villains to LePelt's Paris factory. Cruella locks the couple in a cellar, but they help the puppies escape. Alonzo finally turns on his employer, defeats LePelt and frees Kevin and Chloe, and the puppies trap Cruella inside a giant cake in a bakery. Cruella and LePelt are arrested, her fortune goes to Kevin and Chloe, and Oddball at last grows a few spots.

The film grossed $183.6 million worldwide, less than its predecessor, and earned only 30% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though it was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Costume Design.

overview: A reporter stumbles upon the journal of a murderer with plans to butcher specific girls, and he begins to investigates on his own, and finding that every trail leads to a 9-year-old orphan living in a group home.
title: Ticking Clock
plot:
Ticking Clock is a 2011 American mystery thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash and released direct to DVD in the United States on January 4, 2011. Cuba Gooding Jr. stars as the investigative reporter Louis Hicks, with Neal McDonough as the serial killer Keech, Nicki Aycox as Polly, Austin Abrams as the boy James, Danielle Nicolet as Louis's wife Gina and Yancey Arias as a detective.

The film opens as Keech kills a woman and then comforts her crying baby son. Louis is struggling with a faltering career and a troubled marriage, and is having an affair with a district attorney, Felicia, who ends their relationship. That same day Keech murders her at her home. Louis fights the intruder, who escapes but leaves behind his journal, which lists two more murders planned over the next three days. Louis copies down the names, but Keech steals back both the journal and the note, and when Louis goes to the police he becomes a suspect in Felicia's death.

Louis tracks down one of the intended victims, a schoolteacher named Vicki, but Keech reaches her first and kills her in a bar after talking with her about a boy she reported for hurting a cat. With the police still unconvinced, Louis sends a scrap of Keech's coat and a bloody fingerprint to a friend at a crime lab. The blood matches an eleven-year-old orphan, James, who lives in a boys' home run by Polly, and the coat's fabric behaves unlike any known material. James, a disturbed boy who wishes he could go back in time and fix his life, shows Louis a box of dead animals and then angrily sends him away.

Realising that Polly is the next name on the list, Louis concludes that Keech is James grown up and returned from the future. Jailed by sceptical police, he is visited by Keech posing as his lawyer, who confirms that he has travelled back from 2032 with a pocket-watch time machine. Keech explains that he killed his abusive mother hoping to change his childhood, but every change has led someone else to condemn him to the same fate, and he now plans to kill Polly and frame Louis. On the roof of the boys' home, young James confronts his older self and slashes him with a dropped knife, Keech accidentally knocks the boy off the roof and shoots Louis, and with James's death Keech vanishes and all of his victims are restored to life.

Ticking Clock received negative reviews, with Dread Central calling it an iffy thriller with an intriguing but underdeveloped premise.

overview: As Batman hunts for the escaped Joker, the Clown Prince of Crime attacks the Gordon family to prove a diabolical point mirroring his own fall into madness.
tagline: The madness begins
title: Batman: The Killing Joke
plot:
Batman: The Killing Joke is a 2016 animated thriller film based on the 1988 graphic novel of the same name by Alan Moore and Brian Bolland. The story revolves around the Joker's origin and his complex relationship with Batman.

The main themes of Batman: The Killing Joke include:

1. **The Nature of Chaos and Anarchy**: The Joker represents the ultimate force of chaos, and his actions serve as a catalyst for exploring the consequences of anarchy in society. His presence forces Batman to confront the limits of his own morality and the blurred lines between heroism and villainy.

2. **Trauma and Psychological Scarring**: The film delves into the psychological trauma inflicted upon Barbara Gordon (Commissioner Gordon's daughter, also known as Oracle) by the Joker, highlighting the long-lasting effects of violence on individuals and communities. This theme is particularly relevant in exploring the Joker's own backstory and his connection to Batman.

3. **The Duality of Human Nature**: The Killing Joke explores the dualities present within human nature, with characters like the Joker embodying pure chaos, while others, such as Barbara Gordon, represent a more ordered and rational approach to life. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the complexities of human psychology.

4. **The Impact of Trauma on Heroes**: The film examines how trauma can affect heroes, particularly Batman, who is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities in order to protect others. This theme highlights the psychological toll that heroism can take on individuals and the importance of seeking help when needed.

5. **The Joker's Existential Significance**: The Joker serves as a symbol for the absurdity and randomness of life, highlighting the inherent meaninglessness of existence. His actions serve as a commentary on the human condition, forcing Batman to confront the possibility that there may be no clear moral or rational explanation for the world.

Overall, Batman: The Killing Joke presents a thought-provoking exploration of complex themes, challenging viewers to consider the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of chaos in society.

original_title: GHOST IN THE SHELL／攻殻機動隊2.0
overview: In the year 2029, Section 9, a group of cybernetically enhanced cops, are called in to investigate and stop a highly-wanted hacker known as 'The Puppetmaster'.  Ghost in the Shell 2.0 is a reproduced version of its original 1995 counterpart. Among a numerous enhancements, for the film's 2.0 release, were a number of scenes were overhauled with 3D animation, visual improvements, and soundtrack rerecorded in 6.1 surround sound.
tagline: It Found A Voice... Now It Needs A Body.
title: Ghost in the Shell 2.0
plot: In the year 2029, Section 9, a group of cybernetically enhanced cops, are called in to investigate and stop a highly-wanted hacker known as 'The Puppetmaster'.

overview: A pair of buddies conspire to save their best friend from marrying the wrong woman, a cold-hearted beauty who snatches him from them and breaks up their Neil Diamond cover band.
tagline: They swore nothing would come between them. Then evil walked in the door
title: Saving Silverman
plot:
Saving Silverman is a 2001 American romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of male friendship and the challenges of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of unrequited love, as the protagonist, David (played by Jason Biggs), navigates his feelings for his best friend, Steve (played by Steve Zahn), who has just gotten engaged to a woman named Carol (played by Christina Applegate).

The film also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as David tries to come to terms with his own emotional baggage and figure out what he wants from life. Through David's journey, the movie highlights the struggles of transitioning from adolescence to adulthood, including the loss of innocence and the search for meaning.

Furthermore, Saving Silverman critiques traditional masculine norms and expectations, presenting a more nuanced portrayal of male relationships and emotions. The film's humor and wit are used to subvert these expectations, creating a relatable and endearing character in David, who is both flawed and lovable.

Ultimately, the movie's themes revolve around the power of friendship, love, and self-acceptance, as David learns to let go of his unrequited love and find happiness on his own terms.

overview: A trio of tourists on a fishing trip in the mangrove swamps of Northern Australia are left to fend for themselves when their tour guide is killed by a crocodile.
tagline: What you can't see can hurt you.
title: Black Water
plot:
Black Water is a 2007 Australian psychological thriller film directed by Andrew Traucki. The movie revolves around a young woman named Sarah who goes on a solo diving trip in the Great Barrier Reef, but her adventure takes a dark turn when she encounters a massive saltwater crocodile.

The main theme of Black Water is the struggle for survival and the human will to live against all odds. The film showcases Sarah's determination to escape from the deadly creature that has taken her on a perilous journey through the treacherous waters of the Great Barrier Reef. As Sarah navigates through the unforgiving environment, she must confront her own fears and limitations in order to stay alive.

The movie also explores the theme of isolation and loneliness. Sarah's solo diving trip serves as a metaphor for her emotional state, where she is disconnected from the world around her. The film highlights how this sense of isolation can amplify one's fears and vulnerabilities, making it even more challenging to survive in the face of danger.

Furthermore, Black Water touches on the theme of primal fear and the human psyche's response to threats. The massive saltwater crocodile serves as a symbol of primal terror, representing an unstoppable force that tests Sarah's resolve and pushes her to confront her deepest fears. As the film progresses, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the physical danger posed by the crocodile but also in the psychological toll it takes on Sarah.

Overall, Black Water is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, isolation, primal fear, and the human psyche's response to threats.

overview: Set in the near future, Lockout follows a falsely convicted ex-government agent , whose one chance at obtaining freedom lies in the dangerous mission of rescuing the President's daughter from rioting convicts at an outer space maximum security prison.
tagline: Take no prisoners.
title: Lockout
plot:
Lockout is a 2012 French science fiction action film directed by James Mather and Brian Smith, produced by EuropaCorp and Canal+, and written by James Mather and Brian Smith.

The movie takes place in the future where the United States has created a maximum-security prison called the "Taurus-I" to house the world's most notorious terrorists. The story follows Vincent Moses (played by Guy Pearce), an ex-Special Forces operative who is recruited for a high-stakes mission to rescue his daughter, Sophia (played by Maggie Grace), from the prison.

However, things take a turn when it becomes clear that the real purpose of the mission is not to rescue Sophia but to prevent a catastrophic event. The Taurus-I has been taken over by a group of terrorists led by Admiral William Lynch (played by Peter Stormare) and his second-in-command, General Hugo Gernick (played by Tim Roth). They plan to use the prison's advanced technology to hold the world hostage.

Vincent is paired with Lenina Huxley (played by Carla Gugino), a tough-as-nails prison administrator who becomes his unlikely ally. As they navigate the treacherous landscape of the Taurus-I, Vincent and Lenina must work together to prevent the terrorists from carrying out their plan.

Throughout the movie, Vincent's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his troubled past and grapples with the moral implications of his mission. Meanwhile, Lenina's tough exterior hides a complex and vulnerable individual who is driven by her own motivations for helping Vincent.

As the story unfolds, the tension builds towards a thrilling climax where Vincent and Lenina must face off against Lynch and Gernick in a desperate bid to save the world from destruction. The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including intense hand-to-hand combat and high-stakes chases through the prison's corridors.

Ultimately, Vincent and Lenina succeed in stopping the terrorists' plan, but not without sacrifices. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Vincent reflecting on the true cost of his mission and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to global security.

Overall, Lockout is a gripping sci-fi thriller that explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong in a world where the stakes are high. With its breakneck pace, memorable characters, and pulse-pounding action sequences, Lockout is a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A rich man's daughter is held captive in an abandoned apartment by two former convicts who abducted her and hold her ransom in exchange for her father's money.
tagline: Where is Alice Creed?
title: The Disappearance of Alice Creed
plot:
The Disappearance of Alice Creed is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities of relationships. At its core, the film explores the theme of manipulation and control, as embodied by the character of J.M. Beresford (played by Martin Compston), who uses his intelligence and charm to lure in his victims.

The movie also touches on the idea of class struggle and social inequality, highlighting the stark contrast between the wealthy elite and those living on the fringes of society. The character of Alice Creed (played by Gemma Arterton) is a prime example of this dichotomy, as she navigates a world that seems to be stacked against her.

Furthermore, the film raises questions about the nature of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted for one's own gain. Beresford's use of deception and misdirection serves as a metaphor for the ways in which people present themselves to the world, often hiding their true intentions behind a mask of charm and charisma.

Ultimately, The Disappearance of Alice Creed is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, revealing the darker aspects of our nature and the complexities that lie beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary lives.

overview: Two couples on an oceanside getaway grow suspicious that the host of their seemingly perfect rental house may be spying on them. Before long, what should have been a celebratory weekend trip turns into something far more sinister.
tagline: Secluded getaway. Killer views.
title: The Rental
plot:
The Rental is a 2020 American thriller film written and directed by David Robert Mitchell. The movie follows two couples, Cheyenne and Josh, and Emily and Seth, who rent a vacation home on a remote island for the weekend.

At first glance, the trip seems like a perfect getaway for all four friends. However, as they settle into their new surroundings, it becomes clear that each couple has their own unique issues and conflicts. Cheyenne (Shonali Bose) is feeling suffocated in her relationship with Josh (Bobby Cannavale), while Emily (Lola Kirke) is struggling to come to terms with the end of her engagement.

As the weekend progresses, the group's dynamics become increasingly tense. They engage in a series of awkward and uncomfortable interactions, which are exacerbated by the isolation of their surroundings. The remote location seems to amplify their insecurities and fears, making it difficult for them to connect with each other.

One night, Emily discovers that Josh has been secretly filming her and Cheyenne without their knowledge or consent. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events, as the group's trust is shattered and their relationships are put to the test. As tensions escalate, the group begins to turn on each other, leading to a series of shocking and disturbing events.

Throughout the movie, Mitchell expertly builds tension and suspense, using the isolated setting to create a sense of claustrophobia and unease. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of the island while also highlighting its isolation and vulnerability.

As the weekend wears on, the group's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and disturbing. They engage in a series of bizarre and unsettling activities, which are both captivating and repellent. The movie's climax is both shocking and thought-provoking, leaving the viewer to ponder the true nature of the characters' actions and motivations.

Ultimately, The Rental is a thought-provoking and unsettling exploration of human relationships and the darker aspects of human nature. With its stunning cinematography and expertly crafted tension, the movie is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

overview: In an alternative Victorian Age Gotham City, Batman begins his war on crime while he investigates a new series of murders by Jack the Ripper.
tagline: As the Ripper stalks Gotham City, the Dark Knight reveals the face of terror.
title: Batman: Gotham by Gaslight
plot:
Batman: Gotham by Gaslight is an animated adaptation of the classic Sherlock Holmes story "The Hound of the Baskervilles," set in a dark and gothic version of 19th-century Gotham City, where Batman is portrayed as a character inspired by the iconic detective.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and the blurred lines between good and evil. The main antagonist, Professor James Gordon, has become consumed by his own darkness, driven by a desire for revenge against the villainous Jack the Ripper, who has come to Gotham City from London. As Batman delves deeper into the mystery, he finds himself entangled in a web of corruption and deceit that threatens to destroy the very fabric of Gotham.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and the masks we wear to hide our true selves. Both Batman and Professor Gordon are characters who have taken on personas that serve as a shield against the world, but as the story unfolds, their facades begin to crack, revealing the complexities and vulnerabilities beneath.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the notion of heroism and the morality of vigilantism. Batman's actions are driven by a desire to protect Gotham, but his methods often walk a fine line between justice and revenge. The film raises questions about the nature of heroism and whether it is ever truly justified, especially when the ends justify the means.

Overall, Batman: Gotham by Gaslight is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities of morality in a world where right and wrong are often gray.

overview: Jake Carter and another former Marine, Luke Trapper,  join forces to rescue a young kidnapped girl from a gang of international criminals.
tagline: No one promised them a fair fight.
title: The Marine 6: Close Quarters
plot:
The Marine 6: Close Quarters is an action-thriller film that delves into the world of espionage and counter-terrorism, where a former Marine turned CIA operative must use his skills to take down a group of terrorists. The movie's main theme revolves around the blurred lines between loyalty, duty, and morality in the high-stakes world of international espionage.

The story explores the complexities of a character who has dedicated his life to serving his country, but finds himself torn between his obligations as a CIA operative and his personal sense of justice. As he navigates the treacherous landscape of global terrorism, he must confront the harsh realities of war and the true cost of his actions.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find a way to redeem himself in the eyes of those he has sworn to protect. Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the stakes grow higher, forcing the character to confront his own demons and make impossible choices that will determine the outcome of the mission.

Ultimately, The Marine 6: Close Quarters is a gripping action-thriller that explores the darker corners of the espionage world, where loyalty, duty, and morality are constantly tested.

original_title: The Woman in Black 2: Angel of Death
overview: 40 years after the first haunting at Eel Marsh House, a group of children evacuated from WWII London arrive, awakening the house's darkest inhabitant.
tagline: She Never Left
title: The Woman in Black 2: Angel of Death
plot:
The Woman in Black: Angel of Death is a 2014 British supernatural horror film directed by Tom Harper and written by Jon Croker from a story by Susan Hill, author of the original novel. A sequel to The Woman in Black (2012), produced by Hammer Film Productions and Entertainment One, it stars Phoebe Fox as Eve Parkins, Jeremy Irvine as an RAF pilot, Helen McCrory as headmistress Jean Hogg, Adrian Rawlins, Leanne Best and Ned Dennehy. It was released in December 2014 in the United Kingdom and in January 2015 in the United States.

Some three decades after the events of the first film, during the London Blitz, the young schoolteacher Eve Parkins and the stern headmistress Jean Hogg evacuate a group of children to the remote village of Crythin Gifford. On the train, Eve meets Harry Burnstow, a charming RAF pilot stationed at a nearby airfield. The village is almost deserted, and Eve is frightened by a raving local man, Jacob. The group is billeted at Eel Marsh House, a decaying mansion on an island in the marshes cut off by the tides, which Eve and Jean consider unsuitable, but there is nowhere else to go.

That night Eve dreams of the baby she was forced to give up as a young woman, and she hears a rocking chair in the cellar, where she finds a message reproaching her and glimpses a woman dressed in black. Edward, a boy who has been mute since his parents were killed in the bombing, is bullied by other children and also sees the figure. When one of his tormentors, Tom, is lured out of the house and found dead on the beach, Eve becomes convinced that the vengeful ghost of Jennet Humfrye, the Woman in Black, is targeting the children, as she did decades earlier. With Harry's help, Eve investigates the history of the house and the curse that compels the spirit to kill children, while Jean refuses to believe her. As more children are drawn into danger and Edward seems increasingly under the ghost's influence, Eve must confront her own guilt and find a way to save him before the Woman in Black claims him.

The film received negative reviews. It holds a 24 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it atmospheric and visually sharp but short on tension and scares, and a Metacritic score of 42; audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it a "C." It grossed around $48 million worldwide, considerably less than its predecessor.

overview: On their way to Mexico, six students are stranded in a small town where years before a tragedy took place.
tagline: The Legend of La Llorona
title: The Wailer
plot:
The Wailer (Spanish: La Llorona) is a 2006 American supernatural horror film directed by Andrés Navia from a screenplay by Rafy Rivera, based on a story by Rivera and Al Bravo, and produced by Skyline Films and Laguna Productions. Released direct to video, it draws on the Mexican folk legend of La Llorona, the weeping woman who murdered her own children and whose ghost is said to cry out for them.

A prologue set years earlier shows a woman drowning her two children in a small river. Her horrified husband confronts her, calling her mad, and in the ensuing struggle she weeps over what she has done and kills herself with his knife; he carries her body away and hides it, and no one knows where it was left. In the present, six American students on a road trip to Mexico become stranded in a small town where that tragedy once took place. With nowhere else to stay, they accept the only lodging available, a small cabin, where inexplicable things begin to happen at night: the sound of a woman sobbing echoes through the house, and their growing fear keeps them trapped inside.

Soon they begin to glimpse a woman with a bloodied face who picks off whoever lets their guard down. Julie and Andrew find a rosary that seems to have belonged to the dead woman and search the house, only to hear the ghost crying out for her children as they piece together the truth behind the legend. In the end La Llorona kills all of the friends except Julie, who is possessed by the spirit and murders the man who looks after the cabin before disappearing.

The cast is led by Vanessa Rice as Julie and John Patrick Jordan as Andrew, with Brenda Mejia as Ashley, Eltony Williams as Jay, Nicole Danielle as Michelle and Hugo Medina as Mike. The film was followed by a sequel, The Wailer 2 (2007), in which a professor searches Mexico for his missing daughter Julie, and by a prequel, The Wailer 3 (2012), set before the events of the first two films. Critical response from the horror blogs that reviewed it was largely negative, faulting its clichés, slow pacing, weak acting and reliance on cheap jump scares, though a few reviewers singled out the design of the ghost and some effective moments; the Fringes of Horror blog gave it its lowest rating.

overview: A shy but ambitious film student falls into an intense, emotionally fraught relationship with a charismatic but untrustworthy older man.
tagline: The past never stays in focus.
title: The Souvenir
plot:
The Souvenir is a 2019 British drama film directed by Joanna Hogg, not BBC Film. 

The Souvenir explores the complex and often fraught relationship between nostalgia and reality, as well as the blurred lines between past and present. The film delves into themes of youthful disillusionment, the fragility of relationships, and the struggle to find one's identity.

Through its protagonist, Jodie, the film masterfully weaves a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. As Jodie navigates her way through a tumultuous romance with Anthony, she finds herself caught in a web of nostalgia, where memories are distorted and reality becomes increasingly uncertain.

The Souvenir also touches on the theme of female identity, particularly in the context of women's experiences during the 1980s. The film offers a poignant portrayal of the struggles faced by women at that time, including the constraints placed upon them by societal expectations and the limited opportunities available to them.

Ultimately, The Souvenir is a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that probes the complexities of love, loss, and identity with sensitivity and depth.

overview: A twisted new tale of terror begins for a teenage girl and her family, and revealing more mysteries of the otherworldly realm, 'The Further'.
tagline: This is how you die
title: Insidious: Chapter 3
plot:
Insidious: Chapter 3 is a 2015 American supernatural horror film directed by Marc Forster and written by Leigh Whannell. The movie serves as a prequel to the first two films in the Insidious franchise.

The story follows Dalton Russell (played by Angus Sampson), a young boy who suffers from a rare condition that causes him to fall into a coma-like state, known as "The Further," when he is scared or experiences intense emotions. As a child, Dalton's mother, Renai (played by Rose Byrne), tries to help him cope with his condition.

As Dalton grows older, his condition worsens, and he becomes increasingly isolated from his family. His mother, desperate to find a cure for her son, turns to a psychic medium named Elise Rainier (played by Lin Shaye) who claims to have the ability to communicate with spirits in "The Further."

Elise agrees to help Dalton's mother, but things take a dark turn when Dalton is possessed by a malevolent spirit. The spirit, known as "The Red-Faced Demon," begins to manipulate Dalton and cause chaos in his life.

As Elise delves deeper into the mystery of Dalton's condition, she discovers that he has been experiencing terrifying visions and nightmares. She also learns that Dalton's father, Josh (played by Landon Liboiron), is hiding a dark secret that may be connected to Dalton's condition.

The story takes a thrilling turn when Elise and her team discover that Josh was involved in a tragic accident involving his brother, which led to the death of their younger sister. The guilt and trauma from this event have caused Josh to become increasingly reclusive and isolated.

As Elise tries to help Dalton, she must also confront Josh's dark past and the evil forces that are driving him to madness. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Josh was responsible for his brother's death, and that he has been using his psychic abilities to try and communicate with their sister's spirit.

In the climactic final act, Elise and her team must face off against the malevolent spirits in "The Further" to save Dalton from their clutches. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Dalton is finally able to find peace and closure, thanks to Elise's help.

Overall, Insidious: Chapter 3 is a tense and terrifying horror film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and the supernatural. With its clever plot twists and well-developed characters, it is a must-see for fans of the franchise and horror enthusiasts alike.

overview: A year after his father's death, Oskar, a troubled young boy, discovers a mysterious key he believes was left for him by his father and embarks on a scavenger hunt to find the matching lock.
tagline: This is not a story about September 11th, it's a story about every day after.
title: Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close
plot:
Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close is a poignant and emotional drama that delves into the complexities of grief, loss, and the human experience. The film tells the story of Oskar Schell, a young boy struggling to cope with the sudden and tragic death of his father in the 9/11 attacks.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of grief as a transformative and often painful process. Oskar's journey is marked by a series of encounters that help him navigate his emotions and find a way to heal. Through his interactions with strangers, including a mysterious woman who shares a connection to his father, Oskar begins to unravel the complexities of his own feelings and comes to terms with the loss he has suffered.

One of the primary concerns of the film is the fragility of human relationships in the face of tragedy. The movie highlights the ways in which even the most seemingly ordinary people are affected by extraordinary events, and how these events can forever alter the course of lives. Oskar's father, a kind and gentle man, is portrayed as a symbol of love, kindness, and generosity, whose passing leaves an unfillable void in his son's life.

The film also touches on the theme of memory and its power to both heal and haunt us. Oskar's obsession with finding a mysterious key that he believes will unlock a connection to his father serves as a metaphor for the ways in which we try to hold onto memories and make sense of our experiences. Through Oskar's quest, the movie shows how these efforts can sometimes lead to new insights and understandings, but also how they can become an all-consuming force that threatens to overwhelm us.

Ultimately, Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that grapples with some of life's most fundamental questions – about love, loss, memory, and the search for meaning in a chaotic world.

overview: When a change of circumstances leaves Miriam unable to pay her college tuition, she makes a surprising decision: to start performing in adult films, using the pseudonym Belle Knox. Miriam lies to her family and her friends at school, keeping her double life a secret. But soon rumours spread and Miriam becomes the subject of vicious online attacks and unwanted attention. Miriam fights back: she talks to the media, saying her new line of work empowers her as a feminist. But her confident stand has unintended consequences. Miriam is shunned by her conservative family and her colleagues in the adult film world. One impulsive decision has quickly spiralled out of control - and Miriam's problems are just beginning.
tagline: Inspired by a true story
title: From Straight A's to XXX
plot:
From Straight A's to XXX is a 2017 biographical drama television film directed by Vanessa Parise and written by Anne-Marie Hess, inspired by the story of Miriam Weeks, the Duke University student who performed in adult films as Belle Knox. Produced by Sepia Films and Just Singer Entertainment, it stars Haley Pullos as Miriam, with Judd Nelson, Sasha Clements and Jessica Lu. It premiered on 11 February 2017. Weeks herself was not involved in the production and did not authorise it; the script was based on interviews she had given to newspapers and television.

In 2013, Miriam, a high-achieving student who campaigns on behalf of victims of abuse, is admitted to Duke, but without financial aid. Her father promises to pay her tuition, but after she moves into her dormitory he leaves for work in Afghanistan, and her mother tells her the family cannot afford the fees and suggests a student loan. Desperate, Miriam half-jokingly considers adult films, applies online as Belle Knox, and accepts a shoot in New York, afterwards crying in a bathroom. She then signs with an agent, Don (Nelson), who books her work in Los Angeles. Lying to her family about where the tuition money comes from, she keeps her double life secret until a classmate, Jeff, recognises her, swears to keep quiet and then spreads the news anonymously online.

As rumours spread, Miriam faces vicious online attacks and unwanted attention. She fights back by giving an interview to the student newspaper's reporter Amanda (Lu), describing her work as empowering and feminist, but the published piece distorts her words, and once Belle Knox's identity becomes public she is condemned by many. She tells her conservative family, meeting her mother's condemnation and her father's rejection, appears live on CNN, and later finds her parents ready to accept her, though her brother disowns her. At an adult film awards ceremony in Las Vegas she is shunned by colleagues over her outspoken interviews. The film ends in January 2015, with Miriam giving a motivational speech on women's rights and freedom of choice and telling Amanda that she plans to go into politics.

Reviews were mixed. Lifetime Uncorked gave it four out of five, and The Solute recommended it despite plot holes and an unclear heroine, while The Best Darn Girls gave it three out of five, finding its message muddled. AVN's Peter Warren criticised it as ill-informed about the adult industry and more fiction than biography.

overview: Margot, a documentary filmmaker, heads to a secluded Amish community in the hopes of learning about her long-lost mother and extended family. Following a string of strange occurrences and discoveries, she comes to realize this community may not be what it seems.
tagline: The activity is reborn.
title: Paranormal Activity: Next of Kin
plot:
Paranormal Activity: Next of Kin is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by William Eubank and written by Christopher Landon, produced by Jason Blum and series creator Oren Peli. A reboot and the seventh installment in the Paranormal Activity series, it stars Emily Bader as Margot, a documentary filmmaker, with Roland Buck III as her cameraman Chris, Dan Lippert as sound recordist Dale, Henry Ayres-Brown as Samuel and Tom Nowicki as Jacob. Like the earlier films, it is presented as found footage.

Margot, who was abandoned as a baby outside a hospital by her mother, Sarah, sets out with her friend Chris to make a documentary about her origins. Through a genetics website she connects with Samuel, a young relative from an Amish community, who leads Margot, Chris and Dale to the remote farm where her mother grew up. Jacob, the community's patriarch and Margot's grandfather, welcomes them, explaining that Sarah left after becoming pregnant and is presumed dead.

During their stay, strange events multiply: a little girl speaks cryptically about Sarah, Margot sees a spirit in her mother's old room, and the crew secretly witnesses a nocturnal ritual in which a two-headed goat is sacrificed. Breaking into the community's forbidden church, Margot and Chris discover paintings of the demon Asmodeus and a deep pit. They soon learn that the settlement is not truly Amish and that its members descend from a Norwegian village that trapped a demon inside a woman's body, passing it from mother to daughter through the generations. Margot realizes that she was lured to the farm because she is the next in line, and her friends must try to save her as the community prepares to complete the ritual.

The film moves the franchise away from its suburban home setting toward folk horror, with more polished visuals than earlier entries.

Originally planned for theatrical release, the film was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic and premiered on Paramount+ on October 29, 2021. It received generally negative reviews, with 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 37.

overview: Bilbo Baggins, a hobbit enjoying his quiet life, is swept into an epic quest by Gandalf the Grey and thirteen dwarves who seek to reclaim their mountain home from Smaug, the dragon.
tagline: From the smallest beginnings come the greatest legends.
title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey
plot:
The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey is a 2012 fantasy adventure film directed by Peter Jackson, based on the novel of the same name by J.R.R. Tolkien. The film is set in Middle-earth and follows the journey of Bilbo Baggins (Martin Freeman), a hobbit who joins a group of dwarves led by Thorin Oakenshield (Richard Armitage) on a quest to reclaim their treasure from the dragon Smaug.

The film begins with Bilbo, a comfortable and quiet hobbit living in Bag End, receiving an unexpected visit from the wizard Gandalf (Ian McKellen). Gandalf informs Bilbo that he has been recruited by the dwarves to join them on their perilous journey to reclaim their treasure. Initially reluctant, Bilbo eventually agrees to join the group.

As they set out, the company is ambushed by goblins and trolls, leading to a thrilling escape through the Misty Mountains. The group soon discovers that they are being pursued by the goblin king, Azog (Manu Bennett), who seeks revenge for his defeat at the hands of Thorin's father.

The journey takes them across treacherous landscapes, including the forest of Mirkwood, where they encounter the woodland elves and their leader, Thranduil (Lee Pace). The group also meets Beorn (Mikael Persbrandt), a shape-shifting bear who provides them with shelter and assistance.

As they near the Lonely Mountain, the company faces numerous challenges, including navigating treacherous tunnels and avoiding deadly traps set by Smaug. They eventually reach the mountain, where Bilbo discovers that Smaug has taken over the treasure hoard and is guarding it fiercely.

The film culminates in a dramatic confrontation between Thorin and Smaug, with Bilbo playing a crucial role in distracting the dragon long enough for the dwarves to escape. The journey ends with the company returning to Lake-town, where they are met with suspicion and hostility by the people.

Throughout the film, Jackson's direction brings the world of Middle-earth to life, with stunning visuals and impressive action sequences. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Freeman as Bilbo, who brings a likable and relatable quality to the character.

Overall, The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey sets the stage for the rest of the trilogy, introducing key characters and themes that will be explored in greater depth in the subsequent films.

original_title: The Swan Princess: A Royal Family Tale
overview: Shortly after the Royal Family adopts a young girl named Alise, she is taken away into the forest. Princess Odette, Derek and their woodland friends, must work together to find a way to bring her home to the castle.
production_companies: Motion Makers Animation Studio Pvt. Ltd.
title: The Swan Princess: A Royal Family Tale
plot:
The Swan Princess: A Royal Family Tale is a 2014 American computer-animated musical fantasy film directed by Richard Rich and produced by Crest Animation Productions and Nest Family Entertainment. The fifth film in The Swan Princess series, it features the voices of Laura Bailey as Princess Odette and Yuri Lowenthal as Prince Derek. It was released directly to DVD and Blu-ray on February 25, 2014, marking the twentieth anniversary of the original film.

Centuries earlier, a malevolent force called the Forbidden Arts came from the underworld seeking to destroy every rival to its magical power. It deceived the scullions, a community of talking flying squirrels, into believing that the Swan Princess must be destroyed. When Odette was born, the Forbidden Arts tried to use the sorcerer Rothbart against her, but he was defeated by Derek. In the present, Odette and Derek are pressed by Derek's mother, Queen Uberta, to start a family, unaware that they are being watched by the scullions under their leader, Mangler. The Forbidden Arts attempts to burn Odette but is repelled by her power, and the fire instead destroys a nearby house, killing the father of a little girl named Alise. Odette, who also lost her father, bonds with the silent, grieving child. They decide to adopt her.

The scullions raid Uberta's castle and kidnap Alise to lure the couple into a trap. Derek is struck by a poisoned dart, but a kindly scullion, whom Odette names Scully, cures him and explains the false legend and the true nature of the Forbidden Arts, which is seeking a magical stone that Scully has protected. Odette convinces the scullions that she means them no harm, and when Mangler fires a dart at her, a young scullion named Jojo is hit instead and saved by Odette. The scullions then discover the true prophecy, proving Odette's goodness. They free Uberta and the others. However, the Forbidden Arts seizes the stone.

Odette and Scully enter the cave of the Forbidden Arts to rescue Alise. Scully defeats Mangler, but Odette cannot break Alise's prison. Speaking for the first time, Alise tells her to destroy the crystal that houses the Forbidden Arts. When Odette is unable to do so, Scully throws himself on the crystal, sacrificing himself to destroy the evil force. Alise is freed and calls Odette "Mommy," and the kingdom celebrates as Princess Alise is presented to her people.

The film was followed in 2016 by The Swan Princess: Princess Tomorrow, Pirate Today.

original_title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2
overview: After the birth of Renesmee, the Cullens gather other vampire clans in order to protect the child from a false allegation that puts the family in front of the Volturi.
tagline: The epic finale that will live forever
title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2
plot:
The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 is a 2012 American fantasy romance film directed by Bill Condon, based on the fourth and final novel of Stephenie Meyer's Twilight Saga. The movie concludes the story of Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) and her husband Edward Cullen (Robert Pattinson), who are now a family with their newborn daughter Renesmee.

The story begins with the Volturi, an ancient vampire coven, believing that the Cullens have created an "immortal child," which is against the law of the vampire world. The Volturi, led by Aro (Michael Sheen), believe that the Cullens are hiding a secret and plan to destroy them.

The Cullens gather witnesses from around the world to testify on their behalf, including Jacob Black (Taylor Lautner), who has fallen in love with Renesmee. The Cullens also prepare for a potential battle against the Volturi, while Bella and Edward try to protect their daughter from the danger that surrounds her.

As the story unfolds, the Cullens face off against the Volturi in a dramatic showdown. The movie features stunning action sequences, impressive visual effects, and emotional moments between the characters.

Throughout the film, Bella struggles with her newfound motherhood and her relationship with Edward, who is still struggling to accept their daughter as one of his own. Meanwhile, Jacob's love for Renesmee deepens, and he must come to terms with his role in the Cullens' lives.

Ultimately, the Cullens are able to prove that Renesmee is not an immortal child, but a half-human, half-vampire hybrid, which changes the rules of the vampire world. The Volturi are defeated, and the Cullens are finally able to live in peace with their daughter by their side.

The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 concludes the series on a hopeful note, with Bella and Edward's love stronger than ever, and Renesmee growing up as a powerful and unique individual. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and emotional moments that will leave audiences satisfied and fulfilled.

Overall, The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 is a satisfying conclusion to the series, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers engaged until the very end.

original_title: House at the End of the Street
overview: A mother and daughter move to a new town and find themselves living next door to a house where a young girl murdered her parents. When the daughter befriends the surviving son, she learns the story is far from over.
tagline: Fear reaches out... for the girl next door.
title: House at the End of the Street
plot:
House at the End of the Street is a psychological horror-thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities of relationships. The movie revolves around Elissa (played by Elisabeth Shue) and Ryan (played by Max Thieriot), two young lovers who move to a new town, only to discover that their home is situated at the end of a street where a gruesome murder took place.

As the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that the house has a dark history, and its eerie atmosphere seems to be connected to the traumatic events that occurred there. The film expertly weaves together themes of grief, loss, and the devastating consequences of past traumas on individuals and their loved ones.

One of the primary concerns of the movie is the exploration of the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. As Elissa becomes increasingly entangled in the mystery surrounding the house, she begins to question her own perceptions of reality, leaving the audience wondering what is real and what is just a product of her imagination.

The film also delves into the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The character of Ryan, who has experienced his share of traumatic events, serves as a catalyst for Elissa's journey towards healing and recovery. Through their relationship, the movie highlights the importance of human connection and support in overcoming adversity.

Furthermore, House at the End of the Street touches upon the idea of the "other," exploring how people can be perceived as outsiders or threats to those who are already vulnerable. The film's portrayal of the enigmatic neighbor, Frank (played by Jason Schwartzman), serves as a prime example of this theme, raising questions about the nature of identity and the ease with which people can become objects of suspicion and fear.

Overall, House at the End of the Street is a thought-provoking horror-thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology, exploring themes of trauma, grief, reality, and the complexities of relationships.

overview: Carrie White is a lonely and painfully shy teenage girl with telekinetic powers who is slowly pushed to the edge of insanity by frequent bullying from both classmates at her school, and her own religious, but abusive, mother.
tagline: If only they knew she had the power.
title: Carrie
plot:
Carrie is a 2002 American supernatural horror television film based on Stephen King's 1974 novel, the second adaptation of the book after Brian De Palma's 1976 film. Written by Bryan Fuller and directed by David Carson, it stars Angela Bettis as Carrie White, with Patricia Clarkson as her mother Margaret, Rena Sofer, Kandyse McClure and Emilie de Ravin. Produced by Trilogy Entertainment Group and MGM Television for NBC and filmed in Vancouver, it was conceived as a stand-alone film that could also serve as a pilot for a possible series. It aired on NBC on 4 November 2002.

The story unfolds through police interviews conducted by Detective John Mulcahey, who is investigating a devastating fire and the disappearance of a high-school student, Carrie White. Classmate Sue Snell and gym teacher Rita Desjarden recount the preceding events in flashbacks. A week before the senior prom at Ewen High School, Carrie is a lonely, shy girl tormented by popular students led by Chris Hargensen. When Carrie experiences her first menstrual period in the gym shower, the other girls humiliate her until Ms. Desjarden intervenes. When the principal sends her home and calls her by the wrong name, Carrie's anger makes his desk move.

At home, Carrie's fanatically religious mother, Margaret, who believes menstruation is a sign of sin, locks her in a prayer closet. Ms. Desjarden punishes the bullies with detention, threatening to bar them from the prom if they skip it, and Chris, refusing, is banned. Carrie begins to explore her telekinetic powers. Sue, feeling guilty, persuades her boyfriend, Tommy Ross, to take Carrie to the prom, while Chris and her boyfriend, Billy Nolan, plan a cruel prank. At the prom, Carrie enjoys a rare moment of happiness and is crowned queen, but when a bucket of pig's blood is dumped on her, she unleashes her powers in a rampage of destruction across the school and the town. Unlike the novel, the film ends with Carrie surviving, as Sue helps her escape and the authorities believe she is dead.

The film was poorly received by critics, with a 32 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it brought nothing new and paled in comparison with the 1976 version. Several critics questioned the need for a new adaptation, though Bettis's performance received some praise. The planned series was never produced.

overview: When a hard-working but uninspired sous chef accidentally discovers her boyfriend is going to propose to her on Christmas Eve, she begins doubting their future together; especially when a handsome maple farmer rescues her from a snowstorm.
title: Sappy Holiday
plot:
Sappy Holiday is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Andrew Cymek from a screenplay by Lisa Hepner. Produced by Brigitte Kingsley and Patrick McBrearty for Good Soldier Films and Northern Soul Film Company, it stars Vanessa Sears and Jon McLaren, with Colton Royce, Brigitte Kingsley, Liam Tobin, Rebecca Lamarche, Susan Hamann, Neil Whitely and Ariella Cannon in supporting roles. Released in December 2022, it runs 90 minutes.

Joy (Sears) is a hard-working but uninspired sous chef at a big-city restaurant in New York, where she feels undervalued while striving for promotion to executive chef. Her boyfriend Gabe (Royce) has arranged, without consulting her, a Christmas visit to meet his family at their Vermont mansion. Because Gabe's mother is campaigning for mayor and needs his help, Joy must drive there alone in his expensive car, and while helping him pack she accidentally discovers an engagement ring in his luggage, leaving her uneasy about their future together. Meanwhile James Lewis (McLaren) is struggling to save his family's maple syrup farm, a legacy begun by his great-great-grandfather and maintained by his father, whose leftover debts are taking a toll; his brother David (Tobin) wants to sell. Heading to Vermont through a snowstorm, Joy skids on ice into a snowbank, and Gabe, busy with a press conference for his mother, simply tells her to call a tow truck. James, out on an errand, finds her and takes her to the farm to stay while her car is repaired. Joy, whom James nicknames JJ, loves the peaceful countryside and the warm, welcoming Lewis family, and when young Riley (Cannon) begs her to help save the farm, she comes up with a plan that gets the whole family involved. Rethinking her priorities, Joy realises what has been missing in her life as sparks fly between her and James.

Reception was divided. The family-oriented Dove review, contributed by Super Channel, called it a beautiful Christmas film approved for all ages and praised its message about close-knit families and following one's heart. Wholesome Romance Movies gave it perfect scores, singling out the cabin setting and the inviting family. Cassandra Morgan, however, advised against watching it, finding it slow and boring and complaining that its love triangle failed because Gabe was so dreadful, repeatedly putting his mother's wishes before Joy's needs, that neither suitor seemed a viable option.

overview: Several years after leaving the orphanage, to which her father never returned for her, Gabrielle Chanel finds herself working in a provincial bar. She's both a seamstress for the performers and a singer, earning the nickname Coco from the song she sings nightly with her sister. A liaison with Baron Balsan gives her an entree into French society and a chance to develop her gift for designing.
tagline: Before she was France's famous mademoiselle…
title: Coco Before Chanel
plot:
Coco Before Chanel is a biographical drama film that explores the early life of Gabrielle "Coco" Chanel, a French fashion designer and entrepreneur. The movie delves into her tumultuous childhood, marked by poverty, abandonment, and loss, which ultimately shaped her determination to succeed in a male-dominated world.

The film's main themes revolve around Coco's journey from an orphaned child to a renowned fashion icon. It highlights the struggles she faced as a woman in a society that often marginalized and oppressed women, particularly those who were deemed "unladylike" or "unfeminine." Through her experiences, Coco Chanel developed a strong sense of independence, resilience, and determination, which enabled her to break free from societal expectations and forge her own path.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Coco navigates her way through various relationships and encounters with influential figures, she grapples with finding her place in the world and defining herself outside of the constraints imposed by others. This internal struggle is reflected in her early designs, which were initially met with skepticism but eventually gained recognition for their innovative and liberating qualities.

Furthermore, Coco Before Chanel explores the complex relationships between women, particularly those who are marginalized or overlooked. The film portrays a web of female connections that support and empower each other, providing a sense of belonging and community in a world that often seeks to erase them.

Ultimately, the movie presents Coco Chanel as a symbol of female empowerment and a testament to the transformative power of creativity, hard work, and determination. Through her story, the film inspires viewers to challenge societal norms and forge their own paths, just as Coco did, to create something truly remarkable.

overview: Arn, the son of a high-ranking Swedish nobleman is educated in a monastery and sent to the Holy Land as a knight templar to do penance for a forbidden love.
tagline: A Knight in the Holy Land. A Woman in the Frozen North. A War that Kept Them Apart.
title: Arn: The Knight Templar
plot:
Arn: The Knight Templar is a 2007 Swedish historical drama film directed by Peter Flinth, based on the novel "The Sword" by Jan Guillou.

The main themes of Arn: The Knight Templar revolve around the life of Sir Hans Egede, also known as Arn Magnusson (played by Stellan Skarsgård), a Norwegian knight who becomes embroiled in the politics and intrigue of the Holy Roman Empire during the 12th century. Some of the key themes include:

1. **Loyalty and duty**: The film explores Arn's struggle to balance his personal sense of loyalty and duty with the demands of his lord, King Sigurd I of Norway, and the complexities of his relationships with other characters.
2. **Power struggles and politics**: The movie delves into the cutthroat world of medieval politics, where alliances are forged and broken, and the pursuit of power can lead to devastating consequences.
3. **Faith and spirituality**: As a Templar knight, Arn is deeply committed to his faith and the ideals of the Order. However, he also grapples with the moral ambiguities of war and the nature of God's will.
4. **Identity and self-discovery**: Throughout the film, Arn navigates his own identity, torn between his Norwegian heritage and his adoption into the Templar Order.

The movie's narrative is driven by Arn's journey from a young man to a seasoned knight, as he confronts challenges, forges alliances, and ultimately faces a choice that will determine the course of his life.

overview: Paul Rivers, an ailing mathematician lovelessly married to an English émigré; Christina Peck, an upper-middle-class suburban housewife and mother of two girls; and Jack Jordan, a born-again ex-con, are brought together by a terrible accident that changes their lives.
tagline: How much does life weigh?
title: 21 Grams
plot:
21 Grams is a 2003 American drama directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and written by Guillermo Arriaga. Sean Penn stars as Paul Rivers, a critically ill mathematician, Naomi Watts as Cristina Peck, a grieving mother, and Benicio del Toro as Jack Jordan, an ex-convict and born-again Christian, with Charlotte Gainsbourg, Danny Huston and Melissa Leo. The second part of the director and writer's informal "trilogy of death," after Amores perros (2000) and before Babel (2006), it interweaves its storylines in a nonlinear, fragmented structure. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2003.

Jack Jordan is a former convict who relies on his newfound religious faith to stay away from drugs and alcohol, supporting his wife and children. Paul Rivers, a college mathematics professor, has a fatal heart condition and will die within a month unless he receives a transplant. His wife, Mary, with whom he has a strained relationship, wants to have his child through artificial insemination even if he dies. Cristina Peck, a former drug addict, now leads a happy suburban life with her husband and two young daughters.

The three lives collide one evening when Jack hits Cristina's husband and daughters with his truck, killing them, and flees the scene. The husband's heart is donated to Paul, who begins to recover. Cristina, devastated, falls back into drugs and alcohol. Jack turns himself in, but his faith is shattered and, after his release, he leaves his family. Paul, eager to resume his life, reluctantly agrees to the fertility treatment, but learns that Mary had an abortion during an earlier separation, and their marriage begins to fall apart. Obsessed with discovering whose heart he received, Paul hires a private investigator, finds Cristina and begins to follow her. The two grieving strangers grow close and fall in love. When Cristina learns where Paul's heart came from and who killed her family, she demands that he help her take revenge on Jack, leading to a violent confrontation in a motel room that changes all three of their lives.

21 Grams received widespread acclaim, with particular praise for its performances and its intricate structure. Watts was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress and del Toro for Best Supporting Actor, and Penn won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor at Venice. The title refers to the weight a human body is said to lose at the moment of death.

overview: A police chief about to retire pledges to help a woman find her daughter's killer.
tagline: Detective Jerry Black has made a promise he can't break, to catch a killer he can't find.
title: The Pledge
plot:
The Pledge is a 2001 American neo-noir psychological thriller film directed and co-produced by Sean Penn, based on the 1958 novella by the Swiss writer Friedrich Dürrenmatt. Jack Nicholson stars as a newly retired detective, supported by an ensemble cast including Aaron Eckhart, Helen Mirren, Robin Wright Penn, Vanessa Redgrave and Benicio del Toro. Released on January 19, 2001, it competed for the Palme d'Or at that year's Cannes Film Festival.

On the night of his retirement party, Reno, Nevada, police detective Jerry Black learns that a young girl, Ginny Larsen, has been found murdered. He breaks the news to the girl's parents, and her grief-stricken mother makes him swear on a cross her daughter made that he will find the killer. A suspect, Toby Jay Wadenah, a Native American man with an intellectual disability, is quickly arrested, and under pressure from Jerry's colleague Stan he confesses, then kills himself with a deputy's gun. The case is closed, but Jerry remains unconvinced.

Abandoning his retirement fishing trip, Jerry continues to investigate on his own. A friend of Ginny's reveals that Ginny had befriended a man she called "the Giant," who gave her small porcupine-shaped treats. A drawing by Ginny shows the man with a black station wagon, not Toby's red pickup, and Jerry uncovers similar unsolved killings of young girls in the region that Toby could not have committed.

Determined to keep his promise, Jerry buys a gas station at the center of the area where the murders took place and settles there. He befriends Lori, a waitress fleeing an abusive former partner, and her young daughter, Chrissy. They move in with him,, and Jerry becomes Chrissy's father figure and Lori's lover. When Chrissy tells him that a man she calls "the wizard" has given her porcupine candies and arranged to meet her again, Jerry persuades the police to set a trap, using Chrissy as bait. But the man never arrives: unknown to anyone, he has been killed in a car crash on his way to the meeting. The police leave, Lori furiously rejects Jerry for endangering her daughter, and in the final scene Jerry, drunk and broken, sits alone outside his abandoned gas station, muttering that the killer is still out there.

The Pledge received mainly positive reviews, with praise for Nicholson's subtle performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 78% approval and Metacritic a score of 71. It was a commercial disappointment, grossing $29.4 million against a budget of over $35 million.

overview: Skipper, Kowalski, Rico and Private join forces with undercover organization The North Wind to stop the villainous Dr. Octavius Brine from destroying the world as we know it.
tagline: The Movie Event That Will Blow Their Cover
title: Penguins of Madagascar
plot:
Penguins of Madagascar is a 2014 computer-animated spy comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie serves as a spin-off from the Madagascar franchise and follows the adventures of four penguin characters: Skipper, Kowalski, Rico, and Private.

The story begins with Skipper (Tom McGrath), the leader of the group, who is tasked with protecting the New York City Zoo's penguin exhibit. However, their lives are disrupted when a villainous octopus named Dave (John Malkovich) escapes from the aquarium and starts causing chaos in the city.

As the penguins try to stop Dave, they discover that he has stolen a valuable treasure map that leads to the legendary Golden Chalice of Africa. The chalice is said to have the power to grant any wish, and various villains are after it.

The penguins soon find themselves on a mission to retrieve the Golden Chalice before it falls into the wrong hands. Along the way, they team up with a new character, Classified (Benedict Cumberbatch), a top-secret agent who is sent to help them on their quest.

As the adventure unfolds, the penguins face various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. Through their teamwork and quick thinking, they are able to overcome these hurdles and stay one step ahead of their enemies.

Throughout the movie, the characters' personalities shine through in comedic moments, showcasing their unique skills and quirks. Skipper's leadership is put to the test as he tries to keep his team on track, while Kowalski's genius-level intellect helps them decipher clues and solve puzzles.

As the final showdown approaches, the penguins face off against Dave and his minions in an action-packed battle. In the end, they successfully retrieve the Golden Chalice and use its power to grant a wish that benefits the entire penguin community.

The movie concludes with the penguins returning home as heroes, hailed by their fellow penguins for their bravery and ingenuity. The film ends on a lighthearted note, with the characters enjoying a well-deserved celebration and looking forward to their next adventure together.

Overall, Penguins of Madagascar is a fun and entertaining animated film that showcases the unique personalities and skills of its lovable penguin characters. With its engaging storyline, witty humor, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for fans of the Madagascar franchise and comedy enthusiasts alike.

overview: Mike Milo, a one-time rodeo star and washed-up horse breeder, takes a job from an ex-boss to bring the man's young son home from Mexico.
tagline: A story of being lost... and found.
title: Cry Macho
plot:
Cry Macho is a 2021 American Western drama film directed by Mike Johnson, based on the 1975 novel of the same name by N. Richard Nash.

The movie follows the story of Thomas W. Bond (played by Clint Eastwood), an aging rodeo rider who becomes a ranch hand for a reclusive and wealthy rancher named Crisus "Cry Macho" Parnassus (also played by Clint Eastwood). As Thomas forms a bond with Cry Macho, he begins to see the world through his eyes and learns valuable lessons about life, love, and redemption.

The main themes of Cry Macho include:

1. **Redemption**: The film explores Thomas's journey towards redemption, as he seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find forgiveness.
2. **Mentorship**: The relationship between Thomas and Cry Macho serves as a powerful mentorship, with Thomas learning valuable life lessons from the older man.
3. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Both characters struggle with feelings of loneliness and isolation, which are slowly alleviated through their bond with each other.
4. **Racism and Social Justice**: The film touches on issues of racism and social justice, particularly in the context of the American West during the 1950s.
