Overall, Child's Play is a classic horror film that combines elements of supernatural terror and dark humor to create a unique viewing experience. The movie's success spawned a franchise with multiple sequels, remakes, and spin-offs, cementing its place as a beloved horror icon.

overview: A mother and her 10-year old daughter are trapped in a forest. There is something in this forest. Something unlike anything they have heard before. Something that lurks in the darkness and it’s coming after them.
tagline: Stay in the light
title: The Monster
plot:
The Monster (originally titled There Are Monsters) is a 2016 American independent supernatural horror film written and directed by Bryan Bertino. It stars Zoe Kazan and Ella Ballentine as a troubled mother and her adolescent daughter who become stranded on a remote country road at night while a malicious creature hunts them, with Aaron Douglas, Christine Ebadi and Marc Hickox in supporting roles.

Kathy, an unstable, alcoholic and sometimes abusive mother, is driving her daughter Lizzy to her ex-husband's house because it is his turn for custody. Exhausted from caring for her mother, Lizzy makes it clear that she wants to live with her father for good. As night falls on a lonely road, Kathy hits a wolf, though its wounds look more like the result of an animal attack than a collision. Kathy is hurt in the crash, and Lizzy calls for a tow truck and an ambulance. While the tow-truck driver, Jesse, works under the car, Lizzy notices that the wolf's body has disappeared. Moments later Jesse's severed arm lands on the hood, and the creature drags him away and devours him.

Drawn by the music from Lizzy's teddy bear, the monster pulls Kathy from the car but flees when the ambulance arrives, only to slaughter the paramedics. When Kathy tries to drive the ambulance away, the creature rams it into the woods. Coughing up blood from internal bleeding and realizing that bright light scares the monster off, Kathy makes a torch with her lighter and plans to lure it into the woods so that Lizzy can escape. Before leaving, she tells her daughter that, despite everything, she loves her more than life itself. Kathy lets the creature kill her, believing Lizzy is safe, but Lizzy, unwilling to abandon her mother, drives it off with a flashlight. Grief-stricken and furious, she uses the lighter and an aerosol can to set the monster on fire and then beats it to death with a heavy stick. Recalling one of Kathy's apologies after a drunken fight, in which her mother promised she would grow up to be better than her, Lizzy walks out of the woods as the sun rises.

The film was released through DirecTV Cinema on October 6, 2016, and opened in limited release via A24 on November 11, 2016. Critics praised Kazan's committed, fearless performance, Julie Kirkwood's prowling cinematography and the film's tension, with reviewers in The Hollywood Reporter and Variety noting how much suspense it wrung from a simple premise.

overview: In 1868 during the late Qing Dynasty, rampant corruption on the Imperial Court inflicts much suffering in people's lives. For years, the Black Tiger’s fearsome boss Lei Gong has been trying to get rid of the leader of the Northern Sea. One of his latest recruits is Fei, a fearless fighter who takes the Northern Sea leader’s head after a fierce fight. Just as Lei Gong believes he has total control of the port, a new gang called the Orphans rises in power. Led by Fei’s childhood friend Huo, the Orphans are out to eliminate all the criminal power from the port…
title: Rise of the Legend
plot:
Rise of the Legend is a 2014 Hong Kong-Chinese kung fu action film directed by Roy Chow from a screenplay by Christine To, offering an origin story for the folk hero Wong Fei-hung. Eddie Peng plays the young Wong, leading an ensemble that includes Sammo Hung, Wang Luodan, Jing Boran, Max Zhang, Wong Cho-lam, Angelababy and Tony Leung Ka-fai. It opened in China in November 2014.

The story is set in Guangzhou in 1868, during the late Qing dynasty, where control of the Huangpu port is split between two criminal organisations, the Black Tiger gang and the Northern Sea gang. Master Lui, the ruthless head of the Black Tiger, has long wanted the rival boss eliminated. That task falls to a new recruit, the 21-year-old Wong Fei-hung, who defeats and beheads the Northern Sea leader in a ferocious duel. Impressed, Lui adopts Wong as his godson and elevates him to the Four Tigers, the inner circle of the gang's most trusted enforcers.

Wong, however, is not what he seems. He has infiltrated the Black Tiger to destroy it from within, working with childhood friends on the outside: Fiery, who secretly adores their friend Chun; Chun herself, Wong's sweetheart; the ally Foon; and Big Tooth, a former gang member who joins the mission. Inside the gang, Wong and Chun kill Black Crow, another of the Four Tigers, to obtain his key to the gang's bank vault. Wong also learns that the courtesan Xiao Hua is a childhood friend he had long lost track of. Wu Long, the son of the slain Northern Sea leader, seeks revenge against the Black Tiger, and Lui kills him even as Wong tries to spare his life. The mission exacts a heavy toll: Fiery sacrifices himself to keep Wong's role as a mole from being exposed, and Xiao Hua dies near the end while helping him in her own way. Tony Leung Ka-fai appears as Wong's father, Wong Kei-ying, a martial artist and physician who died in a fire started by a villain while saving his disciples. As the truth about the young man's past comes out, the conflict heads toward a final confrontation with Lui.

The project was announced in August 2013 by Edko Films, Irresistible Delta and BDI Films, with William Kong, Liu Erdong and Ivy Ho producing. Principal photography started in China on 20 August 2013 and wrapped in mid-December. In June 2014 Universal Pictures International acquired the international rights, including North America, while Edko handled distribution in Asia.

overview: Katja's life collapses after a senseless act impacts her. After a time of mourning and injustice, she seeks revenge.
title: In the Fade
plot:
In the Fade (German: Aus dem Nichts) is a 2017 German drama thriller written and directed by Fatih Akin. Diane Kruger stars as Katja Şekerci, a German woman whose Kurdish husband and young son are killed in a bombing carried out by neo-Nazis, with Denis Moschitto as her lawyer, Numan Acar as her husband, Johannes Krisch as the defense attorney and Ulrich Tukur. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival, where Kruger won the award for Best Actress, in her first major German-language role.

Nuri Şekerci, a Kurdish-German man who served time in prison for drug dealing and studied business while inside, now lives a happy life in Hamburg with his German wife, Katja, and their six-year-old son, Rocco, running a small office. One day Katja leaves Rocco with Nuri while she spends the afternoon with a friend. As she leaves, she warns a young blonde woman who has parked a new bicycle in front of the office that it might be stolen if she does not lock it. Returning that evening, Katja finds the street cordoned off: a nail bomb has exploded, killing Nuri and Rocco.

Katja tells the police about the woman with the bicycle and becomes convinced the attack was the work of neo-Nazis, but investigators focus on Nuri's past and possible links to drug traffickers. Overwhelmed by grief, Katja turns to drugs and attempts suicide, but she is stopped by news that suspects have been arrested: a young neo-Nazi couple, André and Edda Möller, whose own father reported his son to the police. The trial in the film's second part becomes a painful ordeal, as the defense attacks Katja's credibility because of her drug use and a Greek neo-Nazi provides the couple with an alibi. When the court acquits them for lack of evidence, Katja, abandoned by the justice system, follows the couple to Greece and contemplates taking justice into her own hands.

In the Fade received generally favorable reviews, with a 77 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Kruger's ability to carry the film, though some felt it did not match her remarkable work. It won the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film and was shortlisted for the Academy Award. The film was inspired in part by the murders committed by the National Socialist Underground in Germany.

original_title: War for the Planet of the Apes
overview: Caesar and his apes are forced into a deadly conflict with an army of humans led by a ruthless Colonel. After the apes suffer unimaginable losses, Caesar wrestles with his darker instincts and begins his own mythic quest to avenge his kind. As the journey finally brings them face to face, Caesar and the Colonel are pitted against each other in an epic battle that will determine the fate of both their species and the future of the planet.
tagline: For freedom. For family. For the planet.
title: War for the Planet of the Apes
plot:
War for the Planet of the Apes is a 2017 science fiction action film directed by Matt Reeves, and it is the third installment in the rebooted Planet of the Apes series. The movie takes place three years after the events of Dawn of the Apes (2014).

The story begins with Caesar (Andy Serkis), the intelligent and empathetic leader of the apes, who has established a peaceful community in San Francisco. However, their tranquility is disrupted by the arrival of a group of human survivors, led by Colonel McCullough (Woody Harrelson). The humans are seeking to reclaim their city from the apes, whom they view as a threat.

Caesar, determined to protect his people and find a way to coexist with humans, decides to embark on a perilous journey across the United States. He is joined by a small group of apes, including Maurice (Jason Clarke), a wise and aged ape who serves as Caesar's advisor, and Nova (Amber Midthunder), a young and fierce warrior.

As they travel through the treacherous landscape, the apes encounter various obstacles, including hostile humans, treacherous terrain, and their own internal conflicts. Along the way, Caesar begins to question his leadership and the morality of his actions, particularly when he is forced to make difficult decisions that put his people in harm's way.

Meanwhile, a ruthless and cunning ape named Aldo (Maurice's brother) seeks to overthrow Caesar and take control of the apes for himself. Aldo's motivations are rooted in a deep-seated resentment towards Caesar, whom he blames for the death of his family.

As the journey progresses, Caesar and his companions face numerous challenges, including encounters with hostile humans and treacherous terrain. They also discover that the humans have been experimenting on them, using them as test subjects for a new vaccine designed to cure Alzheimer's disease in humans.

The climax of the movie takes place at an abandoned asylum, where Caesar and Aldo engage in a fierce battle. In the end, Caesar emerges victorious, but not without great cost. He is forced to make a difficult decision that will determine the fate of his people: he must sacrifice one of his own to save the rest.

In the aftermath of the battle, Caesar realizes that he has become increasingly isolated and detached from his humanity. He begins to question whether it is possible for apes and humans to coexist peacefully, or if their differences are too great to overcome.

The movie ends with Caesar standing alone on a hill, looking out over the ruins of San Francisco. He seems to have come to a profound realization: that the only way for peace to exist between humans and apes is through mutual understanding and respect. However, it is unclear whether this message will be enough to bring about a new era of coexistence, or if the cycle of violence and hatred will continue.

Overall, War for the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores complex themes such as leadership, morality, and the nature of humanity. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive performances from its cast, and a gripping narrative that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Five years after an ominous unseen presence drives most of society to suicide, a survivor and her two children make a desperate bid to reach safety.
tagline: Never lose sight of survival
title: Bird Box
plot:
Bird Box is a Netflix original thriller film directed by Susanne Bier, not Bluegrass Films. The movie was released on December 21, 2018.

The story takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where an unknown entity has caused all the men to become violent and suicidal, forcing them to wear blindfolds at all times to avoid harming themselves or others. The main character, Malorie Hayes (played by Sandra Bullock), is pregnant with her son and trying to survive.

Malorie lives in a small community with her husband, Tom, and their young daughter, Faith. After the apocalypse begins, they try to find safety but eventually lose contact with each other. Malorie sets out on a perilous journey down a river to reach a supposed safe haven, where she hopes to find a better life for herself and her son.

As Malorie navigates through the treacherous landscape, she encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and hostile survivors. She also begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which may be connected to the supernatural entity that has taken over the world.

Throughout her journey, Malorie forms a bond with two other survivors, Tom's friend, Joe (played by John Malkovich), and a mysterious woman named Diana (played by Sarah Paulson). Together, they face numerous challenges and make difficult decisions to ensure their survival.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Malorie is not only fighting for her own life but also for the future of humanity. She discovers that the entity is not just a mindless force but has a sinister purpose: to drive humans to madness and despair.

The climax of the movie takes place when Malorie finally reaches the safe haven, where she finds a community of survivors who have been living in isolation. However, as she tries to integrate into their society, she realizes that they may not be what they seem.

In the end, Malorie makes a heart-wrenching decision to sacrifice her own life for the sake of humanity, ensuring that the entity's malevolent force is contained and preventing it from spreading further.

Bird Box received mixed reviews from critics but was praised for its tense atmosphere, strong performances, and thought-provoking themes. The movie has become a cult classic among Netflix viewers, who appreciate its unique blend of horror and drama.

overview: When a couple of lazy hunter-gatherers are banished from their primitive village, they set off on an epic journey through the ancient world.
tagline: Meet your ancestors
title: Year One
plot:
Year One is a 2009 American comedy film directed by Harold Ramis and written by Gene Stupnitsky and Lee Eisenberg. The movie stars Jack Black and Michael Cera as two of the first humans created by God.

The story begins with the creation of Adam (Jack Black) and Eve (Julianne Hough), the first humans, by God (David Koechner). However, they quickly become bored with their simple life in the Garden of Eden. They start to rebel against God's rules, and things take a turn for the worse.

After being kicked out of the Garden, Adam and Eve find themselves lost in the wilderness. They are forced to navigate through ancient civilizations, including Egypt, Babylon, and Assyria, all while trying to survive and figure out their place in the world.

Along the way, they encounter various historical figures, such as Abraham (Hannibal Buress), Moses (Jemaine Clement), and Noah (Christopher Mintz-Plasse). The duo's misadventures often land them in trouble, but they also learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up.

One of the most significant challenges Adam and Eve face is their own relationship. They start to develop feelings for each other, which complicates their journey. As they navigate through different cultures, they must confront their own desires and learn to accept themselves as individuals.

Throughout their travels, Adam and Eve encounter various obstacles, including wars, plagues, and natural disasters. However, they also experience moments of joy, love, and connection with the people they meet along the way.

As the story unfolds, Adam and Eve begin to realize that they are not just ordinary humans but rather vessels for God's plan. They start to understand their purpose in life and the importance of following God's rules.

The movie culminates with Adam and Eve returning to the Garden of Eden, where they find a new understanding of themselves and their place in the world. However, this time around, they are not just innocent children but rather wise and experienced individuals who have learned from their journey.

Overall, Year One is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that explores themes of identity, community, and growth. The movie features outstanding performances from Jack Black and Michael Cera, who bring depth and humor to their characters. With its witty dialogue, engaging storyline, and impressive historical cameos, Year One is a must-see for fans of comedy and adventure movies.

overview: Marisa Ventura is a struggling single mom who works at a posh Manhattan hotel and dreams of a better life for her and her young son. One fateful day, hotel guest and senatorial candidate Christopher Marshall meets Marisa and mistakes her for a wealthy socialite. After an enchanting evening together, the two fall madly in love. But when Marisa's true identity is revealed, issues of class and social status threaten to separate them. Can two people from very different worlds overcome their differences and live happily ever after?
title: Maid in Manhattan
plot:
Maid in Manhattan is a 2002 American romantic comedy film directed by Wayne Wang and produced by Red Om Films.

The movie follows the story of Marisa Ventura (played by Jennifer Lopez), a hardworking hotel maid who falls in love with Christopher Marshall (played by Ralph Fiennes), a wealthy politician. The main themes of Maid in Manhattan include:

1. Social class differences: The film explores the contrast between Marisa's humble life as a hotel maid and Christopher's privileged world as a politician. This dichotomy serves as a backdrop for their romance, highlighting the challenges they face due to their different social backgrounds.
2. Identity and self-discovery: Throughout the movie, Marisa struggles with her own identity, caught between her modest upbringing and her aspirations for a better life. Her relationship with Christopher forces her to confront her desires and ambitions.
3. Love transcending boundaries: The film showcases how love can bridge gaps between people from different walks of life. Despite their social differences, Marisa and Christopher form a deep connection that helps them overcome their obstacles.
4. Self-sacrifice and compromise: As Marisa navigates her relationship with Christopher, she must make difficult choices about her own future and the sacrifices she's willing to make for love.

The movie features a mix of humor, romance, and drama, making it an engaging watch. The performances by Jennifer Lopez and Ralph Fiennes add to the film's charm, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Maid in Manhattan is a heartwarming story about love, identity, and self-discovery, set against the backdrop of social class differences and the challenges that come with them.

overview: George and Ursula now have a son, George Junior, so Ursula's mother arrives to try and take them back to "civilization".
tagline: Get Back in the Swing of Things.
title: George of the Jungle 2
plot:
George of the Jungle 2 is a 2003 live-action/CGI comedy film directed by Sam Weisman and starring Breckin Meyer, Thandie Newton, and Jeremy Irons. The movie follows the adventures of George, a well-meaning but dim-witted hero who must stop an evil villain from taking over the jungle.

The main themes of George of the Jungle 2 include:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty, as George forms alliances with his animal friends to help him on his quest.
2. Self-discovery: George's journey is also one of self-discovery, as he learns to accept himself for who he is and finds a way to use his unique skills to make a positive impact.
3. Environmentalism: The movie touches on the theme of environmentalism, with George facing off against an evil villain who seeks to destroy the jungle and its inhabitants.
4. Humor: The film relies heavily on slapstick humor and comedic relief, with George's bumbling antics providing much of the laughs.

Overall, George of the Jungle 2 is a lighthearted, family-friendly adventure that explores themes of friendship, self-discovery, and environmentalism in a humorous and entertaining way.

overview: During a post-Christmas play date, the gang find themselves in uncharted territory when the coolest set of action figures ever turn out to be dangerously delusional. It's all up to Trixie, the triceratops, if the gang hopes to return to Bonnie's room in this Toy Story That Time Forgot.
title: Toy Story That Time Forgot
plot:
Toy Story That Time Forgot is an American animated Christmas television special produced by Pixar Animation Studios and Disney Television Animation, written and directed by Steve Purcell. It aired on ABC on December 2, 2014. Set after the Toy Story Toons shorts and months before Toy Story 4, it brings back Tom Hanks, Tim Allen, Kristen Schaal, Wallace Shawn, Timothy Dalton, Don Rickles and Joan Cusack, with Kevin McKidd and Emma Hudak voicing new characters and music by Michael Giacchino. It was Rickles's last television special role before his death in 2017.

Trixie, a toy triceratops, is frustrated that Bonnie never casts her as a dinosaur in playtime. On December 27, Bonnie brings Trixie, Woody, Buzz Lightyear, Rex and Angel Kitty, a Christmas ornament given to spouting holiday morals, to a play date at her cousin Mason's house. Instead of playing with them, Bonnie tosses the toys into Mason's playroom and joins him at his new video game console. The playroom is dominated by Mason's new Battlesaurs playset, a tribe of armored dinosaur warriors led by the gallant Reptillus Maximus and a pteranodon-like shaman called the Cleric. Delighted to be treated as a dinosaur at last, Trixie is armed as a warrior alongside Rex and grows close to Reptillus, unaware that Woody and Buzz have been taken prisoner.

Trixie soon learns that the Battlesaurs have never been played with and do not realize they are toys. When Mason's other toys are attacked in a gladiatorial arena and Woody and Buzz are forced to fight, Trixie defends them, and the Cleric brands her a heretic because Bonnie's name is written on her foot. She flees to fetch Bonnie, and Reptillus, sent after her, is enraged to see his own toy packaging. Meanwhile the Cleric, who knows the truth and has exploited Mason's neglect to rule the playroom, takes control of Rex's robotic weapons and plans to dump Woody, Buzz and Angel Kitty down an air vent. In Mason's bedroom, Trixie explains the meaning of playtime, and Reptillus reluctantly switches off the game. The children rediscover the toys, return to the playroom in time to save Woody and Buzz, and play happily with everyone. Back home, Trixie proudly calls herself Bonnie's dinosaur, content with any role Bonnie gives her.

The special drew 6.79 million viewers on ABC and was acclaimed by critics, earning 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 81.

overview: The boredom of small town life is eating Bill Williamson alive. Feeling constrained and claustrophobic in the meaningless drudgery of everyday life and helpless against overwhelming global dissolution, Bill begins a descent into madness. His shockingly violent plan will shake the very foundations of society by painting the streets red with blood.
production_companies: Boll Kino Beteiligungs GmbH & Co. KG
tagline: Vengeance is ruthless.
title: Rampage
plot:
Rampage is a 2009 action thriller written and directed by Uwe Boll, starring Brendan Fletcher as Bill Williamson, Shaun Sipos as his friend Evan Drince, Michael Paré as Sheriff Melvoy, and Lynda Boyd and Matt Frewer as Bill's parents. It received a theatrical release in Germany and went direct to video elsewhere. Notably, it was the first of Boll's films to earn mainly positive reviews, and it spawned two sequels, Rampage: Capital Punishment (2014) and Rampage: President Down (2016).

Bill Williamson is a 23-year-old mechanic living with his parents in the fictional small town of Tenderville, Oregon. He feels overwhelmed by the world's problems, by constant television and radio news and by the political rants of Evan, apparently his only friend. His parents tell him it is time to move out, a coffee shop owner annoys him, and his boss condescendingly refuses him a raise.

At home, Bill quietly prints counterfeit money and builds a suit of steel body armor with a ballistic helmet and a mask. Heavily armed, he drives into town, first disabling the police by blowing up their headquarters with a remote-controlled van bomb. He then walks through the streets shooting people at random, his armor deflecting the bullets of the officers who try to stop him. Moving from a salon to a bingo hall to a bank, he kills almost indiscriminately, robbing the bank and then burning what appears to be the stolen money while declaring that money is worthless. His rampage leads to a forest where Evan is waiting for a paintball match and where the sheriff pursues him, and as the death toll mounts it becomes clear that Bill's killing spree is part of a calculated plan rather than a sudden outburst.

The film presents a bleak, provocative critique of a society saturated by media and money, with a protagonist who believes the world's population must be reduced, and it is shot in a raw visual style.

Rampage surprised many reviewers. /Film said Boll had finally made a good, if not great, film, and Bloody Disgusting praised his evolution as a director, while Variety's Peter Debruge called it uncompromising and nearly unwatchable, criticizing both its subject and its visual style.

overview: A group of five college graduates rent a cabin in the woods and begin to fall victim to a horrifying flesh-eating virus, which attracts the unwanted attention of the homicidal locals.
tagline: Terror… in the flesh.
title: Cabin Fever
plot:
Cabin Fever is a 2002 American horror-comedy film directed by Eli Roth, not 2003, but I'll provide information on it.

The main themes of Cabin Fever include:

1. Isolation and confinement: The movie takes place in a remote cabin where the characters are trapped with a deadly virus that spreads rapidly, highlighting the vulnerability of those who are isolated from society.
2. Friendship and camaraderie: Despite their differences, the group of friends initially bond over their shared experiences and relationships, but as the situation deteriorates, they turn on each other, revealing the darker aspects of human nature.
3. Social commentary: The film critiques modern society's obsession with superficiality, materialism, and the lack of genuine connections between people. The characters' shallow relationships and priorities are slowly stripped away as they face the harsh realities of their situation.
4. Horror and the supernatural: Cabin Fever is a horror-comedy that uses humor to balance out the scares, but it also explores the idea of a mysterious and deadly virus that seems almost supernatural in its rapid spread and devastating effects.

The movie follows Jeff (Joel David Moore), a medical student who brings his friends to a remote cabin for a weekend getaway. However, their trip quickly turns into a nightmare when they contract a flesh-eating disease from an infected bat. As the group tries to survive and find a cure, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and the true nature of their relationships with each other.

Overall, Cabin Fever is a tense, darkly comedic horror film that explores themes of isolation, friendship, social commentary, and the supernatural.

overview: In the third installment of the Scary Movie franchise, news anchorwoman Cindy Campbell has to investigate mysterious crop circles and killing video tapes, and help the President stop an alien invasion in the process.
tagline: Great trilogies come in threes.
title: Scary Movie 3
plot:
Scary Movie 3 is a horror comedy film directed by David Zucker, released in 2003 by Dimension Films. The movie is a parody of popular horror films, particularly The Ring and Signs.

The story begins with Cindy Campbell (Anna Faris), the protagonist, who is now married to Bobby (Derek Richardson) and has a baby. She receives a mysterious videotape that supposedly predicts her death in 7 days, similar to the one sent to Rachel Keller (Naomi Watts) in The Ring. However, this tape contains a different message: it's a recording of Cindy's own funeral.

As predicted, Cindy starts experiencing strange and terrifying events, including unexplained noises, movements, and visions. She soon discovers that she is being stalked by a supernatural entity known as "The Scary Movie Killer" (also referred to as "The Ringmaster").

Meanwhile, Bobby becomes increasingly paranoid and convinced that the tape is real, leading to comedic moments of tension between the couple. Cindy's best friend, Juno (Rachael Harris), tries to help her uncover the truth behind the tape.

As the predicted death date approaches, Cindy delves deeper into the mystery, discovering a connection between the tape and an ancient ritual that unleashes a malevolent entity. The Scary Movie Killer is revealed to be a cult leader who uses the videotape as a tool for summoning the entity.

In a thrilling climax, Cindy and Bobby must work together to stop the cult and destroy the videotape, saving themselves from certain doom. Along the way, they encounter various comedic characters, including a bumbling FBI agent (Timothy Olyphant) and a group of eccentric cult members.

Throughout the movie, Scary Movie 3 pokes fun at popular horror tropes, exaggerating and distorting familiar elements to create a humorous and irreverent take on the genre. The film's success can be attributed to its clever writing, witty dialogue, and impressive parody skills.

Ultimately, Cindy and Bobby succeed in destroying the videotape, saving themselves from death. However, the movie ends with a twist: as they celebrate their victory, Cindy receives another mysterious tape that predicts her next demise...

overview: An immigrant worker at a pickle factory is accidentally preserved for 100 years and wakes up in modern day Brooklyn. He learns his only surviving relative is his great grandson, a computer coder who he can’t connect with.
tagline: A story of self preservation
title: An American Pickle
plot:
An American Pickle is a 2020 comedy-drama film that tells the story of an immigrant named Herschel Greenbaum who discovers he has a doppelganger in his great-grandson, also named Herschel. As the two Hershels navigate their lives in different eras, they must confront the complexities of identity, community, and belonging.

At its core, An American Pickle explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and cultural backgrounds. The film delves into the idea that our sense of self is not fixed, but rather a dynamic and evolving construct that can be influenced by various factors, including family history, social context, and personal choices.

The movie also touches on the theme of community and how it provides a sense of belonging and connection to others. Herschel's relationships with his family, friends, and community are central to the story, highlighting the importance of these connections in shaping our identities and experiences.

Furthermore, An American Pickle critiques the idea of assimilation and the immigrant experience, suggesting that true belonging can only be achieved by embracing one's cultural heritage while also adapting to new environments. The film's exploration of these themes is nuanced and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationships with identity, community, and culture.

Overall, An American Pickle is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the complexities of human experience, identity, and belonging.

overview: Kingdom of Goguryeo, ancient Korea, 645. The ruthless Emperor Taizong of Tang invades the country and leads his armies towards the capital, achieving one victory after another, but on his way is the stronghold of Ansi, protected by General Yang Man-chu, who will do everything possible to stop the invasion, even if his troops are outnumbered by thousands of enemies.
tagline: Fight to the death.
title: The Great Battle
plot:
The Great Battle (Korean title Ansi-seong, literally "Ansi Fortress") is a South Korean historical action epic from 2018, written and directed by Kim Kwang-sik. It dramatises the siege of Ansi Fortress in 645 CE, when the commander Yang Manchun and his Goguryeo garrison held out for 88 days against an invading army of the Tang dynasty. Zo In-sung stars as Yang Manchun, supported by Nam Joo-hyuk, Park Sung-woong, Bae Seong-woo, Kim Seol-hyun, Uhm Tae-goo, Sung Dong-il, Park Byung-eun, Jung Eun-chae, Oh Dae-hwan and Yu Oh-seong.

The film begins with the Battle of Mount Jupil on 23 June 645, after which the forces of Emperor Taizong (Li Shimin, played by Park Sung-woong) move on Ansi as part of the Tang drive to conquer Goguryeo and expand their territory. Nam Joo-hyuk plays Sa-mul, Bae Seong-woo plays Choo Soo-ji, and Yu Oh-seong appears as Yeon Gaesomun. The Tang army tries to force the defenders into surrender with heavy siege weapons, but the outnumbered garrison under Yang refuses to yield and repels assault after assault. The siege ends when an arrow loosed by Yang gravely wounds the emperor; with their ruler injured and their supplies running low, the Tang troops withdraw.

Filming ran from 23 August 2017 to 24 January 2018. Because Korean sources on the battle are scarce, Kim reportedly read at least 100 Japanese and Chinese publications in preparing the script. The production built a replica of the fortress walls measuring 11 metres high and 180 metres long, and the cast was weighted toward younger actors because of the demanding action sequences.

Released in South Korea on 19 September 2018, during a crowded Chuseok holiday frame that also included Fengshui, The Negotiation and The Nun, the film opened in first place, drew more than one million admissions within four days and topped the box office for its first two weekends, passing four million admissions after ten days. It reached North American theatres on 21 September and was sold to more than 30 territories. Critics generally responded positively, praising Kim's direction, the cinematography, the battle scenes and the performances, though some questioned the characterisation of Yang Manchun and the film's loose approach to history; The Korea Herald's reviewer admitted the film ignored historical accuracy but called the result a lot of fun. Audience reactions were more divided.

original_title: Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy
overview: From the earliest versions of the script to the blockbuster debuts, explore the creation of the Star Wars Trilogy.
title: Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy
plot:
Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy is a documentary film that delves into the creation and evolution of the iconic Star Wars trilogy. At its core, the movie explores the themes of imagination, creativity, and the power of storytelling.

The film showcases George Lucas's journey as a filmmaker, from his early days as a young writer to the making of the original Star Wars film. It highlights how Lucas's passion for mythology, history, and philosophy influenced the development of the Star Wars universe. The documentary also examines the challenges Lucas faced in bringing his vision to life, including the technical and financial hurdles he overcame.

One of the primary themes of Empire of Dreams is the importance of imagination and creativity in shaping our understanding of the world. Through Lucas's story, the film illustrates how a single idea can spark a creative journey that transforms into something greater than its original form. The documentary also touches on the role of nostalgia and the impact of revisiting childhood memories through the Star Wars trilogy.

Furthermore, Empire of Dreams explores the concept of mythology and its significance in storytelling. Lucas's use of mythological references and archetypes in the Star Wars saga is a recurring theme throughout the film. The documentary shows how these elements helped shape the narrative and characters of the trilogy, making it more relatable and engaging for audiences.

Ultimately, Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy is a testament to the enduring power of storytelling and the impact it can have on our lives. By exploring George Lucas's creative journey, the film offers insights into the themes that underpin the Star Wars saga, making it a must-see for fans of the franchise and anyone interested in the art of filmmaking.

overview: Lorraine and Ed Warren travel to north London to help a single mother raising four children alone in a house plagued by malicious spirits.
tagline: The next true story from the case files of Ed and Lorraine Warren.
title: The Conjuring 2
plot:
The Conjuring 2 is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by James Wan and written by Wan and Leigh Whannell. It is the sequel to The Conjuring (2013) and the third installment in The Conjuring Universe.

The film takes place in 1977, six months after the events of the first film. Ed and Lorraine Warren (Patrick Wilson and Vera Farmiga), paranormal investigators, are called to London by a family who claims that their home is haunted by a malevolent spirit. The family, consisting of Peggy Hodgson (Shanley Caswell) and her five children, has been experiencing terrifying events, including unexplained noises, movements, and possessions.

Upon arrival, the Warrens begin to investigate the haunting, which they believe is connected to a dark entity that was once a patient at a nearby psychiatric hospital. The entity, known as Bathsheba, was a 16-year-old girl who was institutionalized for her alleged demonic possession in the 1950s. The Warrens soon discover that Bathsheba's spirit has been awakened by a series of events, including the family's recent move into the new home.

As the investigation progresses, Ed and Lorraine begin to experience strange occurrences themselves, which they attribute to the entity's presence. They also uncover evidence of Bathsheba's dark past, including her history of abuse and trauma. The Warrens soon realize that Bathsheba is not just a simple spirit but a malevolent force that has been awakened by the family's own emotional turmoil.

The film builds up to a climactic confrontation between the Warrens and Bathsheba, which takes place in the abandoned psychiatric hospital where she was once institutionalized. The entity unleashes its full fury on the Warrens, who must use all their skills and knowledge to defeat her.

Throughout the film, Wan expertly crafts tension and suspense, using a combination of jump scares, creepy atmosphere, and clever plot twists to keep the audience on edge. The Conjuring 2 is also notable for its strong female lead, Lorraine Warren, who takes center stage in this installment.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising Wan's direction and the performances of the cast. The Conjuring 2 was a commercial success, grossing over $320 million worldwide and cementing the Conjuring Universe as a major player in the horror genre.

Overall, The Conjuring 2 is a chilling and well-crafted horror film that explores themes of trauma, abuse, and the supernatural. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and expert direction, it is a must-see for fans of the horror genre.

overview: Working-class waitress Slim thought she was entering a life of domestic bliss when she married Mitch, the man of her dreams. After the arrival of their first child, her picture perfect life is shattered when she discovers Mitch's hidden possessive dark side, a controlling and abusive alter ego that can turn trust, love and tranquility into terror. Terrified for her child's safety, Slim flees with her daughter. Relentless in his pursuit and enlisting the aid of lethal henchmen, Mitch continually stalks the prey that was once his family.
tagline: Everyone has a limit.
title: Enough
plot:
Enough is a 2002 American psychological thriller directed by Michael Apted and written by Nicholas Kazan, based on Anna Quindlen's 1998 bestselling novel Black and Blue. Jennifer Lopez stars as Slim, a woman who escapes an abusive marriage and eventually learns to fight back, with Billy Campbell as her husband Mitch and Juliette Lewis, Noah Wyle, Dan Futterman and Fred Ward in supporting roles.

Slim is working as a waitress at a Los Angeles diner when a wealthy customer, Mitch Hiller, comes to her defence against a man pestering her on a bet. They marry, have a daughter, Gracie, and settle into a comfortable home. Six years on, Slim learns that Mitch has been cheating on her without remorse, and when she threatens to leave he beats her and declares that, as the provider, he can do as he pleases. His mother hints at a history of abuse; the police cannot help. After a first escape attempt is foiled at gunpoint, Slim flees with Gracie, but Mitch drains and freezes her accounts and tracks her to a cheap motel. She moves on to Seattle, where her former boyfriend Joe is intimidated by men posing as FBI agents, and turns to her rich, estranged father, Jupiter, who initially dismisses her as a gold digger. Once Mitch's associates threaten him as well, Jupiter sends her enough money to start a new life under a new name in Michigan.

Mitch finds her again with the help of Robbie, a corrupt police officer who, it turns out, was the man in the staged diner incident; the two had been running such cons to seduce women. Slim escapes an attack and a car chase, and a lawyer warns her that the law offers little protection and that a custody hearing may be a trap. Hiding Gracie away, she trains in Krav Maga in San Francisco, recruits a lookalike as a decoy, and breaks into Mitch's new house, hiding his guns and disabling the phone. When he returns, she defeats him in a brutal fight that ends with him falling from a balcony to his death, and the police rule it self-defense.

Sandra Bullock was originally attached to the lead before scheduling conflicts intervened. Filming began on May 21, 2001, and the release, first planned for September 2001, was moved to May 24, 2002. Made for $38 million, the film earned about $40 million in North America and $51.8 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, with 22% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25, though audiences gave it an "A−" CinemaScore. Lopez received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Actress.

overview: Orbiting above a planet on the brink of war, scientists test a device to solve an energy crisis and end up face-to-face with a dark alternate reality.
tagline: The future unleashed every thing
title: The Cloverfield Paradox
plot:
The Cloverfield Paradox is a 2018 science fiction horror film directed by Julius Onah and written by Jeff Nichols. The movie takes place in a space station called Clovers, where scientists are conducting experiments to harness the energy of black holes.

The main themes of The Cloverfield Paradox include:

1. **The Dangers of Playing with Nature**: The film explores the consequences of tampering with forces beyond human control. The scientists on the space station, led by Dr. Catherine Halsey (Gugu Mbatha-Raw), are trying to harness the energy of black holes to create a new source of clean energy. However, their experiments go awry, and they inadvertently unleash a catastrophic event that threatens the entire space station.

2. **The Ethics of Scientific Progress**: The movie raises questions about the ethics of scientific progress and the responsibility that comes with it. The scientists on the space station are driven by a desire to make history and leave a mark on humanity, but their actions have devastating consequences.

3. **Isolation and Confinement**: The film takes place in a confined environment, where the characters are isolated from the rest of the world. This isolation creates tension and paranoia among the crew members, which ultimately contributes to the chaos that unfolds.

4. **The Unpredictability of Technology**: The movie highlights the unpredictability of technology and the dangers of relying on it too heavily. The black hole energy experiments go haywire, and the characters are forced to confront the consequences of their actions.

5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Despite the chaos and destruction that ensues, the film ultimately focuses on the human connection between the characters. The relationships between the crew members are put to the test as they try to survive and find a way to escape the space station.

Overall, The Cloverfield Paradox is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through a sci-fi horror lens.

original_title: ゴジラ2000 ミレニアム
overview: An independent group of researchers called the Godzilla Prediction Network (GPN) actively track Godzilla as he makes landfall in Nemuro.  Matters are further complicated when a giant meteor is discovered in the Ibaragi Prefecture. The mysterious rock begins to levitate as it's true intentions for the world and Godzilla are revealed.
tagline: Witness! A new era of Godzilla!
title: Godzilla 2000: Millennium
plot:
Godzilla 2000: Millennium is a thought-provoking film that delves into the consequences of playing with nature and the dangers of unchecked technological advancement. The movie takes place in an alternate timeline where Godzilla has been awakened due to nuclear testing on the Odo Island.

At its core, Godzilla 2000: Millennium explores the theme of environmentalism and the devastating effects of humanity's reckless disregard for the natural world. The film portrays a world where humans have become increasingly dependent on technology and scientific progress, leading them to neglect their responsibility towards the environment. This is exemplified through the character of Dr. Niko Tatopoulos, who becomes obsessed with harnessing Godzilla's power for human gain.

The movie also touches upon the theme of existentialism, as it raises questions about humanity's place in the world and its relationship with nature. The character of Godzilla serves as a symbol of the uncontrollable forces that lie beyond human understanding, highlighting the limitations of human knowledge and control.

Furthermore, Godzilla 2000: Millennium can be seen as a commentary on the dangers of scientific hubris and the consequences of tampering with nature. The film's portrayal of a world where scientists are willing to risk everything to harness Godzilla's power serves as a warning about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of humility in the face of nature's unpredictability.

Overall, Godzilla 2000: Millennium is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its narrative and characters.

overview: Los Angeles, 1949. Ruthless, Brooklyn-born mob king Mickey Cohen runs the show in this town, reaping the ill-gotten gains from the drugs, the guns, the prostitutes and — if he has his way — every wire bet placed west of Chicago. And he does it all with the protection of not only his own paid goons, but also the police and the politicians who are under his control. It’s enough to intimidate even the bravest, street-hardened cop… except, perhaps, for the small, secret crew of LAPD outsiders led by Sgt. John O’Mara and Jerry Wooters who come together to try to tear Cohen’s world apart.
tagline: No Names. No Badges. No Mercy.
title: Gangster Squad
plot:
Gangster Squad is a 2013 American crime drama film directed by Ruben Fleischer and written by Will Beall. The movie is set in Los Angeles during the late 1940s, specifically between 1947 and 1951.

The main themes of Gangster Squad can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Corruption and Police Corruption**: The film highlights the corruption within the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) at that time, particularly with regards to the police's complicity in protecting organized crime figures like Mickey Cohen. This theme is central to the plot, as the main characters are tasked with taking down Cohen and his empire.

2. **Gangster Culture**: The movie explores the world of gangsters during this period, showcasing their lavish lifestyles, brutal tactics, and code of conduct. The film humanizes these figures, making them more relatable and sympathetic than typical Hollywood portrayals.

3. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: As the story unfolds, the main characters undergo significant personal growth and redemption arcs. They begin as flawed individuals with personal demons but ultimately find a sense of purpose and justice in their quest to take down Cohen.

4. **The American Dream**: The film touches on the idea of the American Dream, which is often associated with success, wealth, and freedom. However, it also explores the darker side of this dream, revealing how corruption and crime can undermine these ideals.

5. **Nostalgia for a Bygone Era**: Gangster Squad has a strong nostalgic tone, capturing the essence of 1940s Los Angeles and its vibrant culture. The film's use of period music, costumes, and settings creates an immersive atmosphere that transports viewers to a bygone era.

Overall, Gangster Squad is a complex and engaging film that explores themes of corruption, redemption, and the American Dream through the lens of a gritty crime drama set in 1940s Los Angeles.

overview: Clawdeen Wolf, half human and half werewolf, has recently started attending Monster High, a school for monsters in all forms. After quickly befriending her classmates Frankie Stein and Draculaura, Clawdeen feels like she has finally found a place where she can truly be herself, or so she thinks. Soon, a devious plan to destroy Monster High threatens to reveal her real identity and Clawdeen must learn to embrace her true monster heart before it's too late.
tagline: Skull's in session.
title: Monster High: The Movie
plot:
I have information on this movie.

Monster High: The Movie is a 2022 computer-animated musical comedy film produced by Brightlight Pictures and directed by Chris Sanders. The story takes place in the fictional town of Coolsville, where monsters live in secret among humans.

The main character, Draculaura (voiced by Atticus Shaffer), is a half-vampire, half-human teenager who struggles to balance her dual identity with her desire to fit in at school. She befriends a group of outcasts, including Frankie Stein (voiced by Brianna Hildebrand), Clawdeen Wolf (voiced by Sherri Shepherd), and Cleo de Nile (voiced by Rosario Dawson).

When Draculaura's parents are kidnapped by the evil King Ghoul (voiced by Rob Riggle), she sets out on a quest to rescue them. Along the way, she discovers that her parents were working to stop an ancient curse that threatens to destroy Coolsville.

As Draculaura navigates this new world of monster politics and ancient magic, she learns valuable lessons about self-acceptance, friendship, and embracing her true identity. The film features a range of colorful characters, catchy musical numbers, and plenty of humor.

Throughout the movie, Draculaura faces challenges from both within and outside her own community. She must confront her own insecurities and learn to trust herself in order to save her parents and restore balance to Coolsville.

Overall, Monster High: The Movie is a fun, lighthearted film that celebrates individuality and the power of friendship. With its vibrant animation, catchy music, and engaging storyline, it's sure to delight both kids and adults who are fans of the Monster High franchise.

overview: A spoof of buddy cop movies where two very different cops are forced to team up on a new reality based T.V. cop show.
tagline: Lights. Camera. Aggravation.
title: Showtime
plot:
Showtime is a 2002 American buddy cop action comedy film directed by Tom Dey and released by Warner Bros. Pictures. It stars Robert De Niro as a gruff detective and Eddie Murphy as an aspiring actor in uniform, alongside Rene Russo, William Shatner, Pedro Damián and De Niro's daughter Drena De Niro.

Detective Mitch Preston of the Los Angeles Police Department's Central Division shoots a news camera after a botched confrontation with drug dealer Lazy Boy, who escapes using a custom-built armor-piercing gun. The cameraman's network, Maxxis Television, sues the department for $10 million but offers to drop the suit if Mitch stars in its new police reality show, and the captain, eager for good publicity, agrees. His partner on the show is Officer Trey Sellars, a patrolman who keeps failing the detective exam and dreams of acting; Trey even stages a purse snatching to impress producer Chase Renzi, who signs him despite the embarrassing ruse. The producers care little for real police work: they build a set inside the station, give Mitch a Humvee and Trey a Corvette, and hire William Shatner, the former star of T. J. Hooker, to coach them. Trey loves it; Mitch is merely irritated, especially after the show redecorates his home and gives him a retired police dog named Powder.

Mitch keeps investigating the supergun, which arms dealer Caesar Vargas uses to kill Lazy Boy. A ruse by Trey yields Vargas's name, leading to a brawl at his nightclub. Vargas's crew then attacks an armored car, and the ensuing chase ends in a destructive crash, after which the chief cancels the show, suspends Mitch and demotes Trey. Reconciling, the two learn that Vargas plans to sell the weapons at a gun show at the Bonaventure Hotel. Vargas takes Chase hostage, but the partners rescue her; a shot ceiling floods the room from the pool above, washing Vargas out of a window to his death, while Mitch and Trey survive handcuffed together. Trey passes his exam and becomes Mitch's partner as a detective, and the show is revived with two new officers.

Released on March 15, 2002, Showtime received generally negative reviews for its flat humor and failed satire of the buddy cop genre; Rotten Tomatoes reported 25% approval. It grossed about $77.7 million against an $85 million budget, and earned Golden Raspberry nominations for Murphy and for the Murphy-De Niro pairing.

overview: After the conclusion of the Battle City Tournament, deep below the sands of Egypt, an ancient evil has awakened. Anubis, who was defeated centuries ago by Yugi’s mysterious alter ego – the ancient Pharaoh – has returned for revenge. Wielding the power of the Eighth Millennium Item, Anubis is determined to destroy Yugi and take over the world.
tagline: Everything else was just practice!
title: Yu-Gi-Oh! The Movie
plot:
Yu-Gi-Oh! The Movie: Pyramid of Light is a 2004 Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series Yu-Gi-Oh!. The movie was produced by Toei Animation, Studio Pierrot, and Shueisha.

The story begins with Yugi Mutou (also known as Yugi Muto), a shy and timid high school student who is haunted by a mysterious spirit known as the Millennium Puzzle. The puzzle is an ancient artifact that contains the spirit of Pharaoh Atem, who was cursed to be trapped in the puzzle for eternity.

When Yugi solves the puzzle, he becomes possessed by the spirit of Atem, which allows him to use his skills and knowledge to compete in a high-stakes card game called Duel Monsters. The movie follows Yugi's journey as he competes against various opponents, including Seto Kaiba, a wealthy and arrogant duelist who seeks to become the world champion.

As Yugi progresses through the tournament, he discovers that the true purpose of the competition is to find the legendary Pyramid of Light, which has the power to bring peace and prosperity to the world. However, Kaiba's true intentions are revealed to be more sinister, as he plans to use the pyramid's power to gain control over the world.

Yugi must now face his greatest challenge yet as he battles against Kaiba and other powerful opponents in a series of intense duels. Along the way, he is aided by his friends Téa Gardner, Tristan Taylor, and Joey Wheeler, who join him on his quest to stop Kaiba's evil plans.

As the story unfolds, Yugi learns more about the history of the pyramid and the true nature of the Millennium Puzzle. He also discovers that Atem's spirit has been guiding him throughout his journey, helping him to unlock his full potential as a duelist.

In the climactic final battle, Yugi faces off against Kaiba in an epic duel that will determine the fate of the world. With the help of his friends and the guidance of Atem's spirit, Yugi is able to outmaneuver Kaiba and claim victory.

The movie concludes with Yugi emerging as a hero, having saved the world from Kaiba's evil plans. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Yugi reflecting on the lessons he has learned about friendship, perseverance, and the power of the human spirit.

Overall, Yu-Gi-Oh! The Movie: Pyramid of Light is an exciting and action-packed adventure that explores the themes of courage, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its engaging characters, thrilling duels, and epic storyline, this movie is a must-see for fans of the Yu-Gi-Oh! franchise.

overview: Newly single, 35, and uninspired by his job, Jesse Fisher worries that his best days are behind him. But no matter how much he buries his head in a book, life keeps pulling Jesse back. When his favorite college professor invites him to campus to speak at his retirement dinner, Jesse jumps at the chance. He is prepared for the nostalgia of the dining halls and dorm rooms, the parties and poetry seminars; what he doesn’t see coming is Zibby – a beautiful, precocious, classical-music-loving sophomore. Zibby awakens scary, exciting, long-dormant feelings of possibility and connection that Jesse thought he had buried forever.
title: Liberal Arts
plot:
Liberal Arts is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Josh Radnor, who also stars as Jesse Fisher, a thirty-five-year-old college admissions officer. Elizabeth Olsen plays Zibby, a nineteen-year-old student, with Richard Jenkins, Allison Janney, Elizabeth Reaser, John Magaro and Zac Efron. The film was shot largely at Kenyon College in Ohio, Radnor's alma mater, and premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2012 before its release that September.

Jesse, a New York college admissions officer who loves literature, is newly single and dissatisfied with his life and career. He believes that the happiest time of his life was his years at a small liberal arts college in Ohio, where he could read and study surrounded by like-minded people. When his favorite former professor, Peter Hoberg, invites him back to campus for his retirement dinner, Jesse eagerly returns.

There he meets Zibby, a sophomore drama student and the daughter of Peter's friends. They run into each other at a campus party and spend the next day together walking around the campus, talking about life, books and music. Jesse also reconnects with Judith Fairfield, his former professor of Romantic literature, whom he has long admired, and meets Nat, an eccentric free spirit, and Dean, a brilliant but depressed student who, like Jesse, always carries a book. After Jesse returns to New York, he and Zibby begin a correspondence through handwritten letters, sharing music and growing closer. Meanwhile, Peter, lost at the prospect of retirement, asks to stay on but learns that his replacement has already been hired. When Zibby invites Jesse back to campus, hinting that she is ready to take their relationship further, he must confront the sixteen-year age difference between them, his own nostalgia for a past that may not have been as perfect as he remembers, and what it means to grow up.

Liberal Arts received generally positive reviews, with a 71 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that, while it could have used more bite, it succeeded as a good-natured and surprisingly clever look at the addictive pull of nostalgia for youth. It scored 55 on Metacritic, and critics praised Olsen's and Jenkins's performances.

overview: A father lives a double life as a counterfeiter, bank robber and con man in order to provide for his daughter.
tagline: Loving his daughter was the only honest work he ever did.
title: Flag Day
plot:
Flag Day is a 2021 American drama film that explores the complexities of identity, family dynamics, and the struggles of growing up in America. The movie delves into the life of Gary Lindbergh, a young man who becomes embroiled in a kidnapping plot involving his own father, Richard Lindbergh.

At its core, Flag Day is a story about the fragility of American ideals and the darker aspects of human nature. It examines how the country's founding principles can be twisted and distorted by personal ambition, greed, and the pursuit of power. The film also touches on themes of identity, as Gary struggles to come to terms with his own sense of self and find his place in the world.

The movie is also a nuanced portrayal of family dynamics, particularly the complicated relationships within the Lindbergh family. It highlights the tension between the idealized image of America's founding fathers and the harsh realities of their personal lives. Through Gary's story, Flag Day sheds light on the darker aspects of American history, revealing the complexities and contradictions that underlie the country's mythology.

Ultimately, Flag Day is a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be an American, and how the ideals of freedom and democracy can be both celebrated and compromised.

overview: Turo is stuck in a small village and the best thing in his life is being the lead vocalist for the amateur metal band Impaled Rektum. He and his bandmates have practiced for 12 years without playing a single gig. The guys get a surprise visitor from Norway -- the promoter for a huge heavy metal music festival -- and decide it's now or never. They steal a van, a corpse, and even a new drummer to make their dreams a reality.
tagline: Better shit thighs than eternal constipation.
title: Heavy Trip
plot:
Heavy Trip is a 2018 Canadian stoner comedy film directed by Chris Craddock and written by Adam Brooks and Jay Baruchel. The movie follows the story of Justin, a shy and awkward teenager who becomes obsessed with heavy metal music after discovering a vinyl record in his attic.

The main theme of Heavy Trip revolves around the transformative power of music, particularly heavy metal, on the protagonist's life. As Justin delves deeper into the world of heavy metal, he finds solace and empowerment through the genre's raw energy and rebellious spirit. The film explores how music can be a catalyst for self-discovery, creativity, and rebellion against societal norms.

Through Justin's journey, the movie also touches on themes of adolescence, identity, and the struggles of growing up. As Justin navigates his relationships with family and friends, he must confront his own insecurities and find his place in the world. The film's portrayal of these themes is often humorous and lighthearted, but also nuanced and relatable.

Furthermore, Heavy Trip critiques the excesses of the heavy metal subculture, particularly its tendency towards pretentiousness and elitism. The movie pokes fun at the genre's stereotypes and conventions, while also acknowledging its power to inspire creativity and community.

Overall, Heavy Trip is a heartwarming and humorous coming-of-age story that celebrates the transformative power of music and the importance of embracing one's individuality.

overview: During an ordinary day in Hundred Acre Wood, Winnie the Pooh sets out to find some honey. Misinterpreting a note from Christopher Robin, Owl convinces Pooh, Tigger, Rabbit, Piglet, Kanga, Roo, and Eeyore that their young friend has been captured by a creature named "Backson" and they set out to rescue him.
tagline: Oh Pooh.
title: Winnie the Pooh
plot:
Winnie the Pooh (2011) is a computer-animated film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the adventures of Winnie the Pooh, a friendly and lovable bear, and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood.

The main themes of Winnie the Pooh (2011) include:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty among the characters, particularly between Pooh and his best friend Piglet.
2. Imagination: The movie celebrates the power of imagination and creativity, as seen in Pooh's love for honey and his fantastical adventures with his friends.
3. Growing up: The story also touches on the theme of growing up and letting go, as Pooh and his friends face challenges and learn to navigate the complexities of life.
4. Emotional intelligence: The film promotes emotional intelligence and self-awareness, as the characters learn to recognize and manage their emotions in a healthy way.

The movie features a talented voice cast, including Jim Cummings as Winnie the Pooh, Craig Ferguson as Rabbit, and Travis Oates as Piglet. The animation is beautiful and vibrant, bringing the beloved characters to life in a way that will delight both children and adults.

Overall, Winnie the Pooh (2011) is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the joys of friendship, imagination, and growing up.

belongs_to_collection.name: I Know What You Did Last Summer Collection

original_title: I'll Always Know What You Did Last Summer
overview: Several teenagers in a small-town in Colorado concoct a July 4th prank based on a frightening legend that goes awry when their friend ends up accidentally killed; however, the teens agree to keep their involvement a secret from the authorities, who continue to search for the man who apparently killed their friend. A year later, with the July 4th celebration coming up again, the teenagers realize that they're being stalked by someone who clearly intends on keeping the horrible legend alive by killing them off.
tagline: What he knows might kill you…
title: I'll Always Know What You Did Last Summer
plot:
I'll Always Know What You Did Last Summer is a psychological horror-thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the consequences of guilt and the devastating effects of trauma. The movie follows Julie James, a young woman who seeks revenge against the people she believes wronged her in a tragic accident.

At its core, the film explores the theme of guilt and how it can consume individuals, leading them down a path of destruction and chaos. The main character's relentless pursuit of justice is driven by her own feelings of guilt and responsibility for the events that transpired, highlighting the destructive nature of unchecked emotions.

The movie also touches on the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and their relationships. Julie's past experiences have left emotional scars, which she struggles to overcome, ultimately leading her down a dark path of revenge and self-destruction.

Furthermore, I'll Always Know What You Did Last Summer critiques the notion of vigilantism and the dangers of taking the law into one's own hands. The film suggests that seeking revenge can lead to further harm and suffering for all parties involved, rather than providing closure or justice.

Overall, the movie is a gripping exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, delving into themes of guilt, trauma, and the destructive consequences of unchecked emotions.

overview: In 1987, during the austere days of Thatcher’s Britain, a teenager learns to live life, understand his family, and find his own voice through the music of Bruce Springsteen.
tagline: For anyone who has ever wanted to dream. You're not alone.
title: Blinded by the Light
plot:
Blinded by the Light is a 2019 British comedy-drama film directed by Gurinder Chadha, inspired by the life of journalist Sarfraz Manzoor and his love of Bruce Springsteen's music. Manzoor wrote the screenplay with Chadha and Paul Mayeda Berges, based on his 2007 memoir Greetings from Bury Park. Viveik Kalra stars, with Hayley Atwell, Rob Brydon, Kulvinder Ghir and Nell Williams in supporting roles.

In Luton in 1987, during Margaret Thatcher's premiership, British-Pakistani teenager Javed Khan writes poetry and song lyrics but feels stifled by his strict father Malik, who forbids him to socialize, and by the racism he faces from neighbors and classmates. At sixth form college his writing teacher, Ms Clay, encourages him to pursue writing, and he develops a crush on activist Eliza. Then Malik loses his job at Vauxhall Motors after sixteen years, and the family struggles. On the night of the great storm of 1987, Javed throws away his poems, but a classmate, Roops, has lent him two Springsteen cassettes, and the lyrics seem to describe his own life. Inspired, he retrieves his poems, publishes a piece on Springsteen in the student paper, wins over Eliza and lands an unpaid internship at the Luton Herald.

Tensions mount as the National Front marches through town, and Malik objects to Javed's ambitions. On the morning of his cousin Yasmeen's wedding, Javed rushes off to buy Springsteen concert tickets with money from a front-page article, while Malik is assaulted by National Front members. In the ensuing fight, Malik tears up the tickets, and Javed declares that he will study at the University of Manchester. After his Springsteen essay wins him a trip to New Jersey, Javed goes despite his father's threats. At a college prize-giving, with his family in the audience, he speaks instead about being blinded by his dreams, vowing to build a bridge to his ambitions rather than a wall between himself and his family. Javed and Malik reconcile, and Javed sells his memorabilia to recover his mother's jewellery before leaving for university.

Blinded by the Light premiered at the 2019 Sundance Film Festival and was released in the United Kingdom by Entertainment One on 9 August 2019 and by New Line Cinema in the United States a week later. It received positive reviews, with 89% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71, but grossed only about $19.6 million worldwide.

overview: When young couple Sarah and Kyle move next door to Helen, a charismatic older woman, they have no idea she's a deeply disturbed psychopath who will stop at nothing to become Sarah's surrogate mother, and grandmother to the child she is expecting. Julia Borsellino, Mark Taylor, Deborah Grover, Marium Carvell star. (2021)
title: Next-Door Nightmare
plot:
Next-Door Nightmare is a 2021 Canadian thriller television film directed by Gordon Yang and written by Stephen Romano, produced by NB Thrilling Films with Reel One Entertainment for Lifetime, which premiered it in July 2021. It stars Julia Borsellino as Sarah Collins, Mark Taylor as her husband Kyle and Deborah Grover as their neighbor Helen Henderson, with Marium Carvell as Kyle's mother Judith, Michelle Chiu as Sarah's best friend Jennifer, Cait Alexander as Kyle's ex Angela, Deanna Jarvis as the social worker Grace and Ash Catherwood as her colleague David. It runs 86 minutes.

In a snowy prologue, the wealthy widow Helen hounds Kelly, a pregnant young woman whom she insists is her daughter. Fleeing Helen's house, Kelly is killed when she loses control of her car while answering her phone, and when the police come to question Helen she stabs an officer and is committed to a mental hospital. Some nine months later Helen is back in the same house, and Sarah and Kyle, a young couple, move in next door. Helen's own daughter took her life years before, and since then Helen has fixated on young women in troubled marriages who are about to have children, trying to recast them as her family. Sarah, who grew up in a group home with Jennifer and was never adopted, is drawn to Helen's warmth, confiding that Kyle once had an affair, and when she learns she is pregnant Helen celebrates with her like a mother. When Grace, the social worker monitoring her, discovers Helen's shrine to her past obsessions, Helen stabs her and buries her in the snow, and she later kills Judith, who has grown suspicious and found out about Helen's past online. With Kyle often away on business, Helen bribes Angela to set him up in compromising photographs, and Sarah, believing he is cheating again, leaves him. Helen then takes her to a remote country house she has bought, drugs her and holds her captive, intending to raise Sarah and the baby as an all-female family. Jennifer finds the property's address in Helen's trash and Grace's buried body, and Kyle races to rescue his wife as Helen opens fire with a gun.

Mark Gabrish Conlan of Movie Magg considered it better done than most Lifetime films of its type, praising Romano's quick, economical setup, Yang's suspenseful direction and Grover's deliciously unsubtle, full-throated performance. Patrick Serrano of Lifetime Uncorked recapped it with enthusiasm, lamenting the death of Judith.

overview: A crew of officers at an armored transport security firm risk their lives when they embark on the ultimate heist against their own company. Armed with a seemingly fool-proof plan, the men plan on making off with a fortune with harm to none. But when an unexpected witness interferes, the plan quickly unravels and all bets are off.
tagline: To protect and serve yourself.
title: Armored
plot:
Armored is a 2009 American heist action thriller directed by Nimród Antal from a script by James V. Simpson. Columbus Short leads a cast that includes Matt Dillon, Laurence Fishburne, Jean Reno, Skeet Ulrich, Amaury Nolasco, Milo Ventimiglia and Fred Ward. It was released on December 4, 2009.

Ty Hackett is a military veteran who now works on an armored transport crew for the security firm Eagle Shield. Since their parents died he has been raising his younger brother Jimmy, but the bills are piling up: the bank is threatening to foreclose on the house, and social services are considering placing the truant Jimmy in foster care. Mike Cochrane, Ty's godfather and colleague, lets him in on a plan to rob two of their own trucks of the $42 million they are carrying from the Federal Reserve to local banks. Ty initially refuses, but agrees after Mike promises that nobody will get hurt.

The six guards unload the first truck at an abandoned steel mill, but a homeless man living there sees them, and Baines shoots him dead. Horrified, Ty locks himself inside the second truck with the remaining $21 million. When he cannot drive away, he trips the alarm, drawing sheriff's deputy Jake Eckehart to the mill. Baines shoots the deputy, and Ty pulls the wounded man into the truck while the others try to knock out the door hinges. Dobbs wavers and secretly tries to replace an engine fuse Mike removed, but Palmer catches and kills him; later, after Ty persuades Palmer that the robbery is wrong, Palmer, consumed by guilt, takes his own life. The surviving robbers then reveal that they have kidnapped Jimmy, and Ty is forced to cooperate. Quinn and Baines are killed by a booby trap rigged to the cash, and Mike, chasing Ty in the other truck, crashes into a pit and dies. Recovering in hospital, Jake tells Duncan Ashcroft how Ty tried to stop the thieves, a reward is mentioned, and the brothers go home.

Screen Gems bought Simpson's spec script in 2006, Dillon and Short were announced as leads in 2007, and the film was shot in Los Angeles. It was not screened for critics in advance and drew mostly negative reviews, scoring 42% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus faulted plot holes and a messy finale despite the good cast; CinemaScore audiences gave it a "B−". A. O. Scott of The New York Times was kinder, calling it a basic, brutal and sometimes clumsy B movie that was far from dumb, and praising Andrzej Sekuła's cinematography.

overview: A bumbling Paris policeman is doggedly determined to capture the master thief that repeatedly eludes him, even when they're the last two men on Earth.
tagline: What if Paris was yours?
title: 2 Alone in Paris
plot: A bumbling Paris policeman is doggedly determined to capture the master thief that repeatedly eludes him, even when they're the last two men on Earth.

overview: When LeBron and his young son Dom are trapped in a digital space by a rogue A.I., LeBron must get them home safe by leading Bugs, Lola Bunny and the whole gang of notoriously undisciplined Looney Tunes to victory over the A.I.'s digitized champions on the court. It's Tunes versus Goons in the highest-stakes challenge of his life.
tagline: Welcome to the Jam!
title: Space Jam: A New Legacy
plot:
Space Jam: A New Legacy is a live-action/animated sports comedy film directed by Malcolm D. Lee, starring LeBron James and Don Cheadle. The movie takes place in a world where AI has become an integral part of our lives, and the main character, LeBron James, finds himself trapped in a virtual reality game called "Soulstar" created by a powerful AI named Al-G Rhythm.

In this virtual world, LeBron is forced to compete against his digital doppelganger, Dunks, who is controlled by Al-G. The AI has taken over the real world and is using its vast powers to enslave humanity, forcing people to play the game of "Soulstar" for their entertainment.

LeBron teams up with Bugs Bunny, a wise-cracking cartoon rabbit, and his friends from the Looney Tunes universe, including Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, and Lola Bunny. Together, they embark on a mission to defeat Al-G and free humanity from its digital shackles.

As LeBron navigates this virtual world, he must confront his own fears and doubts about being a hero. He also learns valuable lessons about the importance of teamwork, friendship, and believing in oneself. The movie features a mix of live-action and animation, blending humor, action, and heartwarming moments.

Throughout the film, LeBron faces off against Al-G's army of digital creatures, including the "Monstars," who are similar to the Monstars from the original Space Jam. The movie also explores themes of technology addiction, social media, and the impact of AI on our lives.

Overall, Space Jam: A New Legacy is a fun, entertaining film that combines humor, action, and heartwarming moments with a thought-provoking exploration of the consequences of relying too heavily on technology.

overview: Kept locked inside the house by her father, 7-year-old Chloe lives in fear and fascination of the outside world, where Abnormals create a constant threat—or so she believes. When a mysterious stranger offers her a glimpse of what's really happening outside, Chloe soon finds that while the truth isn't so simple, the danger is very real.
tagline: They look just like us
title: Freaks
plot:
