Pet is a 2016 psychological thriller film directed by Carles Torrens and written by Jeremy Slater, who had sold the script in 2007. It stars Dominic Monaghan as Seth, Ksenia Solo as Holly, Jennette McCurdy as Claire, Nathan Parsons as Eric and Da'Vone McDonald as Nate.

Seth, a painfully introverted man who works at an animal control center, becomes obsessed with Holly, a waitress and former high school classmate, after seeing her writing in a journal on a bus. Encouraged by Nate, a security guard at work, he studies her online profiles and asks her out, but she rejects him. When he follows her to the bar where her ex-boyfriend Eric works and refuses to accept her rejection, a scuffle breaks out, and Seth steals her journal, which he reads obsessively. In an abandoned wing of the shelter he finds a hidden room, builds a steel cage, then breaks into Holly's apartment and kidnaps her.

Seth tells the caged Holly that he loves her and has imprisoned her to "save" her. From the journal he has learned that Holly's friend Claire had an affair with Eric, and that Holly, in a rage, crashed their car into a truck and then stabbed the injured Claire with a shard of glass, a death blamed on the accident. Since then Holly has committed a series of gruesome murders and recorded them in her journal, and Seth has found a purpose in stopping her. The two engage in psychological games, with Seth insisting she kills out of guilt and Holly answering that she kills for pleasure. When the suspicious Nate discovers Holly, she distracts him so Seth can overpower him, and at her urging Seth kills Nate and disposes of the body. Holly then persuades Seth to prove his love by cutting off his finger, seizes his knife, threatens suicide unless he frees her, and slits his throat. Some time later, Holly is back with Eric and has published her journal entries as fiction through a vanity press. Discovering that Eric is cheating again, she spares him and instead visits a warehouse where Seth, still alive but horribly mutilated, is kept in a cage, thanking him for absorbing her murderous impulses.

Pet premiered at South by Southwest on March 11, 2016, and was released in nine US theaters on December 2, 2016, by Orion Pictures and Samuel Goldwyn Films, grossing just $8,004. Reviews were mixed, praising its subversive themes and lead performances but criticizing implausible twists; Rotten Tomatoes reported 56% approval and Metacritic a score of 48.

overview: A determined Angela makes a wish to reunite her family in time for Christmas, then launches a plan to find her way from Ireland to Australia.
title: Angela's Christmas Wish
plot:
Angela's Christmas Wish is a heartwarming animated film produced by Brown Bag Films, released in 2020. The movie follows the story of Angela, a young girl who lives with her grandmother, Granny May, in a small Irish village.

The story begins on Christmas Eve, where Angela is struggling to come to terms with the fact that she will be spending Christmas alone this year. Her parents have gone away for work, and she's feeling lonely and left out. As she's walking through the snowy streets of her village, she stumbles upon a mysterious old shop called "The Wish Shop." The shop is run by an eccentric old man named Mr. Jenkins, who claims to grant wishes to those who believe in them.

Angela is immediately drawn to the shop and decides to make a wish for a family Christmas. However, things take a surprising turn when she discovers that her wish has been granted, but not in the way she expected. Instead of having a traditional family Christmas with her parents, Angela finds herself transported to a magical world where she meets a group of children who are also waiting for their wishes to be granted.

As Angela navigates this new world, she learns valuable lessons about the true meaning of Christmas and the importance of kindness, generosity, and believing in oneself. Along the way, she befriends a young boy named Finn, who becomes her ally and companion on this magical journey.

Throughout the movie, Angela faces various challenges and obstacles as she tries to find a way back home. However, with the help of Mr. Jenkins and the other children in the magical world, she eventually discovers that the true magic of Christmas lies within herself and those around her.

The ending of the movie is heartwarming and uplifting, as Angela returns home to find that her wish has been granted in a way that brings her even closer to her family. The movie concludes with Angela reflecting on what she's learned about the importance of believing in oneself and the power of kindness and generosity during the holiday season.

Overall, Angela's Christmas Wish is a delightful animated film that celebrates the spirit of Christmas and the magic of believing in oneself. With its beautiful animation, engaging storyline, and lovable characters, it's a must-watch for families and fans of animated films alike.

original_title: Once Upon a Time in Mexico
overview: Hitman "El Mariachi" becomes involved in international espionage involving a psychotic CIA agent and a corrupt Mexican general.
tagline: The Time Has Come.
title: Once Upon a Time in Mexico
plot:
Once Upon a Time in Mexico is a 2003 American crime drama film directed by Robert Rodriguez, written by Robert Rodriguez and Shiny Rodriguez, and starring Antonio Banderas, Johnny Depp, and Salma Hayek.

The film takes place after the events of El Mariachi (1992) and Desperado (1995), and serves as a sequel to both films. The story follows El Mariachi (Antonio Banderas), a Mexican musician who becomes embroiled in a violent struggle between rival cartels, led by the ruthless Don Carlos (Javier Bardem).

The film begins with El Mariachi performing at a bar in Mexico City, where he is mistaken for a famous singer. He soon finds himself caught up in a complex web of violence and deception as he tries to uncover the truth about his past and the identity of the mysterious woman who has been following him.

As El Mariachi delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he becomes embroiled in a cat-and-mouse game with Don Carlos, who will stop at nothing to eliminate him. Along the way, he meets a beautiful woman named Carolina (Salma Hayek), who is being pursued by Don Carlos' henchmen.

The plot thickens as El Mariachi discovers that Carolina is actually the daughter of Don Carlos, and that she has been trying to escape her father's clutches. As the stakes grow higher, El Mariachi finds himself in a desperate bid for survival, using his wits and his musical talents to outsmart his enemies.

Meanwhile, Johnny Depp plays Jack Buechner, an American hitman who is hired by Don Carlos to eliminate El Mariachi. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jack's true loyalties lie with Carolina, and he finds himself torn between his duty to Don Carlos and his growing feelings for the beautiful woman.

As the film hurtles towards its climax, El Mariachi and Jack engage in a series of intense battles, using everything from guns to musical instruments to try and outmaneuver each other. In the end, it is up to El Mariachi to use all his cunning and resourcefulness to defeat Don Carlos and bring peace to the troubled region.

Throughout the film, Robert Rodriguez pays homage to classic Westerns and Mexican cinema, incorporating a range of clever references and Easter eggs into the narrative. The result is a thrilling and entertaining ride that combines action, drama, and music in a way that is both unique and captivating.

Overall, Once Upon a Time in Mexico is a gripping and stylish film that showcases the talents of its cast and crew. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning visuals, it is a must-see for fans of Robert Rodriguez and anyone who loves a good action movie.

overview: Self-proclaimed ethical hacker Mel Bandison's life is turned upside down when she stops a data breach on a high-tech self-driving bus that also happens to shut down an international criminal network. She then becomes a target and is framed with a deepfake video that “shows” that she murders someone.
title: The Takeover
plot:
The Takeover is a 2022 Dutch action thriller directed by Annemarie van de Mond and produced by Fiction Valley for Netflix, billed as the streamer's first original action film set in the Netherlands. Holly Mae Brood stars as the ethical hacker Mel Bandison, with Géza Weisz as Thomas, Frank Lammers as the hacker Buddy Benschot, and Susan Radder, Noortje Herlaar, Walid Benmbarek and Lawrence Sheldon in supporting roles.

Mel, a talented 26-year-old IT security expert in Rotterdam, is auditing the software that controls the country's first self-driving bus for the transport company Rotramax. The system processes images of passengers' faces to allow secure payment, and Mel discovers that this biometric data is secretly being sent to outside recipients. To stop the leak, she plants her own Trojan, unknowingly making herself the target of an international criminal network. Two armed men break into her apartment and chase her; when she escapes to a police station, she sees them chatting amiably with officers and flees again. She is helped by Thomas, the man she met the night before on a failed blind date. Soon a video appears on television apparently showing Mel shooting a man, and she becomes a fugitive. A man named Rogers offers to make her "video problem" disappear if she decrypts the Trojan, threatening Thomas as well. To prove that the footage is a deepfake, Mel turns to the eccentric Buddy, a former partner she once reported for keeping money they had seized from criminals. Their search leads to a facial-recognition company working with Rotramax that steals personal data, and Mel realizes the fake video was built from data captured when she boarded the bus. After Rogers's men kill Buddy, Mel breaks into the Rotramax server room, where a shootout cuts the link to the driverless bus on its maiden trip with fifteen passengers aboard. With Thomas's help on board, she stops the bus before it plunges toward an opened bridge, clears her name and inherits a digital network Buddy built.

Filming lasted two months, partly in Rotterdam, where the Erasmus Bridge was closed to traffic for night shoots. Released on Netflix on 1 November 2022, the film drew largely negative reviews, with critics citing clichéd plotting, flat dialogue and limited budget in the final action scenes, though some praised Brood. It nonetheless became an international hit, ranking second among Netflix's non-English films worldwide in its first week with more than 25 million hours viewed.

overview: A bravado period action film set at the end of Japan's feudal era in which a group of unemployed samurai are enlisted to bring down a sadistic lord and prevent him from ascending to the throne and plunging the country into a war-torn future.
tagline: Take up your sword.
title: 13 Assassins
plot:
13 Assassins (Jūsannin no Shikaku) is a 2010 Japanese samurai film directed by Takashi Miike, a remake of Eiichi Kudo's 1963 period drama of the same name. Koji Yakusho leads the cast as the veteran samurai Shimada Shinzaemon, with Takayuki Yamada, Yusuke Iseya, Hiroki Matsukata, Mikijirō Hira and Gorō Inagaki as the depraved Lord Naritsugu.

In 1844, late in the Edo period, the Tokugawa shogunate is weakening. Lord Matsudaira Naritsugu of Akashi rapes, tortures and kills nobles and commoners at will, shielded by his half-brother, the Shōgun. When Naritsugu is slated for a seat on the shogunate council, the justice minister Sir Doi Toshitsura fears his elevation will plunge the country into civil war, and after a lord whose family Naritsugu murdered commits seppuku in protest, Doi secretly engages Shinzaemon to kill him. Shinzaemon assembles a band of samurai, including his wayward nephew Shinrokurō and a rōnin, while Naritsugu's loyal retainer Hanbei, an old acquaintance of Shinzaemon, discovers the plot.

The conspirators plan an ambush at the town of Ochiai on Naritsugu's journey home from Edo. Attacked by hired rōnin along the way, they take to the mountains, get lost and free a hunter, Kiga Koyata, who leads them to Ochiai and becomes the thirteenth assassin. Lord Makino, whose son Naritsugu killed, blocks the highway to force a detour, then takes his own life to hide his role. With Doi's money, the assassins buy the town and turn it into a maze of traps and fortifications. Naritsugu arrives with some 200 men, far more than expected, and a long, savage battle ensues as the assassins fight with arrows, explosives and swords while Naritsugu revels in the slaughter. Most of the thirteen die. Shinzaemon kills Hanbei in a duel, and he and Naritsugu mortally wound each other; the terrified lord thanks him for the most exciting day of his life before Shinzaemon beheads him and dies. Shinrokurō and the seemingly indestructible Koyata survive and go their separate ways. An epilogue records that the death was blamed on illness and that the shogunate fell 23 years later.

The film competed for the Golden Lion at the 67th Venice International Film Festival in September 2010. Made for about $6 million, it grossed $17.6 million worldwide. Critics praised its 45-minute final battle, giving it 95% on Rotten Tomatoes and 84 on Metacritic; Roger Ebert called it terrifically entertaining. It won four Japan Academy Prizes.

overview: Join Barbie in a colourful, modern-day fairytale filled with fashion, friends and fun! Barbie and her dog Sequin jet off to visit her Aunt's amazing fashion house in Paris, and much to her surprise it's about to be shut down forever. After she discovers three enchanting Flairies with sparkle-magic powers, Barbie comes up with a brilliant idea to save the business. She even inspires Alice, a shy fashion designer, and together they create a dazzling runway fashion show. Barbie shows that magic happens when you believe in yourself.
tagline: Discover your inner sparkle!
title: Barbie: A Fashion Fairytale
plot:
Barbie: A Fashion Fairytale is a 2010 computer-animated fantasy adventure film directed by William Lau and produced by Mattel through Barbie Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment. The eighteenth film in the Barbie series, it marked the first time Diana Kaarina voiced Barbie, replacing Kelly Sheridan. Adrian Petriw voices Ken, with Tabitha St. Germain, Patricia Drake and Alexa Devine. The film was released on DVD on 14 September 2010 and premiered on Nickelodeon that November.

While filming an adaptation of The Princess and the Pea, Barbie questions the director's strange creative choices and is fired. She is immediately mocked online and then receives a phone call from her boyfriend, Ken, who appears to break up with her. Heartbroken, she flies to Paris to visit her aunt Millicent, a celebrated fashion designer. Meanwhile, Barbie's friends Teresa and Grace confront Ken and discover that the breakup message was a recording made by Barbie's rival, Raquelle, while Ken was reading a script. Ken rushes to Paris to make things right, facing a series of comic mishaps along the way.

In Paris, Barbie learns from a rival designer, Jacqueline, that Millicent's fashion house is going out of business. Millicent has lost customers after bad reviews and has sold the building to a hot-dog restaurant chain. Her shy assistant, Alice, shows Barbie the attic and tells her about the magical creatures said to have lived in the fashion house. Placing one of Alice's dress designs in a magic wardrobe and reciting a chant, the two summon the Flairies, Glimmer, Shimmer and Shyne, tiny fairies whose sparkling magic can transform clothes. With their help and Alice's designs, Barbie persuades her aunt to stage one last fashion show to save the business. But Jacqueline, who wants to steal the Flairies' powers for herself, schemes to sabotage the event, and Barbie, Alice and Millicent must rally together, regain their confidence and put on a dazzling show in time to save the fashion house.

As with other entries in the series, the film was accompanied by a line of tie-in dolls and toys, including figures of the Flairies. Its themes of confidence, creativity and believing in oneself were consistent with Mattel's other Barbie films of the period.

overview: A man against capital punishment is accused of murdering a fellow activist and is sent to death row.
tagline: The crime is clear. The truth is not.
title: The Life of David Gale
plot:
The Life of David Gale is a 2003 American drama film directed by Alan Parker, produced by Mikona Productions GmbH & Co. KG, and released by Columbia Pictures.

The movie revolves around the life of David Gale, a death row inmate who becomes an advocate for capital punishment reform after his own execution. The main themes of the film include:

1. **Capital Punishment**: The film explores the complexities and moral dilemmas surrounding the death penalty, raising questions about justice, morality, and the value of human life.
2. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Through David Gale's character, the movie highlights the possibility of redemption and personal growth, even in the face of adversity and tragedy.
3. **Love and Sacrifice**: The relationship between David Gale and his wife, Celeste, serves as a catalyst for his transformation, demonstrating the power of love and sacrifice to inspire change.
4. **Social Justice and Activism**: The film showcases David Gale's advocacy work, highlighting the importance of standing up for what one believes in, even if it means challenging the status quo.

The movie features a strong performance by Kevin Spacey as David Gale, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of a complex character. The supporting cast, including Kate Beckinsale, Edgar Ramírez, and Peter Friedman, adds to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, The Life of David Gale is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of justice, redemption, love, and social activism, leaving audiences with much to consider long after the credits roll.

overview: Husband and wife Gabe and Adelaide Wilson take their kids to their beach house expecting to unplug and unwind with friends. But as night descends, their serenity turns to tension and chaos when some shocking visitors arrive uninvited.
tagline: Watch yourself
title: Us
plot:
Us is a 2019 American horror film written, produced, and directed by Jordan Peele. The movie follows the story of the Wilson family, who are forced to confront their doppelgangers, known as "the Tethered."

The film begins with Adelaide Wilson (Lupita Nyong'o), a young girl who, as a child, escapes from a haunted house at a carnival in Santa Cruz, California. The experience leaves her with a traumatic memory that she tries to suppress.

Years later, Adelaide is now an adult and living in the suburbs with her husband Gabe (Winston Duke) and their son Jason (Evan Alex). They are preparing for a family vacation to the same Santa Cruz beach where Adelaide had her terrifying childhood experience. Unbeknownst to them, this trip will bring about a series of events that will change their lives forever.

Upon arrival at the beach, Adelaide begins to feel an inexplicable sense of unease and disconnection from her surroundings. She starts to notice strange occurrences around her, which she initially dismisses as mere coincidence. However, it soon becomes clear that something is amiss.

As the night falls, a group of masked figures emerges from the shadows, revealing themselves to be Adelaide's doppelgangers, known as "the Tethered." The Tethered are identical in appearance to their human counterparts but have been living underground for years, feeding on the fear and suffering of those above ground.

The Tethered, led by Red (Lupita Nyong'o), begin to terrorize Adelaide's family, using their knowledge of the Wilsons' deepest fears against them. As the night wears on, it becomes clear that the Tethered are not just mindless monsters but rather a manifestation of the darker aspects of human nature.

As the situation spirals out of control, Adelaide is forced to confront her own dark past and the trauma she has been trying to suppress. She also begins to realize that the Tethered are not just random duplicates but rather a product of a sinister experiment designed by the government to create an army of mindless drones.

In the end, Adelaide must make a choice between saving herself or saving her family. In a shocking twist, she decides to sacrifice herself to save her loved ones, using her knowledge of the Tethered's weaknesses to defeat them.

The film ends with Adelaide and her family escaping from the beach, but not before Red reveals that there are more Tethered out there, waiting to be unleashed. The final shot is of a group of children playing in the park, unaware of the horrors that lie beneath their feet.

Throughout the movie, Peele explores themes of identity, class, and the duality of human nature. The film's use of horror elements serves as a metaphor for the darker aspects of society, highlighting the ways in which we often turn on each other when faced with fear and uncertainty.

Overall, Us is a thought-provoking and terrifying film that challenges audiences to confront their own fears and insecurities. With its clever plot twists and outstanding performances, it has become a modern horror classic.

overview: As the Japanese surrender at the end of WWII, Gen. Fellers is tasked with deciding if Emperor Hirohito will be hanged as a war criminal. Influencing his ruling is his quest to find Aya, an exchange student he met years earlier in the U.S.
tagline: After the war was won, the battle for peace began.
title: Emperor
plot:
Emperor is a 2012 American war drama film directed by Francis Lawrence, not Krasnoff / Foster Entertainment.

The movie tells the story of General Tom Hagen, played by Jeremy Irons, who serves as an advisor to Emperor Hirohito of Japan during World War II. The main themes of the film include:

1. **Diplomacy and Politics**: The film explores the complex web of diplomacy and politics that led to Japan's surrender in 1945. It highlights the efforts of General Hagen, who played a crucial role in convincing Emperor Hirohito to accept the Allied terms of surrender.
2. **Personal Sacrifice**: The movie showcases the personal sacrifices made by General Hagen, who had to navigate the complexities of Japanese politics and culture while also dealing with his own demons. His character's struggles serve as a metaphor for the human cost of war and the weight of responsibility that comes with leadership.
3. **Cultural Exchange and Understanding**: Through the story of General Hagen's interactions with Emperor Hirohito, the film promotes cultural exchange and understanding between Japan and the United States. It highlights the importance of empathy and cooperation in resolving conflicts and building bridges between nations.
4. **The Weight of History**: The movie grapples with the weight of history, particularly for those who lived through World War II. It explores the emotional toll of war on individuals and communities, as well as the long-term consequences of historical events.

Overall, Emperor is a thought-provoking film that offers a nuanced portrayal of a pivotal moment in world history.

overview: Journalist Michael Ausiello embarks on a rollercoaster ride of emotions when Kit Cowan, his partner of 14 years, is diagnosed with terminal cancer.
tagline: Love never stops surprising you. Even when you know how it ends.
title: Spoiler Alert
plot:
Spoiler Alert is a 2022 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Michael Showalter and written by David Marshall Grant and Dan Savage, based on the 2017 memoir Spoiler Alert: The Hero Dies by entertainment journalist Michael Ausiello. It stars Jim Parsons as Ausiello and Ben Aldridge as his partner Kit Cowan, with Sally Field as Kit's mother, Marilyn, and Bill Irwin in a supporting role.

In 2001, Michael, a writer for TV Guide, meets photographer Kit at a gay nightclub in Manhattan, and they begin dating. Michael, once overweight, worries that he is not attractive enough for Kit, and Kit admits to a past affair; neither has had a long-term relationship before, but they persist. At their first Christmas, Kit gives Michael closet space at his apartment. A year later, when Kit has an appendectomy, his parents visit, and his mother, Marilyn, grows suspicious of Michael, prompting Kit, who has never come out to them, to reveal that Michael is his boyfriend. Marilyn is hurt that he hid it but welcomes Michael. The couple move into a townhouse, and Kit joins Michael in his childhood fantasy of lying under the Christmas tree with a partner.

By 2013, their relationship has deteriorated: Michael is consumed by his company TVLine and drinking heavily, and suspects Kit of an affair with a colleague, Sebastian. Their therapist suggests a separation, and Kit moves out, though they stay together. In 2014, Kit is diagnosed with a rare stage-4 neuroendocrine cancer. Michael, still haunted by his mother's death from cancer, moves him back in and cares for him through treatment. With Kit given six weeks to live, the two apologize to each other, Kit admitting the affair with Sebastian, and they marry the day after he proposes. In 2015, as Kit lies dying in hospital, Michael lets Sebastian say goodbye and imagines interviewing Kit as an actor whose character is being written out of a television show. After Kit's death, Michael remains close to his parents and prepares to move to Los Angeles.

Focus Features gave the film a limited release on December 2, 2022, expanding nationwide a week later; it opened to just $679,690 from 789 theaters. Critics responded favorably, singling out the strong performances despite its uneven tone; Rotten Tomatoes reported 87% approval and Metacritic a score of 61.

overview: The story of journalist Edward R. Murrow's stand against Senator Joseph McCarthy's anti-communist witch-hunts in the early 1950s.
tagline: They took on the Government with nothing but the truth.
title: Good Night, and Good Luck.
plot:
Good Night, and Good Luck. is a 2005 American historical drama film directed by George Clooney, who co-wrote it with producer Grant Heslov. It stars David Strathairn as the veteran CBS broadcaster Edward R. Murrow, alongside Patricia Clarkson, Clooney, Jeff Daniels, Robert Downey Jr. and Frank Langella, and dramatizes Murrow's conflict with Senator Joseph McCarthy of Wisconsin. Shot on color stock on a grayscale set and converted to black and white, it explores media responsibility and journalism's role in voicing dissent.

The film opens in 1958 at a tribute dinner where Murrow begins a speech, then flashes back to October 1953 at CBS, as McCarthy claims that over 200 communists work in the government. Murrow and his producer, Fred Friendly, decide to cover the case of Milo Radulovich, an Air Force officer discharged because his father and sister were accused of communist sympathies, on evidence kept in a sealed envelope. Despite objections from CBS executive Sig Mickelson and pressure from military officers, the segment airs on See It Now, and the team turns its attention to McCarthy himself, exposing his questioning methods and falsehoods and inviting him onto the program to respond. The Air Force reinstates Radulovich.

On April 6, 1954, McCarthy appears on the show and accuses Murrow of being a communist, as Murrow expected. In his reply, Murrow flatly denies the charge and points out that anyone who opposes the senator's methods is branded a communist. The tide then turns against McCarthy, who faces investigation over charges brought by the Army, but the newsroom's celebration is cut short by the suicide of colleague Don Hollenbeck, who had been smeared as a "pinko" by a columnist. After the Army-McCarthy hearings, CBS chief Paley, having lost a major sponsor, cuts See It Now to five more episodes in a Sunday afternoon slot and orders layoffs; Joe Wershba, secretly married to colleague Shirley in breach of company policy, volunteers to leave. Returning to 1958, Murrow warns that television can inform and enlighten only if used for that purpose, or it is "merely wires and lights in a box."

The film was a box office success and was widely acclaimed for Clooney's direction, the writing, cinematography, production design and performances, especially Strathairn's. Rotten Tomatoes reported 93% approval and Metacritic a score of 80. It received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor.

overview: In the puppet state of Manchukuo in the 1930s, four Communist party special agents, after returning to China, embark on a secret mission. Sold out by a traitor, the team find themselves surrounded by threats on all sides.
title: Cliff Walkers
plot:
Cliff Walkers (Chinese: 悬崖之上), released earlier in English as Impasse, is a 2021 Chinese spy thriller directed by Zhang Yimou from a screenplay by Quan Yongxian. Set in the early 1930s in Manchukuo, the puppet state Imperial Japan established in northeastern China, it stars Zhang Yi as Zhang Xianchen, a former journalist turned Communist agent, Qin Hailu as his wife and comrade Wang Yu, Zhu Yawen and Liu Haocun as the young lovers Chu Liang and Xiao Lan, Yu Hewei as Zhou Yi, an agent embedded among the enemy, Ni Dahong as the security chief Gao Bin and Lei Jiayin as a Communist agent turned traitor.

Four agents returning to China from abroad parachute into a snowbound forest outside Harbin on a covert mission code-named Utrennya, Russian for "dawn." Their aim is to extract a former prisoner who can reveal to the world the atrocities committed by the Japanese army, including the human experiments of Unit 731. Prepared to die rather than betray their cause, each carries a suicide pill in a matchbox marked in Russian. On landing they split into two pairs, separating the married couple and the young lovers so that no one is distracted by personal attachment; Xianchen and Yu promise that whichever of them survives will send for their children.

Their mission is compromised from the start. A local contact, broken by electric-shock torture and drugs after witnessing the execution of his comrades, has betrayed the operation, and the people waiting to meet one pair are enemy agents posing as allies. The pair recognize the trap and escape, and the Japanese try to use one team to draw out the other. As the agents make their way through the snowy streets of Harbin, they can never be sure who is working for the enemy, while Zhou Yi works covertly on their behalf from inside the enemy's security apparatus.

Filmed between December 2019 and May 2020 in Xuexiang National Forest Park, with a score by Jo Yeong-wook, the film was released in China and the United States on 30 April 2021 and was selected as China's submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film. Critics were generally favorable, with an 80% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, which called it stylish and exciting, and a Metacritic score of 64; RogerEbert.com called it one of Zhang's coldest but most alluring films.

overview: The true story of a brilliant but politically radical debate team coach who uses the power of words to transform a group of underdog African-American college students into a historical powerhouse that took on the Harvard elite.
tagline: When the nation was in need, he inspired them to give us hope.
title: The Great Debaters
plot:
The Great Debaters is a powerful and inspiring film that explores several profound themes. At its core, the movie delves into the transformative power of education and the impact it can have on individuals and communities.

The film tells the story of Melvin B. Tolson, a high school debate team coach who uses debate as a means to empower his students from an impoverished background. Through Tolson's guidance, the team discovers their voices, builds confidence, and develops critical thinking skills that go beyond the confines of the classroom.

One of the primary themes of The Great Debaters is the struggle for social mobility and the quest for equality. The film highlights the systemic barriers that prevent marginalized communities from accessing quality education and opportunities, leaving them with limited prospects for a better life. Tolson's team faces these challenges head-on, using debate as a tool to challenge stereotypes, break down barriers, and assert their rights.

The movie also explores the theme of self-discovery and personal growth. As the students navigate the world of debate, they learn to articulate their thoughts, express themselves with confidence, and develop a sense of purpose. Through this process, they discover their strengths, weaknesses, and passions, ultimately transforming into confident individuals who are equipped to make a positive impact in their communities.

Furthermore, The Great Debaters touches on the theme of mentorship and the importance of role models in shaping young minds. Tolson's leadership and guidance serve as a catalyst for his students' growth, providing them with a supportive environment where they can explore their potential and develop into capable leaders.

The film's portrayal of the debate team's journey is also infused with a sense of hope and resilience. Despite facing numerous obstacles and setbacks, the team perseveres, driven by their determination to succeed and make a difference in the world. This narrative thread serves as a powerful reminder that even in the face of adversity, individuals can come together to achieve great things.

Overall, The Great Debaters is a movie that celebrates the transformative power of education, debate, and community. Through its compelling story and memorable characters, the film inspires audiences to reflect on their own values, aspirations, and potential for growth.

overview: Two female scam artists, one low rent and the other high class, compete to swindle a naïve tech prodigy out of his fortune. A remake of the 1988 comedy "Dirty Rotten Scoundrels."
tagline: They're giving dirty rotten men a run for their money
title: The Hustle
plot:
The Hustle is a 2019 American comedy film directed by Chris Addison and written by Kay Cannon. The movie stars Anne Hathaway, Rebel Wilson, Alex Sharp, and Justin Theroux.

The story follows Josephine Chesterfield (Anne Hathaway), a high-class escort who has been in the business for over 20 years. She is known for her exceptional skills and ability to seduce wealthy clients. On the other hand, Penny Rust (Rebel Wilson) is a young and ambitious con artist who wants to make it big by scamming men.

The two women meet at a high-end nightclub where Josephine is working. Initially, they are rivals, but after a series of events, they decide to team up and take down their common target: a wealthy businessman named Dabney (Alex Sharp). The plan involves Josephine using her charm to seduce Dabney's business partner, while Penny poses as his assistant.

As the story unfolds, we see the two women navigating their complicated pasts and learning to trust each other. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including a rival con artist (Justin Theroux) who is also after Dabney's money.

Throughout the film, Josephine and Penny develop an unlikely friendship, with Josephine becoming a mentor to Penny. The movie explores themes of female empowerment, friendship, and self-discovery as the two women learn to rely on each other and find their own identities outside of their respective professions.

The Hustle received mixed reviews from critics but was praised for its chemistry between Hathaway and Wilson. The film's tone is lighthearted and comedic, with plenty of witty banter and humorous moments. While it may not be a groundbreaking film, The Hustle provides an entertaining and fun ride, thanks to the talents of its lead actresses.

Overall, The Hustle is a charming comedy that explores themes of female friendship and empowerment. With strong performances from Anne Hathaway and Rebel Wilson, the movie delivers on its promise of laughter and entertainment.

overview: Everybody has one—the sibling who is always just a little bit behind the curve when it comes to getting his life together. For sisters Liz, Miranda and Natalie, that person is their perennially upbeat brother, Ned. But as each of their lives begins to unravel, Ned's family comes to realise that Ned isn't such an idiot after all.
tagline: Everybody has one
title: Our Idiot Brother
plot:
Our Idiot Brother is a 2011 American comedy-drama film directed by Jesse Peretz and written by David Gordon Green. The movie follows the story of Ned (played by Paul Rudd), a free-spirited and eccentric man who moves from New York to Oregon, where he becomes entangled in the lives of his three sisters.

The main theme of Our Idiot Brother revolves around the complexities of family relationships and the struggles of finding one's place within them. The film explores how Ned's carefree nature often clashes with the more structured and conventional lifestyles of his sisters, leading to comedic misunderstandings and heartwarming moments of connection.

At its core, the movie is a poignant exploration of the human need for belonging and acceptance. As Ned navigates his relationships with his sisters, he forces them to confront their own insecurities and flaws, ultimately leading to a deeper understanding and appreciation of each other's quirks.

The film also touches on themes of identity, community, and the search for meaning in life. Through Ned's character, the movie highlights the importance of embracing one's individuality and finding a sense of purpose that aligns with one's values and passions.

Overall, Our Idiot Brother is a charming and humorous exploration of the human experience, tackling complex themes with wit and sensitivity.

overview: The film tells a story of a divorced couple trying to raise their young son. The story follows the boy for twelve years, from first grade at age 6 through 12th grade at age 17-18, and examines his relationship with his parents as he grows.
tagline: 12 years in the making.
title: Boyhood
plot:
Boyhood is a coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Richard Linklater, released in 2014. The film follows the life of Mason Jr., played by Ellar Coltrane, from age 6 to 18 over the course of 12 years.

The film begins with Mason Jr. (played as a child) living with his parents, Mason Sr. (played by Ethan Hawke) and Olivia (played by Patricia Arquette), in Austin, Texas. The family is shown to be struggling financially, but they are loving and supportive. As the story progresses, we see Mason Jr. grow up alongside his siblings, including his older sister Samantha (played by Lorelei Linklater).

The early years of Mason Jr.'s life are marked by a sense of stability and normalcy, with his parents trying to provide for him and his siblings despite their financial struggles. However, as the years pass, we see Mason Jr. face various challenges, including bullying at school, romantic relationships, and family conflicts.

One of the most significant plot points in the film is the divorce of Mason Sr. and Olivia, which occurs when Mason Jr. is 14. This event has a profound impact on Mason Jr., who struggles to come to terms with his parents' separation. The film also explores Mason Jr.'s relationships with his friends, including his best friend, Joe (played by Kyle Chandler), and his romantic interests, including his first love, Jessica (played by Emma Wright).

Throughout the film, Linklater uses a unique narrative structure, where each year of Mason Jr.'s life is represented by a different actor playing him. This allows for a sense of continuity and growth, as we see Mason Jr. evolve from a young boy to a teenager and eventually an adult.

The film's climax occurs when Mason Jr. graduates from high school and sets off on his own path in life. The final scenes show Mason Jr. as a young man, struggling to find his place in the world and navigate the challenges of adulthood.

Overall, Boyhood is a powerful and poignant coming-of-age story that explores themes of family, love, and identity. Through its unique narrative structure and strong performances, the film provides a nuanced and realistic portrayal of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

overview: In the near future, Major is the first of her kind: a human saved from a terrible crash, then cyber-enhanced to be a perfect soldier devoted to stopping the world's most dangerous criminals.
tagline: There's nothing sadder than a puppet without a ghost.
title: Ghost in the Shell
plot:
Ghost in the Shell is a 2017 cyberpunk action thriller directed by Rupert Sanders and written by Jamie Moss, William Wheeler and Ehren Kruger, the first live-action adaptation of Masamune Shirow's Japanese manga franchise. Scarlett Johansson stars as Major Mira Killian, with Takeshi Kitano, Michael Pitt, Pilou Asbæk, Chin Han and Juliette Binoche in supporting roles.

In a near future where people routinely enhance their bodies with cybernetics, the corporation Hanka Robotics secretly develops a synthetic body, or shell, that can house a human brain instead of an artificial intelligence. Killian, told she is the lone survivor of a cyberterrorist attack that killed her parents, becomes its first successful subject, and Hanka's chief executive, Cutter, overrides her designer Dr. Ouelet to turn her into a weapon. A year later she is a Major in the anti-terrorism unit Section 9, serving with Batou and Togusa under Chief Daisuke Aramaki, though she is troubled by hallucinations and a past she cannot recall.

After the team foils an attack on a Hanka conference, Killian learns that a hacker called Kuze is murdering the company's senior scientists. Tracking him, the team is lured into a trap at a yakuza nightclub, and an explosion destroys Batou's eyes. When Killian is captured, Kuze reveals that he is an earlier, failed subject of the same programme and tells her that her medication suppresses her real memories. Ouelet admits that 98 subjects died before Killian and that her past was fabricated; ordered by Cutter to kill her, she instead helps her escape, and Cutter murders Ouelet and brands Killian a rogue. An address leads Killian to a widowed woman whose daughter, Motoko Kusanagi, ran away and supposedly took her own life in custody. Killian finds Kuze at their old hideout, where they recall being anti-augmentation radicals abducted by Hanka. Killian destroys a spider-tank Cutter sends after them, losing an arm, but a sniper kills Kuze. Aramaki executes Cutter, and Killian, embracing her identity as Motoko, reconnects with her mother and returns to Section 9.

Shot mainly in New Zealand in 2016, the film grossed $169.8 million worldwide against a $110 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 43% on Rotten Tomatoes, praising the visuals and Johansson's performance but faulting the story, and her casting drew accusations of whitewashing.

keywords.name: based on magazine, newspaper or article

overview: A superintendent of a school district works for the betterment of the student’s education when an embezzlement scheme is discovered, threatening to destroy everything.
tagline: Some people learn the hard way.
title: Bad Education
plot:
Bad Education is a 2019 American biographical crime drama film directed by Cory Finley. The movie is based on the true story of Vito LoGrasso, a high school teacher who was convicted of embezzling over $500,000 from his school.

The main theme of Bad Education revolves around the corrupting influence of power and greed. The protagonist, Frank Tassone, played by Hugh Jackman, is a charismatic and well-respected school administrator who becomes embroiled in a web of deceit and embezzlement. As he rises through the ranks, his obsession with wealth and status consumes him, leading him to compromise his values and relationships.

The film also explores the theme of toxic masculinity, as Frank's behavior is driven by a desire to prove himself as a man and maintain control over those around him. His actions are motivated by a need for validation and respect, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

Furthermore, Bad Education touches on the theme of class struggle and economic inequality. The film highlights the stark contrast between the wealthy and privileged lives of those in power and the struggles faced by the working-class individuals who are often left behind.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and performance, as Frank's character is revealed to be a masterful manipulator who uses his charm and charisma to hide his true nature. This theme is particularly evident in the film's portrayal of Frank's relationships with those around him, including his wife and colleagues, whom he expertly deceives.

Overall, Bad Education is a thought-provoking drama that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of unchecked ambition and greed.

overview: Brad and Kate have made something of an art form out of avoiding their families during the holidays, but this year their foolproof plan is about go bust -- big time. Stuck at the city airport after all departing flights are canceled, the couple is embarrassed to see their ruse exposed to the world by an overzealous television reporter. Now, Brad and Kate are left with precious little choice other than to swallow their pride and suffer the rounds.
tagline: His father, her mother, his mother and her father all in one day.
title: Four Christmases
plot:
Four Christmases is a 2008 American Christmas romantic comedy film directed by Seth Gordon and written by Caleb Wilson. The movie stars Vince Vaughn, Reese Witherspoon, Robert Duvall, Mary Steenburgen, and Kristin Chenoweth.

The story begins with Brad (Vince Vaughn) and Kate (Reese Witherspoon), a couple who have been together for five years but are feeling unfulfilled in their relationship. They decide to take a break from each other and go on separate holidays with their respective families, hoping that the experience will help them re-evaluate their feelings.

Brad's family is eccentric and overbearing, consisting of his parents, Howard (Robert Duvall) and Marilyn (Mary Steenburgen), as well as his three siblings. His father is a bit of a control freak who wants Brad to settle down with someone like his wife, while his mother is a free spirit who encourages Brad's independence.

Kate's family, on the other hand, is equally dysfunctional. Her parents, Jimmy (Jon Voight) and Sandy (Sissy Spacek), are divorced and have a strained relationship. Kate's siblings are also a handful, with her brother being a bit of a ladies' man and her sister being a drama queen.

As Brad and Kate navigate their respective family holidays, they begin to realize that they may be better off together than apart. They start to reconnect and rekindle their romance, but their feelings for each other are complicated by the fact that they both have unresolved issues with their families.

Throughout the movie, Brad and Kate face various challenges as they try to reconcile their differences and find a way to make their relationship work. Along the way, they also learn valuable lessons about family, love, and acceptance.

In the end, Brad and Kate come to a realization that they need each other and are willing to work through their issues with their families in order to build a stronger relationship. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Brad and Kate embracing each other and looking forward to a brighter future together.

Overall, Four Christmases is a heartwarming holiday romance that explores the complexities of family relationships and the power of love to overcome even the most difficult challenges.

overview: A light hearted comedy about the beginnings of Professional American Football. When a decorated war hero and college all star is tempted into playing professional football. Everyone see the chance to make some big money, but when a reporter digs up some dirt on the war hero... everyone could lose out.
tagline: If Love Is a Game, Who'll Make the First Pass?
title: Leatherheads
plot:
Leatherheads is a 2008 American sports comedy directed by George Clooney, who also stars, written by Duncan Brantley and Rick Reilly. Set in the early years of professional American football, it co-stars Renée Zellweger, John Krasinski, Jonathan Pryce, Stephen Root and Wayne Duvall. Universal Pictures released it on 4 April 2008.

In 1925, Jimmy "Dodge" Connelly, an aging player, captains the Duluth Bulldogs, a struggling professional football team. With the professional game on the verge of collapse and players unpaid, Dodge persuades Carter "the Bullet" Rutherford, a star player at Princeton and a celebrated First World War hero, to join the Bulldogs, hoping that his fame will draw crowds. Carter's arrival transforms the team's fortunes, and the games attract huge audiences.

Lexie Littleton, a fast-talking reporter for the Chicago Tribune, is assigned to prove that Carter's wartime heroics, which supposedly involved capturing a group of German soldiers single-handedly, are a fabrication. As she travels with the team, she finds herself caught in a love triangle with Dodge and Carter. Carter eventually confesses to her that the German platoon surrendered to him by mistake, but he also discovers her assignment and learns that she has shared a kiss with Dodge. Pressured by threats from Carter's slick manager, Lexie publishes the story, while the manager uses underhanded tactics, including bribing a key witness, to discredit her. Meanwhile, a commissioner appointed to clean up the sport introduces formal rules that threaten the improvised tricks on which Dodge relies. When public opinion turns against Lexie, Dodge intervenes at a hearing, forcing the truth into the open, and the story builds toward a muddy, decisive game between the Bulldogs and Carter's new team in Chicago, in which Dodge must use all his cunning to win.

Leatherheads received mixed reviews; critics appreciated its affectionate homage to the screwball comedies of the 1930s and its period atmosphere but found it uneven and slow. It grossed about $41 million worldwide against a budget of $58 million.

overview: A married couple are faced with a difficult decision - to improve the life of their child by moving to another country or to stay in Iran and look after a deteriorating parent who has Alzheimer's disease.
tagline: Ugly truth, sweet lies.
title: A Separation
plot:
A Separation is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of human relationships, societal expectations, and the moral dilemmas that arise when individuals are forced to confront their own flaws. The film masterfully weaves together themes of marital infidelity, divorce, and custody battles, all set against the backdrop of Iranian society.

At its core, A Separation is a nuanced exploration of the tensions between traditional values and modernity. The protagonist, Nader, is a man struggling to come to terms with his own identity and sense of purpose, while his wife Simin is grappling with her own desires for independence and autonomy. As their relationship deteriorates, they are forced to navigate the complexities of Iranian law and societal norms, which often prioritize family honor over individual happiness.

One of the film's most striking aspects is its portrayal of the inner lives of its characters, particularly Nader and Simin. Through their conversations and interactions, we gain insight into their thoughts, feelings, and motivations, revealing a deep-seated desire for connection and understanding that is ultimately thwarted by societal expectations.

The film also raises important questions about the nature of truth and deception. As Nader's infidelity is revealed, he becomes embroiled in a custody battle with his ex-wife, forcing him to confront the consequences of his actions. Meanwhile, Simin must navigate her own feelings of guilt and responsibility, all while trying to maintain a sense of dignity and self-respect.

Ultimately, A Separation is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges us to consider our own values and priorities in the face of adversity. Through its thought-provoking themes and nuanced characterizations, the film offers a searing critique of societal norms and expectations, inviting us to reflect on what it means to be a good person in a complex and often unforgiving world.

overview: Publicist Alyssa Banks thinks she’s woken up in a fairy tale when she meets Jack, a British Prince. At first, everything seems to be going great–Jack wines and dines Alyssa, taking her to extravagant meals, on romantic helicopter rides over Los Angeles, and whisking her away to Europe on a private jet. But Alyssa’s dream quickly turns into a nightmare when the volatile Prince refuses to let Alyssa leave his family’s luxurious estate in the English countryside. As Alyssa desperately tries to escape, she soon finds a way to turn the tables on her not-so-perfect Prince.
title: Stalked by a Prince
plot:
Stalked by a Prince is a 2022 American-Canadian psychological thriller made for television, directed by Max McGuire from a script by John F. Hayes and Shawn Riopelle and produced by Johnson Production Group and Fireside Pictures, with Timothy O. Johnson and Andrew C. Erin among the executive producers. It premiered on Lifetime on 27 February 2022. Natalie Hall stars as Alyssa Banks, with Jonathan Keltz as Prince Jack, Michael Swatton as his bodyguard Taffer, Konstantina Mantelos as Alyssa's colleague Rachel, Alexander Crowther as Jack's brother Timothy, Mélanie St-Pierre as Timothy's wife Susan and Roderick McNeil as Chuck.

Alyssa, a publicist still recovering from a painful breakup, is sent with Rachel to a promotional event for a vodka brand, where she meets Jack, a British prince sixth in line to the throne, who quickly falls for her. He sweeps her off her feet with lavish dinners and romantic helicopter rides over Los Angeles, and despite some doubts she agrees to fly with him on his private jet to his family's country estate in England, accompanied by his bodyguard Taffer, who tries to subtly warn her. What Alyssa does not know is that Jack is a dangerous psychopath who refuses to take the medication that keeps his violent urges in check; he has already killed other young women lured to the estate, and murdered Chuck, a lawyer who was courting Alyssa, staging it as an accident. He monitors her every move with cameras and listening devices. When Alyssa reads of Chuck's death and discovers a woman's body hidden in an abandoned stable, she realizes she is trapped. Jack's older brother Timothy, believing Jack has reformed, arrives with Susan and their young children. Alyssa's secret plea for help is intercepted, but she manages to broadcast a livestream on Susan's social media account in which Jack confesses to brutal crimes. Jack stabs Taffer, who urged him to surrender, kills his brother and pursues Alyssa into the woods, but he is shot dead by the wounded Taffer, who dies soon after. Back home, Rachel suggests that Alyssa turn her unwanted fame to their company's advantage.

The film is one of Lifetime's thrillers built around a fairy-tale romance that turns into a nightmare. Reviews were unfavorable: the Italian site Movieplayer.it gave it one and a half stars out of five, criticizing a predictable, contrived screenplay and a lack of tension or surprises.

overview: On the brink of a midlife crisis, 30-something Mike O'Donnell wishes he could have a "do-over." And that's exactly what he gets when he wakes up one morning to find he's 17 years old again. With his adult mind stuck inside the body of a teenager, Mike actually has the chance to reverse some decisions he wishes he'd never made. But maybe they weren't so bad after all.
tagline: Who says you're only young once?
title: 17 Again
plot:
"17 Again" is a 2009 American fantasy comedy film directed by Burr Steers and written by Jason Smathius and Thomas Lennon. The movie stars Zac Efron, Matthew Perry, and Leslie Mann.

The story begins with Mike O'Donnell (Matthew Perry), a successful high school basketball coach who has it all - a loving wife, Maggie (Leslie Mann), two beautiful children, and a thriving coaching career. However, Mike's life takes an unexpected turn when he is involved in a car accident on his way to a game.

As a result of the accident, Mike finds himself transported back in time to his 17-year-old self (Zac Efron). Initially confused and disoriented, Mike soon realizes that he has been given a second chance at high school. He decides to take advantage of this opportunity to relive his teenage years and make amends for past mistakes.

Mike's new life as a 17-year-old is filled with excitement and nostalgia. He rekindles an old friendship with his former best friend, Ned Gold (Thomas Lennon), and catches the eye of his high school crush, Scarlett (Amy Poehler). However, Mike soon realizes that being 17 again comes with its own set of challenges.

As Mike navigates his new life, he must confront the consequences of his past actions. He learns to appreciate the present moment and to make better choices. Meanwhile, Maggie is struggling to cope with her husband's absence from their family, and their relationship begins to fray.

Throughout the movie, Mike's dual identity creates comedic situations as he tries to balance his life as a 17-year-old with his responsibilities as a coach and a husband. The film also explores themes of friendship, love, and redemption.

As the story unfolds, Mike must make a choice between staying in the past or returning to his present self. In the end, Mike decides to return to his own time, but not before he has learned valuable lessons about life, love, and the importance of appreciating the present moment.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note as Mike returns to his family, and they are reunited. Mike's experience as a 17-year-old has changed him, and he is now more grateful for the time he has with his loved ones. The film concludes with a sense of closure and new beginnings for Mike and his family.

Overall, "17 Again" is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. With its talented cast and witty script, the film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: As a grisly virus rampages a city, a lone man stays locked inside his apartment, digitally cut off from seeking help and desperate to find a way out.
tagline: You must survive.
title: #Alive
plot:
#Alive (Korean: #saraitda) is a 2020 South Korean action horror film directed by Cho Il-hyung, starring Yoo Ah-in as Oh Joon-woo and Park Shin-hye as Kim Yoo-bin, with Jeon Bae-soo as a mysterious survivor. It is based on Alone, a 2019 screenplay by American writer Matt Naylor, who adapted it with Cho; Naylor's script also became a separate film. The film follows a young video game streamer trying to stay alive alone in his Seoul apartment as a zombie outbreak engulfs the city.

Joon-woo wakes up alone in his family's apartment as people outside begin attacking and infecting each other. After a neighbor bursts in and turns into a zombie, Joon-woo barricades the door with the refrigerator, posts a call for help online and receives a message from his parents saying they are safe. Using a drone, he discovers that the entire neighborhood is overrun. Gradually he loses phone service, the internet and running water, and his food supplies run out.

Isolated, hungry and tormented by a final voicemail suggesting his family's refuge has fallen, Joon-woo sinks into despair and is on the verge of taking his own life when he notices a laser pointer from the building opposite. It belongs to Kim Yoo-bin, another survivor, who has been defending her apartment with a hand axe and booby traps. Using a rope line and walkie-talkies, the two begin to share supplies and support one another. When the noise attracts the infected, they decide to rappel down from their balconies and fight their way through the complex in search of help. Their hopes are tested when a seemingly kind stranger offers them food and water, and they must keep each other alive long enough to be rescued.

The film reflects the loneliness and isolation of the COVID-19 era, and centers on how technology, social media and human connection become means of survival.

#Alive was released in South Korea on June 24, 2020, achieving the strongest first-day admissions of any film there since the pandemic began, and globally on Netflix on September 8, 2020. It received generally positive reviews, with 88 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it well acted, genuinely unsettling and occasionally even funny.

overview: Orphaned at birth and raised by storks, the teenage sparrow Richard believes he is one of them. But when the time comes to migrate to Africa, his stork family is forced to reveal his true identity and leave him behind in the forest, since he is not a migratory bird and would not survive the journey. Determined to prove he is a stork after all, Richard ventures south on his own. But only with the help of Olga, an eccentric owl with an imaginary friend and Kiki, a narcissistic, disco-singing parakeet, does he stand a chance to reach his goal and learn to accept who he really is.
tagline: Their adventure is the destination.
title: A Stork's Journey
plot:
A Stork's Journey is a heartwarming animated film that tells the story of a young stork named Zuri who embarks on an incredible journey to find her place in the world. At its core, the movie explores themes of identity, belonging, and self-discovery.

As Zuri navigates through unfamiliar lands and meets various creatures along the way, she begins to question her purpose and the expectations placed upon her by others. The film delves into the complexities of growing up and finding one's own path in life, often challenging traditional norms and conventions.

One of the main themes that resonates throughout the movie is the importance of embracing individuality and being true to oneself. Zuri's journey is a metaphor for the struggles many young animals face as they try to find their place in the world and assert their unique identities.

The film also touches on the theme of family and community, highlighting the value of forming connections with others and finding one's tribe. Through her encounters with various creatures, Zuri learns about different cultures and ways of life, broadening her perspective and fostering a sense of empathy and understanding.

Ultimately, A Stork's Journey is a story about resilience, courage, and the power of following one's heart. With its beautiful animation and engaging storyline, the movie offers a timeless and uplifting message that will resonate with audiences of all ages.

overview: A careerist from Warsaw, who does not like dogs, has to go to Kraków for professional reasons, where she meets a charming widower, his son and their four-legged pet.
title: Heart Parade
plot:
Heart Parade (Polish: Parada serc) is a 2022 Polish romantic comedy film directed by Filip Zylber from a screenplay by Wiktor Piątkowski, Natalia Matuszek and Marianna Pochroń, produced by Endemol Polska and released by Netflix. Anna Próchniak stars as Magda Grot, a Warsaw television executive, with Michał Czernecki as the widower Krzysztof and Iwo Rajski as his son Karol. The supporting cast includes Piotr Rogucki as Wiktor, Monika Krzywkowska as Zula, Katarzyna Zielińska as Irenka and Leszek Piskorz as the professor. The cinematography is by Malte Rosenfeld and the music by Paweł Lucewicz.

Magda is a headstrong careerist who has organized her whole life around her job and keeps every aspect of it under control, except for one weakness: a dislike of dachshunds rooted in a childhood trauma. On the very day she is due to be promoted, her boss asks her to look after her dachshund for the afternoon. Magda reluctantly agrees, but the dog falls ill, and her boss, blaming her, cancels the promotion and fires her. Hoping to win back her job by proving that she is in fact a dachshund lover, Magda learns of a dachshund parade held in Kraków and travels there to take part. In the city she rents a room from Krzysztof, a young widower who shares an apartment with his son Karol and their dachshund Trombone, without telling them that she has entered their lives for professional reasons. Despite her reservations, she gradually warms to the family, the dog included, and over the following days a connection grows between her and Krzysztof. As the parade approaches, Magda must choose between the career she has been fighting to restore and the promise of a new life.

Heart Parade was released on Netflix on 15 June 2022. Reviews were mixed to negative. Alex Wiggan of It's a Stampede! called it a bright, breezy and whimsical film with splashes of humor that simply sets out to entertain, praising Próchniak's authority and likeability, Rajski's ease as Karol and the attractive views of Kraków, while acknowledging its well-worn story and obvious outcome. Daniel Hart of Ready Steady Cut found it a meandering romantic comedy with little spark, crediting the lead actress's performance but criticizing the lack of chemistry between Magda and Krzysztof and the boredom of its third act.

overview: To find Ilona and unlock the secrets of her disappearance, Karas must plunge deep into the parallel worlds of corporate espionage, organized crime and genetic research - where the truth imprisons whoever finds it first and miracles can be bought but at a great price.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
tagline: Paris 2054. Live forever or die trying
title: Renaissance
plot:
Renaissance, also released as Paris 2054: Renaissance, is a 2006 animated tech-noir thriller directed by Christian Volckman and co-produced by France, the United Kingdom and Luxembourg. Rendered in stark black and white using motion capture, it was released in France in March 2006, in Britain in July and in the United States in September by Miramax. The English-language version features the voices of Daniel Craig as Barthélémy Karas, Romola Garai as Ilona Tasuiev, Catherine McCormack as her sister Bislane, Ian Holm as Jonas Muller and Jonathan Pryce as Paul Dellenbach.

In Paris in 2054, Ilona, a 22-year-old researcher at the all-powerful corporation Avalon, is abducted. The case goes to police captain Karas, fresh from ending a hostage crisis by gunning down the kidnappers. He questions Muller, Avalon's former chief scientist, who quit after failing to cure progeria, the ageing disease that killed his brother, and now runs a free clinic; Muller hints that nobody truly leaves Avalon. Dellenbach, one of the company's executives, stonewalls him. A car chase ending at the Eiffel Tower leads Karas to his childhood friend Farfella, now a gangster, who hands over security footage showing Ilona's car being taken by a very old man. Ilona's sister Bislane, also an Avalon employee, breaks into the company archives and finds that Muller and a Dr. Nakata had experimented on children in search of a progeria cure, destroying their records when the subjects began to mutate. To shield her from Avalon, Karas puts her under a false arrest.

Muller finally confesses that he took Ilona because her research had uncovered the secret of eternal life, which he had found himself decades earlier, and he feared what Avalon would do with it. Before he can surrender, a police marksman shoots him by mistake. Karas realises the old man is Muller's brother, immortal but trapped in an aged body. Karas, mortally wounded, rescues Ilona from Avalon's security forces in the sewers, but she refuses to flee and resolves to hand her discovery to Avalon, so he shoots her as she walks away. Dying, he imagines Bislane forgiving him, as Dellenbach watches it all on a live video feed.

Made over six years for about €14 million, the film won the Cristal for best feature at the Annecy animation festival. It grossed only $1.8 million worldwide and drew mixed reviews, with 49% on Rotten Tomatoes and 57 on Metacritic.

overview: When Major Susan Turner is arrested for treason, ex-investigator Jack Reacher undertakes the challenging task to prove her innocence and ends up exposing a shocking conspiracy.
tagline: Justice is Coming.
title: Jack Reacher: Never Go Back
plot:
Jack Reacher: Never Go Back is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Edward Zwick and starring Tom Cruise as the titular character. The movie is based on the novel "Never Go Back" by Lee Child.

The story begins with Jack Reacher (Tom Cruise), a former military policeman, who receives an email from his estranged daughter, Josephine Reacher (Fiona Peltz). She claims that she has been kidnapped and held captive by a group of rogue soldiers. The government denies any involvement in her disappearance, but Reacher knows that he must take action to rescue her.

Reacher sets out on a mission to find Josephine, following a trail of clues that lead him from the United States to Europe. Along the way, he encounters a former Army Ranger named Bob Lincoln (Cobie Smulders), who claims to have information about his daughter's whereabouts. However, Reacher soon discovers that Lincoln is not what she seems.

As Reacher delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a conspiracy involving a group of rogue soldiers who are being led by a man named James Barron (Robert Duvall). Barron is a former Army general who has been involved in various nefarious activities, including human trafficking and murder. He has also stolen a highly classified document that could compromise national security.

Reacher's investigation takes him to the United Kingdom, where he encounters Lincoln again. However, it becomes clear that Lincoln is working for Barron, and Reacher must use his skills to take her down. In a thrilling action sequence, Reacher fights off Lincoln and several of Barron's henchmen in a hotel room.

As Reacher gets closer to the truth, he discovers that Josephine has been brainwashed by Barron and is now working for him. However, she eventually breaks free from his control and helps her father take down Barron and his accomplices.

In the end, Reacher and Josephine confront Barron in a final showdown. Reacher uses his military training to outmaneuver Barron's henchmen and ultimately kills Barron in a intense hand-to-hand combat sequence. With Barron defeated, Reacher is able to rescue his daughter and bring her home safely.

Throughout the movie, Cruise reprises his role as Jack Reacher, bringing his signature blend of action hero charm and wit to the character. The film's plot is engaging and suspenseful, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

overview: For five men, the opportunity to share a penthouse in the city -- in which to carry on extramarital affairs -- is a dream come true, until the dead body of an unknown woman turns up. Realizing that her killer must be one of their group, the men are gripped by paranoia as each one suspects another. Friendships are tested, loyalties are questioned, and marriages crumble while fear and suspicion run rampant.
tagline: The right place to do wrong.
title: The Loft
plot:
The Loft is a 2014 American thriller film directed by Erik Skjoldbjærg and written by Eric Roth. The movie stars Karl Urban, James Marsden, Wentworth Miller, Dylan McDermott, Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Taylor Kitsch, and Mark Pellegrino.

The story revolves around five friends - Mike (Karl Urban), Chris (James Marsden), Patrick (Wentworth Miller), Blake (Dylan McDermott), and Rick (Jeffrey Dean Morgan) - who have been friends since college. They all share a dark secret: they are serial killers, and they use an old mansion called The Loft as their hunting ground.

The movie begins with the five friends meeting at The Loft for a weekend getaway. However, unbeknownst to each other, they are all being watched by a mysterious figure who has been monitoring their activities. As the weekend progresses, the group's dynamics and relationships begin to unravel, revealing their true nature as serial killers.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each of the friends is hiding a dark secret from his past. Mike, for example, is haunted by a traumatic event from his childhood, while Chris has a troubled relationship with his wife. Patrick, on the other hand, is struggling to come to terms with his own identity.

Throughout the weekend, the group engages in various activities, including drinking, playing games, and engaging in physical confrontations. However, as the night wears on, their behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent.

As the mystery deepens, it becomes clear that one of the friends is not what he seems. The group's dynamics are further complicated by a series of flashbacks and revelations about each character's past.

In the end, the true nature of the mysterious figure watching them from the shadows is revealed. However, the movie takes an unexpected turn when it becomes clear that the figure is actually one of the friends themselves, who has been manipulating events to bring out their darker selves.

The ending is a twisty and suspenseful climax that leaves the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of the characters' imaginations. The final shot of the movie shows the group's true nature being exposed, but the audience is left wondering whether they will be able to escape their dark pasts.

Overall, The Loft is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of friendship, trauma, and the darker aspects of human nature. With its twisty plot and complex characters, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

overview: Feeling career burnout, pop star Angelina escapes to grant a young fan's wish in small-town New York, where she not only finds the inspiration to revitalize her career but also a shot at true love.
title: Christmas with You
plot:
Christmas with You is a 2022 American Christmas romantic comedy directed by Gabriela Tagliavini and written by Paco Farias, Jennifer C. Stetson and Michael Varrati. It stars Aimee Garcia as Angelina Costa, a pop star, and Freddie Prinze Jr. as Miguel, a high school music teacher and single father, with Deja Monique Cruz as his daughter Cristina, Zenzi Williams as Angelina's manager Monique, Gabriel Sloyer as Ricardo, Socorro Santiago as Cristina's grandmother Frida and Lawrence J. Hughes as Barry. It was released on Netflix.

Angelina, a Latina singer-songwriter who has been famous since her teens, feels pressure from her record label to stay relevant against younger stars, and her executive Barry expects a new Christmas song in time for a gala. Overwhelmed and suffering a panic attack, she takes her manager on an impromptu road trip to a small town in upstate New York to meet Cristina Torres, a teenage fan whose Christmas wish is to meet her after posting a cover online.

When a snowstorm hits, Angelina and Monique are invited to stay with the Torres family. Angelina discovers that she and Cristina have both lost their mothers recently, and she finds a song that Miguel has been writing on the piano. The two begin to collaborate, and while working on the tune, Angelina helps the teens with the choreography for her quinceañera, bonds with the family over home cooking and visits the Christmas lights with Miguel, who helps her find the missing lyrics. Their growing connection is interrupted by the arrival of Ricardo, a soap opera star she has been dating, who takes her back to New York for the gala. Torn between her image and her feelings, Angelina must decide what truly matters to her before the holidays end.

The film is a warm holiday story about family, grief, creativity and rediscovering one's passion, with Latino family traditions such as the quinceañera at its heart.

Christmas with You premiered on Netflix on November 17, 2022. It received mixed reviews, with 67 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. The Los Angeles Times found the stars likable enough to make it satisfying, while IndieWire gave it a D grade, quipping that not even Santa Claus could save it.

overview: Leo Borlock is an average student at Mica High School. He gets decent grades, is a member of the school's marching band and has always been content flying under the radar. But all that changes when he meets Stargirl Caraway, a confident and colorful new student with a penchant for the ukulele, who stands out in a crowd. She is kind, finds magic in the mundane and touches the lives of others with the simplest of gestures. Her eccentricities and infectious personality charm Leo and the student body, and she quickly goes from being ignored and ridiculed to accepted and praised, then back again, sending Leo on a rollercoaster ride of emotions.
tagline: Why be ordinary when you could be extraordinary.
title: Stargirl
plot:
Stargirl is a 2020 American romantic drama film directed by Julia Leona. The movie revolves around the life of Leo Borlock, a shy and introverted high school student who falls in love with an eccentric and free-spirited girl named Stargirl Caraway.

The main theme of Stargirl is the power of individuality and self-expression. Stargirl's unique personality and style inspire those around her to be more authentic and true to themselves, while also challenging the conventional norms of their small town community. Through Leo's journey, the film explores the tension between conformity and nonconformity, highlighting the importance of embracing one's quirks and passions.

The movie also delves into themes of love, acceptance, and the complexities of relationships. Leo's relationship with Stargirl is portrayed as a beautiful and all-consuming romance that pushes him out of his comfort zone and forces him to confront his own insecurities. The film ultimately suggests that true connection and understanding can only be achieved by embracing our differences and being open to new experiences.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of small-town life and the constraints it can place on individuals. Stargirl's arrival in town serves as a catalyst for change, highlighting the limitations and expectations that come with living in a close-knit community. The film ultimately celebrates the beauty of individuality and nonconformity, suggesting that true freedom and happiness can only be achieved by breaking free from societal norms.

Overall, Stargirl is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores themes of self-expression, love, acceptance, and the power of individuality.

overview: Secure within a desolate home as an unnatural threat terrorizes the world, a man has established a tenuous domestic order with his wife and son, but this will soon be put to test when a desperate young family arrives seeking refuge.
title: It Comes at Night
plot:
It Comes at Night is a 2017 post-apocalyptic horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of isolation. The movie takes place in a world where a mysterious threat has wiped out most of humanity, leaving only a few scattered survivors.

At its core, It Comes at Night explores the theme of paranoia and mistrust, as the characters are constantly on edge, suspecting each other of being infected or working against their survival. This atmosphere of tension and suspicion creates an sense of claustrophobia, where the characters' own fears and doubts become a more formidable enemy than the external threat.
