Meanwhile a mismatched troop of animals, fleeing an ancient magic, crosses paths with Manu and Nica as the two children escape a strange whirlwind. Together with their family and these new animal companions, the young guardian must keep the key out of the hands of Calabar, Manu's uncle and a renegade former guardian who wants to seize the immense power of Natocchue for himself.

Rotten Tomatoes lists its streaming release as 15 January 2019, and its computer animation was widely criticized as dated. Ready Steady Cut found the opening exposition overlong and the animation reminiscent of a 2004 video game, though it judged the voice casting, the banter among the animals and the underlying story reasonable.

original_title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
overview: Dr. Steven Murphy is a renowned cardiovascular surgeon who presides over a spotless household with his wife and two children. Lurking at the margins of his idyllic suburban existence is Martin, a fatherless teen who insinuates himself into the doctor's life in gradually unsettling ways.
title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
plot:
The Killing of a Sacred Deer is a 2017 absurdist psychological horror thriller directed and co-produced by Yorgos Lanthimos, who wrote the screenplay with Efthimis Filippou. Colin Farrell plays Steven Murphy, a cardiac surgeon, with Nicole Kidman as his wife Anna, Barry Keoghan as the teenager Martin, Raffey Cassidy and Sunny Suljic as the couple's children Kim and Bob, and Alicia Silverstone as Martin's mother. The title alludes to Euripides' tragedy Iphigenia in Aulis.

Steven, a Cincinnati heart surgeon, has been meeting 16-year-old Martin at a diner, whose father died a few years earlier. He introduces the boy to his family, and Martin charms them all, especially Kim. When Steven dines at Martin's home, the boy's mother makes advances at him, saying it is what her son wants, and Steven leaves. Martin's demands on his time become more frequent and insistent, and Steven grows uneasy, particularly after Martin gives Kim a ride on his motorcycle.

Then Bob suddenly loses the use of his legs. Martin explains that his father died on Steven's operating table and that, to restore the balance, Steven must kill one member of his own family; otherwise all of them will die, first becoming paralysed, then refusing food, then bleeding from the eyes before death. Soon Bob will not eat, and Kim, now infatuated with Martin, collapses at choir practice. Steven admits to Anna that he had been drinking before the fatal surgery. Martin demonstrates his hold over Kim by telling her over the phone to stand, then leaving her paralysed again. Pressed by Anna, Steven imprisons Martin in the basement, beats him and shoots him in the legs, but the boy only bites his own arm to illustrate his notion of justice. The children compete for their father's favour, Steven asks their school principal which child is better, and Anna argues that he should sacrifice one of the children rather than her. When Bob's eyes begin to bleed, Steven binds his family in a circle, covers his own face and fires a rifle blindly while spinning; the third shot kills Bob. Later, the surviving Murphys see Martin at the diner and walk out.

Shot in Cincinnati in 2016, the film competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2017 and won the prize for Best Screenplay. It was released in the United States by A24 in October 2017 and grossed $10.7 million worldwide. Reviews were positive, with 79% on Rotten Tomatoes and 73 on Metacritic.

overview: Eva is a divorced soon-to-be empty-nester wondering about her next act. Then she meets Marianne, the embodiment of her perfect self. Armed with a restored outlook on being middle-aged and single, Eva decides to take a chance on her new love interest Albert — a sweet, funny and like-minded man. But things get complicated when Eva discovers that Albert is in fact the dreaded ex–husband of Marianne...
title: Enough Said
plot:
Enough Said is a poignant and nuanced exploration of human connection, vulnerability, and the complexities of relationships. The film delves into the intricate web of emotions that arise when two people, both navigating their own personal struggles, find themselves drawn to each other.

At its core, Enough Said is a movie about the fragility of human intimacy and the ways in which we often hide behind masks of confidence and self-assurance. The protagonist, Eva (played by Julia Louis-Dreyfus), is a complex and multifaceted character, struggling to come to terms with her own emotional baggage and the loss of her husband.

As Eva forms a connection with Albert (played by James Gandolfini), a divorced man who is also navigating his own emotional landscape, the film expertly captures the ebb and flow of their relationship. Through their interactions, we see the ways in which they both use humor and vulnerability to shield themselves from the pain of their pasts.

One of the primary themes of Enough Said is the power of human connection to heal and transform us. Despite the risks and uncertainties involved, Eva and Albert find solace in each other's company, and through their relationship, we see the ways in which they both learn to confront their fears and let go of their defenses.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. As Eva and Albert navigate their feelings for each other, they are forced to confront the ways in which their identities have been defined by their past experiences and relationships.

Ultimately, Enough Said is a movie about the beauty and complexity of human connection, and the ways in which it can both heal and hurt us. Through its nuanced portrayal of Eva and Albert's relationship, the film offers a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply moving and profoundly insightful.

overview: Italy, early '90s. Calm, clever and inscrutable, politician Giulio Andreotti has been synonymous with power for decades. He has survived everything: electoral battles, terrorist massacres, loss of friends, slanderous accusations; but now certain repentant mobsters implicate him in the crimes of Cosa Nostra.
production_companies: Fonds Eurimages du Conseil de l'Europe
title: Il Divo
plot:
Il Divo is a 2008 Italian biographical drama film directed by Paolo Sorrentino, which tells the story of Giulio Andreotti, a former Prime Minister of Italy. The movie delves into the complexities of power, politics, and identity, as embodied by its titular character.

At its core, Il Divo explores the theme of the corrupting influence of power and the blurred lines between personal and public life. As Giulio navigates the treacherous waters of Italian politics, he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit, manipulation, and self-preservation. The film masterfully captures the sense of moral ambiguity that often accompanies those in positions of authority.

The movie also examines the tension between tradition and modernity, as embodied by Giulio's character. As a product of Italy's post-war era, he represents a bygone age of politics and society, struggling to adapt to the changing times. This internal conflict is reflected in his relationships with younger politicians and his own sense of identity.

Furthermore, Il Divo touches on the theme of nostalgia and the romanticization of the past. Giulio's character is often portrayed as a nostalgic figure, clinging to the ideals of Italy's fascist past while navigating the complexities of modern politics. This nostalgia serves as a coping mechanism, allowing him to maintain a sense of control and purpose in a rapidly changing world.

Throughout the film, Sorrentino employs a unique visual style, blending elements of drama and comedy to create a captivating narrative. The result is a nuanced portrayal of a complex individual, whose flaws and contradictions are both fascinating and repellent. Ultimately, Il Divo presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own assumptions about power, identity, and the nature of politics.

overview: Master chef Kate Armstrong runs her life and her kitchen with intimidating intensity. However, a recipe for disaster may be in the works when she becomes the guardian of her young niece while crossing forks with the brash sous-chef who just joined her staff. Though romance blooms in the face of rivalry, Kate needs to look outside the kitchen to find true happiness.
tagline: Life isn't always made to order.
title: No Reservations
plot:
No Reservations is a romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and personal growth. The story revolves around Kate (played by Catherine Zeta-Jones), a successful food blogger who has given up on love after a string of failed relationships. When she meets Ian (played by Aaron Eckhart), a charming and handsome chef, their initial encounter is marked by a series of awkward and humorous misunderstandings.

As the film progresses, Kate and Ian embark on a whirlwind romance, navigating their differences and confronting their emotional baggage. Through their relationship, the movie delves into themes of vulnerability, trust, and the importance of human connection. The film also touches on the idea of finding one's true passion and purpose in life, as embodied by Kate's love for food and Ian's dedication to his craft.

The movie's portrayal of a complex and flawed female protagonist, who is both strong-willed and vulnerable, adds depth to the narrative. The chemistry between Kate and Ian is undeniable, making their romance both captivating and relatable. Ultimately, No Reservations is a heartwarming exploration of love, self-discovery, and the power of human relationships to transform our lives.

overview: After 12 years in prison, former high school football star Eddie Palmer returns home to put his life back together—and forms an unlikely bond with Sam, an outcast boy from a troubled home. But Eddie's past threatens to ruin his new life and family.
tagline: Family is who you make it.
title: Palmer
plot:
Palmer is a 2021 American drama film directed by Fisher Stevens and written by Alex Metcalf. The movie stars Justin Timberlake, Juno Temple, Alisha Wainwright, and Ryder Allen.

The main theme of the movie Palmer revolves around the concept of redemption and second chances. The story follows Eddie Palmer (played by Justin Timberlake), a former rodeo rider who is struggling to find his place in the world after being released from prison. He takes care of an 8-year-old boy named Max (played by Ryder Allen) whom he meets at a gas station, and together they embark on a journey across America.

Throughout the film, Eddie's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his past mistakes and learns to let go of his anger and bitterness. He finds solace in his relationship with Max, who becomes like a surrogate son to him. As they travel from town to town, Eddie begins to rebuild his life and find a new sense of purpose.

The movie explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human need for connection and belonging. It also touches on issues of racism, poverty, and the struggles faced by people living in rural America. Through Eddie's journey, the film highlights the importance of empathy, kindness, and compassion towards others, particularly those who are marginalized or overlooked.

The title "Palmer" refers to the act of taming and domesticating wild animals, which serves as a metaphor for Eddie's own transformation from a troubled individual to someone who is capable of love and connection. The film ultimately suggests that it's never too late to change one's life and find redemption through the power of human relationships.

Overall, Palmer is a heartwarming and thought-provoking drama that explores themes of personal growth, redemption, and the transformative power of human connections.

overview: At Mr. Rad's Warehouse, the best hip-hop crews in Los Angeles compete for money and respect. But when a suburban crew crashes the party, stealing their dancers - and their moves - two warring friends have to pull together to represent the street. Starring hip-hop sensations Marques Houston, Omari Grandberry, Lil' Kim and comedian Steve Harvey.
tagline: If you want respect, you've got to take it.
title: You Got Served
plot:
You Got Served is a 2004 dance film that revolves around the world of competitive breakdancing. The movie delves into the theme of perseverance and dedication, as the characters strive to perfect their craft and overcome obstacles to achieve success.

The film also explores the idea of identity and self-expression through dance. The main character, Cassie (played by Omar Epps), is a talented dancer who finds his passion in breakdancing, but struggles to balance his love for the art form with his desire to fit in with his peers.

Furthermore, You Got Served touches on the theme of rivalry and competition, as Cassie and his friend Eddie (played by Kenya Moore) engage in a series of dance battles against their opponents. This aspect of the movie highlights the importance of sportsmanship and respect for one's opponents, even in the face of intense competition.

Ultimately, the film suggests that success is not just about winning, but also about personal growth and self-discovery. Through Cassie's journey, the movie shows how embracing one's passion and working hard to achieve goals can lead to a sense of fulfillment and purpose.

overview: A young woman returns to her small hometown intent on killing her abusive father only to discover someone murdered him the day before. As the girl searches for answers, she uncovers a family legacy more dangerous than she'd imagined.
title: Girl
plot:
Girl is a 2020 Canadian-American thriller written and directed by Chad Faust, who also appears in the film. Bella Thorne stars as a young woman known only as Girl, who returns to her hometown intending to kill her abusive father, with Mickey Rourke as the town's sheriff, Elizabeth Saunders, Lanette Ware and Glen Gould. Shot in 2019 in Sudbury, Ontario, it was released in December 2020.

Girl travels by bus back to the small, decaying town of Golden, carrying her father's hatchet, with the intention of killing him. Before arriving, she calls her mother, who reveals that her father has sent a letter threatening to kill her; Girl asks for the return address, but her mother refuses to give it. Walking into town from the highway, Girl turns down a ride from the local sheriff and stops at a bar, where she finds her father's address in a phone book and has a tense encounter with a woman named Betty.

When she reaches her father's house, she discovers that someone has already murdered him. Her attempt to report the killing gets nowhere, and when she calls her mother, she vows to find out who is responsible, although her mother urges her to come home. At a laundromat she meets a man who calls himself Charmer, and after initial wariness she begins to flirt with him, telling him how her father taught her to throw hatchets expertly when she was a child. However, Charmer soon reveals himself to be dangerous, and Girl realizes that her father's death is connected to a wider web of secrets in the town. As she digs deeper, she finds that the people of Golden know more about her father and his death than they admit, and that her family's past is bound up with violence. Using her skill with the hatchet and her determination, Girl must fight to survive and uncover the truth about her father, her mother and the town.

Girl received mixed reviews, with a 59 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that despite Thorne's impressive work in the title role, it struggled to distinguish itself from other female-led revenge thrillers. Critics noted its bleak, atmospheric setting and its deliberately minimalist approach.

overview: A celebrity journalist and renowned womanizer starts to rethink his life choices after he falls for a mysterious model who leads a double life.
title: Squared Love
plot:
Squared Love (Polish: Miłość do kwadratu) is a 2021 Polish romantic comedy film directed by Filip Zylber and written by Marzanna Polit and Wiktor Piątkowski. Produced by Endemol Polska and set in Warsaw, it stars Adrianna Chlebicka and Mateusz Banasiuk, with Mirosław Baka, Agnieszka Żulewska, Krzysztof Czeczot, Anna Smołowik, Tomasz Karolak, Bartłomiej Kotschedoff, Jacek Knap and Helena Mazur in supporting roles. It was released on Netflix on 11 February 2021, and Netflix later reported in its first-quarter investor letter that 31 million households had sampled it. It was followed in 2023 by two sequels, Squared Love All Over Again and Squared Love Everlasting.

Monika Grabarczyk (Chlebicka) is a devoted primary-school teacher, beloved by her pupils though disliked by her demanding, test-obsessed principal (Karolak). Early each morning, however, she swaps her glasses and ponytail for a curly wig, blue contact lenses and glamorous clothes to work as Klaudia, a mysterious model on billboards across the city who only works before nine. She hates modelling and keeps it secret, believing no school would tolerate it, but needs the money to pay off the debts her widowed mechanic father (Baka) owes to loan sharks; he knows nothing of it and only laments that she is not in love. Stefan Tkaczyk (Banasiuk), known to the world as Enzo, is a shallow, womanising model who loves the sports cars he gets to borrow and lives with his boss and lover Alicja (Żulewska) in an open relationship. Their first meeting goes badly when he picks Klaudia up after her car breaks down on the way to a shoot and mistakes her for a prostitute. When Alicja throws Enzo out, he moves in with his brother, whose wife has left the family, and has to look after his young niece Ania (Mazur), who turns out to be one of Monika's pupils. Cast together in an advertising campaign, Enzo feels a spark with Klaudia on set while also being drawn to Monika on school trips, unaware that they are the same woman, while her double life grows ever harder to keep hidden.

The film was poorly received; on Rotten Tomatoes only 17% of six critics' reviews were positive. John Serba of Decider found its secret-identity premise unconvincing and its script cluttered, though he credited Chlebicka with bringing some sincerity to the dual role, while Roger Moore of Movie Nation called it vapid and noted the leads' thin chemistry, singling out its soundtrack of mostly American pop songs.

overview: Following the dumping of gallons of toxic waste in the river, a giant mutated squid-like creature appears and begins attacking the populace. Gang-du's daughter Hyun-seo is snatched up by the creature; with his family to assist him, he sets off to find her.
tagline: Monsters are real.
title: The Host
plot:
The Host is a 2006 South Korean monster film directed by Bong Joon-ho. The movie tells the story of a giant mutant creature that emerges from the Han River and begins to wreak havoc on Seoul.

The main themes of The Host can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Environmentalism**: The film is a commentary on the consequences of playing with nature and ignoring environmental warnings. The monster, known as "Geon-Woo," is a result of toxic waste dumped into the Han River by a chemical plant. This serves as a metaphor for the dangers of pollution and the importance of protecting our environment.

2. **Government Incompetence**: The government's slow response to the crisis and their attempts to cover up the truth are major plot points in the film. This highlights the theme of bureaucratic inefficiency and the need for accountability in times of crisis.

3. **Human Connection**: Despite the chaos and destruction caused by the monster, the film focuses on the relationships between the characters, particularly the bond between the father and daughter. This emphasizes the importance of human connection and empathy in the face of adversity.

4. **Social Commentary**: The Host also contains social commentary on issues such as class struggle, consumerism, and the effects of globalization. The character of Du-Deok, a young woman who becomes infected with the alien parasite, serves as a symbol of the struggles faced by marginalized communities.

5. **Science vs. Nature**: The film explores the tension between scientific progress and the natural world. The scientists' attempts to understand and control the monster ultimately fail, highlighting the limitations of human knowledge in the face of nature's power.

Overall, The Host is a thought-provoking film that combines elements of horror, science fiction, and social commentary to create a unique and engaging viewing experience.

overview: Karen, Sarah, and Emma Tunney are all moving to a small town in Pennsylvania where, unknown to them, in 1913, a horrid mine accident trapped dozens of children alive, underground. But there's a problem. They're still alive.
tagline: Prey for Them
title: Wicked Little Things
plot:
Wicked Little Things is a 2006 American horror film directed by Stuart Gordon and starring Katie Aselton, Brian Anthony Wilson, and Laura Harring.

The movie revolves around a group of friends who embark on a road trip to New Orleans, only to find themselves in the midst of a supernatural nightmare. The main theme of Wicked Little Things is the exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the themes of desire, temptation, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the characters are not what they seem, and their true intentions are shrouded in mystery. The film masterfully weaves together elements of horror, suspense, and the supernatural to create a sense of unease and tension that keeps the viewer on edge.

One of the primary themes of Wicked Little Things is the idea that our deepest desires can be both our greatest strengths and weaknesses. As the characters navigate their way through the treacherous landscape of New Orleans, they are forced to confront their own dark impulses and the true nature of their relationships with one another.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted by external forces. The characters' perceptions of themselves and each other become increasingly distorted as the story progresses, leading to a sense of disorientation and confusion that mirrors the chaos and disorder that surrounds them.

Ultimately, Wicked Little Things is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into the darker corners of human psychology, revealing the complexities and nuances of human nature in all its messy, imperfect glory.

original_title: PAW Patrol: Jet to the Rescue
overview: A royal relative steals a gem with the power to make things fly, the Paw Patrol takes to the skies to stop him and save Barkingburg.
title: PAW Patrol: Jet to the Rescue
plot:
PAW Patrol: Jet to the Rescue is a 2020 Canadian-American animated adventure special based on PAW Patrol, the computer-animated preschool television series created by Keith Chapman and produced by Spin Master Entertainment with animation by Guru Studio. Running 56 minutes, it was released in September 2020 and sends the team into the skies in a fleet of jets. The voice cast includes Joey Nijem as Ryder, Lilly Bartlam as Skye, Justin Paul Kelly as Chase, Lukas Engel as Marshall, Keegan Hedley as Rubble, Berkley Silverman as Everest and David López as Tracker, with Caoimhe Judd as the Princess of Barkingburg, Anya Cooke as her pampered dog Sweetie and Ashton Frank as the Duke of Flappington.

Ryder and the pups are invited to Barkingburg Castle for the Princess's birthday, where they hope to surprise her with a gift, but attention centres on the precious Gem of Barkingburg, which has been passed to her that evening and has the power to make things fly. The Duke of Flappington, a boy who claims to be her distant cousin, is welcomed to the party but secretly conspires with the selfish Sweetie to steal the gem and seize power. When the team tries to stop the theft, Ryder and most of the pups slide into a dungeon and are locked in a remote chamber deep inside the castle, while Skye and two others escape capture but are shut outside and unable to reach Ryder. The Duke combines the gem with the Gem of Flappington in a sceptre and uses it to lift Barkingburg into the clouds as his own kingdom, sending a giant eagle-shaped aircraft and eagle drones against the pups' jets. Skye, who leads the mission, has to overcome her fear of eagles to free her friends, and Sweetie, double-crossed by the Duke, backs out of the scheme before the pups save the Princess and her kingdom.

Common Sense Media rated it suitable from age four, describing it as a standalone adventure with only minor peril and a more involved, action-packed story that might hold the interest of fans who had outgrown the television show, and praising its messages about teamwork and the courage to face one's fears, as well as Tracker's use of Spanish phrases. The Australian Council on Children and the Media judged it best suited to children aged three to five, highlighting its messages of kindness and self-belief.

overview: In the year 2524, four centuries after humans started colonizing the outer planets, retired General James Ford gets called back into service when a hostile alien fleet attacks soldiers on a remote planet. The threat against mankind soon escalates into an interstellar war as Ford and a team of elite soldiers try to stop the imminent attack before it's too late.
tagline: First contact has been made. It's war.
title: Cosmic Sin
plot:
Cosmic Sin is a 2021 American science fiction action film directed by Edward Drake. It stars Bruce Willis, Frank Grillo, Brandon Thomas Lee, Corey Large, Perrey Reeves, C.J. Perry, Lochlyn Munro, Costas Mandylor and Adelaide Kane, and follows a disgraced general recruited to lead a desperate mission after humanity's first contact with a hostile alien species.

In the film's future history, humanity colonizes Mars in 2031, forms a world government called the Alliance in 2042 and uses quantum propulsion to travel beyond the Solar System. In 2519, when the colony of Zafdie tries to secede, General James Ford ends the war by dropping a quantum bomb on it, killing 70 million people. Dishonorably discharged and branded "the Blood General", he is left by his wife, Dr. Lea Goss. In 2524, miners on a distant planet encounter unseen aliens, and General Eron Ryle summons Ford and Goss. Infected survivors turn violent and spread the infection, and a signal sent during the attack may soon reveal Earth's location to the invaders.

Ryle launches Operation Cosmic Sin, sending Ford, Goss and a small team of soldiers, along with technician Corporal Ardene, to the colony world Ellora, armed with powered suits and a quantum bomb, to study a downed alien ship and find the aliens' home world. Arriving in the middle of a battle, the team is scattered and learns that the planet is overrun by aliens and infected humans. Ardene discovers that the aliens are a hive mind that reproduces by infecting hosts and that they have built a quantum gate near Ellora to invade the galaxy. Speaking through an infected Goss, the aliens call themselves the Sigea and offer humanity assimilation or death. The team decides to fire the bomb through the gate, while Ryle, stranded in orbit with a damaged suit, offers himself as a target for an orbital gun, and Ardene reluctantly fires, destroying the gate. The bomb creates a black hole that wipes out the Sigea fleet and home system. Seven days after first contact, the survivors gather in a bar as the Alliance announces the Sigea's surrender, and Ford mourns Goss.

Saban Films released Cosmic Sin in theaters and on digital platforms on March 12, 2021. It was panned by critics, receiving 6% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 9. It won a Golden Raspberry Award for Willis's performance, later rescinded after his aphasia diagnosis.

overview: A night guard at an armored car company in the Southern U.S. organizes one of the biggest bank heists in American history.
tagline: What Would You Do With $17 Million?
title: Masterminds
plot:
Masterminds is a 2016 American heist comedy film directed by Jared Hess and written by Chris Henchy. The movie follows the story of a group of misfits who plan to rob a bank in Minnesota.

The main theme of Masterminds revolves around the idea of friendship and camaraderie among outcasts. The main characters, including Jody (Owen Wilson), H.I. McDunnough (Zach Galifianakis), and Buddy Slade (Kristofer Hivju), are all outsiders who come together to achieve a common goal. Through their shared experience, they learn to rely on each other and develop an unbreakable bond.

Another significant theme in Masterminds is the power of imagination and creativity. The characters' elaborate plan to rob the bank showcases their resourcefulness and ingenuity, highlighting the importance of thinking outside the box and pushing boundaries.

The movie also explores the idea of redemption and second chances. Jody, who has a troubled past, sees this heist as an opportunity to redeem himself and start anew. Through his journey, he learns to let go of his past mistakes and find a sense of purpose.

Finally, Masterminds pokes fun at societal expectations and the pressures that come with conforming to norms. The characters' desire for independence and nonconformity is reflected in their rejection of mainstream values and their pursuit of individuality.

Overall, Masterminds is a heartwarming and hilarious film that celebrates the power of friendship, creativity, and self-discovery.

overview: As adults, best friends Julien and Sophie continue the odd game they started as children -- a fearless competition to outdo one another with daring and outrageous stunts. While they often act out to relieve one another's pain, their game might be a way to avoid the fact that they are truly meant for one another.
tagline: When is love a game, and when is it not?
title: Love Me If You Dare
plot:
Love Me If You Dare is a French romantic drama film that explores the complex and tumultuous relationship between two individuals, Sophie and Laurent. The movie delves into the darker aspects of love, obsession, and the blurred lines between desire and possession.

At its core, Love Me If You Dare is a story about the intense and all-consuming nature of passion, which can both elevate and destroy us. The film portrays a relationship that is marked by a deep emotional connection, yet also by a sense of possessiveness and control. Sophie, the protagonist, finds herself trapped in a cycle of codependency with Laurent, who struggles to let go of his need for her.

The movie also touches on themes of vulnerability, trust, and the fragility of human relationships. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that both characters have been hurt in past relationships and are struggling to open themselves up to love again. The film's portrayal of their emotional journey is raw and unflinching, capturing the pain and uncertainty that can accompany falling deeply in love.

Furthermore, Love Me If You Dare explores the societal expectations placed on women, particularly in regards to their relationships with men. Sophie's character is often at the mercy of those around her, including Laurent, who exercises a significant amount of control over her life. The film critiques this dynamic, highlighting the ways in which women can be manipulated and exploited by those they love.

Ultimately, Love Me If You Dare is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that challenges its viewers to confront the complexities of human relationships and the nature of love itself.

overview: A virus spreads through an office complex causing white collar workers to act out their worst impulses.
tagline: Hostile. Work. Environment.
title: Mayhem
plot:
Mayhem is an American action thriller film released in 2017, directed by Joachim Trier and written by Joachim Trier and Eskil Vogt. The movie follows the story of Stig Håkansson, a Norwegian hitman who is forced to return to his hometown after being diagnosed with cancer.

The main theme of Mayhem revolves around the destructive nature of violence and the consequences of a life spent in the shadows. Stig's character is a complex exploration of a man who has built walls around himself to cope with the trauma of his past, but ultimately finds it difficult to escape the darkness that haunts him.

As the story unfolds, we see how Stig's actions have a ripple effect on those around him, causing chaos and destruction in his wake. The film raises questions about the morality of violence and whether it can ever be justified, or if it is simply a means to an end for those who use it.

The movie also explores the theme of redemption, as Stig grapples with his own mortality and tries to make amends for past mistakes. Through Stig's character, we see a nuanced portrayal of a man who is both capable of great evil and great vulnerability, highlighting the complexity of human nature.

Overall, Mayhem is a thought-provoking film that delves into the darker aspects of human behavior, raising important questions about the consequences of violence and the possibility of redemption.

overview: With his wife Elizabeth on life support after a boating accident, Hawaiian land baron Matt King takes his daughters on a trip from Oahu to Kauai to confront a young real estate broker, who was having an affair with Elizabeth before her misfortune.
tagline: The South Pacific ain't that terrific.
title: The Descendants
plot:
The Descendants is a 2011 American drama film directed by Alexander Payne, starring George Clooney, Shailene Woodley, and Amara Miller.

The movie revolves around Matt King (played by George Clooney), a wealthy businessman who finds himself at the center of a family crisis when his wife Elizabeth (played by Patricia Hastings) is in a coma after a boating accident. As Matt navigates this challenging situation, he must confront his own identity and relationships with his daughters, including his eldest daughter Alex (played by Shailene Woodley), who has been estranged from him due to her rebellious nature.

The main themes of The Descendants include:

1. **Family dynamics**: The film explores the complexities of family relationships, particularly between parents and children. Matt's journey is marked by a desire to reconnect with his daughters and understand their perspectives.
2. **Identity crisis**: As Matt navigates his wife's coma and his own sense of purpose, he begins to question his identity as a husband, father, and businessman. This theme is reflected in his relationships with his daughters, who are trying to find their own paths in life.
3. **Guilt and redemption**: Matt's past mistakes come back to haunt him, and he must confront the consequences of his actions. Through his journey, he seeks redemption and a chance to make amends with those around him.
4. **Love and forgiveness**: The film highlights the importance of love, forgiveness, and understanding in relationships. Matt's relationships with his daughters, particularly Alex, are marked by a desire for forgiveness and connection.
5. **Self-discovery**: Through his experiences, Matt undergoes a process of self-discovery, learning to let go of his ego and find meaning in his life beyond his business and wealth.

Overall, The Descendants is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of family relationships, identity, guilt, love, and forgiveness.

overview: When teenager Elle's first kiss leads to a forbidden romance with the hottest boy in high school, she risks her relationship with her best friend.
tagline: She can tell her best friend anything, except this one thing
title: The Kissing Booth
plot:
The Kissing Booth is a 2018 American teen romantic comedy film written and directed by Vince Marcello, based on Beth Reekles's 2012 novel of the same name. It stars Joey King as Elle Evans, a quirky late bloomer, Jacob Elordi as Noah Flynn and Joel Courtney as Noah's younger brother Lee, with Molly Ringwald in a supporting role.

Elle and Lee have been best friends since birth in Los Angeles, and they live by a set of friendship rules. After losing her mother to illness, Elle quietly nurses a crush on Lee's popular, bad-boy older brother Noah. On the first day of junior year, Noah gets into a fight with a classmate who touches Elle inappropriately, and later warns every boy at school to stay away from her. Elle and Lee organize a kissing booth for a school fundraiser, and Elle rashly promises that Noah will take part. When he does not show up, Lee takes his place and leaves with a classmate, Rachel, and a group of popular girls set Elle up to kiss an unwanted partner, but at the last moment Noah steps in and kisses the blindfolded Elle, and they kiss again in front of everyone.

Sheltering from the rain in a gazebo, Elle tells Noah she will not be just another conquest, and he admits his feelings for her. After he defends her at a beach party, they detour to the Hollywood Sign and spend their first night together, agreeing to keep the relationship secret from Lee until Elle can tell him. Elle also learns that Noah has been accepted to Harvard University. When Lee discovers them kissing, he storms off, feeling betrayed, and Elle blames Noah, who disappears from school for weeks. Elle and Lee eventually reconcile at an arcade, and she attends prom with Lee and his new girlfriend, Rachel. When Noah declares his love for her publicly at the prom, Elle runs away. At Elle and Lee's birthday costume party the next day, she confesses her love for Noah to Lee, who gives his blessing; driving off to find Noah, she discovers that the "Lee" in a Batman costume beside her is Noah himself. They spend the following weeks together before he leaves for college.

Released on Netflix on May 11, 2018, the film was panned by critics as clichéd and regressive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 15% approval, but Netflix deemed it a major success because of its viewership and re-watch rate. It was followed by The Kissing Booth 2 in 2020 and The Kissing Booth 3 in 2021.

overview: A Minnesota police officer crosses paths with a committed and tireless vigilante as he follows the trail of a ruthless predator responsible for several abductions and murders.
tagline: When the predator becomes the prey
title: Night Hunter
plot:
Night Hunter, originally titled Nomis, is a 2018 Canadian crime thriller written and directed by David Raymond. Henry Cavill stars as Detective Walter Marshall, with Ben Kingsley as a former judge turned vigilante, Alexandra Daddario as a police profiler, Stanley Tucci, Brendan Fletcher as the suspect Simon Stulls, Minka Kelly and Nathan Fillion. It premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in September 2018 and was released on video on demand in August 2019 and in theaters that September by Saban Films.

When the body of a young woman is found on a logging truck in Minnesota, Detective Walter Marshall suspects that she leapt to her death to escape a captor. A breakthrough comes unexpectedly when Michael Cooper, a former judge who runs vigilante stings to trap sexual predators, sees one of his operations go wrong and his young ward, Lara, is abducted. Tracking her through a device hidden in her earrings, Marshall finds Lara and several other captive women in a house owned by Simon Stulls, a man who appears to be intellectually disabled.

Simon is arrested, and police profiler Rachel Chase, played by Daddario, tries to determine whether he could really be behind the abductions. Investigating his past, they learn that he was conceived through rape and that his mother attempted suicide before he was born. While Simon is in custody, the police themselves come under attack: a technician is killed by a car bomb, and another is forced to free Simon after his infant daughter is threatened. The police recapture Simon after he has killed his own father, just as Cooper discovers that Lara has been taken again. Convinced that Simon is responsible, Cooper ambushes the police transport but encounters a man who looks exactly like him. It is revealed that Simon has an identical twin, and the two brothers have been working together. As the twin's plan targets those closest to the investigation, Marshall, who is also struggling with his estrangement from his wife and daughter, races to stop him.

Night Hunter received negative reviews, with a 14 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it contrived and clichéd, wasting a solid cast, and a Metacritic score of 31.

overview: Cathy is a sous-chef wanting to open a restaurant. With financial difficulties, Cathy accepts a job at a shelter for young migrants. At first she hates the job then her passion for cuisine starts to change children's lives.
title: Kitchen Brigade
plot:
Kitchen Brigade (French: La Brigade) is a 2022 French comedy-drama film directed by Louis-Julien Petit, who wrote the screenplay with Liza Benguigui, Sophie Bensadoun and Thomas Pujol. Inspired by a true story from the Corrèze region, it stars Audrey Lamy, François Cluzet and Chantal Neuwirth, alongside young non-professional performers drawn from a real reception centre. Produced by Odyssée Pictures, it was shot over 38 days in Île-de-France and Hauts-de-France. The film premiered at the L'Alpe d'Huez Film Festival on 20 January 2022, where Lamy won the award for best actress, and opened in French cinemas on 23 March 2022.

Cathy Marie (Lamy), a gifted sous-chef at an upscale restaurant, has long dreamed of running her own place and is close to achieving it when a clash with her boss leaves her out of work and in financial trouble. Unable to find a job that matches her skills, she reluctantly accepts a post as the cook at the canteen of a shelter for young migrants, mostly from Africa and South Asia, who risk deportation once they turn 18. Instead of fine dining there are tinned ravioli and a microwave, and her kitchen brigade will have to be made up of the residents themselves. Having grown up in a care home herself, Cathy understands the teenagers and wants to give them skills that could let them earn a living, but she meets resistance: the boys have trouble with authority, especially from a woman, and the shelter's director Lorenzo (Cluzet) is sceptical too. Supported by her colleague Sabine (Neuwirth) and by Fatou (Fatoumata Kaba), she starts organising the kitchen like a football coach, and the young people become increasingly committed. Lorenzo comes round, a television cookery show takes an interest in the project, and Cathy finally wins approval for a cooking class, becoming a teacher at a training centre.

The film topped the French box office for new releases on its opening day and reached about 119,000 admissions in its first week, before being released in some 24 countries, including the United States through Samuel Goldwyn Films in 2023. French reviews were divided: Ouest-France praised Lamy in a popular, never miserabilist social comedy, while L'Obs and La Libre found the direction lacking. In Germany it won the Bernhard Wicki Prize at the Emden-Norderney festival. Variety called it a sweet, slightly undercooked diversion, and The New York Times found it a white-saviour story, though with lovely young people and food.

overview: A secret military project endangers Neo-Tokyo when it turns a biker gang member into a rampaging psychic psychopath that only two teenagers and a group of psychics can stop.
tagline: Neo-Tokyo is about to E.X.P.L.O.D.E.
title: Akira
plot:
Akira is a 1988 anime science fiction film directed by Katsuhiro Otomo, based on his own manga series of the same name.

In post-apocalyptic Neo-Tokyo, a young biker gang member named Shotaro Kaneda is involved in a street racing accident that kills one of his friends. As a result, he is hospitalized and discovers that he has developed telekinetic powers after being exposed to a mysterious energy known as "Akira".

The story begins with the introduction of Colonel Shikishima, who is investigating a series of bizarre occurrences in Neo-Tokyo. He soon discovers that Akira, a powerful psychic child, has been released from his containment facility and is wreaking havoc on the city.

Kaneda's friend Tetsuo Shima, who was involved in the accident that gave Kaneda his powers, begins to exhibit similar telekinetic abilities after being exposed to Akira. As Tetsuo's powers grow stronger, he becomes increasingly unstable and violent, causing chaos throughout the city.

Meanwhile, a secret government agency known as the Public Security Section 9 is formed to deal with the crisis. The team consists of Colonel Shikishima, his deputy Lieutenant Gendo, and three other members: Bodo, Lila, and Kei. They are tasked with capturing Akira and stopping Tetsuo's rampage.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Akira is not just a simple psychic child, but a powerful being who has been manipulated by the government to further their own interests. The true purpose of the government's experiments on Akira is revealed to be the creation of a new breed of super-soldiers using his powers.

The climax of the film takes place in an abandoned amusement park, where Kaneda and Tetsuo engage in a fierce battle. In the end, Kaneda manages to defeat Tetsuo by using his own telekinetic powers against him, but not before Tetsuo's body is severely damaged.

In the aftermath, Akira is taken into custody by Colonel Shikishima, who reveals that he has been working to uncover the truth about the government's experiments on Akira. The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as Kaneda reflects on the events that have transpired and the lessons he has learned.

Throughout the film, Otomo explores themes of psychic powers, government conspiracies, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The animation is highly detailed and expressive, bringing the post-apocalyptic world to life in a way that is both visually stunning and thought-provoking.

Overall, Akira is a classic anime film that has become a cult favorite around the world. Its blend of science fiction, action, and psychological drama makes it a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: Two high school girls are best friends until one dates the other's older brother, who is totally his sister's nemesis.
tagline: You're only young once… is it over yet?
title: The Edge of Seventeen
plot:
The Edge of Seventeen is a coming-of-age comedy-drama film released in 2016, directed by Kelly Fremon Craig and produced by Lianne Halfon, Molly Smith, and Jennifer Ventimilia. The movie follows the life of Nadine Byrd (played by Hailee Steinfeld), a high school junior navigating her senior year while dealing with her complicated relationships and family dynamics.

The story begins with Nadine's mother, Mary (played by Kyra Sedgwick), who is recently divorced from her husband, Jim (played by Woody Harrelson). The tension between the two parents is palpable, and Nadine struggles to cope with the changes in her life. Her father has moved out, and she feels abandoned.

Nadine's best friend, Krista (played by Haley Lu Richardson), tries to be supportive, but their friendship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. The two girls try to navigate high school cliques, relationships, and social pressures while dealing with Nadine's emotional turmoil.

As the story unfolds, Nadine develops feelings for her classmate, Eric (played by Blake Jenner), who seems perfect on the surface but turns out to be shallow and unfaithful. Meanwhile, she also starts to develop a crush on her English teacher, Mr. Bruner (played by Tom Holland).

Throughout the film, Nadine's relationships with her family members are explored in depth. Her mother is portrayed as a complex character struggling to balance her own emotions and needs with those of her daughter. The tension between them is evident, but they also share moments of tenderness and understanding.

As the school year progresses, Nadine faces various setbacks, including a failed relationship and a disappointing college acceptance letter. However, she eventually finds solace in her friendship with Krista and begins to develop a stronger sense of self.

The film's climax revolves around Nadine's confrontation with Eric, who has been unfaithful to her. The scene is intense and emotional, showcasing Nadine's growth and resilience. In the end, Nadine comes to terms with her feelings and learns to move on from her past heartbreak.

The Edge of Seventeen received widespread critical acclaim for its authentic portrayal of teenage life, nuanced character development, and outstanding performances from the cast. The film's exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, relationships, and identity resonated with audiences worldwide.

overview: Daniel Lugo, manager of the Sun Gym in 1990s Miami, decides that there is only one way to achieve his version of the American dream: extortion. To achieve his goal, he recruits musclemen Paul and Adrian as accomplices. After several failed attempts, they abduct rich businessman Victor Kershaw and convince him to sign over all his assets to them. But when Kershaw makes it out alive, authorities are reluctant to believe his story.
tagline: Their American dream is bigger than yours.
title: Pain & Gain
plot:
Pain & Gain is a biographical crime comedy-drama film directed by Michael Bay, released in 2013. The movie is based on the true story of Daniel Lugo, a personal trainer who recruits two men, Adrian Balboa and Paul Doyle, to help him carry out a complex heist.

The film begins with Daniel Lugo (played by Mark Wahlberg), a struggling personal trainer at a Miami gym. Lugo's life takes a drastic turn when his girlfriend, Paige (played by Christiana Cole), leaves him for another man. Desperate and feeling unappreciated, Lugo turns to crime as a way to escape his miserable life.

Lugo recruits Adrian Balboa (played by Dwayne Johnson) and Paul Doyle (played by Anthony Mackie), two men with different skill sets but shared desperation. The three form an unlikely trio, bound together by their desire for wealth and success. They devise a plan to rob Lugo's wealthy clients, using his knowledge of their personal lives and habits.

As the heist unfolds, the group faces numerous challenges, including a series of mishaps and unexpected twists. Meanwhile, Lugo becomes increasingly unhinged, driven by his own ego and desire for wealth. The group's dynamics become strained as they struggle to work together and maintain their relationships.

The film takes a dark turn when Lugo's obsession with wealth and power leads him to commit atrocities against his partners. Balboa and Doyle are forced to confront the consequences of their actions, leading to a violent confrontation that ultimately results in tragedy.

Throughout the film, Michael Bay's signature style is evident, with fast-paced action sequences and over-the-top violence. The movie also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the corrupting influence of power.

The film received mixed reviews from critics, but Dwayne Johnson's performance as Adrian Balboa was widely praised. Mark Wahlberg's portrayal of Daniel Lugo was also notable, capturing the character's complexity and charisma.

Overall, Pain & Gain is a gripping and intense film that explores the darker side of human nature. With its talented cast and Michael Bay's direction, the movie delivers an unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: Comet longs to be taken seriously as a full-fledged space chimp. He journeys to the fantastical Planet Malgor and bonds with the adorable alien Kilowatt, living out his ultimate fantasy. However, it's time for Comet to prove himself when the feared alien ruler Zartog takes over Mission Control! Comet must show he has the right stuff, and join fellow chimps Ham, Luna and Titan, to save the day.
tagline: Get ready to blast off on a new adventure.
title: Space Chimps 2: Zartog Strikes Back
plot:
Space Chimps 2: Zartog Strikes Back is an animated science fiction comedy film that explores several thought-provoking themes. At its core, the movie delves into the concept of identity and self-discovery, as the main character, Zartog, navigates his newfound status as a leader among his fellow chimps.

The film also touches on the idea of responsibility and power, as Zartog must confront the consequences of his actions and learn to balance his desire for control with the needs of those around him. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, often in humorous and unexpected ways.

Furthermore, Space Chimps 2: Zartog Strikes Back pokes fun at the conventions of science fiction and adventure films, using satire to comment on the genre's tropes and clichés. The movie's lighthearted tone and comedic approach make it an entertaining ride, while also inviting viewers to think critically about the themes and ideas presented.

Overall, Space Chimps 2: Zartog Strikes Back is a fun and engaging film that uses humor and wit to explore complex themes and ideas, making it a delightful watch for both children and adults.

overview: King Randolph sends for his cousin Duchess Rowena to help turn his daughters, Princess Genevieve and her 11 sisters, into better ladies. But the Duchess takes away all the sisters fun, including the sisters favorite pastime: dancing.Thinking all hope is lost they find a secret passageway to a magical land were they can dance the night away.
tagline: Enchanted dancing in a magical world!
title: Barbie in The 12 Dancing Princesses
plot:
Barbie in the 12 Dancing Princesses is a 2006 computer-animated musical fantasy film directed by Greg Richardson and written by Elana Lesser and Cliff Ruby, loosely based on the Brothers Grimm fairy tale "The Twelve Dancing Princesses." The ninth film in the Barbie series, it features Kelly Sheridan as the voice of Princess Genevieve, with Catherine O'Hara as the scheming Duchess Rowena, Christopher Gaze as King Randolph, Nicole Oliver and Lalainia Lindbjerg. Its music was composed by Arnie Roth. It premiered on Nickelodeon on 10 September 2006 and was released on DVD nine days later, the first Barbie film distributed in North America by Universal.

Genevieve is one of twelve princesses who share a passion for dancing and live in a castle with their widowed father, King Randolph. Although the girls are kind, members of the court disapprove of their lively, unconventional pastimes. The king summons his cousin, Duchess Rowena, to turn them into proper ladies, but Rowena drains the palace of color, music and joy, forbidding the sisters to dance and trying to break their spirits.

On the birthday of the youngest princesses, the others give them a copy of their late mother's favorite story, in which a princess discovers a magical land and dances there for three nights before it disappears. Studying the book and the tiles on their bedroom floor, Genevieve discovers how to open a portal to an enchanted world. The sisters enter and dance through the night, discovering that its golden flowers grant wishes, its statues come to life and its water has healing powers. The next morning, the princesses are exhausted and Rowena finds their new dancing shoes worn out, which arouses her suspicion. When King Randolph falls mysteriously ill, Genevieve asks Derek, the royal cobbler, who shares her love of dance, to investigate. Derek discovers that Rowena has been slowly poisoning the king with the help of her lackey in a scheme to seize the throne. Imprisoned and separated from their father, Genevieve and her sisters must use their courage, teamwork and the magic of the hidden land to save the king and the kingdom, while Genevieve and Derek grow closer.

The film proved popular with its young audience and is frequently cited by fans as a favorite among the Barbie films, remembered for its music, its elaborate dance sequences and Catherine O'Hara's villainous performance as Rowena.

overview: A sixteen-year-old boy insinuates himself into the house of a fellow student from his literature class and writes about it in essays for his French teacher. Faced with this gifted and unusual pupil, the teacher rediscovers his enthusiasm for his work, but the boy’s intrusion will unleash a series of uncontrollable events.
tagline: There's always a way in
title: In the House
plot:
In the House, released in France as Dans la maison, is a 2012 French comedy-drama written and directed by François Ozon, loosely adapted from Spanish playwright Juan Mayorga's play The Boy in the Last Row. Fabrice Luchini stars as literature teacher Germain Germain and Ernst Umhauer as his student Claude Garcia, with Kristin Scott Thomas as Germain's wife, Jeanne, Emmanuelle Seigner and Denis Ménochet as Esther and Raphaël Artole, and Bastien Ughetto as their son, Rapha.

Germain, a disillusioned teacher at the Lycée Gustave Flaubert, despairs of his pupils' writing until the new school year brings an essay from 16-year-old Claude describing a visit to the home of his classmate Rapha. Struck by the boy's sharp, voyeuristic eye, Germain reads it to Jeanne, who runs an art gallery, and begins tutoring Claude privately to help him develop the story. The film unfolds chapter by chapter, alternating between Claude's narrative and real life until the two become hard to tell apart.

Claude gains entry to the Artoles' house by helping Rapha with mathematics, and the visits stretch ever later into the evenings. Raised by a disabled father and never having known a real family, he is fascinated by the household and especially drawn to Esther. Germain, increasingly caught up in the story and its uncomfortable echoes of his own life, goes so far as to steal a colleague's math test so that Rapha will pass and Claude can keep visiting. As the narrative grows more transgressive, it becomes unclear how much is happening and how much Claude is inventing. He seduces Esther, wounding Rapha, who sees him as his best friend and has fallen in love with him; a draft in which Rapha hangs himself is later revised. Barred from the Artoles' home, Claude seduces Jeanne to find an ending for his story. Germain, suspended over the stolen test, confronts his wife, and she leaves him. In the final scene, teacher and student sit together on a bench, inventing stories about the people they can see in the windows of the building opposite.

In the House screened at the Toronto International Film Festival, where it won the FIPRESCI Prize, and went on to win the Golden Shell and the jury prize for best screenplay at San Sebastián. It received six César nominations, including Best Film, grossed about $18.2 million worldwide, and earned 88% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 72.

overview: Evan Birch, a family man and esteemed philosophy professor at a distinguished college, is the prime suspect when a female student goes missing.
tagline: The only truth is knowing you know nothing.
title: Spinning Man
plot:
Spinning Man is a 2018 psychological thriller directed by Simon Kaijser from a screenplay by Matthew Aldrich, adapted from George Harrar's 2003 novel. Produced by Irish DreamTime and Chimney, with Ellen S. Wander and Keith Arnold as producers, cinematography by Polly Morgan and music by Jean-Paul Wall, it stars Guy Pearce, Pierce Brosnan and Minnie Driver, with Alexandra Shipp, Clark Gregg, Odeya Rush, Jamie Kennedy, Freya Tingley, Eliza Pryor and Noah Salsbury Lipson.

Evan Birch (Pearce) is a popular, respected philosophy professor at a distinguished college, married to Ellen (Driver) and the father of two children. Beneath his polished surface, however, he has a weakness for young women: he was once driven out of another university by scandal, has had affairs with students and constantly fantasizes about women he encounters. When Joyce Bonner (Rush), a high school cheerleader, disappears near a local lake, his past dalliances lead Ellen to doubt his alibi. The meticulous detective Robert Malloy (Brosnan) begins asking questions, and Evan's indignant refusal to let him search his car, invoking the Fourth Amendment, is only the first of many red flags. Evan insists he never met the girl, yet strands of her hair are found in his impounded car, and he turns out to have arrived forty minutes late to pick up his daughter from camp on the afternoon in question. His attraction to his admiring student Anna (Shipp) and the counsel of his cynical lawyer Paul (Gregg) complicate matters. Increasingly, Evan suffers memory lapses that are never fully explained, and he begins to justify his evasions with ideas from his lectures on the philosophy of language, arguing that truth is relative. The film deliberately keeps viewers uncertain whether he is a killer, a self-deceiving liar or simply a man who no longer trusts his own memory.

The project was first announced in 2016 with Peter Flinth directing and Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, Greg Kinnear and Emma Roberts attached, but in April 2017 a new cast and director were announced, and principal photography began in May 2017. Lionsgate Premiere released the film in limited theaters and on demand on 6 April 2018. Reviews were mixed, with a 50% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 44. Variety praised Pearce's performance and Brosnan's crisp detective but felt the film's game of toying with the audience left viewers guessing without caring, while The Hollywood Reporter credited the cast as its main reason for watching.

overview: Lil and Roz are two lifelong friends, having grown up together as neighbors in an idyllic beach town. As adults, their sons have developed a friendship as strong as that which binds their mothers. One summer, all four are confronted by simmering emotions that have been mounting between them, and each find unexpected happiness in relationships that cross the bounds of convention.
title: Adore
plot:
Adore is a 2013 Australian drama film directed by Ant Toney, based on the novel of the same name by Gillian Mears.

The movie revolves around two women, Ruth (played by Naomi Watts) and Tina (played by Robin Wright), who meet at a support group for people with same-sex attraction. The story explores their complex and intense relationship, which begins as an affair but eventually evolves into a deep emotional bond.

Some of the main themes present in Adore include:

1. Unconventional love: The film portrays a non-traditional romantic relationship between two women, challenging societal norms and expectations.
2. Identity and self-discovery: Both Ruth and Tina struggle with their own identities, desires, and sense of belonging, which are intertwined as they navigate their relationship.
3. Trauma and healing: The characters' past traumas and emotional scars are slowly revealed throughout the film, highlighting the importance of confronting and overcoming these issues to form meaningful connections.
4. Motherhood and family: The movie explores the complexities of motherhood, particularly for women who choose not to conform to traditional expectations, and the challenges they face in building a sense of family and belonging.
5. Mortality and the human condition: As the story unfolds, the characters confront their own mortality, leading to introspection about the meaning and significance of life.

The film features powerful performances from its leads, Naomi Watts and Robin Wright, who bring depth and nuance to their complex characters.

overview: In a dystopian Detroit, grand houses that once housed the wealthy are now homes of the city's most-dangerous criminals. Surrounding the area is a giant wall to keep the rest of Detroit safe. For undercover cop Damien Collier, every day is a battle against corruption as he struggles to bring his father's killer, Tremaine, to justice. Meanwhile, Damien and an ex-con named Lino work together to save the city from a plot to destroy it.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
tagline: Undercover and never Outgunned
title: Brick Mansions
plot:
Brick Mansions is a 2014 American action-drama film directed by Court Gains and starring David Belle, Freida Pinto, and Malin Åkerman.

The movie takes place in the fictional neighborhood of Brick City, which is modeled after Detroit. The story follows Damien (David Belle), a young man who returns to his hometown of Paris after serving time in prison for a crime he didn't commit. Damien's sister, Leila (Freida Pinto), has been kidnapped by a powerful and ruthless gang leader named Big Wiz (Idris Elba).

Damien sets out on a mission to rescue his sister, navigating the treacherous streets of Brick City and facing off against Big Wiz's henchmen. Along the way, he meets a local woman named Lulu (Malin Åkerman), who becomes his ally in the fight against Big Wiz.

As Damien delves deeper into the world of Brick City, he discovers that Leila has been brainwashed by Big Wiz and is now working for him. Damien must use his wits and fighting skills to break through to his sister's mind and free her from Big Wiz's control.

The plot thickens as Damien uncovers a deeper conspiracy involving corruption, crime, and violence in the city. He also discovers that Lulu has a personal connection to Big Wiz, which adds an extra layer of complexity to their relationship.

As the story unfolds, Damien faces off against Big Wiz and his henchmen in a series of intense battles. The action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with plenty of martial arts moves and gunfights.

In the end, Damien is able to rescue Leila from Big Wiz's clutches and bring him down. However, the movie ends on a bittersweet note, as Damien realizes that he has lost his chance at redemption and must continue to fight for justice in Brick City.

Overall, Brick Mansions is an action-packed thrill ride with a strong performance from David Belle. The movie explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption, set against the gritty backdrop of a fictional urban landscape.

overview: U.S. marshal Britt MacMasters returns from a mission to find his father wounded and his son kidnapped by the outlaw Jed Blake. Hot on their trail, Britt forms a posse with a gunslinging deputy and a stoic Pawnee tracker. But Jed and Britt tread dangerously close to the Red Desert’s Sioux territory.
tagline: The sun never sets on vengeance.
title: Catch the Bullet
plot:
Catch the Bullet is a 2021 American Western action film directed by Michael Feifer and written by Jerry Robbins, produced by Feifer Worldwide and released by Lionsgate and Grindstone Entertainment Group. It stars Jay Pickett as U.S. Marshal Britt McMasters, Tom Skerritt as his father Dex, Mason McNulty as his son Chad, Gattlin Griffith as the outlaw Jed Blake, Callder Griffith as Deputy Clay Tucker, Cody Jones as the tracker Chaska and Peter Facinelli as Sheriff Wilkins. It was Pickett's last film, released after his death from a heart attack in July 2021, and is dedicated to him. It runs 88 minutes under the tagline "The sun never sets on vengeance."

In Buffalo, Wyoming, in the late nineteenth century, McMasters is a widowed marshal with a reputation for bringing outlaws back dead, whose long absences have left his twelve-year-old son Chad resentful and in the care of his grandfather Dex. While Britt is away for three months tracking a bank robber and his accomplices, Jed Blake, an escaped prisoner whom McMasters once sent to jail for bank robbery, rides up to the ranch with his gang looking for revenge. Finding the marshal absent, Jed shoots Dex, leaving him badly wounded on the porch, kills Chad's young friend Albert and kidnaps Chad, knowing that his father will follow. When Britt returns and learns what has happened, Sheriff Wilkins, a longtime friend, cannot join the pursuit and assigns his inexperienced deputy Clay Tucker to accompany him. Because Tucker lacks tracking skills, they enlist Chaska, a Pawnee tracker with a white missionary mother, whom the racist deputy refuses to trust. Hot on the gang's trail, the small posse follows Jed into the Red Desert and into Sioux territory, where war parties have left dead settlers in their wake, while Chad tries to escape his captors and Jed prepares to settle his old score with the marshal.

The film was released in select US cinemas and on digital platforms on 10 September 2021, and on DVD and Blu-ray days later. Reviews were mostly negative. Mark Franklin of Once Upon a Time in a Western found it not bad for a modern Western, praising the gritty performances of Pickett and Gattlin Griffith. Jim Morazzini of Nerdly gave it 2.5 out of 5, calling it predictable and flatly directed, and noting that Skerritt and Facinelli had little screen time. Carla Hay of Culture Mix dismissed it as an amateurish dud with cringeworthy dialogue.

overview: Princess Leia is captured and held hostage by the evil Imperial forces in their effort to take over the galactic Empire. Venturesome Luke Skywalker and dashing captain Han Solo team together with the loveable robot duo R2-D2 and C-3PO to rescue the beautiful princess and restore peace and justice in the Empire.
tagline: A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away...
title: Star Wars
plot:
Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope is a groundbreaking science fiction film written and directed by George Lucas, released on May 25, 1977, by Lucasfilm Ltd.

In a distant galaxy, the evil Galactic Empire, led by Darth Vader, has taken over the planet of Alderaan. Princess Leia Organa, a leader in the Rebel Alliance, possesses the stolen Death Star plans, which could lead to the downfall of the Empire. She hides the plans in the droid R2-D2, who escapes with C-3PO, a protocol droid.

The film begins on the desert planet Tatooine, where we meet our hero, Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), a young farm boy who dreams of adventure beyond his desert home. Luke's life changes when he encounters Obi-Wan Kenobi, an old Jedi Knight who reveals that Luke's father was a Jedi and that he himself is strong in the Force.

Obi-Wan gives Luke his father's lightsaber and begins to teach him about the Force, a metaphysical energy that binds the galaxy together. They are pursued by Darth Vader and his stormtroopers, who are searching for the stolen Death Star plans.

Luke, Obi-Wan, and their new allies, Han Solo (Harrison Ford) and Chewbacca, join the Rebel Alliance to rescue Leia from the Empire's clutches. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including navigating through an asteroid field and avoiding Imperial TIE fighters.

As they journey to the Rebel base on Yavin 4, Luke begins to understand his connection to the Force and trains with Obi-Wan to harness its power. Meanwhile, Han Solo and Chewbacca form a bond as they navigate their roles in the Rebel Alliance.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Rebel Alliance and the Galactic Empire. Luke, with the help of his new friends, uses the Force to guide his proton torpedoes into the Death Star's vulnerable exhaust port, leading to its destruction.

In the aftermath, Luke, Han, Leia, Chewbacca, C-3PO, and R2-D2 are celebrated as heroes by the Rebel Alliance. Obi-Wan sacrifices himself to save Luke from Darth Vader, who reveals that he is actually Anakin Skywalker, Luke's father. The film concludes with Luke, now a confident Jedi, setting out on his journey to confront the Empire and restore balance to the Force.

Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope was a game-changer in the science fiction genre, introducing iconic characters, worlds, and themes that have become synonymous with popular culture. Its influence can still be felt today, inspiring countless fans around the world.

overview: After crossing the border illegally for work, Miguel, a hard-working father and devoted husband, finds himself wrongfully accused of murdering a former sheriff’s wife. After learning of his imprisonment, Miguel’s pregnant wife tries to come to his aid and lands in the hands of corrupt coyotes who hold her for ransom. Dissatisfied with the police department’s investigation, the former sheriff tries to uncover the truth about his wife’s death and discovers disturbing evidence that will destroy one family’s future, or tear another’s apart.
tagline: Truth is the only justice.
title: Frontera
plot:
Frontera is a 2014 American drama film directed by Peter Mullan. The movie revolves around an elderly widow, Adela (played by Demián Bichir's character's mother, but actually played by actress Salma Hayek's character's mother), who embarks on a journey to find her son after he goes missing in the Mexican desert.

The main theme of Frontera is the unyielding power of love and family bonds. Adela's relentless pursuit of her son is driven by her unwavering devotion to him, which becomes an all-consuming force that propels her forward despite the harsh realities she faces on her journey. As she traverses the unforgiving desert landscape, Adela's determination is tested by the cruel conditions and her own mortality.

Throughout the film, Frontera explores the complexities of human relationships, particularly the intricate web of love, loyalty, and sacrifice that exists between family members. The movie delves into themes of identity, belonging, and the search for meaning in a seemingly meaningless world. Adela's journey is also a metaphor for the human spirit's capacity to persevere in the face of adversity, even when all hope seems lost.

Ultimately, Frontera is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that celebrates the resilience of the human heart and the transformative power of love.

overview: A lowly stable elf finds that he is the only one who can stop an invasion of the North Pole by using the secret of Santa's Sleigh, a TimeGlobe, to travel back in time to Save Santa - twice.
tagline: Adventures of a time traveling elf
title: Saving Santa
plot:
Saving Santa is a 2013 British animated Christmas musical comedy created and written by Tony Nottage and directed by Leon Joosen, produced by Nottage, Terry Stone and Nick Simunek. Martin Freeman voices Bernard, a lowly elf who works in Santa's stables, with Tim Curry as the villainous businessman Neville Baddington, Tim Conway as Santa Claus, Pam Ferris and Ashley Tisdale. It was released direct-to-video in November 2013.

At the North Pole, Bernard is a cheerful but clumsy elf whose job is mucking out the reindeer stables. He dreams of doing something more important and longs for the respect of his fellow elves, who regard him as a well-meaning nobody, but his chance to prove himself seems unlikely ever to come. Few people know how Santa manages to deliver presents to every child in the world in a single night; the secret lies in Santa's sleigh, which contains a magical TimeGlobe that allows it to travel through time.

Neville Baddington, a ruthless tycoon who heads a powerful corporation, becomes obsessed with discovering the location of Santa's workshop and the secret behind Santa's deliveries, so that he can exploit them for profit. When he and his private army invade the North Pole and capture Santa, Bernard, who is the only one to have discovered the secret of the sleigh, finds himself the only one able to stop them. Using the TimeGlobe, he travels back in time to warn everyone and prevent the invasion, but his efforts do not go as planned, and he is forced to go back a second time, encountering earlier versions of himself and complicating events further. With the help of his friends and his own ingenuity, Bernard must outwit Baddington, rescue Santa and save Christmas for children everywhere, proving to the other elves that even the humblest worker can be a hero.

Saving Santa received mixed to negative reviews, with a 17 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on six reviews. Critics praised the voice cast, particularly Freeman and Curry, but found the animation and story unremarkable compared with major studio holiday films.

overview: An American backpacker gets involved with a ring of drug smugglers as their driver, and winds up on the run from his employers across Cologne’s autobahns.
title: Collide
plot:
Collide is a 2016 action thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions. The movie follows a young American backpacker, Brian, who becomes embroiled in a complex web of crime and deception while traveling through Eastern Europe.

At its core, Collide explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships with others. Brian's character, in particular, is a study in contrasts - he is both naive and resourceful, vulnerable and resilient. As the story unfolds, his sense of self is constantly tested and challenged, leading to a profound exploration of what it means to be human.

The film also examines the theme of morality and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong. The characters in Collide are multidimensional and often flawed, making it difficult for the audience to distinguish between good and evil. This moral ambiguity serves as a commentary on how our perceptions of others can be skewed by circumstance and our own biases.

Furthermore, Collide touches on the theme of loneliness and disconnection in modern society. The characters in the film are all outsiders in their own way, struggling to form meaningful connections with others. This sense of isolation is palpable throughout the movie, adding to the overall sense of tension and unease.

Overall, Collide is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes and ideas through its intricate plot and well-developed characters.

overview: A team of Arctic geologists stumble across an abandoned laboratory in which the Nazis developed an incredible and brutal secret weapon during the final months of WW2. Deep in the ice, they accidentally awake a deadly army of flying zombie sharks ridden by genetically mutated, undead super-humans, who are unleashed into the skies, wreaking their bloodthirsty revenge on any aircraft that takes to the air. An elite task force is assembled to take on this deadly threat and stop the Sky Sharks from conquering the air, but as time runs out, the task force realises they will have to fight fire with fire, and the stage is set for the greatest flying super-mutant zombie shark air battle the world has ever seen....
tagline: In a shark no one can hear you scream.
title: Sky Sharks
plot:
Sky Sharks is a 2020 German science fiction comedy horror film directed by Marc Fehse. Deliberately conceived as an over-the-top B-movie, it features an international cast of genre performers including Thomas Morris, Barbara Nedeljakova, Eva Habermann, Michaela Schaffrath, Tony Todd, Robert LaSardo, Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa, Lynn Lowry, Lar Park Lincoln and Nick Principe. The production was partly financed through a Kickstarter campaign launched in 2015, and after years of work on its visual effects, it was released in 2020, screening at genre festivals including London's FrightFest.

During an expedition in the polar ice, a team of geologists accidentally uncovers a secret Nazi laboratory from the Second World War, hidden for decades deep beneath the ice. Inside lies a terrifying secret weapon developed in the final years of the war: an army of genetically modified flying sharks, ridden by superhuman undead Nazi soldiers who were created through monstrous experiments. When the long-dormant creatures are awakened, they take to the skies, attacking aircraft and slaughtering everyone in their path, threatening to unleash destruction on the modern world.
