The film also touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, both positive and negative. As the protagonist navigates her past and present, she is forced to confront aspects of herself that she had previously suppressed or denied, leading to a deeper understanding of who she is and where she comes from.

Overall, Come True is a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, tackling complex themes with sensitivity and nuance.

overview: A cover-up that spanned four U.S. Presidents pushed the country's first female newspaper publisher and a hard-driving editor to join an unprecedented battle between journalist and government. Inspired by true events.
tagline: Truth be told
title: The Post
plot:
The Post is a 2017 American historical political thriller directed and produced by Steven Spielberg and written by Liz Hannah and Josh Singer. Meryl Streep stars as Katharine Graham, publisher of The Washington Post, and Tom Hanks as its executive editor, Ben Bradlee, with Sarah Paulson, Bob Odenkirk, Tracy Letts, Bradley Whitford, Bruce Greenwood, Carrie Coon, Alison Brie and Matthew Rhys. Set in 1971, it depicts the newspaper's struggle to publish the Pentagon Papers, classified documents about the American government's involvement in the Vietnam War.

In 1966, the State Department analyst Daniel Ellsberg accompanies American troops in Vietnam and concludes that the war is unwinnable. Secretary of Defense Robert McNamara privately agrees but publicly continues to justify sending more troops, leaving Ellsberg disillusioned. Later, working at the RAND Corporation, Ellsberg secretly copies thousands of pages of a classified study documenting decades of American involvement in Vietnam, going back to the Truman administration, and leaks them to Neil Sheehan of The New York Times.

In 1971, Katharine Graham has run the Post for eight years, since the suicide of her husband, Phil, who had taken over the paper from her father. Often underestimated by the men around her, she is preparing to take the company public to secure its future, while Bradlee pushes to make the Post a national paper able to compete with the Times. When the Times begins publishing stories based on the leaked study, the Nixon administration obtains a court injunction to stop it. Post editor Ben Bagdikian tracks down Ellsberg and obtains the papers. Bradlee and his reporters race to prepare their own story, but the company's lawyers and board warn that publication could jeopardize the stock offering and expose Graham and Bradlee to criminal prosecution. Graham, torn by her friendship with McNamara and the risk to her family's legacy, must make the decision whether to publish, leading to a battle that reaches the Supreme Court.

The Post received widespread acclaim, with praise for Streep's and Hanks's performances and its timely defense of press freedom. It grossed about $180 million worldwide and received Academy Award nominations for Best Picture and Best Actress for Streep.

overview: Kai—an outcast—joins Oishi, the leader of 47 outcast samurai.  Together they seek vengeance upon the treacherous overlord who killed their master and banished their kind.  To restore honour to their homeland, the warriors embark upon a quest that challenges them with a series of trials that would destroy ordinary warriors.
tagline: For courage. For loyalty. For honor.
title: 47 Ronin
plot:
47 Ronin is a 2013 American fantasy action film directed by Carl Rinsch, his only theatrical feature, and written by Chris Morgan and Hossein Amini from a story by Morgan and Walter Hamada. It is a fantastical reimagining of Chūshingura, the story of the forty-seven ronin, real masterless samurai of 18th-century Japan who avenged the death of their lord, Asano Naganori, by killing his rival, Kira Yoshinaka. Keanu Reeves stars as Kai, a half-English, half-Japanese outcast, with Hiroyuki Sanada as Oishi, Tadanobu Asano as Lord Kira, Rinko Kikuchi as the witch Mizuki and Kou Shibasaki as Mika. Universal Pictures released it in December 2013.

Kai, found as a boy in a forest, is taken in by Lord Asano, the benevolent ruler of the Akō domain. He and Asano's daughter, Mika, fall in love, despite the contempt of Asano's samurai for Kai's mixed ancestry. Lord Kira, the shogun's master of ceremonies, plots to seize Akō with the help of Mizuki, a shape-shifting witch. During a hunt, a monstrous creature attacks Asano's party, and Kai kills it. When Shogun Tsunayoshi visits Akō, Kai recognizes one of Kira's concubines as the witch, but the chief counselor, Oishi, ignores his warning.

At a tournament for the shogun's entertainment, Kira's champion, a giant armored warrior, is pitted against Asano's chosen samurai, whom Mizuki incapacitates with magic. Kai fights in his place but is unmasked and beaten. That night, Mizuki bewitches Asano into attacking the unarmed Kira, and Asano is ordered to commit ritual suicide. His samurai are made ronin, forbidden to seek revenge, while Kai is sold into slavery and Mika is given a year to mourn before she must marry Kira. A year later, Oishi, released from imprisonment, gathers the scattered ronin and frees Kai, and together they seek weapons from mysterious forest demons who raised Kai, and plan to infiltrate Kira's castle during the wedding to avenge their lord, knowing that their act of loyalty will cost them their lives.

47 Ronin received negative reviews, with critics finding its fantasy elements at odds with the classic story and its characters underdeveloped, though the visuals and Sanada's performance were praised. It was a major box-office failure, grossing about $151 million worldwide against a budget estimated at over $175 million.

overview: A woman’s life is upended when an engagement ring meant for someone else leads her to the person she’s meant to be with.
title: Something from Tiffany's
plot:
Something from Tiffany's is a 2022 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Gillian Robespierre, written by Emily Halpern and Sarah Haskins, and produced by Amazon Studios.

The movie follows the story of Jill Newman (played by Zoey Deutch), a young woman who has just been fired from her job as an editor at a publishing company. Feeling lost and uncertain about her future, Jill returns to her hometown in New Jersey after being away for several years.

Upon her return, Jill is forced to confront her complicated past and the choices she made that led her to where she is today. She also reconnects with her high school best friend, Kate (played by Gigi Hadid), who has become a successful businesswoman.

As Jill navigates her way through this new chapter in her life, she meets a charming and handsome stranger named Max (played by Pierce Brosnan) at Tiffany & Co., where he is buying a ring for his girlfriend. Despite their instant attraction, Jill is hesitant to get involved with someone new, fearing that it will distract her from finding herself.

Throughout the film, Jill's journey is interwoven with flashbacks of her past relationships and experiences, which provide insight into her character development and growth. The movie explores themes of identity, love, and self-discovery, as Jill learns to let go of her fears and take control of her life.

The title "Something from Tiffany's" refers to a phrase that Max tells Jill, suggesting that sometimes the best things in life come from unexpected places. As Jill navigates her way through this new chapter, she begins to realize that this phrase holds true for her as well.

Overall, Something from Tiffany's is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of identity, love, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and relatable protagonist, the movie is sure to resonate with audiences looking for a feel-good romantic comedy-drama.

overview: Zed and Addison are back at Seabrook High, where, after a groundbreaking semester, they continue to steer both their school and community toward unity. But the arrival of a new group of outsiders – mysterious werewolves – threatens to shake up the newfound peace and causes a rift in Zed and Addison’s budding romance.
tagline: There's a new pack in town
title: Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 2
plot:
Zombies 2, styled Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 2, is a 2020 American musical comedy Disney Channel Original Movie that premiered on February 14, 2020. Directed by Paul Hoen from a script by David Light and Joseph Raso, it is the sequel to Zombies (2018). Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly return as the zombie Zed and the cheerleader Addison, with Trevor Tordjman, Kylee Russell and Carla Jeffery reprising their roles and Chandler Kinney, Pearce Joza and Ariel Martin joining as a pack of werewolves.

A prologue shows the settlers who founded Seabrook battling werewolves for a powerful glowing artifact later called the moonstone. In the present, the zombies have been accepted into town life. Zed plans to invite Addison to Prawn, Seabrook's version of the prom, while Addison hopes to become cheer captain after Bucky, her self-absorbed cousin, quits to run for class president. When the cheer squad's bus passes through the forbidden forest, they spot werewolves, and the mayor responds by reviving the anti-monster laws, which bar zombies from Prawn. Zed decides to run for president himself so he can take Addison to the dance.

The werewolves, whose moonstone necklaces are losing their power, believe a prophecy that a white-haired girl, the Great Alpha, will lead them to the moonstone itself, and they enrol at Seabrook to find Addison. Wyatt, brother of the pack leader Willa, invites Addison to their den and offers her a fully charged necklace that will transform her if she is truly one of them. They also reveal that the planned demolition of the Seabrook Power plant will destroy the moonstone buried beneath it. A jealous Zed steals the necklace; its energy shorts out his Z-Band during the election debate, turning him fully zombie and costing him the vote. The werewolves are arrested trying to stop the demolition, and when Zed confesses, Addison puts on the necklace and discovers she is not a werewolf. The plant is destroyed anyway, but on Prawn night, as the monsters crash the dance and Zed and Addison reconcile, the ground splits open to reveal the intact moonstone. Zed removes his Z-Band and uses his strength to move a boulder so it can be recovered, and he and Addison share their first kiss. Finally, a blue meteor falls from the moon and makes Addison's hair glow.

Filmed around Toronto in 2019, the movie drew 2.46 million viewers on its premiere, outperforming the original among adults aged 18 to 49. Critics praised its message of tolerance, and it was followed by Zombies 3.

overview: Two penniless orphans, Black and White, struggle to survive on the mean streets of Treasure Town. When a megacorporation threatens to tear down the town to build an amusement park, Black and White engage in the fight of their life.
title: Tekkonkinkreet
plot:
Tekkonkinkreet (鉄コン筋クリート, Tekkon Kinkurīto) is a 2006 Japanese animated action drama directed by Michael Arias and produced by Studio 4°C, adapted from Taiyō Matsumoto's manga of the same name, which was serialised in Big Comic Spirits in 1993–94 and also published in English as Black & White. The title is a childish mispronunciation of the Japanese word for reinforced concrete. Anthony Weintraub wrote the screenplay, Hiroaki Ando served as co-director, and the film was produced with Aniplex, Asmik Ace and Shogakukan.

The story is set in Treasure Town, a sprawling, ageing city of alleys and rooftops that is changing fast under pressure from the yakuza and outside speculators. Two orphaned boys, the hardened, violent Black and the dreamy, childlike White, live there as street kids who treat the town as their own territory and defend it against all comers, while dreaming of a house by the sea. Their world is upended when a ruthless outsider known as the Snake arrives with plans to tear down the old neighbourhood and replace it with a vast amusement park, backed by three uncanny, seemingly unstoppable assassins. Under this pressure the brothers are separated: White is taken into the care of two police detectives, while Black, cut off from the one person who anchors him, sinks deeper into violence and confronts a darker side of himself embodied by a figure called the Minotaur. In the end it is the bond between the brothers that pulls him back.

The Japanese voice cast is led by Kazunari Ninomiya as Black and Yū Aoi as White, with Yūsuke Iseya as the yakuza Kimura, Kankurō Kudō and Min Tanaka, who voices the old gangster known as the Rat, and Masahiro Motoki as the Snake. The score is by the British electronic duo Plaid, with a closing song by Asian Kung-Fu Generation.

Arias, an American who had worked as a producer on The Animatrix, had first developed the project in 1999 with a computer-animated pilot made with Koji Morimoto, and the feature became one of the first major Japanese animated films directed by a non-Japanese filmmaker. It premiered at the Tokyo International Film Festival on 21 October 2006 and opened in Japanese cinemas that December. Critics were generally favourable, and the film won the Ōfuji Noburō Award at the Mainichi Film Awards and the Japan Academy Prize for Animation of the Year.

overview: Peter Parker is unmasked and no longer able to separate his normal life from the high-stakes of being a super-hero. When he asks for help from Doctor Strange the stakes become even more dangerous, forcing him to discover what it truly means to be Spider-Man.
tagline: The Multiverse unleashed.
title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
plot:
Spider-Man: No Way Home is a 2021 superhero film directed by Jon Watts, produced by Marvel Studios and Columbia Pictures.

The movie takes place after the events of Spider-Man: Far From Home. Peter Parker (Tom Holland) is struggling to balance his life as a superhero with his personal relationships. He confides in Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), who reveals that there's a way to make the world forget about Spider-Man, erasing him from existence.

However, this plan goes awry when Mysterio (Jake Gyllenhaal) appears and steals the spellbook, causing multiple universes to merge into our own. This leads to various villains from different universes, including Doctor Octopus (Alfred Molina), Electro (Jamie Foxx), Sandman (Thomas Haden Church), Lizard (Rhys Ifans), and Green Goblin (Willem Dafoe), entering our world.

As Spider-Man tries to stop these villains, he also attracts the attention of Norman Osborn's (Willem Dafoe) alternate universe version, who seeks revenge against Peter for killing his son. The web-slinger must navigate this multiverse chaos while dealing with personal relationships and the consequences of his actions.

Throughout the film, Spider-Man teams up with Doctor Strange to find a way to send these villains back to their respective universes. Along the way, he also reconnects with his friends MJ (Zendaya) and Ned (Jacob Batalon), who help him cope with the stress of being a superhero.

The movie features an impressive cast, including Benedict Cumberbatch, Alfred Molina, Willem Dafoe, and Jamie Foxx, among others. The film's climax features an epic battle between Spider-Man and his enemies from different universes.

Overall, Spider-Man: No Way Home is a thrilling adventure that explores the complexities of identity, friendship, and the consequences of playing with the fabric of reality. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning visual effects, this movie is a must-watch for fans of the Spider-Man franchise and superhero enthusiasts alike.

overview: Battle-hardened O’Hara leads a lively mercenary team of soldiers on a daring mission: rescue hostages from their captors in remote Africa. But as the mission goes awry and the team is stranded, O’Hara’s squad must face a bloody, brutal encounter with a gang of rebels.
tagline: When the hunter becomes the prey.
title: Rogue
plot:
Rogue is a 2020 American action thriller film directed by Jeremy Saulnier and starring Ana de Armas, Margot Robbie, and Christopher Abbott.

The main themes of Rogue (2020) include:

1. **Survival and Self-Reliance**: The movie explores the theme of survival in a post-apocalyptic world where women are forced to fend for themselves after a catastrophic event wipes out most of humanity. The protagonist, Georgia "Rogue" Hudson (Ana de Armas), must rely on her wits, strength, and resourcefulness to survive.
2. **Feminism and Empowerment**: Rogue is a feminist film that celebrates the strength and resilience of women in a patriarchal society. The movie features a cast of strong female characters who take charge of their own lives and destinies, challenging traditional notions of femininity and power.
3. **Trauma and PTSD**: The film explores the psychological effects of trauma on its characters, particularly Georgia, who has experienced unimaginable horrors in her past. The movie delves into the complexities of PTSD and how it can shape a person's identity and behavior.
4. **Human Connection and Community**: Despite the harsh environment, Rogue highlights the importance of human connection and community. The film shows how women come together to support each other and form strong bonds, which becomes crucial for their survival.

Overall, Rogue (2020) is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores themes of survival, feminism, trauma, and human connection in a post-apocalyptic world.

overview: A woman wakes in a cryogenic chamber with no recollection of how she got there, and must find a way out before running out of air.
tagline: No escape. No memory. 90 min to live.
title: Oxygen
plot:
Oxygen is a 2021 French thriller film directed by Alexandre Moors and written by Juliette Grandet. The movie follows the story of Hana, a pregnant woman who wakes up in a sealed room with no memory of how she got there.

The main themes of Oxygen include:

1. **Survival and Resilience**: Hana's primary goal is to survive and find a way out of the room, which serves as a metaphor for the human spirit's ability to persevere in the face of adversity.
2. **Motherhood and Protection**: As Hana navigates her confinement, she becomes increasingly desperate to protect herself and her unborn child from the unknown forces that are holding her captive.
3. **Psychological Trauma and Memory Loss**: The film explores the psychological effects of trauma on Hana's memory and identity, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of her imagination.
4. **Isolation and Confinement**: The sealed room serves as a symbol of isolation, highlighting the themes of confinement and the loss of freedom that can occur in life.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a tense and suspenseful narrative that keeps the audience on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Havana, Cuba, 1990. René González, an airplane pilot, unexpectedly flees the country, leaving behind his wife Olga and his daughter Irma, and begins a new life in Miami, where he becomes a member of an anti-Castro organization.
tagline: Traitors or heroes?
title: Wasp Network
plot:
Wasp Network is a biographical drama film that tells the story of María Belón, a Cuban exile who became a key figure in the CIA's plots to assassinate Fidel Castro. The movie delves into themes of politics, loyalty, and personal identity.

At its core, Wasp Network explores the complexities of being caught between two worlds: Cuba and the United States. María Belón is torn between her love for her homeland and her desire to fight against the communist regime that has taken over. This internal conflict drives the narrative, as she navigates the moral gray areas of espionage and counter-revolution.

The film also examines the theme of female empowerment in a male-dominated world. María Belón is a strong-willed woman who refuses to be defined by her circumstances. She takes charge of her own destiny, using her intelligence and wit to outmaneuver those around her.

Furthermore, Wasp Network touches on the idea of identity and belonging. As a Cuban exile living in the United States, María Belón struggles to find her place in both cultures. Her experiences serve as a microcosm for the larger themes of displacement and dislocation that are prevalent in contemporary society.

Overall, Wasp Network is a thought-provoking film that sheds light on a fascinating chapter in modern history. Through its portrayal of María Belón's story, it raises important questions about politics, loyalty, and personal identity, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values and beliefs.

overview: Barbie stars as Blair Willows, a kind-hearted girl who is chosen to attend Princess Charm School: a magical, modern place that teaches dancing, how to have tea parties, and proper princess manners. Blair loves her classes -- as well as the helpful magical sprites and her new friends, Princesses Hadley and Isla. But when royal teacher Dame Devin discovers that Blair looks a lot like the kingdom’s missing princess, she turns Blair’s world upside down to stop her from claiming the throne. Now Blair, Hadley and Delancy must find an enchanted crown to prove Blair’s true identity in this charming and magical princess story!
title: Barbie: Princess Charm School
plot:
Barbie: Princess Charm School is a 2011 computer-animated fantasy film directed by Zeke Norton and written by Elise Allen, produced by Mattel Entertainment under the Barbie Entertainment name together with Rainmaker Entertainment. The twentieth installment in the Barbie film series, it was released on DVD on September 13, 2011, and made its television debut on Nickelodeon two months later. Barbie stars as Blair Willows, an ordinary girl who discovers a hidden royal destiny.

In the kingdom of Gardania, teenage Blair works as a waitress in a small café to help support her adoptive mother and her younger sister, Emily. One day she learns from a television broadcast that she has won the lottery for a scholarship to Princess Charm School, a magical academy where princesses from many kingdoms are educated and where commoners can train as Lady Royals, the advisors to princesses. Emily confesses that she entered Blair's name many times, and their mother encourages her to seize the opportunity.

At the school, Blair is welcomed by a golden retriever named Prince and Headmistress Privet, and is assigned a fairy assistant called Grace. She befriends her roommates, Princess Isla, who mixes electronic music, and the sporty Princess Hadley. She also meets the haughty Dame Devin, sister-in-law of the late queen, and her daughter Delancy, who is due to be crowned ruler of Gardania at graduation. Clumsy and struggling in her classes, Blair improves with the headmistress's help despite repeated sabotage by Devin and Delancy. Exploring the palace, the girls notice Blair's striking resemblance to the late Queen Isabella and come to suspect that she may be the long-lost Princess Sophia, believed to have died with the royal family. Determined to find the legendary crown that glows only for the true heir, Blair and her friends must outwit Dame Devin before the coronation.

The film is a lighthearted fairy tale about friendship, kindness and self-confidence, emphasizing that true royalty comes from character.

Like other entries in the long-running series, Princess Charm School was made for a young audience and distributed primarily on home video, following its DVD debut in September 2011 with a Nickelodeon broadcast that November.

original_title: ワンピース 珍獣島のチョッパー王国
overview: As the Straw Hat Pirates sail through the Grand Line.A line of geysers erupted from under the Going Merry. And the whole crew find themselves flying over the island. Unfortunatly, Chopper fell off the ship and was separated from his friends. Luffy and the others landed on the other side of the island. Chopper meanwhile finds himself being worshiped as the island's new king by the animals. To make matters worse, a trio of human "horn" hunters are on the island. The leader, Count Butler is a violin playing/horn eating human who wants to eat the island's treasure to inherit immense power. Will Luffy & the rest be able to prevent the count from terrorizing the island? And will they be able to convince Momambi that not all pirates are bad?
tagline: Tony T. Chopper, the new Animal King!
title: One Piece: Chopper's Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals
plot:
One Piece: Chopper's Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals is a 2002 Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series "One Piece" created by Eiichiro Oda. The movie follows the story of Chopper, also known as Usopp's friend and doctor, who gets lost in the Amazon jungle while searching for a rare plant to cure his friends.

The main themes of One Piece: Chopper's Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals include:

1. Friendship and camaraderie: The film highlights the strong bond between Chopper and his friends, particularly Usopp, Sanji, and Nami. Their friendship is put to the test as they work together to rescue Chopper from the jungle.
2. Exploration and discovery: The movie showcases the wonders of the Amazon rainforest, introducing viewers to exotic animals and plants that are native to the region. This theme emphasizes the importance of exploration and discovery in understanding the natural world.
3. Bravery and selflessness: Chopper's journey is marked by his bravery and willingness to risk himself to save his friends. His actions demonstrate the value of putting others before oneself and being willing to make sacrifices for the greater good.

The movie also explores some of the lighter themes, such as:

1. Humor and comedy: The film features many comedic moments, particularly courtesy of Usopp's antics and Sanji's culinary mishaps.
2. Adventure and excitement: The movie is full of action-packed sequences, including a thrilling chase scene through the jungle.

Overall, One Piece: Chopper's Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals is an entertaining and heartwarming film that celebrates the power of friendship and exploration.

overview: An alliance of evil-doers, led by Frieda, looks to take over Fairy Tale Land. But when Ella realizes her stepmother is out to ruin her storybook existence, she takes a dramatic turn and blossoms into the leader of the resistance effort.
tagline: Fairy Tale Endings Aren't What They Used To Be.
title: Happily N'Ever After
plot:
Happily N'Ever After is a 2007 American computer-animated comedy film produced by Lionsgate. The movie follows the story of Goldilocks, who breaks into the Three Bears' house and causes chaos in their lives.

The main themes of Happily N'Ever After include:

1. **Rebellion against authority**: Goldilocks, the protagonist, is a free-spirited and independent character who rejects the traditional roles and expectations imposed upon her by society. She takes matters into her own hands and challenges the authority of the Three Bears, leading to a series of comedic misunderstandings.
2. **Self-discovery**: Throughout the movie, Goldilocks learns more about herself and her place in the world. She discovers that she is not just a curious and mischievous child, but also a strong-willed and determined individual who can make her own choices.
3. **Family dynamics**: The Three Bears' family relationships are central to the story. The movie explores the complexities of sibling rivalry, parental expectations, and the challenges of maintaining harmony within a family.
4. **Social commentary**: Happily N'Ever After pokes fun at traditional fairy tale tropes and societal norms. The film's use of satire and parody allows it to comment on issues like conformity, obedience, and the constraints placed on individuals by society.

The movie features a blend of humor, action, and heart, making it an entertaining and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

original_title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
overview: When Clara’s mother leaves her a mysterious gift, she embarks on a journey to four secret realms—where she discovers her greatest strength could change the world.
tagline: Let the mystery unfold.
title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
plot:
The Nutcracker and the Four Realms is a 2018 American Christmas fantasy film directed by Lasse Hallström and Joe Johnston from a screenplay by Ashleigh Powell, retelling E. T. A. Hoffmann's 1816 tale The Nutcracker and the Mouse King and Tchaikovsky's 1892 ballet. It stars Mackenzie Foy as Clara Stahlbaum, Keira Knightley as the Sugar Plum Fairy, Jayden Fowora-Knight as Captain Philip Hoffman, Helen Mirren as Mother Ginger and Morgan Freeman as Drosselmeyer, with Eugenio Derbez, Matthew Macfadyen, Richard E. Grant and Misty Copeland. Johnston directed a month of reshoots after Hallström's principal photography at Pinewood Studios.

On Christmas Eve in Victorian London, Clara receives a locked egg-shaped box left to her by her late mother, Marie, with a note saying that everything she needs is inside. At the party of her godfather, the engineer Drosselmeyer, she follows a string bearing her name into a parallel world, where a mouse steals the key. With the help of Captain Philip, a nutcracker soldier, she reaches a palace and meets the regents of three realms: the Sugar Plum Fairy of the Land of Sweets, Shiver of the Land of Snowflakes and Hawthorne of the Land of Flowers, who say they are at war with Mother Ginger and the Fourth Realm. Clara learns that Marie created this world and was its queen, making Clara a princess, and that a machine Marie used to bring toys to life could defend the realms if activated with the key.

Clara and Philip retrieve the key from Mother Ginger, ignoring her warning, but the egg turns out to be a music box. The Sugar Plum Fairy then reveals her treachery: resentful at feeling abandoned by Marie, she uses the machine to create an army of toy soldiers to conquer all four realms and imprisons Clara and her allies. Finding a mirror inside the music box, Clara realizes she needed only herself. She escapes, wins Mother Ginger's help and reverses the machine, turning the Sugar Plum Fairy back into a doll. Clara returns to London, reconciles with her father and dances with him to the music box, which plays the first song he and Marie danced to.

Released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures in November 2018, the film grossed $174 million worldwide but was a box office flop, with an estimated loss of $75-90 million. Critics found it lovely to look at but hollow, and it received 32% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Eccentric consulting detective Sherlock Holmes and Doctor John Watson battle to bring down a new nemesis and unravel a deadly plot that could destroy England.
tagline: Nothing escapes him.
title: Sherlock Holmes
plot:
Sherlock Holmes is a 2009 action mystery film directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Robert Downey Jr. as the iconic detective Sherlock Holmes and Jude Law as his trusted sidekick Dr. John Watson.

The film begins with a prologue set in 1891, where we see a young Sherlock Holmes (Eddie Marsan) being bullied at school due to his exceptional intelligence. He is eventually befriended by Mycroft Holmes (Jude Law), who recognizes his exceptional abilities and encourages him to use them for the greater good.

The story then jumps forward to 1895, where we meet Dr. John Watson (Jude Law), a veteran of the British Army who has just returned from Afghanistan. He is struggling to find purpose in his life until he meets Sherlock Holmes (Robert Downey Jr.), who is now a consulting detective in London.

The two men form an unlikely partnership, with Watson serving as both Holmes' biographer and partner in crime-solving. Their first case together involves a mysterious murder at Reichenbach Falls, where they encounter the villainous Lord Blackwood (Mark Strong).

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Holmes and Watson uncover a sinister plot by Blackwood to use a deadly gas to kill thousands of people in London. Along the way, they must navigate a complex web of clues, red herrings, and double-crosses.

Throughout the film, Ritchie's signature fast-paced dialogue and witty banter are on full display, as Holmes and Watson engage in clever repartee and intellectual sparring matches. Downey Jr.'s portrayal of Holmes is particularly notable, capturing the character's eccentricities and intensity with remarkable accuracy.

As the story unfolds, Holmes and Watson must use all their skills and resources to stay one step ahead of Blackwood and his accomplices. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with a memorable showdown between Holmes and Blackwood at Reichenbach Falls.

In the end, Holmes and Watson succeed in stopping Blackwood's plot, but not before he reveals that he has been working for a larger organization known as the "Shadow." The film concludes with Holmes and Watson reflecting on their adventure, while also hinting at future cases to come.

Overall, Sherlock Holmes is a fun and engaging adaptation of the classic characters, with Ritchie's unique style and Downey Jr.'s energetic performance bringing new life to the iconic detective.

overview: A couple fights to hold their relationship together as a memory loss virus spreads and threatens to erase the history of their love and courtship.
tagline: Love is unforgettable.
title: Little Fish
plot:
Little Fish is a 2020 American science fiction romantic drama film directed by Chad Hartigan and written by Mattson Tomlin, based on Aja Gabel's 2011 short story of the same name; Tomlin's script had appeared on the 2018 Black List of the best unproduced screenplays. It stars Olivia Cooke, Jack O'Connell, Raúl Castillo and Soko. Produced under the Black Bear Pictures, Automatik, Tango Entertainment and Oddfellows Entertainment banners, with Cooke among the executive producers, it was shot in British Columbia from March to April 2019, with music by Keegan DeWitt.

A pandemic of NIA, a neuroinflammatory affliction that erodes people's memories, is spreading rapidly around the world, sometimes slowly picking away at recollections and sometimes wiping out years in an instant. In Seattle, Emma (Cooke), whose work brings her face to face with pets abandoned by owners who have forgotten them, and her husband Jude (O'Connell), a photographer, have been married for barely a year. Narrated by Emma, who records the memories of their relationship in an attempt to preserve them, the film moves back and forth through their courtship. The couple see the disease's toll on their friends Ben (Castillo), a musician who forgets his own music and then fails to recognise his girlfriend Samantha (Soko), who eventually leaves him. When Jude begins to show symptoms, Emma enrols him in an experimental clinical trial, but he is rejected after testing positive for cocaine taken with an old friend, a lapse he can no longer remember. Their attempt to carry out the experimental procedure themselves fails, and Jude begins to wake up not knowing who Emma is, relying on labelled photographs on the walls. As the couple fight to hold on to the history of their love, Emma realises that she too is beginning to lose her memories.

Little Fish was due to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2020, but the festival was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic; the film was instead made available online to festival participants and later shown at the Newport Beach Film Festival. IFC Films acquired North American rights and released it in theatres and on demand on 5 February 2021, with Stage 6 Films handling international distribution. Critics were enthusiastic: it holds a 91% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it tough but stirring, using one couple's pandemic love story to show the strength of human connection, and a Metacritic score of 71.

original_title: ฉลาดเกมส์โกง
overview: Lynn, a brilliant student, after helping her friends to get the grades they need, develops the idea of starting a much bigger exam-cheating business.
tagline: Genius students with one mission... Turning exam answers into millions.
title: Bad Genius
plot:
Bad Genius is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly among young women navigating the cutthroat world of high-stakes academic competition. The movie masterfully weaves together themes of ambition, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong.

At its core, Bad Genius explores the intense pressure to succeed in a highly competitive environment, where individuals are often forced to make difficult choices that compromise their values and relationships. The film's protagonist, Jen, is a brilliant and resourceful student who finds herself at the center of a complex web of deceit and manipulation.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jen's actions are motivated by a desire for validation and recognition, which she believes can only be achieved through extreme measures. Her relationships with her peers and mentors are fraught with tension, as they grapple with their own moral compasses and the consequences of their actions.

One of the most striking aspects of Bad Genius is its portrayal of the toxic dynamics between women who are driven by a desire to succeed at any cost. The film highlights the ways in which these individuals can both support and sabotage one another, often without even realizing it.

Throughout the movie, the director skillfully subverts expectations, leaving the audience questioning what is truly right or wrong. This moral ambiguity is a hallmark of the film's thought-provoking nature, inviting viewers to consider the complexities of human behavior and the difficult choices we face in our own lives.

Ultimately, Bad Genius is a gripping and unsettling exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, one that challenges us to confront our own values and motivations.

overview: When a mysterious animal attack leaves a mutilated body in the forest, a conservative small town detective must enlist the help of an eager wildlife specialist to uncover the dark and disturbing truth that threatens the town.
tagline: Hunger runs deep.
title: The Hunting
plot:
The Hunting is a 2021 American werewolf horror film written and directed by Mark Andrew Hamer, co-written by Heather Ryan and Terrance Ryan; all three were making their feature debuts. Produced by Moonphase Media and Bright Shiny Things, it stars former NFL fullback Peyton Hillis, a Madden NFL 12 cover athlete appearing in his first leading film role, alongside Joelle Westwood, Joaquin Guerrero, Keith Migra, Angela Cole, Daniel Repas, Alan Tuskes, Heidi Azaro, Billy Grimm and Matt Tifft. Vertical Entertainment gave the film a limited theatrical release and put it on digital and video-on-demand platforms in January 2022. It runs 91 minutes.

The film opens with a half-glimpsed furry creature killing a drunken fisherman on a lake under the full moon. When he fails to come home, his wife Sarah (Cole) reports him missing, one of several disappearances troubling the small town. Police chief Galligan (Repas) sends Detective Ryan Conner (Hillis), a tough, conservative military veteran haunted by memories of his wartime service, to investigate with his partner Dave (Migra), the chief's son. Meanwhile, at Talbot's Wolf Sanctuary, Maggie Talbot (Westwood) marks the first anniversary of her parents' deaths while trying, with the help of Todd (Guerrero), to keep their dream alive. When a mutilated body is found in the forest after a mysterious animal attack, Conner is forced to enlist the eager wildlife specialist to help him uncover the dark truth threatening the town. Flashbacks to Conner's combat experience punctuate the investigation, and the hunt ends with a twist revealing the identity of the creature.

The film drew mixed reviews. Jim Morazzini, writing for Voices From the Balcony in a review republished by Nerdly, gave it two and a half stars out of five, finding it badly flawed but watchable; he praised the use of a practical man-in-a-suit creature rather than CGI but felt the heavy subplot about post-traumatic stress disorder would alienate viewers expecting a werewolf film, and called the final reveal, which hinges on a character never established as a suspect, a lazy cheat. Jeff Turner of Action Reloaded was more enthusiastic, calling it a howling good time with solid performances from Hillis and Westwood, intriguing backstories, a gruesome war flashback and an effective practical-effects creature, and noting that the ending left the door open for a sequel.

overview: An eclectic foursome of aspiring teenage witches get more than they bargained for as they lean into their newfound powers.
tagline: Let the ritual begin
title: The Craft: Legacy
plot:
The Craft: Legacy is a 2020 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Zoe Lister-Jones, a legacy sequel to The Craft (1996) produced by Blumhouse. It stars Cailee Spaeny, Gideon Adlon, Lovie Simone and Zoey Luna as four teenage girls who form a coven of witches, with Nicholas Galitzine, Michelle Monaghan and David Duchovny, and a cameo by Fairuza Balk.

Lily Schechner moves to a new town with her mother, Helen, a therapist, to live with Helen's boyfriend Adam Harrison and his three sons. On her first day at school, she is humiliated when she gets her period in class, and when the bully Timmy Andrews taunts her, she telekinetically hurls him into the lockers. Three girls who witness it, Frankie, Tabby and Lourdes, reveal themselves to be witches and invite Lily to complete their coven, which allows them to perform powerful rituals such as freezing time. They cast a spell that makes Timmy kinder, and he becomes their friend, confiding to Lily that he is bisexual and has been with Adam's son Isaiah. After Lily secretly casts a love spell on him and they kiss, Timmy is found dead in an apparent suicide. Horrified by Lily's confession, her friends cut ties with her and bind themselves from using magic.

Uneasy about Adam's authoritarian manner, Lily searches his office and finds her own adoption papers, and Helen reveals that Lily's birth mother is one of her psychiatric patients. When "Helen" later asks Lily to hand over her powers, Lily realizes it is Adam in disguise; he reveals that he belongs to a pagan cult that has coveted her power from the start and knocks her out. In a forest at night, Adam admits that he murdered Timmy and plans to kill her too. Contacted by Timmy's spirit through a Ouija board, the other girls come to her rescue, and the four combine their elemental powers to burn Adam to death. Afterward, the coven reunites, and Helen takes Lily to a psychiatric hospital to meet her birth mother, who turns out to be Nancy Downs.

Sony Pictures released the film on video on demand in the United States on October 28, 2020, with theatrical runs in some international markets. Amid pandemic cinema closures it earned only $2.3 million on an $18 million budget. Reviews were mixed (47% on Rotten Tomatoes, 54 on Metacritic), and it received a GLAAD Media Award nomination.

overview: As children, Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy spend their childhood at an idyllic and secluded English boarding school. As they grow into adults, they must come to terms with the complexity and strength of their love for one another while also preparing for the haunting reality awaiting them.
tagline: These students have everything they need. Except time.
title: Never Let Me Go
plot:
Never Let Me Go is a 2010 period drama film directed by Mark Romanek, based on the novel of the same name by Kazuo Ishiguro.

The main themes of Never Let Me Go revolve around:

1. **Humanity and Identity**: The film explores what it means to be human, particularly in the context of a society where humans are raised and used for organ harvesting. The characters' struggles with their own identities, humanity, and mortality serve as a central theme.
2. **Friendship and Love**: The complex relationships between Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy form the emotional core of the film. Their bond is tested by the harsh realities of their existence, yet they find ways to cherish each other in the face of adversity.
3. **Loss and Grief**: As the characters confront their own mortality, they must come to terms with the loss of innocence, youth, and the people they love. The film's exploration of grief and mourning serves as a poignant reminder of the human experience.
4. **Social Commentary on Class and Inequality**: The film critiques the class system in 1990s England, where those born into wealth and privilege are afforded certain luxuries and opportunities, while those from lower backgrounds are relegated to menial jobs and limited prospects.
5. **Mortality and the Human Condition**: Never Let Me Go confronts the inevitability of death and the fragility of human life. The film's exploration of these themes serves as a reminder to appreciate the present moment and cherish the time we have with loved ones.

The film's narrative is structured around Kathy's reflections on her past, which serve as a framing device for the story. Through her memories, the audience experiences the characters' struggles, joys, and losses, ultimately leading to a poignant exploration of what it means to be human in the face of mortality.

Overall, Never Let Me Go is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its nuanced character development and atmospheric storytelling.

original_title: Bardo, falsa crónica de unas cuantas verdades
overview: A renowned Mexican journalist and documentary filmmaker living in Los Angeles, after being named the recipient of a prestigious international award, is compelled to return to his native country, unaware that this simple trip will push him to an existential limit.
tagline: Experience a state of mind.
title: BARDO, False Chronicle of a Handful of Truths
plot:
Bardo, False Chronicle of a Handful of Truths (Spanish: Bardo, falsa crónica de unas cuantas verdades) is a 2022 Mexican epic psychological black comedy-drama film directed, produced, co-written, co-scored and co-edited by Alejandro G. Iñárritu. Daniel Giménez Cacho stars as Silverio Gama, with Griselda Siciliani as his wife Lucía, Ximena Lamadrid as their daughter Camila and Íker Sánchez Solano as their son Lorenzo. The title refers to the Buddhist bardo, a liminal state between death and rebirth.

Silverio is a Mexican journalist turned documentary filmmaker living in Los Angeles, whose work has become increasingly personal; his latest film is an autobiographical docufiction. He and Lucía are still haunted by the death of their first son, Mateo, a day after his birth, and keep his ashes. Silverio experiences daily life surreally, with dreams, memories and fantasies unfolding alongside reality: meeting the US ambassador at Chapultepec Castle, he sees the 1847 battle and the deaths of the Niños Héroes around him. Named the first Latin American to receive a prestigious American journalism award, he suspects it is a gesture to ease tensions between the two countries, inflamed by migration politics and by Amazon's attempt to buy Baja California, and he faces intense scrutiny in Mexico.

Back home, he skips a talk-show interview, attends a party in his honor where he insults the host who has attacked his work, imagines reconciling with his dead parents, and sees visions of Mexico's historic atrocities, including Hernán Cortés atop a pile of corpses in the Zócalo lecturing him about the conquest. Guilty about having emigrated when so many cannot, he vacations with his family in Baja California as Amazon completes the purchase, and they scatter Mateo's ashes at sea. Back in Los Angeles, Silverio suffers a stroke on a Metro train and falls into a coma; the film's events are revealed as his mind's attempt to process his life. Camila accepts the award in his place while his family keeps vigil, and the film ends as it began, with Silverio imagining himself flying across a desert.

Bardo premiered in competition at the 79th Venice International Film Festival on September 1, 2022, opened in Mexican theaters on October 27 and streamed on Netflix from December 16. Reviews were polarized: critics praised the performances, Darius Khondji's cinematography and the direction, but many found it self-indulgent and overlong; Rotten Tomatoes reported 60% approval.

overview: A portal transports Cpt. Artemis and an elite unit of soldiers to a strange world where powerful monsters rule with deadly ferocity. Faced with relentless danger, the team encounters a mysterious hunter who may be their only hope to find a way home.
tagline: Behind our world, there is another.
title: Monster Hunter
plot:
Monster Hunter is a 2020 action fantasy film written, directed and produced by Paul W. S. Anderson, based on Capcom's video game series. It stars Milla Jovovich, in her sixth film with her husband Anderson, as U.S. Army Ranger Captain Natalie Artemis, with Tony Jaa as the Hunter and Ron Perlman as the Admiral, alongside T.I., Meagan Good, Diego Boneta, Josh Helman and MC Jin as members of Artemis's squad. The film follows soldiers transported to a hostile world ruled by gigantic monsters.

In a parallel world, humans struggle to survive among huge, savage creatures. A warrior known as the Hunter is separated from the Admiral's crew when their ship is attacked by the Diablos, an enormous horned beast that tunnels beneath the dunes. On Earth, Artemis and her United Nations security team are searching the desert for a missing squad of soldiers when a sudden storm pulls them through a dimensional portal into the new world, where they find the charred remains of the soldiers they were looking for.

The team's bullets and grenades prove useless against the Diablos, and the survivors take refuge in a cave, only to be attacked by spider-like monsters called Nerscylla. Artemis escapes alone and encounters the Hunter. After fighting each other, the two grudgingly agree to cooperate. She learns that the portals are created by the Sky Tower, a structure across the desert, and that they must kill the Diablos to cross safely. Learning to use the Hunter's weapons, Artemis helps him lay a trap for the beast, and their journey eventually leads them to the Admiral and his crew, and into a deadly confrontation with the fire-breathing Rathalos, which threatens to break through the portal into our world.

The film emphasizes large-scale creature battles and visual effects, borrowing monsters and characters from the game Monster Hunter: World.

Monster Hunter opened in China on December 4, 2020, and in the United States on December 18 amid the COVID-19 pandemic. It was a box office bomb, grossing 47.9 million dollars against a 60 million dollar budget, and received mixed reviews, with 44 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 47; critics praised the action and effects but faulted the direction and editing.

overview: The legendary Roberto Duran and his equally legendary trainer Ray Arcel change each other's lives.
tagline: No más. No surrender.
title: Hands of Stone
plot:
Hands of Stone is a biographical sports drama film directed by John Stockwell, released in 2016. The movie is based on the life of boxer Roberto Durán, played by Edgar Ramírez.

The main themes of Hands of Stone include:

1. **Perseverance and Resilience**: The film showcases Durán's incredible journey from a young boy growing up in poverty to becoming a world champion boxer. Despite facing numerous challenges, including poverty, abuse, and personal struggles, Durán perseveres and rises to become one of the greatest boxers of all time.

2. **The Corrupting Influence of Fame**: The movie highlights how fame and wealth can corrupt even the strongest individuals. Durán's rise to fame is accompanied by his increasing involvement in organized crime and his eventual downfall.

3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: Throughout the film, Durán struggles with his identity and sense of self-worth. He grapples with his humble beginnings, his relationships, and his place in the world, ultimately discovering a new sense of purpose and redemption.

4. **The Power of Redemption**: The movie's climax revolves around Durán's decision to retire from boxing and seek redemption for past mistakes. This theme is central to the film's narrative, as Durán seeks to make amends and find peace after years of turmoil.

5. **The Human Cost of Ambition**: Hands of Stone portrays the human cost of ambition and the sacrifices that come with it. Durán's relentless pursuit of success takes a toll on his personal relationships and overall well-being, serving as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition.

Overall, Hands of Stone is a powerful and emotional biographical drama that explores themes of perseverance, identity, redemption, and the human cost of ambition.

overview: After a battle in a power plant, Ben notices something strange is happening with the omnitrix, but doesn't tell anyone. Tetrax arrives, and tells them the omnitrix is broadcasting a self destruct signal. Tetrax and Ben go to find the creator of the omnitrix to fix the omnitrix before it destroys itself and the universe along with it. Gwen stows away to help her cousin.
title: Ben 10: Secret of the Omnitrix
plot:
Ben 10: Secret of the Omnitrix is a 2007 animated science fiction comedy-adventure film directed by Alex Zamm and produced by Cartoon Network Studios. The movie follows the story of Ben Tennyson, a 10-year-old boy who discovers a powerful alien device called the Omnitrix.

The main themes of Ben 10: Secret of the Omnitrix include:

1. **Self-discovery**: Ben's journey is also one of self-discovery as he learns to control and understand the power of the Omnitrix, which allows him to transform into different alien creatures.
2. **Responsibility**: As Ben becomes more confident in his abilities, he must learn to take responsibility for using the Omnitrix for good, rather than letting it consume him.
3. **Friendship**: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and teamwork as Ben works with his grandfather Max and cousin Gwen to stop the villainous Vilgax from obtaining the Omnitrix.
4. **Power and corruption**: The film explores the dangers of power and corruption, as Vilgax's desire for control and domination drives him to seek out the Omnitrix at any cost.

The movie follows Ben's initial discovery of the Omnitrix, his subsequent battles against Vilgax, and his ultimate realization that he must learn to use the device responsibly in order to save the world.

overview: When Stargirl's mother is hired as the costume designer on a movie, they relocate to L.A., where Stargirl quickly becomes involved with an eclectic assortment of characters.
tagline: Find your place among the stars.
title: Hollywood Stargirl
plot:
Hollywood Stargirl is a 2022 American musical drama film directed by Julia Hart. The movie revolves around the life of Stargirl, a free-spirited and creative teenager who moves to Los Angeles with her family.

The main theme of Hollywood Stargirl is the struggle for individuality and self-expression in a world that often values conformity and commercialism. Stargirl's character embodies this theme as she navigates her new surroundings and tries to stay true to herself despite the pressures of fame, social media, and the expectations of those around her.

The film also explores the idea of creativity and its power to bring people together and transcend boundaries. Through Stargirl's passion for art and music, the movie highlights the importance of pursuing one's passions and finding ways to express oneself authentically.

Furthermore, Hollywood Stargirl touches on the theme of family and the complexities that come with it. The film shows how Stargirl's relationships with her parents and brother are affected by her desire for independence and self-expression, leading to a deeper understanding of the importance of communication, empathy, and support in family dynamics.

Overall, Hollywood Stargirl is a heartwarming and inspiring story about embracing one's uniqueness and finding the courage to be true to oneself, even in the face of adversity.

overview: In stifling Edwardian London, Wendy Darling mesmerizes her brothers every night with bedtime tales of swordplay, swashbuckling and the fearsome Captain Hook. But the children become the heroes of an even greater story, when Peter Pan flies into their nursery one night and leads them over moonlit rooftops through a galaxy of stars and to the lush jungles of Neverland.
tagline: All children grow up except one.
title: Peter Pan
plot:
Peter Pan is a 2003 fantasy adventure film directed by P. J. Hogan, who wrote the screenplay with Michael Goldenberg, adapted from J. M. Barrie's 1904 play and 1911 novel. Jeremy Sumpter plays Peter, Rachel Hurd-Wood plays Wendy Darling and Ludivine Sagnier plays Tinker Bell, while Jason Isaacs, following stage tradition, takes the double role of Captain Hook and Wendy's father, George Darling. Olivia Williams and Lynn Redgrave co-star.

In Edwardian London, Wendy entertains her younger brothers, John and Michael, with tales of Captain Hook, unaware that Peter Pan is listening at the nursery window. Their Aunt Millicent urges the parents to think about Wendy's future prospects. When Peter returns one night, the family's dog, Nana, bites off his shadow, and after Wendy sews it back on he invites her and her brothers to Neverland to tell stories to his Lost Boys. Sprinkled with Tinker Bell's fairy dust, they fly away.

In Neverland the children are soon attacked by Hook's pirates. The jealous Tinker Bell tricks the Lost Boys into shooting Wendy down, but an acorn Peter gave her saves her life, and Peter banishes the fairy. Wendy becomes a mother to the Lost Boys, with Peter as their father. After Hook captures John, Michael and the princess Tiger Lily, Peter and the boys rescue them, and the pirate captain is chased off by the crocodile that has stalked him for years. Peter and Wendy share a dance among the fairies, but when she asks him to admit his feelings, he angrily insists she go home, unable to accept love if it means growing up. Wendy decides to return to London, and the Lost Boys choose to go with her. Hook's crew captures them and poisons Peter's medicine, which Tinker Bell drinks to save him. Peter's pleas for everyone in Neverland and London to believe in fairies revive her, and together they free the prisoners. Hook gains the power of flight, taunts Peter that Wendy will grow up and marry someone else, and nearly defeats him, but Wendy's kiss restores Peter's spirit, and Hook ends up inside the crocodile. Peter flies everyone home aboard the fairy-dusted Jolly Roger; the Darlings adopt the Lost Boys and Peter returns to Neverland, as Wendy goes on telling his story to her descendants.

It was the first live-action theatrical version to cast a boy as Peter. Released at Christmas 2003, it was well reviewed, with 77% on Rotten Tomatoes and 64 on Metacritic, but grossed only about $122 million worldwide amid competition from The Return of the King.

overview: By 2017, the global economy has collapsed and U.S. society has become a totalitarian police state, censoring all cultural activity. The government pacifies the populace by broadcasting a number of game shows in which convicted criminals fight for their lives, including the gladiator-style The Running Man, hosted by the ruthless Damon Killian, where “runners” attempt to evade “stalkers” and certain death for a chance to be pardoned and set free.
tagline: 2019. A game nobody survives. This year might be the exception.
title: The Running Man
plot:
The Running Man is a dystopian science fiction film released in 1987, directed by Paul Michael Glaser and produced by Keith Barish Productions.

In the year 2035, the United States has become a totalitarian government where corporations have replaced the government. The main character, Ben Richards (played by Arnold Schwarzenegger), is a former police officer who was wrongly convicted of murder and sentenced to death. However, just as he is about to be executed, he is offered a deal by the corporation that owns the prison: participate in a deadly game show called "The Running Man" where contestants must survive a treacherous terrain while being pursued by ruthless hunters.

Ben agrees to participate in the game, which becomes a form of entertainment for the masses. The game is broadcasted live on television, and Ben's survival is monitored by the corporation's agents. As the game progresses, Ben discovers that he has been framed for murder and that his only hope of survival is to clear his name.

Throughout the film, Ben faces numerous challenges and obstacles as he navigates through a post-apocalyptic landscape filled with danger and violence. He encounters other contestants who are also trying to survive, including a mysterious woman named Amy (played by Maria Conchita Alonso) who becomes his ally.

As the game progresses, Ben's determination to clear his name grows stronger, and he begins to uncover the truth behind his wrongful conviction. However, the corporation will stop at nothing to keep him from escaping, and Ben must use all his skills and resources to stay alive.

The film's climax features a thrilling showdown between Ben and the corporation's agents, as well as a dramatic confrontation with the mastermind behind the game show. In the end, Ben emerges victorious, but not without scars, both physical and emotional.

Throughout the film, the themes of oppression, rebellion, and survival are explored, making The Running Man a thought-provoking commentary on our society's obsession with entertainment and violence. The film's action-packed sequences, coupled with its social commentary, make it a classic of 80s science fiction cinema.

Overall, The Running Man is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of a totalitarian government. With its blend of action, suspense, and social commentary, it remains a cult classic to this day.

overview: Two policemen, one an old-timer, the other his volatile younger partner, find themselves suspended when a video of their strong-arm tactics becomes the media's cause du jour. Low on cash and with no other options, these two embittered soldiers descend into the criminal underworld to gain their just due, but instead find far more than they wanted awaiting them in the shadows.
tagline: Those who can't earn a living must find another way to provide
title: Dragged Across Concrete
plot:
Dragged Across Concrete is a 2018 American crime thriller film written and directed by S. Craig Zahler. The movie stars Vince Vaughn, Jennifer Carpenter, Don Johnson, and Melissa Leo.

The story follows two detectives, Detective Brett Ridgeway (Vince Vaughn) and Detective Anthony Lopez (Don Johnson), who work for the Dallas Police Department's Vice and Narcotics division. They are a mismatched duo, with Ridgeway being a by-the-book, straight-laced cop, while Lopez is a loose-cannon, street-smart veteran.

The movie begins with a gruesome crime scene: a young woman named Sarah (Jennifer Carpenter) has been brutally murdered in a motel room. The investigation that follows reveals that the killer left behind a mysterious symbol carved into the victim's body - a symbol that will become a recurring motif throughout the film.

As Ridgeway and Lopez delve deeper into the case, they discover that Sarah was involved in a sex trafficking ring, and that she had been working to take down the operation from within. The detectives soon realize that they are dealing with a highly organized and ruthless crime syndicate, led by a mysterious figure known only as "The Devil" (Melissa Leo).

As the investigation unfolds, Ridgeway and Lopez's partnership is put to the test. They have different working styles, and their differing approaches often lead to clashes. However, they are both driven by a desire to solve the case and bring justice to Sarah's killer.

Throughout the film, Zahler expertly ratchets up the tension and violence, creating a sense of unease and dread that permeates every scene. The cinematography is stark and unsettling, capturing the dark underbelly of Dallas's seedy side.

As the story builds towards its climax, Ridgeway and Lopez discover that they are in over their heads. They are dealing with a crime syndicate that will stop at nothing to silence them. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that The Devil is none other than Sarah's own mother, who has been using her daughter as leverage to manipulate the detectives.

The film's final act is a tense and violent showdown between Ridgeway, Lopez, and The Devil. The outcome is far from certain, and the audience is left on the edge of their seats as the two detectives fight for their lives.

Ultimately, Dragged Across Concrete is a gripping and unflinching portrayal of the darker side of human nature. Zahler's direction is masterful, creating a sense of unease and tension that propels the film towards its shocking conclusion. The performances from Vaughn, Carpenter, Johnson, and Leo are all top-notch, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Dragged Across Concrete is a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

overview: The Cobol Job is a fourteen-minute animated prequel to Christopher Nolan’s award-winning movie: Inception, detailing the heist on Mr. Kaneda's mind by Nash, Cobb, Arthur, and several Cobol Engineering thugs.
title: Inception: The Cobol Job
plot:
Inception: The Cobol Job is a 2010 animated motion comic that serves as a prequel to Christopher Nolan's science fiction thriller Inception, leading directly into the dream heist that opens the film. Written by Jordan Goldberg and directed by Ian Kirby, it runs roughly fourteen minutes and adapts a comic illustrated by Long Vo, Joe Ng and Crystal Reid of the studio Udon. The comic was first published online on Inception's official website and on Yahoo! Movies as part of Warner Bros.' viral marketing campaign for the film, and the animated version was later included among the bonus features on the second disc of the film's Blu-ray release in December 2010.

The story opens with Cobb recalling the lessons of his mentor Miles, who taught him the art of shared dreaming and insisted that creation should be for its own sake rather than for profit. Cobb, his point man Arthur and Nash, an unreliable architect chosen only because he was available, have been hired by Cobol Engineering to extract a secret from the mind of Mr. Kaneda, a paranoid executive. The dream takes the form of a downtown district of skyscrapers, a bank and an office tower, and Cobol insists on sending along several armed thugs as "tourists" to make sure the job gets done. Early on Cobb is distracted by a vision of his late wife Mal and is nearly killed by a bus, saved only by Arthur.

While Arthur and the tourists stage a jewellery-store robbery to draw off the police, Nash guides Cobb to Kaneda's office. Cobb threatens the executive and produces a bomb, but the dream begins to collapse after Nash is killed by Kaneda's receptionist. When Kaneda finally unlocks his computer, Cobb finds that the file he wants, the RDS-1 Energy Expansion Program, is protected by a password that only its originator, Saito, knows. The bomb goes off and Cobb wakes in a hostage room guarded by Cobol's men. The firm's chief, Woodruff, reveals that the information was meant to win Fischer Morrow's backing for an oil pipeline along Africa's eastern coast. Cobb agrees to go after Saito himself, on condition that there are no tourists and only he, Arthur and Nash take part, since Saito is trained in dream-sharing and will be on guard from the start. The prequel ends as Cobb prepares the plan that becomes the opening sequence of Inception.

overview: After a disease kills 98% of America's children, the surviving 2% develop superpowers and are placed in internment camps. A 16-year-old girl escapes her camp and joins a group of other teens on the run from the government.
tagline: The ones who changed will change everything
title: The Darkest Minds
plot:
The Darkest Minds is a 2018 American science fiction thriller film directed by Jennifer Yuh Nelson and written by Alexandra Bracken. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Alexandra Bracken.

In a dystopian future, the United States government has been ravaged by a mysterious disease that affects children and young adults, causing them to develop supernatural abilities at an alarming rate. These children, known as "orbs," are hunted by the government for their powers, which they use to wreak havoc on society.

The story follows Ruby Daly (Chloe Moretz), a 16-year-old girl who possesses one of the most powerful abilities among her peers. She is taken into custody by the government and sent to a "rehabilitation" camp, where she meets other orbs, including Liam Stenbeck (Auggie Maturo), Chubs (Braxton Brice), and Zu (Harris Dickinson).

At the camp, Ruby discovers that she has been subjected to experimental treatments designed to suppress her powers. However, these treatments have only made her stronger, and she soon escapes from the camp with Liam and a few other orbs.

The group embarks on a perilous journey across the country, pursued by the government's forces, known as "the Division." Along the way, they meet a mysterious figure named Marcus (Patton Oswalt), who claims to be working for a secret organization that seeks to protect orbs from persecution.

As Ruby and her friends navigate their new reality, they begin to uncover the truth about the government's intentions and the origins of the disease. They also discover that Ruby has a unique connection to Liam, which could hold the key to unlocking the secrets of their powers.

Throughout the journey, Ruby struggles with her own identity and the weight of her abilities. She is forced to confront the harsh realities of her world and make difficult choices about who she can trust and how far she is willing to go to protect herself and those she cares about.

Ultimately, Ruby and her friends reach a safe haven, where they hope to find acceptance and protection from the government's forces. However, the movie ends on a cliffhanger, setting the stage for a potential sequel.

The Darkest Minds explores themes of identity, power, and resistance in a world that seeks to control and exploit those with extraordinary abilities. The film features a strong performance from Chloe Moretz as Ruby, who brings depth and nuance to the complex and dynamic protagonist.

overview: Stranded and alone on a desert island during a cruise, a spoiled rich woman and a deckhand fall in love and make a date to reunite after their rescue.
tagline: Paradise makes strange bedfellows
title: Swept Away
plot:
Swept Away is a 2002 adventure romantic comedy film written and directed by Guy Ritchie, a remake of Lina Wertmüller's 1974 Italian film of the same name. It stars Ritchie's then-wife Madonna as Amber Leighton and Adriano Giannini as Giuseppe Esposito, the role played in the original by his father, Giancarlo Giannini, with Bruce Greenwood as Amber's husband Tony, Jeanne Tripplehorn as Marina and Elizabeth Banks as Debi. It was produced by Matthew Vaughn and released by Screen Gems.

Amber, the wealthy, spoiled wife of millionaire Tony Leighton, joins two other couples on a private cruise from Greece to Italy. From the start she takes an intense dislike to Giuseppe, a deckhand, and insults him relentlessly. Ignoring his warnings about an approaching storm, she demands to be taken out in a dinghy, and berates him even more when they run out of fuel. After a series of mishaps, in which Amber damages the boat, the two wash up on a deserted island.

There the balance of power is reversed. Giuseppe, who has the skills to survive, takes control and treats Amber with growing dominance, while she becomes increasingly submissive. Over time, their relationship turns into a passionate romance, and Amber discovers that she is truly happy on the island. When she spots a boat anchored in the bay, she hides so that they will not be rescued. Eventually they are found and return to their former lives. Giuseppe tries repeatedly to contact Amber to rekindle their love, but his messages go unanswered, and he concludes, heartbroken, that she has rejected him. In the final scenes it is revealed that Tony has intercepted the letters, making sure that Amber never sees them, or Giuseppe, again.

The film, originally titled Love, Sex, Drugs and Money, was shot in Sardinia and Malta from October to November 2001 under heightened security after the September 11 attacks, shortly after Madonna finished her Drowned World Tour. It was savaged by critics, who faulted Madonna's performance and Ritchie's direction and judged it far inferior to the original, lacking its political context; Rotten Tomatoes reported 6% approval and Metacritic a score of 18. A commercial failure, it grossed about $1 million worldwide against a $10 million budget, and it has since been described as one of the worst films ever made.

overview: Back from war in Afghanistan, a young British soldier struggling with depression and PTSD finds a second chance in the Amazon rainforest when he meets an American scientist, and together they foster an orphaned baby ocelot.
title: Wildcat
plot:
Wildcat is a 2022 American documentary film directed by the photojournalist Trevor Frost and Melissa Lesh about animal rescue work in the Peruvian Amazon. It premiered at the 2022 Telluride Film Festival and was released in theaters on 21 December 2022 by Amazon Studios before streaming on Prime Video. In 2023, it won the Emmy Award for Outstanding Nature Documentary.

The film follows Harry Turner, a young British army veteran who suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder after serving in Afghanistan. Struggling to find his footing after leaving the military, he travels to a remote part of the Amazon rainforest in Peru, where he meets Samantha Zwicker, an American wildlife biologist who runs a project rescuing animals threatened by poaching and habitat destruction. The documentary also explores Zwicker's own troubled personal history and her driven, sometimes fraught approach to her mission.

At the heart of the film is the pair's effort to raise an orphaned baby ocelot named Khan and prepare him to survive on his own in the jungle. Turner devotes himself completely to the animal, living alongside him, teaching him to hunt and gradually encouraging his independence, and the bond becomes a lifeline for the young veteran. But before Khan is old enough to be released, he is killed by an illegal shotgun trap set by poachers, a loss that devastates Turner and plunges him back into crisis. A year later, Turner and Zwicker take on another baby ocelot, Keanu, and this time succeed in raising him to the age at which he can return to the wild. The film also follows a visit from Turner's family, drawing parallels between his devotion to his younger brother and the care he gives to the ocelots, and charts the strain that the work and their own traumas place on the relationship between Turner and Zwicker.

The film was assembled from footage gathered over several years in the rainforest. Wildcat received largely positive reviews, holding a 92 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 49 reviews; the site's consensus noted that, although it raises uncomfortable ethical questions, the film is an affecting testament to the healing power of bonds between species. Stephen Farber of The Hollywood Reporter called it a riveting journey into the wild, while noting that it leaves questions about its subjects' relationship unanswered.

overview: When The Man in the Yellow Hat befriends Curious George in the jungle, they set off on a non-stop, fun-filled journey through the wonders of the big city toward the warmth of true friendship.
tagline: Show me the Monkey!
title: Curious George
plot:
Curious George is a 2006 computer-animated adventure comedy film based on the children's book series by H.A. and Margret Rey.

The main theme of Curious George revolves around curiosity, exploration, and learning from one's mistakes. The story follows the adventures of Curious George, a mischievous monkey who gets into various predicaments while exploring the city with his friend, the Man in the Yellow Hat.

As the film progresses, George learns valuable lessons about responsibility, empathy, and understanding the consequences of his actions. He also develops a strong bond with the Man in the Yellow Hat, who teaches him important life skills and encourages him to think critically.

Throughout the movie, Curious George faces various challenges, including navigating obstacles, overcoming fears, and learning to work together with others. These experiences help shape George's character and teach him essential values such as friendship, kindness, and self-control.

The film also explores themes of creativity, imagination, and problem-solving, highlighting the importance of thinking outside the box and finding innovative solutions to complex problems.

Overall, Curious George (2006) is a heartwarming story that promotes positive values and encourages children to think creatively, explore their surroundings, and learn from their mistakes.

overview: The patriarch of a wealthy and powerful family suddenly passes away, leaving his wife and daughter with a shocking secret inheritance that threatens to unravel and destroy their lives.
tagline: Some secrets should stay buried
title: Inheritance
plot:
Inheritance is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Vaughn Stein and written by Matthew Kennedy. It stars Lily Collins, Simon Pegg, Connie Nielsen, Chace Crawford and Patrick Warburton, and centers on the dark secret left behind when the patriarch of a wealthy and powerful family dies suddenly. Collins joined the cast in early 2019, replacing Kate Mara, and filming took place in Birmingham, Alabama.

After the sudden death of Archer Monroe, the patriarch of a powerful political family, his estate is divided among his wife, Catherine; his son, William, a politician running for reelection; and his daughter, Lauren, the Manhattan District Attorney. The family lawyer, Harold Thewlis, gives Lauren a private message from her father revealing a secret and directing her to an underground bunker on the family estate. Inside, she finds a man chained to the wall who calls himself Morgan Warner.

Morgan tells Lauren that he was Archer's friend and business partner, and that years ago the two of them, driving drunk, killed a pedestrian. To protect his career, Archer imprisoned Morgan rather than risk exposure, and over the years he used his captive as a confessor. Morgan's information leads Lauren to the victim's body, to Archer's longtime mistress and illegitimate son, and to evidence that Archer paid bribes to help his children win public office. Convinced, Lauren frees Morgan and has Harold arrange an offshore account and a private jet so he can disappear. But when his fingerprints are identified, Catherine recognizes the man in the photographs as Carson, calling him evil. Lauren discovers that his flight never left and that Harold has been murdered. At the house, Carson has taken Catherine to the bunker.
