He overpowers Lauren and reveals that 30 years earlier he drugged and raped Catherine; Archer had been taking him away to kill him when they struck the pedestrian, and imprisoned him instead. Archer died from the poison he had meant for Carson. As they fight, Carson claims to be Lauren's father, before Catherine shoots him dead. The women set the bunker on fire and leave.

Planned to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival before its postponement due to COVID-19, the film was released on DirecTV Cinema on April 23, 2020, and by Vertical Entertainment on May 22. It received negative reviews, with 25% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

overview: A soldier and his team battle hordes of post-apocalyptic zombies in the wastelands of the Korean Peninsula.
tagline: Escape the apocalypse.
title: Peninsula
plot:
Peninsula (Korean: Bando), marketed internationally as Train to Busan Presents: Peninsula, is a 2020 South Korean post-apocalyptic action horror film co-written and directed by Yeon Sang-ho, a standalone sequel to his 2016 hit Train to Busan. It stars Gang Dong-won as Han Jung-seok, a former Marine officer haunted by guilt, Lee Jung-hyun as Min-jung, Kwon Hae-hyo as her father Elder Kim, and Kim Min-jae as Sergeant Hwang, the sadistic leader of a rogue militia.

As a zombie outbreak overwhelms South Korea and the country is placed under quarantine, Jung-seok escapes aboard an evacuation ship with his sister, her husband Chul-min and their young son. During the escape he refuses to help a desperate family after noticing that the father is bleeding. When an infected passenger turns aboard the ship, his sister and nephew are bitten, and Jung-seok seals them in their cabin.

Four years later, Jung-seok and Chul-min are living as refugees in Hong Kong when a gang of mobsters recruits them for a mission back to the abandoned peninsula: to retrieve a truck containing twenty million dollars, in exchange for half the money. They find the truck, but the noise draws a horde of zombies, and the team is ambushed by Unit 631, a degenerate militia that stages survival games pitting captives against the undead. Chul-min is captured, while Jung-seok is rescued by two young sisters, Joon-yi and Yu-jin, who live in hiding with their mother Min-jung and grandfather Elder Kim. Jung-seok realizes that Min-jung is the woman he abandoned four years earlier. Together they plan to steal back the truck and reach a ship waiting at Incheon Port, setting off a frantic chase through the zombie-infested ruins.

The film moves the series from claustrophobic survival horror toward large-scale action and car chases, while returning to themes of guilt, redemption and sacrifice.

Selected for the cancelled 2020 Cannes Film Festival, Peninsula was released in South Korea on 15 July 2020, setting the best opening day of the year there. It grossed 42.7 million dollars worldwide on a 16 million dollar budget, but reviews were mixed, with 55 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51.

overview: Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car driven to succeed, discovers that life is about the journey, not the finish line, when he finds himself unexpectedly detoured in the sleepy Route 66 town of Radiator Springs. On route across the country to the big Piston Cup Championship in California to compete against two seasoned pros, McQueen gets to know the town's offbeat characters.
tagline: Ahhh... it's got that new movie smell.
title: Cars
plot:
Cars is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film released in 2006 by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place in a world where cars are living beings, and it follows the story of Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car who gets stranded in a small town called Radiator Springs.

The film begins with Lightning McQueen (voiced by Owen Wilson), a talented but arrogant racing car from North Carolina. He is on his way to California to participate in the Piston Cup Championship, a prestigious racing competition that will make him a legend in the racing world. During his journey, he gets lost due to a faulty GPS system and ends up in Radiator Springs, a small town on Route 66.

Initially, McQueen is reluctant to stay in Radiator Springs, as he believes it's not a place for high-performance cars like himself. However, he soon befriends the town's residents, including Mater (voiced by Larry the Cable Guy), a rusty but lovable tow truck; Sally Carrera (voiced by Bonnie Hunt), a sleek and sophisticated Porsche; and Doc Hudson (voiced by Paul Newman), a wise and aged Hudson Hornet.

As McQueen spends more time in Radiator Springs, he learns about the town's history and the struggles its residents have faced due to the decline of Route 66. He also discovers that his arrival has brought new life to the town, but at the cost of its former glory. McQueen decides to help the townspeople by participating in the annual "Cozy Cone" festival, which is a celebration of the town's heritage.

However, things take a turn when McQueen's rival, Chick Hicks (voiced by Michael Keaton), arrives in Radiator Springs, seeking to sabotage McQueen's chances of winning the Piston Cup. As the championship approaches, McQueen must balance his racing ambitions with his newfound friendships and sense of responsibility towards the people of Radiator Springs.

In the end, McQueen learns a valuable lesson about the importance of friendship, community, and being true to oneself. He decides to abandon his original plan to win the Piston Cup and instead focuses on helping Radiator Springs revitalize its economy and restore its former glory. The film concludes with McQueen's return to Radiator Springs as a champion, but not just for winning the championship – for being a part of a community that has become like family to him.

Throughout the movie, Cars features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a heartwarming story that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, and finding one's true purpose. The film was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $462 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Cars 2 (2011) and Cars 3 (2017).

overview: Friends since childhood, a magazine editor and a hip-hop record executive stumble into romantic territory.
tagline: When did you first fall in love with hip-hop?
title: Brown Sugar
plot:
Brown Sugar is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of relationships, identity, and social class. The movie delves into the lives of two young African American women, Cheryl (Megan Good) and Darryl (Tasha Smith), who are struggling to find their place in the world.

The film's narrative is woven around themes of love, loyalty, and the pursuit of one's passions. Cheryl and Darryl's relationship is put to the test as they navigate their careers, family expectations, and personal desires. The movie also touches on issues of social class, highlighting the disparities between the haves and have-nots in the African American community.

One of the main themes of Brown Sugar is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Both Cheryl and Darryl are torn between their desire to pursue their dreams and the pressure to conform to societal expectations. The film suggests that true fulfillment can only be achieved by embracing one's authenticity and taking risks.

The movie also explores the complexities of female friendships, highlighting the ways in which women support and empower each other. The bond between Cheryl and Darryl is a central theme, as they navigate their relationships with men and themselves.

Ultimately, Brown Sugar is a film about finding one's own path and embracing the imperfections that make us human. It's a story about love, loss, and self-discovery, set against the vibrant backdrop of 1990s hip-hop culture.

overview: In 1940, the world is besieged by World War II. Wendy, all grown up, has two children; including Jane, who does not believe Wendy's stories about Peter Pan.
tagline: The Classic Continues
title: Return to Never Land
plot:
Return to Neverland is a 2002 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to Peter Pan, but it deviates from the original story and characters.

The film begins with Captain Hook's pirate ship being destroyed by the pirates of Neverland, led by Smee. The pirates are forced to flee, leaving Hook's right hand, Crocodile, behind. The Crocodile is left to guard Hook's treasure, which he believes will bring him back to life.

Meanwhile, Peter Pan and his fairy friend Tinker Bell are enjoying a peaceful life in Neverland with Wendy Darling and her children, John and Michael. However, their tranquility is disrupted when the pirates return, seeking revenge against Captain Hook for abandoning them.

The Crocodile, who has grown tired of waiting for Hook's return, decides to take matters into his own hands. It sets its sights on Peter Pan, believing that he will be the one to bring about Hook's resurrection. The Crocodile begins to terrorize Neverland, and Peter Pan must find a way to stop it.

As the story unfolds, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell embark on a journey to find the magical mermaid lagoon, where they hope to find a solution to the Crocodile's curse. Along the way, they meet new characters, including the mermaids and the pirate Smee, who has become disillusioned with his life of piracy.

The film takes a darker turn as Peter Pan and Tinker Bell face numerous challenges and obstacles, including the Crocodile's relentless pursuit. In the end, they discover that the only way to break the curse is for Hook to confront his own darkness and let go of his desire for revenge.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Hook's obsession with Peter Pan was fueled by his own feelings of inadequacy and jealousy. By confronting these emotions, Hook is able to find redemption and make amends with Peter Pan. The Crocodile, now freed from its curse, disappears into the sea, leaving Neverland in peace once again.

The film ends with a heartwarming moment between Peter Pan and Wendy Darling, as they reflect on the lessons learned from their adventures together. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even the most unlikely of heroes can find redemption and forgiveness.

Overall, Return to Neverland offers a unique take on the classic Peter Pan story, exploring themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of friendship. While it may not be as well-received as some of Disney's other films, it remains a beloved addition to the Peter Pan franchise.

original_title: Christmas Vacation 2: Cousin Eddie's Island Adventure
overview: Though Eddie's fired right at Christmastime, his boss sends him and his family on a South Pacific vacation, hoping Eddie won't sue him after being bitten by a lab monkey. When the Tuttle family winds up trapped on a tropical island, however, Eddie manages to provide for everyone and prove himself a real man.
title: Christmas Vacation 2: Cousin Eddie's Island Adventure
plot:
National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation 2: Cousin Eddie's Island Adventure is a 2003 American made-for-television comedy film, a spin-off and sequel to National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation (1989). Written by Matty Simmons, producer of the original Vacation film, it is the only entry in the franchise without Chevy Chase and Beverly D'Angelo as Clark and Ellen Griswold. Randy Quaid, Miriam Flynn and Dana Barron reprise their roles as Cousin Eddie, his wife Catherine and Audrey Griswold, with Jake Thomas and Fred Willard in the cast. It premiered on NBC on December 20, 2003.

Some time after the earlier film, Eddie's dirt farm has been foreclosed and his RV repossessed, so Audrey has taken in Eddie, Catherine, their dog Snots and their precocious youngest son, Clark III, known as "Third." Eddie works for the Chicago Atomic Testing Agency, which measures his brain waves for radioactivity, but when a chimpanzee named Roy outperforms him on every test, the budget-strapped agency fires him just before Christmas. After Eddie insults Roy and gets bitten, his boss, Professor Doornitz, fearing a lawsuit, offers the family an all-expenses-paid Christmas holiday in Maluka, a South Pacific island nation. They are joined by their cantankerous, lecherous Uncle Nick, whose wife Jessica has left him, and by Audrey, recently dumped by her boyfriend. Third, embarrassed by his father's failures, is not keen on the trip.

In Maluka, during a boat tour, Eddie hooks a huge shark that drags the boat far out to sea, and Nick crashes it on a reef off a seemingly deserted island. Determined to prove himself to his son, Eddie goes hunting and, falling from a tree onto his homemade spear, accidentally kills a wild boar, which the castaways roast for Christmas dinner; Third tells him for the first time that he is proud of him. On Christmas morning they exchange homemade gifts, but the grass hut Eddie and Third built collapses. A seaplane pilot, Melbourne Jack, reveals that his resort is just on the other side of the island, then suffers a concussion and passes out in mid-flight, and Eddie lands the plane with guidance from the Maluka tower. Jessica reconciles with Nick, and when Doornitz offers Eddie his old job back, Eddie declines: he is now a pilot in Maluka, with Roy as his co-pilot.

The film continued the Vacation franchise on television, with Barron becoming the first of the Griswold children to reprise an original role.

original_title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For
overview: Some of Sin City's most hard-boiled citizens cross paths with a few of its more reviled inhabitants.
tagline: There is no justice without sin.
title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For
plot:
Sin City: A Dame to Kill For is a 2014 American neo-noir crime anthology film directed by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller and written by Miller, the follow-up to the 2005 film Sin City. Its central story adapts A Dame to Kill For, the second book of Miller's comic series, a shorter segment comes from "Just Another Saturday Night", and two tales, "The Long Bad Night" and "Nancy's Last Dance", were written for the film. Mickey Rourke, Jessica Alba, Rosario Dawson, Jaime King, Powers Boothe and Bruce Willis return, joined by Josh Brolin, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Eva Green, Dennis Haysbert, Christopher Meloni, Jeremy Piven, Christopher Lloyd, Ray Liotta and Lady Gaga.

In the brief opening story, the brutish Marv wakes beside a wrecked police car surrounded by bodies and pieces together how he chased a group of rich college boys who had set a homeless man on fire. In "The Long Bad Night", a cocky young gambler, Johnny, wins a fortune from the ruthless Senator Roark at a backroom poker game. Roark, who recognizes him as his illegitimate son, has his fingers broken and his money taken, and later murders the waitress Johnny had taken out. Johnny scrapes together enough cash to challenge Roark again, humiliating him at the table a second time knowing the senator will kill him for it.

The title story, set before the events of the first film, follows Dwight McCarthy, a private detective struggling to keep his violent impulses in check, who is drawn back into the life of his former lover Ava Lord. Claiming that her wealthy husband, Damien, and his giant chauffeur, Manute, are abusing her, she persuades Dwight to help her, and with Marv's aid he storms the Lord estate and kills Damien, only for Ava to shoot him and reveal that she has manipulated him to gain her husband's fortune. Rescued and given a new face in Old Town with the help of Gail and the assassin Miho, Dwight returns for revenge, while Ava's seduction of a detective, Mort, ends in murder and suicide. In "Nancy's Last Dance", Nancy Callahan, haunted by the death of John Hartigan, whose ghost watches over her, scars herself and enlists Marv to help her storm Roark's compound and take her revenge.

After a premiere at Hollywood's TCL Chinese Theatre on August 19, 2014, The Weinstein Company opened it three days later. Unlike its predecessor, it was a box-office disappointment, earning about 40.7 million dollars against a production budget of around 65 million, and it received mixed reviews from critics.

overview: A gang of young thieves flee Paris during the violent aftermath of a political election, only to hole up at an Inn run by neo-Nazis.
tagline: What are your boundaries...
title: Frontier(s)
plot:
Frontier(s) is a 2007 French black comedy film directed by Hélène Cattet and Bruno Forzani. The movie follows a group of young friends who are stalked by a mysterious and sinister figure, known as "The Man in Black", during a weekend getaway at a remote cabin.

At its core, Frontier(s) explores the themes of toxic masculinity, violence, and the darker aspects of human nature. The film presents a world where men's aggression and competitiveness are normalized, and women are often seen as objects to be exploited or dominated. The main character, Pierre, embodies this toxic masculinity, and his actions drive the plot forward.

The movie also delves into the idea of isolation and how it can bring out the worst in people. As the group becomes more and more disconnected from society, their behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent. This serves as a commentary on how societal norms and expectations can shape our behavior, often leading us down a path of destruction.

Furthermore, Frontier(s) touches on the theme of power dynamics and control. The Man in Black is a symbol of patriarchal oppression, using his physical presence and intimidation to exert control over those around him. This serves as a commentary on how societal structures can perpetuate violence and oppression against marginalized groups.

Overall, Frontier(s) is a dark and unsettling film that critiques the toxic aspects of masculinity and societal norms. It presents a world where violence and aggression are normalized, and women are often seen as objects to be exploited or dominated.

original_title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Masters
overview: Po and the Furious Five uncover the legend of three of kung fu's greatest heroes: Master Thundering Rhino, Master Storming Ox, and Master Croc.
title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Masters
plot:
Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Master is an animated adventure film that delves into the complexities of mentorship, self-discovery, and the pursuit of one's true calling. The movie follows Po, a lovable and unlikely kung fu master, as he embarks on a journey to uncover the secrets of his legendary predecessor, Oogway.

At its core, the film explores the theme of finding one's purpose in life. Po's quest for knowledge and understanding is driven by his desire to become a true kung fu master, but along the way, he discovers that his unique strengths and weaknesses are what make him special. This realization allows him to break free from the constraints of traditional kung fu and forge his own path.

The movie also touches on the idea of legacy and the weight of expectation. Oogway's legacy is a powerful force that shapes Po's journey, but as Po delves deeper into the secrets of the master, he must confront the pressure to live up to expectations and forge his own identity.

Furthermore, Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Master explores the theme of balance and harmony in life. The film highlights the importance of embracing one's flaws and weaknesses, rather than trying to suppress or hide them. Po's journey is a metaphor for the human experience, where we must learn to accept ourselves and find balance within our own unique strengths and limitations.

Overall, Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Master is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that celebrates self-discovery, mentorship, and the power of embracing one's true nature.

overview: When an old collaborator gets severely injured, a veteran policeman tries to figure out the way to bring to justice the ultimately suspected aggressor, a spoiled young executive, heir to a mega corporation, who believes he is above the law.
tagline: The unstoppable. The untouchable.
title: Veteran
plot:
Veteran is a 2015 South Korean war drama film directed by Ryoo Seung-wan. The movie tells the story of a veteran police officer who returns to his hometown after serving in the military and struggles with PTSD, as well as the consequences of his actions during the war.

The main theme of Veteran revolves around the psychological toll of war on soldiers and civilians alike. It explores the emotional scars that veterans carry with them long after they return home, and how these scars can affect their relationships with loved ones. The film also delves into the themes of guilt, responsibility, and redemption, as the protagonist grapples with the consequences of his actions during the war.

Through the character's journey, the movie sheds light on the struggles faced by veterans who have seen and experienced things that no human should ever have to endure. It highlights the importance of acknowledging and addressing these issues, rather than trying to suppress or deny them. Ultimately, Veteran is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war and the need for empathy, understanding, and support for those affected by it.

The film's portrayal of PTSD and its effects on individuals and families is particularly noteworthy, as it adds depth and nuance to the story. The movie also touches on the theme of masculinity and how societal expectations can sometimes conflict with individual experiences, adding another layer of complexity to the narrative.

Overall, Veteran is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that sheds light on some of the most pressing issues facing veterans today.

overview: After she’s permanently blinded in a tragic car accident, Rebecca receives some bizarre news: her long-lost mother has recently passed away, leaving her their family’s ancestral castle in rural Albania. Traveling to the estate with a group of friends, Rebecca hopes it will be an opportunity for her to reconnect with a past she never knew and a mother who seemingly left her behind. When mysterious events begin to occur and her friends begin to die, Rebecca must unravel the secrets of her family’s history before she too falls prey to the Castle Freak.
tagline: Night has fallen
title: Castle Freak
plot:
Castle Freak is a 2020 American horror film directed by Stuart Gordon, based on the 1981 short story of the same name by H.P. Lovecraft.

The main themes of Castle Freak include:

1. **Isolation and confinement**: The story takes place in a remote location, where the protagonist, Dr. Marsten, is trapped with his niece, Lavinia, and her husband, William. This isolation creates an atmosphere of claustrophobia and heightens the sense of fear.
2. **The dangers of meddling with nature**: The film explores the idea that some things are better left alone, and that tampering with the natural world can have disastrous consequences. Dr. Marsten's experiments with the creature from Castle Freak ultimately lead to his downfall.
3. **The power of the unknown**: The movie taps into the fear of the unknown, as the characters are faced with a monstrous entity that defies explanation. This theme is classic Lovecraftian horror, where the protagonist's attempts to understand and control the creature only lead to more terror.
4. **Family dynamics and trauma**: The story also explores the complex relationships within the Marsten family, particularly between Dr. Marsten and his niece Lavinia. The film suggests that past traumas can have a lasting impact on individuals and families.

Overall, Castle Freak is a tense, atmospheric horror film that builds on the classic Lovecraftian themes of isolation, the unknown, and the dangers of meddling with nature.

overview: A group of teens discover secret plans of a time machine, and construct one. However, things start to get out of control.
tagline: Today is better the second time around
title: Project Almanac
plot:
Project Almanac is a 2015 American science fiction thriller film directed by Dean Georgaris and written by Dean Georgaris and Jeremy M. Johnson. The movie stars Jonny Weston, Allen Leinman, and Brittany Snow.

The story begins with three high school friends - Jake (Jonny Weston), Will (Allen Leinman), and Chris (Brittany Snow) - who are struggling to find their place in the world after graduation. They decide to make a time capsule that will be opened on December 31, 2015, as a way to cope with their impending adulthood.

While working on the project, they stumble upon an unusual equation that seems to defy the laws of physics. Intrigued, they begin to experiment with it, and after several failed attempts, they finally succeed in creating a functioning time machine.

Excited by their discovery, the friends decide to use the time machine to alter events from their past, hoping to improve their lives. However, as they start making changes, they realize that every decision has unintended consequences, and their actions begin to unravel the fabric of reality.

As the night wears on, Jake becomes increasingly obsessed with using the time machine to change his own life, while Will tries to keep a level head and maintain control over the situation. Chris, who had initially been hesitant about the project, begins to see the potential benefits of altering their past.

The friends' actions start to have catastrophic consequences, causing events from their past to unfold in unexpected ways. They soon realize that they are trapped in a time loop, reliving the same night over and over again as they try to fix their mistakes.

As the night wears on, Jake becomes more and more reckless, using the time machine to alter events for his own gain. Will tries to intervene, but Jake's actions become increasingly erratic, putting everyone at risk.

In a desperate attempt to break the cycle, Will uses the time machine to send Chris back in time, hoping that she will be able to prevent the catastrophic events from occurring. However, this plan ultimately fails, and the friends are left with no choice but to try and destroy the time machine before it's too late.

In the end, Jake is killed by a car while trying to use the time machine, and Will manages to destroy the device in an attempt to prevent further chaos. As the night comes to a close, Will reflects on the events that have transpired, realizing that some things are meant to be and that altering the past can have devastating consequences.

The movie ends with Will standing alone, looking out at the cityscape, as the clock strikes midnight, marking the end of 2015. The final shot is of the time capsule, which has been left untouched, a reminder of the friends' failed attempt to alter their lives and the unpredictable nature of time itself.

overview: While leading a police investigation of a massacre in a public school at the border of Mexico and U.S.A, special Agent Emanuel Ritter links this strange case to the coming and rising of the ancient demon Belzebuth. But in order to stop the trail of upcoming infanticides, Ritter shall have to confront himself before dealing with the forces of good and evil.
production_companies: Fondo de Inversión y Estímulos al Cine (FIDECINE)
tagline: Don't stop praying
title: Belzebuth
plot:
Belzebuth is a 2017 Mexican supernatural horror film directed by Emilio Portes, who co-wrote the screenplay. Joaquín Cosío stars as the police detective Emmanuel Ritter, with Tobin Bell, Tate Ellington, José Sefami and Yunuen Pardo in supporting roles. The film, which features dialogue in both Spanish and English, was completed in 2017 and released in January 2019.

The film opens in a hospital, where Ritter and his wife are celebrating the birth of their son. After Ritter leaves in response to a call from work, the baby is taken to the nursery. A nurse beginning her shift locks the nursery door, takes out a scalpel and murders Ritter's son and every other newborn in the room before slitting her own throat, all before anyone can break in to stop her.

Years later, Ritter remains traumatized and emotionally closed off, unable to come to terms with his son's death, haunted by the loss. He is called to investigate a mass shooting at an elementary school, which turns out to be one of a series of horrific massacres of children in the region, carried out by seemingly ordinary people who appear to have been overtaken by some outside force. Joined by Ivan Franco, an investigator who specializes in paranormal cases, Ritter begins to suspect that the killings are linked and that they share a supernatural cause. Their inquiry leads them to Vasilio Canavas, an excommunicated priest played by Bell, who may hold the key to understanding the evil behind the murders. As the investigation deepens, Ritter is drawn into a confrontation with a demonic force that appears to be targeting the children for a specific purpose, and he must face his own grief and loss of faith in order to stop it.

Belzebuth drew attention as an ambitious Mexican genre production combining a police procedural with demonic-possession horror, and for Bell's casting, which recalled his role as Jigsaw in the Saw series. It received generally favorable reviews, with 80 percent of 15 critics' reviews on Rotten Tomatoes being positive. Reviewers frequently singled out its shocking hospital prologue and its blend of crime-thriller and religious-horror conventions.

overview: Las Vegas showroom magician Cris Johnson has a secret which torments him: he can see a few minutes into the future. Sick of the examinations he underwent as a child and the interest of the government and medical establishment in his power, he lies low under an assumed name in Vegas, performing cheap tricks and living off small-time gambling "winnings." But when a terrorist group threatens to detonate a nuclear device in Los Angeles, government agent Callie Ferris must use all her wiles to capture Cris and convince him to help her stop the cataclysm.
tagline: If you can see the future, you can save it.
title: Next
plot:
Next is a 2007 American science fiction thriller film directed by Lee Tamahoni and starring Nicolas Cage.

The movie follows the story of Cris Johnson (played by Nicolas Cage), a professional gambler who has the ability to see glimpses of the future. He uses this gift to win at cards, but his life takes a dramatic turn when he is forced to go on the run after being targeted by a mysterious assassin.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cris's visions are not just random predictions, but rather fragments of a larger conspiracy involving a powerful organization known as "The Syndicate." The main theme of the movie revolves around the idea of fate and free will. Cris's ability to see glimpses of the future raises questions about whether his actions are truly his own or if they are predetermined by the events that have already transpired.

Throughout the film, Cage delivers a performance that showcases his signature intensity and charisma, bringing depth and nuance to the complex character of Cris Johnson. The movie's plot is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience engaged and guessing until the very end.

One of the main themes of Next is the concept of destiny vs. personal choice. As Cris navigates a world where his visions are both a blessing and a curse, he must confront the idea that his life has been predetermined by forces beyond his control. This theme is explored through Cris's relationships with other characters, particularly his love interest, Eva (played by Julia Stiles), who represents a chance for him to break free from his predetermined path.

Overall, Next is a thought-provoking thriller that explores complex themes and ideas, making it a compelling watch for fans of science fiction and action movies.

overview: In an alternate universe where twinned worlds have opposite gravities, a young man battles interplanetary prejudice and the laws of physics in his quest to reunite with the long-lost girl of his dreams in this visually stunning romantic adventure that poses the question: what if love was stronger than gravity?
tagline: Two worlds. One future.
title: Upside Down
plot:
"Upside Down" is a French science fiction film directed by Juan Pablo Gorostiza, released in 2012 under the production company France 2 Cinéma. The movie revolves around the story of two women from different worlds who fall in love despite being separated by a magical boundary.

The main themes of "Upside Down" include:

1. **Love transcending boundaries**: The film explores the idea that true love can conquer even the most impossible obstacles, including physical and emotional barriers.
2. **Identity and self-discovery**: The protagonist, Aurora (played by Ksenia Solo), is a young woman from a world where everything is upside down, literally. As she navigates her new reality, she must confront her own identity and sense of belonging.
3. **Social commentary on class and privilege**: The film critiques the social hierarchy of the two worlds, highlighting the disparities between the wealthy and powerful "Upsiders" and the poor and marginalized "Downsiders".
4. **Environmentalism and sustainability**: The magical boundary that separates the two worlds serves as a metaphor for the fragility of our planet's ecosystems and the consequences of human actions on the environment.
5. **Empowerment and female agency**: Aurora, as a strong-willed and determined protagonist, embodies the theme of female empowerment, challenging the patriarchal norms and expectations imposed upon her by society.

The movie's narrative is marked by a sense of wonder, curiosity, and adventure, as Aurora navigates this new world and falls in love with Samantha (played by Elisha Cuthbert), an "Upsider" who lives in a world that is literally the opposite of hers. The film's climax features a poignant and emotional confrontation between the two women, highlighting the power of their love to overcome even the most daunting obstacles.

Overall, "Upside Down" is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores complex themes and ideas through its unique blend of science fiction and romance.

overview: Black Panther is the ruler and protector of the African nation of Wakanda. Using technology, wits, and extraordinary fighting ability he must protect his nation from an invasion led by Ulysses Klaw, the man who killed his father.
title: Black Panther
plot:
Black Panther is an American motion comic series from Marvel Knights Animation, released here as a single two-hour feature compiling its six 20-minute episodes. Based on the Marvel Comics hero, it closely adapts "Who Is the Black Panther?", the story arc written by Reginald Hudlin and drawn by John Romita Jr., both of whom supervised the production, with Hudlin then serving as BET's president of entertainment; the main change from the comic is that Juggernaut replaces the Rhino. Mark Brooks and Jon Schnepp directed. Djimon Hounsou voices T'Challa, with Kerry Washington as Princess Shuri, Alfre Woodard as the Queen Mother and others, Jill Scott as Storm, Carl Lumbly as Uncle S'Yan, Stephen Stanton as Ulysses Klaw and Stan Lee as General Wallace.

In a secret briefing in Washington, the intelligence agent Everett K. Ross recounts the history of Wakanda, a technologically advanced African nation ruled by a warrior king who bears the title Black Panther, including King T'Chaka's defeat of a young Captain America. In the present, a masked challenger wins Wakanda's annual tournament for the throne, defeating the reigning Black Panther, T'Chaka's brother, and is revealed as Prince T'Challa, to the chagrin of his sister Shuri, who had hoped to compete. Now king, T'Challa must manage jealousy within the royal court while hunting the man who murdered his father.

That man, the assassin Klaw, has been rebuilt with cybernetic enhancements and is assembling a team of villains, among them Juggernaut, Batroc the Leaper, Cannibal, the Black Knight and the Radioactive Man, to invade Wakanda for its vibranium. The Queen Mother recalls T'Challa's youthful travels in Egypt, where he befriended the young mutant Storm, and Klaw remembers how he killed T'Chaka. When the assault comes, Juggernaut and the Black Knight lead the attack, Shuri is trapped in a vibranium mine with the Radioactive Man, and Storm comes to help on her own. T'Challa defeats the Black Knight in aerial combat, Shuri uses his fallen Ebony Blade against the Radioactive Man, and after a final battle in which Klaw is killed, T'Challa orders a force of American Deathlok soldiers out of his country.

The series aired on Australia's ABC3 in January 2010 and on BET in November 2011, was released on DVD in January 2011, and was posted free on Marvel's YouTube channel in 2018. Reviewers praised its cast and political themes while noting the limits of the motion-comic format.

original_title: Madagascar: A Little Wild Holiday Goose Chase
overview: Melman the Giraffe meets Hank, a goose who has been separated from his family and along with his friends, they embark on a wild goose chase around the city to reunite Hank with his merry flock.
title: Madagascar: A Little Wild Holiday Goose Chase
plot:
Madagascar: A Little Wild Holiday Goose Chase is a 2021 American animated holiday television special based on the preschool series Madagascar: A Little Wild, itself a spin-off of the Madagascar film franchise. Directed by Chad Van De Keere from a script by Laura Zak, it features the voices of Luke Lowe as Melman the giraffe, Shaylin Becton as Gloria the hippo, Tucker Chandler as Alex the lion and Amir O'Neil as Marty the zebra, with Mark Whitten as a lost goose, alongside Jasmine Gatewood and Eric Petersen. The 24-minute special premiered on 26 November 2021 on the streaming services Hulu and Peacock.

As in the series, the franchise's heroes are portrayed as young animals living together in the same habitat at New York's Central Park Zoo. With the holidays approaching, the anxious Melman has been meticulously charting the friends' naughty and nice deeds and fears that the naughty column is too long to earn them a place on the nice list. He leads the group in a series of good deeds around the zoo, involving the zoo train and a troop of chimpanzees who communicate in sign language, but each attempt backfires. Deciding they need to do good in the wider world, the friends slip out of the zoo by sliding through the city's sewers and emerge in the streets of New York, decorated for both Christmas and Hanukkah. There they meet Hank, a scatterbrained Canada goose who has become separated from his migrating family and cannot tell north from south. Seeing their chance at the perfect good deed, the friends embark on a wild goose chase around the city to reunite Hank with his flock, repeatedly confused by city noises that honk like geese. Along the way Melman learns that being good for its own sake matters more than being rewarded, and that being together is more important than presents.

John Serba of Decider recommended streaming it, calling the special mildly amusing and almost charming, a gentle and perfectly fine distraction for young children that would hold its target audience's attention, though unlikely to make anyone older than ten laugh out loud and not exactly a holiday classic. Joly Herman of Common Sense Media rated it suitable for ages five and up, noting its strong diversity, its mild peril and its messages about helping strangers and doing good deeds, while observing that male characters received more dialogue than female ones.

overview: Led by a strange dream, scientist Aki Ross struggles to collect the eight spirits in the hope of creating a force powerful enough to protect the planet. With the aid of the Deep Eyes Squadron and her mentor, Dr. Sid, Aki must save the Earth from its darkest hate and unleash the spirits within.
tagline: Unleash a new reality
title: Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within
plot:
Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within is a 2001 computer-animated science fiction film directed by Hironobu Sakaguchi, the creator of the Final Fantasy video game series. A Japanese-American co-production made by Square Pictures, it was the first feature film to attempt photorealistic computer-generated humans and, for nearly a decade, the most expensive film inspired by a video game. The voice cast includes Ming-Na Wen as Dr. Aki Ross, Alec Baldwin as Captain Gray Edwards, Donald Sutherland as Dr. Sid, James Woods as General Hein, Ving Rhames, Peri Gilpin and Steve Buscemi.

In 2065, Earth has been overrun by alien beings known as Phantoms, which kill living creatures on contact by consuming their spirit, while lesser contact can cause infection. The surviving humans live in "barrier cities" protected by energy shields. Aki, who has been infected by a Phantom, works with her mentor, Dr. Sid, who believes that the Phantoms can be neutralized by combining eight spirit waves, unique energy patterns found in various life forms. While searching for the sixth spirit in the ruins of New York City, Aki is rescued by Gray, her former lover, and his squad, the Deep Eyes, consisting of Ryan Whittaker, Neil Fleming and Jane Proudfoot.

Before the ruling council, Aki and Sid clash with General Hein, who wants to use the Zeus cannon, a powerful space-based weapon, to destroy the Phantoms at the site of the meteor on which they arrived. Sid warns that firing the cannon could harm the Earth's own spirit, or Gaia. Hein, embittered by the loss of his family to the Phantoms, manipulates events to win approval for the weapon, including allowing Phantoms into the barrier city. As Aki's infection worsens, her dreams reveal the truth about the Phantoms: they are the spirits of the inhabitants of a destroyed alien planet, still trapped in the throes of their death. With Hein determined to fire the cannon regardless of the consequences, Aki, Gray and Sid race to gather the final spirits and save the planet.

The film was celebrated for its technical achievement, but critics found its story dull and emotionally distant; it holds a 44 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49. It grossed about $85 million worldwide against a budget of around $137 million, becoming one of the biggest animated box-office failures and contributing to the closure of Square Pictures.

overview: On 15 January 2009, the world witnessed the 'Miracle on the Hudson' when Captain 'Sully' Sullenberger glided his disabled plane onto the Hudson River, saving the lives of all 155 souls aboard. However, even as Sully was being heralded by the public and the media for his unprecedented feat of aviation skill, an investigation was unfolding that threatened to destroy his reputation and career.
tagline: The Untold Story Behind the Miracle on the Hudson.
title: Sully
plot:
Sully is a biographical drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, released in 2016. The movie is based on the true story of Chesley Sullenberger III, an American commercial airline pilot who became a hero after landing a commercial airliner on the Hudson River in New York City on January 15, 2009.

The film begins with Chesley Sully (played by Tom Hanks), a seasoned pilot with over 40 years of experience flying for US Airways. He is married to his wife Lorrie (played by Anna Gunn) and has two children. Sully is known for his exceptional piloting skills and calm demeanor in emergency situations.

On the day of the incident, Sully is flying Flight 1549, a Boeing 767 aircraft carrying 155 people from New York's LaGuardia Airport to Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Shortly after takeoff, both engines fail due to a bird strike, leaving the plane without power. With no other options, Sully must make an emergency landing on the Hudson River.

As the situation unfolds, Sully and his co-pilot Jeff Skiles (played by Aaron Eckhart) work together to assess the damage and prepare for the landing. Despite the odds against them, Sully's experience and training enable him to navigate the plane through the icy waters of the Hudson River.

The film depicts the tense moments leading up to the landing, as well as the heroic actions taken by Sully and Skiles to save the lives of everyone on board. The movie also explores the aftermath of the incident, including the media frenzy and the subsequent investigation into the cause of the engine failure.

Throughout the film, Eastwood masterfully weaves together the drama and tension, using a combination of real-life footage and reenactments to recreate the events of that fateful day. Hanks delivers a nuanced performance as Sully, capturing the pilot's calmness and confidence in the face of disaster.

The movie also delves into the personal struggles of Sully, who is haunted by the incident and grapples with the weight of responsibility for saving the lives of everyone on board. The film ultimately concludes with Sully being cleared of any wrongdoing and receiving widespread acclaim for his heroism.

Overall, Sully is a gripping and emotionally charged drama that showcases Tom Hanks' exceptional acting skills. The film's attention to detail and commitment to accuracy make it a compelling watch, offering a unique glimpse into the life of one of America's most celebrated pilots.

original_title: Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li
overview: When a teenager, Chun-Li witnesses the kidnapping of her father by wealthy crime lord M. Bison. When she grows up, she goes on a quest for vengeance and becomes the famous crime-fighter of the Street Fighter universe.
tagline: Some fight for power. Some fight for us.
title: Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li
plot:
Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li is a 2009 American martial arts action film based on Capcom's Street Fighter video game series, directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak from a screenplay by Justin Marks. A non-canonical spin-off and tie-in to Street Fighter IV, and the second live-action adaptation after the 1994 film, it stars Kristin Kreuk as Chun-Li, Neal McDonough as M. Bison, Chris Klein as Interpol agent Charlie Nash, Michael Clarke Duncan as Balrog, Moon Bloodgood as detective Maya Sunee, Taboo as Vega and Robin Shou as Gen.

As a child, Chun-Li moves from San Francisco to Hong Kong with her family and trains in wushu under her father, Xiang. One night, the criminal organization Shadaloo abducts her father in front of her. Years later, Chun-Li has abandoned martial arts and become a celebrated concert pianist. After her mother dies of cancer, she receives a mysterious scroll written in ancient Chinese.

Meanwhile in Bangkok, the ruthless M. Bison seizes control of Shadaloo with the help of the masked assassin Vega, and police detective Maya Sunee teams up with Interpol agent Charlie Nash to investigate a massacre of crime families. Following the scroll's message, Chun-Li travels to Bangkok in search of a man named Gen. After days of fruitless searching, a fight with local gangsters leaves her unconscious, and she is rescued by Gen, a former associate of Bison, who offers to help her find her father on condition that she complete her martial arts training. Learning that Bison is forcing property owners to sign over their land so that Shadaloo can operate in the open, Chun-Li sets out to disrupt his plans, including a mysterious shipment known as the White Rose, and to confront the man who destroyed her family.

The film presents itself as an origin story for one of the series' most popular characters, focusing on revenge and self-discovery rather than the tournament format of the games.

Released on February 27, 2009, the film was not screened in advance for critics and opened in ninth place. It was a box office bomb, grossing 12.8 million dollars against a 50 million dollar budget, and was savaged by reviewers, holding just 3 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus blamed its shallow plot and miscast performers.

overview: The story of the first major battle of the American phase of the Vietnam War and the soldiers on both sides that fought it.
production_companies: Motion Picture Production GmbH & Co. Erste KG
tagline: 400 U.S paratroopers. 4,000 Vietnamese soldiers. 12,000 miles away from home. 1 man led them into battle.
title: We Were Soldiers
plot:
We Were Soldiers is a 2002 American war drama film directed by Randall Wallace, based on the book "We Were Soldiers Once... And Young" by Harold G. Schrier and George E. Wahlen. The film stars Mel Gibson as Lieutenant Colonel Hal Moore, a U.S. Army officer who led a company of soldiers during the Battle of Ia Drang in 1965.

The film begins with Lieutenant Colonel Hal Moore (Mel Gibson) arriving in Vietnam with his company, A Company, 1st Battalion, 7th Cavalry Regiment. The unit is tasked with conducting reconnaissance and gathering intelligence on the enemy. As they settle into their new surroundings, tensions rise between the American soldiers and the local Vietnamese villagers.

The story takes a dramatic turn when the North Vietnamese Army (NVA) launches a surprise attack on A Company's position in the Ia Drang Valley. The battle is intense and chaotic, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. Despite being outnumbered, Lieutenant Colonel Moore's leadership and tactical skills help to hold off the NVA, but not before several of his soldiers are killed or wounded.

As the battle rages on, it becomes clear that the NVA is using guerrilla tactics, employing hit-and-run attacks and booby traps to devastating effect. The American soldiers are forced to adapt quickly in order to survive, but they soon realize that they are facing a formidable enemy.

The film's climax features an intense and emotional confrontation between Lieutenant Colonel Moore and his men as they fight for their lives against overwhelming odds. Despite being vastly outnumbered, the Americans manage to hold off the NVA long enough for reinforcements to arrive, but not before several of their comrades have fallen in battle.

In the aftermath of the battle, Lieutenant Colonel Moore is hailed as a hero by his superiors, but he is also deeply shaken by the experience. The film ends with him reflecting on the cost of war and the sacrifices made by those who fight it.

Throughout the film, Mel Gibson delivers a powerful performance as Lieutenant Colonel Hal Moore, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Greg Kinnear, Adam Beach, and Sam Elliott, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall impact of the film.

Overall, We Were Soldiers is a gripping and intense war drama that explores the complexities and challenges of modern warfare. The film's attention to historical detail and its commitment to telling a true story make it a compelling watch for anyone interested in military history or drama.

original_title: The Kid Who Would Be King
overview: Old-school magic meets the modern world when young Alex stumbles upon the mythical sword Excalibur. He soon unites his friends and enemies, and they become knights who join forces with the legendary wizard Merlin. Together, they must save mankind from the wicked enchantress Morgana and her army of supernatural warriors.
tagline: An army to fight. A demon to slay. A world to save. No pressure.
title: The Kid Who Would Be King
plot:
The Kid Who Would Be King is a 2019 adventure fantasy film that pays homage to the classic Arthurian legend while infusing it with modern sensibilities. At its core, the movie explores the timeless themes of identity, responsibility, and the struggle between good and evil.

The story follows Alex, an awkward teenager who discovers he's the chosen one destined to save the world from the forces of darkness. As Alex navigates his newfound role, he must confront the weight of expectation and the pressure to live up to a legend. This internal conflict serves as a powerful metaphor for the challenges of adolescence, where self-discovery and growth are paramount.

The film also delves into the theme of friendship and camaraderie, highlighting the importance of supportive relationships in times of need. Alex's friendships with his peers serve as a counterbalance to the isolation and loneliness that often accompany adolescence, emphasizing the value of human connection in overcoming adversity.

Furthermore, The Kid Who Would Be King explores the idea of power and its corrupting influence. The villainous Mordru represents the dangers of unchecked ambition and the destructive nature of greed, serving as a cautionary tale about the importance of humility and selflessness.

Ultimately, the movie suggests that true heroism lies not in grand gestures or external validation but in the quiet, everyday acts of courage and kindness that define us as individuals. Through Alex's journey, the film reminds us that being a hero is not about destiny or privilege but about embracing our unique strengths and weaknesses to make a positive impact on the world around us.

overview: Jake and Sunti go to meet Mongkol, the leader of the Abu Karaf. Mongkol confirms that ever since the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, Jantapan has worked to corner the narcotics and arms markets. Jake must engage in a battle that will put both his physical and spiritual powers to the ultimate test.
tagline: A father's rage knows no limit.
title: Belly of the Beast
plot:
Belly of the Beast is a 2003 South Korean martial arts comedy film directed by Kang Je-gyu. The movie follows the story of a young man named Shin Joon-oh, who is sent to Japan to study and later becomes embroiled in a series of misadventures.

At its core, Belly of the Beast explores themes of cultural identity, belonging, and self-discovery. Shin Joon-oh's journey from Korea to Japan serves as a metaphor for the challenges of navigating unfamiliar cultures and finding one's place within them. As he navigates the complexities of Japanese society, he must confront his own sense of identity and reconcile his Korean heritage with his growing connection to Japanese culture.

The film also delves into themes of social class and economic inequality, particularly in the context of Japan's rigid social hierarchy. Shin Joon-oh's experiences as a poor Korean student in a wealthy Japanese high school serve as a commentary on the stark contrasts between different socioeconomic groups in Japan.

Furthermore, Belly of the Beast touches on the theme of mentorship and the importance of finding guidance from those who can offer wisdom and support. The character of Mr. Han, Shin Joon-oh's sensei, serves as a source of mentorship and encouragement, helping him navigate the challenges he faces in Japan.

Overall, Belly of the Beast is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores themes of identity, belonging, social class, and mentorship, all set against the vibrant backdrop of Japanese culture.

overview: On the gritty streets of LA, the destinies of four people desperate for connection and redemption are about to collide.
tagline: Every life has a breaking point
title: Powder Blue
plot:
Powder Blue is a 2009 American independent drama written and directed by Timothy Linh Bui, built around several interconnected stories set in Los Angeles in the days before Christmas. The ensemble cast includes Jessica Biel as the stripper Rose-Johnny, Forest Whitaker as Charlie, Eddie Redmayne as the undertaker Qwerty Doolittle, Ray Liotta as Jack Doheny, Lisa Kudrow as Sally, Kris Kristofferson as Randall and Alejandro Romero as Lexus. It also features Patrick Swayze as the club owner Velvet Larry, his final film role before his death in September 2009.

The film opens with a vision of a man walking naked into the sea and drowning. Charlie, a suicidal priest still grieving the wife he lost on their wedding day, drives around the city with a gun and fifty thousand dollars, trying to pay someone to kill him because his faith forbids him to do it himself. He approaches Lexus, a transgender sex worker, who refuses. Elsewhere, Rose-Johnny, a stripper at Velvet Larry's club who dreams of seeing Paris, loses her dog when her landlord throws it out.

Qwerty, a lonely, nervous undertaker facing eviction, accidentally hits the dog with his hearse and nurses it back to health, growing attached to it. Jack Doheny, an aging gangster dying of cancer, has just been released after twenty-five years in prison and receives a suitcase of money along with a lead on how to find his estranged family, which leads him to Velvet Larry's club and to Rose-Johnny, whose young son lies in a coma in a hospital. As Charlie bonds with a kind waitress named Sally and offers Qwerty money to end his life, the lives of these lonely, damaged people converge in unexpected ways.

The film is a melodrama about loneliness, grief, redemption and the healing power of human connection, set against the backdrop of the holiday season.

Powder Blue received only a limited theatrical release in the United States and was released principally on DVD in May 2009. Critics were negative: Variety found its heartstring-pulling contrivances over the top, felt that Biel overacted and called Bui's message about love both loud and tone-deaf.

overview: Presenting the tale of American founding father Alexander Hamilton, this filmed version of the original Broadway smash hit is the story of America then, told by America now.
tagline: An American Musical.
title: Hamilton
plot:
Hamilton is a 2020 American filmed stage production of the Broadway musical Hamilton, written by Lin-Manuel Miranda and inspired by Ron Chernow's 2004 biography of Alexander Hamilton. Directed by Thomas Kail, who staged the original production, and co-produced by Kail, Jeffrey Seller and Miranda, it was recorded over three performances at the Richard Rodgers Theatre in New York in June 2016 with the show's original Broadway cast. Miranda stars as Hamilton, with Leslie Odom Jr. as Aaron Burr, Phillipa Soo as Eliza Hamilton, Renée Elise Goldsberry as Angelica Schuyler, Christopher Jackson as George Washington, Daveed Diggs as the Marquis de Lafayette and Thomas Jefferson, Jonathan Groff as King George III, Anthony Ramos and Okieriete Onaodowan.

Told almost entirely through song, blending hip hop, R&B, jazz and traditional show tunes, and performed by a deliberately diverse cast portraying the Founding Fathers, the musical follows Hamilton's life in two acts, with Burr serving as the principal narrator. The first act traces Hamilton's arrival in New York as an ambitious, penniless immigrant from the Caribbean, his friendships with revolutionary figures, his service as aide-de-camp to George Washington during the American Revolutionary War, his marriage to Eliza Schuyler and his close bond with her sister Angelica, and his rise as a lawyer and one of the authors of The Federalist Papers.

The second act follows Hamilton's tenure as the first Secretary of the Treasury, his political clashes with Thomas Jefferson and James Madison, and his affair with Maria Reynolds, which becomes a public scandal. Tragedy strikes when his son Philip is killed in a duel, and the family must reckon with grief. Meanwhile, Hamilton's long rivalry with Burr intensifies as their political ambitions collide, culminating in the 1804 duel in which Burr fatally shoots him. The finale reflects on legacy and on Eliza's decades of work preserving her husband's memory.

Disney originally planned a theatrical release in 2021 but, because of the COVID-19 pandemic, released the film on Disney+ on 3 July 2020, where it drew a large audience. It received universal acclaim for its performances and for Kail's filming, which used multiple cameras and close-ups to capture the stage show. It won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Variety Special (Pre-Recorded), among other honors.

overview: Alex, an assassin-for-hire, finds that he's become a target after he refuses to complete a job for a dangerous criminal organization. With the crime syndicate and FBI in hot pursuit, Alex has the skills to stay ahead, except for one thing: he is struggling with severe memory loss, affecting his every move. Alex must question his every action and whom he can ultimately trust.
tagline: His mind is fading. His conscience is clear.
title: Memory
plot:
Memory is a psychological thriller film directed by Michael Cusack, released in 2022 by Open Road Films.

The movie follows the story of Ruth (played by Alba Baptista), a young woman who suffers from short-term memory loss due to an accident. She wakes up every day with no recollection of her past or identity. As she tries to navigate her life, she meets a mysterious man named Marcus (played by Daniel Radcliffe) who seems to know more about her than he's letting on.

As Ruth and Marcus grow closer, they begin to unravel the mystery surrounding Ruth's past and the circumstances that led to her memory loss. Along the way, they encounter a series of cryptic clues and eerie events that suggest something sinister is at play.

Throughout the film, Ruth's memories are fragmented and unreliable, making it difficult for her (and the audience) to distinguish reality from fantasy. The movie's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each scene building upon the previous one to create a sense of tension and unease.

One of the standout aspects of Memory is its exploration of themes such as identity, trauma, and the human condition. Ruth's struggles to come to terms with her past serve as a metaphor for the fragility of human memory and the ways in which our experiences shape us.

The film features strong performances from both Baptista and Radcliffe, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the eerie atmosphere of Ruth's world with a blend of stark realism and surrealism.

Overall, Memory is a thought-provoking and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its complex narrative and exploration of themes, it's sure to leave you pondering long after the credits roll.

overview: “My plan was to die before the money ran out,” says 60-year-old penniless Manhattan socialite Frances Price, but things didn’t go as planned. Her husband Franklin has been dead for 12 years and with his vast inheritance gone, she cashes in the last of her possessions and resolves to live out her twilight days anonymously in a borrowed apartment in Paris, accompanied by her directionless son Malcolm and a cat named Small Frank—who may or may not embody the spirit of Frances’s dead husband.
title: French Exit
plot:
French Exit is a 2021 American comedy-drama film directed by Susanna White. The movie follows the story of Delphine Hallett, a former socialite who embarks on a journey to Paris with her cat, Mimi, after being abandoned by her husband.

The main theme of French Exit revolves around the exploration of identity, loneliness, and the human desire for connection in a world that often seems to be moving away from traditional values. Delphine's character is a complex and nuanced portrayal of a woman who has been stripped of her social status and forced to confront the emptiness of her life.

As Delphine navigates the streets of Paris, she begins to rediscover herself and find solace in the city's beauty and culture. The film also touches on themes of class, privilege, and the societal expectations placed upon women, particularly those who have been marginalized or excluded from mainstream society.

Through Delphine's journey, French Exit offers a poignant commentary on the human condition, highlighting the importance of self-discovery, resilience, and the power of human connection in the face of adversity. The film is a nuanced exploration of what it means to be alone, and how one can find meaning and purpose in a world that often seems to be moving too fast.

overview: Set in postwar America, a man watches his seemingly perfect life fall apart as his daughter's new political affiliation threatens to destroy their family.
tagline: A radically ordinary story.
title: American Pastoral
plot:
American Pastoral is a 2016 drama film directed by Ewan McGregor, based on Philip Roth's novel of the same name.

The movie delves into the complexities of the American Dream and its illusions. It explores the theme of disillusionment as it follows the story of Seymour "Swede" Levov, a successful businessman who appears to have it all - wealth, status, and a beautiful family. However, beneath the surface, Swede's life is marked by emptiness, disconnection, and a sense of disorientation.

The film also examines the tension between individualism and conformity, as embodied by Swede's wife, Naomi, who struggles with her own identity and desires within the confines of their seemingly perfect suburban life. The movie portrays the ways in which societal expectations can suffocate personal freedom and creativity.

Furthermore, American Pastoral touches on the theme of violence and its effects on individuals and communities. The film's portrayal of a violent confrontation between Swede and his son, Danny, serves as a catalyst for exploring the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of unchecked emotions.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced critique of the American Dream, revealing it to be an unattainable illusion that can lead to feelings of disconnection, disillusionment, and despair.

overview: A chronicle biopic of the 22-year career of soccer star Roberto Baggio, including depictions of his difficult debut as a player, his deep rifts with some of his coaches, his triumph over injuries and personal discovery of Buddism.
title: Baggio: The Divine Ponytail
plot:
Baggio: The Divine Ponytail (Italian: Il Divin Codino) is a 2021 Italian biographical sports drama directed by Letizia Lamartire and written by Ludovica Rampoldi and Stefano Sardo, based on the life of the footballer Roberto Baggio. Andrea Arcangeli plays Baggio, with Valentina Bellè as his wife, Andreina, Andrea Pennacchi as his father, Florindo, and Thomas Trabacchi. Netflix released the film for streaming on 26 May 2021.

The film chronicles the 22-year career of one of Italy's greatest footballers, from his youth to his retirement, focusing on his relationships with his family, his difficult beginnings as a professional, his conflicts with some of his coaches, his many injuries and his embrace of Buddhism. It opens with the young Baggio dreaming of winning the World Cup for Italy against Brazil and avenging the defeat in the 1970 final, a dream encouraged by his demanding father, whose approval he spends much of his life seeking.

After a serious knee injury early in his career threatens to end it, Baggio finds strength in Buddhist practice and recovers to become a star of Italian football. The defining moment of his career comes at the 1994 World Cup in the United States, where, after a difficult start, he almost single-handedly leads Italy to the final against Brazil, the chance to fulfil his childhood dream. The match goes to a penalty shoot-out, and Baggio misses the decisive kick, handing the trophy to Brazil. In the later part of his career, he hopes to play in the 2002 World Cup, but suffers a serious injury near the end of the Serie A season. He returns to the field just 77 days later, yet the national coach, Giovanni Trapattoni, controversially leaves him out of the squad. The film ends with Baggio surrounded by the support of his family and friends and the enduring affection of the fans who have followed him throughout his career.

The film received mixed reviews; it holds a 75 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on a small number of reviews. Ben Kenigsberg of The New York Times found it muddled, arguing that it never conveys why Baggio became so beloved and that it treats the football perfunctorily on the pitch.

overview: Laura and Massimo's relationship hangs in the balance as they try to overcome trust issues while a tenacious Nacho works to push them apart.
title: The Next 365 Days
plot:
The Next 365 Days is a Polish erotic drama film directed by Olaf Modrzejowski, based on the novel "365 Dni Prawdziwe" (365 Days) by Blanka Lipińska. The movie serves as a sequel to the original 2020 film.

The story follows Ola Młynarska (played by Anna Maliszewska), who has just been released from prison after serving her sentence for murdering her abusive boyfriend, Sławomir (played by Łukasz Rysiński). As she tries to rebuild her life, Ola is approached by a wealthy and charming businessman named Massimo Torricelli (played by Michele Morrone), who offers her a deal: in exchange for his help with her financial situation, she will become his girlfriend.

Ola accepts the offer, but soon realizes that Massimo's intentions are not entirely pure. Despite their tumultuous relationship, Ola finds herself drawn to Massimo's charismatic and confident personality. As they navigate their complicated feelings for each other, Ola must confront her past traumas and learn to trust herself again.

Throughout the film, Ola struggles with her own darkness and the consequences of her actions in the previous installment. The movie explores themes of toxic relationships, emotional manipulation, and the blurred lines between love and obsession.

The Next 365 Days received mixed reviews from critics, who praised Anna Maliszewska's performance but criticized the film's handling of sensitive topics such as domestic abuse and consent. Despite this, the movie has maintained a dedicated fan base, particularly among viewers who enjoyed the original 2020 film.

Overall, The Next 365 Days is a complex and thought-provoking exploration of toxic relationships and personal growth. While it may not be to everyone's taste, fans of the original film will likely find themselves invested in Ola's journey as she navigates her complicated feelings for Massimo.

overview: At the age of 89, Julián Moreno takes one last bus ride to El Paso, Texas, to visit his daughters and their children – a lengthy trip he has made without fail every month for decades. After returning to rural Mexico, he quietly starts building a house in the empty lot next to his home. In the absence of his physical visits, can this new house bridge the distance between his loved ones?
title: What We Leave Behind
plot:
What We Leave Behind is a 2022 Mexican-American documentary film directed by Iliana Sosa, who co-wrote it with editor Isidore Bethel. A Spanish-language portrait of Sosa's grandfather, Julián Moreno, filmed over several years, it was produced by Emma D. Miller and Sosa through Borderchild Productions and Marcona Media with JustFilms, and developed with support from the Sundance Institute, the IDA, the Austin Film Society and the Gotham Documentary Lab, among others. It premiered at South by Southwest in March 2022, received a theatrical release from Ava DuVernay's ARRAY, and debuted on Netflix in several English-speaking countries on 30 September 2022. It runs 71 minutes.

For about twenty years, Julián made a monthly 560-mile bus trip from his home in San Juan del Río, in the Mexican state of Durango, to El Paso, Texas, to visit his daughters and grandchildren, bringing candy and gifts and leaving after a day or two. As the film begins, he is 89 and making the last of these journeys. Widowed at 45 and the father of seven, some still in his hometown and some in the United States, he once worked as a bracero, a seasonal contract labourer in the US, and he shows his granddaughter his 1964 Alien Laborer's Identification Card. Back in rural Mexico he begins building a cinderblock house on the empty lot beside the small home he shares with his son Jorge, who is blind, and their dog Pinto, a project that, like his cross-border visits, is meant to keep the family close. In a conversation with Jorge, Sosa explores the death of her grandmother at 39 and its effect on the family, and the film visits her grave in the busy local cemetery. Lyrical interludes pair Sosa's voiceover with images of the surrounding landscape, while the soundtrack features an a cappella song by the Cardencheros de Sapioriz, also from Durango. Over the following years the film records Julián's growing frailty and his final days.

What We Leave Behind won the Fandor New Voices Award and the Louis Black "Lone Star" Award at SXSW and was nominated for Best Documentary at the Gotham Awards. It drew universal acclaim, with a Metacritic score of 89 and a perfect Rotten Tomatoes rating. Sheri Linden of The Hollywood Reporter called it first-person filmmaking at its eloquent best, the Boston Globe found it limpid and poetically resonant, and The New York Times named it a Critic's Pick.

overview: The story begins with a regular Joe who tries desperately to seek employment, but embarks on a violent rampage when he teams up with cult leader Uncle Dave. Their first act is to heist an amusement park, only to learn that the Taliban are planning the same heist as well. Chaos ensues, and now the Postal Dude must not only take on terrorists but also political figures.
tagline: Some comedies go too far... others start there.
title: Postal
plot:
Postal is a 2007 action comedy based on the Postal video game series, directed by Uwe Boll, who co-wrote the screenplay. It stars Zack Ward as the Postal Dude, Dave Foley as his Uncle Dave, Chris Coppola, Jackie Tohn as Faith, J. K. Simmons, Verne Troyer as himself, Larry Thomas as Osama bin Laden, David Huddleston and Seymour Cassel. Known for its deliberately offensive humor, the film satirizes terrorism, religion, politics and Boll's own reputation, with the director appearing as himself.

The film opens with a provocative parody of the September 11 attacks. Five years later, in the dead-end town of Paradise, Arizona, the Postal Dude is thrown out of the unemployment office and discovers that his wife is cheating on him. Desperate to leave town, he teams up with his slovenly Uncle Dave, a con artist turned doomsday cult leader who owes the government more than a million dollars in back taxes.

The Dude comes up with a plan to hijack a shipment of Krotchy Dolls, a rare and highly sought-after plush toy, so that his uncle can resell them online. Unknown to them, Osama bin Laden and a band of al-Qaeda operatives have been hiding in Paradise since 9/11 and plan to steal the same shipment, infect the dolls with avian influenza and distribute them to American children. When both groups converge on Little Germany, a German-themed amusement park where the dolls are being delivered, the result is a massive shootout. Escaping with the dolls and the park's guest of honor, Verne Troyer, the Dude and the cult are pursued by terrorists, police and an angry mob. After betrayal within the cult, the Dude and a barista named Faith set out on a violent rampage against everyone who wants them dead.

Boll framed the film as a political satire attacking all sides, mixing slapstick, shock humor and graphic violence in the anarchic spirit of the games.

Postal was released in Germany on October 18, 2007, and in the United States on May 23, 2008. It was a box office flop, earning about 146,000 dollars against a 15 million dollar budget, and holds 9 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a witless satire, though one of Boll's more successful films, and a Metacritic score of 22.

overview: Several ordinary high school students go through their daily routine as two others prepare for something more malevolent.
title: Elephant
plot:
Elephant is a 2003 American drama film written and directed by Gus Van Sant. The movie is loosely based on the 1967 film "Easy Rider" and explores several themes, including:

1. **Violence and its consequences**: The film depicts a series of violent events that unfold in Los Angeles after a high school football game, leading to a tragic confrontation between two rival gangs. The movie examines the devastating effects of violence on individuals and society.
2. **Youth culture and disillusionment**: Elephant portrays a group of disaffected teenagers struggling with identity, belonging, and purpose. The characters' experiences reflect the frustrations and disillusionments of young people in contemporary America.
3. **Social hierarchy and class divisions**: The film highlights the stark contrasts between different social classes, particularly in Los Angeles. The characters from different backgrounds interact, revealing tensions and conflicts that arise from their differences.
4. **Mortality and existentialism**: Elephant grapples with the inevitability of death and the search for meaning in life. The characters' experiences are marked by a sense of disorientation and disconnection, reflecting the uncertainty and anxiety that accompany adolescence.
5. **The impact of media on society**: The film critiques the way media can shape public perception and influence social behavior. In this case, the violence depicted in the movie serves as a catalyst for further conflict.

Throughout the film, Van Sant employs a non-linear narrative structure, using multiple storylines to explore these themes. The movie's title, Elephant, refers to the massive animal that is both majestic and intimidating, reflecting the complex emotions and conflicts that arise among the characters.

Overall, Elephant is a thought-provoking drama that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of human relationships, social dynamics, and the search for meaning in a chaotic world.

overview: In 1981, an enthusiastic young adventurer follows his dreams into the Bolivian Amazon jungle with two friends and a guide with a mysterious past. Their journey quickly turns into a terrifying ordeal as the darkest elements of human nature and the deadliest threats of the wilderness lead to an all-out fight for survival.
tagline: Nature has only one law - Survival
title: Jungle
plot:
Jungle is a 2017 Australian biographical drama film directed by David Wenham, based on the memoir of the same name by Yossi Ghinsberg.

The main themes of Jungle include:

1. **Survival and Resilience**: The film tells the story of Yossi Ghinsberg's harrowing experiences in the Amazon jungle, where he was stranded for 76 days with limited supplies. The movie showcases his determination to survive against all odds, highlighting his resilience and resourcefulness.
2. **Self-Discovery and Identity**: As Yossi navigates the unforgiving environment, he is forced to confront his own identity, values, and sense of purpose. The film explores his journey of self-discovery, as he grapples with feelings of isolation, loneliness, and disconnection from his past.
3. **Human Connection and Loneliness**: Despite being surrounded by nature's beauty, Yossi feels deeply disconnected from the world around him. The movie highlights the importance of human connection in our lives, emphasizing the need for relationships and community to overcome even the most daunting challenges.
4. **Cultural Exchange and Understanding**: Jungle also explores the complexities of cultural exchange and understanding between Westerners and indigenous communities. Yossi's experiences with the Ticuna people serve as a catalyst for his growth, forcing him to confront his own biases and assumptions about different cultures.

The film features stunning cinematography, capturing the breathtaking beauty of the Amazonian rainforest, which serves as a backdrop for Yossi's transformative journey.

overview: When an evil emperor executes their leader, his band of knights – bound by duty and honour – embarks on a journey of vengeance that will not come to an end until they've destroyed their mortal foe.
title: Last Knights
plot:
