Last Knights is an action-adventure film that delves into the complexities of honor, loyalty, and redemption in a medieval setting. The movie follows William Thatcher, a humble blacksmith who becomes embroiled in a battle between good and evil as he seeks to protect his village from the forces of darkness.

At its core, Last Knights explores the theme of redemption, as William's journey is driven by a desire to make amends for past mistakes and prove himself as a worthy knight. The film also examines the nature of honor, highlighting the tension between personal code and societal expectations. As William navigates the treacherous world of medieval politics, he must confront the gray areas between right and wrong, ultimately leading him to question what it truly means to be a hero.

Furthermore, Last Knights touches on the theme of loyalty, as William forms strong bonds with his fellow knights and villagers, who come to rely on him for protection. The film's portrayal of these relationships serves as a counterpoint to the more cynical, self-serving motivations of the villainous characters, emphasizing the importance of genuine connections in a world often driven by power and ambition.

Overall, Last Knights is a story about personal growth, the power of redemption, and the enduring value of loyalty and honor in the face of adversity.

overview: A chronicle of country music legend Johnny Cash's life, from his early days on an Arkansas cotton farm to his rise to fame with Sun Records in Memphis, where he recorded alongside Elvis Presley, Jerry Lee Lewis and Carl Perkins.
tagline: Love is a burning thing.
title: Walk the Line
plot:
Walk the Line is a 2005 American biographical drama directed by James Mangold, who wrote the screenplay with Gill Dennis, drawing on Johnny Cash's autobiographies Man in Black (1975) and Cash: The Autobiography (1997). Joaquin Phoenix stars as Cash and Reese Witherspoon as June Carter, with Ginnifer Goodwin as Cash's first wife, Vivian Liberto, Robert Patrick as his father, Ray, and Dallas Roberts as Sam Phillips.

The film opens in 1968 as Cash waits backstage at Folsom State Prison, where the sight of a table saw takes him back to his childhood. In 1944, 12-year-old Johnny lives on a cotton farm in Dyess, Arkansas, with his brother Jack and a harsh father. When Jack dies in a sawmill accident while Johnny is off fishing, Ray tells him the Devil took the wrong son. Johnny joins the Air Force in 1950 and, while stationed in West Germany, buys a guitar and starts writing songs, among them "Folsom Prison Blues".

Back home in 1954, he marries Vivian and settles in Memphis, struggling as a door-to-door salesman until he forms a band and auditions for Phillips at Sun Records, who signs them after hearing "Folsom Prison Blues". Touring as Johnny Cash and the Tennessee Two alongside Elvis Presley, Carl Perkins, Roy Orbison and Jerry Lee Lewis, he falls for country singer June Carter, who keeps him at arm's length but becomes his friend. As his fame grows, so does his dependence on pills and alcohol. Over Vivian's objections he brings June on tour; after a night together in Las Vegas, June sees him taking pills and pulls back, and he collapses on stage. Watching his decline, she starts writing "Ring of Fire". Cash is arrested after buying drugs in Mexico, his marriage collapses, and he moves to Nashville, buying a lakeside house in Hendersonville in an attempt to win June back. After a bitter Thanksgiving argument with his father, he goes through detox with June at his side. They begin a tentative romance, though she keeps turning down his proposals. Learning that most of his fan mail comes from prisoners, he records a live album at Folsom. On a later tour, he halts a duet of "Jackson" to propose on stage, and June finally accepts.

The film grossed $186.4 million worldwide on a $28 million budget and earned strong reviews, with 83% on Rotten Tomatoes. Witherspoon won the Academy Award for Best Actress, Phoenix was nominated for Best Actor, and the film won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy.

overview: Sara is a teen girl who is looking forward to her 18th birthday to move away from her controlling father Don. But before she could even blow out the candles, Don imprisons her in the basement of their home.
title: Girl in the Basement
plot:
I have information on "Girl in the Basement" (2021). 

"Girl in the Basement" is a psychological thriller television film that premiered on Lifetime in 2021. The movie follows the story of Sarah, a young woman who returns to her childhood home after being away for several years. She discovers that her mother has been living in the basement and claims she's been taking care of herself.

As Sarah tries to reconnect with her mother, she begins to uncover disturbing secrets about their family's past. Her mother reveals that she was involved in a cult-like group when Sarah was younger, and that she had been hiding from the outside world for years.

Sarah becomes increasingly unsettled as she learns more about her mother's past and the reasons behind her isolation. She starts to question everything she thought she knew about her family and their history. As tensions rise between Sarah and her mother, it becomes clear that there is more to the story than meets the eye.

Throughout the film, Sarah struggles with feelings of anger, betrayal, and confusion. Her relationship with her mother deteriorates as she tries to understand why her mother has been keeping such a dark secret from her for so long.

The movie takes a dark turn when it's revealed that Sarah's mother was involved in some sinister activities, including human trafficking and abuse. As the truth comes to light, Sarah is forced to confront the reality of her family's past and the harm that has been done.

Ultimately, "Girl in the Basement" is a gripping thriller that explores themes of trauma, family secrets, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly the lead actress who brings depth and nuance to the complex character of Sarah.

overview: A woman's seaside vacation takes a dark turn when her obsession with a young mother forces her to confront secrets from her past.
tagline: Being a mother is a crushing responsibility.
title: The Lost Daughter
plot:
The Lost Daughter is a 2021 psychological drama film directed by Maggie Gyllenhaal, based on the novel of the same name by Elena Ferrante.

The main themes of The Lost Daughter include:

Identity: The film explores the theme of identity through the character of Leda Caruso (played by Olivia Colman), who is struggling to reconcile her past and present selves. As she reflects on her life, she grapples with feelings of disconnection and fragmentation, highlighting the complexities of female identity.

Motherhood: The movie delves into the complexities of motherhood, particularly the expectations placed upon women to be perfect caregivers. Leda's experiences as a mother are marked by guilt, anxiety, and self-doubt, underscoring the societal pressures that can lead to feelings of inadequacy.

Trauma and Memory: The film explores the theme of trauma and its impact on memory and identity. Leda's past is marked by traumatic events, which she tries to suppress or forget, but ultimately resurface in her present. This highlights the complex relationship between memory, trauma, and personal growth.

Feminism and Empowerment: Through Leda's character, the film critiques societal expectations of women and challenges traditional notions of femininity. As Leda navigates her past and present, she begins to reclaim her agency and assert her own desires, illustrating a path towards empowerment and self-discovery.

The Lost Daughter also explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for connection, as Leda grapples with feelings of disconnection from herself and others.

overview: When Pete and Ellie decide to start a family, they stumble into the world of foster care adoption. They hope to take in one small child but when they meet three siblings, including a rebellious 15 year old girl, they find themselves speeding from zero to three kids overnight.
tagline: Just add chaos, laughter, awkwardness, mistakes, love...
title: Instant Family
plot:
Instant Family is a 2018 American comedy-drama film directed by Sean Anders and John Morris, written by Anders and Morris, and produced by Peter Chernin, James Lassiter, and others.

The movie follows Pete (played by Mark Wahlberg), a police officer who has been married to his wife Ellie (played by Rose Byrne) for five years. They have been trying to start a family but are having trouble conceiving. After a series of failed attempts at adoption, they decide to become foster parents through the local social services agency.

The couple is initially met with skepticism and resistance from their neighbors and friends, who think that becoming foster parents will be too much for them. However, after meeting Lizzie (played by Isabela Moner), a 15-year-old girl who has been living in foster care, they decide to take the plunge and become foster parents.

As Pete and Ellie navigate the world of foster parenting, they face numerous challenges, including dealing with difficult children, navigating the complexities of social services, and trying to balance their own relationship. They also meet Juan (played by Gustavo Quiroz), a 17-year-old boy who becomes part of their family.

Throughout the movie, Pete and Ellie learn valuable lessons about love, sacrifice, and the importance of being present for their children. As they navigate the ups and downs of foster parenting, they come to realize that their own relationship is stronger than ever.

One of the standout aspects of Instant Family is its portrayal of the complexities of foster care. The movie tackles tough topics such as trauma, attachment issues, and the emotional challenges faced by foster children. However, it also offers a hopeful and heartwarming message about the power of love and family to overcome even the toughest obstacles.

The cast delivers strong performances throughout the movie, with Mark Wahlberg and Rose Byrne bringing warmth and humor to their roles as Pete and Ellie. Isabela Moner shines as Lizzie, bringing a depth and nuance to her character that is both heartbreaking and inspiring.

Overall, Instant Family is a heartwarming and hilarious comedy-drama that explores the ups and downs of foster parenting with sensitivity and wit. With its talented cast, engaging storyline, and uplifting message, it's a must-see for anyone who has ever wondered what it takes to become a parent.

overview: Corinne (Barbie) is a young country girl who heads to Paris to pursue her big dream – to become a female musketeer! Never could she imagine she would meet three other girls who secretly share the same dream! Using their special talents, the girls work together as a team to foil a plot and save the prince. It's all for one and one for all!
title: Barbie and the Three Musketeers
plot:
Barbie and the Three Musketeers is a 2009 computer-animated fantasy film, the sixteenth entry in the Barbie film series, loosely inspired by Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel The Three Musketeers. Kelly Sheridan voices Barbie as Corinne, daughter of the famous musketeer d'Artagnan, with Tim Curry as the villainous Philippe, and Kira Tozer, Willow Johnson and Dorla Bell. It was released on DVD on 15 September 2009 and made its television debut on Nickelodeon that November.

In 17th-century France, seventeen-year-old Corinne lives on a farm with her mother and dreams of becoming a musketeer like her father, while her kitten, Miette, dreams of being a "mus-cat-eer." When they travel to Paris, Corinne's hopes are quickly dashed. She is mocked, especially by Philippe, the cousin and adviser of Prince Louis, whose dog, Brutus, steals and damages her letter of introduction to Monsieur Tréville, the former captain of the musketeers, who tells her she is not ready. A chase involving Brutus and Miette leads to trouble with three palace maids, Aramina, Viveca and Renée, and Corinne ends up hired by Madame de Bosse as a maid herself.

The four young women soon become friends. When a chandelier falls and nearly crushes the prince, they defend themselves from the fragments with remarkable skill, and Corinne finds evidence that the rope was cut deliberately. Discovering that the others share her dream of becoming musketeers, Corinne and her friends are led through a secret passageway by the old maid Hélène, who reveals herself to be a former musketeer and agrees to train them, teaching them to use everyday objects such as fans and ribbons as weapons. As the girls uncover a plot by Philippe to murder Louis and seize the throne before the prince's coronation, they must use their training to protect the prince, culminating in a confrontation at a masked ball.

Common Sense Media gave the film three stars out of five, finding it a decent attempt that misses the mark, while DVD Verdict judged its animation unremarkable and said it offered little for adults, though children would find it perfectly enjoyable. The film's story emphasizes friendship, teamwork and the courage to pursue one's dreams despite the doubts of others.

overview: A thief makes a disturbing discovery in the house where he breaks in. Later, when he returns to the same house with his partner in crime, things are no longer how he expected.
title: Bad Samaritan
plot:
Bad Samaritan is a 2018 American thriller film directed by David Mackenzie and written by Matt Bomer, based on the novel "The 7 1/2 Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle" by Stuart Turton.

The main themes of Bad Samaritan (2018) include:

1. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The protagonist, Cale Erendreich (played by Robert Sheehan), is a complex character struggling to find his place in the world. As he navigates his relationships with others, particularly the wealthy and influential family he becomes embroiled with, he grapples with questions of identity and self-discovery.

2. **Social Class and Inequality**: The film critiques the social hierarchy and class divisions that exist in society. Cale's desire to infiltrate the wealthy family's lives serves as a commentary on the ways in which those from lower socio-economic backgrounds often feel like outsiders, seeking acceptance and belonging through any means necessary.

3. **Psychological Manipulation and Gaslighting**: The film explores the theme of psychological manipulation, particularly in the context of relationships between men and women. Cale's actions are motivated by a desire to control and manipulate those around him, while also being manipulated himself.

4. **Morality and Ethics**: As Cale becomes more entrenched in his scheme, he is forced to confront the moral implications of his actions. The film raises questions about right and wrong, encouraging viewers to consider the consequences of their own behavior.

5. **Isolation and Loneliness**: Throughout the film, Cale's isolation and loneliness are palpable. His inability to form genuine connections with others serves as a reminder that even those who appear confident and self-assured can be hiding deep-seated vulnerabilities.

Overall, Bad Samaritan (2018) is a thought-provoking thriller that explores complex themes and characters, leaving viewers to ponder the moral implications of Cale's actions long after the credits roll.

overview: Alice Kingsleigh returns to Underland and faces a new adventure in saving the Mad Hatter.
tagline: It's time for a little madness.
title: Alice Through the Looking Glass
plot:
Alice Through the Looking Glass is a 2016 American fantasy adventure film directed by James Bobin and written by Linda Woolverton, based on the 1865 novel "Through the Looking-Glass" by Lewis Carroll. The film serves as a sequel to the 2010 film Alice in Wonderland.

The story begins with Alice (Mia Wasikowska) living a mundane life in London, struggling to cope with the loss of her mother and the pressures of growing up. She is visited by the Red Queen's (Helena Bonham Carter) sister, the White Queen (Anne Hathaway), who informs Alice that she has been chosen to fulfill an ancient prophecy that will determine the fate of Wonderland.

The White Queen explains that the Red Queen's power is waning, and only Alice can restore balance to the kingdom by finding the three magical mirrors. The mirrors hold the secrets of Wonderland's past, present, and future, and their combined power can bring peace to the land.

Alice embarks on a perilous journey through the Looking Glass, facing various obstacles and creatures along the way. She encounters the Cheshire Cat (Barney Williams), who serves as her guide and confidant, and Tarrant Hightopp (Rhys Ifans), a charming but troubled pirate who becomes her ally.

As Alice navigates the fantastical world, she discovers that the Red Queen's power is fueled by the negative emotions of those around her. The more people fear and hate, the stronger the queen's magic becomes. Alice realizes that she must confront her own fears and doubts in order to break the curse and restore balance to Wonderland.

Throughout her journey, Alice encounters a range of characters, including the Mad Hatter (Johnny Depp), who is struggling with his own identity crisis, and the Tweedle brothers (Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Sonya Walger), who serve as comedic relief. She also meets the Queen of Hearts' (Helena Bonham Carter) loyal subjects, the playing cards, who are determined to stop Alice from fulfilling her destiny.

As Alice draws closer to finding the magical mirrors, she faces increasingly formidable challenges. The Red Queen's power grows stronger, and Alice must confront her own darkness in order to overcome the obstacles in her path.

In the end, Alice successfully retrieves the three mirrors and uses their combined power to break the curse that has been cast over Wonderland. The Red Queen's power is restored, but not at the cost of her own humanity. Alice returns home, forever changed by her experiences in Wonderland, with a newfound appreciation for the complexities of life and the importance of facing one's fears.

The film concludes with Alice reflecting on the lessons she learned during her journey, realizing that the true magic lies within herself and that the power to change the world begins with understanding oneself.

overview: Novelist Catherine Tramell is once again in trouble with the law, and Scotland Yard appoints psychiatrist Dr. Michael Glass to evaluate her. Though, like Detective Nick Curran before him, Glass is entranced by Tramell and lured into a seductive game.
production_companies: IMF Internationale Medien und Film GmbH & Co. 3. Produktions KG
tagline: Everything interesting begins in the mind
title: Basic Instinct 2
plot:
Basic Instinct 2 (released in some markets as Basic Instinct 2: Risk Addiction) is an erotic thriller from 2006, directed by Michael Caton-Jones and written by Leora Barish and Henry Bean, the sequel to Basic Instinct (1992). Sharon Stone reprises her role as the crime novelist Catherine Tramell, opposite David Morrissey as the psychiatrist Dr. Michael Glass, with Charlotte Rampling and David Thewlis.

In London, Catherine is speeding through the city at night with her companion, the football star Kevin Franks, when she loses control during a reckless sexual encounter and plunges the car into the West India Docks. She gets out, but Franks dies, and she coolly tells police that her own life mattered more to her than his. Detective Superintendent Roy Washburn of Scotland Yard reveals that a paralysing drug was found in both the car and the dead man's body and that Franks had stopped breathing before the crash, but Catherine denies the drug dealer's claim that he sold it to her.

Dr. Glass, who assessed her for the court and judged her a narcissist, begins treating her. She toys with him, and he becomes frustrated and fascinated, even though he has just begun dating a fellow psychiatrist, Michelle. Then people in his life start dying: the journalist boyfriend of his ex-wife, Denise, who had been writing a critical article about one of Glass's old cases, is strangled; Denise and Catherine's dealer are murdered too. As police suspicion turns toward Glass, Washburn tells him Catherine is the killer and is setting him up. Glass confronts her, they sleep together, and she hands him the manuscript of her new novel, The Analyst, which turns recent events into fiction and names a character based on his colleague Dr. Milena Gardosh as the next victim. Racing to Gardosh's flat, he finds Catherine already there; Gardosh tells him she has taken over Catherine's case and that his licence will be revoked. In the struggle he knocks Gardosh out, seizes Catherine's gun and shoots Washburn when the detective arrives. Later, visiting Glass in a psychiatric hospital, Catherine suggests that he committed the murders himself and is feigning madness, leaves him a signed copy of her bestseller, and walks out as he smiles.

The film was cut to avoid an NC-17 rating. It was a notorious flop, grossing $38.6 million worldwide on a $70 million budget, and was savaged by critics, with 6% on Rotten Tomatoes. It won four Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture and Worst Actress.

overview: Heidi, a radio DJ, is sent a box containing a record - a "gift from the Lords". The sounds within the grooves trigger flashbacks of her town's violent past. Is Heidi going mad, or are the Lords back to take revenge on Salem, Massachusetts?
tagline: We've been waiting... we've always been waiting
title: The Lords of Salem
plot:
The Lords of Salem is a 2012 supernatural horror film written, produced and directed by Rob Zombie. It stars Sheri Moon Zombie as Heidi, a troubled disc jockey in Salem, Massachusetts, alongside Bruce Davison, Jeff Daniel Phillips, Ken Foree, Patricia Quinn, Dee Wallace, María Conchita Alonso, Judy Geeson and Meg Foster. A novelization by Zombie and B. K. Evenson was published a month before the film's release.

Heidi, a recovering drug addict, hosts a hard rock radio show with her colleagues Whitey and Munster. She receives a wooden box containing a record by a band called the Lords, whose eerie music gives her a vision of Satan-worshipping women ritually giving birth to a baby. When the station plays the record, Salem's women fall into a trance. Heidi's landlady, Lacy, and Lacy's sisters, Sonny and Megan, take an unusual interest in her, and in the supposedly vacant apartment 5 she experiences visions of a demon and a witch who commands her to "bleed us a king." Her nightmares worsen, and she relapses into drug use.

Meanwhile Francis Matthias, an author who interviewed Heidi about his book on the Salem witch trials, discovers that the Lords' music matches a centuries-old score. He learns that in the late 17th century Reverend Jonathan Hawthorne had a coven of witches executed for using the music to control Salem's women, and that their leader, Margaret Morgan, cursed the town's women and Hawthorne's descendants, whose bloodline would bear the devil's child. Matthias realizes Heidi is a descendant of Hawthorne, but before he can warn her, Lacy and her sisters, themselves witches, murder him while Heidi listens and does nothing. At the Lords' concert, the sisters and the ghosts of Margaret's coven perform a satanic rite. The music drives the women in the audience to strip, and amid surreal visions Heidi gives birth to a monstrous creature. The next day, the radio reports the mass suicide of 32 female descendants of Salem's original settlers at the concert and Heidi's disappearance.

Shot from October 2011, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 10, 2012, and was given a limited US release by Anchor Bay Films on April 19, 2013, grossing about $1.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, praising its atmosphere but finding it short on scares; Rotten Tomatoes reported 45% approval and Metacritic a score of 57. Several critics have read it as a metaphor for drug addiction.

overview: The Angels are charged with finding a pair of missing rings that are encoded with the personal information of members of the Witness Protection Program. As informants are killed, the ladies target a rogue agent who might be responsible.
tagline: This summer the Angels are back.
title: Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle
plot:
Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle is a 2003 action comedy film directed by McG and written by John Brancato, Michael Ferris, and Shane Black. The movie stars Cameron Diaz, Drew Barrymore, and Lucy Liu as the iconic Charlie's Angels trio.

The film begins with Dylan Sanders (Drew Barrymore) and Natalie Cook (Cameron Diaz), two of the top Angels, on a mission to stop a group of thieves who have stolen a valuable artifact. However, things take a turn when they discover that the thief is none other than their former partner, Madison Lee (Lucy Liu).

Madison has been working with a new partner, Alex Munday (Derek Zane Unger), and together they plan to steal a valuable diamond necklace. The Angels must use their skills and teamwork to stop them.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Madison's betrayal is not just about personal gain, but also about revenge against her former partners. She has been working with a wealthy businessman, Will Stacks (Derek Zane Unger), who has been using his wealth and influence to manipulate people and get what he wants.

The Angels soon discover that Will is behind the theft of the diamond necklace and that Madison's betrayal was just a ruse to get close to him. The team must now work together to stop Will and his accomplices, including a group of skilled thieves known as "The Shadow Syndicate."

Throughout the film, the Angels face various challenges and obstacles as they try to stay one step ahead of their enemies. Along the way, they also have to deal with their own personal demons and relationships.

In the end, the Angels successfully stop Will and his accomplices, but not before Madison reveals that she has been working undercover to bring down Will from the inside. The film ends with the Angels celebrating their victory and reflecting on the lessons they've learned about teamwork, loyalty, and trust.

Overall, Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle is an action-packed comedy that follows the adventures of three iconic female characters as they take on a complex web of villains and challenges. With its blend of humor, style, and high-stakes action, the film is a fun and entertaining ride from start to finish.

overview: The true story of how businessman Oskar Schindler saved over a thousand Jewish lives from the Nazis while they worked as slaves in his factory during World War II.
tagline: Whoever saves one life, saves the world entire.
title: Schindler's List
plot:
Schindler's List is a historical drama film directed by Steven Spielberg, released in 1993 by Universal Pictures. The movie is based on the true story of Oskar Schindler, a German businessman who saves the lives of thousands of Jews during the Holocaust.

The film begins in 1939, with Oskar Schindler (played by Liam Neeson), a charismatic and cunning German entrepreneur, arriving in Krakow, Poland. Schindler is initially drawn to the city's thriving industrial scene and sees an opportunity to make a fortune by producing enamelware for the Polish army. However, as the Nazi occupation of Poland intensifies, Schindler becomes increasingly aware of the atrocities being committed against the Jewish population.

Despite his initial reluctance, Schindler begins to employ Jewish workers in his factory, including a young man named Itzhak Stern (played by Ben Kingsley). As the Nazis' persecution of Jews escalates, Schindler uses his connections and charm to persuade the Nazi authorities to allow him to continue employing Jewish laborers. In return, he agrees to provide them with food, shelter, and protection.

As the war rages on, Schindler's factory becomes a hub for Jewish refugees, including women and children. He also begins to use his influence to smuggle Jews out of the ghetto and into his factory, where they are protected from persecution. Schindler's actions are motivated by a combination of self-interest and a growing sense of empathy for the Jewish people.

However, as the Nazis' grip on Poland tightens, Schindler faces increasing pressure to comply with their demands. He is forced to make difficult choices, including turning over some of his Jewish workers to the Nazis in exchange for protection. Despite these challenges, Schindler continues to find ways to help more and more Jews escape persecution.

The film's climax takes place in 1944, as the Nazis prepare to liquidate the Krakow ghetto. Schindler uses his connections with high-ranking Nazi officials to persuade them to spare the lives of his Jewish workers. In a dramatic and emotional scene, Schindler presents his list of employees to the Nazi commander, Amon Göth (played by Ralph Fiennes), in an effort to save as many lives as possible.

The film ends with Schindler's factory being liberated by Soviet troops, and Schindler standing outside, surrounded by the survivors he has saved. The final shot is of a list, which appears to be Schindler's original list of employees, now inscribed with the names of over 1,000 Jews who were saved from certain death.

Throughout the film, Spielberg masterfully weaves together historical fact and fiction, creating a powerful and emotional portrayal of one man's courage in the face of unimaginable evil. The performances by the cast, particularly Liam Neeson and Ben Kingsley, are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. Schindler's List is a testament to the human spirit's capacity for compassion, empathy, and resilience in the face of adversity.

overview: A disgraced basketball coach is given the chance to coach Los Amigos, a team of players who are intellectually disabled, and soon realizes they just might have what it takes to make it to the national championships.
tagline: When winning isn't everything
title: Champions
plot:
Champions (Spanish: Campeones) is a 2018 Spanish sports comedy-drama directed by Javier Fesser, who co-wrote it with David Marqués. Javier Gutiérrez stars as the basketball coach Marco Montes, with Athenea Mata as his wife, Sonia, and Juan Margallo as Julio, alongside a team of players with intellectual disabilities. The story was inspired by Aderes, a team from Burjassot, near Valencia, made up of people with intellectual disabilities, which won twelve Spanish championships between 1999 and 2014.

Marco is the arrogant, short-tempered assistant coach of the professional basketball club CB Estudiantes. During a game he argues with the head coach over strategy and shoves him, and is promptly fired. That same night he drives drunk into the back of a police car. In court he is given a choice between two years in prison and ninety days of community service, which will consist of coaching Los Amigos, a team of players with intellectual disabilities.

At first Marco makes no secret of his contempt for the players and refers to them with a slur. As the weeks pass, though, he comes to know each of them, their individual histories and quirks, and he is struck by their persistence and their commitment to one another. His home life, meanwhile, is strained: Sonia wants a baby, and Marco insists he is not ready. A friend of Marco's, Iván, who is attracted to Sonia, tries to manoeuvre some time alone with her, but Marco turns up anyway, and the couple leave still at odds. Travelling to away games proves chaotic, as the team's blunt and boisterous behaviour constantly clashes with fellow passengers on public transport. When Marco confides in Sonia, she borrows a camper van from a colleague at the sporting-goods shop where she works and starts travelling with the team, and their marriage begins to heal. Los Amigos fight their way to second place in the national championship, Marco agrees to start a family with Sonia, and when he returns to professional coaching the players thank him for changing their lives.

Released in Spain by Universal on 6 April 2018, it was the country's highest-grossing Spanish-language film of the year, taking €19.1 million from 3.3 million admissions. It won three Goya Awards, including Best Film and Best New Actor for Jesús Vidal, and was Spain's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. It inspired a sequel and remakes in Arabic, German, English, directed by Bobby Farrelly, and Hindi.

overview: Better watch out! The big guy in red is coming to town once again. This time, Scott Calvin -- also known as Santa Claus -- finds out there's an obscure clause in his contract requiring him to take on a wife. He has to leave the North Pole to fulfill his obligations, or else he'll be forced to give up his Yuletide gig.
tagline: What's Christmas Fun without some Reindeer Games?
title: The Santa Clause 2
plot:
The Santa Clause 2 is a Christmas comedy film released in 2002, directed by Michael Lembeck and written by Leo Benvenuti, Steve Rudnick, and Rick Mulvaney. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1994 film The Santa Clause.

The story begins with Scott Calvin (Tim Allen), who has now been living as Santa Claus for over five years. He is struggling to balance his life as a father and husband with his duties as the new Santa. His wife, Carol (Elizabeth Mitchell), is pregnant with their first child, but she's not sure if Scott can handle being Santa full-time.

Meanwhile, a group of elves from the North Pole arrive at Scott's house, warning him that Christmas Eve is approaching and he must return to the North Pole to prepare for the holiday. However, Scott is hesitant to leave his family behind, especially since Carol has just discovered she's pregnant with their first child.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Scott's doubts about being Santa grow stronger. He begins to question whether he's truly cut out for the job and starts to feel like a "fake" Santa. The elves try to convince him that he's doing a great job as Santa, but Scott is unconvinced.

On Christmas Eve, disaster strikes when a group of naughty children, led by a young boy named Tucker (Eric Lloyd), steal the magical crystal that gives Scott his powers. Without the crystal, Scott loses his Santa powers and is forced to return home for Christmas.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Scott's son Charlie (Eric Lloyd) discovers the truth about his father's identity as Santa. Charlie is initially excited to have a real-life Santa Claus as a dad, but he soon realizes that being Santa comes with its own set of challenges and responsibilities.

As Christmas Day approaches, Scott must find a way to regain his powers and save Christmas. With the help of his elves and Carol, Scott embarks on a journey to retrieve the magical crystal and restore his powers. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about being a good father, husband, and Santa Claus.

In the end, Scott successfully retrieves the crystal and regains his powers as Santa. The movie concludes with Scott returning to the North Pole, where he is welcomed back by the elves and Mrs. Claus (Judge Reinhold). Scott also gets to spend Christmas with his family, including his son Charlie, who has learned to appreciate the challenges and joys of being a part of the Claus family.

The Santa Clause 2 received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $140 million worldwide. The movie's blend of humor, heart, and holiday cheer made it a beloved favorite among families around the world.

overview: Two brothers live in the economically-depressed Rust Belt, when a cruel twist of fate lands one in prison. His brother is then lured into one of the most violent crime rings in the Northeast.
tagline: Sometimes your battles choose you.
title: Out of the Furnace
plot:
Out of the Furnace is a 2013 American drama film directed by Scott Cooper and written by Brad Pitt, David Michôd, and Scott Cooper. The movie stars Christian Bale, Casey Affleck, and Woody Harrelson.

The main themes of Out of the Furnace revolve around:

1. **The struggle for survival**: The film is set in a small Pennsylvania town where coal mining is the primary source of employment. The story follows two brothers, Russell (Casey Affleck) and Chris (Christian Bale), who are struggling to survive amidst economic hardship, poverty, and personal demons.
2. **Brotherly love and loyalty**: The bond between the two brothers is a central theme in the film. Despite their differences, they rely on each other for support and protection. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that their relationship is tested by external circumstances and internal conflicts.
3. **The American Dream**: Out of the Furnace critiques the idea of the American Dream, which promises prosperity and success to those who work hard enough. The film shows how this dream can be an illusion, especially for those living in poverty-stricken areas with limited job opportunities.
4. **Trauma and PTSD**: Chris's experiences during the Iraq War have left him with physical and emotional scars. His struggles to cope with his trauma are a significant aspect of the story, highlighting the long-term effects of war on individuals and families.
5. **Redemption and forgiveness**: Throughout the film, characters grapple with guilt, shame, and redemption. The brothers' relationship is particularly affected by Chris's past mistakes, which he tries to make amends for through his actions in the present.

The movie explores these themes through a gritty, realistic portrayal of life in a small American town struggling with economic decline and personal hardship.

overview: Something bizarre has come over the land. The kingdom is deteriorating. People are beginning to act strange... What's even more strange is that people are beginning to see dragons, which shouldn't enter the world of humans. Due to all these bizarre events, Ged, a wandering wizard, is investigating the cause. During his journey, he meets Prince Arren, a young distraught teenage boy. While Arren may look like a shy young teen, he has a severe dark side, which grants him strength, hatred, ruthlessness and has no mercy, especially when it comes to protecting Teru. For the witch Kumo this is a perfect opportunity. She can use the boy's "fears" against the very one who would help him, Ged.
tagline: Once Man and Dragon were one. Man chose Land and Sea, Dragon chose Wind and Fire.
title: Tales from Earthsea
plot:
Tales from Earthsea (Gedo Senki) is a 2006 Japanese animated epic fantasy produced by Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, marking the directorial debut of Gorō Miyazaki, who also co-wrote it. It draws on elements of the first four books of Ursula K. Le Guin's Earthsea series and on Hayao Miyazaki's illustrated story Shuna's Journey. The Japanese voice cast includes Junichi Okada as Prince Arren, Aoi Teshima as Therru, Bunta Sugawara as the archmage Sparrowhawk, Yūko Tanaka as the warlock Cob and Teruyuki Kagawa as the slaver Hare; the English dub features Timothy Dalton, Willem Dafoe and Cheech Marin.

Dragons fighting in the skies above a storm are taken as an omen that the world's balance is failing. In the kingdom of Enlad, where plague is spreading, young Prince Arren inexplicably kills his father the king, takes his sword and runs away. Rescued from wolves in the desert by the archmage Sparrowhawk, he travels with him to Hort Town, where he saves a girl, Therru, from the slaver Hare, only to be captured himself. Sparrowhawk frees him and brings him to the farm of his old friend Tenar, who has taken in Therru, a scarred girl abandoned by her parents. Sparrowhawk's meddling angers Cob, the sorcerer who rules Hort Town.

Arren admits to Therru what he has done and confesses that he feels something pursuing him, which turns out to be his own double. Fleeing it, he collapses in a swamp and is taken to Cob's castle, where the warlock learns his true name, Lebannen, and uses it to control him. Hare kidnaps Tenar to lure Sparrowhawk, who discovers that Cob is upsetting the balance by opening the door between life and death in pursuit of immortality. Sparrowhawk breaks Cob's hold over Arren but is captured. Therru meets Arren's double, the light within him, and learns his true name; she finds the despairing prince and restores his hope, sharing her own true name, Tehanu. Arren finally draws his sword, sealed by magic until then, and cuts off Cob's hand. The ageing warlock seizes Therru and strangles her atop a tower, but she is revealed to be an immortal dragon and destroys him. Arren returns home with Sparrowhawk to atone, promising to come back.

Released in July 2006, the film topped the Japanese box office for five weeks and was the year's highest-grossing domestic film, but reviews were mixed; it won the Bunshun Raspberry Award for worst film while earning a Japan Academy Prize nomination.

overview: A group of teens in a small town come across a strange object that tests their loyalties to each other with increasingly destructive consequences the deeper into the game they go.
tagline: Win together or die alone
title: The Friendship Game
plot:
The Friendship Game is a 2022 Canadian science fiction horror film directed by Scooter Corkle, his second feature, from the first feature-length screenplay by Damien Ober. Produced by Social Construct and Scythia Films, it stars Peyton List, Brendan Meyer, Kelcey Mawema, Kaitlyn Santa Juana and Dylan Schombing, with Miranda Edwards and Jennifer Copping in supporting roles. RLJE Films released it in the United States on 11 November 2022.

Zooza, known as Z (List), Rob (Meyer), Courtney (Mawema) and Cotton (Santa Juana) are close friends in a small town who are at a turning point in their lives as they prepare to leave for college. While browsing at a yard sale, Z and Cotton come across a strange orb-like object, and the ominous woman selling it tells them that it is "the Friendship Game", which tests true friendship by having the players reveal their deepest desires. Unfazed, they buy it, and all four friends place their fingers on the object and confess what they most want. Their wishes come at an unexpected cost that begins to consume their lives: at a party soon afterwards, Cotton tries to warn the others that something is wrong, discovers Z and Rob together and storms off, and then disappears, prompting a police investigation. Meanwhile Kyle (Schombing), who spends most of his time at his computer, has been secretly watching the four friends, and the film increasingly blurs the digital and physical worlds with glitching, warped imagery. Told in chapters from each character's perspective, the story shows how the game sets the friends against one another with increasingly destructive consequences the deeper they go.

Reviews were largely negative, although Peyton List's performance was widely praised. Chase Hutchinson of Collider likened the premise to Wish Upon (2017) and felt the film gestured at the existential, internet-age concerns of We're All Going to the World's Fair, but said that, despite some occasionally enrapturing visuals, it spun its wheels and leaned on conventional scares that failed to land. Bobby LePire of Film Threat called it awful on every level except for List, who he said made the cringe-inducing dialogue believable and was the only cast member to inject real drama or fear, while criticising the rest of the cast, singling out Meyer for lacking screen presence. Screen Rant described it as a frustrating horror mystery that felt like a messy rough draft.

overview: In 2013 there are no highways, no I-ways, no dreams of a better tomorrow, only scattered survivors across what was once the Unites States. Into this apocalyptic wasteland comes an enigmatic drifter with a mule, a knack for Shakespeare and something yet undiscovered: the power to inspire hope.
tagline: The year is 2013. One man walked in off the horizon and hope came with him.
title: The Postman
plot:
The Postman is a post-apocalyptic drama film directed by Kevin Costner, released in 1997 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

In a dystopian future, the United States has been ravaged by nuclear war and environmental disasters, leaving behind a barren wasteland. The story follows a grizzled survivor, known only as "The Postman" (played by Kevin Costner), who embarks on a perilous journey to deliver a message of hope to the scattered communities.

The film begins with The Postman, a former postal worker, living in a desolate world where people have lost all sense of community and connection. He is haunted by his past and struggles to find purpose in this new world. One day, he discovers a cache of letters and newspapers that had been preserved in a bunker, which sparks a glimmer of hope within him.

The Postman sets out on a mission to deliver these messages to the remaining communities, using his knowledge of the pre-war world to navigate the treacherous landscape. Along the way, he encounters various obstacles, including marauders, raiders, and other hostile groups who seek to exploit the vulnerable.

As The Postman travels across the country, he begins to inspire others with his message of hope and unity. He forms alliances with a group of survivors, including a young woman named Abby (played by Olivia Williams) and her son, Wyatt (played by Brian Bloom). Together, they face numerous challenges and dangers, but also experience moments of tenderness and connection.

Throughout the film, The Postman's character undergoes significant development. He begins to see himself as a leader and a symbol of hope for the people he encounters. His actions inspire others to come together and rebuild their communities, and he becomes a beacon of light in a world that has lost its way.

The climax of the film takes place at a community center where The Postman delivers a final message of hope to a group of survivors. In a poignant moment, he reads out a letter from his wife, who had passed away before the nuclear war, and shares it with the community. This act of vulnerability and connection brings the people together, and they begin to rebuild their lives.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with The Postman standing in front of a newly rebuilt community center, surrounded by people who have come together to start anew. Though the world is still scarred by the nuclear war, there is a sense of possibility and renewal that fills the air.

Overall, The Postman is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores themes of hope, resilience, and community in the face of adversity. Kevin Costner's performance as The Postman is nuanced and compelling, bringing depth and complexity to this iconic character.

overview: After leaving a life of crime and violence, Ray is a reformed good guy, enjoying a quiet family life in the ‘burbs. But when his past is discovered, Ray is blackmailed into one last job to collect a mysterious package. After a deadly double-cross, he finds himself wounded and on the run from ruthless assassins who will stop at nothing to get what he has. Now, with the lives of his loved ones hanging in the balance and danger at every turn, Ray’s only hope is to draw upon his violent past to survive.
title: Run & Gun
plot:
Run & Gun, also known as The Ray, is an American action thriller written and directed by Christopher Borrelli, set among the ruins of California's Salton Sea. It stars Ben Milliken as Ray, a former criminal, with Mark Dacascos as Brando, Janel Parrish as Ray's girlfriend Faith, Richard Kind as the eccentric mob boss Grayson, Celestino Cornielle as Ninni, Brad William Henke as Billings, Ari Barkan as Perry and Hudson Yang.

The story opens with two men being driven into the desert by a mobster to be executed. One of them, Ray, survives a hanging, kills the assassin and befriends the other captive, Lupe. Two years later, Ray has gone straight as a successful insurance investigator, living in an RV and dating Faith, a single mother who invites him to move in with her and her son. His new life is threatened when Lupe, now in prison, warns him that gangsters have seen him visiting.

Soon afterwards, Ray is summoned by Grayson, who forces him to carry out two tasks or see Faith and her son killed: poison a neighbor's tree, and intercept a mysterious package bound for a rival. Grayson's assistant Brando gives Ray a bag containing 440,000 dollars to exchange for the package, but after the handover Ray is ambushed and shot in the stomach by Ninni and his brother, who pursue him across the desert. Ray kills the brother, hides the money and the package in an abandoned car, and staggers wounded through the wasteland until he reaches a factory, where a security guard named Billings offers to help. Ray soon discovers that his rescuer is even more dangerous than the gangsters hunting him, and he must survive long enough to recover the bags and protect the people he loves.

The film combines a crime thriller with darkly comic touches, including Grayson's obsession with the Mandela effect and the theory that the package can influence what the world believes.

Run & Gun was released in the United States in 2022 after a limited release under its original title. Reviewers generally described it as a modest, quirky low-budget crime thriller with uneven pacing and a predictable plot.

overview: A story about the complex connection with a brother who is based in Mexico, meant to be a metaphor of the relationship between neighboring countries America and Mexico.
tagline: There's no running from family.
title: Half Brothers
plot:
Half Brothers is a 2020 American road comedy-drama film directed by Luke Greenfield from a screenplay by Eduardo Cisneros and Jason Shuman. Luis Gerardo Méndez stars as Renato, a successful Mexican businessman, and Connor Del Rio as Asher, his carefree American half-brother, with José Zúñiga as their father, Flavio, Vincent Spano, Pia Watson and Juan Pablo Espinosa. Focus Features released it on 4 December 2020.

Renato, an executive at an aviation company in Mexico, is about to get married when he receives a call from a woman named Katherine, who tells him that his father, Flavio, is gravely ill and wants to see him in Chicago. Renato reluctantly agrees, though he has long resented Flavio, who emigrated to the United States during the Mexican peso crisis when Renato was a boy and never came back for him. At the hospital, Renato discovers that he has a half-brother, Asher, an irresponsible free spirit whom he had already crossed paths with at a coffee shop without knowing who he was.

Flavio asks his two sons to deliver an envelope marked "Eloise" to a man named Evaristo in St. Louis, the first stage in a series of clues that will take them on a journey across the country. Asher eagerly accepts, while Renato refuses, but after Flavio's death he grudgingly agrees to go. The trip proves chaotic: Asher steals a goat, which he names Renatito, from a ranch guarded by armed men, and the brothers clash repeatedly. In St. Louis they find an old factory that makes the radio-controlled planes Renato once flew with his father, and Evaristo, a friend who emigrated with Flavio, who reveals how the two men worked there as cheap laborers before Flavio helped turn the business around with Katherine. Following the trail of clues, the brothers gradually piece together their father's life in America and the reasons he never returned to Mexico, learning to understand him, and each other, along the way as they face their own failings and the meaning of family.

Combining broad road-trip comedy with a family drama about immigration, absent fathers and reconciliation, Half Brothers gave Méndez, known for Mexican comedies and the series Club de Cuervos, a leading role in an American studio release, playing opposite Del Rio in a bilingual story.

overview: Star race car Lightning McQueen and his pal Mater head overseas to compete in the World Grand Prix race. But the road to the championship becomes rocky as Mater gets caught up in an intriguing adventure of his own: international espionage.
tagline: Ka-ciao!
title: Cars 2
plot:
Cars 2 is a 2011 animated adventure comedy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

The movie takes place after the events of the first film, where Lightning McQueen (voiced by Owen Wilson) has become an international racing sensation. He's invited to participate in the World Grand Prix, a prestigious racing tournament that will take him around the globe.

However, things take a turn when Mater (voiced by Larry the Cable Guy), Lightning's best friend and tow truck, gets caught up in a spy plot involving the villainous Professor Zündapp (voiced by Peter Fonda) and his henchmen. Mater is recruited by the British Secret Service to help them infiltrate the World Grand Prix and gather intel on the nefarious plans of the evil organization.

Meanwhile, Lightning McQueen teams up with Francesco Bernoulli (voiced by John Turturro), a sleek Italian racing car who becomes his rival in the World Grand Prix. As they compete against each other, Lightning begins to question his own identity and purpose beyond just being a racing champion.

Throughout the film, Mater navigates the world of espionage, encountering various characters from different countries, including Finn McMissile (voiced by Michael Caine) and Holley Shiftwell (voiced by Emily Mortimer). The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, witty humor, and heartwarming moments as Mater forms new friendships and learns to trust himself.

As the story unfolds, Lightning McQueen discovers that Francesco is actually working for Professor Zündapp's organization, leading him to confront his rival in a thrilling finale. In the end, Lightning emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and staying true to oneself.

Overall, Cars 2 offers an exciting adventure filled with humor, heart, and stunning animation. The film explores themes of identity, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself, making it a delightful addition to the Cars franchise.

overview: After an extremely regrettable one night stand, two strangers wake up to find themselves snowed in after sleeping through a blizzard that put all of Manhattan on ice. They're now trapped together in a tiny apartment, forced to get to know each other way more than any one night stand should.
tagline: Before love. After sex.
title: Two Night Stand
plot:
Two Night Stand is a 2014 American romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and intimacy. The movie delves into the theme of vulnerability, as the two main characters, Brian and Kate, navigate their way through a casual encounter that gradually evolves into something more meaningful.

The film also touches on the idea of emotional connection and how it can be found in unexpected places. As Brian and Kate get to know each other, they begin to open up about their past experiences and insecurities, revealing a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Furthermore, Two Night Stand examines the concept of intimacy beyond physical relationships. The movie shows how two people can form a strong bond through shared conversations, laughter, and emotional vulnerability, highlighting the importance of genuine human connection in our lives.

Overall, the film presents a nuanced portrayal of relationships, encouraging viewers to look beyond surface-level interactions and explore the depths of human connection.

overview: The story of Daniel Jones, lead investigator for the US Senate’s sweeping study into the CIA's Detention and Interrogation Program, which was found to be brutal, immoral and ineffective. With the truth at stake, Jones battled tirelessly to make public what many in power sought to keep hidden.
tagline: Truth matters
title: The Report
plot:
The Report is a 2019 American thriller film directed by Scott Z. Burns, starring Adam Driver as Daniel J. Jones, a Senate staffer who uncovers the CIA's use of torture during the George W. Bush administration.

The main themes of The Report include:

1. **Government Accountability and Transparency**: The film highlights the importance of holding those in power accountable for their actions. Daniel J. Jones' investigation into the CIA's torture program exposes the agency's wrongdoing, leading to a re-evaluation of its policies.
2. **Torture and Its Consequences**: The movie delves into the moral implications of torture, both on individuals and society as a whole. It raises questions about the nature of truth, the limits of human endurance, and the long-term effects of trauma on those who have been subjected to it.
3. **The Power of Investigative Journalism**: The Report showcases the crucial role that investigative journalists play in uncovering and exposing government wrongdoing. Daniel J. Jones' work serves as a testament to the importance of a free press in holding those in power accountable.
4. **The Complexity of Morality**: Throughout the film, characters grapple with complex moral dilemmas, often finding themselves torn between their personal values and the demands of their profession. This theme adds depth to the narrative, encouraging viewers to consider the nuances of right and wrong.
5. **The Legacy of 9/11 and the War on Terror**: The Report is set against the backdrop of the post-9/11 era, exploring the consequences of the War on Terror and the subsequent erosion of civil liberties. The film serves as a commentary on the ongoing debate about national security, individual freedoms, and the role of government in times of crisis.

Overall, The Report is a thought-provoking thriller that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of unchecked power.

overview: The adventure begins when Lucas, a 13 year old boy, embarks on the vacation of a lifetime. When disaster strikes, Lucas finds himself stranded in a strange land littered with ghost ships and prehistoric creatures. While searching for other signs of life, Lucas hears a radio broadcast in the distance and is drawn into the jungle where he encounters a beautiful young girl who claims to have come from the 1950s. Together they set out on a quest to get home all the while uncovering secrets that will forever change the future.
tagline: Their world is closer than you think.
title: Dinosaur Island
plot:
Dinosaur Island, released in the United Kingdom as Journey to Dinosaur Island, is a 2014 British-Australian family adventure film written and directed by Matt Drummond, with Jason Moody and Megan Williams as co-producers. It concerns a mysterious island where a special type of crystal acts as a portal, drawing in people and objects from different eras. Darius Williams stars as the 13-year-old Lucas Winton, with Kate Rasmussen as the young Kathryn, Juliette Palmer as her adult self, and Nicole Yardley, Paul Padagas and Joe Bistaveous in supporting roles.

Visiting his grandmother's old house, now up for sale, Lucas finds a crystal in a box on a bookshelf and pockets it. On a flight, he places it on the empty seat beside him, where it begins to glow; disaster strikes the plane, and Lucas wakes up stranded in a strange land strewn with ghost ships and roamed by prehistoric creatures. Following a distant radio broadcast into the jungle, he meets Kate, a girl who says she comes from the 1950s and once owned a crystal like his. She gives him her diary as a survival guide and introduces him to Mimos, a Sinornithosaurus that can mimic any sound, like a lyrebird. Lucas learns that mists appear during earthquakes and bring empty airplanes from different times, past and future, often loaded with useful supplies.

While investigating a newly arrived plane, the two are captured by tribespeople and locked in a wooden cage. A fellow prisoner recognises Lucas's crystal as a "sing sing stone" and explains that huge formations of it between the island's twin volcanoes create the mists. Lucas deduces that the cluster is a giant piezoelectric crystal set resonating by seismic activity, and that it could carry him home. The pair escape, catch a ride on a pterosaur Kate has freed, and survive a chase by a Tyrannosaurus, which Mimos scares away by imitating its roar, then outrun a pack of dromaeosaurs. In the cave between the volcanoes, Lucas uses a singing jar of water to activate the crystals. As the portal opens, Kate stays behind to retrieve her diary, promising to follow. Lucas wakes up in hospital and meets his grandmother Kathryn, who reveals that she is Kate, and who later wins a Nobel Prize with the evidence in her diary.

The film was released in Australian cinemas by Hoyts and United Cinemas in February 2015 and sold to more than 50 countries after its rights were acquired at Cannes in 2014.

overview: On a bet, a gridiron hero at John Hughes High School sets out to turn a bespectacled plain Jane into a beautiful and popular prom queen in this outrageous send-up of the teen movies of the 1980s and '90s.
tagline: They served you Breakfast. They gave you Pie. Now we’re gonna stuff your face.
title: Not Another Teen Movie
plot:
Not Another Teen Movie is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Joel Zwick and written by Todd Phillips. The movie is a parody of popular teen movies from the late 1990s, particularly She's All That, Can't Hardly Wait, I Know What You Did Last Summer, and 10 Things to Do Before Bedtime.

The film begins with Janey Briggs (Chyler Leigh), a beautiful high school student who has been dumped by her boyfriend. To win back her ex-boyfriend, she makes a bet that if she can lose weight and become more popular, he will come crawling back. However, things don't go as planned, and Janey finds herself caught up in a series of misadventures with her new friends.

Meanwhile, Joe (Chris Evans), the star quarterback of the school football team, is struggling to find his place in the world after being dumped by his girlfriend. He becomes infatuated with Janey and tries to win her back, but their relationship is complicated by a series of misunderstandings and miscommunications.

As the story unfolds, the movie parodies various teen movie tropes, including the "popular girl" archetype (Janey), the "jock" character (Joe), and the "nerd" character (Deb). The film also pokes fun at popular culture, including music videos, fashion trends, and high school cliques.

One of the most memorable scenes in the movie is a parody of the iconic scene from I Know What You Did Last Summer, where the characters are stalked by a mysterious figure. In Not Another Teen Movie, the "stalker" character is played for laughs, with hilarious results.

Throughout the film, the characters navigate love triangles, high school drama, and self-discovery. Along the way, they encounter a series of wacky supporting characters, including a eccentric teacher (Donald Faison) and a group of bumbling cheerleaders.

In the end, Janey and Joe must confront their feelings for each other and figure out what they really want from life. The movie ends on a lighthearted note, with the characters learning valuable lessons about friendship, love, and being true to oneself.

Overall, Not Another Teen Movie is a hilarious and irreverent comedy that lovingly parodies the teen movie genre. With its witty script, memorable characters, and over-the-top humor, it's a must-see for fans of 90s pop culture and comedy.

belongs_to_collection.name: Batman: Under the Red Hood Collection

overview: One part vigilante, one part criminal kingpin, Red Hood begins cleaning up Gotham with the efficiency of Batman, but without following the same ethical code.
tagline: Dare to Look Beneath the Hood.
title: Batman: Under the Red Hood
plot:
Batman: Under the Red Hood is a 2010 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics/Vertigo imprint character Jason Todd, the second Robin. The movie takes place after the events of Batman: Year One and follows Bruce Wayne's (Bruce Greenwood) quest for justice in Gotham City.

The story begins with Jason Todd (Jensen Ackles), the original Robin, who was brutally murdered by the Joker (John Noble) during a confrontation at the hands of the Clown Prince of Crime. The event is still fresh in Bruce's mind as he tries to rebuild his life and protect his city from various villains.

Years later, Jason returns from the dead, resurrected by Ra's al Ghul (Liam Neeson), who seeks to use him for his own purposes. However, Jason soon discovers that he has been transformed into a vengeful anti-hero known as Red Hood, driven by a desire for revenge against those who wronged him.

As Red Hood begins to wreak havoc on Gotham City, Bruce Wayne is forced to confront his past and the consequences of his actions. He teams up with Tim Drake (Alan Tudyk), the third Robin, and Nightwing (Moriarty's voice actor not specified) to stop Red Hood and uncover the truth behind his resurrection.

Throughout the movie, Bruce struggles with his own morality and the weight of his responsibilities as a hero. He is torn between his desire for justice and his need to protect those he cares about from the destructive path that Jason has taken.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ra's al Ghul's plan was not just to resurrect Jason but also to use him as a pawn in his own game of revenge against Bruce. The villainous League of Assassins is also involved, adding an extra layer of complexity to the plot.

The climax of the movie features an intense confrontation between Red Hood and Nightwing, with Bruce forced to make a difficult choice between saving his former protégé or stopping him from causing harm to others. In the end, Bruce manages to reach out to Jason's humanity, and he begins to see that there is more to life than just revenge.

The movie concludes with Jason finally finding redemption and making amends for his past mistakes. He also begins to forge a new path, one that is separate from his time as Red Hood but still driven by a desire for justice. The ending sets the stage for future stories featuring Jason Todd, offering a glimmer of hope for his character's development.

Overall, Batman: Under the Red Hood is a gripping and emotionally charged tale that explores the complexities of heroism and redemption. With its well-developed characters and intricate plot, it offers a compelling take on the DC Comics universe.

overview: A surreal mosaic pieced together from fractured memories and childhood recollections as told by an unnamed narrator who relives a traumatic incident from his past. A time when people went about their lives, and yet, they told tales of a predator who stalked the streets at night, sneaking into windows and adducting the innocent; this menace went by one name, Pastor Jessup.
title: Burnt by the Sun
plot: A surreal mosaic pieced together from fractured memories and childhood recollections as told by an unnamed narrator who relives a traumatic incident from his past. A time when people went about their lives, and yet, they told tales of a predator who stalked the streets at night, sneaking into windows and abducting the innocent; this menace went by one name, Pastor Jessup.

overview: Taking place after alien crafts land around the world, an expert linguist is recruited by the military to determine whether they come in peace or are a threat.
tagline: Why are they here?
title: Arrival
plot:
Arrival is a 2016 American science-fiction drama directed by Denis Villeneuve and written by Eric Heisserer, adapted from Ted Chiang's Nebula-winning 1998 novella "Story of Your Life". Amy Adams stars as the linguist Louise Banks, with Jeremy Renner as the theoretical physicist Ian Donnelly, Forest Whitaker as Colonel Weber, Michael Stuhlbarg as the CIA agent Halpern and Tzi Ma as General Shang of China.

The film opens with what seem to be Louise's memories of her daughter, Hannah, who dies of an illness at twelve. Then twelve alien spacecraft appear above sites around the globe, causing worldwide panic. Weber recruits Louise and Ian to lead the American effort at the craft hovering over Montana. Inside, they meet two seven-limbed, cephalopod-like beings they call heptapods and nickname Abbott and Costello, who write in complex logograms. As Louise makes progress, she is visited by vivid images of her daughter.

When the team finally asks why the visitors have come, the reply seems to say "offer weapon". China, which has been using mahjong to communicate, reads it as a threat and cuts off contact, as do others; Louise argues that "weapon" may simply mean "tool". Rogue soldiers plant a bomb in the Montana craft, but the heptapods eject Louise and Ian before it explodes. With Shang issuing an ultimatum for the ship above China to leave, Ian finds that the message fills exactly one-twelfth of its space, and Louise concludes that it is split among the twelve ships to force nations to cooperate. Returning alone, Louise learns from Costello that Abbott is dying and that the heptapods have come to help humanity because they will need its help in 3,000 years. Their gift is the language itself, which frees its speakers from a linear experience of time. Louise understands that her visions are not memories but glimpses of the future. In one, at a celebration of global unity, Shang tells her that she stopped his attack by calling his private number and repeating his late wife's dying words. Grabbing Halpern's satellite phone, she does so; China stands down, the nations share their data and the ships depart. Louise accepts the future she has foreseen with Ian, including Hannah's birth and death.

After premiering at Venice in September 2016, the film grossed $213 million worldwide on a $47 million budget and was acclaimed, with 94% on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned eight Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, and won Best Sound Editing.

overview: A military vessel on the search for an unidentified submersible finds themselves face to face with a giant shark, forced to use only what they have on board to defend themselves from the monstrous beast.
tagline: Danger Is Rising!
title: Megalodon
plot:
Megalodon is a 2018 American creature-feature television film directed by James Thomas, who also worked on the script, and produced by The Asylum, the studio known for low-budget "mockbusters" released alongside major studio films. Made to capitalize on Jon Turteltaub's The Meg, which opened in theaters three days earlier, it premiered on the Syfy channel on 13 August 2018. Michael Madsen leads the cast as Admiral King, with Caroline Harris as Commander Lynch, Dominic Pace as Captain Streeper, Ego Mikitas as the Russian captain Ivanov, Aimee Stolte as Yana Popov, Paulina Nguyen as Cheng and Scott C. Roe as Jameson.

A few hundred miles west of Hawaii, a Russian submarine is secretly tapping an American communications cable when the noise of its drilling awakens a gigantic prehistoric shark, which tears the vessel apart. Ivanov escapes into the bow with three crew members, abandoning the others. The US Navy destroyer Shaw finds the wreck, and Lynch dives in the submersible she designed, rescuing the Russians, who claim to be whale researchers, before the shark swallows the submersible whole. Admiral King wants to cut the crew loose to protect the ship, but Streeper insists on a rescue, and the loyal crew locks the admiral in his cabin. Cheng rigs an anchor with high-voltage current as bait; when the shark opens its mouth, the submersible escapes, and the jolt appears to stop the creature, though one sailor dies in the electrified water.

Under questioning, Popov admits the Russians were on an intelligence mission. Ivanov breaks free, arms a comrade and kills the tactical adviser Jameson, while the shark resurfaces and devours a yacht. Cheng turns the submersible into a bomb, but Ivanov forces her to throw the detonator overboard, and the backup remote she builds only works at close range. Streeper orders the crew into the lifeboats and prepares to go down with his ship, and Lynch swims back to help him. King, freed from his cabin, kills Ivanov in a shootout but is mortally wounded, and when the shark crashes through the hull, he detonates the explosives, destroying the beast and the destroyer as the survivors salute him.

The exterior shipboard scenes were filmed aboard the SS Lane Victory, a World War II vessel now serving as a museum ship in San Pedro, California. A sequel, Megalodon Rising, followed in 2021.

overview: Two fledgling criminals kidnap a pizza delivery guy, strap a bomb to his chest, and advise him that he has mere hours to rob a bank or else...
tagline: A lot can happen in 30 minutes.
title: 30 Minutes or Less
plot:
30 Minutes or Less is a 2011 American action comedy film directed by Ruben Fleischer and produced by Stuart Cornfeld, Ben Stiller and Jeremy Kramer. Jesse Eisenberg stars as Nick, a pizza delivery driver, with Aziz Ansari as his friend Chet, Danny McBride and Nick Swardson as a pair of inept criminals, Michael Peña and Fred Ward. Released by Sony Pictures on 12 August 2011, it was filmed in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where the story is set.

Nick is an aimless young man in Grand Rapids who rarely manages to deliver pizzas within his employer's thirty-minute guarantee. His friendship with Chet, a schoolteacher, falls apart when Chet learns that Nick slept with his twin sister, Kate, on the night of their high school graduation; Nick also learns that Kate is about to leave for a job in Atlanta. Meanwhile, Dwayne and his friend Travis live in the shadow of Dwayne's domineering father, known as the Major, who won a large lottery jackpot years earlier. Eager to get his inheritance, Dwayne learns from a stripper, Juicy, that a hitman named Chango could kill his father, but he needs $100,000 to pay him.

Dwayne and Travis decide to kidnap a stranger, strap a bomb to him and force him to steal the money. They order a pizza, knock Nick unconscious when he arrives and lock him into a vest rigged with explosives, which they threaten to detonate if he goes to the police or fails to bring them the money within ten hours. Nick turns to Chet, who reluctantly helps him rob a bank. The heist is chaotic, but the two escape with the cash. When Dwayne and Travis demand the money and take Kate hostage, the situation escalates into a showdown at a scrapyard with Chango, involving bluffs, a flamethrower and the bomb itself, which Nick eventually turns against his captors.

The film received mixed reviews, with critics finding the cast's comic energy engaging but the story slight and the humor uneven. It grossed about $40 million worldwide against a $28 million budget. It also attracted controversy for its resemblance to the real 2003 death of Brian Wells, a pizza delivery man in Erie, Pennsylvania, who was killed by a bomb locked around his neck during a bank robbery; the filmmakers said they had not been aware of the case.

overview: Charlie Kenton is a washed-up fighter who retired from the ring when robots took over the sport. After his robot is trashed, he reluctantly teams up with his estranged son to rebuild and train an unlikely contender.
tagline: If you get one shot, make it real.
title: Real Steel
plot:
Real Steel is a 2011 American science fiction sports film produced and directed by Shawn Levy, based on Richard Matheson's 1956 short story "Steel," which had earlier been adapted as an episode of The Twilight Zone. Hugh Jackman stars as Charlie Kenton, a washed-up former boxer, with Dakota Goyo as his son, Max, Evangeline Lilly as Bailey Tallet, Anthony Mackie and Kevin Durand. The film was released by Touchstone Pictures in October 2011, with Steven Spielberg among its executive producers.

In the 2020s, human boxing has been replaced by fights between giant robots. Charlie, a former contender who scrapes a living fighting robots in small venues, loses his machine, Ambush, in a bout against a bull at a Texas carnival run by Ricky, and flees without paying the bet he lost. He then learns that his former girlfriend has died and that he must attend a custody hearing for their eleven-year-old son, Max, whom he has never known. Max's wealthy aunt, Debra, and her husband, Marvin, want custody, and Charlie agrees to give it up in exchange for money, on the condition that he takes care of Max for the summer while the couple travels.

Using the money, Charlie buys Noisy Boy, a once-famous robot from the World Robot Boxing league, but it is destroyed in an underground arena. While scavenging for parts in a junkyard, Max finds Atom, an old sparring robot that saves him from a fall. Atom is built to withstand punishment and has a rare "shadow" function that allows it to mimic human movements. Max insists on fighting with Atom, and Charlie, drawing on his boxing experience, teaches the robot to fight. The underdog robot wins a series of bouts and becomes a crowd favorite, earning a chance to face Zeus, the undefeated champion of the World Robot Boxing league. Along the way, Charlie grows closer to Max and Bailey and begins to rediscover the man he once was, and he must decide whether to give up his son.

Real Steel received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its visual effects, Jackman's and Goyo's performances and its crowd-pleasing spirit, though some found it formulaic. It grossed about $300 million worldwide and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects.

original_title: Curious George: Go West, Go Wild
overview: While farm-sitting, George accidentally lets the farm animals escape. Ted, George and wannabe cowboy Emmett must round 'em up, accounting for every animal -- and emerging with some new skills, to boot.
title: Curious George: Go West, Go Wild
plot:
Curious George: Go West, Go Wild is a 2020 American animated family comedy, the fifth feature in the film franchise based on Margret and H. A. Rey's books about the mischievous monkey George and his friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat. Directed by Michael LaBash from a screenplay by Sherri Stoner and Jana Howington, it was produced by Imagine Entertainment, Universal Animation Studios and Universal 1440 Entertainment, with Brian Grazer, Ron Howard and David Kirschner among the executive producers and music by Germaine Franco. Frank Welker voices George and Jeff Bennett voices Ted, with Max Mittelman as Emmett, April Stewart as Ginny, Phil Morris as Frank Stetson, Adrienne Barbeau as Ginny's mother and Dee Bradley Baker in several animal roles.

George and Ted travel west by train to Ted's cousin Ginny's farm, having promised to look after it while she goes on vacation with her adventurous mother. Ted, however, knows nothing about farms and little about country life, and the place is run day to day by Emmett, a young farmhand and would-be cowboy who is still learning the ropes himself. George's curiosity and antics quickly upend the farm's routine, and when a runaway wagon rolls down a hill and smashes the corrals, the animals escape and scatter into the countryside.

Despite his inexperience, Emmett keeps his head and organizes a roundup, and the three set off to bring home every last cow, sheep and even a llama. Their trek takes them across a rickety old covered bridge and a wide river, where Emmett rescues a sheep and a dog swept away on a log, and they must flee a shelter threatened by a flash flood.
