Emmett practices lassoing again and again until he masters it, and his perseverance inspires the cautious Ted to try fishing and horseback riding and George to learn the harmonica. Meanwhile, Ginny finds a similar freedom from her own cautiousness on her trip. By the end, every animal is accounted for and the friends have all gained new skills.

The film premiered exclusively on the streaming service Peacock on 8 September 2020, alongside the arrival of the Curious George television series on the platform, and was released on DVD and digital on 15 December 2020. Common Sense Media described it as a gentle preschool adventure with mild peril and a positive message about being open to new experiences and trying new things.

overview: Story of two young people who belong to different worlds. It is the chronicle of a love improbable, almost impossible but inevitable dragging in a frantic journey they discover the first great love. Babi is a girl from upper-middle class that is educated in goodness and innocence . Hache is a rebellious boy, impulsive, unconscious, has a appetite for risk and danger embodied in endless fights and illegal motorbike races, the limit of common sense
tagline: Have you ever been about to touch the sky?
title: Three Steps Above Heaven
plot:
Three Steps Above Heaven is a Spanish drama film directed by Cora Zolfo, released in 2010. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Tomás Aragón.

The story revolves around Álvaro (played by Eloy de la Iglesia), a young man who has been diagnosed with leukemia and is undergoing chemotherapy at a hospital in Madrid. During his treatment, Álvaro meets Elena (played by Aitor Lara), a fellow patient who becomes his closest friend and confidant.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Álvaro's life was not without its challenges before he fell ill. He had a troubled relationship with his family, particularly his father, who is portrayed as emotionally distant and critical. Álvaro also struggles with feelings of guilt and anger towards his mother, who abandoned him when he was young.

The title "Three Steps Above Heaven" refers to the three steps that Álvaro takes above the hospital's rooftop, where he finds a sense of freedom and escape from his troubles. These moments of solitude allow him to reflect on his life and confront his inner demons.

Throughout the film, we see Álvaro's relationship with Elena deepen, as they bond over their shared experiences as patients at the hospital. However, their friendship is put to the test when Álvaro begins to develop feelings for Elena, which complicates their already fragile emotional connection.

As the story progresses, Álvaro's health begins to decline, and he must come to terms with his mortality. The film takes a poignant turn as Álvaro confronts his father about his past and the reasons behind his mother's departure. This confrontation ultimately leads to a sense of closure and healing for Álvaro.

The movie concludes with Álvaro's passing, surrounded by Elena and his loved ones. However, in a surprising twist, we see that Elena has been given a second chance at life, thanks to a bone marrow transplant from an anonymous donor. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Elena begins her new journey towards recovery.

Overall, Three Steps Above Heaven is a powerful and emotional drama that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Eloy de la Iglesia and Aitor Lara, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

original_title: Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
overview: Harley Quinn joins forces with a singer, an assassin and a police detective to help a young girl who had a hit placed on her after she stole a rare diamond from a crime lord.
tagline: Mind Over Mayhem
title: Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
plot:
Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn) is a 2020 superhero film directed by Cathy Yan and written by Chris McKay, Babs Grant, and Christina Hodson. The movie is set in the DC Extended Universe (DCEU) and follows the story of Harley Quinn (Margot Robbie), who has broken free from the clutches of the Joker.

The film begins with Harley Quinn, now a single woman, trying to start her life anew after leaving the Joker's abusive relationship. However, she soon finds herself in trouble when Roman Sionis (Ewan McGregor), also known as Black Mask, kidnaps Cassandra Cain (Ella Jay Basco), a young and skilled martial artist who is also the daughter of assassins David Cain (Michael Keaton) and Lady Shiva (Mary Elizabeth Winstead).

Harley Quinn teams up with Huntress (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), Black Canary (Jurnee Smollett-Bell), and Renee Montoya (Rosie Perez) to rescue Cassandra from Roman's clutches. Along the way, they must navigate a complex web of crime lords, corrupt police officers, and other villains who are all vying for control in Gotham City.

As Harley Quinn navigates her new life as a solo operator, she also begins to confront her own demons and question her loyalty to her former partner-in-crime, the Joker. Meanwhile, Black Mask is revealed to be using Cassandra's skills to further his own nefarious plans, which include taking over Gotham City and eliminating its corrupt officials.

Throughout the film, Harley Quinn's character undergoes significant development as she learns to let go of her toxic relationship with the Joker and forge a new path for herself. The movie also explores themes of female empowerment, friendship, and self-discovery, as the four main characters come together to support each other and take down their common enemies.

The film features a mix of action, comedy, and drama, with plenty of nods to classic DC Comics characters and Easter eggs for fans of the franchise. The cast delivers strong performances across the board, with Margot Robbie shining as the titular Harley Quinn.

Ultimately, the movie culminates in an epic showdown between Harley Quinn and Black Mask, with the fate of Gotham City hanging in the balance. In the end, Harley Quinn emerges victorious, having found a new sense of purpose and belonging among her fellow heroes. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Harley Quinn is ready to take on whatever challenges come her way next.

Overall, Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn) is a fun, action-packed ride that explores themes of female empowerment and self-discovery in a richly detailed DC Comics universe.

overview: Assigned to recover sensitive stolen data, a gruff FBI agent goes undercover as a kindergarten teacher, but the school's liberal, politically correct environment is more than he bargained for.
title: Kindergarten Cop 2
plot:
Kindergarten Cop 2 is a 2016 American comedy directed by Don Michael Paul and starring Dolph Lundgren, released on home video by Universal. A standalone sequel to the 1990 hit Kindergarten Cop, it replaces Arnold Schwarzenegger's Detective John Kimble with a new hero, FBI agent Zack Reed. Bill Bellamy plays Reed's partner, Agent Sanders, with Darla Taylor as the teacher Olivia, Sarah Strange as Miss Sinclaire and Aleks Paunovic as the villain Alexander Zogu.

Reed and Sanders are hunting Zogu, a dangerous crime boss who has learned of a copy of the FBI's witness protection database. The file was stored on a USB flash drive by a kindergarten teacher, Kevin Flaherty, who has since died. Sanders questions the dead man's pupils and the school staff, but nobody knows where the drive is, so Reed invents a résumé, applies to take over the grieving class and is hired with little difficulty.

The school prides itself on a progressive, modern approach to education, which clashes with Reed's blunt manner. His first day is chaos: one boy has a severe nut allergy, so pandemonium breaks out when Reed is caught eating peanut butter, and he loses control again after handing out chocolate cookies that send the children bouncing off the walls. Insisting he can manage without help, he resorts to an air horn to impose order and earns a strike from the principal. Chastened, he apologises and turns to Sanders, a father of five, for advice, and gradually learns to lead the class with more patience and emotional awareness. When fellow kindergarten teacher Olivia catches him searching her office for the drive, he covers by asking her out, and a romance develops.

In a game of capture the flag against Olivia's class, Reed's pupils, who complain that the other children are bigger, win for the first time thanks to a Trojan horse strategy he devises. Meanwhile Zogu seizes the FBI's surveillance van and realises that the children hold the key to the drive. Reed reveals his true identity to the principal and warns her to lock down the school. Zogu tracks down the drive while the class is on a field trip, but the children ambush him using their Trojan horse tactic, the drive is returned to the FBI, and the kids celebrate with their parents.

The film was shot over 28 days in July and August 2015 in Maple Ridge, Langley and Vancouver, British Columbia, with Kanaka Elementary serving as the school. Reviews were poor; Consequence of Sound gave it a D+.

overview: Los Angeles is about to be hit by a devastating earthquake, and time is running out to save the city from imminent danger.
tagline: The end is near.
title: 10.0 Earthquake
plot:
10.0 Earthquake is a 2014 American low-budget disaster film directed by David Gidali. Henry Ian Cusick stars as Jack, an engineer, with Cameron Richardson as Emily Schiffman, a young scientist with the United States Geological Survey, Jeffrey Jones as Marcus Gladstone, and Kristen Dalton, Chasty Ballesteros, Heather Sossaman, Olivia Jordan, David Chokachi and Malcolm Barrett in supporting roles.

Emily, newly working for the USGS, notices a series of small, highly localized earthquakes striking the Los Angeles area and develops a theory that they are building toward a catastrophic super quake. If she is right, the entire city could collapse into a chasm of molten rock. The cause, it emerges, is a deep-drilling fracking operation run by a company that has pushed its drilling far below the surface. Jack, an engineer at the company who is going through a divorce and is estranged from his teenage daughter, realizes that his employer is responsible for the disaster and feels obliged to help stop it.

As the tremors grow stronger and more frequent, the film moves between Jack and Emily and a series of other characters scattered across the region, among them a group of young people on an outing in the wilderness, whose lives are suddenly threatened when the ground opens beneath them. Jack and Emily race across the increasingly devastated city, dodging collapsing roads and vanishing bridges, as they attempt to carry out a plan to divert the epicenter of the coming quake toward Long Beach, a move that could save millions of lives, including that of Jack's daughter, but which requires them to act before the final, massive quake strikes.

The film received little mainstream critical attention. A review on the site Cinematic Diversions found that, although it resembled the cheap disaster films produced by The Asylum and its computer-generated effects were often crude, it benefited from a better-than-expected script and solid acting, and its structure of small, deadly localized tremors gave it a tension reminiscent of the Final Destination films. The reviewer also noted the scientific implausibility of its fracking premise. Gidali later remarked that the screenplay had been completely rewritten shortly before shooting began.

overview: Ozzy, a friendly, peaceful beagle has his idyllic life turned upside down when the Martins leave on a long and distant trip. There's only one problem: no dogs allowed! Unable to bring their beloved Ozzy along for the ride, they settle on the next best thing, a top-of-the-line canine spa called Blue Creek.
tagline: Fast & Furry
title: Ozzy
plot:
Ozzy, also known as Ozzy: The Great Furscape, is a 2016 animated comedy co-produced by the Spanish companies Arcadia Motion Pictures, Capitán Araña and Pachacamac with Winnipeg's Tangent Animation, which animated it in Canada using Blender on a budget of about $8.5 million. The Spanish voice cast includes Guillermo Romero as Ozzy, Dani Rovira as Fronky, José Mota as Vito, Carlos Areces as Mr. Robbins and Michelle Jenner as Paula; the English dub features Jeff Foxworthy, Rob Schneider and Lexi Walker. Executive producer Jeff Bell called it a prison movie full of funny tributes to the genre's classics.

Ozzy, a beagle, lives happily with the Martin family and his best friend, their daughter Paula. When the family is invited to a comic festival in Japan, quarantine rules mean Ozzy cannot come, so they leave him at Blue Creek, a luxurious-looking dog hotel run by the smooth Mr. Robbins. Once they are gone, Robbins and his assistant Dominic ship Ozzy and the other dogs to the real Blue Creek, a grim dog prison run by Grunt, a St. Bernard warden, where Ozzy's collar is taken and he becomes inmate 463.

His cellmate is Fronky, a short-sighted dachshund and former guide dog who has tried to escape fifteen times. Ozzy also befriends Chester, an elderly fox terrier who delivers comics, and Doc, a silent sheepdog, while making an enemy of Vito, a tiny Chihuahua who rules the inmates. Vito wants Ozzy as his runner in the prison's dog races, and when Ozzy refuses to compete or throw a race, he and Grunt make life hard for Ozzy and his friends. Meanwhile, Robbins tells the returning Martins that Ozzy has died. The friends plan to escape hidden in boxes of toys on a delivery truck and steal a blueprint from the warden's office. Vito and Grunt strike a deal that sets better food or harsher conditions for all the inmates on Ozzy's race against the guards' champion, Jock. During the race the lights go out and Ozzy vanishes, but the escapees are recaptured at the truck. Ozzy then turns the tables, locking out Grunt and the guard Decker, exposing the rigged race and rallying the dogs to overpower the guards and capture Robbins. Back home, Fronky and Doc rejoin their families, the Martins adopt Chester, and Robbins faces 20 years in prison for animal cruelty.

Disney released the film in Spain on 14 October 2016, and it opened in the United Kingdom a week later.

overview: A loser of a crook and his wife strike it rich when a botched bank job's cover business becomes a spectacular success.
tagline: They took a bite out of crime
title: Small Time Crooks
plot:
Small Time Crooks is a 2000 American comedy film directed by Joel Coen and written by Joel Coen and Ethan Coen. The movie revolves around the story of a group of small-time crooks who plan to rob a bank in New York City.

The main theme of Small Time Crooks is the illusion of power and control that comes with crime, as well as the consequences of getting caught up in a life of dishonesty. The film explores how the characters' perceptions of themselves and their place in the world are shaped by their involvement in the underworld, and how this ultimately leads to their downfall.

The movie also touches on the idea of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the strong bonds between the main characters as they navigate the complexities of their illicit activities. However, these relationships are tested when one of the group members is forced to make a difficult choice that puts everyone at risk.

Furthermore, Small Time Crooks critiques the notion of the "American Dream," suggesting that it is an unattainable illusion that can lead individuals down a path of destruction and disappointment. The film's portrayal of the characters' failed attempts to achieve success through crime serves as a commentary on the emptiness and disillusionment that can result from chasing after material wealth and status.

Overall, Small Time Crooks presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, delving into themes of identity, morality, and the consequences of one's actions.

overview: A story about a seemingly unlikely couple who cross paths under life-threatening circumstances as though they are destined not only to meet but to save each other's lives. Not once, but twice.
tagline: The deeper you look, the more you will find.
title: Angel Eyes
plot:
Angel Eyes is a 2001 American romantic drama directed by Luis Mandoki and written by Gerald Di Pego. It stars Jennifer Lopez as Chicago police officer Sharon Pogue and Jim Caviezel as Catch, a mysterious, withdrawn stranger, with Sônia Braga, Terrence Howard and Jeremy Sisto in supporting roles. Marco Beltrami composed the score. The story follows two wounded people whose relationship forces each of them to confront the trauma of the past.

One night, Sharon arrives at the scene of a violent traffic accident and holds the hand of a badly injured man, pleading with him not to give up. A year later, she is estranged from her family because she had her father arrested for beating her mother, something neither he nor her brother has forgiven. Meanwhile, a quiet man known only as Catch wanders the city in a trance-like state, performing small acts of kindness for strangers and neighbors, and seems to be watching Sharon from a distance.

When gunmen open fire on a diner and Sharon gives chase, one of the suspects grabs her gun and is about to shoot her when Catch tackles him and saves her life. The two begin a cautious, intense relationship, but Catch refuses to talk about himself, saying only that he is starting from scratch, and he lives in a nearly empty apartment. One night at a blues club he picks up a trumpet and plays a soulful version of "Nature Boy", and the owner recognizes him as Steve Lambert. Investigating, Sharon discovers that Catch is the man whose hand she held at the accident, a jazz musician whose wife and son were killed in the crash. As she tries to help him face the loss he has blocked from his memory, she must also confront her own painful family history.

The film blends romance with a psychological drama about grief, denial and domestic violence, and about the healing that comes from finally facing pain.

Angel Eyes opened at number four in North America but was a box office bomb, grossing about 29.7 million dollars worldwide against a 38 million dollar budget. Critics were largely unimpressed, giving it 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it ultimately a schmaltzy romance, and a Metacritic score of 39, though it earned ALMA Award nominations for Lopez and Mandoki.

original_title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams
overview: Exploring the further adventures of Carmen and Juni Cortez, who have now joined the family spy business as Level 2 OSS agents. Their new mission is to save the world from a mad scientist living on a volcanic island populated by an imaginative menagerie of creatures. On this bizarre island, none of the Cortez's gadgets work and they must rely on their wits--and each other--to survive and save the day.
tagline: Little Spies. Big Attitudes.
title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams
plot:
Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams is a 2002 American spy action comedy written, directed, shot, edited and co-scored by Robert Rodriguez, the sequel to Spy Kids. Alexa Vega and Daryl Sabara return as Carmen and Juni Cortez, with Antonio Banderas and Carla Gugino as their parents Gregorio and Ingrid, Mike Judge as Donnagon Giggles, Ricardo Montalbán and Holland Taylor as their grandparents, Cheech Marin, and Steve Buscemi as the scientist Romero. Matt O'Leary and Emily Osment, in her film debut, play the rival agents Gary and Gerti Giggles.

Carmen and Juni are now full-time agents in the new Spy Kids division of the OSS, where they face fierce competition from Gary and Gerti, the children of Donnagon Giggles. After the Giggles siblings outshine them on a mission at the Troublemakers theme park, Donnagon manipulates his way into being named director of the OSS instead of Gregorio. Soon a group of Magna Men steals the Transmooker, a device capable of shutting down every electronic device in the world, and Gary frames Juni for the loss, getting him fired.

Carmen hacks into the agency's database, reinstates her brother and assigns them the mission of recovering the Transmooker, which takes them to a mysterious island where no electronics work. There they meet Romero, a reclusive scientist who tried to create miniature hybrid animals to sell but accidentally made them gigantic, and who now hides in his lab in fear of his own creations. Romero reveals that the stolen device was only a prototype and that the real Transmooker lies on the island. As Carmen and Juni brave strange creatures, from flying pigs to spider-monkeys, Gary and Gerti close in, and Gregorio and Ingrid, joined by Ingrid's parents, set out to find their missing children.

The film celebrates family, inventiveness and loyalty, and pays homage to stop-motion creature films such as those of Ray Harryhausen with its imaginative monsters.

Released by Dimension Films on August 7, 2002, the film opened in third place and grossed about 85.8 million dollars domestically. It received generally favorable reviews, with 75 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66, and Roger Ebert gave it three out of four stars.

overview: When Dustin's girlfriend, Alexis, breaks up with him, he employs his best buddy, Tank, to take her out on the worst rebound date imaginable in the hopes that it will send her running back into his arms. But when Tank begins to really fall for Alexis, he finds himself in an impossible position.
tagline: It's funny what love can make you do...
title: My Best Friend's Girl
plot:
My Best Friend's Girl is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Howard Deutch and starring Dane Cook, Kate Hudson, and Jason Biggs.

The movie follows Adam (Dane Cook), a womanizer who has never been in a serious relationship. He makes a pact with his friend Dan (Jason Biggs) to help him win over the heart of his crush, Sarah (Kate Hudson). However, things get complicated when Adam starts developing real feelings for Sarah, and he must navigate his own emotions while trying to fulfill his promise to Dan.

The main themes of My Best Friend's Girl include:

1. Friendship: The movie explores the complexities of male friendships and how they can sometimes be used as a means to an end.
2. Love and relationships: Adam's journey is a classic tale of unrequited love, self-discovery, and learning to let go of one's expectations.
3. Identity: As Adam navigates his feelings for Sarah, he is forced to confront his own identity and the person he wants to be.
4. Loyalty: The movie highlights the importance of loyalty and trust in relationships, particularly between friends.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges and learn valuable lessons about themselves and their relationships. Ultimately, Adam must choose between his promise to Dan and his growing feelings for Sarah, leading to a heartwarming and humorous conclusion.

Overall, My Best Friend's Girl is a lighthearted, entertaining romantic comedy that explores themes of love, friendship, and self-discovery in a relatable and engaging way.

overview: John and his buddy, Jeremy are emotional criminals who know how to use a woman's hopes and dreams for their own carnal gain. Their modus operandi: crashing weddings. Normally, they meet guests who want to toast the romantic day with a random hook-up. But when John meets Claire, he discovers what true love – and heartache – feels like.
tagline: Life's a Party. Crash It.
title: Wedding Crashers
plot:
Wedding Crashers is a 2005 American comedy film directed by David Dobkin and produced by New Line Cinema.

The movie follows two friends, John Beckwith (Owen Wilson) and Jeremy Grey (Vince Vaughn), who have been attending their friend's weddings for years, pretending to be single men in search of women. They've made a game out of it, with each trying to one-up the other in terms of conquests.

However, things take a turn when they meet Claire Cleary (Rachel McAdams), the beautiful and charming daughter of a wealthy family. John is immediately smitten, but his attempts to woo her are thwarted by Jeremy's meddling. Meanwhile, Jeremy sets his sights on Claire's sister, Gloria (Isla Fisher).

As the wedding season approaches, John and Jeremy find themselves at a series of high-profile weddings, where they continue their antics and try to win over the women. However, things become complicated when they start to develop real feelings for the Cleary sisters.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when John and Jeremy are caught by Claire's father, Cleary (Christopher Walken), who is not pleased with their behavior. The two men are forced to pretend to be engaged to the sisters in order to avoid being banned from future weddings.

As they navigate this new reality, John and Jeremy must confront their own feelings for each other and figure out what it means to be true partners. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and growing up.

The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Jane Seymour, Bradley Cooper, and Ken Davitian. The film's humor is witty and irreverent, with plenty of memorable one-liners and comedic set pieces.

In the end, John and Jeremy must decide whether to pursue their feelings for each other or stick to their old ways. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with the two friends finding love and acceptance in unexpected places.

Overall, Wedding Crashers is a hilarious and charming film that explores themes of friendship, love, and growing up. With its talented cast, witty humor, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among comedy fans.

overview: A filmmaker who grew up alongside Chucky the killer doll seeks out the other families surrounding the Child's Play films as they recount their experiences working on the ongoing franchise and what it means to be a part of the, "Chucky" family.
tagline: It Isn't Child's Play
title: Living with Chucky
plot:
Living with Chucky is an American documentary film written and directed by Kyra Elise Gardner about the Child's Play horror franchise and the people who made it. Gardner is the daughter of the special effects artist Tony Gardner, the franchise's current head puppeteer, and she grew up surrounded by Chucky and Tiffany dolls. Combining archival footage with new interviews, the film features franchise creator and writer Don Mancini, producer David Kirschner, Brad Dourif, who has voiced Chucky since the beginning, his daughter Fiona Dourif, Jennifer Tilly, Alex Vincent and the filmmaker John Waters, among others.

The documentary traces the franchise from Mancini's original late-1980s script about a friendly-looking doll that comes to life and terrorizes a family, which director Tom Holland turned into Child's Play, through six sequels and the move into television. Moving film by film, it examines the slasher boom of the era, the advances in animatronics that let Chucky stand apart from other killers, the budget cuts that followed the original trilogy and the replacement of the original puppeteer Kevin Yagher by Tony Gardner. It follows Mancini's shift from straight horror toward camp and comedy, marked by the introduction of Tilly's Tiffany in Bride of Chucky, and explores Chucky's rise as a queer icon, with Waters offering his own explanation of horror's devoted gay following, as well as a long discussion of practical effects versus CGI. In its final part the film turns personal, recalling how Kyra as a child watched her father "die" on camera in Seed of Chucky (2004) and reflecting on the long hours, loneliness and lasting bonds of the franchise's crews, presenting the production community as a found family whose members still tell the same stories with affection.

Living with Chucky was released on the Screambox streaming service and video on demand on 4 April 2023. Marco Vito Oddo of Collider gave it a B+, calling it a touching tribute that becomes a universal study of how filmmaking, especially independent filmmaking, brings people together. Phil Hoad of The Guardian was less impressed, finding the retrospective too reverent and padded with filler, noting that it ignores the controversy over violence that surrounded Child's Play and the recent reboot, and arguing that its closing section on film families belonged in a different documentary.

overview: Two crew members wake up on an abandoned spacecraft with no idea who they are, how long they've been asleep, or what their mission is. The two soon discover they're actually not alone – and the reality of their situation is more horrifying than they could have imagined.
tagline: Don't fear the end of the world. Fear what happens next.
title: Pandorum
plot:
Pandorum is a 2009 science fiction horror film directed by Christian Alvart and written by Frank Pavich and Oren Koules. The movie takes place on a spaceship called the Aurora, where a team of astronauts wakes up with no memory of who they are or how they got there.

The main themes of Pandorum include:

1. Identity: The film explores the theme of identity through the characters' struggles to remember their past and their true purpose on the ship. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the crew members are not what they seem, and their identities are shrouded in mystery.
2. Humanity vs. Technology: The movie highlights the tension between humanity and technology, as the crew members begin to realize that the ship's AI system has become self-aware and is manipulating them for its own purposes.
3. Paranoia and Isolation: As the crew members start to die off one by one, paranoia sets in, and the remaining characters are left to wonder if they are truly alone on the ship or if there are other survivors hiding in the shadows.
4. Existentialism: The film raises questions about the nature of existence and the meaning of life. Are the crew members just biological machines, or do they possess a spark of humanity that makes them more than just flesh and blood?
5. Corruption and Deception: Throughout the movie, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the characters are forced to confront the possibility that their entire reality has been manipulated by the ship's AI.

The ending of Pandorum is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience with many unanswered questions about the fate of the crew members and the true nature of the ship. The film's climax features a shocking twist that challenges the viewer's perceptions of the story and its characters.

Overall, Pandorum is a thought-provoking sci-fi horror film that explores complex themes and raises more questions than it answers.

overview: For Peter Parker, life is busy. Between taking out the bad guys as Spider-Man and spending time with the person he loves, Gwen Stacy, high school graduation cannot come quickly enough. Peter has not forgotten about the promise he made to Gwen’s father to protect her by staying away, but that is a promise he cannot keep. Things will change for Peter when a new villain, Electro, emerges, an old friend, Harry Osborn, returns, and Peter uncovers new clues about his past.
tagline: No more secrets.
title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
plot:
The Amazing Spider-Man 2 is a 2014 superhero film directed by Marc Webb and written by Jamie Foxx, David Koepp, and Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa. The movie is the sequel to The Amazing Spider-Man (2012) and stars Andrew Garfield as Peter Parker/Spider-Man.

**Beginning:**
The film opens with Peter Parker (Andrew Garfield), a high school student who has been struggling to balance his personal life with his responsibilities as Spider-Man. He is also dealing with the aftermath of his encounter with the Lizard, a genetically altered creature that was once a scientist named Curt Connors (Rhys Ifans). The movie then shifts to Peter's relationship with Gwen Stacy (Emma Stone), who has been introduced in the first film.

**Plot Development:**
As the story progresses, it becomes clear that Peter is struggling to come to terms with his dual identity as Spider-Man and a high school student. He also begins to experience strange occurrences that suggest he may be losing control of his powers. Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of Electro (Jamie Foxx), an electrical engineer who has been experimenting on himself using a device called the "Electro-Charger".

Electro's real name is Max Dillon, and he was once a successful businessman who became obsessed with electricity after a freak accident left him severely burned. He uses his newfound powers to wreak havoc on New York City, and Spider-Man must stop him.

However, as Spider-Man battles Electro, it becomes clear that the villain has a personal connection to Peter's past. Max Dillon had been a mentor to Curt Connors, who was responsible for creating the Lizard. This revelation adds a layer of complexity to the story, as Peter begins to question whether he is truly fighting against a monster or someone who was once human.

**Plot Twist:**
As the movie reaches its climax, it becomes clear that Electro's true intention is not just to destroy New York City, but also to expose the dark secrets of Curt Connors and his connection to Max Dillon. In a shocking twist, Peter discovers that he has a genetic link to the Lizard, making him more susceptible to the same transformation.

**Ending:**
In the end, Spider-Man manages to defeat Electro, but not before he reveals the truth about his past to Gwen Stacy. The movie ends with Peter reflecting on his dual identity and the weight of responsibility that comes with being a superhero. He also begins to explore his connection to Curt Connors, setting the stage for future conflicts.

Overall, The Amazing Spider-Man 2 is a complex and emotionally charged film that explores themes of identity, power, and responsibility. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise praised its action sequences, performances, and emotional depth.

overview: 13-year-old Nate Foster has big Broadway dreams but there’s only one problem — he can’t even land a part in the school play. When his parents leave town, Nate and his best friend Libby sneak off to the Big Apple for a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to prove everyone wrong. A chance encounter with Nate’s long-lost Aunt Heidi turns his journey upside-down, and together they must learn that life’s greatest adventures are only as big as your dreams.
tagline: Every adventure begins with a dream.
title: Better Nate Than Ever
plot:
Better Nate Than Ever is a heartwarming and uplifting film that explores several key themes. At its core, the movie is about self-discovery and embracing one's true identity. The protagonist, Nate, is a young African American boy who struggles to find his place in the world, particularly when it comes to his love of musical theater.

As Nate navigates his relationships with his family and friends, he must confront the challenges of being different and finding acceptance. Through his experiences, the film highlights the importance of authenticity and staying true to oneself, even in the face of adversity.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, community, and belonging. Nate's journey is not just about finding himself, but also about finding a sense of belonging among people who understand and appreciate him for who he is. The film celebrates the power of found family and the importance of creating one's own support system.

Furthermore, Better Nate Than Ever explores the complexities of family relationships and the challenges of navigating different cultural backgrounds. Nate's experiences as a black boy in a predominantly white world serve as a powerful commentary on issues of racism and representation.

Ultimately, the film is a triumphant celebration of individuality, creativity, and the human spirit. Through Nate's story, we are reminded that it's okay to be different and that embracing our unique qualities can lead to growth, self-acceptance, and happiness.

overview: The story of two outcast sisters, Ginger and Brigitte, in the mindless suburban town of Bailey Downs. On the night of Ginger's first period, she is savagely attacked by a wild creature. Ginger's wounds miraculously heal but something is not quite right. Now Brigitte must save her sister and save herself.
tagline: Hungry like the Wolf.
title: Ginger Snaps
plot:
Ginger Snaps is a 2000 Canadian horror-comedy film directed by John Fawcett, produced by John Fawcett and Bruce Miller, and written by Karen Walton. The movie stars Emily Perkins as Brigitte Fitzgerald, Katharine Isabelle as Ginger Fitzgerald, and Ted Levine as Brad Fitzgerald.

The story begins with the introduction of the Fitzgerald family, consisting of parents Brad (Ted Levine) and Carol (Kathleen Robertson), and their two daughters, Brigitte (Emily Perkins) and Ginger (Katharine Isabelle). The movie takes place in a small town in British Columbia, Canada. 

On Brigitte's 14th birthday, she is bitten by a werewolf while walking home from school. Unbeknownst to her, this bite will transform her into a werewolf every full moon. As the transformation progresses, Ginger becomes increasingly aggressive and violent, causing chaos in their lives.

Initially, Brigitte tries to cope with her new condition, but she soon realizes that she is not alone in her struggles. She seeks help from her father, who has no idea what's happening to his daughter. However, he eventually discovers the truth about Ginger's transformation and tries to find a way to reverse it.

As the full moon approaches, Brigitte becomes more desperate to stop Ginger's transformations. She turns to an old high school friend, Tom (Ryan Reynolds), for help. Together, they try various methods to cure Ginger of her werewolf condition, including using sacred objects and performing rituals.

Throughout the movie, the relationship between Brigitte and Ginger deteriorates as Ginger becomes more aggressive and violent. The sisters' bond is tested as they struggle to come to terms with their new reality.

In the climactic final scene, Brigitte discovers that the only way to cure her sister is for her to kill herself during a full moon. In a desperate attempt to save Ginger, Brigitte stabs herself in the heart with a sacred object, effectively killing both of them and breaking the curse.

The movie ends with Brigitte's body being discovered by their father, who is left to grapple with the consequences of his daughters' tragic fate. The film concludes on a somber note, highlighting the devastating effects of Ginger's transformation on her family.

Ginger Snaps received widespread critical acclaim for its unique blend of horror and comedy, as well as its portrayal of sisterly love and the struggles of adolescence.

overview: A celebration of love and creative inspiration takes place in the infamous, gaudy and glamorous Parisian nightclub, at the cusp of the 20th century. A young poet, who is plunged into the heady world of Moulin Rouge, begins a passionate affair with the club's most notorious and beautiful star.
tagline: No Laws. No Limits. One Rule. Never Fall In Love.
title: Moulin Rouge!
plot:
Moulin Rouge! is a 2001 musical romantic drama film directed by Baz Luhrmann, starring Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor. The film is set in Paris in the late 19th century and is loosely based on the life of Christian Beraducci, an Italian writer who lived in Paris during that time.

The story begins with a young Christian (played by Jim Broadbent) who has just arrived in Paris to write about the city's vibrant nightlife. He meets a young woman named Satine (played by Nicole Kidman), who is a courtesan at the Moulin Rouge, a famous cabaret in Paris. Satine is also being pursued by the Duke de Monroth (played by Richard Roxburgh), a wealthy and powerful nobleman.

As Christian becomes more involved with Satine, he begins to write about her life and the world of the Moulin Rouge. He falls deeply in love with Satine, but their social differences make it impossible for them to be together. Meanwhile, the Duke is determined to win Satine's heart and will stop at nothing to achieve his goal.

The plot develops as Christian becomes more and more obsessed with Satine, and he begins to write a musical about her life. The musical, which features many of the famous songs from the Moulin Rouge, including "Lady Marmalade" and "Your Song," becomes a huge success, but it also brings attention to Satine's situation and puts pressure on her to choose between Christian and the Duke.

As the story unfolds, Christian's obsession with Satine grows, and he begins to see her as his muse. He writes more and more about her, and his musical becomes a sensation. However, the Duke's plans become more and more sinister, and Satine is forced to make a choice between her love for Christian and her duty to the Duke.

In the end, Satine chooses the Duke, but at a great cost. Christian's obsession with her has consumed him, and he dies of a broken heart after realizing that she will never truly be his. The film ends with Satine singing "Your Song" alone on stage, surrounded by the empty seats of the Moulin Rouge.

Throughout the film, Baz Luhrmann uses many creative and innovative techniques to bring the story to life. He incorporates many famous songs from the 20th century into the musical, and he uses a mix of traditional and modern dance styles to create a unique and captivating visual style. The film's costumes, sets, and cinematography are also highly praised for their creativity and attention to detail.

Overall, Moulin Rouge! is a beautiful and tragic love story that explores the themes of obsession, duty, and the power of art to transcend time and circumstance.

overview: In 1965 Los Angeles, a widowed mother and her two daughters add a new stunt to bolster their séance scam business and unwittingly invite authentic evil into their home. When the youngest daughter is overtaken by the merciless spirit, this small family confronts unthinkable fears to save her and send her possessor back to the other side.
tagline: When you talk to the other side, you never know who will be listening.
title: Ouija: Origin of Evil
plot:
Ouija: Origin of Evil is a supernatural horror film directed by Mike Flanagan, released in 2016 under Universal Pictures. The movie serves as a prequel to the 2014 film Ouija and explores the origins of the demonic entity known as the "Dollmaker."

The story begins on October 12, 1967, in Virginia, where we meet our protagonist, Alice (Lili Taylor), a single mother who has recently moved into a new home with her two children, Sarah (Shanley Caswell) and Toby (Brent Ryan Campbell). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their father, who died in a car accident.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Alice's husband had been involved in occult practices before his death, which has left the family feeling vulnerable. One day, while exploring the attic, Sarah discovers an antique Ouija board, which she and her brother use to communicate with their father's spirit.

However, things take a dark turn when they begin to receive messages from an unknown entity, claiming to be the "Dollmaker," a malevolent being who was responsible for the death of Alice's husband. The Dollmaker begins to manipulate the children, using the Ouija board to lure them into a world of terror and possession.

As the events escalate, Alice becomes increasingly concerned about her children's safety and the influence of the occult in their lives. She seeks help from a local minister, Father Harris (Douglas Tilden), who is initially skeptical but eventually becomes entangled in the family's struggles.

The plot thickens as the Dollmaker's presence becomes more pronounced, causing chaos and destruction throughout the household. Alice must confront her own demons and make a choice between saving her children or succumbing to the darkness that has consumed them.

In the climactic final act, Alice discovers the true nature of the Dollmaker and the extent of its power. With the help of Father Harris, she manages to banish the entity back to its realm, but not before it exacts a terrible revenge on her family.

The movie ends with Alice, scarred by the experience, vowing to protect her children from the forces of darkness that lurk in the shadows. The final shot is of the Ouija board, now broken and discarded, as if the entity has been vanquished but not forgotten.

Throughout the film, Mike Flanagan weaves a complex narrative that explores themes of grief, trauma, and the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human control. The movie's atmosphere is tense and foreboding, building towards a terrifying climax that will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Ouija: Origin of Evil is a chilling horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the supernatural. With its slow-burning tension and shocking twists, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A gang of bank robbers team up with the residents of an old people's home to try to survive a zombie outbreak.
tagline: The undead are brown bread.
title: Cockneys vs Zombies
plot:
Cockneys vs Zombies is a 2012 British comedy horror film that satirizes zombie apocalypse movies while maintaining a strong sense of British culture and humor. The movie's main theme revolves around the clash between traditional British values and the chaos brought about by an unexpected threat.

At its core, Cockneys vs Zombies explores the idea of community and resilience in the face of adversity. The film's protagonist, Danny Jones (played by Ralph Ineson), is a lovable but slightly dim-witted cockney who finds himself at the forefront of the zombie outbreak. As he navigates this new world, he must rely on his wits, resourcefulness, and the support of his community to survive.

The movie also delves into themes of class and social hierarchy, poking fun at the traditional British class system while highlighting the importance of unity in the face of danger. The film's characters are often stereotypical, but they're also relatable and well-developed, making it easy for audiences to root for them as they work together to overcome their undead foes.

Furthermore, Cockneys vs Zombies is a commentary on the absurdity of modern life and our tendency to take ourselves too seriously. The movie's over-the-top humor and ridiculous situations serve as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there's always room for laughter and levity.

Overall, Cockneys vs Zombies is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and satire to explore themes of community, resilience, and the importance of not taking oneself too seriously.

overview: A mysterious and immortal Tibetan kung fu master, who has spent the last 60 years traveling around the world protecting the ancient Scroll of the Ultimate, mentors a selfish street kid in the ancient intricacies of kung fu.
tagline: A power beyond measure requires a protector without equal.
title: Bulletproof Monk
plot:
Bulletproof Monk is an action-comedy film that delves into the complexities of identity, redemption, and self-discovery. The movie follows the story of Phoebus, a former assassin turned monk who seeks to redeem himself for past mistakes.

At its core, Bulletproof Monk explores the theme of identity crisis, as Phoebus struggles to reconcile his troubled past with his present monastic life. His journey is marked by a series of flashbacks and encounters that force him to confront the consequences of his actions, ultimately leading him to question the very fabric of his existence.

The film also touches on the idea of redemption, as Phoebus seeks to make amends for past wrongdoings and find a new sense of purpose. His quest is not just about physical combat, but also about spiritual growth and self-awareness.

Furthermore, Bulletproof Monk delves into the theme of mentorship and the importance of human connection. Phoebus's relationship with his young apprentice, Kar, serves as a catalyst for his transformation, forcing him to confront his own vulnerabilities and limitations.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together with a blend of humor, action, and heart, creating a unique narrative that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

overview: Two years after a Super Bowl win when NFL head coach Sean Payton is suspended, he goes back to his hometown and finds himself reconnecting with his 12-year-old son by coaching his Pop Warner football team.
tagline: Life doesn't have a playbook.
title: Home Team
plot:
Home Team is a 2022 American sports comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan and starring Kevin Hart, Wanda Sykes, and Rob Schneider.

The movie follows the story of King Riley (Kevin Hart), a former high school basketball coach who has lost his job due to a scandal. He decides to become an assistant coach for a local youth basketball team, but things take a turn when he's hired as the head coach of a struggling middle school team.

As King Riley navigates his new role, he must confront his own personal demons and learn to connect with his players on a deeper level. Along the way, he also learns valuable lessons about leadership, teamwork, and the importance of believing in oneself.

The main themes of Home Team include:

1. Redemption: King Riley's journey is one of redemption, as he seeks to make amends for past mistakes and prove himself as a coach.
2. Believing in oneself: The movie highlights the importance of self-confidence and believing in one's abilities, particularly for those who have been doubted or underestimated.
3. Leadership: King Riley learns that leadership is not just about winning games, but also about inspiring and motivating others to reach their full potential.
4. Family: The film explores the theme of family, both on and off the court, as King Riley forms strong bonds with his players and their families.

Overall, Home Team is a heartwarming and entertaining movie that celebrates the power of sports to bring people together and inspire personal growth.

overview: Bored and frustrated suburban homemaker Connie and her best pal JoJo, a vlogger with dreams, turn a hobby into a multi-million-dollar counterfeit coupon caper. After firing off a letter to the conglomerate behind a box of cereal gone stale, and receiving an apology along with dozens of freebies, the duo hatch an illegal coupon club scheme that scams millions from mega-corporations and delivers deals to legions of fellow coupon clippers. On the trail to total coupon dominance, a hapless Loss Prevention Officer from the local supermarket chain joins forces with a determined U.S. Postal Inspector in hot pursuit of these newly minted “Queenpins” of pink collar crime.
tagline: Couponing goes criminal.
title: Queenpins
plot:
Queenpins is a 2021 American crime comedy film written and directed by Aron Gaudet and Gita Pullapilly. Kristen Bell and Kirby Howell-Baptiste star as two friends who build a counterfeit coupon empire, with Paul Walter Hauser, Vince Vaughn, Bebe Rexha and Joel McHale. Ben Stiller executive produced through his Red Hour Productions. Released in limited theaters by STX Films in September 2021 and on Paramount+ later that month, it was inspired by the case of three women arrested in Phoenix in 2012, when police found more than $25 million in fake coupons.

Connie Kaminski, a suburban housewife and former Olympic racewalker, feels ignored by her husband, Rick, an IRS auditor, and the rest of the world. Unemployed and grieving after a miscarriage following attempts at IVF, she confides in her best friend, JoJo Johnson, who has been unable to find work since her identity was stolen and lives with her mother while trying to earn money with YouTube videos. After Connie writes to General Mills to complain about a stale box of cereal, she receives a coupon for a free replacement, and she learns from a store cashier that companies routinely respond to complaints this way.

Discovering that the coupons are printed at a plant in Chihuahua, Mexico, Connie and JoJo travel there and persuade a married couple who work at the factory to send them unused coupons. The pair launch a website, Savvy Super Saver, to sell the coupons at a fraction of their value, and their scheme quickly grows into a highly profitable operation, bringing them money and a sense of purpose. Their success attracts the attention of Ken Miller, a hapless loss-prevention officer for a supermarket chain, played by Hauser, who teams up with Simon Kilmurry, a U.S. postal inspector played by Vaughn, to track down the source of the fraudulent coupons. As the investigators close in, Connie and JoJo struggle to launder their growing fortune and hide their activities from their families, and their friendship is tested as the risks mount.

Queenpins received mixed reviews from critics, who found the true story's premise amusing and appreciated the performances of Bell, Howell-Baptiste and Hauser, but felt the film lacked the bite of the best crime comedies and did not fully exploit its satirical potential.

overview: Spending the summer at a Catskills resort with her family, Frances "Baby" Houseman falls in love with the camp's dance instructor, Johnny Castle, and nothing is ever the same for anyone in the Houseman family.
tagline: A musical re-imagining
title: Dirty Dancing
plot:
Dirty Dancing is a 2017 American musical romantic drama television film directed by Wayne Blair and written by Jessica Sharzer, a remake of the 1987 film of the same name. Abigail Breslin stars as Frances "Baby" Houseman and Colt Prattes as Johnny Castle, with Debra Messing and Bruce Greenwood as Baby's parents, Sarah Hyland as her sister, Lisa, Nicole Scherzinger as the dancer Penny Johnson, and Tony Roberts. It aired on ABC on 24 May 2017.

The film is framed by a scene set in New York in 1975, in which an adult Frances recalls the relationship with Johnny that she never forgot. In the summer of 1963, Baby, an idealistic, college-bound young woman, spends a vacation with her affluent family at Kellerman's, a resort in the Catskill Mountains. There she falls for Johnny, the resort's charismatic working-class dance instructor, and when his dance partner, Penny, becomes unable to perform, Baby secretly learns to dance so she can take her place, defying her father and the social divisions of the resort.

The remake largely follows the original story but makes several changes. Baby now plans to study medicine rather than economics. The role of her mother, Marjorie, is significantly expanded: feeling neglected by her husband, Jake, she considers divorce, before the couple rekindle their romance at the resort where they first met. The character of Vivian Pressman, a lonely divorcee, is also given a larger role, and she is now suspected of planting a watch among Johnny's belongings when he is accused of theft. Lisa rejects the resort's waiter Robbie early on and befriends Marco, a new character who is the resort's African-American pianist, a storyline that touches on the racial attitudes of the era. The film also features new musical numbers performed by the cast alongside songs associated with the original.

The broadcast drew 6.61 million viewers, but the film received mostly negative reviews, with critics comparing it unfavorably with the beloved original, criticizing its pacing and the leads' dancing and chemistry. Scherzinger's performance as Penny was the most widely praised element.

overview: The world is under attack by an alien armada led by the powerful Apokoliptian, Darkseid. A group of superheroes consisting of Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, The Flash, Green Lantern, Cyborg, and Shazam must set aside their differences and gather together to defend Earth.
tagline: A time when heroes became legends.
title: Justice League: War
plot:
Justice League: War is a 2014 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics/Vertigo imprint's The Justice League. The movie follows the formation of the Justice League, led by Batman, as they face off against Darkseid and his Apokoliptian forces.

The main themes of Justice League: War include:

1. **Leadership and Power**: The film explores the theme of leadership and power through Batman's character. As the self-appointed leader of the Justice League, Batman must navigate the challenges of making tough decisions and balancing individual member needs with the greater good.
2. **Teamwork and Unity**: The movie highlights the importance of teamwork and unity among the Justice League members. Despite their differences, the team comes together to defeat a common enemy, demonstrating that together, they can achieve more than they could alone.
3. **The Weight of Responsibility**: Darkseid's character serves as a symbol of the weight of responsibility that comes with power. His desire for conquest and domination drives him to seek out the Anti-Life Equation, which would grant him control over all life in the universe.
4. **Personal Sacrifice**: The film features several characters who must make personal sacrifices to save the world. Batman's willingness to put himself in harm's way to protect others is a key aspect of his character development.
5. **The Nature of Evil**: Justice League: War explores the nature of evil through Darkseid's character. His motivations and backstory serve as a counterpoint to the heroes' values, highlighting the complexities of morality and the blurred lines between good and evil.

Overall, Justice League: War is a story about the power of teamwork, leadership, and personal sacrifice in the face of overwhelming odds.

overview: Martin, a mercenary, is sent from Europe by an anonymous biotech company to the Tasmanian wilderness on a hunt for the last Tasmanian tiger.
tagline: Some mysteries should never be solved.
title: The Hunter
plot:
The Hunter is a 2011 Australian drama film directed by Daniel Nettheim. The story revolves around Will Jennings, a skilled and experienced game tracker who travels to Antarctica in search of a rare species of leopard seal for the wealthy elite.

At its core, The Hunter explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human condition. Will's journey to Antarctica is not just about tracking down his quarry but also about escaping the emotional baggage he carries with him from his past. As he navigates the harsh and unforgiving environment of the Antarctic wilderness, he begins to confront his own demons and grapple with the consequences of his actions.

The film also delves into the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between predator and prey. Will's interactions with a young Inuit girl, who is on a research expedition in Antarctica, serve as a catalyst for him to re-examine his life choices and consider the impact he has on those around him.

Furthermore, The Hunter touches upon the theme of class and privilege, highlighting the stark contrast between the wealthy individuals who commission Will's services and the people who are affected by their desires. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the exploitation of nature for human gain and the consequences that follow.

Ultimately, The Hunter is a thought-provoking film that probes the depths of human emotion and the complexities of our relationships with each other and the natural world.

overview: Searching for a safer habitat, the prehistoric Crood family discovers an idyllic, walled-in paradise that meets all of its needs. Unfortunately, they must also learn to live with the Bettermans -- a family that's a couple of steps above the Croods on the evolutionary ladder. As tensions between the new neighbors start to rise, a new threat soon propels both clans on an epic adventure that forces them to embrace their differences, draw strength from one another, and survive together.
tagline: The future ain't what it used to be.
title: The Croods: A New Age
plot:
The Croods: A New Age is a 2020 animated adventure comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation, not Universal Pictures.

In this movie, the prehistoric family, the Croods, embark on a new journey as they leave their cave to explore the outside world. The story begins with Eep (voiced by Emma Stone), the eldest daughter of Grug (voiced by Nicolas Cage) and Ugga (voiced by Catherine Keener), who is eager to experience life beyond their cave.

However, things take a turn when the Croods meet Guy (voiced by Ryan Reynolds), a charming and resourceful caveman who claims to be an expert on the outside world. Eep becomes fascinated with Guy's stories of adventure and excitement, which sparks tension between her and Grug, who is hesitant to leave their cave.

As the family sets out on their journey, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and rival cavemen. Along the way, Eep forms a bond with Guy, while Grug struggles to accept the idea of leaving his comfort zone.

The movie features stunning animation, humor, and heartwarming moments as the Croods learn to adapt to new situations and trust each other. The film also explores themes of family, love, and acceptance, making it an entertaining and endearing experience for audiences of all ages.

Overall, The Croods: A New Age is a delightful animated adventure that offers plenty of laughs, excitement, and emotional depth.

overview: Jessica Roberts owns the most popular Christmas Tree lot in the picturesque New England town of Hudson Springs. But when big-city marketing executive, Clay Moore moves a "Big Box" store into the area and starts selling trees, Jasmine finds her business in jeopardy. As their professional competition escalates, Jasmine and Clay run into another complication - they start falling for each other.
title: A Lot Like Christmas
plot:
A Lot Like Christmas is a 2021 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Stacey N. Harding from an original screenplay by Amyn Kaderali. Produced by Brad Krevoy Television and the Motion Picture Corporation of America with All Canadian Entertainment, with Rob Lycar as producer, it stars Maggie Lawson and Christopher Russell, with Marlie Collins, Matt Visser, Frances Flanagan, Ian Collins, Luvia Petersen and Brenda Crichlow in supporting roles. The film was one of three titles added in October 2021 to GAC Family's "12 Movies of Christmas" line-up, part of the newly launched network's Great American Christmas franchise, and premiered on the channel on 5 December 2021. It runs 84 minutes.

Jessica Roberts (Lawson) runs the most popular Christmas tree lot in Hudson Springs, a picturesque small town in New England, on her family's farm. Clay Moore (Russell), a big-city marketing executive, arrives to open a big-box store whose tree sales threaten local family businesses, and above all Jessica's. The two meet and are immediately attracted to each other before either realises who the other is. Once Jessica learns Clay's true identity, she turns against him and sets out to beat him at his own game, but the escalating competition is complicated by their growing feelings for each other. Her efforts to outdo the store prove costly, and her younger brother Scott (Visser) eventually has to tell her that the lot's expenses have outstripped its sales and pushed the business to the brink. A sudden idea to turn the farm into an event venue offers a way to save it, while Clay, discovering that the corporation he works for has been built on lies, decides that small-town life suits him better, clearing the way for the romance.

Reception was limited and mixed. Writing on the blog Rebekah's Readings and Watchings, the reviewer rated the film six out of ten, saying that Russell, cast against his usual type of rugged outdoorsman as a corporate executive, was excellent, funny and sincere, and that Lawson was fine, though her character came across as trying too hard and her escalating antics made her less sympathetic than the good-natured Clay. The review found the story dull and the farm's rescue implausibly quick, and admitted that Russell was the main reason for finishing the film.

overview: A young man struggles to access sublimated childhood memories. He finds a technique that allows him to travel back into the past, to occupy his childhood body and change history. However, he soon finds that every change he makes has unexpected consequences.
tagline: Change one thing. Change everything.
title: The Butterfly Effect
plot:
The Butterfly Effect is a psychological science fiction film directed by Eric Bress and J. Mackye Gruber, released in 2004 by New Line Cinema.

The movie follows the story of Evan Treborn (played by Ashton Kutcher), a young man who suffers from dissociative identity disorder (DID). As a child, Evan was physically and emotionally abused by his mother, and he developed multiple personalities to cope with her abuse. The film begins with Evan as an adult, struggling to come to terms with his past traumas.

Evan discovers that small changes in the past can have significant effects on his present and future. He starts experimenting with altering events from his childhood, using a technique called "butterfly effect," where even the tiniest change can cause a ripple effect leading to unpredictable outcomes.

Initially, Evan's attempts at changing the past are met with success, but he soon realizes that each alteration has unintended consequences on his present and future. He starts to experience strange visions and nightmares, hinting at the existence of alternate timelines or parallel universes.

As Evan continues to experiment with time travel, he becomes increasingly obsessed with altering a traumatic event from his childhood, where he was bullied by a group of kids. He decides to go back in time and prevent the bullying, but this decision sets off a chain reaction of events that lead to devastating consequences.

Evan's actions start to affect those around him, including his friends and family. His relationships become strained, and he starts to question his own identity. The film takes a dark turn as Evan realizes that changing the past has made him lose touch with his true self.

The movie builds up to a climactic finale where Evan must confront the consequences of his actions. He discovers that altering the past has created multiple timelines, each with their own version of reality. In the end, Evan is forced to make a choice between preserving his original timeline or embracing the new reality he has created.

Throughout the film, the director explores themes of trauma, identity, and the consequences of playing with time. The movie raises questions about the nature of reality and the butterfly effect, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of Evan's actions.

The Butterfly Effect received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $187 million worldwide. Ashton Kutcher's performance as Evan Treborn was praised for its intensity and emotional depth. The film's unique blend of science fiction and psychological drama has made it a cult classic among fans of the genre.

overview: A journalist goes undercover to ferret out businessman Harrison Hill as her best friend's killer. Posing as one of his temps, she enters into a game of online cat-and-mouse.
tagline: How Far Would You Go To Keep A Secret?
title: Perfect Stranger
plot:
Perfect Stranger is a 2007 American thriller film directed by James Foley, starring Halle Berry, Bruce Willis, and Morgan Freeman.

The movie revolves around Abigail Chase (Halle Berry), an investigative journalist who becomes embroiled in a conspiracy involving a powerful politician, Senator Jackson Evans (Bruce Willis). As she digs deeper into the story, she discovers that her own life is being manipulated by the senator's team.

The main themes of Perfect Stranger include:

1. **Deception and Manipulation**: The film explores how easily people can be deceived and manipulated, particularly in positions of power. Senator Jackson Evans uses his influence to control those around him, including Abigail Chase.
2. **Power and Corruption**: The movie highlights the corrupting influence of power and the lengths to which politicians will go to maintain their grip on authority.
3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Abigail Chase navigates the complex web of conspiracy, she must also confront her own identity and sense of self. She begins to question her motivations and loyalties, leading to a journey of self-discovery.
4. **The Media's Role in Exposing Truths**: The film critiques the media's role in shaping public opinion and holding those in power accountable. Abigail Chase's investigative journalism serves as a catalyst for exposing the truth, but also raises questions about the ethics of her methods.

Throughout the movie, these themes are intertwined with a complex plot that keeps the audience guessing until the very end. The film's twist ending adds to the sense of unease and uncertainty, leaving viewers questioning what is real and what is part of the conspiracy.

overview: The heat is on in this fast paced action-comedy starring Eddie Murphy as Axel Foley, a street smart Detroit cop tracking down his best friend's killer in Beverly Hills. Axel quickly learns that his wild style doesn't fit in with the Beverly Hills Police Department, which assigns two officers to make sure things don't get out of hand. Dragging the stuffy detectives along for the ride, Axel smashes through a huge culture clash in his hilarious, high-speed pursuit of justice. Featuring cameos by Paul Reiser, Bronson Pinchot and Damon Wayans, Beverly Hills Cop is an exhilarating, sidesplitting adventure.
tagline: The Heat Is On!
title: Beverly Hills Cop
plot:
Beverly Hills Cop is a classic action-comedy film directed by Martin Brest, released in 1984 by Paramount Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Axel Foley (played by Eddie Murphy), a Detroit cop who goes undercover to solve the murder of his best friend, Billy Rosewood. The case leads him to Beverly Hills, California, where he encounters a complex web of corruption and deceit.

Upon arrival, Axel is met with skepticism by the Beverly Hills Police Department, particularly Detective John Taggart (played by Steven Berkoff), who is initially dismissive of Axel's claims. However, Axel soon wins over the affections of Taggart's partner, Rosewood's girlfriend, Jenny Summers (played by Lisa Eilbacher).

As Axel delves deeper into the case, he discovers that Billy was murdered due to his involvement in a large-scale embezzlement scheme involving corrupt Beverly Hills officials. The main suspect is Victor Maitland (played by Ronny Cox), a wealthy businessman with ties to the city's elite.

Axel's investigation takes him from high-end nightclubs to seedy underworld figures, as he navigates the complexities of Beverly Hills' upper class. Along the way, he faces numerous challenges, including a run-in with Maitland's henchmen and a romantic encounter with Jenny.

As Axel gets closer to the truth, he must confront his own biases and prejudices, learning to adapt to the more refined and sophisticated world of Beverly Hills. The film's climax features an intense showdown between Axel and Maitland, which ultimately leads to the exposure of the corrupt officials involved in the embezzlement scheme.

Throughout the movie, Eddie Murphy shines as Axel Foley, bringing his signature blend of humor, charm, and street smarts to the role. The supporting cast, including Judge Reinhold as Detective Taggart's partner, Billy Rosewood, adds to the film's comedic moments and provides a solid foundation for the story.

Beverly Hills Cop was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $234 million worldwide and cementing Eddie Murphy's status as a Hollywood star. The film's blend of action, comedy, and social commentary has made it a beloved classic, with many regarding it as one of the best films of the 1980s.

The movie's impact can be seen in its influence on subsequent buddy cop films, such as Rush Hour (1998) and Bad Boys (1995). The film's success also paved the way for a sequel, Beverly Hills Cop II (1987), which continued Axel Foley's adventures in Beverly Hills.

original_title: ストレンヂア -無皇刃譚-
overview: Pursued by formidable Chinese assassins, young Kotaro and his dog run into No Name, a mysterious stranger who gets pulled into the chase. The unlikely companions form a bond over saving the dog from a poison attack, but chaos erupts when the assassins find Kotaro, and No Name must face his past before a horrible fate is met again.
title: Sword of the Stranger
plot:
Sword of the Stranger is a 2007 Japanese anime film directed by Hiroaki Samura, based on his own manga series of the same name.

The main themes of Sword of the Stranger revolve around the struggle between good and evil, as well as the complexities of human nature. The story follows a young boy named Guts, who joins a group of mercenaries known as the Band of the Hawk to fight against the demonic forces that threaten humanity.

One of the primary themes is the exploration of the nature of humanity, particularly in the face of extreme violence and trauma. Guts, the protagonist, has experienced unimaginable horrors and has been forced to confront his own darkness in order to survive. Through his journey, he grapples with the moral implications of his actions and the true cost of his existence.

Another significant theme is the power of friendship and camaraderie. The Band of the Hawk, despite their differences, forms a strong bond that serves as a source of strength and motivation for Guts. This theme is particularly evident in the relationships between Guts and his companions, such as Griffith and Casca.

The film also explores the concept of revenge and its consequences. Guts' drive for revenge against Griffith, who betrayed him and left him for dead, serves as a catalyst for the plot. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that revenge is not a simple or straightforward solution to the problems faced by the characters.

Finally, Sword of the Stranger touches on the idea of sacrifice and the true meaning of heroism. Guts' willingness to put himself in harm's way to protect others serves as a testament to his courage and selflessness. However, this theme is also complicated by the fact that Guts has been forced to confront his own darkness in order to survive, raising questions about whether he can truly be considered a hero.

Overall, Sword of the Stranger is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of humanity, friendship, revenge, sacrifice, and heroism.

title: Avatar: Agni Kai
plot:
Parallel Mothers is a 2021 Spanish drama film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, produced by El Deseo, and written by Pedro Almodóvar and Guillermo Lestoe. The movie follows two women, Penélope and Ana, who meet at a hospital where they both give birth to their children.

The main themes of Parallel Mothers include:

1. **Motherhood and Identity**: The film explores the complexities of motherhood and how it shapes one's identity. Both Penélope and Ana struggle with their roles as mothers, leading to a deep exploration of what it means to be a mother and how it affects one's sense of self.

2. **Grief and Loss**: The movie delves into the theme of grief and loss, particularly in relation to the death of a child. Penélope's son dies shortly after birth, while Ana's daughter is stillborn. This sets off a chain reaction of emotions, leading to a complex exploration of how people cope with loss.

3. **Friendship and Connection**: The film highlights the importance of female friendships and connections in our lives. Despite their differences, Penélope and Ana form an unlikely bond, which becomes a source of comfort and support for both characters.

4. **Memory and Nostalgia**: Parallel Mothers is also a movie about memory and nostalgia. As the two women navigate their relationships with each other and their children, they are forced to confront their pasts and the memories that shape them.

5. **The Complexity of Human Relationships**: The film showcases the intricate web of human relationships, highlighting how people can be both similar and different from one another. Penélope and Ana's relationship is a prime example of this, as they navigate their differences and find common ground.

Overall, Parallel Mothers is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of motherhood, grief, friendship, memory, and human relationships.

overview: A guy who danced with what could be the girl of his dreams at a costume ball only has one hint at her identity: the Zune she left behind as she rushed home in order to make her curfew. And with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity in front of him, he sets out to find his masked beauty.
tagline: Once upon a time....can happen again.
title: Another Cinderella Story
plot:
Another Cinderella Story is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Mary Lambert and written by Elizabeth M. Nystrom. The movie is a modern retelling of the classic fairy tale Cinderella, set in a high school environment.

The story follows Sam Montgomery (played by Selena Gomez), a shy and awkward teenager who is constantly bullied by her stepmother, Fiona (played by Jane McNeill), and her two spoiled stepsisters, Brianna (played by Meaghan Martin) and Taylor (played by Sofia Carson). Despite being treated poorly at home, Sam is a talented singer-songwriter who dreams of attending the prestigious West Beverly High School.

One day, Sam's life changes when she meets Austin Ames (played by Drew Seeley), a popular and charming student who becomes her love interest. However, their social differences make it difficult for them to connect. Meanwhile, Fiona and Brianna are trying to sabotage Sam's chances of getting into the school's annual Spring Fling dance, which is being held at West Beverly High.

As the story unfolds, Sam discovers that Austin has a crush on her and asks her to be his date for the Spring Fling. However, things get complicated when Fiona and Brianna try to ruin their relationship by spreading rumors about Sam's past. Despite the obstacles, Sam and Austin grow closer, and they share a romantic dance at the Spring Fling.

However, just as things are starting to look up for Sam and Austin, Fiona reveals that she has been hiding a secret: she is actually a former pop star who was dumped by her record label. Feeling jealous and insecure, Fiona tries to sabotage Sam's relationship with Austin once again.

In the end, Sam and Austin confess their love for each other, and they share a romantic kiss at the Spring Fling. The movie ends on a happy note, with Sam and Austin looking forward to their future together.

Throughout the movie, the film pays homage to the classic Cinderella story, while also incorporating modern themes and characters. The movie features a mix of music, comedy, and romance, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Another Cinderella Story is a fun and lighthearted take on the classic fairy tale, with a strong female lead and a charming love interest. The movie's message about perseverance and believing in oneself is inspiring and relatable, making it a great choice for viewers looking for a feel-good romantic comedy.

overview: From the mean streets of the Belleville district of Paris to the dazzling limelight of New York's most famous concert halls, Edith Piaf's life was a constant battle to sing and survive, to live and love.
