Raised in her grandmother's brothel, Piaf was discovered in 1935 by nightclub owner Louis Leplee, who persuaded her to sing despite her extreme nervousness. Piaf became one of France's immortal icons, her voice one of the indelible signatures of the 20th century.
tagline: The Extraordinary Story of Edith Piaf.
title: La Vie en Rose
plot:
La Vie en Rose is a biographical drama film that tells the story of Édith Piaf, a French singer and cabaret performer. The movie explores the tumultuous life of Piaf, from her early days as a struggling street urchin to her rise to fame as one of France's most beloved singers.

At its core, La Vie en Rose is a film about the power of music to transcend adversity and bring people together. Through Piaf's story, the movie highlights the redemptive qualities of art, showcasing how it can provide solace, comfort, and a sense of purpose in the face of hardship.

The film also delves into themes of love, loss, and identity. Piaf's relationships with her mother and her lover, Marcel Cassian, are central to the story, and their complexities serve as a backdrop for exploring the fragility of human connections. The movie suggests that even in the midst of turmoil, it is possible to find moments of beauty, joy, and connection.

Furthermore, La Vie en Rose touches on the theme of female empowerment, particularly in the context of Piaf's rise to fame. The film portrays her as a strong-willed and determined individual who refuses to be defined by societal expectations or constraints. Through Piaf's story, the movie celebrates the idea that women can be powerful, independent, and unapologetically themselves.

Overall, La Vie en Rose is a poignant and captivating film that explores the complexities of human experience through the lens of Édith Piaf's extraordinary life.

overview: After a mysterious global crisis, a young girl is left alone to hide from a malevolent power that stalks her home. Her parents eventually return and the struggle begins to save their daughter.
title: Stephanie
plot:
Stephanie is a 2017 American supernatural horror film directed by Akiva Goldsman from a screenplay by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski. Shree Crooks plays the title character, a young girl left alone in her family's home, with Frank Grillo and Anna Torv as her parents, Eric and Jane, and Jonah Beres as her brother, Paul. Blumhouse Productions was among its producers.

Stephanie has been abandoned by her parents and lives alone in the house with only a toy turtle named Frances for company, watched by a dark supernatural presence. News reports hint at a catastrophe unfolding in the outside world, but she flicks past them in search of cartoons. She keeps the body of her dead brother in his bed, alternately scolding and beating it and, after they make up, holding his cold hand, which squeezes back. Her games and tea parties are repeatedly interrupted by a shadowy figure, and each encounter ends with her waking up in bed.

Eventually Eric and Jane come home, apologise for leaving, bury Paul in the yard and try to resume normal life, though Eric always carries a gun and Jane bears deep scars across her stomach. That night Paul's corpse comes crashing back through the attic window, terrifying the parents while Stephanie remains calm. Questioned about the day they left, she recalls that Paul spoiled her pumpkin and that she broke his neck with telekinesis, a power that manifests as huge invisible tentacles and that also slashed Jane when she came to see what had happened. Her parents explain that the monster she has been seeing is not real: the monster is Stephanie herself. They sedate her and attempt brain surgery to remove her powers, but she wakes and destroys the makeshift lab.

Broadcasts reveal that murderous telekinetic children like her are appearing all over the world, with no cure, and that they must be killed. The parents' attempt to poison her cocoa fails when her power knocks the cup away, and when it lashes out at Eric he shoots her several times. She returns unhurt, tells them they never should have come back, and kills them both. After destroying the house, she leaves their bodies at Paul's grave, crushes her toy turtle and goes on to level the neighbourhood, while the closing images show destruction spreading across the planet.

The film premiered at the Overlook Film Festival on April 27, 2017, and was released by Universal on video on demand in April 2018. It received a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of reviews.

overview: Following the events of Captain America: Civil War, Peter Parker, with the help of his mentor Tony Stark, tries to balance his life as an ordinary high school student in Queens, New York City, with fighting crime as his superhero alter ego Spider-Man as a new threat, the Vulture, emerges.
tagline: Homework can wait. The city can't.
title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
plot:
Spider-Man: Homecoming is a 2017 superhero film directed by Jon Watts, produced by Kevin Feige, and based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. The movie follows the story of Peter Parker (played by Tom Holland), a high school student who has been living with his Aunt May (Marisa Tomei) in Queens, New York.

Peter is still trying to balance his life as a teenager with his responsibilities as Spider-Man, a superhero who has been fighting crime and protecting the city from various villains. However, he feels that he needs more guidance and mentorship from someone experienced in the field of superheroism.

Enter Tony Stark/Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.), who is impressed by Peter's skills and decides to take him under his wing as a protégé. Tony becomes Peter's mentor, teaching him how to be a better Spider-Man and helping him navigate the complexities of being a superhero.

However, a new villain emerges in the form of the Vulture (Michael Keaton), a former Air Force pilot who has become obsessed with technology and wealth. The Vulture is determined to steal valuable technology from various sources, including a high-tech company called Oscorp, which is owned by Norman Osborn (Michael Chernus).

As Peter tries to stop the Vulture, he also faces challenges from his peers at school, particularly his friend Ned Leeds (Jacob Batalon), who becomes increasingly jealous of Peter's newfound fame as Spider-Man. Meanwhile, Peter's relationship with his Aunt May is put to the test when she discovers that he has been using his powers to fight crime.

Throughout the movie, Peter learns valuable lessons about responsibility, humility, and the importance of teamwork. He also comes to terms with his own identity and the weight of being a superhero. The film features plenty of action-packed sequences, witty banter, and heartfelt moments, making it a delightful addition to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Overall, Spider-Man: Homecoming is a fun and engaging movie that explores themes of identity, responsibility, and friendship. With its talented cast, clever script, and impressive visuals, it's a must-see for fans of superhero movies and anyone looking for a light-hearted, entertaining film experience.

original_title: È stata la mano di Dio
overview: In 1980s Naples, Italy, an awkward Italian teen struggling to find his place experiences heartbreak and liberation after he's inadvertently saved from a freak accident by football legend Diego Maradona.
title: The Hand of God
plot:
The Hand of God is a 2021 Italian sports drama film directed by Paolo Sorrentino, not "by The Apartment". 

The Hand of God explores the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The story revolves around a young boy who becomes obsessed with playing football and finds solace in his imagination, which he uses to cope with the difficulties of his life.

Through the protagonist's journey, the film delves into themes of isolation, loneliness, and the struggle for human connection. It also touches on the idea of escapism, as the boy uses his imagination to temporarily escape the harsh realities of his environment.

The Hand of God is a poignant and introspective film that examines the fragility of childhood innocence and the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

overview: As Stitch, a runaway genetic experiment from a faraway planet, wreaks havoc on the Hawaiian Islands, he becomes the mischievous adopted alien "puppy" of an independent little girl named Lilo and learns about loyalty, friendship, and ʻohana, the Hawaiian tradition of family.
tagline: There's one in every family.
title: Lilo & Stitch
plot:
Lilo & Stitch is a 2002 American animated science fiction comedy-drama film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation. The movie tells the story of an unlikely friendship between a young girl named Lilo and an alien experiment known as Stitch.

The film begins with Lilo, a young Hawaiian girl who lives with her older sister Nani on the island of Kauai. Lilo is a bit of an outcast among her peers due to her eccentric behavior and love for all things weird and unusual. She adopts a dog named Pluto, but soon finds herself in trouble when she gets into a fight at school.

Nani tries to take care of Lilo on her own, but their financial situation becomes increasingly dire. They are forced to move into a low-income housing project, where they struggle to make ends meet. One day, while Nani is out running errands, Lilo adopts a dog from the local animal shelter - only to discover that it's actually an alien experiment known as Stitch.

Stitch is a genetic experiment created by the Galactic Federation, designed to destroy everything in its path. However, during his escape from the Federation's spaceship, Stitch crash-lands on Earth and is taken in by Lilo. Despite initial reservations, Nani agrees to let Stitch stay with them, hoping that it will help improve their financial situation.

As Lilo and Stitch spend more time together, they form an unlikely bond. Stitch, despite his destructive tendencies, begins to show a softer side as he forms a connection with Lilo. Meanwhile, Captain Gantu, a Galactic Federation officer tasked with capturing Stitch, becomes obsessed with finding the alien and bringing him back to the Federation.

As tensions rise between Nani and Gantu, Lilo and Stitch must work together to evade capture and protect each other from those who seek to harm them. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about family, acceptance, and the importance of having someone to care for you.

In the end, Lilo and Stitch's bond is put to the test when Gantu arrives at their doorstep with a plan to capture Stitch once and for all. In a heartwarming climax, Lilo stands up to Gantu and refuses to give up on her beloved alien friend. With the help of Captain Gantu's own feelings of loneliness and disconnection, Lilo is able to show him that family comes in many forms.

The film ends with Lilo and Stitch finally finding a sense of belonging and acceptance within their community. Nani and Lilo are reunited as a family unit, and Stitch finds a new purpose in life - using his unique abilities to help those in need. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, celebrating the power of love, acceptance, and the unbreakable bonds between humans and animals alike.

Overall, Lilo & Stitch is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of family, identity, and acceptance. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it has become a beloved classic among Disney fans around the world.

overview: In the slums of Rio, two kids' paths diverge as one struggles to become a photographer and the other a kingpin.
tagline: If you run, the beast catches you; if you stay, the beast eats you.
title: City of God
plot:
City of God is a 2002 Brazilian crime drama film directed by Fernando Meirelles and Kátia Lund. The film is set in the slums of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, during the 1990s.

The story begins with the introduction of Buscapé (played by Seu Jorge), an aspiring photographer who moves to the city from a rural area. He becomes fascinated with the world of crime and violence that surrounds him in the slums. Buscapé's life takes a dramatic turn when he witnesses a brutal murder committed by a group of young men, led by the ruthless and cunning Crôa (played by Douglas Silva).

Crôa is the leader of a powerful gang that controls much of the city's underworld. He is determined to expand his empire and eliminate any competition. Buscapé becomes entangled in Crôa's world and begins to work for him, but he soon realizes that he has made a terrible mistake.

As Buscapé becomes more deeply embroiled in the gang's activities, he witnesses numerous violent acts, including murders, robberies, and kidnappings. He also meets Lula (played by Leandro Firmino), Crôa's right-hand man, who becomes his friend and confidant.

However, Buscapé soon discovers that Crôa is planning to take over the entire city, and he must decide whether to continue working for him or try to escape. The film's plot thickens as Buscapé becomes increasingly disillusioned with Crôa's actions and begins to question his own morality.

The turning point in the story comes when Buscapé witnesses a brutal murder committed by Crôa's men, which leads to a violent confrontation between Buscapé and Lula. In the end, Buscapé manages to escape from the gang and starts a new life as a photographer.

The film ends with Buscapé reflecting on his experiences in the slums and the lessons he has learned about violence, loyalty, and redemption. The final shot of the film shows Buscapé taking a photograph of a cityscape, symbolizing his newfound perspective and hope for a better future.

Throughout the film, Meirelles and Lund use vivid imagery and gritty realism to portray the harsh realities of life in the slums. The film's cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty and ugliness of the city's underbelly. The performances by the cast are also noteworthy, particularly Seu Jorge's portrayal of Buscapé.

Overall, City of God is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores themes of violence, redemption, and the human condition. It is a searing indictment of the social and economic inequalities that exist in Brazil, and it offers a hopeful message about the possibility of transformation and renewal.

overview: A sinful martial arts expert wants to start a new tranquil life, only to be hunted by a determined detective and his former master.
production_companies: JSBC Eudemonia Blue Ocean TV & Movie Group
tagline: Blood Always Leaves a Trail.
title: Dragon
plot:
Dragon (Chinese title Wu Xia) is a 2011 Hong Kong-Chinese martial arts film from director Peter Chan, starring Donnie Yen, who also served as action director, alongside Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tang Wei, with Jimmy Wang Yu and Kara Hui in support. Conceived as a remake of Chang Cheh's 1967 classic The One-Armed Swordsman, it soon became an original story, though it retains echoes of that film, including the casting of Wang, its original star.

In 1917, Liu Jinxi lives quietly in a village in Yunnan with his wife, Yu, her son Fangzheng and their younger son Xiaotian. When two bandits try to rob a shop while Liu is inside, a scuffle breaks out and both robbers end up dead, apparently through Liu's clumsy luck. The villagers hail him as a hero, but Xu Baijiu, a Sichuanese-speaking detective sent to look into the case, is suspicious, since one of the dead men was a feared fighter. By performing an autopsy he discovers that the robber died of a brain haemorrhage caused by a precise blow to the vagus nerve, and further evidence convinces him that Liu is a master martial artist hiding his skill behind misdirection and a former member of the 72 Demons, a savage gang of killers.

Confronted, Liu admits his past but insists he has changed. Xu nevertheless obtains a warrant for his arrest, and the corrupt magistrate sells Liu's location to the Master of the 72 Demons in hope of a reward. The Master, revealing that Liu is his son, kills the magistrate and sends his men to bring Liu back. Liu kills them and sends the villagers to shelter in a fortress, and Xu uses his knowledge of anatomy to help him fake his death, but the deception fails. To prove he has broken with the gang, Liu cuts off his own left arm. The Master, holding Liu's family hostage, agrees to release him only if Xiaotian takes his place. Liu attacks, but the Master's qigong makes him impervious to blades. Xu slips in beneath the floorboards and drives acupuncture needles into the Master's heel and neck, weakening him; the Master mortally wounds the detective but is then struck dead by lightning, drawn by the needles. Xu declares the case closed with his last breath, and Liu returns to peaceful family life.

The film premiered in the Midnight Screenings section at Cannes in May 2011 and topped the Chinese box office with more than 100 million yuan in its first week. Critics were positive; Variety likened it to A History of Violence set in 1917 China. It won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Cinematography.

original_title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Furious Five
overview: Ordered to teach a martial arts class of rambunctious bunny kittens, Po tells stories of each of the Furious Five's pasts.
title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Furious Five
plot:
Secrets of the Furious Five, also known as Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Furious Five, is a 2008 American animated short film produced by DreamWorks Animation as a spin-off of the feature Kung Fu Panda. It was included on a companion disc of the film's deluxe DVD release, broadcast on NBC in February 2009 and released separately on DVD. Jack Black returns as Po and Dustin Hoffman as Master Shifu, with David Cross as Crane and Randall Duk Kim as Oogway. The framing story is computer-animated, while Po's tales are told in traditional two-dimensional animation, in the style of the feature's opening and closing sequences.

Shifu leaves Po in charge of teaching an introductory kung fu class to a group of unruly bunny children. Struggling to hold their attention, Po tries to show them that the true meaning of kung fu lies in excellence of self, illustrating his point with the stories of how each member of the Furious Five learned a key virtue.

Mantis, as a youth, was impatient and impulsive, and his rashness led to his capture by crocodile bandits; the long wait in their cage taught him patience, which he used to play dead and ambush his captors. Viper was born without venomous fangs, and her father, Great Master Viper, the protector of their village, believed she could never be a warrior; when a gorilla bandit with poison-proof armor broke her father's fangs during a festival, she found the courage to defeat him using her ribbon-dancing skills. Crane, a timid janitor at a kung fu academy, was encouraged by a fellow student, Mei Ling, to try out, and discovered confidence in himself and his slender frame. Tigress, an orphan whose strength frightened others, learned to control her power and use it gently. Monkey, once a prankster who mocked the villagers, was confronted by Oogway, who showed him compassion and taught him to share it with others. At the end of the lesson, Shifu returns expecting chaos and is surprised to find the children inspired, and Po, though bruised by the experience, assures them that he enjoyed his first day as a teacher.

The short was well received, earning eight nominations at the 36th Annie Awards in the category of animated television production or short form, and winning four, for character animation, character design, music and production design.

overview: After his classmate and crush is diagnosed with a pancreatic disease, an average high schooler sets out to make the most of her final days.
tagline: This is a story about an unforgettable spring...
title: I Want to Eat Your Pancreas
plot:
I Want to Eat Your Pancreas is a Japanese anime film directed by Takahiro Niino, based on the manga of the same name written and illustrated by Yōko Kamio. The story revolves around Sawa Makoto, a high school student who discovers that her classmate, Meiko "Jirachi" Rokkanji, has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer.

The film begins with Sawa's daily life as a high school student, where she is portrayed as an ordinary and somewhat introverted girl. However, when she meets Jirachi in the school's bathroom, her world is turned upside down. Jirachi reveals that she has pancreatic cancer and will not survive for much longer.

As Sawa spends more time with Jirachi, she begins to form a deep bond with her, and they develop an unlikely friendship. Despite their differences, they find comfort in each other's company, and Sawa becomes determined to make the most of their remaining time together.

Throughout the film, Sawa learns about Jirachi's life, including her struggles with cancer and her relationships with her family and friends. As their bond grows stronger, Sawa begins to confront her own emotions and fears, particularly regarding her own mortality.

As Jirachi's condition worsens, Sawa becomes more determined to make the most of their time together. She starts to explore her own desires and feelings, including a romantic interest in a classmate named Takumi. Meanwhile, Jirachi's family and friends struggle to come to terms with her diagnosis, leading to a deeper understanding of the complexities of human relationships.

The film takes a poignant turn when Sawa discovers that Jirachi has been keeping a secret from her - she is planning to die in a way that will allow her to transcend into a digital realm. This revelation sparks a series of emotional confrontations between Sawa and Jirachi, as they grapple with the meaning of life, death, and their own mortality.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a heart-wrenching climax as Sawa and Jirachi face the reality of their impending separation. In a poignant and powerful conclusion, Sawa makes a choice that will change her life forever, allowing her to find closure and move forward in the face of loss.

Throughout its narrative, I Want to Eat Your Pancreas explores themes of mortality, friendship, love, and the human condition. The film features beautiful animation, evocative music, and outstanding voice acting from the cast, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both authentic and emotionally resonant.

Overall, I Want to Eat Your Pancreas is a powerful and moving anime film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the fragility of life.

overview: Driver is a skilled Hollywood stuntman who moonlights as a getaway driver for criminals. Though he projects an icy exterior, lately he's been warming up to a pretty neighbor named Irene and her young son, Benicio. When Irene's husband gets out of jail, he enlists Driver's help in a million-dollar heist. The job goes horribly wrong, and Driver must risk his life to protect Irene and Benicio from the vengeful masterminds behind the robbery.
tagline: There are no clean getaways.
title: Drive
plot:
Drive is a 2011 neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, produced by Bold Films, and written by Hossein Amini.

The film takes place in Los Angeles, California, and follows the story of Driver (played by Ryan Gosling), a mysterious and introverted stunt driver who lives a solitary life. He is haunted by his past and struggles to form connections with others.

Driver's life changes when he meets Irene (played by Carey Mulligan), a single mother working as a waitress at a diner. She hires him to drive her and her son, Benicio (played by Kaden Leos), to a new home on the outskirts of town. Driver is drawn to Irene and begins to form a bond with her and her son.

However, their lives are disrupted when Irene's ex-boyfriend, Standard (played by Oscar Isaac), comes back into the picture. Standard is involved in a life of crime and has a history of violence. He becomes increasingly aggressive towards Irene and Benicio, putting them in danger.

As Driver tries to protect Irene and her son, he also becomes embroiled in Standard's world of crime. Driver agrees to drive Standard's partner, Bernie (played by Albert Brooks), on a series of heists, which puts him at odds with the law.

Throughout the film, Refn uses long takes and atmospheric soundscapes to create a sense of tension and unease. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the dark and gritty underbelly of Los Angeles.

As the story unfolds, Driver's past begins to surface. It is revealed that he was once involved in a violent incident with Standard, which left him with emotional scars. This backstory adds depth to Driver's character, making him more than just a stoic protagonist.

The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Driver and Standard, which ends in tragedy. In the end, Driver must confront his own demons and make a choice that will determine the fate of Irene and Benicio.

Drive is a critically acclaimed film known for its atmospheric tension, stunning cinematography, and Ryan Gosling's nuanced performance as Driver. The film has been praised for its exploration of themes such as loneliness, violence, and redemption.

overview: Elisabeth and John-John live in the same city, but they inhabit different worlds.
tagline: Two worlds. One love.
title: JJ+E
plot:
JJ+E (Swedish: Vinterviken, "Winter Cove") is a 2021 Swedish romantic drama film directed by Alexis Almström and written by Dunja Vujovic, based on the young adult novel Vinterviken by Mats Wahl. Produced by Filmlance International with SVT and released by Netflix, it stars Elsa Öhrn as Elisabeth and Mustapha Aarab as John-John, with Magnus Krepper as Elisabeth's father Frank, Marika Lagercrantz as Victoria, Simon Mezher as Jacob, the singer Loreen as John-John's mother Maria, Albin Grenholm as Patrik, Jonay Pineda Skallak as Sluggo and Elsa Bergström Terent as Patricia. The music was composed by Vittorio Grasso.

John-John, known as JJ, is the son of a single immigrant mother and grows up in a working-class housing estate in Stockholm, surrounded by a multicultural group of friends led by his downstairs neighbor Sluggo, whose gang drifts into burglary and petty crime; his mother's boyfriend, a security guard, warns that they will all end up behind bars. Elisabeth lives in a seaside villa with her wealthy father and younger sister Patricia and is withdrawn and sarcastic, still grieving the death of her mother. Their worlds collide when JJ, out on a joyride in a stolen boat with Sluggo, rescues Patricia from drowning. Both are then admitted to the same performing arts school, and a slow, hesitant courtship develops as they rehearse for a school performance, explore the city and meet each other's friends, while hiding the relationship from her disapproving father. Sluggo's crimes, which include breaking into Elisabeth's home, increasingly entangle JJ, and when he is backed into a corner with no way out, the gulf between their lives threatens to tear the couple apart in a dark final act.

JJ+E premiered on Netflix on 8 September 2021. Critical reception was mixed. Decider's Jade Budowski praised its grounded portrait of Stockholm, the chemistry of the leads and the star quality of Elsa Öhrn, but felt the film wavered between romance and crime story before taking an absurd turn in its last minutes. Roger Moore of Movie Nation found the courtship scenes the strongest and valued its depiction of Sweden's multicultural underclass, yet called the surrounding melodrama a collection of clichés and the whole a formulaic, tepid teen romance.

overview: A headstrong Chinese-American woman returns to China when her beloved grandmother is given a terminal diagnosis. Billi struggles with her family's decision to keep grandma in the dark about her own illness as they all stage an impromptu wedding to see grandma one last time.
tagline: Based on an actual lie.
title: The Farewell
plot:
The Farewell is a poignant and nuanced exploration of cultural identity, family dynamics, and the complexities of navigating one's heritage.

At its core, the film delves into the theme of cultural identity and the tensions that arise when an individual struggles to reconcile their birth culture with their adopted culture. The protagonist, Billi, finds herself caught between her Chinese-American upbringing and her desire to connect with her roots in China, where her grandmother is terminally ill.

The movie masterfully weaves together themes of family, love, and loyalty, as Billi navigates the intricate web of relationships within her family. Her decision to keep her grandmother's illness a secret from her mother, who has always been critical of their cultural heritage, sets off a chain reaction of emotions that exposes deep-seated wounds and unspoken resentments.

One of the most striking aspects of The Farewell is its exploration of the immigrant experience and the sacrifices that come with it. Billi's journey is a powerful metaphor for the struggles faced by many immigrants who must navigate multiple cultures, languages, and identities in order to find their place in the world.

Throughout the film, director Lulu Wang skillfully employs humor, wit, and poignancy to convey the complexities of family relationships and cultural identity. The Farewell is ultimately a heartwarming and thought-provoking exploration of what it means to belong, to be loved, and to find one's place in the world.

The film's title, "The Farewell," takes on a deeper meaning as the story unfolds, becoming a powerful symbol of the bittersweet nature of cultural identity and the complexities of family relationships.

overview: Caleb Holt, a heroic fire captain who values dedication and service to others above all else. But the most important partnership in his life, his marriage, is about to go up in smoke. This gripping story follows one man's desire to transform his life and marriage through the healing power of faith and fully embrace the fireman's code: "Never leave your partner behind."
tagline: Never leave your partner behind.
title: Fireproof
plot:
Fireproof is a 2008 American Christian drama film directed by Alex Kendrick and written by Alex and Stephen Kendrick. The movie stars Kirk Cameron as Captain David Thompson, a firefighter who must confront his own faith and relationship with his wife, played by Erin Cottrell.

The story begins with Captain David Thompson, a respected firefighter in the community, who is struggling to balance his career and family life. He is married to his high school sweetheart, Katherine (Erin Cottrell), and they have two young children together. However, their relationship has become stale, and they are no longer intimate.

One day, Captain David's friend, played by Ted McGinley, challenges him to read the Bible and apply its teachings to his life. The challenge is a test of faith, and Captain David accepts it. As he begins to study the Bible, he starts to see his marriage and relationships in a new light.

Meanwhile, Katherine has been feeling unappreciated and unheard in their relationship. She feels like she's carrying the load of parenting and household responsibilities while Captain David is always busy with work. The tension between them builds, and they start to drift apart.

As Captain David delves deeper into his faith, he begins to see the importance of communication, forgiveness, and intimacy in marriage. He starts to make changes in his behavior, such as being more present and attentive to Katherine, and apologizing for his mistakes.

However, Katherine is resistant to change, and she feels like Captain David is trying to "fix" their problems without really listening to her concerns. The situation escalates, and they have a series of confrontations that leave them both feeling hurt and angry.

In the climax of the movie, Captain David has an epiphany and realizes that he needs to make a choice between his faith and his marriage. He decides to take a stand and fight for their relationship, using the principles of the Bible to guide him.

The ending is redemptive, as Captain David and Katherine work through their issues and come out stronger on the other side. They learn to communicate effectively, forgive each other, and rekindle their romance. The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as they look forward to rebuilding their relationship and growing together.

Throughout the movie, Alex Kendrick brings his signature Christian values to the story, emphasizing the importance of faith, forgiveness, and redemption. While some critics have accused the movie of being overly simplistic or heavy-handed, many viewers have found it to be a powerful and inspiring exploration of marriage and relationships.

Overall, Fireproof is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that challenges viewers to think about their own relationships and priorities. With its strong performances, engaging storyline, and uplifting message, it's no wonder why this movie has become a beloved favorite among Christian audiences.

original_title: デスノート, Light up the NEW world
overview: 10 years has passed since the confrontation between Kira and L. Again, Shinigami sends death notes to the ground and due to this, the world soon falls into chaos. Tsukuru is a member of the Death Note special task force team with 6 other investigators including Matsuda who experienced the Kira case of 10 years ago.  Mass murders caused by the death note takes place on Wall Street in the U.S., Shibuya in Japan and other places. World famous private investigator Ryuzaki, who is the rightful successor of L, also investigates the mass murders. They discover that 6 death notes exists in the world.  A computer virus called Kira spreads in the world. A message in the Kira virus says to turn in 6 death notes.  A person who has 6 death notes overwhelm the world. The confrontation begins between the person who wants Kira’s revival and the people who want to stop it.
title: Death Note: Light Up the New World
plot:
Death Note: Light Up the New World is a 2016 Japanese supernatural thriller directed by Shinsuke Sato, based on the manga Death Note by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata. A sequel to the 2006 film Death Note 2: The Last Name, it features an original story set after the miniseries Death Note: New Generation. It stars Masahiro Higashide as Detective Tsukuru Mishima, Sosuke Ikematsu as Ryuzaki, the successor of L, Masaki Suda as the cyber-terrorist Yuki Shien and Erika Toda as Misa Amane, with Rina Kawaei and Mina Fujii, and Shidō Nakamura voicing the Shinigami Ryuk.

Ten years after the deaths of Light Yagami, known as Kira, and his nemesis L, a world troubled by cyber-terrorism is struck by a wave of unexplained deaths suggesting that Death Notes, notebooks that kill anyone whose name is written in them, are being used again. Interpol assigns Ryuzaki, L's biological successor, to a new Death Note Task Force led by Mishima. After a killing spree in Shibuya, the team learns from a Shinigami that six Death Notes are now in the human world, the maximum allowed at once.

The race to gather all six notebooks begins. Yuki Shien, a brilliant hacker who worships Kira and believes he is carrying out Light's will, hunts down the notebooks and their owners. He restores the memories of Misa Amane, Light's former girlfriend, and asks for her help in finding where Light might be hiding. Shien then spreads a computer virus featuring Light's image and threatens a massacre unless L's successor reveals himself. As Ryuzaki and Mishima try to outmaneuver him, the Task Force is disbanded, Mishima falls under suspicion, and the mystery surrounding Light's secret successor deepens, building to a showdown in which no one can be fully trusted.

The film continues the franchise's cat-and-mouse battle of wits and its moral questions about justice and the power over life and death.

Released in Japan by Warner Bros. on October 29, 2016, Light Up the New World opened at the top of the Japanese box office, displacing Your Name, and became one of the year's highest-grossing Japanese films.

overview: Emily, who is saddled with student debt and locked out of the job market due to a minor criminal record, gets involved in a credit card scam that pulls her into the criminal underworld of Los Angeles, ultimately leading to deadly consequences.
title: Emily the Criminal
plot:
Emily the Criminal is a 2022 American crime drama film written and directed by John Patton Ford. The movie follows the story of Emily, a young woman who feels trapped in her mundane life and struggles to make ends meet.

The film centers around Emily (played by Aubrey Plaza), a college student who works multiple part-time jobs to support herself and her family. She is desperate for financial stability and a sense of purpose, but her circumstances seem hopeless. One day, Emily meets a charismatic and confident woman named Sarah (played by Molly Gordon) who introduces her to the world of online shopping scams.

As Emily becomes more involved in Sarah's scheme, she begins to see an opportunity to escape her difficult life and create a better future for herself. However, as she delves deeper into the world of crime, Emily starts to realize that it comes with its own set of risks and consequences.

Throughout the film, Ford explores themes of class struggle, financial insecurity, and the desperation that can drive people to make questionable choices. The movie also touches on issues of female empowerment and the ways in which women are often forced to navigate patriarchal systems to survive.

The cast delivers strong performances, with Plaza bringing a sense of vulnerability and determination to her portrayal of Emily. Gordon is equally impressive as Sarah, capturing the character's confidence and charisma while also conveying a sense of complexity and depth.

Overall, Emily the Criminal is a thought-provoking and engaging film that sheds light on the struggles faced by many young people today. With its strong performances, nuanced direction, and timely themes, it is a must-see for fans of crime dramas and anyone interested in exploring the complexities of modern life.

overview: After assuming his dead cellmate's identity to get with his girlfriend, an ex-con finds himself the reluctant participant in a casino heist.
tagline: The trap is set. The game is on.
title: Reindeer Games
plot:
Reindeer Games is a 2000 American action thriller film directed by John Frankenheimer and starring Nicolas Cage, Christina Ricci, and Gary Sinise.

The main themes of Reindeer Games revolve around survival, redemption, and the human condition. The movie follows Rusty Ryan (Nicolas Cage), a wrongly convicted man who escapes from prison and must use his wits and resourcefulness to survive in a series of deadly games set up by his captors.

Throughout the film, Rusty's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his past mistakes and grapples with the consequences of his actions. The movie explores themes of guilt, shame, and redemption, as Rusty tries to make amends for his past wrongdoings.

The film also touches on the idea of survival in a hostile environment, as Rusty must use his skills and ingenuity to stay alive in the face of overwhelming odds. This theme is particularly evident in the game's final act, where Rusty faces off against his captors in a desperate bid for freedom.

Furthermore, Reindeer Games can be seen as a commentary on the American justice system and the harsh treatment of prisoners. The film highlights the flaws in the system and the ways in which innocent people can be wrongly convicted and subjected to cruel punishment.

Overall, Reindeer Games is a tense, suspenseful thriller that explores complex themes and features a standout performance from Nicolas Cage.

overview: The story of Kurt, a young art student who falls in love with fellow student, Ellie. Ellie’s father, Professor Seeband, a famous doctor, is dismayed at his daughter’s choice of boyfriend, and vows to destroy the relationship. What neither of them knows is that their lives are already connected through a terrible crime Seeband committed decades ago.
title: Never Look Away
plot:
Never Look Away is a 2018 German drama film directed by Sebastian Schipper and written by Malte Grunert. The movie revolves around the life of a young photographer, Johnny Spillane, who becomes entangled in the world of East German art and politics during the Cold War era.

The main theme of Never Look Away is the struggle for artistic freedom and the human cost of oppression. The film explores how the regime's strict control over art and culture stifled creativity and individuality, leading to a sense of desperation and rebellion among artists. Johnny Spillane's journey serves as a metaphor for the search for authenticity and truth in a world where propaganda and censorship reign supreme.

The movie also delves into the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and society. As Johnny becomes more deeply embroiled in the art world, he is forced to confront his own dark past and the traumas inflicted upon him by the regime. The film's portrayal of the psychological toll of living under totalitarian rule serves as a powerful commentary on the human cost of oppression.

Furthermore, Never Look Away touches on the theme of identity and the search for one's place in the world. Johnny's journey is also a quest to find his own voice and purpose, amidst the chaos and uncertainty of the Cold War era. The film raises questions about the role of art in shaping our understanding of ourselves and the world around us.

Overall, Never Look Away is a powerful exploration of the human spirit, artistic expression, and the struggle for freedom in the face of oppression.

overview: An archaeological team attempt to unlock the secrets of a lost pyramid only to find themselves hunted by an insidious creature.
tagline: You Only Enter Once.
title: The Pyramid
plot:
The Pyramid is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Stiles White and written by Stiles White and David White. The movie follows a group of friends who travel to Egypt in search of adventure, only to find themselves trapped in an ancient pyramid with a malevolent spirit.

The main themes of The Pyramid include:

1. **Hubris and the dangers of meddling with the unknown**: The film's protagonist, Nick (Lorenzo Lamas), is a treasure hunter who becomes obsessed with finding the lost city of Zerzura. His arrogance and disregard for the supernatural forces at work in the pyramid ultimately lead to his downfall.
2. **Friendship and loyalty**: As the group navigates the treacherous pyramid, they are forced to rely on each other for survival. The bonds of friendship and loyalty between the characters are tested as they face increasingly terrifying challenges.
3. **The power of ancient cultures and civilizations**: The Pyramid explores the mythology and symbolism of ancient Egyptian culture, highlighting the reverence and fear with which these civilizations viewed their deities and supernatural forces.
4. **Descent into madness and the blurring of reality**: As the group delves deeper into the pyramid, they begin to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that challenge their perceptions of reality. The film's climax features a descent into madness, as the characters are forced to confront the true nature of the malevolent spirit.

Overall, The Pyramid is a tense, supernatural thriller that explores themes of hubris, friendship, and the power of ancient cultures. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has developed a cult following among horror fans.

overview: Trying to escape her broken past, Sarah O’Neill is building a new life on the fringes of a backwood rural town with her young son Chris. A terrifying encounter with a mysterious neighbour shatters her fragile security, throwing Sarah into a spiralling nightmare of paranoia and mistrust, as she tries to uncover if the disturbing changes in her little boy are connected to an ominous sinkhole buried deep in the forest that borders their home.
tagline: Fear the familiar.
title: The Hole in the Ground
plot:
The Hole in the Ground is a psychological horror film that delves into the complexities of motherhood, grief, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows a young mother, Sarah, who becomes increasingly unhinged as she tries to protect her son from an unknown threat.

At its core, The Hole in the Ground explores the intense emotional turmoil that can arise when a parent's perception of their child is challenged. As Sarah's grip on reality begins to slip, the film raises questions about the fragility of motherly love and the devastating consequences of trauma.

The movie also touches on the theme of grief and loss, as Sarah struggles to come to terms with her own past traumas and the pain of losing a loved one. Her fixation on protecting her son becomes an all-consuming force that drives her actions, leading to a downward spiral of paranoia and desperation.

Throughout the film, the director skillfully crafts a sense of unease and tension, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just Sarah's fevered imagination. The result is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling exploration of the darker aspects of human psychology.

original_title: Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of Eternals
overview: Join director Chloe Zhao and the Cast of Eternals as they recount their experiences during the making of Marvel Studios’ most ambitious film to date. Discover how the ensemble cast felt stepping into their roles, filming in remote locations, and creating bonds that would help to create the on-screen relationships that span over 7,000 years.
tagline: From comic to screen, discover the making of Marvel's first heroes.
title: Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of Eternals
plot:
Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of Eternals is a documentary series that delves into the creation and production of the 2021 film Eternals. At its core, the series explores the themes of identity, community, and the struggle for belonging.

The film's narrative revolves around the Eternals, a group of immortal beings with extraordinary abilities, who have been living among humans for centuries. However, they are forced to confront their past and their true nature when they are discovered by humans. This revelation sparks an existential crisis, as the Eternals grapple with the consequences of their immortality and their place in the world.

Throughout the series, it becomes clear that the Eternals' struggle for belonging is deeply intertwined with their search for identity. They have been living among humans for so long that they have begun to lose touch with their own culture and heritage. The film highlights the tension between their desire to fit in and their need to hold on to their unique identity.

The series also explores the theme of community and the importance of found family. The Eternals, despite their differences, come together as a group to support one another and fight for their rights. This sense of camaraderie is a powerful force that drives the narrative forward and serves as a testament to the enduring power of human connection.

Ultimately, Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of Eternals presents a nuanced exploration of what it means to be human, even in the face of extraordinary circumstances. Through the lens of the Eternals' story, the series sheds light on the complexities of identity, community, and belonging, leaving viewers with a deeper understanding of these universal themes.

original_title: Power Rangers Samurai: Clash of the Red Rangers - The Movie
overview: The Samurai Rangers team up with the mysterious RPM Ranger Red to fight off Master Xandred's Mooger army and a robotic supervillain from the RPM Ranger's dimension. But when both Red Rangers get struck with hypnobolts, they turn against one another.
title: Power Rangers Samurai: Clash of the Red Rangers - The Movie
plot:
Power Rangers Samurai: Clash of the Red Rangers - The Movie is an action-packed adventure that delves into the world of friendship, teamwork, and self-discovery. At its core, the movie explores the theme of identity and how it shapes one's sense of purpose.

The main character, Jason, struggles to find his place in the world as he navigates his new role as a Power Ranger. He grapples with feelings of inadequacy and uncertainty, questioning whether he truly has what it takes to be a hero. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for growth, as Jason learns to come to terms with his strengths and weaknesses.

Throughout the movie, the Power Rangers face off against their arch-nemesis, Lord Zedd, who represents the ultimate force of evil. The battle between good and evil serves as a backdrop for Jason's personal journey, highlighting the importance of perseverance, loyalty, and trust in the face of adversity.

The film also touches on the theme of mentorship, as Jason learns valuable lessons from his fellow Power Rangers and their wise leader, Zordon. This guidance helps Jason develop his skills and confidence, ultimately leading him to become a true hero.

Ultimately, Power Rangers Samurai: Clash of the Red Rangers - The Movie is a heartwarming tale about self-discovery, friendship, and the power of believing in oneself.

overview: When three skiers find themselves stranded on a chair lift at a New England ski resort that has closed for the next week, they are forced to make life or death choices that prove to be more perilous than staying put and freezing to death.
tagline: No one knows you're up there.
title: Frozen
plot:
Frozen is a 2010 American psychological horror survival film written and directed by Adam Green, starring Shawn Ashmore and Kevin Zegers and introducing Emma Bell. It follows three friends stranded on a chairlift after a day of skiing, forced to make life-or-death choices. It was filmed at Snowbasin near Ogden, Utah, in February 2009.

Dan Walker, his girlfriend Parker O'Neal and his best friend Joe Lynch spend a day at a ski resort. On the last evening, with the resort about to close for the week because of incoming bad weather, they persuade the lift operator to let them take one final run. A replacement operator takes over and, mistaking three other skiers for them, shuts down the lift, leaving the friends stranded high above the ground. As a snowstorm sets in, a snow groomer passes below without its driver noticing them.

Realizing that no one knows where they are and that they will not survive until the resort reopens, Dan jumps from the chair, breaking both legs. Unable to reach him, Parker and Joe can only listen as a pack of wolves tears him apart. Grieving, the two blame each other before finding comfort, and Parker admits that she had hoped to marry Dan. The next morning, Joe shimmies along the razor-sharp cable to a support tower, badly cutting his hands and loosening the bolt that secures their chair. Climbing down, he fends off the wolves with a ski pole and sets off down the mountain on Parker's snowboard, promising to bring help, with the pack in pursuit. Parker spends another night alone on the lift. When Joe does not return, she tries to reach the tower herself, but the chair's bolt gives way and it drops to a few meters above the ground. She jumps, and the falling chair crushes her ankle. Sliding and crawling down the slope, she passes the wolves feeding on Joe's body, but they ignore her. Reaching a road, she is picked up by a passing driver who takes her to hospital, and she closes her eyes remembering Dan's words.

Frozen premiered at the 2010 Sundance Film Festival, where audience members reportedly fainted, and was released by Anchor Bay Films in North American theaters on February 5, 2010, grossing slightly less than $2.7 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 64% approval and Metacritic a score of 43. Bell later reprised her role in an epilogue scene in Hatchet II.

overview: Rei helps the woman she's been in love with for years escape her abusive husband. While on the run, their feelings for each other catch fire.
title: Ride or Die
plot:
Ride or Die (Japanese: 彼女, Kanojo, meaning both "she" and "girlfriend") is a 2021 Japanese romantic thriller directed by Ryūichi Hiroki and written by Nami Kikkawa for Netflix, adapted from Ching Nakamura's adult manga Gunjō. The screenplay departs freely from its source, recasting the story as a road movie and giving names to the two heroines, who are anonymous in the manga. Kiko Mizuhara stars as Rei Nagasawa and Honami Sato as Nanae Shinoda, with Yōko Maki as Rei's lover Mika, Shunsuke Tanaka and Anne Suzuki as Rei's brother Masato and his wife Yu, and Shinya Niiro as Nanae's husband Kotaro; Sara Minami and Yui Uemura play the women as schoolgirls.

The film opens with Rei, glamorous and assured, picking up a man in an elegant bar and going home with him to his high-rise apartment, where they have sex beneath his wedding photograph; she then kills him. The man, it emerges, is Nanae's husband. Rei is an independently wealthy plastic surgeon and a lesbian living semi-openly with Mika when, out of the blue, she receives a call from Nanae, a classmate from their elite girls' school whom she has not seen in ten years and has loved since adolescence. Seeing the bruises left by Kotaro's abuse, Rei needs only a slight push from Nanae to resolve to kill him, abandoning her partner and career.

Nanae is nonetheless shocked that Rei took her literally, and insists that she is straight, yet she does not abandon her friend, and the two flee together in a red BMW convertible. On the road their first euphoria gives way to strain as they realise they cannot escape, and they talk more and more seriously of dying together. Encounters with controlling men, including a presumptuous taxi driver and Rei's well-meaning but overbearing brother, punctuate the journey, while flashbacks trace their history back to the art class where they first met. Hiding at Masato's home, they plan to surrender but run away once more for a final night by the sea, where they confront their conflicting feelings and finally make love. The next morning Rei calls the police from a payphone, so that she can claim sole responsibility for the killing and shield Nanae.

The film was shot in sequence during the COVID-19 pandemic and released worldwide on Netflix on 15 April 2021. Variety praised its sensual, female-driven storytelling as far ahead of typical Japanese LGBTQ films and Mizuhara's committed performance, while finding its 142 minutes drawn out; reviews were generally favorable.

overview: In 13th century Ireland a group of monks must escort a sacred relic across a landscape fraught with peril.
production_companies: Centre du Cinéma et de l'Audiovisuel de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
tagline: A journey paved in blood.
title: Pilgrimage
plot:
Pilgrimage is a 2017 Irish drama film directed by Vincent Ward, not Screen Ireland. 

The movie follows the story of James Lafferty, an American writer who travels to Ireland in search of inspiration for his novel. He becomes fascinated with the legend of St. Patrick and decides to embark on a pilgrimage along the route that St. Patrick took when he converted the Irish people to Christianity.

As James navigates the rugged landscape of Ireland, he encounters various characters who challenge his perceptions and force him to confront his own demons. The film explores themes of spirituality, identity, and the search for meaning in life.

One of the main themes of Pilgrimage is the struggle between faith and doubt. James's journey is marked by moments of profound spiritual insight, but also by periods of darkness and uncertainty. Through his experiences, he grapples with questions about the nature of God and the role of spirituality in everyday life.

Another significant theme is the power of storytelling and the impact it has on our lives. As a writer, James is drawn to the stories of St. Patrick and the Irish people, but he also begins to realize that his own experiences are intertwined with those of others. The film suggests that our individual stories are part of a larger narrative that connects us all.

The movie also explores the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships. James's journey is not just about finding inspiration for his writing, but also about discovering who he is as a person. Through his encounters with various characters, he begins to see himself in a new light and to understand the complexities of human nature.

Overall, Pilgrimage is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of spirituality, identity, and the power of storytelling.

overview: A group of friends head to the land of oaky Chardonnays and big, bold Cabernet Sauvignons for one member of the squad’s 50th birthday party.
tagline: Friendship is a trip
title: Wine Country
plot:
Wine Country is a 2019 American comedy film that follows a group of friends who embark on a wine-tasting tour in Napa Valley. The movie explores the complexities of female friendships, particularly among women in their 50s and 60s.

At its core, Wine Country delves into themes of female empowerment, self-discovery, and the importance of nurturing relationships with others. As the characters navigate their personal struggles, they find solace in each other's company, sharing laughter, tears, and life experiences over glasses of wine.

The film also touches on the idea of midlife crises and the search for identity, as the characters confront their own mortality and the changing landscape of their lives. Through their adventures in Napa Valley, they discover new aspects of themselves and rekindle old friendships, ultimately finding a sense of purpose and belonging.

Furthermore, Wine Country pokes fun at societal expectations and stereotypes surrounding women's roles, particularly those related to aging and motherhood. The movie playfully subverts these norms, showcasing strong, independent women who refuse to be defined by their age or circumstances.

Overall, Wine Country is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of female friendship, self-discovery, and the power of community in navigating life's challenges.

overview: Two FBI agent brothers, Marcus and Kevin Copeland, accidentally foil a drug bust. To avoid being fired they accept a mission escorting a pair of socialites to the Hamptons--but when the girls are disfigured in a car accident, they refuse to go. Left without options, Marcus and Kevin decide to pose as the sisters, transforming themselves from black men into rich white women.
tagline: They're going deep undercover.
title: White Chicks
plot:
White Chicks is a 2004 American comedy film directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans and written by Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans. The movie stars Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans as two FBI agents who go undercover as white women to solve a kidnapping case.

The story begins with Kevin Copeland (Shawn Wayans) and Marcus Copeland (Marlon Wayans), two African American brothers who work for the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). The brothers are assigned to investigate the kidnapping of two wealthy heiresses, Brittany and Tiffany Wilson (played by Jennifer Carpenter and Brittany Daniel respectively).

The FBI's top brass decide that the best way to get close to the kidnappers is for Kevin and Marcus to go undercover as white women. They undergo a radical transformation, complete with wigs, breast implants, and fake accents.

As they navigate their new lives as "Christine" and "Nikki," the brothers struggle to maintain their cover. However, they soon discover that being white isn't all it's cracked up to be. They face racism from some of the people they meet, including a group of white supremacists who are also after the Wilson sisters.

As Kevin and Marcus delve deeper into the case, they uncover a complex web of deceit and corruption involving the kidnappers, the FBI, and even their own agency. Along the way, they encounter a range of colorful characters, including a bumbling FBI agent (played by Snoop Dogg) and a seductive nightclub singer (played by Faizon Love).

Throughout the movie, Kevin and Marcus's fish-out-of-water experiences provide plenty of comedic moments. However, as the story unfolds, the brothers also discover that being white isn't just about looks - it's also about attitude and behavior.

In the end, Kevin and Marcus are able to solve the kidnapping case and bring the perpetrators to justice. Along the way, they learn a valuable lesson about identity, community, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

Overall, White Chicks is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that explores themes of identity, racism, and brotherhood. With its talented cast, witty script, and outrageous humor, it's no wonder that this movie has become a cult classic.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 銀翼の奇術師
overview: Once again, Kaitou Kid crosses swords with Conan Edogawa in this annual installment of the Detective Conan movie franchise. After receiving a letter from the thief, famous actress Juri Maki seeks the help of private detective Kogorou Mouri to protect the Star Sapphire—the "Jewel of Destiny," said to represent faith, fate, and hope.
title: Detective Conan: Magician of the Silver Sky
plot:
Detective Conan: Magician of the Silver Sky is a mystery film that delves into the world of magic and illusion, while maintaining the core elements of the popular Detective Conan series. The movie's main themes revolve around deception, perception, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The story revolves around a mysterious magician who uses his skills to manipulate people's perceptions, creating an atmosphere of confusion and uncertainty. As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the characters are forced to confront their own biases and assumptions.

One of the primary themes of the movie is the power of deception and how easily it can be used to manipulate others. The magician's abilities allow him to create elaborate illusions, making it difficult for the characters (and the audience) to distinguish reality from fantasy. This theme is closely tied to the idea of perception and how our individual perspectives shape our understanding of the world.

The movie also explores the concept of identity and how easily it can be manipulated. The magician's ability to change his appearance and persona raises questions about the nature of self and whether one's true identity can ever be truly known.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of obsession and the dangers of becoming too invested in a particular idea or fantasy. The characters' fixation on uncovering the truth behind the magician's identity leads them down a rabbit hole of confusion and paranoia, highlighting the risks of allowing our desires to cloud our judgment.

Overall, Detective Conan: Magician of the Silver Sky is a thought-provoking mystery that challenges its audience to question their perceptions and assumptions. By exploring the complexities of deception, perception, and identity, the movie creates a thrilling and unpredictable ride that keeps viewers engaged until the very end.

overview: A retired pop singer turned actress' sense of reality is shaken when she is stalked by an obsessed fan and seemingly a ghost of her past.
tagline: The color of illusion is Perfect Blue.
title: Perfect Blue
plot:
Perfect Blue is a psychological thriller anime film written and directed by Satoshi Kon, released in 2002 (not 1997) but it was originally produced as an OVA (original video animation) series in 1997. The story follows the life of Mima Kirigoe, a former member of the popular idol group CHAM! or CHAM!, who decides to leave the entertainment industry and pursue a career in acting.

The film begins with Mima's departure from CHAM!, where she is struggling to cope with the pressures of fame. She then starts taking acting classes and lands a role in a television drama, "On Air". As Mima becomes more immersed in her new role, she begins to experience strange and unsettling events that blur the lines between reality and fantasy.

Mima's mental state deteriorates as she becomes increasingly paranoid and detached from reality. Her relationships with those around her begin to fray, including her friends and colleagues. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between Mima's past and present, making it difficult for the viewer to discern what is real and what is not.

As the story progresses, Mima's grip on reality begins to slip further. She becomes convinced that her alter ego, a character she plays in "On Air", has taken over her life. The film's climax features a surreal and disturbing sequence where Mima's identity is torn apart, leaving the viewer questioning what is left of her.

Throughout the film, Kon explores themes of identity, celebrity culture, and the blurring of reality and fantasy. Perfect Blue is a thought-provoking and unsettling work that challenges the viewer to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

It's worth noting that while the film was released in 2002, it was originally produced as an OVA series in 1997 by Madhouse. The story has undergone some changes since its initial release, but the core themes and narrative remain intact.

overview: The tale of an ordinary garden snail who dreams of winning the Indy 500.
tagline: SLO NO MO
title: Turbo
plot:
Turbo is a 2013 computer-animated comedy-adventure film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Theo, a garden snail who dreams of becoming a racing champion.

The film begins with Theo, a humble and unassuming garden snail, living in a small pond with his family. Despite his slow pace, Theo has a big dream: to become the fastest snail in the world. However, his family and friends think he's crazy, as snails are not built for speed.

One day, while swimming in the pond, Theo is exposed to a strange substance that gives him superhuman speed. He becomes the fastest snail in the world, but also develops a turbo-powered engine that allows him to move at incredible velocities.

Excited by his newfound abilities, Theo sets out on an adventure to become a racing champion. He meets a group of street-smart racers who teach him how to navigate the high-speed world of racing. There's Guy Gagne, a cocky and arrogant car driver; Tito, a wise-cracking and fast-talking street rat; and Burn, a tough and intimidating motorcycle rider.

As Theo navigates this new world, he faces numerous challenges and obstacles. He must learn to control his turbo-powered engine, avoid danger, and outsmart his rivals. Along the way, he befriends a young girl named Tito's sister, Tola, who becomes his love interest.

However, not everyone is happy about Theo's newfound success. Guy Gagne, in particular, sees Theo as a threat to his own racing career and tries to sabotage him at every turn. The two engage in an epic rivalry that takes them on a wild ride through the streets of New York City.

As the big racing championship approaches, Theo must confront his own doubts and fears. Can he overcome his slow start and become the champion? Will he be able to balance his love for racing with his newfound fame?

The film's climax features an action-packed racing sequence that takes Theo and his friends on a thrilling ride through the streets of New York City. In the end, Theo emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and believing in himself.

Turbo is a heartwarming and hilarious animated film that celebrates the power of dreams and determination. With its colorful characters, witty humor, and high-speed action sequences, it's a movie that will leave audiences cheering for more.

overview: In the wake of their friends' marriages and eventual offspring, longtime pals Julie and Jason decide to have a child together without becoming a couple. By becoming "time-share" parents, they reason, they can experience the joys of parenthood without significantly curbing their personal freedom. However, when Julie and Jason both become involved with others, they discover that they secretly harbor romantic feelings for each other.
tagline: Love. Happiness. Kids. Pick two.
title: Friends with Kids
plot:
Friends with Kids is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of relationships and growing up. The movie delves into the theme of unrequited love, as its protagonist, Cole, finds himself stuck in a rut with his long-term girlfriend, Mary, while he secretly develops feelings for her best friend, Kristin.

As the story unfolds, the film examines the challenges of navigating adulthood, including the pressure to settle down and start a family. The characters' struggles with commitment and identity serve as a backdrop for their relationships, highlighting the tension between desire and responsibility.

The movie also touches on the theme of nostalgia, as Cole and Kristin's friendship is rooted in their shared experiences from college days. This nostalgia serves as a reminder of the past and the what-ifs that often accompany unrequited love.

Ultimately, Friends with Kids presents a nuanced portrayal of relationships, love, and growing up, inviting viewers to reflect on their own experiences and desires.

overview: A couple off for a romantic weekend in the mountains are accosted by a biker gang. Alone in the mountains, Brea and John must defend themselves against the gang, who will stop at nothing to protect their secrets.
tagline: Refuse to Be a Victim
title: Traffik
plot:
Traffik is a 2018 American crime thriller film directed by Deon Taylor. The movie follows the story of Brea Kelly (played by Paula Patton), a mother whose life is turned upside down when her son is kidnapped and she discovers that he was involved in human trafficking.

The main themes of Traffik include:

1. **Human Trafficking**: The film sheds light on the dark reality of human trafficking, highlighting its devastating effects on victims and their families.
2. **Motherly Love and Sacrifice**: Brea's journey is driven by her unwavering love for her son, which motivates her to risk everything to rescue him and bring the perpetrators to justice.
3. **Corruption and Injustice**: The movie exposes the corruption and complicity of law enforcement officials and other authorities in enabling human trafficking, highlighting the need for accountability and reform.
4. **Trauma and Recovery**: Brea's experiences leave her with physical and emotional scars, forcing her to confront her own trauma and find a way to heal and move forward.
5. **Redemption and Justice**: Throughout the film, Brea seeks redemption by taking down those responsible for her son's kidnapping and exploitation, ultimately finding a sense of justice and closure.

Overall, Traffik is a powerful and thought-provoking film that tackles tough subjects with sensitivity and nuance, offering a hopeful message about the resilience of the human spirit.

overview: Four months after the death of her husband, a woman on the brink of motherhood is tormented in her home by a strange woman who wants her unborn baby.
tagline: Terror comes calling.
title: Inside
plot:
Inside (French: À l'intérieur) is a 2007 French horror film directed by Julien Maury and Alexandre Bustillo in their feature debut, from a screenplay by Bustillo. It stars Alysson Paradis as Sarah Scarangella, a pregnant widow, and Béatrice Dalle as a mysterious woman who invades her home. Often cited as a key work of the New French Extremity movement, it is known for its relentless, graphic violence.

On Christmas Eve, four months after surviving a car crash that killed her husband, Sarah is due to give birth the following day. Grieving and depressed, she turns down her mother's offer to stay the night and arranges for her boss, Jean-Pierre, to drive her to the hospital in the morning. That evening, a woman appears at her door asking to use the phone. When Sarah refuses, saying her husband is asleep, the stranger reveals that she knows he is dead. Sarah, a photographer, tries to take her picture and calls the police, but by the time they arrive the woman has vanished.

Developing her photographs, Sarah realizes that the woman appears in the background of earlier pictures and has been stalking her. That night she awakens to find the intruder in her bedroom, stabbing at her pregnant belly with scissors. Sarah locks herself in the bathroom as the woman makes clear that she wants to take the unborn child for herself. Over the course of the night, a series of visitors arrives at the house, including Sarah's mother, Jean-Pierre and a group of police officers, and each is drawn into the escalating carnage, while Sarah, trapped and injured, fights desperately to survive and protect her baby.

The film uses its confined setting and the vulnerability of its heroine to create unbearable tension, exploring maternal grief and obsession through extreme imagery.

Inside was selected for the International Critics' Week at the 2007 Cannes Film Festival and was released in France on 13 June 2007. It received positive reviews, with 88 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes; The Village Voice called it repellent but uncompromising, and Ain't It Cool News hailed it as a traumatically entertaining experience.

overview: Steve Freeling lives with his wife, Diane, and their three children, Dana, Robbie, and Carol Anne, in Southern California where he sells houses for the company that built the neighborhood. It starts with just a few odd occurrences, such as broken dishes and furniture moving around by itself. However, when he realizes that something truly evil haunts his home, Steve calls in a team of parapsychologists led by Dr. Lesh to help before it's too late.
tagline: It knows what scares you.
title: Poltergeist
plot:
Poltergeist is a 1982 American supernatural horror film directed by Tobe Hooper. Steven Spielberg conceived the story and wrote the script with Michael Grais and Mark Victor, and produced it with Frank Marshall. JoBeth Williams and Craig T. Nelson star as Diane and Steve Freeling, with Beatrice Straight as the parapsychologist Dr. Lesh, Heather O'Rourke as Carol Anne, Dominique Dunne and Oliver Robins as her siblings and Zelda Rubinstein as the medium Tangina Barrons.

The Freelings live in Cuesta Verde, a planned community in California, where Steve sells real estate and Diane looks after their children, teenage Dana, eight-year-old Robbie and five-year-old Carol Anne. One night the little girl begins talking to the static on the television; the next night a ghostly hand reaches out of the screen, the house shakes, and she announces, "They're here." Harmless-seeming phenomena follow, such as bending cutlery and furniture that moves by itself, until a stormy night turns them deadly. The gnarled tree outside smashes through the children's window and grabs Robbie, and while the family rescues him, Carol Anne is sucked into a portal in the bedroom closet.

Dr. Lesh's team detects multiple spirits, and Steve learns from his boss that the neighbourhood was built on a former cemetery whose graves were relocated. Tangina, the medium they call in, explains that Carol Anne is trapped in a realm of restless spirits who are drawn to her life force, and that a malevolent being she calls the Beast is using the girl to keep them from moving on. With a rope threaded through the closet portal and out through the living-room ceiling, Diane goes in after her daughter, and the two tumble back covered in ectoplasm. Tangina declares the house clean. On the family's last night before moving out, the Beast attacks again. Diane falls into the flooded pit of an unfinished swimming pool where corpses rise around her, and as she flees with the children, more bodies erupt from the ground. Steve realises that only the headstones were moved, not the bodies. The family escapes as the house collapses into the portal, and they spend the night in a motel, where Steve promptly removes the television.

Released by MGM in June 1982, the film earned about $76.6 million in the United States, the year's top horror gross. It received three Oscar nominations, is widely seen as a horror classic, with 88% on Rotten Tomatoes, and "They're here" made AFI's list of the greatest movie quotes.

overview: An ambitious young woman, desperate for followers and fame, fakes a trip to Paris to up her social media presence. When a terrifying incident takes place in the real world and becomes part of her imaginary trip, her white lie becomes a moral quandary that offers her all the attention she’s wanted.
tagline: Get famous or lie trying.
title: Not Okay
plot:
Not Okay is a 2022 American satirical black comedy-drama film written and directed by Quinn Shephard. Zoey Deutch stars as Danni Sanders, a young woman desperate for online fame, with Mia Isaac, Dylan O'Brien, Nadia Alexander, Embeth Davidtz and Karan Soni. It was released by Searchlight Pictures on Hulu on 29 July 2022. The film opens with a mock content warning about an "unlikable female protagonist," a self-aware joke about audiences' reactions to flawed women characters.

Danni is an aspiring writer working as a photo editor at Depravity, an online magazine in New York City, where she struggles both professionally and socially. Hoping to impress Colin, a coworker and social media influencer on whom she has a crush, she claims she has been invited to a writers' retreat in Paris. She spends the following week in her Brooklyn apartment posting doctored photos of herself in Paris and creates a website for the fictional retreat, gaining a modest following, Colin included. Moments after she posts an edited image of herself at the Arc de Triomphe, terrorist bombings strike several Paris landmarks, including the Arc.

To maintain her lie, Danni claims to have witnessed the attacks and stages her return from Paris. Showered with sympathy by her parents, colleagues and a growing online audience, she leans into the deception and becomes a social media sensation as a survivor. At a trauma support group, she befriends Rowan Aldren, a teenage survivor of a school shooting who has become a prominent anti-gun activist, and, inspired by her, writes a viral essay about her supposed trauma that brings her fame, a hashtag movement and the attention she always craved. But as her friendship with Rowan deepens and her public profile grows, keeping the lie becomes increasingly difficult, and its eventual exposure brings devastating consequences for Danni and for those she has deceived.

Not Okay received generally positive reviews. Critics praised Deutch's daring performance as a deliberately unsympathetic heroine, O'Brien's comic turn as the vapid influencer Colin, and Isaac's moving portrayal of Rowan, as well as Shephard's sharp satire of internet culture and the pursuit of online fame, although some felt its tonal shifts were uneven.

overview: Two demon brothers enlist the aid of Kat Elliot — a tough teen with a load of guilt — to summon them to the Land of the Living. But what Kat demands in return leads to a brilliantly bizarre and comedic adventure like no other.
title: Wendell & Wild
plot:
Wendell & Wild is a stop-motion animated fantasy comedy film directed by Henry Selick, written by Selick and Noelle Stevenson, and produced by The Gotham Group.

The story follows two brothers, Wendell and Will, who are struggling to cope with their father's absence.
