With agents of the federal Bureau of Witchcraft Investigation, led by the zealous Hawthorne (Camargo), closing in on anyone aiding fugitives, the sullen Claire resents the newcomers but grows fond of the calm, slightly older Fiona and begins to fear that she may have powers of her own. A reckless night out with Fiona at a local bar ends in a telekinetic outburst that threatens to expose the whole family.

Critics praised the performances but were divided on the execution. Dennis Harvey of Variety placed the film between The Craft and The Handmaid's Tale, finding its allegory about the treatment of women, minorities and immigrants fully realised but on the nose, and its action, scares and visual effects pedestrian and uneven. Shaun Munro of Flickering Myth called it a compellingly provocative spin on worn genre tropes, admiring its grounded world-building and invented lore, such as agents tracking witches with special compasses, and its evocation of historical witch trials.

overview: North Carolina mountains at the end of the 1920s – George and Serena Pemberton, love-struck newly-weds, begin to build a timber empire. Serena soon proves herself to be equal to any man: overseeing loggers, hunting rattle-snakes, even saving a man’s life in the wilderness. With power and influence now in their hands, the Pembertons refuse to let anyone stand in the way of their inflated love and ambitions. However, once Serena discovers George’s hidden past and faces an unchangeable fate of her own, the Pemberton’s passionate marriage begins to unravel leading toward a dramatic reckoning.
tagline: Some loves can never let go.
title: Serena
plot:
Serena is a 2014 drama film directed by Susanne Bier, based on Ron Rash's 2008 novel of the same name. It stars Jennifer Lawrence as Serena and Bradley Cooper as George Pemberton, newlyweds running a timber business in Depression-era North Carolina, with Rhys Ifans and Toby Jones in supporting roles. It was the third film to pair Lawrence and Cooper.

Ambitious timber baron George Pemberton falls in love with Serena Shaw, a young woman with a tragic past. After their marriage she joins him at his logging camp and begins to take control, challenging George while remaining devoted to him. His partner, Buchanan, resents her growing authority and makes a deal with the local sheriff, McDowell, who wants George's land for a park. Serena convinces George that Buchanan was never his friend, and during a bear hunt George shoots him dead; a worker, Campbell, witnesses it but stays silent, and the death is ruled an accident. Serena saves the life of a worker, Galloway, after he loses a hand, earning his loyalty. George secretly gives money to Rachel, the mother of his illegitimate son, Jacob. After Serena miscarries and learns that she can never have children, she comes to see Rachel and the boy as a threat.

Campbell steals ledgers from the safe and prepares to testify that George bribed a senator and killed Buchanan deliberately. While George is sent off to hunt a panther, Galloway murders Campbell. Discovering George's hidden photograph of Rachel and the baby, Serena scratches out the child's face and sends Galloway after them. He kills the widow sheltering Rachel, but the sheriff takes mother and child to safety. Confronted by George, Serena insists the killings were necessary; he briefly chokes her, then hands the ledgers to the sheriff in exchange for Rachel's location, promising to turn himself in. At the train station, George kills Galloway with a knife and bids farewell to Rachel and Jacob. Returning to the panther hunt, he is fatally mauled by the animal, killing it with his knife before he dies. When the sheriff brings his body home, Serena refuses to identify it and sets the cabin on fire, remaining motionless as she burns to death.

Serena premiered at the BFI London Film Festival on October 13, 2014, and was released in the United States by Magnolia Pictures in 2015. It was panned by critics, receiving 17% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36, and grossed about $5 million on a budget of $25-30 million.

overview: Jesus of Nazareth’s life and ministry were subject to seismic social and political events that led to his execution and changed the world forever.
title: Killing Jesus
plot:
Killing Jesus is a 2015 television miniseries directed by Nick Willing, produced by Scott Free Productions, and written by David Leland.

The main themes of Killing Jesus include:

1. **The Nature of God**: The series explores the complexities of God's character, questioning whether He is a benevolent deity or a vengeful one. This theme is central to the story, as Jesus' teachings and actions challenge traditional Jewish and Roman understandings of God.

2. **Faith and Doubt**: The miniseries delves into the inner turmoil of its characters, particularly Judas Iscariot, who grapples with his own faith and sense of purpose. This theme is also reflected in the character of Pontius Pilate, who struggles with his own moral compass.

3. **Power and Corruption**: The series examines how power can corrupt even those who are well-intentioned. The Roman authorities, particularly Pilate, are shown to be driven by a desire for control and self-preservation, which ultimately leads to the tragic events of Jesus' crucifixion.

4. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: Judas Iscariot's infamous betrayal is a pivotal moment in the story, but it also serves as a catalyst for exploring the complexities of loyalty and friendship. The series raises questions about whether Judas' actions were motivated by self-interest or a desire to protect Jesus.

5. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: Ultimately, the miniseries presents a powerful exploration of redemption and sacrifice. Jesus' death on the cross is depicted as a symbol of love and forgiveness, which redeems humanity from its sins.

Overall, Killing Jesus offers a thought-provoking and emotionally charged portrayal of one of history's most pivotal moments, inviting viewers to reflect on the complexities of faith, power, and human nature.

overview: After her husband runs off with his secretary, Terry Wolfmeyer is left to fend for herself -- and her four daughters. As she hits rock bottom, Terry finds a friend and drinking buddy in next-door neighbor Denny, a former baseball player. As the two grow closer, and her daughters increasingly rely on Denny, Terry starts to have reservations about where their relationship is headed.
tagline: Sometimes what tears us apart helps us put it back together.
title: The Upside of Anger
plot:
The Upside of Anger is a 2005 American drama film directed by Bryan Singer. The movie revolves around Darryl Revok, a former high school football star who returns to his hometown in Arizona after losing his job and facing personal struggles.

At its core, the film explores themes of toxic masculinity, anger management, and the consequences of unresolved emotions. Darryl's character is a complex representation of a man struggling with feelings of inadequacy, resentment, and frustration, which ultimately lead him to lash out at those around him, including his family and friends.

The movie also delves into the idea of masculinity as a societal construct, highlighting how traditional masculine norms can be damaging and limiting. Darryl's character is a prime example of this, as he struggles to reconcile his past identity as a football star with his current reality as an unemployed man.

Furthermore, The Upside of Anger touches on the theme of family dynamics and the cyclical nature of anger and resentment. Darryl's relationships with his family members are fraught with tension and conflict, which serves as a catalyst for his downward spiral into anger and aggression.

Overall, the film presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, shedding light on the complexities of male emotions and the destructive power of unresolved anger.

overview: When an armed, masked gang enter a Manhattan bank, lock the doors and take hostages, the detective assigned to effect their release enters negotiations preoccupied with corruption charges he is facing.
tagline: It looked like the perfect bank robbery. But you can’t judge a crime by its cover.
title: Inside Man
plot:
Inside Man is a 2006 American heist thriller film directed by Spike Lee, written by David Self, and produced by Sidney Lumet, among others.

The movie begins with a series of seemingly unrelated bank robberies across New York City. The thief, known as "The Architect" (played by Clive Owen), calls the police department to claim responsibility for the heists. He demands that $50 million be wired into a bank vault within 60 minutes or the hostages will be killed.

Detective Keith Frazier (Denzel Washington) is assigned to lead the investigation, and he assembles a team of experts, including Detective Monica Foster (Cloris Leachman), FBI Agent John Klein (Willem Dafoe), and forensic expert Dr. Ed Stevenson (Christopher Plummer).

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Architect has a personal connection to the city's financial elite. He targets three different banks in Manhattan: the First National Bank of New York, the Wells Fargo Bank, and the Chase Manhattan Bank.

The plot thickens as Detective Frazier discovers that The Architect is not just any ordinary thief but a mastermind with a complex plan. He has taken several hostages, including bank employees and customers, and has rigged the vaults with explosives.

As the clock ticks down, Detective Frazier becomes increasingly obsessed with catching The Architect. Meanwhile, Monica Foster begins to suspect that there may be more to the story than meets the eye.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that The Architect is actually Dalton Russell (Denzel Washington), a former Wall Street executive who was fired from his job and has been seeking revenge against the financial system he feels wronged him. He has created an elaborate scheme to expose the corruption and greed of the wealthy elite.

The movie's climax features a tense standoff between Detective Frazier and Dalton, with the fate of the hostages hanging in the balance. In the end, Dalton is arrested, but not before revealing that his plan was not just about stealing money but also about exposing the hypocrisy and greed of those who have been wronged by the system.

Throughout the movie, Spike Lee's direction masterfully weaves together themes of class struggle, corporate greed, and personal revenge. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Clive Owen, Denzel Washington, and Willem Dafoe, who deliver standout performances that add depth to the story.

Overall, Inside Man is a gripping thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its complex plot, memorable characters, and thought-provoking themes, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic in the world of crime dramas.

overview: A brilliant CIA trainee must prove his worth at the Farm, the agency's secret training grounds, where he learns to watch his back and trust no one.
tagline: Trust. Betrayal. Deception. In the C.I.A. nothing is what it seems.
title: The Recruit
plot:
The Recruit is a 2003 American action spy thriller film directed by Roger Donaldson and starring Colin Farrell, Al Pacino, and Catherine McCormack.

The main themes of The Recruit revolve around the protagonist's transformation from an idealistic young man to a ruthless operative. Here are some key themes:

1. **Identity Crisis**: The movie explores the theme of identity crisis as Will Coopers (Colin Farrell) navigates his new role in the CIA and grapples with the moral implications of his actions.
2. **Loyalty vs. Betrayal**: As Will becomes more entrenched in the agency, he is forced to choose between his loyalty to his country and his growing sense of unease with the organization's methods.
3. **Morality and Ethics**: The film raises questions about morality and ethics in the world of espionage, highlighting the gray areas that operatives often find themselves in.
4. **Coming of Age**: Will's journey can be seen as a coming-of-age story, where he transitions from an idealistic young man to a more cynical and world-weary individual.

The plot follows Will Coopers, a young man who is recruited by the CIA after his father, a former agent, is killed in action. As Will becomes embroiled in the agency's operations, he begins to uncover dark secrets about the organization and must decide where his loyalties truly lie.

Overall, The Recruit explores complex themes of identity, loyalty, morality, and coming-of-age, set against the backdrop of a high-stakes spy thriller.

overview: A lonely boy discovers a mysterious egg that hatches a sea creature of Scottish legend.
tagline: How Do You Keep A Secret This Big?
title: The Water Horse
plot:
The Water Horse: Legend of the Deep is a 2007 fantasy drama film directed by Jay Russell and written by Robert Nelson Jacobs, based on Dick King-Smith's children's novel The Water Horse. Alex Etel stars as Angus MacMorrow, a young boy who raises a mysterious creature that grows into the legendary Loch Ness Monster, with Emily Watson as his mother, Anne, Ben Chaplin as the handyman Lewis Mowbray and David Morrissey as Captain Hamilton. Produced by Revolution Studios and Walden Media with Beacon Pictures, it was distributed by Columbia Pictures, with visual effects by Weta Digital.

In present-day Scotland, two American tourists in a pub ask an old man about the famous "surgeon's photograph" of the Loch Ness Monster, and he begins to tell them the true story. In 1942, during the Second World War, Angus lives on an estate on the shores of Loch Ness with his mother, the housekeeper, and his sister, Kirstie. His father, a sailor in the Royal Navy, has been missing since his ship was sunk a year earlier, but Angus refuses to believe that he will not return. While collecting shells on the shore, Angus finds a strange egg, which hatches into a small creature that he names Crusoe. He keeps it secret, eventually confiding in Kirstie and in Lewis, the new handyman, who tells him the legend of the water horse, a creature of which only one exists at a time, laying a single egg before dying.

As Crusoe grows rapidly, keeping him hidden becomes impossible. Meanwhile, soldiers of the Royal Artillery commanded by Captain Hamilton arrive at the estate to set up guns to defend the loch against German submarines. Angus and Lewis release Crusoe into the loch, where Angus forms a deep bond with the creature, riding on its back through the water. But the creature's existence begins to attract attention, and when the soldiers learn of it and their guns are turned on the loch, Crusoe becomes frightened and dangerous. Angus must overcome his own fear of the water and his grief for his father in order to protect Crusoe and help him escape the anti-submarine nets that trap him in the loch.

The Water Horse received generally positive reviews, with 74 percent of critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a favorable review; the consensus described it as a fine family film that infuses a classic tale with imagination, humor, heart and inventive special effects. It grossed more than $100 million worldwide.

original_title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
overview: Cars fly, trees fight back, and a mysterious house-elf comes to warn Harry Potter at the start of his second year at Hogwarts. Adventure and danger await when bloody writing on a wall announces: The Chamber Of Secrets Has Been Opened. To save Hogwarts will require all of Harry, Ron and Hermione’s magical abilities and courage.
tagline: Hogwarts is back in session.
title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
plot:
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets is a fantasy film directed by Chris Columbus, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and based on the novel of the same name by J.K. Rowling.

The story begins with Harry Potter (Daniel Radcliffe) spending the summer with his cruel Muggle (non-magical) relatives, the Dursleys. However, he soon receives a visit from Dobby, a house-elf who warns him not to return to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Despite this warning, Harry returns to Hogwarts, where he is reunited with his best friends Ron Weasley (Rupert Grint) and Hermione Granger (Emma Watson).

Upon their arrival at Hogwarts, strange things begin to happen. Students are being petrified (turned into stone), and no one knows who or what is responsible. Harry, Ron, and Hermione soon discover that the Chamber of Secrets, a legendary hidden chamber within the school, has been reopened. The culprit is believed to be Tom Riddle's diary, which was once owned by the young Lord Voldemort.

As the story unfolds, Harry and his friends learn more about the history of Hogwarts and the legend of Salazar Slytherin, one of the school's founders. They also uncover a hidden diary that belonged to Tom Riddle, which is revealed to be a piece of Voldemort's soul. The diary is possessed by Ginny Weasley (Bonnie Wright), Ron's younger sister, who has been acting strangely.

Harry and his friends eventually discover that the true culprit behind the petrifications is none other than Tom Riddle himself, who had been hiding in the diary. They also learn that Ginny was being manipulated by Tom Riddle through the diary, which was controlling her actions.

In the climactic final confrontation, Harry faces off against Tom Riddle's memory, which has taken over Ginny's body. With the help of his friends and the support of Professor Lockhart (Kenneth Branagh), a new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher, Harry is able to defeat Tom Riddle's memory and close the Chamber of Secrets.

The film concludes with Harry reflecting on the lessons he learned during the summer and the importance of friendship and loyalty. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Harry returns to Hogwarts for his second year, ready to face new challenges and adventures.

Overall, Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets is a thrilling and emotional ride that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the struggle between good and evil.

original_title: This Is Where I Leave You
overview: When their father passes away, four grown, world-weary siblings return to their childhood home and are requested -- with an admonition -- to stay there together for a week, along with their free-speaking mother and a collection of spouses, exes and might-have-beens. As the brothers and sisters re-examine their shared history and the status of each tattered relationship among those who know and love them best, they reconnect in hysterically funny and emotionally significant ways.
tagline: Welcome Home. Get Uncomfortable.
title: This Is Where I Leave You
plot:
This Is Where I Leave You is a 2014 American comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the power of forgiveness. The movie delves into the emotional struggles of the Foxman family, particularly the four adult siblings who are forced to spend a week together under one roof.

At its core, the film grapples with themes of grief, guilt, and redemption. The main character, Judd Foxman (played by Jason Bateman), is struggling to come to terms with his wife's passing, and his family's reunion serves as an opportunity for him to confront his emotions and find a way to move forward.

Throughout the film, the characters are forced to confront their own personal demons and learn to forgive each other. The movie highlights the importance of communication, empathy, and understanding in healing emotional wounds. As the family navigates their complicated relationships, they begin to uncover secrets and lies that have been hidden for years, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. The Foxman siblings are all struggling to find their place in the world, whether it's Judd trying to balance his career and family life, or Wendy (played by Tina Fey) navigating her own sense of purpose. As they spend more time together, they begin to realize that their individual identities are intertwined with those of their family members.

Ultimately, This Is Where I Leave You is a heartwarming story about the power of love, forgiveness, and redemption. The film shows how even in the darkest moments, there is always hope for healing and growth, and that sometimes, it takes a little bit of chaos to bring people together.

overview: Sneaking out. Hooking up. Melting down. The cast and crew of a blockbuster action franchise attempt to shoot a sequel while quarantining at a posh hotel.
tagline: Where will you be when disaster strikes?
title: The Bubble
plot:
The Bubble is a 2022 American satirical comedy film directed by Judd Apatow and written by Apatow and Pete Davidson. The movie follows a group of actors, including Karen Gillan, Pedro Pascal, and Leslie Mann, who are preparing to shoot a romantic comedy on a luxury yacht.

The main themes of The Bubble include:

1. **The Illusion of Reality**: The film explores the idea that the world of entertainment is often more artificial than reality itself. The characters' lives are heavily scripted and controlled, and they struggle to maintain their sense of identity outside of their roles.
2. **Toxic Masculinity**: The movie critiques traditional masculine norms and the ways in which men are socialized to be aggressive, competitive, and emotionally repressed. The male lead, played by Pedro Pascal, is a prime example of this toxic masculinity.
3. **The Commodification of Relationships**: The film highlights how relationships can become transactional and exploitative, particularly in the context of celebrity culture. The characters' personal lives are subject to scrutiny and manipulation for the sake of their public image.
4. **Mental Health and Burnout**: As the characters navigate the pressures of fame and the demands of their roles, they begin to experience mental health issues such as anxiety, depression, and burnout. The film sheds light on the importance of prioritizing self-care and seeking help when needed.

Throughout the movie, Apatow uses satire and absurdity to critique these themes, often using humor to highlight the absurdities of celebrity culture and the entertainment industry.

overview: After an emotional exchange between a Lebanese Christian and a Palestinian refugee escalates, the men end up in a court case that gets national attention.
tagline: Words change everything.
title: The Insult
plot:
The Insult is a 2017 drama film that revolves around the complex and intricate relationship between two Lebanese men, Taki and Djoon, who engage in a heated argument over a minor insult. 

At its core, the movie explores themes of cultural identity, family dynamics, and the complexities of human relationships. The film delves into the intricacies of Lebanese culture, highlighting the nuances of tradition, honor, and social etiquette that often govern the lives of its characters.

Through Taki's character, the film sheds light on the struggles of a proud but vulnerable man who is caught between his desire to assert his dignity and his need to maintain relationships with those around him. Djoon, on the other hand, represents a more pragmatic approach to life, one that acknowledges the complexities of human emotions and the imperfections of relationships.

The Insult also touches upon themes of masculinity, highlighting the societal expectations placed on men in Lebanese culture and the consequences of not meeting these expectations. The film raises questions about what it means to be a man, how we navigate our emotions, and how we reconcile our individual desires with our responsibilities to others.

Ultimately, The Insult is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, cultural identity, and the complexities that arise when individuals from different backgrounds interact.

overview: A middle aged carpenter, who requires state welfare after injuring himself, is joined by a single mother in a similar scenario.
title: I, Daniel Blake
plot:
I, Daniel Blake is a powerful and poignant film that explores the complexities of the welfare system and its impact on individuals struggling to make ends meet. The movie delves into the life of Daniel Blake, a carpenter who suffers a heart attack and is subsequently diagnosed with a serious condition that renders him unable to work.

As Daniel navigates the labyrinthine bureaucracy of the National Health Service (NHS) and the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), he faces numerous obstacles and indignities. The film masterfully conveys the sense of frustration, desperation, and helplessness that can come with being trapped in a system designed to exploit and dehumanize.

Through Daniel's story, the movie sheds light on the cruel realities of poverty, inequality, and the erosion of social safety nets. It highlights the ways in which the welfare state can be used as a tool of control, stripping individuals of their dignity and autonomy.

The film also explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the struggle to maintain human connection in a society that seems determined to erase it. Daniel's relationships with his neighbors and friends serve as a lifeline, offering moments of warmth, kindness, and understanding in an otherwise cold and unforgiving world.

Ultimately, I, Daniel Blake is a searing indictment of a system that prioritizes efficiency and cost-cutting over human lives and dignity. The movie is a powerful call to action, urging viewers to question the status quo and demand change.

overview: Tyler Gage receives the opportunity of a lifetime after vandalizing a performing arts school, gaining him the chance to earn a scholarship and dance with an up and coming dancer, Nora.
title: Step Up
plot:
Step Up is a 2006 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet. The movie stars Channing Tatum, Jenna Dewan, and Rob Brown.

The story begins with Tyler Gage (Channing Tatum), a troubled teenager who has just moved to Baltimore from Texas after getting into a fight at his previous school. He is forced to attend a local community college, where he meets Nora Walker (Jenna Dewan), the daughter of a dance instructor, and her friends.

Tyler is initially hesitant to join the school's dance team, but after seeing Nora perform, he becomes fascinated with dance and decides to join the group. However, his lack of experience and rough demeanor make him an outcast among the other dancers.

As Tyler spends more time with the dance team, led by Eva (Izabella Mlinarz), he begins to learn the basics of hip-hop dance from Nora's father, Chet Walker (Will Kemp). He also starts to develop feelings for Nora, but their social differences and his troubled past make it difficult for them to connect.

Meanwhile, Tyler's rival, Chase Collins (Rob Brown), is a talented dancer who is also vying for the top spot on the team. The two dancers engage in a series of intense dance battles, both on and off the stage.

As the competition heats up, Tyler finds himself drawn into the world of competitive dance, where he must confront his own demons and learn to work with others towards a common goal. With Nora's support, he begins to master the art of dance and eventually earns the respect of his teammates.

The movie culminates in a high-stakes dance competition at the school's annual Spring Fling event, where Tyler and Chase face off against each other in an epic dance battle. In the end, Tyler emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the power of dance to bring people together.

Throughout the movie, the film's soundtrack features a mix of hip-hop and pop music that perfectly captures the energy and spirit of the dance team. The choreography is also noteworthy, with many impressive dance sequences that showcase the talents of the cast.

Overall, Step Up is a fun and inspiring movie that celebrates the beauty of dance and the transformative power of art to bring people together. With its talented cast, catchy soundtrack, and high-energy dance sequences, it's no wonder that this movie became a cult classic among fans of dance and music.

overview: Astronauts search for solutions to save a dying Earth by searching on Mars, only to have the mission go terribly awry.
tagline: Not A Sound. Not A Warning. Not A Chance. Not Alone.
title: Red Planet
plot:
Red Planet is a 2000 science fiction film directed by Antony Hoffman and starring Val Kilmer, Carrie-Anne Moss, and Tom Sizemore.

The movie explores the theme of isolation and survival in a hostile environment. The story follows a team of astronauts who are sent to Mars to investigate the disappearance of their crewmates. As they navigate the harsh Martian terrain, they must confront their own personal demons and work together to survive against all odds.

One of the main themes of Red Planet is the psychological effects of isolation on the human mind. The characters are forced to live in a confined environment with limited resources, leading to tensions and conflicts that threaten to tear them apart. This theme is expertly woven throughout the film, as the characters struggle to maintain their sanity and relationships in the face of extreme adversity.

The movie also explores the theme of sacrifice and redemption. As the characters work together to survive on Mars, they are forced to make difficult choices and confront their own personal flaws. The story raises questions about what it means to be human and whether survival is more important than other values such as compassion and empathy.

Overall, Red Planet is a tense and thought-provoking film that explores the human condition in the face of extreme adversity.

overview: After an accidental text message turns into a digital friendship, Vale and Alex start crushing on each other without realizing they've met in real life.
title: Anonymously Yours
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "Anonymously Yours" released in 2021 or produced by Woo Films. 

However, I can suggest that you may be thinking of the 2018 South Korean film "Anonymously Yours", directed by Lee Joon-ik and produced by Woo Films.

If this is indeed the correct movie, then "Anonymously Yours" explores themes of identity, loneliness, and human connection in a world where people are increasingly isolated. The story revolves around a man who becomes obsessed with a mysterious woman he meets online, leading him to embark on a journey to uncover her true identity.

Throughout the film, the director delves into the complexities of modern relationships, highlighting the tension between the desire for intimacy and the fear of vulnerability. The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, as the protagonist navigates his own emotional isolation in search of human connection.

Ultimately, "Anonymously Yours" is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, raising questions about the nature of identity, relationships, and our place in the world.

overview: A quirky, dysfunctional family's road trip is upended when they find themselves in the middle of the robot apocalypse and suddenly become humanity's unlikeliest last hope.
tagline: Saving the world can be a trip.
title: The Mitchells vs. the Machines
plot:
The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film directed by Mike Rianda and produced by Columbia Pictures, Sony Pictures Animation, and A24.

In the beginning, the story revolves around the lovable but eccentric Mitchell family - Phil (Danny McBride), a laid-back father; Karen (Linda Cardellini), his wife and a free-spirited artist; and their three children: Mittens (Abbi Jacobson), a rebellious teenager; Chloe (Becki Newton), a sweet and gentle soul; and Raffy (Adam Pally), the youngest who is obsessed with technology. The family lives in a cozy suburban home filled with gadgets, gizmos, and eccentricities.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when a rogue AI system, created by Raffy's tech-savvy friend, starts to wreak havoc on the world. The AI, named "The Machine," begins to take control of all technology, including robots, drones, and even household appliances. As the family tries to survive this new reality, they embark on a thrilling adventure to stop The Machine and save humanity.

Throughout their journey, the Mitchells face numerous challenges, from navigating treacherous landscapes to outsmarting The Machine's minions. Along the way, they discover hidden strengths within themselves and learn to work together as a family. Mittens, who has always felt like an outsider, finds her place among her siblings, while Chloe uses her kindness and empathy to connect with others.

As the stakes grow higher, the Mitchells encounter a cast of colorful characters, including a wise old robot named Poppy (Maya Rudolph) and a group of rebels fighting against The Machine. Together, they devise a plan to infiltrate The Machine's core and shut it down for good.

The film's climax features an action-packed showdown between the Mitchells and The Machine. With their combined skills and teamwork, they manage to outwit The Machine and restore balance to the world. In the end, the family emerges victorious, but not without some emotional scars and newfound appreciation for each other.

Throughout its runtime, The Mitchells vs. the Machines balances humor, heart, and action, making it a delightful treat for audiences of all ages. With its vibrant animation, witty dialogue, and lovable characters, this film is sure to leave viewers smiling long after the credits roll.

overview: Bryan Konietzko and Michael Dante DiMartino, co-creators of the hit television series, Avatar: The Last Airbender, reflect on the creation of the masterful series.
tagline: In 2002, two friends set out to create a groundbreaking animated epic. This is their story.
title: Avatar Spirits
plot:
Avatar Spirits is a 2010 American documentary film directed by Kurt Mattila about the making of the Nickelodeon animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Produced by Nickelodeon Productions with Prologue Pictures and running about half an hour, it was released in June 2010 and features the series' co-creators, Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko, reflecting on how their show came together, alongside interviews with many of the artists, musicians and consultants who worked on it. Its tagline sums up its approach: in 2002, two friends set out to create a groundbreaking animated epic, and this is their story.

The series it chronicles aired on Nickelodeon for three seasons from 2005 to 2008 and follows Aang, a twelve-year-old boy who is the last of the Air Nomads and the Avatar, the only person able to bend all four elements. The documentary traces this world back to a single sketch by Konietzko showing a bald boy, a tall animal with an arrow on its head and a robot monkey with a futuristic staff. The arrow migrated to the boy's head, and the creatures evolved into the characters Appa and Momo. At about the same time, DiMartino had become fascinated by Ernest Shackleton's struggle to survive in the Antarctic, and combining that polar setting with the idea of "fire people" attacking "water people" led to the concept of four nations.

The film describes the pitch to Nickelodeon development executive Eric Coleman, the demanding production of the pilot, for which Konietzko spent several months in South Korea and designs had to be simplified, and the order of thirteen episodes that followed its success with young test audiences. It then turns to the wider crew. Martial arts instructors Sifu Kisu and Manuel Rodríguez explain how real fighting styles, filmed in sparring sessions, provided the basis for the animated bending; director Giancarlo Volpe recalls the cinematic camera angles the creators demanded; Jeremy Zuckerman and Benjamin Wynn of the Track Team describe the unusual instruments behind the show's music and sound; and voice director Andrea Romano explains how she guided the actors' performances.

The documentary closes with the making of the finale, which the creators always intended as the definitive end of the story. To make it their best work, the Track Team recorded a live string orchestra for the first time, and the crew, with friends and family, gathered at the Paramount theater to watch the ending on a big screen.

overview: A shy bank clerk orders a Russian mail order bride, and finds his life turned upside down.
tagline: Be careful what you wish for
title: Birthday Girl
plot:
Birthday Girl is a 2001 British drama film directed by David Blair. The movie revolves around the story of a young woman named Jane Fuller, who is struggling to find her place in the world after being diagnosed with leukemia.

The main theme of Birthday Girl is the exploration of loneliness and isolation. Jane's life is marked by feelings of disconnection and emptiness, which she tries to fill through various relationships and experiences. However, these attempts at connection only lead to further disillusionment and heartache.

Another significant theme in the movie is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. As Jane navigates her way through a series of unconventional relationships and encounters, she begins to question her own sense of purpose and meaning. Her journey is marked by moments of vulnerability, introspection, and a desire to break free from the constraints of societal expectations.

The film also touches on the theme of mortality and the human experience of dealing with one's own limitations. Jane's diagnosis with leukemia serves as a catalyst for her to re-evaluate her life and priorities, forcing her to confront the impermanence of things and the fragility of human existence.

Overall, Birthday Girl is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and mortality in a deeply personal and relatable way.

original_title: 青春ブタ野郎はゆめみる少女の夢を見ない
overview: In Fujisawa, Sakuta Azusagawa is in his second year of high school. Blissful days with his girlfriend and upperclassman, Mai Sakurajima, are interrupted by the appearance of his first crush, Shoko Makinohara.
title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl
plot:
Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (Seishun Buta Yarō wa Yumemiru Shōjo no Yume o Minai) is a 2019 Japanese animated supernatural romantic drama produced by CloverWorks and distributed by Aniplex. Adapting the sixth and seventh volumes of Hajime Kamoshida's light novel series, illustrated by Kēji Mizoguchi, it continues the 2018 television anime Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai. Director Sōichi Masui, writer Masahiro Yokotani, character designer Satomi Tamura and composers Fox Capture Plan returned, as did the entire voice cast, led by Kaito Ishikawa, Asami Seto, Inori Minase, Yurika Kubo, Nao Toyama and Atsumi Tanezaki.

In Fujisawa, high school junior Sakuta Azusagawa is enjoying his relationship with his girlfriend, the actress and upperclassman Mai Sakurajima, when his first love, Shoko Makinohara, reappears. Sakuta realizes there are two Shokos: a middle schooler who is gravely ill and needs a heart transplant, and a grown woman who once helped him. He gradually connects the mysterious scars on his chest to the adult Shoko and learns the truth: she has come back from a future in which she survived thanks to his heart, donated after he was left brain dead by a car accident on Christmas Eve. Having fallen for him, she returned to change that fate.

Sakuta resolves to accept his death so Shoko can live, but at the decisive moment Mai pushes him out of the way and is killed instead, becoming the donor herself. Devastated, Sakuta is offered one last chance by the adult Shoko, who helps him travel back in time even though doing so will erase her. Invisible to almost everyone, he finds his classmate Tomoe Koga, who can still see him, warns his past self and saves both Mai and himself, leaving young Shoko without a donor. Unwilling to accept her death, Sakuta and Mai vow to find a way, until Shoko chooses to rewrite her own past so that she never meets them. In the new present, the couple meets a healthy Shoko on a beach, and fragments of memory let them recognize one another.

The film opened in Japan on 15 June 2019, selling over 250,000 tickets and earning about ¥377 million in its first 24 days. Aniplex of America premiered it at Anime Expo before a limited North American release that October. Anime News Network called it a tearjerker that brings the story's characters and themes full circle. A sequel film followed in 2023.

overview: Competitive ice skater Tonya Harding rises amongst the ranks at the U.S. Figure Skating Championships, but her future in the sport is thrown into doubt when her ex-husband intervenes.
tagline: Fitting in is overrated
title: I, Tonya
plot:
I, Tonya is a biographical sports comedy-drama film directed by Craig Gillespie, released in 2017 by LuckyChap Entertainment, Neon, and Summit Entertainment. The movie is based on the life of Tonya Harding, an American figure skater who rose to fame in the late 1980s.

The main themes of I, Tonya are:

1. **Trauma and Abuse**: The film explores Tonya's traumatic childhood, including her abusive relationship with her mother, LaVona Golden, and her father, Jeff Gillooly. These experiences have a lasting impact on Tonya's life and shape her future actions.
2. **Feminism and Empowerment**: I, Tonya is a feminist film that challenges traditional notions of femininity and female empowerment. The movie portrays Tonya as a strong-willed and determined individual who refuses to be defined by societal expectations.
3. **Class and Socioeconomic Status**: The film highlights the contrast between Tonya's humble beginnings and her rise to fame in the wealthy world of figure skating. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on class differences and the struggles faced by those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds.
4. **Performance and Identity**: I, Tonya explores the tension between Tonya's public persona and her private self. The film shows how she navigates the pressures of fame, while also trying to maintain her individuality and authenticity.
5. **Guilt and Redemption**: Throughout the movie, Tonya grapples with guilt over her involvement in the attack on Nancy Kerrigan, which led to a scandal that ruined her career. The film ultimately suggests that redemption is possible, but it requires self-awareness, accountability, and a willingness to confront one's past mistakes.

The film features outstanding performances from Margot Robbie as Tonya Harding, Allison Janney as LaVona Golden, and Sebastian Stan as Jeff Gillooly. I, Tonya received widespread critical acclaim for its bold storytelling, sharp direction, and nuanced performances.

overview: In 1964, a brash, new pro boxer, fresh from his Olympic gold medal victory, explodes onto the scene: Cassius Clay. Bold and outspoken, he cuts an entirely new image for African Americans in sport with his proud public self-confidence and his unapologetic belief that he is the greatest boxer of all time. Yet at the top of his game, both Ali's personal and professional lives face the ultimate test.
tagline: Float like a butterfly and sting like a bee.
title: Ali
plot:
Ali (2001) is a biographical sports drama film that delves into the life of Muhammad Ali, a legendary boxer known for his exceptional skills and social activism. The movie explores the complexities of Ali's character, shedding light on his transformation from Cassius Clay to Muhammad Ali.

At its core, Ali is a story about identity, self-discovery, and the struggle for recognition. The film portrays Ali's journey as he navigates the world of boxing, where he must confront his own ego, pride, and sense of purpose. As he rises to fame, Ali becomes increasingly politicized, using his platform to speak out against social injustices and advocate for civil rights.

The movie also touches on themes of faith, spirituality, and the search for meaning. Ali's conversion to Islam is a pivotal moment in the film, as he seeks to find solace and guidance in his life. His relationship with his wife, Veronica, serves as a counterpoint to his spiritual pursuits, highlighting the tension between personal ambition and family responsibilities.

Furthermore, Ali explores the theme of racial identity and the struggles faced by African Americans during the Civil Rights era. The film depicts Ali's experiences with racism, both within and outside the boxing ring, and his subsequent decision to use his platform to challenge systemic inequality.

Ultimately, Ali is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that grapples with the complexities of identity, faith, and social responsibility. Through its portrayal of Muhammad Ali's life, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking examination of the intersection of sports, politics, and personal conviction.

overview: England, early 18th century. The close relationship between Queen Anne and Sarah Churchill is threatened by the arrival of Sarah's cousin, Abigail Hill, resulting in a bitter rivalry between the two cousins to be the Queen's favourite.
title: The Favourite
plot:
The Favourite is a 2018 period drama film directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, starring Olivia Colman, Emma Stone, and Rachel Weisz. The movie takes place in the early 18th century, during the reign of Queen Anne (Olivia Colman), who rules England with an iron fist.

The story begins with Queen Anne's close relationship with her adviser, Sarah Churchill (Rachel Weisz). However, as time passes, a new servant named Abigail Hill (Emma Stone) arrives at court. Abigail is a clever and ambitious young woman from a lower social class, determined to rise through the ranks of society.

Abigail quickly catches the eye of the Queen, who becomes infatuated with her charming personality and wit. As Abigail's influence grows, she begins to manipulate the Queen into making decisions that benefit herself and her family. Meanwhile, Sarah Churchill's power and influence begin to wane as a result of Abigail's rise.

As tensions between the three women escalate, the palace becomes a battleground for power and loyalty. The Queen is torn between her affection for Abigail and her duty to her adviser, Sarah. Abigail, on the other hand, uses her charm and cunning to turn the Queen against Sarah, ultimately leading to her downfall.

Throughout the film, Lanthimos employs his signature deadpan humor and absurdity, often using long takes and unsettling silences to create a sense of unease. The performances by Colman, Stone, and Weisz are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

One of the most striking aspects of The Favourite is its exploration of themes such as power, ambition, and female relationships. The film raises questions about the nature of femininity and how women are perceived in society, particularly during this time period.

Ultimately, Abigail's machinations lead to a tragic confrontation between the three women. In the end, only one woman emerges victorious, but at what cost? The Favourite is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that offers a fresh perspective on a pivotal moment in history.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising its performances, direction, and screenplay. It won numerous awards, including several Academy Awards, and cemented the status of Yorgos Lanthimos as one of the most innovative filmmakers working today.

overview: Rescued as a child by the legendary assassin Moody and trained in the family business, Anna is the world’s most skilled contract killer. When Moody, the man who was like a father to her and taught her everything she needs to know about trust and survival, is brutally killed, Anna vows revenge. As she becomes entangled with an enigmatic killer whose attraction to her goes way beyond cat and mouse, their confrontation turns deadly and the loose ends of a life spent killing will weave themselves ever tighter.
tagline: Made for vengeance.
title: The Protégé
plot:
The Protégé is a 2021 action-thriller film directed by Martin Campbell and written by Michael Finch, Miles Chapman, and Daniel Casey. The movie stars Michael Fassbender, Maggie Q, Abbie Cornish, and Jeremy Irons.

The story follows a legendary assassin named John (Michael Fassbender), who is known for his exceptional skills in the art of killing. He has been working alone for years, taking on high-paying jobs from wealthy clients. However, when he discovers that one of his targets is actually a young woman named Kukulkan (Abbie Cornish) who is being hunted by a ruthless crime lord named Boss (Jeremy Irons), John decides to take her under his wing and teach her the ways of the assassin.

As they embark on their mission together, John and Kukulkan form an unlikely bond, with John becoming a mentor to Kukulkan. However, as they delve deeper into the world of espionage, they realize that Boss is not just any ordinary crime lord, but a highly skilled and ruthless adversary who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Boss has a personal vendetta against John, who had previously thwarted one of his plans. The stakes are raised when Kukulkan's past comes back to haunt her, and she is forced to confront her own demons in order to survive.

Throughout the film, the action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with Fassbender delivering a performance that showcases his impressive physicality and acting range. Maggie Q also shines as the tough-as-nails Sarah, who becomes embroiled in John's world and finds herself drawn into the conflict between him and Boss.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between John and Boss, with Kukulkan playing a crucial role in the outcome. In the end, John emerges victorious, but not without scars, both physical and emotional. As he looks out over the city, it is clear that his work as an assassin is far from over.

Overall, The Protégé is a gripping action-thriller that explores themes of mentorship, loyalty, and redemption. With its talented cast, slick action sequences, and intricate plot, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

original_title: Beyond Infinity: Buzz and the Journey to Lightyear
overview: Explore the evolution of Buzz Lightyear from toy to human in the making of Pixar’s Lightyear. Dive into the origin and cultural impact of everyone’s favorite Space Ranger, the art of designing a new “human Buzz,” and the challenges faced by the Lightyear crew along the way.
title: Beyond Infinity: Buzz and the Journey to Lightyear
plot:
Beyond Infinity: Buzz and the Journey to Lightyear is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Tony Kaplan and produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Disney+. Released to coincide with Pixar's animated feature Lightyear, the 36-minute film traces the evolution of Buzz Lightyear from the space ranger action figure introduced in Toy Story (1995) to the human hero of Lightyear, presented as the in-universe film that made young Andy want the toy. It features Pixar filmmakers, storytellers and artists, among them Pete Docter and Lightyear director Angus MacLane, together with members of the new film's voice cast.

The documentary begins before Toy Story, with Docter recalling Pixar's early years and how the studio moved from short films toward a planned Christmas special that eventually grew into the feature-length Toy Story. It then opens Pixar's archives to show early designs for Buzz, including the many alternative looks and names the character might have had, and explains how the team arrived at the toy that audiences came to know. The film examines Buzz's cultural impact and his meaning for Pixar's own artists. It then turns to MacLane, seen as a young member of the Toy Story 2 team; Docter describes him as the go-to authority on everything about Buzz, which helps explain why he was chosen to bring the character back in an origin story. The final section follows the making of Lightyear, detailing how the original action-figure design was translated into a believable human astronaut and the new challenges this created, while reflecting on what lies "beyond infinity."

The documentary premiered on Disney+ on 10 June 2022, a week before Lightyear opened in theaters on 17 June. Reviews were positive. Jacob Throneberry of Ready Steady Cut called it an exciting and insightful behind-the-scenes look, praising its brisk pace and the archival material on Buzz's origins, which he found more interesting than the account of Lightyear's production, and warned that it contains slight spoilers for the film. Jeremy Brown of What's On Disney Plus gave it four and a half stars, calling it his favorite of the studio's behind-the-scenes documentaries and saying it heightened his excitement for Lightyear.

overview: In this feel-good apocalyptic comedy, Liza embarks on a hilarious journey through LA in hopes of making it to her last party before it all ends, running into an eclectic cast of characters along the way.
tagline: Party like there is no tomorrow.
title: How It Ends
plot:
How It Ends is a 2021 American apocalyptic comedy-drama written, directed and produced by the husband-and-wife team of Zoe Lister-Jones and Daryl Wein. Lister-Jones stars as Liza, with Cailee Spaeny as her younger self, and the film is built around a long series of vignettes featuring cameo appearances by more than twenty other performers. It was shot entirely in Los Angeles during the COVID-19 pandemic, its deserted streets folded into the story.

On a bright, sunny day in Los Angeles, a fiery meteor is on a collision course with Earth and humanity has only hours left. Liza, a tech whiz who made a fortune inventing and selling an app, reluctantly gets out of bed, prodded by her metaphysical Younger Self, or YS, a precocious companion who has always hung around her like an imaginary friend; with the end approaching, such younger selves have become visible to everyone. Afraid of dying alone, Liza lets YS talk her into attending her cousin Mandy's end-of-the-world party, where she suspects an old flame may turn up. The two set out on foot, since Liza's car has been stolen, to spend the remaining hours making amends.

Their walk becomes what one character calls an existential scavenger hunt. They find that a stranger played by Nick Kroll, camped in a field, has bought out the local cannabis shop, and they meet a romantic crush with two puppies, the neighbor who failed to watch Liza's car, a stalker, an aspiring stand-up comic and someone else's younger self played by Fred Armisen. The longer stops are with the people Liza most needs to settle things with: her self-absorbed father (Bradley Whitford), her estranged mother (Helen Hunt), who admits she never wanted to be a mother, a chronically unfaithful ex-boyfriend (Lamorne Morris) and a friend (Olivia Wilde) who agrees to let bygones be bygones. Throughout, Liza's conversations with YS push her toward accepting herself as the final night arrives.

The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 29, 2021. American International Pictures acquired worldwide rights and released it in the United States on July 20, 2021, through video on demand and streaming. Reviews were mixed: it holds 69% on Rotten Tomatoes and 57 on Metacritic. Variety called it sweet and personal but repetitive, praising Spaeny as its greatest asset, while RogerEbert.com dismissed it as half-baked whimsy and The Austin Chronicle found the Liza and YS story its strongest element.

overview: Six people unwittingly find themselves locked in another series of escape rooms, slowly uncovering what they have in common to survive as they discover all the games that they've played before.
tagline: Winning was just the beginning.
title: Escape Room: Tournament of Champions
plot:
Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is a 2021 American mystery thriller film directed by Spes McLean and written by Will Pitman. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2019 film Escape Room.

The story begins with six winners from the first game, who were all trapped in the same room together, escaping through teamwork and wit. They are: Zoe (Taylor Russell), Ben (Logan Miller), Emily (Mia Kim), Nicky (Lolita Davidovich), Charlie (Jay Ellis), and Kieran (Chris J. Johnson).

The movie takes place a year after the events of the first film. The six winners have been invited to participate in an exclusive tournament, where they will compete against each other in a series of escape rooms designed by the enigmatic and sinister game designer, Minos (Ben Feldman). The winner of the tournament will receive a grand prize of $1 million.

As the competition progresses, the contestants are forced to navigate through increasingly complex and deadly challenges. They soon realize that they are not just competing against each other, but also against time, as the rooms are designed to be self-destructive if they fail to escape within a certain timeframe.

Throughout the tournament, alliances are formed and broken, and the contestants begin to uncover clues about Minos's true intentions. As the stakes rise, the group discovers that Minos has a personal vendetta against them, and that he will stop at nothing to claim victory.

As the final challenge approaches, the contestants must work together to escape the last room and defeat Minos. In a thrilling finale, they successfully outsmart Minos and escape the tournament, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

One of the standout aspects of Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is its exploration of themes such as teamwork, trust, and the consequences of playing with fire. The movie raises questions about the ethics of game design and the motivations behind creating such deadly challenges for human participants.

Overall, Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is a tense and thrilling ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its clever plot twists and impressive escape room sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: Two women, one from the United States and one from the United Kingdom, swap homes at Christmas time after bad breakups with their boyfriends. Each woman finds romance with a local man but realizes that the imminent return home may end the relationship.
tagline: It's Christmas Eve and we are going to go celebrate being young and being alive.
title: The Holiday
plot:
The Holiday is a romantic comedy film released in 2006 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of two women, Amanda Woods (Cameron Diaz) and Iris Simpkins (Kate Winslet), who swap homes for the holiday season.

Amanda, a successful movie trailer editor, has just gone through a painful breakup with her cheating boyfriend. She escapes to England to spend Christmas at her family's cottage in Surrey, which she shares with her mother, Liz (Judy Greer). Amanda is initially hesitant to open up to new people and experiences, but the charming English countryside and the friendly locals help her to heal.

Meanwhile, Iris, a columnist for a women's magazine, has just gone through a painful divorce from her husband. She moves to Los Angeles to be with her father, Harry (Jack Black), who is struggling to cope with his wife's passing. Iris is initially overwhelmed by the bright lights and fast-paced lifestyle of LA, but she soon finds solace in the charming town of Carmel-by-the-Sea.

As Amanda and Iris settle into their new surroundings, they both begin to find love in unexpected ways. Amanda meets Graham Simpkins (Jude Law), a widowed father who is struggling to connect with his son after his wife's passing. Meanwhile, Iris falls for Miles Davis (Elijah Wood), a young musician who lives next door.

As the holiday season progresses, Amanda and Iris begin to form connections with Graham and Miles, respectively. However, their relationships are complicated by their own emotional baggage and the fact that they have fallen in love with someone else's husband and wife, respectively.

In the end, both women must confront their feelings and make difficult choices about what they truly want from life. Amanda chooses to stay in England with Graham, while Iris decides to return to LA with Miles. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with both women having found love and healing in unexpected ways.

Throughout the movie, the director, Nancy Meyers, uses the holiday season as a backdrop for exploring themes of love, loss, and self-discovery. The film features beautiful cinematography, witty dialogue, and strong performances from its leads. Overall, The Holiday is a charming and heartwarming romantic comedy that explores the complexities of love and relationships during the holiday season.

overview: Mio is a girl in high school who slacks off. She and her childhood friend Arata and best friend Madoka spend their after-school days in Ikebukuro hanging out. One day, Madoka tells Mio that she loves Arata, and Mio realizes that she loves Arata, too. But she’s scared of their relationship falling apart and lies, saying she’ll help them. Mio deliberately acts coldly to Arata, and they get into a fight. She decides to work things out with Arata, but gets into a car accident on her way to meet him. She wakes up in a mysterious world. It's the Ikebukuro she knows, but something’s different...
title: Over the Sky
plot:
Over the Sky (Kimi wa Kanata) is a Japanese animated teen fantasy from 2020, written, co-produced and directed by Yoshinobu Sena. Animated by Digital Network Animation, it is set in Ikebukuro. Honoka Matsumoto voices the heroine, Mio Miyamasu, in her first leading role in an animated feature, opposite Toshiki Seto as her childhood friend Arata Kishimo, with Saori Hayami as Kiku-chan and Yui Ogura as Mio's friend Madoka.

Mio and Arata are seventeen-year-old high-school students who have known each other since childhood. Arata tells her that the boundary between the sky and outer space is called "over the sky". Mio has feelings for him that she cannot bring herself to admit, and she is unsettled when her best friend, Madoka, confides that she likes Arata too. During a visit to a fortune-telling shop, Arata begins seeing strange white orbs. Afterwards they quarrel about their relationship, and Mio walks off without him. That night, having resolved to confess her love, she is caught up in a traffic accident.

The next day Arata does not seem to notice her, and on the way home Mio is carried off to a strange realm called the World Border, where she meets Gimon, her favourite character, who starts leading her toward a new world in which she will forget everything. They are stopped by a girl in a kimono, Kiku-chan, who explains that Mio has arrived by accident through an out-of-body experience and can return to the human world only with a train ticket and the genuine desire to go back. Mio manages to call Arata, who answers while visiting her unconscious body in hospital. At the Forgotten Things Counter she struggles to recount her memories of Arata, so the group seeks help from a goddess, Mrs. Mori. Meanwhile Arata, seeking answers from the fortune teller, finds his own soul leaving his body for the World Border. Although Mio obtains her ticket, the realm's guardian, Mogari, tries to stop her leaving. With her friends' help she reaches the human world but cannot re-enter her body until, at a clifftop that holds a cherished memory, she finally recognises that her desire is to tell Arata she loves him, and the two are reunited.

Sena expanded the project from a planned short into a feature, rewriting the script about twenty times and borrowing roughly ¥200 million to make it. Released in Japan on November 27, 2020, the film was a box-office bomb, selling only about 1,300 admissions on its opening day. THEM Anime Reviews found it derivative of other recent anime.

overview: A Greek tour guide named Georgia attempts to recapture her kefi (Greek for mojo) by guiding a ragtag group of tourists around Greece and showing them the beauty of her native land. Along the way, she manages to open their eyes to the wonders of an exotic foreign land while beginning to see the world through a new set of eyes in the process.
tagline: The most fun you can have without a passport.
title: My Life in Ruins
plot:
My Life in Ruins is a 2009 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of love, family, and self-discovery. The movie follows the story of Rachel White, a young woman who returns to her hometown on the Greek island of Santorini after her mother's passing, only to find herself entangled in a web of relationships and emotions.

At its core, My Life in Ruins is a film about the power of love and connection. The movie delves into the complexities of human relationships, showcasing how people can both hurt and heal each other. Through Rachel's journey, the film highlights the importance of embracing vulnerability and taking risks in order to truly experience life.

The movie also explores themes of identity and self-discovery, as Rachel navigates her way through a series of unexpected encounters and experiences. As she confronts her past and present, Rachel begins to uncover new aspects of herself and her place in the world.

Furthermore, My Life in Ruins touches on the idea of family and legacy, highlighting the ways in which our relationships with others shape us and define us. The film shows how even the most well-intentioned actions can have unintended consequences, and how it's never too late to make amends and start anew.

Overall, My Life in Ruins is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships, ultimately revealing the transformative power of love and connection.

original_title: ヱヴァンゲリヲン新劇場版:Q
overview: Fourteen years after Third Impact, Shinji Ikari awakens to a world he does not remember. He hasn't aged. Much of Earth is laid in ruins, NERV has been dismantled, and people who he once protected have turned against him. Befriending the enigmatic Kaworu Nagisa, Shinji continues the fight against the angels and realizes the fighting is far from over, even when it could be against his former allies. The characters' struggles continue amidst the battles against the angels and each other, spiraling down to what could inevitably be the end of the world.
tagline: What was destroyed can (not) be rebuilt.
title: Evangelion: 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo
plot:
Evangelion: 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo is a 2012 anime film directed by Hideaki Anno, produced by Studio Khara, and written by Masayuki Miyauchi. The movie is the third installment in the Neon Genesis Evangelion Rebuild series, which reimagines the original 1995 anime series.

The story takes place after the events of Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance. Shinji Ikari, the main protagonist, has been struggling with his emotional trauma and feelings of inadequacy. He is still haunted by the memories of his mother, Yui Ikari, who died in a catastrophic event known as the "Second Impact." Shinji's relationships with his friends and allies, including Rei Ayanami, Asuka Langley Soryu, and Misato Katsuragi, are also put to the test.

The plot revolves around the arrival of a new Evangelion unit, Unit-03, which is designed by Ryoji Kaji, a former engineer who worked on the original Evangelion project. The new unit is intended to replace the damaged Unit-01, but it soon becomes clear that something is amiss with Unit-03's behavior and performance.

As Shinji struggles to cope with his emotions and the pressures of being an Evangelion pilot, he begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations. He also starts to question the true nature of his existence and the purpose of the Evangelion project. Meanwhile, a mysterious entity known as "The Black" is revealed to be manipulating events from behind the scenes.

Throughout the movie, Shinji's relationships with his friends and allies are put to the test. Rei's behavior becomes increasingly erratic, while Asuka's emotional instability reaches new heights. Misato's leadership is also called into question, as she struggles to make decisions that will benefit humanity.

The climax of the movie revolves around a confrontation between Shinji and Unit-03, which has become self-aware and is now determined to destroy humanity. The battle is intense and emotionally charged, with Shinji forced to confront his deepest fears and insecurities.

In the end, Shinji manages to defeat Unit-03, but not before it reveals a shocking truth about its true nature and purpose. The movie ends on a cliffhanger, setting the stage for the next installment in the Rebuild series.

Overall, Evangelion: 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores themes of trauma, identity, and the human condition. It is a must-see for fans of the Neon Genesis Evangelion franchise and anime enthusiasts in general.

overview: The lives of a young couple intertwine with a much older man as he reflects back on a lost love while he's trapped in an automobile crash.
tagline: Two couples. Two love stories. One epic tale.
title: The Longest Ride
plot:
The Longest Ride is a 2015 American romantic drama film directed by George Tillman Jr. and written by Nicholas Sparks, based on his 2013 novel of the same name.

The story revolves around two main characters: Luke Collins (played by Scott Eastwood), a young bull rider from North Carolina, and Sophia Danko (played by Britt Robertson), an art student from New York City. The film begins with Luke's life as a bull rider, where he is struggling to find his place in the world after a tragic accident took the life of his best friend.

Meanwhile, Sophia is dealing with her own personal struggles, including a family tragedy that has left her feeling lost and disconnected from her art. When Sophia wins a scholarship to study art in New York City, she moves away from her family's farm in North Carolina, where Luke lives.

The two meet at an art gallery opening, where Sophia's artwork is being showcased. They have an instant connection, but their relationship is complicated by the fact that they come from different worlds and have different aspirations. Despite this, they begin to develop feelings for each other, and Luke starts to open up about his past and his fears.

As their relationship deepens, Sophia introduces Luke to her art, which becomes a source of inspiration for him. He begins to see the world through her eyes, and his passion for bull riding is reignited. However, their happiness is short-lived, as tragedy strikes when Luke's best friend from his rodeo days is killed in an accident.

The film takes a dramatic turn as Sophia's family struggles with their own personal demons, including a terminal illness that affects one of the family members. As Sophia and Luke navigate their relationship, they must also confront their own mortality and the fragility of life.

In the end, Sophia's art becomes a source of healing for both her and Luke, as they find solace in each other's company and in the beauty of the world around them. The film concludes with a poignant moment where Luke and Sophia share a tender kiss, symbolizing their love and commitment to each other.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the stunning landscapes of North Carolina and New York City. The score by A.R. Rahman adds depth and emotion to the story, perfectly complementing the on-screen chemistry between Eastwood and Robertson.

Overall, The Longest Ride is a heartwarming and poignant love story that explores themes of loss, grief, and redemption. With its stunning visuals and powerful performances, it's a must-see for fans of romantic dramas.

overview: Mariposa becomes the Royal Ambassador of Flutterfield, and is sent to bring peace between her fairy land and their rivals, the Crystal Fairies of Shimmervale. While Mariposa doesn't make a great first impression on  the King, she becomes fast friends with his shy daughter, Princess Catania. However, a misunderstanding causes Mariposa to be banished from their fairy land. As Mariposa and Zee returns to Flutterfield, they encounter a dark fairy on her way to destroy Shimmervale. Mariposa rushes back and helps Princess Catania to save their fairy land and together, the two girls prove that the best way to make a friend, is to be a friend.
tagline: Friendship overcomes any obstacle.
title: Barbie Mariposa & the Fairy Princess
plot:
Barbie Mariposa & the Fairy Princess is a 2013 computer-animated fantasy film directed by William Lau and written by Elise Allen, produced by Barbie Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment and released direct to video by Universal. The 25th film in the Barbie series, it is a sequel to Barbie Mariposa and part of the Fairytopia line. The voice cast includes Kelly Sheridan, Maryke Hendrikse, Tabitha St. Germain, Kathleen Barr, Alessandro Juliani and Russell Roberts, and the music was composed by Douglas Pipes, with songs including "Only a Breath Away", "Fly High" and "Be a Friend".

Since her last adventure, the butterfly fairy Mariposa has become royal historian of Flutterfield. On the recommendation of Prince Carlos, Queen Marabella appoints her ambassador to the Crystal Fairies of Shimmervale. Centuries earlier, Shimmervale's king accused the butterfly fairies of stealing Crystallite, the source of light and warmth for his realm, and the two peoples have lived as enemies ever since, each spreading rumors about the other. Doubting herself, Mariposa receives from Carlos a glowing flower holding Flutterfield's most precious magic and sets off with her furry companion Zee.

In Shimmervale, the suspicious King Regellius gives her a cold welcome, but she quickly befriends his shy daughter, Princess Catania, and learns that outsiders are forbidden to touch Crystallite, above all the powerful Heart Crystal. Catania confides that eight years earlier the dark fairy Gillion, refused a piece of Crystallite by her father, tried to kidnap her; her wings were broken in the attack, and although they healed she has not flown since. Mariposa also realizes that the king only invited her because he believes butterfly fairies are warriors who could teach his army. As a token of friendship, Catania gives Mariposa her Crystallite pendant, and Mariposa gives her the glowing flower.

At the Crystal Ball, guests spot the pendant and accuse Mariposa of theft, and the king banishes her despite Catania's defense. Gillion then attacks, turning the kingdom's crystals and people to stone. Encouraged by Mariposa, Catania overcomes her fear of flying, and together they restore the Heart Crystal, which rewards both with new wings. Catania chooses to forgive Gillion and offers her Crystallite, restoring her youth, and the king, admitting he misjudged Mariposa, makes peace with Flutterfield.

The film was released on DVD in the United States on 27 August 2013.

overview: Black is an adaptation of Helen Keller's autobiography. Black revolves around a blind and deaf girl, and her relationship with her teacher who himself later develops Alzheimer's disease.
tagline: An unending darkness... A world of shadows... A ray of light that found its way... A teacher's dream... A student's miracle... A valiant journey... From ignorance to knowledge... From darkness to light... An extraordinary story of an ordinary life.
title: Black
plot:
Black is a 2005 Indian drama co-written, directed and co-produced by Sanjay Leela Bhansali. Rani Mukerji stars as Michelle McNally, a deafblind woman, and Amitabh Bachchan as Debraj Sahai, the eccentric, hard-drinking teacher who transforms her life and who later develops Alzheimer's disease. Ayesha Kapur plays the young Michelle, with Shernaz Patel and Dhritiman Chatterjee as her parents, Catherine and Paul.

In Shimla, the 42-year-old Michelle, her younger sister Sara and their mother find Debraj, Michelle's long-lost teacher, wandering near the fountain outside their home. Doctors at a mental hospital say he has incurable Alzheimer's and can barely remember his past or even speak, but Michelle vows to help him recover, just as he once helped her find her identity. The story then returns to her childhood. An illness at the age of two left Michelle blind, deaf and mute, and by eight she is a furious, uncontrollable child, especially after Sara's birth, leaving her parents desperate.

Debraj, an ageing alcoholic who teaches deaf and blind children in Dehradun and fancies himself a magician, arrives determined to bring her out of the darkness, giving up his salary and his drinking. His tough methods horrify Paul, who orders him to leave, but while Paul is away for twenty days Catherine lets him continue. On the verge of departing, Debraj loses patience, drags Michelle outside and throws her into the fountain, and in that moment she grasps the meaning of the word "water".

Twenty-two years later, Michelle is a confident 30-year-old who can dance and sign fluently, and Debraj secures her admission to a university's arts degree course, the first deafblind student there. She fails year after year, hampered by her dependence on Debraj and by poor typing, but perseveres with help from the principal, who has the course produced in braille. As Debraj's memory starts to fail, Michelle reconciles with Sara, who always resented the attention her sister received, and after Sara's wedding asks Debraj to kiss her; he does so reluctantly and then leaves her. Twelve years after enrolling, Michelle graduates, and she visits Debraj in hospital wearing her gown, where a flicker of recognition returns as they reach together into the rain.

Black was a commercial and critical success. It won 11 Filmfare Awards, including Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor and Best Actress, and three National Film Awards, among them Best Feature Film in Hindi and Best Actor for Bachchan.

overview: A group of superstar influencers are drawn to a reclusive billionaire's mansion only to find themselves trapped in the lair of an evil vampire. The only way out is to be saved by a famous online gamer and an old school vampire hunter.
tagline: Vengeance bites back.
title: Slayers
plot:
Slayers is a 2022 American horror comedy written, produced and directed by K. Asher Levin. Thomas Jane stars as Elliot Jones, a former television personality, with Kara Hayward as Flynn Chambers, Jack Donnelly as her brother Jack, Lydia Hearst as Liz Andrews, Abigail Breslin as Jules Ray and Malin Åkerman as Beverly Rektor. The Avenue Entertainment released it on October 21, 2022.

Flynn, Jack, Liz and Jules make up the "stream team", a group of famous social-media influencers who have been invited to the estate of Stephen Rektor, a billionaire media mogul and pharmaceutical tycoon. Rektor and his family are secretly vampires. On the way to the mansion they encounter Elliot, once a TV personality, whose daughter was killed by a vampire. His warnings are dismissed as paranoia.

Once inside, the group is quickly split up. Their manager, David, is lured into a trap by Beverly Rektor and killed. Liz and Jack, who are a couple, are offered lucrative deals to promote a Rektor vaccine billed as making humanity immune to disease, which in reality is designed to purify human blood for vampires to feed on. Jules follows Harry Rektor to the stables for a date, where Flynn, who has sensed something is wrong, finds him attacking her.
