Jules is killed, but Elliot arrives and destroys Harry, and he and Flynn retreat to his camper, where he explains the history of the vampires.

Back at the mansion, Beverly injects Liz with a serum that turns her into a vampire, while Jack is drawn into a virtual-reality world where he meets Stephen, the vampire leader and Dark Lord. The Rektors achieve immortality not only by drinking blood but by transferring their blood and spirits into new hosts when their bodies wear out, and they have chosen Liz and Jack as their next vessels. Flynn and Elliot storm the house to save Jack, overcome the henchmen and confront Beverly, now inhabiting Liz's body, as she guards the unfinished transfer between Stephen and Jack. Stephen wakes before the process is complete, but the pair knock out both vampires. With no other known way to kill a Dark Lord, Elliot stays behind with a bomb while Flynn and Jack escape; a post-credits scene confirms that he destroyed the Rektors and their followers.

Announced in 2020 under the title With Teeth, the film was shot in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in November 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics were unimpressed, giving it a 22% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: The final candidates for a highly desirable corporate job are locked together in an exam room and given a test so simple and confusing that tension begins to unravel.
tagline: How far would you go to win the ultimate job?
title: Exam
plot:
Exam is a psychological thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of corporate culture and the cutthroat world of job interviews. The movie masterfully weaves together a complex narrative that explores the themes of deception, manipulation, and the blurring of reality.

At its core, Exam is a commentary on the superficiality of modern society, where people are reduced to mere commodities, and their true selves are hidden behind masks of confidence and charm. The film's use of multiple characters, each with their own agenda, serves as a metaphor for the way we present ourselves to the world, often hiding our true intentions and motivations.

The movie also touches on the theme of power dynamics, highlighting how those in positions of authority can exploit and manipulate others to achieve their goals. This is particularly evident in the character of Tom, who uses his charm and charisma to get what he wants, while simultaneously manipulating those around him.

Furthermore, Exam explores the idea of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted. The characters' true selves are slowly revealed throughout the film, exposing the façades they have built around themselves. This theme is closely tied to the concept of social hierarchy, where individuals are judged based on their perceived worth and status.

Ultimately, Exam presents a bleak vision of modern society, where people are reduced to mere pawns in a game of corporate politics. The film's tense atmosphere and shocking plot twists serve as a commentary on the darker aspects of human nature, leaving the viewer with a sense of unease and discomfort.

overview: A man caught in the middle of two simultaneous robberies at a bank desperately tries to protect the teller with whom he's secretly in love.
tagline: Two sets of bank robbers.  One very sticky heist.
title: Flypaper
plot:
Flypaper is a 2011 American thriller film directed by David M. Evans and produced by Rising Star Entertainment.

The main theme of Flypaper revolves around the cat-and-mouse game between two characters, Jack Taylor (played by Brandon Routh) and Nick (played by Mischa Barton), who are both involved in a complex web of deceit and manipulation. As their relationship unfolds, it becomes clear that each character is hiding secrets and using their charm to get what they want.

At its core, Flypaper explores the theme of deception and the blurred lines between truth and lies. The film takes a dark and twisted turn as the characters' true intentions are revealed, exposing a tangled web of relationships, power struggles, and revenge.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the characters engage in a game of psychological manipulation, each trying to outsmart the other. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that neither character is what they seem, and the lines between good and evil become increasingly blurred.

Ultimately, Flypaper is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the destructive power of deception and the devastating consequences of playing with fire.

original_title: Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy
overview: An upcoming animated Sesame Street special premiering on HBO Max on August 5, 2021. The special serves as an introduction to Tango, Elmo's new pet puppy.
title: Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy
plot:
Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy is a 2021 American animated musical television special from Sesame Workshop, the nonprofit organisation behind the children's series Sesame Street. Running about 26 minutes, it premiered on HBO Max on 5 August 2021 and tells the origin story of Tango, a music-loving puppy who becomes Elmo's pet. The voice cast is drawn from the show's regular Muppet performers: Ryan Dillon as Elmo, Eric Jacobson as Grover and Oscar the Grouch, Leslie Carrara-Rudolph as Tango and Abby Cadabby, David Rudman as Cookie Monster and Matt Vogel as Big Bird, with Tyler Bunch and Stephanie D'Abruzzo. Sesame Workshop said the character had been in development for nearly two years.

During a playdate, and with some reluctant help from Oscar the Grouch, Elmo and Grover discover a sweet, energetic stray puppy, whom they soon name Tango. Finding that she has no owner, they set off through the neighbourhood in search of the local pet adoption fair, hoping to find her a "forever home". Along the way, their friends help them learn how to look after a dog: Cookie Monster shows that dogs like special doggie treats, and Abby Cadabby helps give Tango a bath, during which a mishap with some magic bubbles suggests that the puppy has a knack for using a magic wand. Tango turns out to love dancing and to understand what monsters say. When Elmo and Grover arrive at the fair too late, Elmo adopts Tango himself, and the special ends, after a song about home, with Elmo giving his new puppy a tour of his house, much to Oscar's displeasure.

Sesame Workshop presented the special as the first step in using Tango, intended as a mainstay of future Sesame Street content, to model for preschoolers how to meet a new animal, play with it gently, brush and bathe it, teach it tricks and show it affection. It was accompanied by new digital content, games and merchandise, and Tango was set to join the show's 52nd season as both an animated character and a live Muppet. Reviewing it for the Muppet fan site ToughPigs, Matthew Soberman called it a pleasant introduction with a brisk running time and palpable chemistry between Elmo and Tango, noting that it arrived at a time when many families had adopted pets during COVID-19 lockdowns, but questioned why it had been animated when nothing in it could not have been done with puppets on the Sesame Street set.

overview: Two girlfriends on a summer holiday in Spain become enamored with the same painter, unaware that his ex-wife, with whom he has a tempestuous relationship, is about to re-enter the picture.
tagline: Life is the ultimate work of art.
title: Vicky Cristina Barcelona
plot:
Vicky Cristina Barcelona is a 2008 romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Woody Allen. Rebecca Hall and Scarlett Johansson star as Vicky and Cristina, two young American women spending a summer in Spain, with Javier Bardem as the painter Juan Antonio and Penélope Cruz as his volatile ex-wife, María Elena, with Patricia Clarkson, Kevin Dunn and Chris Messina in supporting roles and Christopher Evan Welch as the narrator. Filmed in Barcelona, Avilés and Oviedo, it premiered at the 2008 Cannes Film Festival.

Vicky and Cristina, close friends with very different attitudes toward love, spend a summer in Barcelona staying with Vicky's relative Judy and her husband, Mark. Vicky, practical and conventional, is engaged to the dependable Doug, while Cristina sees herself as a free spirit but is uncertain about what she wants. At an art exhibition, they notice Juan Antonio, an attractive painter rumored to have had a violent relationship with his former wife. He boldly invites both women to fly with him to Oviedo for a weekend of sightseeing, food, wine and, he frankly hopes, lovemaking. Cristina is immediately enthusiastic; Vicky, unimpressed, comes along to keep an eye on her friend.

When Cristina falls ill with food poisoning on the first night, Vicky and Juan Antonio spend the weekend together, and despite her resistance she is charmed and sleeps with him, an experience that leaves her shaken. Back in Barcelona, Cristina begins a relationship with Juan Antonio and moves into his home, while Vicky, troubled by her feelings, goes ahead with her marriage to Doug. Then María Elena, a brilliant but unstable artist, arrives after a suicide attempt, and Juan Antonio takes her in. Instead of driving Cristina away, the situation evolves into a passionate three-way relationship in which Cristina finds inspiration for her photography. As the summer progresses, however, Cristina grows restless, Vicky remains drawn to Juan Antonio, and the tangled relationships come to a head in a dramatic confrontation that sends the two Americans home changed, if not wiser.

The film received widespread acclaim, particularly for Cruz's fiery performance and Bardem's charm, and was one of Allen's biggest late-career successes, grossing nearly $100 million worldwide. Cruz won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, and the film won the Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy.

overview: An aging cop is assigned the ordinary task of escorting a fast-talking witness from police custody to a courthouse, but they find themselves running the gauntlet as other forces try to prevent them from getting there.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG III
tagline: 1 witness… 118 minutes…
title: 16 Blocks
plot:
"16 Blocks" is a crime drama film released in 2006, directed by Rob Cohen and starring Bruce Willis and Mos Def. The movie is based on the true story of a 1999 New York City police standoff.

The main themes of "16 Blocks" include:

1. Redemption: The protagonist, Detective Kevin Corcoran (played by Mos Def), is a young and ambitious cop who is determined to prove himself in the NYPD. He is assigned to work with veteran detective Eddie Johnson (played by Bruce Willis), who is nearing retirement. Through their partnership, Corcoran seeks redemption for his past mistakes and proves himself as a capable officer.

2. Redemption through mentorship: The relationship between Corcoran and Johnson serves as a catalyst for both characters' growth and redemption. Johnson, who has seen it all, takes Corcoran under his wing and teaches him the ways of the job. In return, Corcoran helps Johnson to see that he still has something to offer.

3. Corruption and institutional failure: The movie highlights the corruption within the NYPD and the systemic failures that led to the 1999 standoff. The story is based on real events, which were sparked by a corrupt police officer who was involved in a sex scandal with a young woman. This event sets off a chain reaction of mistakes and missteps that ultimately lead to the standoff.

4. Personal sacrifice: Throughout the movie, both Corcoran and Johnson face personal sacrifices as they work together to resolve the crisis. They put their lives at risk to protect the innocent and bring justice to those responsible for the corruption.

5. The power of partnership: The unlikely partnership between Corcoran and Johnson serves as a reminder that even the most disparate individuals can come together to achieve great things. Their differences become strengths, allowing them to approach problems from different angles and find creative solutions.

Overall, "16 Blocks" is a gripping drama that explores themes of redemption, mentorship, corruption, personal sacrifice, and the power of partnership.

original_title: Codename: Kids Next Door - Operation Z.E.R.O.
overview: The villains of the Kids Next Door, lead by Father, join forces to resurrect the Ultimate Evil, Grandfather, a tyrant who once ruled the world many years ago when most of the villains were themselves kids. However, Father disgraced him that he can't even try to destroy the KND and the Villains were quickly betrayed when they are turned into Senior Citizombies, creatures that are immortal and can transform any living creature into one of them and slaves who are forced to make Tapioca to refuel Grandfather so he can find and destroy the Book of K.N.D.
tagline: Every hero starts from zero.
title: Codename: Kids Next Door - Operation Z.E.R.O.
plot:
Codename: Kids Next Door – Operation Z.E.R.O. is a 2006 American animated television film based on the Cartoon Network series Codename: Kids Next Door, created by Tom Warburton (credited as Mr. Warburton). It was the show's first feature-length story, written by Warburton, Mo Willems and Benjamin Wilgus and produced by the New York studio Curious Pictures with the regular series crew, slotted in between the fifth and sixth seasons. The title is an acronym, standing for "Zero Explanation Reveals Origins". The regular voice cast returns, with Ben Diskin as Numbuh 1 and Numbuh 2, Lauren Tom as Numbuh 3, Dee Bradley Baker as Numbuh 4 and Cree Summer as Numbuh 5, alongside Maurice LaMarche as Father, Neil Ross as Grandfather, Frank Welker as Monty Uno and Mark Hamill.

A prologue recounts the legend of Numbuh 0, a boy who long ago discovered the Book of KND and its 2x4 technology and led a revolt against Grandfather, a tyrant who forced children to make tapioca in his factories, stripping him of his power. In the present, Numbuh 1, leader of Sector V, still believes the legend. While the Kids Next Door fight off simultaneous villain attacks on their museum and Moonbase, Father steals the Recommissioning Module, a device that restores lost memories, and uses it to revive Grandfather, who promptly takes over the coalition of villains. Grandfather begins turning children, and anyone who was once a child, into wrinkled, tapioca-making "Senior Citizombies", overrunning the organization and converting treehouses around the world into tapioca factories.

Blaming himself, Numbuh 1 becomes one of the last free operatives and sets out to find and recommission Numbuh 0, only to discover that the legendary hero is his own father, Monty Uno. Further revelations follow: Father is Monty's brother, making him Numbuh 1's uncle and Grandfather his grandfather, and the Delightful Children from Down the Lane are the lost Sector Z, brainwashed long ago. While Monty holds off Grandfather, who is searching for the Book of KND, Numbuh 1 and his restored teammates bring the Moonbase crashing down on the villain, and Monty lures him into a decommissioning chamber, erasing both their memories and restoring the world. Afterwards Numbuh 1, now keeper of the book, writes in it, "We are Kids Next Door."

Operation Z.E.R.O. premiered on Cartoon Network on August 11, 2006. Warburton said the script took about two months to write, compared with the usual two weeks for an episode.

overview: In 1966, Texas Western coach Don Haskins led the first all-black starting line-up for a college basketball team to the NCAA national championship.
tagline: The incredible story of the team that changed the game forever.
title: Glory Road
plot:
Glory Road is a 2006 sports drama film that tells the story of the first all-black starting lineup in college basketball history at Texas Western University. The movie follows the journey of Coach Don Haskins, played by Dennis Quaid, as he navigates the challenges of integrating his team with players from different racial backgrounds.

At its core, Glory Road is a powerful exploration of themes such as unity, perseverance, and overcoming adversity. The film highlights the struggles faced by the team as they work to overcome their differences and come together as a cohesive unit, ultimately achieving great success on the court. Through the characters' experiences, the movie shows how these values can lead to personal growth, healing, and redemption.

The film also delves into the historical context of the time, shedding light on the racial tensions and segregation that were prevalent in the United States during the 1960s. The story is a testament to the power of sports to bring people together and transcend differences, as the team's success serves as a symbol of hope and unity for their community.

Overall, Glory Road is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the triumph of the human spirit over adversity, highlighting the importance of teamwork, empathy, and understanding in overcoming even the most daunting challenges.

overview: It ain't easy bein' green -- especially if you're a likable (albeit smelly) ogre named Shrek. On a mission to retrieve a gorgeous princess from the clutches of a fire-breathing dragon, Shrek teams up with an unlikely compatriot -- a wisecracking donkey.
tagline: The greatest fairy tale never told.
title: Shrek
plot:
Shrek, released in 2001 by DreamWorks Pictures, is a hilarious and irreverent animated film that pokes fun at traditional fairy tale tropes. The movie follows the story of an ogre named Shrek (voiced by Mike Myers), who lives a solitary life in a swamp.

The story begins with Lord Farquaad (voiced by John Lithgow), a short-statured and power-hungry ruler, who sets out to rid his kingdom of fairy tale creatures. Shrek makes a deal with Farquaad to rescue Princess Fiona (voiced by Cameron Diaz) from a dragon-guarded tower in exchange for the return of his swamp.

Shrek sets off on his journey, accompanied by Donkey (voiced by Eddie Murphy), a fast-talking and wise-cracking sidekick. Along the way, they encounter various fairy tale creatures, including a trio of singing and dancing knights, who are more interested in having fun than fighting.

When Shrek arrives at the tower, he rescues Fiona, but things don't go as planned. Fiona is not your typical princess; she's strong-willed, independent, and has a secret: she turns into an ogre at night. Shrek and Donkey return to Farquaad's kingdom, where they must navigate the complexities of royal politics and Shrek's own feelings for Fiona.

As the story unfolds, Shrek and Fiona develop a romance, but their love is put to the test when Shrek discovers that Fiona has been hiding her true nature from him. In the end, Shrek and Fiona must confront Farquaad and his plans to marry Fiona against her will.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with clever references to classic fairy tales and pop culture. The voice acting is also top-notch, with memorable performances from Myers, Diaz, and Murphy.

One of the standout aspects of Shrek is its subversive humor, which pokes fun at traditional notions of beauty, love, and identity. The movie's irreverent tone and clever writing make it a delight to watch, and its impact on popular culture cannot be overstated.

Overall, Shrek is a hilarious and heartwarming film that will leave you laughing and rooting for the lovable ogre at its center.

overview: Observational documentary unlocking the doors of Britain's hidden swinging scene via access to one of the country's most popular swinging clubs and candid interviews with the club's founder, staff and clientele.
title: Swingers
plot:
Swingers is a 2020 British observational documentary made for Channel 4, which broadcast it on 24 August 2020; the 47-minute film, which credits Belinda Stewart-Wilson, later remained available on the channel's streaming service All 4. One of Channel 4's observational documentaries exploring British sexuality, likened by reviewers to programmes such as A Very British Brothel and Dogging Tales, it unlocks the doors of Britain's hidden swinging scene through unusually open access to Liberty Elite, a swinging and fetish club with around 12,000 members and one of roughly 200 such clubs in the United Kingdom, at a time when, according to the programme, more than 1.5 million Britons take part in swinging.

The documentary centres on Valentine's Day, one of the biggest nights in the club's calendar. Behind the scenes, the 78-year-old owner John painstakingly uncovers the jacuzzi and prepares a buffet of cocktail sausages, dips and crisps, while the manager, Chantelle, puts up heart-shaped decorations; the club also hosts regular themed evenings such as Mature Mischief on Wednesdays. The film then follows several guests as they pack their lingerie and sex toys for the night and talk candidly to the camera about their lives. Siobhan, 67 and single, enjoys a joyful sex life through swinging and has a playroom of her own. Justin and Hannah, who have been swinging at home for two years, are visiting the club for the first time. Simon and Carolyn, a couple who have swung for four years and feel it strengthens their connection, are dismayed by the poor grammar of some messages on swinging apps. Malika, a single mother and lap dancer, says she has not met a decent man in thirty years, and Martyn turned to the scene after a bad break-up. Interviews touch on difficult episodes in some of the guests' pasts, and the film also shows the morning-after clean-up, as staff deal with what has been left behind.

Reviewers welcomed its candour. Barbara Speed of the i called it a pleasingly banal, human look at British swinging rather than a display of glamour, though she found the interviewer's repeated questions about whether guests were looking for love irritating, concluding that the real taboo was the idea that people might enjoy swinging for its own sake. Rhiannon Evans of Grazia hailed it as the best documentary of 2020, noting that it caused a stir on social media and praising its warm, sympathetic and non-judgemental approach.

original_title: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン 劇場版 DEATH & REBIRTH シト新生
overview: Originally a collection of clips from the Neon Genesis Evangelion TV series, Death was created as a precursor to the re-worked ending of the series. Rebirth was intended as that re-worked ending, but after production overruns Rebirth became only the first half of the first part of The End of Evangelion, with some minor differences.
tagline: When our HEARTS are melting together, I will be destroyed.
title: Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth
plot:
Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth is a 1997 Japanese animated film directed by Hideaki Anno, based on the popular anime series Neon Genesis Evangelion. The film serves as a conclusion to the series and provides closure for the characters.

The story begins with Shinji Ikari, the main protagonist, still struggling with his emotional baggage from his past experiences. He is haunted by the guilt of not being able to save his mother, Yui, who died in a catastrophic event known as the "Second Impact." Shinji's relationships with his father, Gendo Ikari, and his friends, Rei Ayanami and Asuka Langley Soryu, are also still unresolved.

The film takes place after the events of the original series, where Shinji has become increasingly isolated and withdrawn. He is visited by a mysterious figure known as "Death," who claims to be an angel from the future. Death reveals that Shinji's existence is tied to the creation of the Evangelion Unit-01, a giant humanoid robot designed to fight against other angels.

As the story unfolds, Shinji discovers that he has the ability to pilot the Evangelion Unit-02, which was created by his father as an alternative to the original unit. However, this new development only serves to further complicate Shinji's emotions and relationships with those around him.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the nature of humanity. The story is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between different timelines and perspectives.

Ultimately, the film culminates in a confrontation between Shinji and his father, Gendo, who reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes to bring about the Second Impact. In a final act of desperation, Shinji sacrifices himself to save humanity by destroying the Evangelion Unit-01, which is revealed to be a vessel for the angel Lilith.

In the end, it is implied that Shinji's sacrifice has created a new timeline, one in which he is no longer trapped by his emotional baggage. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Shinji's spirit is reborn into a new existence.

Overall, Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged conclusion to the series. It provides closure for the characters while also leaving room for interpretation and speculation about the nature of reality and the human condition.

overview: A tight-knit group of New York City street dancers, including Luke and Natalie, team up with NYU freshman Moose, and find themselves pitted against the world's best hip hop dancers in a high-stakes showdown that will change their lives forever.
tagline: Two Worlds. One Dream.
title: Step Up 3D
plot:
Step Up 3D is a 2010 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet, John Stockwell, and Stephen Peters. The movie stars Kenny Wormald, Amanda Seyfried, Adam G. Sevani, and Sharni Vinson.

The story begins with Tyler Gage (Kenny Wormald), a rebellious teenager who has just been released from juvenile detention after getting into a fight in his hometown of Baltimore. Tyler is determined to turn his life around and prove himself as a dancer. He meets Emily (Amanda Seyfried), the daughter of a wealthy businessman, at an art gallery opening where she is showcasing her mother's artwork.

Tyler and Emily meet again at a high school dance competition, where they bond over their shared passion for dance. Tyler is impressed by Emily's talent and decides to ask her out on a date. As they spend more time together, Tyler learns that Emily is struggling to find her place in the world after being diagnosed with a rare eye condition.

Meanwhile, Tyler's friend Chase (Adam G. Sevani) is trying to make it big as a dancer by performing at various events and competitions. However, his rival, Moose (Sharni Vinson), is also vying for attention and tries to sabotage Chase's performances.

As the story unfolds, Tyler and Emily grow closer, but their relationship is put to the test when Tyler's past comes back to haunt him. His ex-girlfriend, Nora (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), returns to town and tries to win him back. Tyler must choose between his old life and his new one with Emily.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Moose's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and threatening. In a tense confrontation, Moose attacks Chase, leaving him severely injured. Tyler and his friends band together to protect their friend and take down Moose.

In the end, Tyler and Emily confess their love for each other and decide to pursue their dreams together. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Tyler and Emily performing a romantic dance routine in 3D, surrounded by their friends and family.

Throughout the film, the dance sequences are showcased in stunning 3D, adding an extra layer of excitement and energy to the performances. The movie features a range of dance styles, from hip-hop to contemporary, and showcases the talents of its cast.

Overall, Step Up 3D is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of love, friendship, and redemption. With its impressive dance sequences and strong performances, it's no wonder why this movie became a fan favorite among dance enthusiasts and music lovers alike.

overview: Deep in the heart of Jakarta's slums lies an impenetrable safe house for the world's most dangerous killers and gangsters. Until now, the run-down apartment block has been considered untouchable to even the bravest of police. Cloaked under the cover of pre-dawn darkness and silence, an elite swat team is tasked with raiding the safe house in order to take down the notorious drug lord that runs it.  But when a chance encounter with a spotter blows their cover and news of their assault reaches the drug lord, the building's lights are cut and all the exits blocked. Stranded on the sixth floor with no way out, the unit must fight their way through the city's worst to survive their mission. Starring Indonesian martial arts sensation Iko Uwais.
tagline: 1 Ruthless Crime Lord, 20 Elite Cops, 30 Floors of Hell
title: The Raid
plot:
The Raid, released in the United States as The Raid: Redemption, is a 2011 Indonesian action thriller written, edited and directed by the Welsh filmmaker Gareth Evans. Iko Uwais stars as Rama, a rookie member of the police Mobile Brigade, with Joe Taslim as Sergeant Jaka, Donny Alamsyah as Andi, Yayan Ruhian as Mad Dog, Pierre Gruno as Lieutenant Wahyu and Ray Sahetapy as the drug lord Tama Riyadi. Its fights showcase the Indonesian martial art pencak silat, choreographed by Uwais and Ruhian.

Rama joins a 20-man squad led by Jaka and Wahyu on a raid to arrest Tama, who rules a rundown apartment block in Jakarta that shelters criminals and addicts, aided by his lieutenants Andi and Mad Dog. The officers clear the lower floors undetected but are spotted on the sixth. Tama's reinforcements wipe out the men outside, he cuts the power and announces over the loudspeakers that the police are trapped. Wahyu admits that the raid was his own unauthorised scheme to remove Tama, who has corrupt friends in the police, and that no backup is coming. Most of the squad is massacred. Rama hacks through a floor with an axe so the survivors can escape to the apartment below, then blows up the attackers with a propane tank rigged in a refrigerator.

The survivors split up. Rama hides the wounded officer Bowo with a reluctant law-abiding tenant before fighting his way past a machete gang. He then meets Andi, who turns out to be his estranged elder brother, the man their father urged him to find; Andi refuses to leave his criminal life. Mad Dog fights Jaka hand to hand and kills him, while Tama discovers Andi's betrayal on his surveillance cameras and has him captured. Rama, rejoining Wahyu and officer Dagu, battles through a drug laboratory, then splits off to rescue Andi, and the brothers kill Mad Dog after a brutal fight. Wahyu murders Dagu and seizes Tama, who reveals he was warned of the raid and that Wahyu's corrupt superior has set him up. Wahyu shoots Tama and tries to kill himself, but his gun is empty. Andi arranges the survivors' escape and gives Rama Tama's recordings of corrupt officials, choosing to remain in the underworld where he can protect his brother.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and earned strong reviews, with 87% on Rotten Tomatoes; The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw gave it five stars. It was followed by The Raid 2 in 2014.

overview: Two tigers are separated as cubs and taken into captivity, only to be reunited years later as enemies by an explorer (Pearce) who inadvertently forces them to fight each other.
tagline: Two infant tiger cubs, separated from their parents and each other.
title: Two Brothers
plot:
Two Brothers (French: Deux frères) is a 2004 adventure drama directed by Jean-Jacques Annaud about two Indochinese tiger cubs, Kumal and Sangha, who are separated from their parents and from each other, then reunited a year later as adults and find their way back home. Guy Pearce plays the adventurer and hunter Aidan McRory and Freddie Highmore plays Raoul Normandin, the young son of a French colonial administrator, with Jean-Claude Dreyfus as his father and Oanh Nguyen as a local prince. Pathé distributed the film in Europe and Universal in the United States.

The story is set in French colonial Cambodia in the 1920s. The cubs are born to a protective tigress and a tiger that McRory later kills. When the brothers are separated, their lives take very different paths. Kumal is caught by villagers and sold to a cruel circus run by Zerbino and Saladin, where abusive training forces him to perform dangerous tricks. Sangha is adopted for a time by eight-year-old Raoul, son of the administrator Eugene Normandin, but after a clash with the family dog he is sent to the menagerie of a palace.

McRory, a morally ambiguous figure, becomes tangled up in the fates of both tigers. After failing to satisfy the vain prince with a counterfeit tiger skin taken from the circus's elderly tiger, Caesar, he learns that the prince's prized fighting tiger is Sangha. The prince stages a fight between Sangha and Kumal as a public spectacle. The brothers attack each other at first but recognise one another in the middle of the fight and fall back into the playful games of their cubhood. When their handlers try to provoke them, chaos breaks out and the two tigers escape together into the wilderness, causing havoc in nearby villages as they go. McRory and Raoul set off to track them down. Raoul persuades Sangha to go back to the jungle, away from the dangers posed by people, and Kumal, remembering McRory's past kindness, spares the hunter. The brothers return to their ancestral temple and are reunited with their mother, whom they recognise by the bullet wound McRory once left in her ear.

Around 30 tigers were used in the film, most from French zoos and others from Thailand. Two Brothers opened in the United States on 25 June 2004 and earned about $62 million worldwide. Reviews were generally positive, with 79% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it an "A−".

overview: Curmudgeonly old Frank lives by himself. His routine involves daily visits to his local library, where he has a twinkle in his eye for the librarian. His grown children are concerned about their father’s well-being and buy him a caretaker robot. Initially resistant to the idea, Frank soon appreciates the benefits of robotic support – like nutritious meals and a clean house – and eventually begins to treat his robot like a true companion. With his robot’s assistance, Frank’s passion for his old, unlawful profession is reignited, for better or worse.
tagline: Friendship doesn't have an off switch
title: Robot & Frank
plot:
Robot & Frank is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, technology's impact on society, and the importance of human connection in an increasingly isolated world.

At its core, the movie delves into the theme of loneliness and isolation. The protagonist, Frank, played by Peter Sarsgaard, is a retired cat burglar who has lost his wife and struggles to form meaningful connections with others. His life is marked by emptiness and disconnection, until he receives a robot companion, which he names "B.O.B." (Brain-Operated Bot). The introduction of B.O.B. serves as a catalyst for Frank's transformation, forcing him to confront his past and reevaluate his relationships.

The film also explores the theme of nostalgia and the importance of holding onto memories. Frank's life is filled with fond memories of his wife and his past exploits, which he shares with B.O.B. through stories and anecdotes. These shared experiences serve as a bridge between Frank's past and present, allowing him to find solace in the company of his robot companion.

Furthermore, Robot & Frank critiques our society's reliance on technology and its effects on human relationships. The film portrays a world where people are increasingly isolated and disconnected from one another, with technology serving as a substitute for genuine human interaction. Frank's initial reluctance to accept B.O.B.'s presence is a commentary on the fear of losing one's humanity in the face of technological advancements.

Ultimately, Robot & Frank is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, loneliness, nostalgia, and the importance of human connection in an increasingly technology-driven world.

overview: When Sheriff Roy Pulsipher finds himself in the afterlife, he joins a special police force and returns to Earth to save humanity from the undead.
tagline: Meet the new law of the Afterlife.
title: R.I.P.D. 2: Rise of the Damned
plot:
R.I.P.D. 2: Rise of the Damned is a 2022 direct-to-video buddy cop supernatural action film directed by Paul Leyden, who co-wrote it with Andrew Klein. Based on the Dark Horse comic book series R.I.P.D., it is a prequel to the 2013 film. It stars Jeffrey Donovan as Sheriff Roy Pulsipher, Penelope Mitchell as Jeanne d'Arc, Rachel Adedeji and Evlyne Oyedokun as their earthly avatars, Jake Choi as Slim Samuels, Richard Brake as the villain Otis Clairborne and Tilly Keeper as Roy's daughter Charlotte.

In the film's opening, Otis Clairborne opens a gateway to hell while searching for gold, and a sinister being takes possession of him. Months later, Sheriff Roy Pulsipher is gunned down in Red Creek, Utah, by a gang led by Clairborne. On his way to the afterlife, Roy arrives at the office of the Rest In Peace Department, an agency that hunts Deados, the souls of the dead hiding on Earth, and agrees to join its ranks.

Sent back to Earth, Roy is partnered with Jeanne d'Arc, the legendary French heroine, now an R.I.P.D. officer. To the living, the two appear as a pair of very different women. Convinced that the men who killed him are Deados, Roy and Jeanne intercept a prison transport, eliminate one of the undead criminals and take a third prisoner, Slim Samuels, to learn more about Clairborne's plans. In a nearly deserted mining town, they discover that the townspeople are sick from mysterious gases coming from a mine, where Clairborne is forcing prisoners to open a gateway to hell so that escaped souls can take over human bodies. Facing betrayal and the demon Astaroth, Roy and Jeanne must close the gate, while Roy also seeks to protect his daughter and her fiancé.

The film mixes western, buddy comedy and supernatural action, adding an origin story for Roy Pulsipher, the gunslinging lawman introduced in the first film, and for his partnership in the R.I.P.D.

R.I.P.D. 2 was released directly on Blu-ray and DVD on November 15, 2022, by Universal. Reviews were negative, with only 25 percent of a handful of critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive review.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 業火の向日葵
overview: Conan tries to track down Kaito Kid, who supposedly steals a replica of one of Van Gogh's Sunflowers paintings during an auction.
title: Detective Conan: Sunflowers of Inferno
plot:
Detective Conan: Sunflowers of Inferno is a thrilling mystery film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The story revolves around the mysterious Sunflower Organization, a group of individuals who are seemingly ordinary but possess extraordinary abilities.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of deception and manipulation, as the protagonist, Shinichi Kudo, navigates through a complex web of lies and half-truths to uncover the truth behind the Sunflower Organization. The film masterfully weaves together elements of psychological suspense, action, and mystery, keeping the audience on the edge of their seats.

One of the primary themes that emerges in Detective Conan: Sunflowers of Inferno is the concept of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted. The characters within the Sunflower Organization are expertly crafted to be charismatic and believable, making it difficult for Shinichi to distinguish between friend and foe. This theme is further underscored by the film's exploration of the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The movie also touches on the idea of obsession and the dangers of becoming too entrenched in one's own desires. The Sunflower Organization's leader, a character known as "Sunflower," is driven by an all-consuming passion that ultimately leads to their downfall. This theme serves as a cautionary tale about the perils of allowing oneself to become consumed by one's own ambitions.

Throughout the film, TMS Entertainment expertly crafts a sense of tension and unease, creating an atmosphere that is both captivating and unsettling. The result is a movie that is both entertaining and thought-provoking, leaving viewers with a lasting impression long after the credits roll.

overview: Two sisters on Mexican vacation are trapped in a shark observation cage at the bottom of the ocean, with oxygen running low and great whites circling nearby, they have less than an hour of air left to figure out how to get to the surface.
tagline: No way out. No way up. No chance in hell.
title: 47 Meters Down
plot: [No information found]

overview: A story centered around an Indian family who moves to France and opens a restaurant across the street from a Michelin-starred French restaurant.
tagline: Life's greatest journey begins with the first step.
title: The Hundred-Foot Journey
plot:
The Hundred-Foot Journey is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the universal themes of cultural identity, community, and the power of food to bring people together. At its core, the movie is a poignant tale of two men from different walks of life who find common ground through their shared passion for cooking.

The film delves into the complexities of cultural heritage and the struggles of navigating one's roots in a rapidly changing world. The protagonist, Hassan, a young Indian chef, must reconcile his traditional upbringing with his desire to forge a new path in France. Through his journey, the movie highlights the importance of preserving cultural traditions while embracing innovation and adaptation.

The Hundred-Foot Journey also explores the theme of community and the role that food plays in building relationships and fostering a sense of belonging. The film's portrayal of the Indian restaurant, Tandoori Nights, as a vibrant hub of activity and connection is particularly noteworthy. As Hassan navigates his new life in France, he finds solace in the warmth and camaraderie of his colleagues, who become like a surrogate family to him.

Ultimately, The Hundred-Foot Journey is a film about the transformative power of food and the human spirit. It reminds us that even in the face of adversity and cultural differences, we can find common ground and build bridges through our shared passions and values.

overview: A mother and son find themselves faced with a brutal alien invasion where survival will depend on discovering the unthinkable truth about the enemy.
title: War of the Worlds: Annihilation
plot:
War of the Worlds: Annihilation is a 2021 American science fiction action film directed by Maximilian Elfeldt, who also co-edited it, from a screenplay by Conor Dowling. It was produced by The Asylum as an original film for the streaming service Tubi, the studio's second for the platform after Swim. It stars Arie Thompson, William Baldwin, Noel Gugliemi and Rashod Freelove. Shot in Los Angeles, with some scenes filmed at the March Field Air Museum, it was released in December 2021 and, unusually for an Asylum production, runs almost two hours.

A shower of meteorites, undetected even by NASA's constant monitoring, strikes the Earth, and each impact releases a gas that is toxic to humans. The military, led by General Skuller (Baldwin), insists that this is a deliberate alien attack and prepares for battle, while cyber-operations specialist Ashlaya Wellish (Thompson) sees flaws in his theory and has her warnings ignored. Skuller is proved right when vast spaceships appear in the sky and beings from another galaxy land, finding the planet's atmosphere and vegetation ideal for their survival. As chaos spreads, Ashlaya's husband Jutta (Michael Marcel) is sent out on patrol, and their son Lucas (Kennedy Porter) is trapped at his school, trying to seal the building against the poisonous substance. Giant tentacles, mech-like robots and looters soon join the danger. Along the way the family's story crosses with that of Tiago (Gugliemi), a survivalist, and Patlin (Freelove), a doctor who survived the attack on his hospital and who rescues a young alien named Gwen (Emree Franklin). Eventually Ashlaya and her companions join Skuller and what is left of his troops, and Ashlaya, seeking to make amends, finds a way to fight back, as survival comes to depend on discovering the unthinkable truth about the enemy.

The supporting cast includes Joseph Michael Harris, Andrew Rogers and Bradford Haynes. The film received little promotion. The website Voices From the Balcony called it surprisingly good for an Asylum film, finding the computer-generated alien ships and giant robots mostly convincing and the tone more serious than many of the studio's releases, and judged it enjoyable though somewhat long; Germany's TV Movie described Elfeldt as a low-budget professional. A sequel, War of the Worlds: Extinction, followed in 2024.

overview: Posing as a wealthy, jet-setting diamond mogul, an Israeli conman wooed women online then conned them out of millions of dollars. Now some victims plan for payback.
tagline: Modern love is a dangerous game.
title: The Tinder Swindler
plot:
The Tinder Swindler is a documentary film directed by Selena Samelson that premiered on Netflix in 2022. The film tells the true story of Simon Leviev, a con artist who preyed on vulnerable women through online dating apps.

The movie begins with Shimon "Shai" Hadad, an Israeli man who was diagnosed with leukemia and had only a short time left to live. He created a fake profile on Tinder, claiming to be a wealthy and charming Israeli businessman named Simon Leviev. Shai's goal was to scam women out of money by posing as a wealthy and successful individual.

Shai's methods were sophisticated and manipulative. He would create elaborate stories about his wealth and business dealings, often using fake photos and videos to convince his victims that he was who he claimed to be. Once he had gained their trust, Shai would start asking for money, claiming that he needed it to cover medical expenses or other urgent financial matters.

One of the women who fell victim to Shai's scam was Romaine "Rom" Gotfert, an American woman from California. Rom met Shai on Tinder and quickly became smitten with him. Over the course of several months, Shai convinced Rom that he was a wealthy businessman who had made his fortune through real estate investments.

However, as their relationship progressed, Rom began to notice some red flags. She discovered that Shai's stories were often inconsistent, and she couldn't find any information about his business dealings or wealth online. Despite her reservations, Rom continued to send money to Shai, believing that he was genuinely in need of financial assistance.

As the film progresses, we see more women who fell victim to Shai's scam, including a woman from Australia and another from the United Kingdom. Each of these stories is heartbreaking, as the women were convinced by Shai's charming facade and ultimately lost significant amounts of money to him.

The documentary also explores how Shai managed to evade law enforcement for so long. Despite being identified as a suspect in several countries, Shai was able to stay one step ahead of his pursuers through his cunning use of technology and social engineering tactics.

In the end, Shai's scam came to an end when Rom discovered that he had been using her own photos from their online conversations to create fake profiles for other women. Armed with this information, Rom contacted the authorities and helped bring Shai to justice.

The Tinder Swindler is a cautionary tale about the dangers of online dating scams and the importance of being vigilant when meeting new people online. The film is both heartbreaking and infuriating, highlighting the ways in which scammers like Shai are able to exploit vulnerable individuals for their own gain.

overview: A fast-talking lawyer transforms his body and takes a vow of silence, not to be broken until he finds out who killed his wife and daughter and has his revenge.
tagline: Payback Speaks Louder Than Words
title: Acts of Vengeance
plot:
Acts of Vengeance is a 2017 action thriller film directed by Isaac Florentine. Antonio Banderas stars as Frank Valera, a Pittsburgh lawyer seeking revenge for the murder of his wife and daughter, with Karl Urban as the police officer Hank Strode, Paz Vega, Robert Forster, Cristina Serafini and Johnathon Schaech. It was released in theaters and on demand in October 2017.

Frank, a fast-talking, successful defense lawyer, is stuck in traffic and misses his young daughter Olivia's performance at a school talent show, watching only a video of her singing that his wife, Sue, sends him. That night, Sue and Olivia are murdered, and their bodies are dumped near a railway yard. After the funeral, Frank's grieving father-in-law, Chuck, blames him and cuts off contact. At the police station, Detective Bill Lustiger tells Frank that a gold fiber was found at the crime scene and suspects the Russian mafia that operates in the area. Consumed by guilt, Frank seeks punishment by taking beatings in illegal underground fights, until he is rescued by Officer Strode, who later tells him that the case has gone cold.

While trying to help a young girl being exploited on the street, Frank crashes through the window of a bookshop and comes across a copy of the Meditations of the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius. Inspired by the Stoic philosophy, he takes a vow of silence, swearing not to speak again until he has found the killers and avenged his family. Frank devotes himself to intense martial arts training, transforming himself into a disciplined fighter, and begins his own investigation, going after the criminals who operate in the area of the murders. As he follows the trail, he uncovers evidence that the crime was not what the police assumed, and that the truth reaches closer to people he trusted than he had imagined, forcing him to confront corruption and betrayal on his path to vengeance.

Acts of Vengeance received mixed reviews. It holds a 64 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 11 reviews and a Metacritic score of 49 based on four critics. Reviewers noted Banderas's commitment to the physically demanding role and the efficient fight choreography typical of Florentine, a director known for martial-arts action films, while finding the story familiar.

overview: A myriad of outrageous calamities befall an eccentric English clan with more than a few skeletons in its closets, when its patriarch dies an unexpected death. Soon, every complication imaginable befall the grief-stricken mourners.
tagline: Last rites... and wrongs.
title: Death at a Funeral
plot:
Death at a Funeral is a 2007 comedy film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and cultural differences through the lens of a traditional African funeral. The movie delves into the theme of cultural identity, highlighting the tensions between the protagonist's desire to honor his father's heritage and the expectations of his more modern, Westernized relatives.

The film also examines the concept of grief and mourning, showcasing how different cultures approach death and bereavement in unique ways. Through the character of Zahir (played by Simon Pegg), a well-meaning but awkward British man who is struggling to navigate his father's funeral, we see the challenges of bridging cultural divides and finding common ground with those from different backgrounds.

Furthermore, Death at a Funeral touches on the theme of identity and belonging. As Zahir tries to reconcile his own sense of self with the expectations of his family and community, he begins to question what it means to be a good son, a good friend, and a good person in the face of death and loss.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, revealing that even in the midst of chaos and cultural confusion, there is room for love, laughter, and connection.

overview: During the early 16th Century idealistic German monk Martin Luther, disgusted by the materialism in the church, begins the dialogue that will lead to the Protestant Reformation.
tagline: Rebel. Genius. Liberator.
title: Luther
plot:
Luther is a 2003 German drama film directed by Oliver Hirschbiegel, not ARD. 

The movie follows the story of Martin Luther, a theologian who sparked the Protestant Reformation in Europe during the 16th century. The main themes of the film include:

1. Faith vs. Authority: The movie explores the tension between Luther's personal faith and the authority of the Catholic Church. Luther's conviction that salvation comes through faith alone puts him at odds with the Church, leading to a series of conflicts.

2. Power Struggle: The film depicts the power struggle between Luther and the Catholic Church, as well as within the Protestant movement itself. This struggle for dominance shapes the plot and ultimately leads to Luther's downfall.

3. Personal Sacrifice: Throughout the movie, Luther faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including persecution from the Church and personal losses. Despite these obstacles, he remains committed to his faith, demonstrating remarkable courage and conviction.

4. The Role of Women: The film also touches on the role of women in society during this period. Luther's wife, Katharina von Bora, is portrayed as a strong-willed and intelligent woman who plays an important role in supporting her husband's work.

5. The Impact of Ideas: The movie highlights the impact that ideas can have on individuals and societies. Luther's writings and teachings inspire others to question authority and challenge traditional beliefs, leading to significant changes in European history.

Overall, Luther (2003) is a thought-provoking drama that explores complex themes and historical events, shedding light on the life and legacy of this influential figure.

overview: Bond has left active service and is enjoying a tranquil life in Jamaica. His peace is short-lived when his old friend Felix Leiter from the CIA turns up asking for help. The mission to rescue a kidnapped scientist turns out to be far more treacherous than expected, leading Bond onto the trail of a mysterious villain armed with dangerous new technology.
tagline: The mission that changes everything begins…
title: No Time to Die
plot:
No Time to Die is a 2021 spy thriller and the twenty-fifth James Bond film produced by Eon Productions, the fifth and final film to star Daniel Craig as Bond. Directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, who wrote the screenplay with Neal Purvis, Robert Wade and Phoebe Waller-Bridge, it co-stars Rami Malek as Lyutsifer Safin, Léa Seydoux as Madeleine Swann, Lashana Lynch as the new 007 Nomi, Ana de Armas as Paloma, and returning cast members Ralph Fiennes, Naomie Harris, Ben Whishaw, Jeffrey Wright, Rory Kinnear and Christoph Waltz.

After an ambush in Italy convinces him that Madeleine has betrayed him, Bond leaves her and retires from MI6. Five years later, he is living quietly in Jamaica when his old CIA friend Felix Leiter asks him to help rescue a kidnapped scientist, Valdo Obruchev, who has been taken from a secret MI6 laboratory along with Project Heracles, a bioweapon of DNA-targeted nanobots that can be programmed to kill only people with a specific DNA.

Bond infiltrates a SPECTRE gathering in Cuba with the agent Paloma, but the plot is far larger than it appears: the nanobots kill the assembled SPECTRE members instead of Bond, and Bond learns that Obruchev is working for Safin, a man whose family was murdered by Madeleine's father on Blofeld's orders. As Felix is betrayed and killed, Bond is drawn back into the world he left, crossing paths with Nomi, confronting the imprisoned Blofeld and reconnecting with Madeleine, who has a young daughter. Safin, operating from a hidden island base, plans to unleash Heracles on millions, and Bond must stop him at a devastating personal cost.

The film closes the arc of Craig's Bond, emphasizing family, love and sacrifice, and features a theme song performed by Billie Eilish and a score by Hans Zimmer.

Delayed repeatedly by the COVID-19 pandemic, No Time to Die premiered at London's Royal Albert Hall on 28 September 2021. It grossed over 774 million dollars, the fourth-highest gross of 2021, and received generally positive reviews, with a Metacritic score of 68, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Song.

overview: When a congressional aide is killed, a Washington, D.C. journalist starts investigating the case involving the Representative, his old college friend.
tagline: Find the Truth
title: State of Play
plot:
State of Play is a 2009 American thriller film directed by Kevin Macdonald and written by Matthew Michael Carnahan. The movie stars Russell Crowe, Ben Affleck, and Robin Wright.

The story begins with Stephen Collins (Russell Crowe), a veteran journalist who works for the fictional Capitol News Network (CNN). Collins is investigating the death of a young woman named Darcy Spitz, who was found dead in her apartment. As Collins digs deeper into the case, he discovers that Spitz's death may be linked to a larger conspiracy involving corruption and murder.

Meanwhile, Tom Shayes (Ben Affleck), a young and ambitious journalist at Capitol News Network, is assigned to work with Collins on the story. Shayes is initially portrayed as a rival to Collins, but as they work together, their mutual respect for each other grows.

As Collins and Shayes dig deeper into the case, they uncover evidence of a massive conspiracy involving corrupt politicians, corporate interests, and murder. The investigation leads them to a mysterious woman named Janine (Robin Wright), who is somehow connected to Spitz's death.

Throughout the movie, Collins and Shayes face numerous obstacles and challenges as they try to expose the truth behind Spitz's death. They are pursued by powerful forces, including corrupt politicians and corporate interests, who will stop at nothing to silence them.

As the investigation unfolds, Collins becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth, while Shayes begins to question his own motivations and loyalties. The two men's relationship is put to the test as they work together to expose the conspiracy.

In the end, Collins and Shayes finally uncover the truth behind Spitz's death, which leads them to a shocking revelation about Janine's connection to the conspiracy. The movie ends with Collins and Shayes reflecting on the cost of their investigation and the sacrifices they made in pursuit of the truth.

Overall, State of Play is a gripping thriller that explores themes of corruption, power, and the importance of investigative journalism. The movie features strong performances from its leads, particularly Crowe and Affleck, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

overview: The spirited Boruto Uzumaki, son of Seventh Hokage Naruto, is a skilled ninja who possesses the same brashness and passion his father once had. However, the constant absence of his father, who is busy with his Hokage duties, puts a damper on Boruto's fire. He ends up meeting his father's friend Sasuke, and requests to become... his apprentice!? The curtain on the story of the new generation rises!
tagline: Forge your own path.
title: Boruto: Naruto the Movie
plot:
Boruto: Naruto the Movie is a Japanese animated martial-arts fantasy released in 2015, marking Hiroyuki Yamashita's debut as a director. Based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto franchise, it is the second film in the series' canonical storyline and a sequel to the manga. Yūko Sanpei voices Boruto Uzumaki and Junko Takeuchi his father, Naruto, with Kokoro Kikuchi and Noriaki Sugiyama also starring.

Fifteen years after the Fourth Great Ninja War and Naruto's final duel with Sasuke Uchiha, the village of Konohagakure is prospering under Naruto as the Seventh Hokage. Married to Hinata, he has two children, Boruto and Himawari. Boruto has joined a ninja team with Sarada, the daughter of Sasuke and Sakura, and the enigmatic Mitsuki, under their teacher Konohamaru, but he resents his father for putting his duties ahead of his family. When Naruto misses Himawari's birthday, an angry Boruto asks Sasuke to train him so he can surpass his father. Sasuke agrees on the condition that Boruto masters the Rasengan, which he learns from Konohamaru, but struggling to perfect it, Boruto turns to a Scientific Ninja Tool given to him by Katasuke, an arrogant scientist.

Boruto uses the device to cheat his way through the Chunin Exams. Naruto sees through it at once and disqualifies his son in public, and Boruto's bitter outburst makes Naruto recognise his own failings. The moment is shattered by the arrival of Momoshiki and Kinshiki Ōtsutsuki, who want the Nine-Tailed Fox Kurama, sealed within Naruto, to create a chakra fruit that will make them immortal. Naruto shields Boruto and the crowd and is taken captive. Learning he is alive, Sasuke and the other Kage set out to rescue him, and Boruto, now understanding his father's role, insists on joining them. After Naruto is freed, father and son acknowledge their mistakes. Momoshiki devours his partner to grow stronger, and when Katasuke's meddling accidentally revives him, Naruto lends Boruto his chakra to create a giant Rasengan that destroys the enemy. Afterwards, Boruto resolves to follow Sasuke's path as a protector working from the shadows while supporting Sarada's dream of becoming Hokage; Mitsuki reveals he is the son of Orochimaru.

Released on August 7, 2015, the film earned ¥2.62 billion in Japan, becoming the highest-grossing Naruto film, and was well received; Anime News Network graded it "A−", and critics praised its fight animation.

original_title: How to Train Your Dragon: Snoggletog Log
overview: When Hiccup and Toothless begin sharing stories of their special relationship with their respective families as they prepare for the Snoggletog Festival, it quickly becomes clear that the new generation of Vikings don’t remember the bond between dragon and human.
title: How to Train Your Dragon: Snoggletog Log
plot: When Hiccup and Toothless begin sharing stories of their special relationship with their respective families as they prepare for the Snoggletog Festival, it quickly becomes clear that the new generation of Vikings don’t remember the bond between dragon and human.

overview: Diane is a mysterious and lonely teenager. Sharing special bonds with her father Christian, she takes care of the education of her brother Marc. The arrival of Julia in the neighborhood, a charismatic and liberated young British woman, is going to disturb Diane’s daily life.  Desperately willing to become an adult, Diane is going to live, for a semester, the most shattering experiences of her life. The more she gets close to Julia, the more she gets irresponsible, ignoring consequences and limits to her desires.
tagline: There are times we need to try everything
title: Puppylove
plot:
Puppylove is a 2013 coming-of-age drama directed by Delphine Lehericey, who wrote it with Martin Coiffier. An international co-production of Belgium, France, Luxembourg and Switzerland, it stars Solène Rigot as Diane, a 14-year-old girl, Audrey Bastien as her new neighbor Julia, and Vincent Pérez as Diane's father Christian, with Vadim Goldberg as her younger brother Marc and Theo Gladsteen as her friend Antoine.

Diane lives with her father, a well-meaning but somewhat distracted single parent, and her little brother. Curious and impatient to grow up, she is preoccupied with the idea of sexuality, though her first tentative attempt at intimacy with her shy friend Antoine ends in awkwardness. At school, her friends talk endlessly about losing their virginity, while at home her relationship with her father is marked by tension and unspoken boundaries.

Her life changes when Julia, a confident and provocative girl, moves in next door with her strict parents. Julia seeks Diane out, and the two quickly become close friends. Fascinated by Julia's boldness, Diane follows her into increasingly risky situations with older boys and men at parties, in cars and on a holiday with Julia's family, often watching from the sidelines and discovering both the thrill and the danger of the adult world. As the friendship deepens into an intense and ambiguous attachment, Diane's behavior strains her bond with Antoine and with her father, who struggles to understand his daughter and to set limits. Julia's influence eventually pushes the friendship, and Diane's family, toward a crisis that forces Diane to reconsider who she is.

The film is an unsentimental portrait of female adolescence, curiosity and peer influence, and of the confusion of a girl growing up with a single father.

Puppylove premiered at the San Sebastián International Film Festival and was released in Belgium on 7 May 2014. It won the Magritte Award for Best Original Score. Critical reaction was divided; The Hollywood Reporter's Jonathan Holland described it as an intriguing but misguided film, more a forum for debate than a fully achieved work, and unsettling in ways it may not itself understand.

overview: A woman's life is thrown into chaos after a freak car accident sends her husband and brother-in-law into comas. Thrills arrive after the brother-in-law wakes up, thinking he's his brother.
tagline: What if the person you loved became someone else?
title: Possession
plot:
Possession is a 2009 American psychological thriller directed by Joel Bergvall and Simon Sandquist, a remake of the 2002 South Korean film Addicted. It stars Sarah Michelle Gellar as Jess, a San Francisco lawyer, Lee Pace as her troubled brother-in-law Roman and Michael Landes as her husband Ryan, with Tuva Novotny as Roman's girlfriend Casey, Chelah Horsdal and William B. Davis. The film was shot in Vancouver from October 2006 under the working title Addicted.

Jess is a driven attorney who often puts her career ahead of her marriage to Ryan, a gentle artist. As they approach their first anniversary, the one source of friction in their happy life is Ryan's younger brother Roman, a moody, violent man whom Jess first met when she defended him on an assault charge and of whom she is deeply afraid. When Roman overhears the couple discussing sending him to a halfway house, he storms off in his car, and Ryan rushes after him. The brothers' cars collide on the Golden Gate Bridge, and both men fall into comas.

Weeks later, Roman wakes up and insists that he is actually Ryan, claiming that something inexplicable happened when the two were revived side by side and that his brother's soul now inhabits his body. Jess is at first hostile and convinced that he is confused by brain damage, but Roman keeps offering romantic gestures and recalling intimate memories only her husband could know. Gradually she comes to believe him, and despite the disapproval of her colleagues and Casey, she resumes her married life with the man in Roman's body and becomes pregnant. Yet small inconsistencies begin to surface, and when Casey goes missing and Jess finds that her private letters and photographs have been tampered with, she must face the terrifying possibility that she has been deceived.

The film explores grief, desire and identity, playing on the question of whether love can recognize a person beyond their physical form.

Because of financial problems at its distributor Yari Film Group, which filed for bankruptcy, the film's U.S. release was postponed repeatedly. It was released in theaters in several territories in South America, Europe and Asia between 2009 and 2011, and went straight to DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on March 9, 2010.

original_title: The Jack in the Box: Awakening
overview: When a vintage Jack-in-the-box is opened by a dying woman, she enters into a deal with the demon within that would see her illness cured in return for helping it claim six innocent victims.
tagline: Once you open the box... you can't escape it.
title: The Jack in the Box: Awakening
plot:
The Jack in the Box: Awakening is a 2022 British supernatural horror film written and directed by Lawrence Fowler and produced by Fowler Media. A thematic sequel to Fowler's The Jack in the Box (2019), it shares none of that film's characters or story, with the demon in the box as the only connecting figure. It stars Matt McClure as Edgar Marsdale, Mollie Hindle as Amy, Nicola Wright as Olga Marsdale and James Swanton as the demon Jack, with Michaela Longden as Janet, Jason Farries as Frank and Victor Mellors as Mr Huxley. The film carries the tagline "Once you open the box... you can't escape it."

Olga Marsdale, a wealthy collector of vintage toys, lies bedridden with terminal bone cancer in her country mansion. Aware of its cursed history, she acquires through the dealer Huxley the oldest jack-in-the-box ever discovered, which is said to contain a demon able to grant a wish in exchange for six sacrifices. She rearranges the revolving letters on its top from "JACK" to "LIFE" and turns the crank, and the dial shows that six lives will be needed for her cure. Huxley becomes the first victim, mauled by a three-clawed demonic clown and pulled into the box, which slams shut as the dial counts the death. Olga browbeats her timid son Edgar, who serves as her factotum, into gathering five more sacrifices, and, horrified yet strangely captivated, he overcomes his squeamishness out of desperation to save his mother. Amy, a young woman recently separated from her boyfriend, has just taken a job as the estate's new housemaid hoping for a fresh start, and with fellow staff members Janet and the chef Frank she finds herself confined within the estate's high walls, with no phone signal, as Edgar feeds one victim after another to the box.

The film was released on digital platforms in the United Kingdom on 3 January 2022 and in the United States later that month, and on DVD through 4Digital Media. Reviews were mixed. Phil Hoad of The Guardian found it too beholden to The Conjuring, noting an atmospheric English gothic strain and a disturbing oedipal mother-son relationship but criticizing rote killings and thin supporting characters. HorrorBuzz praised McClure's rounded performance, Longden and Cameron Bryson's camerawork, while finding it formulaic and wishing for more of Olga and Edgar's relationship. Road Rash Reviews gave it three stars, calling it a solid, creepy and well-made clown horror with impressive monster effects despite a few plot holes.

overview: A group of delinquents are sent to clean the Blackwell Hotel but little do they know reclusive psychopath Jacob Goodnight has holed away in the rotting hotel. When one of the teens is captured, those who remain band together to survive against the brutal killer.
tagline: Evil Gets Raw
title: See No Evil
plot:
See No Evil is a supernatural horror film that revolves around the story of a blind man named Bob, who seeks revenge against the people who brutally murdered his girlfriend. The movie delves into the theme of revenge and its consequences, exploring how it can consume and destroy those who seek it.

The film also touches on the idea of perception and reality, as Bob's blindness serves as a metaphor for the way we perceive the world around us. His inability to see forces him to rely on his other senses, which in turn heightens his sensitivity to the world. This theme is further emphasized through the character of Shosanna, who becomes embroiled in Bob's quest for revenge and begins to question her own perceptions of reality.

The movie also explores the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Bob's past experiences have left him with a deep-seated desire for revenge, which threatens to consume him. As he navigates his way through the story, he is forced to confront the traumas of his past and consider whether his quest for revenge is truly worth the cost.

Overall, See No Evil is a film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, delving into themes of revenge, perception, trauma, and the consequences of our actions.

overview: A single mother, plagued by the violent death of her husband, battles with her son's fear of a monster lurking in the house, but soon discovers a sinister presence all around her.
tagline: If it's in a word, or it's in a look, you can't get rid of the Babadook.
title: The Babadook
plot:
The Babadook is a psychological horror film written and directed by Jennifer Kent, released in 2014. The movie follows the story of Amelia (Essie Davis), a widowed mother who struggles to cope with the loss of her husband, Tom (Noah Wiseman), in a car accident.

Amelia's son, Samuel (Noah Wiseman), is a shy and introverted six-year-old boy who has difficulty adjusting to his new life without his father. As Amelia tries to navigate her grief and care for her son, she begins to experience strange and terrifying events that suggest the presence of a supernatural entity known as the Babadook.

The Babadook is a monster from children's books that comes to life when read aloud. In this case, it appears in Samuel's room, manifesting as a dark figure with a menacing presence. As the story progresses, Amelia becomes increasingly unhinged and paranoid, convinced that the Babadook is a manifestation of her own guilt and grief.

As the events escalate, Amelia's relationship with Samuel deteriorates, and she begins to question her own sanity. The line between reality and fantasy blurs, and Amelia starts to see the world through the eyes of her son. She becomes obsessed with understanding the Babadook and its connection to their family's tragedy.

The film takes a dark and unexpected turn when Amelia discovers that Samuel has been reading the Babadook book repeatedly, which seems to be fueling the monster's presence. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Samuel has been using his imagination to cope with his father's absence, and the Babadook represents his own grief and fear.

In the climactic final act, Amelia confronts her own demons and the Babadook, leading to a tragic and devastating conclusion. The film ends with Amelia, now fully embracing her grief, reading the Babadook book to Samuel, who has seemingly accepted the monster as a part of their reality.

Throughout the movie, Jennifer Kent explores themes of grief, trauma, and mental illness, raising questions about the nature of reality and the power of imagination. The Babadook is a masterclass in psychological horror, building tension through its slow-burning atmosphere and unsettling imagery.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and original storytelling. Essie Davis's portrayal of Amelia earned her numerous awards and nominations, including the AACTA Award for Best Actress.

overview: After 16-year-old Alice Palmer drowns in a local dam, her family experiences a series of strange, inexplicable events centred in and around their home. Unsettled, the Palmers seek the help of psychic and parapsychologist, who discovers that Alice led a secret, double life. At Lake Mungo, Alice's secret past emerges.
tagline: If you've never seen a ghost... Look closer.
title: Lake Mungo
plot:
Lake Mungo is a 2009 Australian drama film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the human psyche. The story revolves around the mysterious death of a young girl named Alice Palmer, whose body is found in a lake near her home.

At its core, Lake Mungo explores the theme of collective trauma and how it can affect an entire community. The film masterfully weaves together multiple narratives, each one shedding light on the dark secrets and unresolved emotions that have been buried beneath the surface of Alice's family and friends.

One of the primary concerns of the movie is the way in which trauma can be passed down through generations, influencing the lives of those who are left behind. The film suggests that the traumatic event that occurred at Lake Mungo has had a profound impact on the community, causing people to become withdrawn, isolated, and even violent.

The movie also delves into the theme of grief and its various forms. Alice's death serves as a catalyst for her family and friends to confront their own emotions and come to terms with their loss. However, this process is fraught with difficulty, as each character struggles to cope with their own unique brand of grief.

Furthermore, Lake Mungo touches on the idea of identity and how it can be shaped by our experiences, particularly those that are traumatic. The film's protagonist, Sarah, grapples with her own sense of self-worth and purpose in life, as she tries to make sense of Alice's death and its impact on her family.

Throughout the movie, the director, Joel Anderson, employs a non-linear narrative structure, which adds to the sense of disorientation and confusion that pervades the story. This mirrors the way in which trauma can disrupt our perceptions of reality, leaving us feeling lost and uncertain about what is real and what is not.

Ultimately, Lake Mungo is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that sheds light on the complexities of grief, trauma, and identity. The film's thought-provoking themes and atmospheric tension make it a haunting and unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: The story of a woman who is slowly losing her sight whilst trying to investigate the mysterious death of her twin sister.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
Generalitat de Catalunya - Institut Català de les Indústries Culturals (ICIC)
tagline: You can't hide in the dark
title: Julia's Eyes
plot:
Julia's Eyes (Spanish: Los ojos de Julia) is a 2010 Spanish psychological horror thriller film directed by Guillem Morales and written by Morales and Oriol Paulo. Belén Rueda stars in the dual role of Julia and her twin sister, Sara, with Lluís Homar as Julia's husband, Isaac, Pablo Derqui, Joan Dalmau and Clara Segura. The film was produced by Guillermo del Toro, Joaquín Padró and Mar Targarona.

In the opening scene, Sara, a blind woman tormented by an unseen presence, prepares to hang herself in her basement but changes her mind; as she tries to remove the noose, the stool is kicked away from beneath her. Far away, Julia, who suffers from the same degenerative eye disease as her sister but can still see, collapses, sensing that something is wrong. Refusing to believe that Sara killed herself, particularly since she had been awaiting surgery that might restore her sight, Julia begins to investigate, despite the objections of Isaac, who has learned from a doctor that Sara's operation had failed.

Julia meets Sara's blind elderly neighbor, Soledad, who predicts that Isaac will leave her, just as Soledad's own son abandoned her after she lost her sight. Learning that Sara had a mysterious boyfriend, Julia follows the trail to a nearby hotel, where an elderly janitor warns her of people who live in the shadows and are so ignored that they become invisible. Soon after, Isaac vanishes, and Julia becomes convinced that the same unseen figure who stalked Sara has taken him, though the police are skeptical. As witnesses connected to the case begin to die, Julia's eyesight deteriorates rapidly under the stress, forcing her to undergo an operation of her own.
