The film combines romantic comedy and action with ideas about artificial intelligence, free will and the meaning of a life lived by someone else's script, along with satire of gaming culture and franchise-driven entertainment.

Delayed repeatedly by the COVID-19 pandemic, Free Guy was released by 20th Century Studios on August 13, 2021. It grossed 331.5 million dollars worldwide and received positive reviews, with 80 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62. It was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects.

overview: Two thieving teenage brothers, stealing money to help their sick mom, match wits with a troubled security guard stuck at the bottom of a forgotten well.
tagline: Some secrets should stay buried.
title: Don't Tell a Soul
plot:
Don't Tell a Soul is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Rob McKittrick. The movie revolves around a family's dark secrets and the consequences of keeping them hidden.

The main theme of Don't Tell a Soul explores the idea of toxic masculinity and the destructive nature of patriarchal expectations. The character of Jack (played by Michael B. Jordan) is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities and the societal pressures that have shaped him into a man who prioritizes strength over emotional expression.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the family's secrets are rooted in a deep-seated fear of vulnerability and a desperate attempt to maintain control. The film highlights how this toxic dynamic can lead to devastating consequences for those involved, particularly women and children.

The movie also touches on themes of trauma, grief, and the cyclical nature of violence. It suggests that unresolved trauma can be passed down through generations, causing harm to those who are closest to us. Through Jack's character, the film explores the idea that true strength lies not in suppressing emotions, but in confronting and working through them.

Overall, Don't Tell a Soul is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of keeping secrets and perpetuating toxic relationships.

overview: In the days following the surrender of Germany in May 1945, a group of young German prisoners of war is handed over to the Danish authorities and subsequently sent to the West Coast, where they are ordered to remove the more than two million mines that the Germans had placed in the sand along the coast. With their bare hands, crawling around in the sand, the boys are forced to perform the dangerous work under the leadership of a Danish sergeant.
tagline: They survived the second World War, now they must survive the cleanup
title: Land of Mine
plot:
Land of Mine is a powerful and emotional drama that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of war and its aftermath. The film tells the story of two young German soldiers, Daniel and Seitz, who are forced to clear a beach of landmines as part of their punishment for being POWs.

At its core, Land of Mine is a movie about the struggle to find humanity in the face of unimaginable trauma and violence. The characters are grappling with the moral implications of their actions during the war, and the film raises important questions about guilt, redemption, and the search for meaning in a world that has been ravaged by conflict.

Through Daniel's character, in particular, the film explores the theme of anger and resentment, as he struggles to come to terms with his past and find a way to move forward. His relationship with Seitz serves as a catalyst for this exploration, forcing him to confront the consequences of his actions and the impact they have had on others.

The film also touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness, highlighting the emotional toll that war can take on individuals. Daniel's character is a prime example of this, as he struggles to form connections with those around him, including Seitz, who becomes a source of comfort and support in his life.

Ultimately, Land of Mine is a movie about hope and resilience in the face of adversity. Despite the bleakness and darkness of the subject matter, the film offers a message of redemption and the possibility of healing and growth, even in the most difficult of circumstances.

belongs_to_collection.name: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes Collection

overview: Suspicion is on high after Batman, Batgirl, Robin and other DC superheroes receive mysterious invitations. However, family values must remain strong when Batman and his team encounter the villainous Red Hood, who is obsessed with destroying the Bat-family and all of Gotham City.
title: Lego DC Batman: Family Matters
plot:
Lego DC Batman: Family Matters is an animated film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and relationships through the lens of the iconic superhero, Batman. The movie delves into the idea of what it means to be a good parent and how one's actions can have far-reaching consequences on those they care about.

At its core, the film is a heartwarming exploration of the importance of family bonds and the sacrifices that must be made for the greater good. Batman's struggles to balance his duties as a crime-fighter with his responsibilities as a father are expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the character.

The movie also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery, particularly in the context of Bruce Wayne's dual life as Batman and his role as a father. As he navigates the challenges of being a superhero and a parent, Bruce must confront the consequences of his choices and learn to prioritize what truly matters.

Furthermore, Lego DC Batman: Family Matters features a richly developed cast of characters, each with their own distinct personalities and motivations. The film's portrayal of these characters adds richness and depth to the narrative, making it easy for audiences to become invested in their stories and relationships.

Overall, the main themes of Lego DC Batman: Family Matters revolve around the complexities of family dynamics, the importance of self-sacrifice, and the challenges of balancing personal and professional responsibilities.

overview: In a quiet suburban town in the summer of 1958, two recently orphaned sisters are placed in the care of their mentally unstable Aunt Ruth. But Ruth's depraved sense of discipline will soon lead to unspeakable acts of abuse and torture that involve her young sons, the neighborhood children, and one 12-year-old boy whose life will be changed forever.
tagline: In this town, murder became the neighborhood game.
title: The Girl Next Door
plot:
The Girl Next Door, also released as Jack Ketchum's Evil, is a 2007 American psychological horror film directed by Gregory M. Wilson from a screenplay by Daniel Farrands and Philip Nutman, based on Jack Ketchum's 1989 novel. The novel was inspired by the real-life torture and murder of Sylvia Likens, and the film is dedicated to her. It stars Blythe Auffarth as Meg Loughlin, Blanche Baker as Ruth Chandler and Daniel Manche as the young David Moran.

In the present day, David, now an adult, witnesses a man struck by a car in New York and tries to save him, an event that brings back memories of the summer of 1958. That summer, as a boy, he meets and falls for Meg, a teenager who, with her disabled younger sister Susan, has come to live with their aunt Ruth and her sons, Willie, Ralphie and Donny, after their parents died in a car crash.

Ruth is popular with the neighborhood children, letting them drink beer and smoke in her house, but she treats Meg with growing cruelty, starving her, berating her and punishing her sister in front of her. When Meg reports the abuse to a local police officer, nothing is done, and Ruth's punishment becomes even more brutal. Meg is tied up in the basement, where Ruth, her sons and the neighborhood children begin to torture her, treating the abuse as entertainment. David, torn between fear, complicity and his feelings for Meg, is unable to tell his parents what is happening. As the violence escalates, he must find the courage to help Meg and Susan escape before it is too late.

The film is an unflinching depiction of child abuse and the way group cruelty and silence enable it, focusing on the moral failure of the bystanders as much as on the abusers.

The film received mixed reviews, with a 67 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 29. The New York Times was harshly critical, while Stephen King praised it as the first authentically shocking American film he had seen since Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer, warning that viewers who are easily disturbed should not watch it.

original_title: The Girl with All the Gifts
overview: In the future, a strange fungus has changed nearly everyone into a thoughtless, flesh-eating monster. When a scientist and a teacher find a girl who seems to be immune to the fungus, they all begin a journey to save humanity.
tagline: Our greatest threat is our only hope.
title: The Girl with All the Gifts
plot:
The Girl with All the Gifts is a 2016 British post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Colm McCarthy, based on the novel of the same name by M.R. Carey.

In a world devastated by a zombie-like fungal infection that turns humans into mindless, violent creatures, a young girl named Melanie (Dakota Buddie) lives in an underground bunker with a small group of survivors. The fungus, known as Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, has wiped out most of humanity and turned the remaining survivors into "Hungries," aggressive and zombie-like creatures that roam the earth.

Melanie is unique among the survivors because she appears to be immune to the infection. She is also incredibly intelligent and possesses a deep understanding of the fungus and its behavior. Melanie's existence is a mystery, even to herself, as she struggles to understand her own nature and purpose.

The story begins with Melanie being taken from the bunker by a scientist named Dr. Caldwell (Gugu Mbatha-Raw), who believes that Melanie may hold the key to finding a cure for the fungus. As they journey through the post-apocalyptic world, they encounter various groups of survivors, some of whom are hostile towards them.

Along the way, Melanie begins to exhibit strange behavior, including an intense desire to infect others with the fungus. Dr. Caldwell is unsure what to make of this behavior and is torn between his scientific curiosity and his growing concern for Melanie's well-being.

As they near their destination, a supposed safe haven called "Ark," Melanie's behavior becomes increasingly erratic. She begins to experience vivid hallucinations and visions, which seem to be connected to the fungus. It becomes clear that Melanie is not just immune to the infection, but may actually be a host for the fungus.

In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Melanie has been infected with the fungus from birth, and her unique behavior is a result of the fungus's influence on her mind. The fungus has been manipulating Melanie's thoughts and actions, using her as a vessel to spread its own kind.

As Dr. Caldwell and his team prepare to enter the Ark, they are met with resistance from the infected survivors. In a tense confrontation, Melanie is forced to confront her true nature and the reality of her existence. In a final act of self-sacrifice, Melanie deliberately infects herself with the fungus, allowing it to spread and potentially find a cure.

The film ends with Dr. Caldwell and his team entering the Ark, hopeful that they may have finally found a way to stop the fungal infection and restore humanity to its former glory. However, as they look out upon the desolate landscape, it is clear that the true extent of Melanie's sacrifice remains unknown, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of her actions.

Overall, The Girl with All the Gifts is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the nature of existence. With its unique blend of science fiction and horror elements, it has become a modern classic in the post-apocalyptic genre.

overview: Wrongfully accused and on the run, a top MI6 assassin joins forces with his long-lost, football hooligan brother to save the world from a sinister plot.
tagline: Behind every hero is an embarrassing sibling
title: Grimsby
plot:
Grimsby, released in the United States and Canada as The Brothers Grimsby, is a 2016 spy action comedy directed by Louis Leterrier and written by Sacha Baron Cohen, Phil Johnston and Peter Baynham. Baron Cohen plays Nobby Butcher, a football hooligan from Grimsby, and Mark Strong his long-lost younger brother Sebastian Graves, MI6's top agent. Isla Fisher, Rebel Wilson, Penélope Cruz, Gabourey Sidibe, Annabelle Wallis and Ian McShane co-star.

Nobby and Sebastian were separated as children 28 years earlier. Nobby has become an alcoholic football hooligan who lives in Grimsby with his partner Dawn and their eleven children, while Sebastian, raised under another name, is an elite spy. Sebastian is sent to protect the philanthropist Rhonda George at a charity event called WorldCure. Tipped off by his friends, Nobby turns up to reunite with his brother and hugs him just as Sebastian is about to shoot an assassin, ruining the shot; an innocent bystander is hit instead. Branded a rogue agent and pursued by MI6's hitman Chilcott, Sebastian reluctantly hides out with Nobby in Grimsby.

When Chilcott's men find them in a pub, Sebastian is hit by poison darts, and Nobby saves him by sucking out the poison. Following a lead from his handler, Jodie, the brothers travel to a lodge in South Africa, where Nobby, attempting to impersonate his brother, mistakes the hotel maid Banu for his target, and the brothers learn from Lina Smit that the assassin has bought a virus shortly before she is shot dead. Fleeing Chilcott's men, they hide inside an elephant in one of its crudest gags. Afterwards Nobby explains that he ran away as a boy because Sebastian's adoptive parents could take only one child, and he wanted his brother to have a better life.

At the football cup final in Chile between England and Germany, Sebastian is captured, and Rhonda reveals herself as the mastermind, planning to spread the virus over the crowd with fireworks. Nobby rescues his brother, Chilcott is stopped by Nobby's children, and when his gun jams, Nobby sits on one of the virus-laden fireworks to contain it, with Sebastian joining him on the other. The blast knocks both unconscious, Rhonda is arrested, and the news reports that the brothers saved the world.

Delayed several times in the United States, the film grossed only $28 million worldwide against a $35 million budget. Critics were largely negative, with 37% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: During the last years of Pinochet's military regime,  a group of militants from the "Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front" plan a prison break of political prisoners, through a tunnel that will take them 18 months to dig.
tagline: Based on the most daring prison escape of all time.
title: Pacto de Fuga
plot:
Jailbreak Pact, released in Chile as Pacto de fuga, is a 2020 Chilean prison drama and thriller directed by David Albala in his feature debut, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Cecilia Ruz, Loreto Caro-Valdés and Susana Quiroz-Saavedra. It stars Benjamín Vicuña as León Vargas and Roberto Farías as Rafael Jiménez, with Francisca Gavilán, Amparo Noguera, Víctor Montero, Diego Ruiz, Mateo Iribarren and Willy Semler. The film is inspired by "Operation Success", the escape of 49 inmates from the Santiago Public Jail on January 30, 1990, among them members of the Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front (FPMR) serving sentences for armed actions against the military dictatorship.

In the final years of Augusto Pinochet's regime, new political prisoners arrive at the Santiago jail. Vargas and Jiménez try to secure neighboring cells so they can communicate, but Vargas arrives late to the assignment, creating friction over the plans they brought with them. Meanwhile the ad hoc prosecutor Andrade and the warden receive Fabiola Pizarro, a defense lawyer from the group CODEPU who has come to check on the prisoners' conditions. The conspirators calculate that a tunnel would require removing some 50 tons of earth, so they open a hole in a cell ceiling to hide the soil, cover it with a fake section of wall painted to match, and devise secret signals to coordinate the work while evading guards and ordinary prisoners. Outside, Jiménez's former wife, Paulina Baeza, organizes logistical support from FPMR and Communist Party contacts for the day of the escape.

Over more than a year, 24 prisoners dig a tunnel over 80 meters long, using little more than a screwdriver, and hide 55 tons of earth inside the prison, while family visits expose the strain between revolutionary commitment and broken relationships, and the military justice system and the regime's security agencies wield power over the prison. Undetected to the end, the plan frees 49 inmates in one of the most astonishing jailbreaks in Chilean history.

Shot in former prisons in La Serena and Buin, the film was advised by Raúl Blanchet, one of the real escapees, who died during post-production. Its October 2019 release was postponed by Chile's social unrest, and it opened on January 23, 2020. It was shortlisted for Chile's Academy Award submission. The Guardian praised the lead performances but found the dialogue forced, while still calling it an entertaining debut.

overview: Shattered illusions are hard to repair -- especially for a good-hearted zebra named Stripes who's spent his life on a Kentucky farm amidst the sorely mistaken notion that he's a debonair thoroughbred. Once he faces the fact that his stark stripes mark him as different, he decides he'll race anyway. And with help from the young girl who raised him, he just might end up in the winner's circle.
tagline: Cheer 'til you're horse!
title: Racing Stripes
plot:
Racing Stripes is a 2005 live-action/CGI comedy film directed by Ben Stiller. The movie follows the story of Stripes, a wild zebra who dreams of becoming a racing horse.

The main theme of Racing Stripes revolves around self-discovery and acceptance. Stripes, being a zebra, faces ridicule and rejection from the horse community due to his unusual appearance. However, with the help of his human friend, Cale, he learns to embrace his uniqueness and find his place in the world.

Another significant theme present in the movie is friendship and loyalty. Stripes forms strong bonds with Cale and other horses, who eventually accept him for who he is. This theme highlights the importance of acceptance and inclusivity.

Additionally, the film touches on the idea of perseverance and believing in oneself. Stripes faces numerous challenges as he tries to become a racing horse, but he never gives up on his dreams. His determination ultimately leads to his success, both on and off the track.

Overall, Racing Stripes is a heartwarming story about embracing one's individuality, forming meaningful relationships, and staying true to oneself.

original_title: Qu'est-ce qu'on a fait au Bon Dieu ?
overview: A catholic French couple sees their life upside down when their four daughters get married to men of different religion and origins.
tagline: 4 marriages, 2 long-faces
title: Serial (Bad) Weddings
plot:
Serial (Bad) Weddings is a 2014 Indian satirical comedy film directed by Shubhankar Bharali and produced by UGC (Utsav Movie Channel). The movie revolves around the story of Raju, a young man who gets married to a woman named Priya, but their wedding ceremony turns out to be a disaster.

The main themes of Serial (Bad) Weddings include:

1. Satire on Indian Wedding Culture: The film pokes fun at the extravagant and often chaotic nature of Indian weddings, highlighting the absurdity and commercialization of these events.
2. Social Commentary on Class Differences: The movie explores the class divide in India, particularly between the wealthy and the poor, and how it affects relationships and social interactions.
3. Critique of Materialism: Raju's obsession with material possessions and his desire to impress Priya's family serve as a commentary on the excesses of modern Indian society.
4. Exploration of Marriage and Relationships: The film delves into the complexities of marriage and relationships, highlighting the challenges and expectations that come with them.

Overall, Serial (Bad) Weddings is a satirical comedy that uses humor to critique various aspects of Indian society, making it an entertaining and thought-provoking watch.

overview: Alice Lantins is 38, ambitious and so committed to her work that she neglects her personal life.  In short, she is the ideal candidate for the next editor of the magazine Rebelle, or would be were it not for the fact that she appears to be stuck in a rut.  When Balthazar, a charming 20-year-old, crosses her path, her colleagues begin to see her in a whole new light...
title: It Boy
plot:
It Boy (20 ans d'écart) is a 2013 French romantic comedy co-written and directed by David Moreau, from an original idea by his co-writer Amro Hamzawi. Produced by Abel Nahmias for EuropaCorp with Echo Films, it stars Virginie Efira and Pierre Niney, with Charles Berling, Gilles Cohen, Amélie Glenn, Camille Japy, Michaël Abiteboul and Louis-Do de Lencquesaing in supporting roles.

Alice Lantins (Efira), 38, is a capable and ambitious journalist at the fashion magazine Rebelle and the obvious candidate to become its next editor-in-chief, except that her boss, Vincent Khan (Cohen), sees her as uptight and old-fashioned. Returning from a trip to Brazil, she sits next to Balthazar (Niney), an architecture student of about twenty who has landed in business class by chance. He finds a USB stick she dropped and, when she picks him up to retrieve it, he puts a helmet on her before giving her a ride on his pink scooter. Two colleagues snap a photo of the moment and post it online, and overnight Alice's image is transformed. Realizing that her boss suddenly sees her as daring, she decides to fake a romance with the younger man to secure the promotion.

Alice adopts a bolder style, visits Balthazar at university and goes out with him, and the pretense slowly turns into real feelings, leading to a passionate night together. Unable to tell him that she first approached him for her career, and afraid that he will one day find her too old, she breaks off the relationship, leaving him heartbroken while Vincent celebrates the "new Alice". When the head of the magazine group wants Balthazar for a photo shoot, he learns how Alice used him and confronts her in front of the whole team, and Vincent fires her for the deception. Alone, Alice revisits the places they shared and finally addresses Balthazar in a university lecture hall, admitting her mistakes and asking for a fresh start. They reunite, and she returns to her old dream of writing.

The film premiered at the Alpe d'Huez comedy festival in January 2013 and opened in France and Belgium on 6 March 2013. Critics welcomed it as a lively, well-written romantic comedy, with Première praising the charm of its two leads despite a predictable story. Niney won the Swann d'Or for best actor at the Cabourg Film Festival.

overview: When a huge hurricane hits her hometown in Florida, Haley ignores evacuation orders to look for her father. After finding him badly wounded, both are trapped by the flood. With virtually no time to escape the storm, they discover that rising water levels are the least of their problems.
tagline: They were here first
title: Crawl
plot:
Crawl is a 2019 American natural horror film directed by Alexandre Aja, who produced it with Sam Raimi and Craig Flores. It stars Kaya Scodelario as Haley Keller, a University of Florida swimmer, and Barry Pepper as her father Dave, who are trapped with the family dog in the crawl space of their home by alligators during a Category 5 hurricane. Morfydd Clark plays Haley's sister Beth and Ross Anderson a state trooper, Wayne. Aja reworked a spec script by brothers Michael and Shawn Rasmussen, and the film was shot largely in a warehouse at the Port of Belgrade, Serbia, over 41 days in 2018.

As a massive hurricane approaches Florida, Haley ignores her sister's advice to leave the state and goes looking for her estranged father. Finding only his dog, Sugar, at his condo, she defies evacuation orders and drives to the family's old house in Coral Lake, an area at risk of flooding. In the crawl space beneath the house she finds Dave, badly mauled but alive. A huge alligator blocks their way out, forcing them into a corner it cannot reach, and when Haley tries to retrieve her dropped phone, a second gator crushes it and injures her leg. Through gaps in the wall she sees three looters at a nearby gas station devoured in the rising water. Wayne, Beth's ex-boyfriend, arrives with his partner Pete to search for them, but Pete is torn apart outside and Wayne is dragged into the crawl space and killed.

With the water rising, Haley swims to a storm drain, where she finds the alligators' nest, kills one with Wayne's gun and escapes into the flooded street. She breaks through the living room floor with a crowbar to free her father, and they head for a boat as the eye of the storm passes, but a levee breach floods the neighborhood and drives them back into the house. Dave loses his forearm to an alligator, and Haley calls for help on a floating police radio, traps one gator in a shower stall and fights off another's death roll by stabbing it in the eye with a flare. Reunited on the roof with Dave and Sugar, she lights a flare to signal a rescue helicopter as her father watches proudly.

Released by Paramount Pictures on July 12, 2019, without conventional press screenings, Crawl was a commercial success, grossing $91.7 million worldwide on a budget of $13.5-15 million. Critics praised it as a fast, frightening creature feature carried by Scodelario; Rotten Tomatoes reported 84% approval and Metacritic a score of 60.

overview: A family must use a magical box of Animal Crackers to save a rundown circus from being taken over by their evil uncle Horatio P. Huntington.
production_companies: Beijing Wen Hua Dong Run Investment
tagline: A magical adventure in every bite
title: Animal Crackers
plot:
Animal Crackers is a 2017 animated fantasy comedy directed by Scott Christian Sava and Tony Bancroft, written by Sava and Dean Lorey, and inspired by the animal-shaped cookies and by Sava's graphic novel. Its voice cast includes John Krasinski and Emily Blunt as Owen and Zoe Huntington, Ian McKellen, Danny DeVito, Sylvester Stallone, Patrick Warburton, Raven-Symoné as Binkley, Harvey Fierstein as the fortune-teller Esmeralda, Gilbert Gottfried as Mario Zucchini, Tara Strong as Talia, James Arnold Taylor as Buffalo Bob and Kevin Grevioux as Samson the Strong Man.

In the 1960s, brothers Buffalo Bob and Horatio Huntington run a successful traveling circus, until both fall for Talia, niece of the circus fortune-teller Esmeralda. When Talia chooses Bob, the jealous Horatio breaks with his brother. As a wedding gift, Esmeralda gives the couple a mysterious box, which allows them to open a new circus famous for animals that perform seemingly impossible feats. Years later, Bob's nephew Owen marries his childhood sweetheart Zoe at the circus, but to please her father, Mr. Woodley, he takes a dull job as a taste tester at Woodley's dog biscuit factory.

After Horatio, whose fortunes have collapsed, accidentally causes a fire that seemingly kills Bob and Talia, Owen and Zoe inherit the circus, and Horatio tries to take it from them. The circus pets give the family the mysterious box, which turns out to contain magical animal crackers: whoever eats one turns into the animal it depicts, while a single human-shaped cracker changes them back. Owen discovers that this was the secret of the circus's success, with performers taking turns as animals. Embracing his new life, he must save the circus from Horatio and his henchmen, keep his family together and recover the precious human cracker that will return him to human form.

The film celebrates family, imagination and following one's dreams, set against the colorful backdrop of a traditional circus.

Animal Crackers premiered at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in 2017 and was released in China in 2018, before reaching Netflix in July 2020. It received mixed-to-positive reviews, with 67 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 60.

overview: Three juvenile delinquents arrive at a correctional center and are put under the care of an experienced guard.
tagline: Fighting Back Is The Only Way Out
title: Dog Pound
plot:
Dog Pound is a 2010 Canadian prison drama and psychological thriller directed and co-written by Kim Chapiron. A reworking of the 1979 British borstal film Scum, it moves the story to a juvenile detention center in the United States, and it is the only one of Chapiron's films to go direct to video in some markets. Since its release it has developed a cult following for its raw portrayal of life behind bars.

Three teenagers, Butch, Davis and Angel, arrive at the Enola Vale juvenile detention center in Montana. Butch has been transferred after attacking and blinding a guard at another facility, and the intake officer singles him out from the start. Goodyear, a tough but fair correctional officer, urges the new arrivals to keep their heads down and follow the rules so they can earn a second chance on the outside.

Butch tries at first to conform, but he and his friends are soon targeted by the facility's chief bully, Banks, and his henchmen. Refusing to name his attackers, Butch is thrown into solitary confinement, and when he gets out he takes brutal revenge, establishing his place in the inmate hierarchy and providing temporary protection for Davis and Angel. That fragile balance collapses when a confrontation during a work detail leaves Angel fatally injured, and Butch, a witness, is sent back to solitary during the investigation. Without his protection, Davis falls victim to further abuse and despair. As grief and anger spread through the dormitory, the inmates stage a protest, and Butch's rage finally explodes into a violent uprising that the staff struggle to contain.

The film is a bleak study of institutional violence, showing how a system meant to rehabilitate young offenders instead breeds cruelty, hierarchy and hopelessness.

Dog Pound premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on 24 April 2010 and was released in Canada on 7 September 2010, followed by releases in France, the United States, Spain and the United Kingdom. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 63 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 57; CinemaBlend called it intense and not suited to every viewer.

overview: The story of a drifter named Paul who arrives in a small town seeking revenge on the thugs who murdered his friend. Sisters Mary Anne and Ellen, who run the town's hotel, help Paul in his quest for vengeance.
tagline: A man can only take so much!
title: In a Valley of Violence
plot:
In a Valley of Violence is a 2016 American Western written and directed by Ti West and produced by Jason Blum through Blumhouse Productions. It stars Ethan Hawke as Paul, a drifter and former soldier, John Travolta as U.S. Marshal Clyde Martin, Taissa Farmiga as the young innkeeper Mary-Anne, James Ransone as Clyde's hotheaded son, Deputy Gilly Martin, and Karen Gillan as Mary-Anne's sister Ellen, Gilly's fiancée. The film pays homage to classic revenge Westerns while adding dry, absurdist humor.

In the early 1870s, Paul and his loyal dog Abbie are crossing the desert on their way to Mexico. After fending off a bandit and disgraced clergyman who tries to steal his horse, Paul rides into Denton, a former boomtown on its last legs. In the saloon, the arrogant Gilly picks a fight with him, and Paul knocks him down with a single punch. At the local hotel, Paul meets Mary-Anne, who is delighted that someone stood up to Gilly, while Marshal Clyde Martin, a pragmatic lawman with a wooden leg, admits that his son provoked the fight but orders Paul to leave town by morning.

That night, Gilly and his fellow deputies ambush Paul and Abbie at their camp. Gilly kills the dog, and his men push Paul off a cliff, leaving him for dead. Paul survives, buries Abbie and returns to Denton seeking revenge, breaking his vow never to take another life. As the deputies are picked off one by one, Mary-Anne shelters Paul and begs him to take her away, while Clyde, realizing the full extent of what his son has done, tries to negotiate an end to the bloodshed before it consumes the entire town. Paul, haunted by atrocities he committed during the Indian Wars and by the family he abandoned, must decide how far his vengeance will go.

The film plays with the conventions of the genre, combining stylized violence, a deliberately old-fashioned score and comic exchanges between its characters.

In a Valley of Violence premiered at South by Southwest on March 12, 2016, and was released in limited theaters and on demand by Focus World on October 21. It grossed only about 62,000 dollars in theaters but was well received by critics, earning 78 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 64.

overview: After picking up a traumatized young hitchhiker, five friends find themselves stalked and hunted by a chainsaw-wielding killer and his family of equally psychopathic killers.
tagline: Based on a true story...
title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre
plot:
The Texas Chainsaw Massacre is a 2003 American horror film directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Scott Kosar, based on the 1974 film of the same name by Tobe Hooper. The movie stars Jessica Biel, Jonathan Tucker, Andrew Bryniarski, Eric Balfour, and Erin Daniels.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a young Sally Hardesty (Erin Daniels) being brutally murdered by Leatherface (Andrew Bryniarski), the main antagonist of the film. The scene is presented in a found-footage style, which sets the tone for the rest of the movie.

The present-day narrative follows Erin Harris (Jessica Biel), a college student who has just graduated and is on her way to visit her sister, Sarah (Mike Vogel), in Austin, Texas. Erin's friends, Kirk (Jonathan Tucker) and Pam (Erin Daniels), are also along for the ride. The group decides to take a detour to visit the grave of Sally Hardesty, who was killed by Leatherface many years ago.

As they approach the grave, they notice that it has been recently disturbed, which sets off a chain of events that leads them into the clutches of Leatherface and his family. The group soon discovers that they are lost in rural Texas and that their car has broken down. They decide to seek shelter at an old gas station, where they meet a local named Franklin (Eric Balfour), who claims to be able to fix their car.

However, it becomes clear that Franklin is not what he seems, and the group soon finds themselves being stalked by Leatherface and his family, including his mother, Grandpa, and brother. The group tries to escape, but they are eventually captured and taken to the family's farmhouse, where they are subjected to a series of gruesome and terrifying events.

As the night wears on, Erin and her friends try to find a way to escape, but Leatherface and his family prove to be relentless in their pursuit of them. The group is eventually killed off one by one, with Erin being the last survivor.

In the end, Erin manages to escape from the farmhouse by hiding in a well, where she is rescued by a local sheriff's deputy. As she reflects on her ordeal, it becomes clear that the events at the farmhouse were just a nightmare, and that Erin had been experiencing hallucinations due to stress and fatigue.

The movie ends with Erin driving away from the farmhouse, leaving behind the horrors of the night before. The final shot is of Leatherface's mask, which is left on the ground, serving as a reminder of the terror that Erin experienced.

Overall, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre (2003) is a tense and suspenseful horror film that pays homage to the original 1974 film while also offering a fresh take on the classic story.

original_title: American Pie Presents: The Book of Love
overview: Ten years after the first American Pie movie, three new hapless virgins discover the Bible hidden in the school library at East Great Falls High. Unfortunately for them, the book is ruined, and with incomplete advice, the Bible leads them on a hilarious journey to lose their virginity.
tagline: It's the hottest slice yet!
title: American Pie Presents: The Book of Love
plot:
American Pie Presents: The Book of Love is a 2009 American teen comedy film directed by Jesse Moss and written by Adam Herz, Jon Lucas, and Scott Moore. The movie is the eighth installment in the American Pie franchise.

The story revolves around Jim Levenstein (Eddie Kaye Thomas), who has just been dumped by his girlfriend, Michelle Flaherty (Amanda Crew). Feeling heartbroken, Jim turns to an old high school friend, Kevin (Jason Friedberg), for advice. Kevin suggests that Jim read "The Book of Love," a self-help book written by a mysterious author.

As Jim reads the book, he becomes convinced that it holds the secrets to winning back Michelle and finding true love. The book's advice is based on a series of cryptic messages and codes that Jim must decipher in order to unlock the secrets of love.

Meanwhile, Stifler (Seann William Scott) has become increasingly obsessed with a new girlfriend, who turns out to be a manipulative and controlling woman. As Jim delves deeper into "The Book of Love," he begins to realize that the book's advice is not as straightforward as it seems.

Throughout the movie, Jim's friends, including Finch (Paul Sado), Ozzy (Erik Stolhanske), and Kevin, provide comedic relief and support as Jim navigates his way through the ups and downs of love. Along the way, Jim also encounters a series of eccentric characters who claim to be experts on love and relationships.

As the story unfolds, Jim becomes increasingly obsessed with deciphering the codes in "The Book of Love." He enlists the help of his friends and together, they embark on a series of misadventures as they try to unlock the secrets of true love.

In the end, Jim's journey leads him to a surprising revelation about Michelle and himself. The movie concludes with Jim having learned a valuable lesson about love and relationships, but not necessarily in the way he expected.

Overall, American Pie Presents: The Book of Love is a lighthearted and comedic take on the challenges of love and relationships. While it may not be as sophisticated or nuanced as some other romantic comedies, the movie provides plenty of laughs and entertainment for fans of the franchise.

overview: America is on the search for the murderer Eddie Kim. Sean Jones must fly to L.A. to testify in a hearing against Kim. Accompanied by FBI agent Neville Flynn, the flight receives some unexpected visitors.
tagline: Sit back. Relax. Enjoy the fright.
title: Snakes on a Plane
plot:
Snakes on a Plane is a 2006 action horror film directed by David R. Ellis and produced by New Line Cinema.

The movie follows the story of Neville Flynn (played by Samuel L. Jackson), an FBI agent who must transport a prisoner, Sean Jones (played by Nathan Phillips), to Hawaii for trial. Unbeknownst to Flynn, the plane is infested with deadly cobras that have been smuggled onto the aircraft, and the snakes begin to wreak havoc on the passengers and crew.

The main themes of Snakes on a Plane include:

1. **Survival**: The movie's central plot revolves around the characters' desperate attempts to survive the snake attack and make it out alive.
2. **Fear and Panic**: As the snakes start to appear, the tension builds up, and the passengers and crew succumb to fear and panic, leading to chaos and disorder on the plane.
3. **Human Nature**: The film explores how people react in extreme situations, showcasing both heroism and cowardice as characters face their fears and try to protect themselves and others.
4. **Air Travel Horror**: Snakes on a Plane is often cited as one of the most infamous horror movies about air travel, highlighting the vulnerability of passengers and crew during flights.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic, known for its over-the-top action sequences, memorable performances (particularly Samuel L. Jackson's), and its ability to elicit a strong emotional response from audiences.

Overall, Snakes on a Plane is a thrilling, suspenseful ride that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats as they follow the characters' desperate attempts to survive the deadly snake attack.

overview: On March 21st, 1945, the British Royal Air Force set out on a mission to bomb Gestapo's headquarters in Copenhagen. The raid had fatal consequences as some of the bombers accidentally targeted a school and more than 120 people were killed, 86 of whom were children.
title: The Shadow in My Eye
plot:
The Shadow in My Eye (Danish: Skyggen i mit øje), released internationally as The Bombardment, is a 2021 Danish war drama film written and directed by Ole Bornedal. It depicts Operation Carthage, the 1945 Royal Air Force raid on the Gestapo headquarters in Copenhagen, during which one of the planes crashed near the Institut Jeanne d'Arc, leading other aircraft to mistake the school for the target and bomb it.

In German-occupied Denmark in 1945, an RAF Mosquito strafes a car carrying bridesmaids, mistaking it for a German staff vehicle. A boy named Henry, who witnesses the attack, is so traumatized that he loses the ability to speak, and his parents send him to Copenhagen to stay with his cousin Rigmor. Rigmor and her friend Eva, pupils at the Institut Jeanne d'Arc, a French-language Catholic school run by nuns, help Henry overcome his fear of open skies. Meanwhile, a young novice, Sister Teresa, who teaches the girls' class, struggles with her faith and, in an attempt to test God, begins an illicit romance with Frederik, a HIPO officer serving the German occupation authorities. At the request of the Danish resistance, the RAF plans to bomb the Shellhus, the Gestapo headquarters, to destroy its records and free imprisoned resistance members, though the Germans have placed hostages under its roof.

On the day of the raid, Eva quarrels with her parents over an unfinished bowl of porridge, Frederik, persuaded by Teresa, tells his parents he is deserting, and the head nun, Sister Hanna, moves to expel Teresa from the order. During the attack, the Mosquito flown by the pilots Pete and Andy hits a searchlight tower and crashes near the school, and other bombers strike the building, killing and wounding many pupils and teachers, while the Shellhus is hit and several prisoners escape. Henry regains his voice and helps firefighters identify wounded children. Rigmor and Teresa are trapped beneath the rubble as water from fire hoses floods the basement; Frederik tries to save Teresa, but she plunges into the water, perhaps to reach Rigmor, and the basement collapses. Eva's desperate parents finally find her at home, eating her cold porridge.

The film was released in Denmark in October 2021 and on Netflix internationally in March 2022. It drew criticism from the family of the real RAF pilot Peter Kleboe over its fictional opening attack, and the producers agreed to make editorial changes, an unusual step after a film's premiere.

overview: Young Pietari lives with his reindeer-herding father in arctic Finland. On the eve of Christmas, a nearby excavation makes a frightening discovery and an evil Santa Claus is unleashed…
tagline: He knows if you've been naughty. He knows if you've been nice. And he doesn't give a sh*t.
title: Rare Exports: A Christmas Tale
plot:
Rare Exexports: A Christmas Tale is a dark fantasy film that delves into the complexities of human nature and the true meaning of Christmas. The movie tells the story of a group of people in a small Finnish town who discover that the real Santa Claus is not as jolly as they thought.

At its core, Rare Exports explores the idea of the "other," highlighting how societal norms and expectations can lead to fear, mistrust, and violence towards those who are perceived as different. The film's portrayal of the Tonttu, a small, mischievous creature with a penchant for causing chaos, serves as a metaphor for the unknown and the unexplained.

The movie also delves into themes of isolation and community, showcasing how the town's inhabitants come together to confront their fears and understand the true nature of their surroundings. Through the character of Juha, a young boy who is initially skeptical but eventually becomes embroiled in the mystery, the film explores the idea of innocence and the importance of holding onto one's sense of wonder.

Furthermore, Rare Exports critiques the commercialization of Christmas, suggesting that the holiday has become a time for materialism and conformity rather than genuine connection and community. The film's dark humor and satire serve to highlight the absurdity of this trend, adding to the overall sense of unease and discomfort that pervades the narrative.

Ultimately, Rare Exports presents a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to reexamine their assumptions about the world around them and the true meaning of Christmas.

overview: When the Bad Guys, a crew of criminal animals, are finally caught after years of heists and being the world’s most-wanted villains, Mr. Wolf brokers a deal to save them all from prison.
tagline: Good is no fun at all.
title: The Bad Guys
plot:
The Bad Guys is an animated action-comedy film released in 2022, produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures.

The movie follows the story of a group of animal outcasts who are known as "the bad guys" in their community. The main character, Wolf (voiced by Sam Rockwell), is a cunning and charismatic leader who has been shunned by his peers due to his mischievous behavior. He is joined by his loyal sidekicks, Whitey the rabbit (voiced by Awkwafina) and Shark (voiced by Antonio Banderas).

The trio plans to rob a bank in the city of Dogville, where they hope to escape their troubled pasts and start anew. However, things don't go as planned, and they find themselves on the run from the authorities.

As Wolf navigates his complicated relationships with Whitey and Shark, he begins to question his own morality and the true nature of being a "bad guy." Along the way, he meets a young girl named Fiona (voiced by Marie Gauthier), who becomes an unlikely ally in their quest for redemption.

Throughout the film, Wolf's backstory is slowly revealed, showcasing his troubled childhood and the events that led him to become the leader of the group. The movie also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the power of change.

The animation style in The Bad Guys is vibrant and colorful, with a unique blend of humor and heart. The voice cast delivers impressive performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Bad Guys is a fun and entertaining film that offers a fresh take on the traditional "bad guy" trope. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: A boy begins a grand journey to return Babe Ruth's baseball bat before the deciding game of the 1932 World Series comes to a close.
tagline: No matter where life takes you, always keep swingin'
title: Everyone's Hero
plot:
Everyone's Hero is an animated film that tells the story of a young boy named Metro Man Jr., who dreams of becoming a superhero like his idol, Metro Man. However, when Metro Man is killed in action, Metro Man Jr. discovers that he has inherited not only his father's powers but also his legacy.

The main theme of Everyone's Hero revolves around the idea of identity and self-discovery. Metro Man Jr. must navigate his new role as a superhero while also coming to terms with his own sense of purpose and belonging. As he struggles to live up to his father's expectations, he learns valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

The film also explores the theme of grief and loss, particularly in the context of Metro Man Jr.'s relationship with his deceased father. The movie shows how Metro Man Jr. grapples with the weight of his father's legacy and the pressure to fill his shoes, all while trying to find his own path in life.

Furthermore, Everyone's Hero touches on the idea of heroism and what it means to be a true hero. The film challenges traditional notions of heroism by presenting a more nuanced and relatable portrayal of a superhero, one who is flawed but ultimately driven by a desire to do good.

overview: When the island's dormant volcano begins roaring to life, Owen and Claire mount a campaign to rescue the remaining dinosaurs from this extinction-level event.
tagline: The park is gone.
title: Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom
plot:
Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom is a science fiction adventure film directed by J.A. Bayona and written by Emily Carmichael, Seth Robson, and Colin Trevorrow. The movie takes place three years after the events of Jurassic World (2018) and follows the story of Claire Dearing (Bryce Dallas Howard), the former park manager of Isla Nublar.

The film begins with a prologue that shows the aftermath of the volcanic eruption on Isla Nublar, which caused widespread destruction and killed many of the dinosaurs. The scene then cuts to the present day, where we see Claire living in San Diego with Owen Grady (Chris Pratt), a Velociraptor trainer who has been working with her.

The story takes a dramatic turn when a wealthy entrepreneur named Benjamin Lockwood (James Cromwell) hires Claire and Owen to return to Isla Nublar to rescue his wife, Ellie (DeWanda Wise), who is being held captive by the park's former owner, Simon Masrani (Irrfan Khan). However, upon their arrival, they discover that the island has been taken over by a group of mercenaries led by B.D. Wong's character, Dr. Henry Wu.

The mercenaries plan to capture and sell the dinosaurs to a wealthy collector, but Claire and Owen soon realize that this is not the only reason behind their actions. The true intention is to use the dinosaurs as a means to gain control over the island and its resources. As they try to escape, they are ambushed by the mercenaries, and Owen is captured.

Claire teams up with a group of allies, including ZOologist Dr. Alan Grant (Sam Neill), who had previously worked on the original Jurassic Park project, and a young woman named Maisie Lockwood (Isabella Sermon), Benjamin's daughter. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to rescue Owen and stop the mercenaries from exploiting the dinosaurs.

As they navigate through the island, they encounter various dangers, including the Indominus Rex, a genetically engineered super-dinosaur that has been created by Simon Masrani. The group also discovers that the mercenaries are being led by a mysterious figure known as the "Black Market" dealer, who is revealed to be none other than Claire's former business partner, Eli Mills (Rafe Spall).

The climax of the film takes place at an abandoned volcano on Isla Nublar, where the group faces off against the mercenaries and the Indominus Rex. In a thrilling sequence, Owen and Claire work together to defeat the super-dinosaur and escape the island.

In the end, Claire and Owen manage to rescue Maisie and escape the island, but not before realizing that the dinosaurs are being exploited for their own benefit. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Claire and Owen vow to protect the dinosaurs and ensure their safety.

Overall, Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of conservation, exploitation, and the ethics of playing God with nature. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film was a commercial success and set the stage for the next installment in the Jurassic World franchise.

overview: A heroic story about firefighters and rescuers. What we call an act of bravery is just a usual routine for them, if only one can get used to mortal danger and extreme risk. When people in distress seem to have nobody who may help them, rescuers come to fight against merciless forces of nature.
tagline: Some fires can't be tamed.
title: Fire
plot:
Fire (Russian: Огонь, Ogon), also released in English as No Escapes, is a Russian disaster film from 2020, directed by Aleksey Nuzhnyy and produced by Nikita Mikhalkov's studio TriTe with the broadcaster VGTRK. It celebrates the smokejumpers and rescuers of Russia's Aerial Forest Protection Service and the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Konstantin Khabenskiy stars as Colonel Sokolov, the veteran commander of an elite airborne firefighting crew, with Ivan Yankovsky as the young rescuer Roman Ilyin, Stasya Miloslavskaya as Sokolov's daughter Katya, a dispatcher, Andrey Smolyakov as the head of the forest service, Irina Gorbacheva as a woman about to give birth, and Viktor Dobronravov, Roman Kurtsyn, Tikhon Zhiznevsky and Viktor Sukhorukov among the crew and pilots.

Sokolov's team fights blazes in the remote forests, and the routine turns deadly when a fire claims one of their own. At home, Sokolov learns that Katya is dating Roman, a rookie from Moscow, and to keep an eye on him and teach him what the job demands, he puts the newcomer on his frontline crew.

When wildfires in Karelia encircle the village of Olkhovka, dozens of residents are trapped, and six members of Sokolov's brigade are dropped into the heart of the rapidly spreading inferno. With no hope of stopping the fire, they must solve one desperate problem after another: finding a route through the wall of flame to lead the adults to the safety of the river, working out how to save the children, who would slow the escape, and evacuating a woman who goes into labor in the middle of the blaze. Through it all the firefighters must be ready to sacrifice themselves while staying alive long enough to save the villagers, who cannot survive without them, and Sokolov and Roman are forced to learn to trust each other. The film was inspired by the fires of the summer of 2010 and is dedicated to Russia's forest smokejumpers and rescuers.

Shot in 2019 in Karelia, Moscow Oblast, Taganrog, Vsevolozhsk and Vladimir with the help of real firefighters and aircraft such as the Be-200 water bomber, and incorporating real footage of forest fires, it was released by Central Partnership on 24 December 2020. It grossed more than 926 million rubles against a budget of 550 million, and Yankovsky and Gorbacheva won Golden Eagle Awards for their supporting performances.

overview: Desperate to help her ailing brother, a young woman agrees to compete in a deadly game of "Would You Rather" hosted by a sadistic aristocrat.
tagline: Tell yourself it's just a game.
title: Would You Rather
plot:
Would You Rather is a 2012 American psychological horror thriller film directed by David Guy Levy and starring Brittany Snow as Iris and Jeffrey Combs as Shepard Lambrick, with Jonny Coyne, Lawrence Gilliard Jr. and Enver Gjokaj. Based on the party game of the same name, it follows a young woman who enters a deadly game to pay for her brother's leukemia treatment. Crispin Glover was originally cast as Lambrick but left before filming, which took place in the Los Angeles area in July 2011.

Iris is struggling to pay for the treatment of her younger brother, Raleigh, who has leukemia. Their oncologist, Dr. Barden, introduces her to Shepard Lambrick, a wealthy philanthropist who promises to pay for the treatment and find a bone marrow donor if she wins a game at his dinner party. The other guests include Shepard's arrogant son Julian, a war veteran named Travis, a paralyzed elderly woman named Linda, a gambling addict named Peter, a recovering alcoholic named Conway, and Lucas, Amy and Cal. Over dinner Shepard tempts them with money: Iris, a vegetarian, eats meat for $10,000, and Conway drinks Scotch for $50,000. Shepard then reveals the game, a deadly version of "would you rather", in which the last player standing wins. When Conway tries to leave, he is shot dead by the butler, Bevans.

The rounds grow more brutal. After a round of electric shocks, the players must either stab their neighbor with an ice pick or whip Travis with a sjambok; Linda bleeds to death and Travis is fatally injured. An escape attempt leaves Cal dead, and Dr. Barden, who tries to help Iris, is killed. In the third round, the players choose between two minutes submerged in a barrel of water and an unknown task on a card: Peter dies when a firecracker explodes in his hand, Lucas slices his own eye, Iris survives the water, and Amy drowns after her card doubles the time. In the final round, Iris must kill Lucas to win or spare him and forfeit the prize. She shoots him. Shepard gives her the money and reveals that a donor has already been found, but when Iris returns home she discovers that Raleigh has killed himself with an overdose of his medication, rendering her terrible choices meaningless.

The film premiered at Screamfest on October 14, 2012, and was released in select theaters and on video on demand by IFC Midnight on February 8, 2013. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reported 61% approval, praising the premise but faulting its gore, while Metacritic gave it 20.

overview: Los Angeles Police Department detective Russell Poole has spent years trying to solve his biggest case -- the murders of The Notorious B.I.G. and Tupac Shakur -- but after two decades, the investigation remains open. Jack Jackson, a reporter desperate to save his reputation and career, is determined to find out why. In search of the truth, the two team up and unravel a growing web of institutional corruption and lies.
tagline: The only thing more notorious than the crime, was the cover up.
title: City of Lies
plot:
City of Lies is a crime drama film that delves into the dark underbelly of Los Angeles in the 1990s. The movie follows the story of Detective Russell Poole, who is tasked with investigating the murder of Tupac Shakur. As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that there are those who will stop at nothing to keep the truth hidden.

At its core, City of Lies explores the themes of corruption, power, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The film sheds light on the systemic racism and police brutality that plagued Los Angeles during this time period, highlighting the ways in which these issues can lead to a breakdown in trust between law enforcement and the communities they serve.

The movie also touches on the theme of celebrity culture and its impact on society. Tupac Shakur's rise to fame and his subsequent murder serve as a catalyst for exploring the darker side of the entertainment industry, where fame and fortune can come at a steep price.

Furthermore, City of Lies is a story about loyalty, friendship, and the bonds that form between people in the face of adversity. The relationships between Detective Poole, his partner Brian "Kato" Kaelin, and Tupac Shakur himself are central to the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the film's exploration of these themes.

Overall, City of Lies is a gripping and thought-provoking drama that sheds light on some of the darkest corners of Los Angeles' history, while also celebrating the resilience and strength of its people.

overview: A story based on the life of a struggling Long Island single mom who became one of the country's most successful entrepreneurs.
title: Joy
plot:
Joy is a 2015 American biographical drama film written and directed by David O. Russell, inspired by the life of Joy Mangano, the Long Island inventor of the Miracle Mop who built a business empire. Jennifer Lawrence stars as Joy, with Robert De Niro as her father Rudy, Bradley Cooper as QVC executive Neil Walker, Édgar Ramírez as her ex-husband Tony, Elisabeth Röhm as her half-sister Peggy. Russell rewrote a script by Annie Mumolo.

In 1990, Joy, an airline booking agent in Peconic, New York, struggles to make ends meet while holding together a chaotic household: her two children, her mother Terri, who spends her days watching soap operas in bed, her supportive grandmother Mimi, and her ex-husband Tony, an aspiring singer living in the basement. Her father Rudy moves into the basement too after his third divorce, and her half-sister Peggy constantly belittles her. Encouraged by Mimi and her best friend Jackie to pursue her ambitions as an inventor, Joy designs a self-wringing mop. Rudy's wealthy girlfriend, Trudy, invests in it, and a California company is contracted to make the parts. Advised to pay $50,000 in royalties to a Hong Kong man with a similar product, Joy complies, but she refuses to keep paying the manufacturer's charges to redo faulty parts.

Joy meets Neil Walker at QVC, who agrees to sell the mop on television, and she takes out a second mortgage to produce 50,000 units. When a celebrity host botches the first broadcast, Joy insists on demonstrating it herself, and the mop sells out. Her triumph is darkened by Mimi's death, and then by disaster: Peggy pays the manufacturer's inflated bills without her approval, and a contract loophole lets the company patent Joy's design. Facing bankruptcy, Joy discovers that the Hong Kong product never existed and confronts the owner, Derek Markham, forcing him to refund her, pay damages and give up any claim to the patent. Years later, Joy is a successful businesswoman who supports other inventors, relies on Jackie and Tony as advisers and still cares for her father, despite his and Peggy's failed lawsuit for her company.

Released by 20th Century Fox on December 25, 2015, Joy grossed $101.1 million worldwide on a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed (61% on Rotten Tomatoes), praising Lawrence but criticizing the writing and pacing. Lawrence won the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Comedy or Musical and received an Academy Award nomination.

overview: New York fashion designer, Melanie Carmichael suddenly finds herself engaged to the city's most eligible bachelor. But her past holds many secrets—including Jake, the redneck husband she married in high school, who refuses to divorce her. Bound and determined to end their contentious relationship once and for all, Melanie sneaks back home to Alabama to confront her past.
tagline: Sometimes What You're Looking For Is Right Where You Left It.
title: Sweet Home Alabama
plot:
Sweet Home Alabama is a 2002 American romantic comedy film directed by Andy Tennant and produced by Original Film.

The movie follows Melanie Carmichael (played by Reese Witherspoon), a fashion designer who has built a successful career in New York City. However, she still holds onto her roots and her childhood sweetheart, Jake Perry (played by Josh Lucas), whom she left behind in her hometown of Pigeon Creek, Alabama.

As the story unfolds, Melanie is forced to choose between her old life and her new one when her fiancé, Andrew Hannon (played by Patrick Dempsey), proposes to her. However, just as she's about to accept, she receives news that her father has passed away, leaving her his vast fortune and a requirement that she must get married within 90 days.

Melanie is torn between her love for Jake and her commitment to Andrew, leading to a series of comedic misadventures as she navigates her way through both worlds. Along the way, she also discovers more about herself and what truly makes her happy.

The main themes of Sweet Home Alabama include:

1. Identity: Melanie's journey is all about finding out who she is and where she belongs. She struggles to balance her old life in New York with her roots in Pigeon Creek, ultimately discovering that she can have the best of both worlds.
2. Love: The movie explores different types of love, including romantic love, familial love, and self-love. Melanie's relationships with Jake and Andrew teach her valuable lessons about what truly matters in life.
3. Homecoming: The film celebrates the idea of coming home to one's roots and finding comfort in familiar surroundings. Pigeon Creek becomes a symbol of Melanie's childhood and her connection to her family, which she must reconcile with her adult life.
4. Self-discovery: Through her experiences, Melanie learns more about herself and what makes her happy. She discovers that she doesn't have to choose between two worlds; instead, she can create a new life that combines the best of both.

Overall, Sweet Home Alabama is a heartwarming story about finding one's true self, embracing one's roots, and following one's heart.

original_title: Minuscule - La vallée des fourmis perdues
overview: In a peaceful little clearing, the remains of a hastily abandoned picnic sparks a battle between two tribes of ants. A bold young ladybug finds himself caught in the middle. He befriends the leader of the black ants, Mandible, and helps him save the anthill from the assault of the terrible red ant warriors, led by the fearful Butor. A fantastic journey at ground level.
tagline: An Epic Adventure At Ground Level.
title: Minuscule: Valley of the Lost Ants
plot:
Minuscule: Valley of the Lost Ants is an animated adventure film that delves into the intricate world of ants, exploring their social hierarchy and the consequences of human actions on their environment. The movie follows the journey of a young ant named Reymond, who embarks on a perilous quest to save his colony from destruction.

At its core, Minuscule: Valley of the Lost Ants is a story about community, cooperation, and the importance of preserving one's home. The film highlights the intricate social structure of ants, showcasing their division of labor, communication, and teamwork as they work together to overcome challenges. Through Reymond's adventures, the movie conveys the value of unity and collaboration in the face of adversity.

The film also touches on themes of environmentalism and conservation, emphasizing the delicate balance between humans and nature. The destruction of the ants' habitat serves as a metaphor for the impact of human activities on the natural world, highlighting the need to protect and preserve our planet's ecosystems.

Furthermore, Minuscule: Valley of the Lost Ants explores the concept of courage and determination in the face of overwhelming odds. Reymond's bravery and perseverance inspire his fellow ants, demonstrating that even the smallest creatures can make a significant impact when they work together towards a common goal.

Overall, Minuscule: Valley of the Lost Ants is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the wonders of the natural world while promoting important themes about community, cooperation, and environmental stewardship.

original_title: Chickenhare and the Hamster of Darkness
overview: Young Chickenhare is the adopted son of King Peter, a famous adventurer. Part chicken and part hare, he has a really tough time growing up and disguises himself as a hare to avoid the mockeries of his peers. When the day of the Royal Adventurer Society trials comes, Chickenhare, hampered by his disguise, fails miserably. But he is determined to grab a second chance and find the Scepter of the Hamster of Darkness, before his evil Uncle Lapin. The Scepter will give immense power to its holder. If Lapin gets hold of it, he will be unstoppable. Accompanied by his faithful servant Abe, a sarcastic turtle, and Meg, a martial arts expert skunk, he sets of on an epic and initiatory quest.
title: Chickenhare and the Hamster of Darkness
plot:
Chickenhare and the Hamster of Darkness is a 2022 animated adventure comedy film produced by nWave Pictures, directed by Ben Stassen and Benjamin Mousquet, in his directorial debut, from a screenplay by David Collard. Based on Chris Grine's graphic novel Chickenhare, it follows a hero born half chicken and half hare who longs to fit in and become an adventurer. The English voice cast features Jordan Tartakow as Chickenhare, Joey Lotsko as Abe, Laila Berzins as Meg and Danny Fehsenfeld as Lapin.

The hare brothers Peter and Lapin search a jungle temple for the legendary Hamster of Darkness without success, but outside they find a baby that is half chicken and half hare, whom Peter adopts and names Chickenhare. Growing up as the son of a famous explorer and king of Featherbeard, Chickenhare dreams of becoming an adventurer but is mocked for his differences. Twenty years later, the disguise he wears to hide his chicken features weighs him down and he fails the Royal Adventure Society trials. Determined to prove himself, he visits his uncle Lapin, imprisoned for trying to overthrow Peter, to learn about the Hamster of Darkness, but Lapin escapes with a crew of prisoners to find the artifact himself.

Chickenhare sets off in pursuit with Abe, his sarcastic tortoise servant. In a desert city they are rescued from Lapin's henchmen by Meg, a streetwise skunk adventurer who agrees to guide them through the Desert of Death. Captured by pig-like tribal creatures who mistake Chickenhare for a god, they escape after Meg encourages him to embrace his nature as she has embraced hers. In a temple in the Frosty Mountains they pass three trials and find an ice scepter in the tomb of the extinct hamsters, but Lapin seizes it, summons the hamsters' ghosts to conquer Featherbeard and leaves the trio stranded. Discovering that he can fly, Chickenhare rescues his friends and returns home, wins back the scepter and resolves to destroy it by dropping it into a deep pit beneath the Society's arena. Lapin falls into the pit with it, the ghosts vanish and his henchmen are arrested. Chickenhare becomes an independent adventurer with Meg and Abe, and Peter gives him his treasured golden machete.

The film premiered in Paris on January 23, 2022, opened in France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg on February 16, and was released by Netflix in the United States and other territories on June 10, 2022. A sequel, Chickenhare and the Secret of the Groundhog, followed in 2025.

overview: After being recruited by a group of unconventional thieves, renowned criminal Richard Pace finds himself caught up in an elaborate gold heist that promises to have far-reaching implications on his life and the lives of countless others.
tagline: They're not bad guys. They just steal from them.
title: The Misfits
plot:
The Misfits is a 2021 American heist action film directed by Renny Harlin and written by Robert Henny and Kurt Wimmer. It stars Pierce Brosnan as the master thief Richard Pace, Tim Roth as Werner Schultz, Nick Cannon as Ringo, Hermione Corfield as Pace's daughter Hope, Jamie Chung as Violet, Mike Angelo as Wick and Rami Jaber as the Prince, with Qais Qandil as Jason Quick. Much of the film is set in the Middle East, in a fictional country called Jazeristan.

Richard Pace is a legendary thief who has escaped from three private prisons owned by Werner Schultz. While planning to rob a wealthy figure known as the Prince, Pace walks into a trap and is given a choice: be handed to the FBI or join a team of skilled thieves called the Misfits. On a private jet he meets its members, Ringo, a locksmith and master of disguise, Wick, an explosives expert, and Violet, a deadly martial artist, who fly him to Abu Dhabi for a briefing.

The Misfits reveal that Schultz has laundered money for a terrorist Brotherhood, converting it into gold bars that he keeps in a vault beneath one of his prisons in Jazeristan. They plan to steal the gold before it can be used to fund terrorism, but they need Pace's expertise. He initially refuses, but his daughter Hope, who works with the group, persuades him to join, though he insists on keeping half the loot. As the team prepares to infiltrate the prison, using disguises, tainted food and a fake sanitation crew, the Brotherhood's leader announces that he will come to collect the gold in person on the very day of the heist, raising the stakes for everyone involved.

The film presents itself as a lighthearted caper in the tradition of ensemble heist movies, mixing action, comedy and twists.

The Misfits was released in South Korea on June 3, 2021, and in the United States on June 11 by The Avenue Entertainment. Critics panned it, giving it 17 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25, and it received three nominations at the 42nd Golden Raspberry Awards.

overview: Singer Freddie Mercury, guitarist Brian May, drummer Roger Taylor and bass guitarist John Deacon take the music world by storm when they form the rock 'n' roll band Queen in 1970. Hit songs become instant classics. When Mercury's increasingly wild lifestyle starts to spiral out of control, Queen soon faces its greatest challenge yet – finding a way to keep the band together amid the success and excess.
tagline: Fearless lives forever
title: Bohemian Rhapsody
plot:
Bohemian Rhapsody is a biographical drama film that tells the story of the life of Queen's lead vocalist, Freddie Mercury. The film stars Rami Malek as Mercury and follows his journey from his early days as a musician to the band's rise to fame.

The film begins with Freddie Mercury (Rami Malek) growing up in Zanzibar, Tanzania, where he is born Farrokh Bulsara. He moves to India with his family at a young age and later attends art college in London, where he discovers his passion for music. Mercury forms a band called Ibex, which eventually becomes Queen.

The film then cuts to the early days of Queen, with Mercury meeting Brian May (Gwilym Lee) and Roger Taylor (Ben Hardy). The three musicians form a strong bond and begin to develop their unique sound. They are later joined by John Deacon (Joe Mazzello), who completes the classic lineup.

As Queen gains popularity, they start to tour and perform in front of large crowds. Mercury's charisma and stage presence quickly make him a fan favorite. The film depicts the band's struggles with fame, including their tumultuous relationship with their record label, EMI.

One of the most pivotal moments in the film is Queen's performance at Live Aid in 1985. The band takes the stage to perform "Bohemian Rhapsody," which becomes an instant classic. The film captures the energy and excitement of the event, as well as Mercury's emotional response to performing his iconic song.

Throughout the film, Malek delivers a critically acclaimed performance as Mercury, capturing the singer's flamboyant personality, wit, and vulnerability. The supporting cast, including Lucy Boynton as Mercury's girlfriend Mary Austin, also deliver strong performances.

As Queen's popularity continues to grow, Mercury becomes increasingly reclusive and struggles with his personal life. He is openly gay in a time when it was not widely accepted, which puts him at odds with his record label and the public.

The film's climax depicts Queen's performance at Live Aid, as well as their subsequent tour of Japan. The film ends with Mercury's final performance with Queen, which takes place on November 24, 1991, just months before his death from complications related to AIDS.

Overall, Bohemian Rhapsody is a triumphant and emotional tribute to Freddie Mercury's life and legacy. The film features stunning performances, impressive music sequences, and a gripping narrative that captures the highs and lows of Queen's incredible journey.

overview: On a prom-night dare, a trio of high school friends chant an incantation, unleashing an evil spirit from the past with deadly consequences.
tagline: Turn Off The Light And See What Happens.
title: Urban Legends: Bloody Mary
plot:
Urban Legends: Bloody Mary is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the power of suggestion. The movie revolves around a group of teenagers who, while exploring an abandoned house, inadvertently awaken the vengeful spirit of Bloody Mary.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true terror lies not in the supernatural entity itself, but in the fear and vulnerability that it exploits. The film expertly weaves together themes of teenage angst, peer pressure, and the devastating consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

The movie also touches on the idea of the "power of suggestion," highlighting how a simple phrase or ritual can be twisted into a malevolent force that preys on the deepest fears of those who dare to confront it. This theme is skillfully intertwined with the notion of identity and self-discovery, as the characters are forced to confront their own dark pasts and the true nature of their relationships with one another.

Ultimately, Urban Legends: Bloody Mary presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with forces that are beyond human understanding, and the devastating consequences that can result when fear and curiosity are allowed to get the better of us.

overview: Bernardo is an undertaker. He runs his mortuary business in the same house where he resides. In the front, he has his clients. And in the back, his dysfunctional family lives amongst coffins, wreaths, and the mischievous but nonviolent ghosts that visit on a daily basis. But when a malevolent entity enters the scene, it wreaks havoc on the already fractured household.
tagline: Dare you visit?
title: The Funeral Home
plot:
The Funeral Home (Spanish: La funeraria), also known as The Undertaker's Home, is an Argentine horror film written and directed by Mauro Iván Ojeda. Luis Machín, Celeste Gerez and Camila Vaccarini lead the cast, with Hugo Arana, Graciela Bonomi and Susana Varela in supporting roles. It was Arana's last film; the actor died of COVID-19 in October 2020, two months after its festival premiere.

Bernardo, an undertaker, lives with his wife Estela and his stepdaughter Irina in a funeral home that is haunted by restless spirits. Bernardo and Irina both suspect that the strange occurrences might allow them to see loved ones they have lost, but Estela is miserable. She believes her husband is obsessed with the paranormal and quietly resents her because she could not give him a child of his own, and she is convinced that the house has been poisoned by the occult dabbling of Bernardo's late father, Salvador. The tension in the household is so great that Irina has had to give up the ballet she loves.

Bernardo finally calls in a psychic named Ramona to rid the building of its ghosts. Inside, Ramona receives visions that explain the haunting: Estela had manipulated Bernardo into placing his father in a nursing home, and in revenge Salvador summoned a demon to kill her and Irina. He came to regret the pact once he understood that the creature would not stop until his son was dead too, and the spirits he conjured in an effort to hold it back are what now fill the house. Irina comes back from her grandmother's to help with the cleansing, but soon grows terrified and asks her grandmother to collect her. When the old woman arrives she is possessed, and the demon uses her to murder Ramona. Pursued through the house, Irina briefly encounters the ghost of her dead father before the attacks resume, and she discovers the corpses of Estela and Bernardo. Estela briefly stops the possessed grandmother, and Irina takes refuge in a portable toilet. The assault ends at daybreak, when Salvador's bargain expires.
