The demon leaves Irina a ballet costume, and she puts it on and dances for her family's ghosts.

The film premiered as The Undertaker's Home at the Fantasia festival on 21 August 2020, then opened in a handful of American cinemas in January 2021 before arriving on digital platforms a month later as The Funeral Home. Reviews were positive, with 80% on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: ワンピース エピソード オブ サボ～3兄弟の絆 奇跡の再会と受け継がれる意志～
overview: Sabo visits a grave-site where he reflects back on his childhood with his brothers Luffy and Ace. After a flashback of his past Sabo travels to the Kingdom of Dressrosa and meets up with a fellow member of the Revolutionary Army to discuss their next mission. Unbeknownst to Sabo, Luffy and his crew are also on the island searching to destroy an artificial Devil Fruit factory.
tagline: The Three Brothers' Bond, The Miraculous Reunion
title: Episode of Sabo: The Three Brothers' Bond - The Miraculous Reunion
plot:
Episode of Sabo: The Three Brothers' Bond - The Miraculous Reunion, also known as Sabo no Omoi, is a 2015 anime film that serves as a prequel to the popular manga and anime series One Piece. 

The main theme of this movie revolves around the bond between three brothers, Sabo, Ace, and Luffy, who are connected by their shared experiences and emotions. The story delves into the complexities of sibling relationships, exploring themes of love, loyalty, and sacrifice.

Through the narrative, Toei Animation masterfully weaves together elements of adventure, action, and drama to create a captivating tale that highlights the depth of the characters' emotional connections. The film's focus on the three brothers' bond serves as a poignant reminder of the power of family ties and the unbreakable bonds that form between loved ones.

The movie also touches upon the theme of redemption, as Sabo grapples with his past mistakes and seeks to make amends with his brother Ace. This narrative thread adds a layer of emotional complexity to the story, allowing audiences to reflect on the consequences of one's actions and the importance of forgiveness.

Ultimately, Episode of Sabo: The Three Brothers' Bond - The Miraculous Reunion is a heartwarming and action-packed tale that celebrates the beauty of brotherly love and the unbreakable bonds that connect us all.

overview: The Bellas are back, and they are better than ever. After being humiliated in front of none other than the President of the United States of America, the Bellas are taken out of the Aca-Circuit. In order to clear their name, and regain their status, the Bellas take on a seemingly impossible task: winning an international competition no American team has ever won. In order to accomplish this monumental task, they need to strengthen the bonds of friendship and sisterhood and blow away the competition with their amazing aca-magic! With all new friends and old rivals tagging along for the trip, the Bellas can hopefully accomplish their dreams.
tagline: We're back pitches
title: Pitch Perfect 2
plot:
Pitch Perfect 2 is a musical comedy film directed by Elizabeth Banks and written by Kay Cannon. The movie is the sequel to the 2012 film Pitch Perfect, which was also produced by Universal Pictures.

The story begins with the Bellas, an all-girl a cappella group from Barden University, preparing for their performance at the International Championship of Collegiate A Cappella (ICCA). The group's leader, Aubrey Posen (Anna Camp), is struggling to find her place in the group after being replaced as the lead singer by Chloe Beale (Brittany Snow).

As the competition approaches, the Bellas face a new challenge: they must perform at the ICCA with a male member. The group holds auditions and selects Jesse Swanson (Skylar Astin), a former member of an all-male a cappella group called "The Treblemakers." However, things get complicated when it's revealed that Jesse has a secret: he was kicked out of the Treblemakers for being too emotional.

Despite their initial reservations, the Bellas decide to give Jesse a chance. As they work together, Aubrey and Jesse develop feelings for each other, but their relationship is put to the test as they navigate the pressures of competition and group dynamics.

Meanwhile, the Bellas face off against their arch-rivals, the Treblemakers, who are determined to win the ICCA. The competition heats up as the two groups engage in a series of musical battles, with the Bellas using innovative arrangements and choreography to try and outdo their opponents.

As the championship approaches, the Bellas must also contend with the pressure of performing live on stage. Aubrey's nerves get the better of her, and she struggles to find her place as the lead singer. Jesse tries to help her overcome her fears, but it's clear that he has his own issues to deal with.

In the end, the Bellas face off against the Treblemakers in an epic musical showdown. The competition is fierce, but the Bellas use their unique sound and style to outshine their opponents. In a stunning upset, they win the ICCA championship, and Aubrey finally finds her place as the lead singer.

The movie ends with the Bellas celebrating their victory, surrounded by their friends and loved ones. Jesse and Aubrey share a romantic moment, and it's clear that their relationship is just beginning. The Treblemakers, who had been portrayed as the villains of the first film, are shown to be more complex and nuanced characters, adding depth to the story.

Overall, Pitch Perfect 2 is a fun and entertaining movie that explores themes of identity, friendship, and perseverance. With its catchy musical numbers and witty dialogue, it's a must-see for fans of the original film and anyone who loves music and comedy.

overview: Called in to recover evidence in the aftermath of a horrific explosion on a New Orleans ferry, Federal agent Doug Carlin gets pulled away from the scene and taken to a top-secret government lab that uses a time-shifting surveillance device to help prevent crime.
tagline: If you think it's just a feeling, go back... and look again.
title: Déjà Vu
plot:
Déjà Vu is a 2006 American science fiction action film directed by Tony Scott and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Denzel Washington, Jim Caviezel, Eva Mendes, and Benicio del Toro.

The story begins with ATF agent Doug Carlin (Denzel Washington), who is struggling to cope with the death of his wife in a car accident. He is haunted by flashbacks of that fateful day and feels guilty for not being able to save her. To escape his grief, Doug undergoes a revolutionary new technology called "pre-crime" which allows him to see glimpses of possible future events.

The pre-crime device uses advanced computer algorithms to analyze the brain activity of individuals and predict potential crimes before they occur. The government has been using this technology to prevent terrorist attacks, but it's also being used by rogue agents to alter the course of history for personal gain.

Doug is assigned to a special task force that uses the pre-crime device to investigate a series of seemingly unrelated crimes across the country. As Doug delves deeper into the case, he begins to experience strange visions of his wife's death and realizes that one of the predicted crimes is actually a murder that has already occurred - but in a different time period.

Doug becomes obsessed with preventing the murder from happening, and he travels back in time to November 7, 2004, where he encounters a younger version of himself. He also meets a woman named Kate (Eva Mendes), who becomes his ally in altering the course of events.

As Doug navigates the past, he discovers that the murder is connected to a conspiracy involving corrupt government officials and terrorists. He must use his knowledge of future events to prevent the murder from occurring, while also trying to find a way back to his own time.

However, as Doug tries to alter the timeline, he realizes that every decision he makes has unintended consequences on the present and future. The more he changes, the more chaos ensues, and Doug begins to question whether he's truly making progress or just creating a new reality.

In the climactic final act, Doug must confront his own destiny and make a choice between saving his wife or altering the course of history. In the end, Doug manages to prevent the murder from occurring, but not without sacrificing his own life in the process.

The movie ends with Kate, who has been transported back to her own time, reflecting on the events that transpired. She realizes that Doug's actions have created a new reality where his wife is still alive, and she must come to terms with the consequences of altering the timeline.

Déjà Vu received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $200 million worldwide. The movie's complex plot and themes of time travel and free will were praised by some, while others found it confusing and predictable. Despite its flaws, Déjà Vu remains an entertaining sci-fi action film with a strong performance from Denzel Washington.

overview: A live-action adaptation of Disney's version of the classic tale of a cursed prince and a beautiful young woman who helps him break the spell.
tagline: Be our guest.
title: Beauty and the Beast
plot:
Beauty and the Beast is a 2017 American romantic fantasy film directed by Bill Condon, based on the 1991 animated film of the same name by Walt Disney Pictures. The story is an adaptation of the 1740 French fairy tale "La Belle et la Bête" by Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve.

The film begins with a prologue that sets the tone for the rest of the story, showcasing the Beast's (Dan Stevens) transformation from a prince to a monster after he is cursed by an enchantress. The curse states that the Beast will remain in this form until he finds true love and is loved in return.

In the present day, Belle (Emma Watson), a beautiful and intelligent young woman, lives in a small French village with her inventor father, Maurice (Kevin Kline). When Maurice gets lost in the forest while searching for a rare part to repair his latest invention, he stumbles upon the Beast's castle. The Beast, who is initially hostile towards Belle, imprisons Maurice as punishment.

Belle sets out to rescue her father and offers to take his place as the prisoner. She agrees to stay with the Beast in exchange for her father's freedom. As she spends more time with the Beast, she begins to see beyond his physical appearance and discovers a kind and intelligent person beneath the surface.

The Beast, who is struggling to come to terms with his curse, is initially resistant to Belle's charms but eventually warms up to her. They begin to form a bond, and Belle learns about the Beast's past and the reason for his transformation. The Beast tells Belle that he was once a prince who was cursed by an enchantress as punishment for his arrogance.

As Belle and the Beast spend more time together, they develop feelings for each other. However, their love is threatened when Gaston (Luke Evans), a vain and egotistical hunter, arrives in the village with plans to kill the Beast and win Belle's hand in marriage.

In the climactic final act, Gaston and his mob attack the castle, and Belle must defend her home and the Beast. In the process, she saves the Beast from Gaston's knife and ultimately breaks the curse by confessing her love for him.

The film ends with the Beast transformed back into a prince, and he and Belle share a romantic dance at the ball. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that the two can build a life together despite their differences.

Overall, Beauty and the Beast is a beautifully crafted tale of love, acceptance, and redemption. The film features stunning visuals, memorable characters, and a timeless story that has captivated audiences for centuries.

overview: A white blood cell policeman, with the help of a cold pill, must stop a deadly virus from destroying the human they live in, Frank.
tagline: Every body needs a hero.
title: Osmosis Jones
plot:
Osmosis Jones is an animated comedy film that explores the theme of teamwork and unity among different individuals with unique skills and strengths. The movie follows the story of a white blood cell named Frank, who teams up with a genetically engineered antibiotic pill named Drix to stop a deadly virus from taking over the body.

The main theme of Osmosis Jones is the power of collaboration and diversity in overcoming adversity. Frank and Drix, despite being vastly different, learn to put aside their differences and work together to save the day. This theme is reflected in the film's portrayal of the human immune system, where different cells and organs work together to keep the body healthy.

The movie also explores the idea of individuality and self-acceptance. Frank, as a white blood cell, struggles with his own identity and purpose, while Drix, as an antibiotic pill, is initially seen as an outsider by the other cells in the body. Through their journey, they learn to appreciate and celebrate their unique qualities.

Furthermore, Osmosis Jones touches on the theme of perseverance and determination. Frank and Drix face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to stop the virus, but they never give up. Their unwavering commitment to their mission ultimately leads to a triumphant outcome.

Overall, Osmosis Jones is a heartwarming film that celebrates the importance of teamwork, diversity, and individuality in overcoming adversity.

overview: Nemo, an adventurous young clownfish, is unexpectedly taken from his Great Barrier Reef home to a dentist's office aquarium. It's up to his worrisome father Marlin and a friendly but forgetful fish Dory to bring Nemo home -- meeting vegetarian sharks, surfer dude turtles, hypnotic jellyfish, hungry seagulls, and more along the way.
tagline: There are 3.7 trillion fish in the ocean. They're looking for one.
title: Finding Nemo
plot:
Finding Nemo is a heartwarming animated film directed by Andrew Stanton, released in 2003 by Pixar Animation Studios. The movie follows the story of Marlin, a clownfish and overprotective father, who embarks on an epic journey to rescue his only son Nemo after he gets captured by a diver.

The film begins with Marlin's life in the Great Barrier Reef, where he lives with his son Nemo. However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Nemo is captured by a diver and taken to a fish tank in a dentist's office in Sydney. Desperate to rescue his son, Marlin sets out on an incredible journey across the ocean, facing numerous dangers and challenges along the way.

As Marlin navigates through the ocean, he meets Dory, a friendly but forgetful blue tang fish who suffers from short-term memory loss. Despite her limitations, Dory's optimism and enthusiasm make her a perfect companion for Marlin on his quest. Together, they encounter a group of friendly sea creatures, including a surfer-dude sea turtle named Crush and a school of jellyfish.

Throughout their journey, Marlin learns to let go of his overprotectiveness and trust others, particularly Dory, who becomes like a surrogate daughter to him. Meanwhile, Nemo makes the most of his new surroundings in the fish tank, befriends the other fish, and comes up with a plan to escape.

As Marlin and Dory near their destination, they face one final challenge: navigating through the treacherous waters of the dentist's office. With Dory's help, Marlin is able to rescue Nemo and return him home to the Great Barrier Reef.

The film features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a story that explores themes of parenthood, friendship, and perseverance. The movie's climax, where Marlin finally reunites with Nemo, is both heartwarming and emotionally resonant, leaving audiences cheering for the happy reunion.

Overall, Finding Nemo is a timeless classic that has captured the hearts of audiences worldwide, and its enduring popularity is a testament to Pixar's mastery of storytelling and animation.

overview: When Casper's been being friendly lately even when playing with a boy named Jimmy, Kibosh: The King of the Underworld has Casper enrolled into a Scare School headed by the two-headed headmaster Alder and Dash. He befriends Ra, a mummy with unraveling issues and Mantha, a zombie girl who keeps falling apart. When Casper discovers the two-headed headmaster's plot to use a petrification potion to turn Kibosh into stone and take over the Underworld and Deedstown, he and his new friends must stop him.
title: Casper's Scare School
plot:
Casper's Scare School is a 2006 animated film produced by Classic Media. 

The movie revolves around Casper, a friendly ghost who enrolls in Scare School to learn how to scare humans properly. However, he soon discovers that his classmates are not as interested in scaring as they claim to be.

Throughout the story, Casper learns valuable lessons about friendship, teamwork, and being true to oneself. He also faces challenges from his rival, Fatso, who is determined to become the best scare in Scare School.

As for the main themes of the movie, some of them include:

1. Embracing individuality: Casper's journey teaches him that it's okay to be different and not follow the crowd. He finds his own unique way of scaring, which ultimately helps him connect with others.
2. Friendship and teamwork: The story highlights the importance of building strong relationships and working together towards a common goal. Casper forms close bonds with his classmates, who eventually learn to appreciate his unique approach to scaring.
3. Overcoming rivalries: Fatso's character serves as a foil to Casper's, representing the dangers of rivalry and competition. The movie shows that true success comes from cooperation and mutual respect rather than trying to outdo others.

Overall, Casper's Scare School is a heartwarming tale about self-discovery, friendship, and finding one's own path in life.

overview: The aftermath of a shocking explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power station made hundreds of people sacrifice their lives to clean up the site of the catastrophe and to successfully prevent an even bigger disaster that could have turned a large part of the European continent into an uninhabitable exclusion zone. This is their story.
title: Chernobyl: Abyss
plot:
Chernobyl: Abyss (Russian: Чернобыль), also known as Chernobyl 1986, is a Russian disaster film from 2021, directed by and starring Danila Kozlovsky. It tells a fictionalised story of a firefighter who becomes one of the liquidators during the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster. Oksana Akinshina, Filipp Avdeyev, Ravshana Kurkova and Nikolay Kozak co-star.

In 1986, Alexey Karpushin, a 30-year-old firefighter in the city of Pripyat, rekindles a relationship with his former lover Olga Savostina, a local hairdresser, who tells him that he is the father of her ten-year-old son. The romance falls apart when Alexey fails to show up for a picnic with Olga and the boy, and she tells him never to come back. He requests a transfer to Kyiv to start over, but just as he is about to depart, reactor number 4 at the nearby Chernobyl power plant explodes, and he climbs aboard a fire engine heading to the scene instead. He survives the radiation of the first fight against the fire.

As the true scale of the accident emerges, officials realise that an even worse catastrophe looms: the melting core could fall into a huge reservoir of water beneath the reactor, triggering a steam explosion that would hurl radioactive material high into the atmosphere and threaten the whole of Europe. Because Alexey has inspected the passages underneath the reactors, he is an obvious candidate for the near-suicidal mission to drain the reservoir by hand, though he is reluctant. When he learns that his son has been exposed to radiation and could die, he agrees to go on condition that the boy is sent to Switzerland for treatment. The first attempt fails, and his teammate Valera, an engineer, persuades him to try again. During the second, successful attempt Valera becomes trapped and cuts the line linking them so that Alexey can get out, but Alexey refuses to leave him. He is found gravely irradiated and dies in hospital after Olga embraces him. Three months later, his son returns home from his treatment abroad.

Producer Alexander Rodnyansky, who had filmed the aftermath of the disaster himself, sent the script to Kozlovsky in 2015; mindful of the 2019 HBO miniseries, the filmmakers chose to focus on the personal heroism of the liquidators. Central Partnership released the film in Russia on 15 April 2021, and it reached Netflix in July. Critics were divided: CBC News called it a missed opportunity that downplayed Soviet cover-ups, while the NME described it as a classic disaster movie.

overview: After a heroic job of successfully landing his storm-damaged aircraft in a war zone, a fearless pilot finds himself between the agendas of multiple militias planning to take the plane and its passengers hostage.
tagline: The crash was only the beginning.
title: Plane
plot:
Plane is a 2023 American action thriller written by Charles Cumming and J. P. Davis and directed by Jean-François Richet. Gerard Butler stars as a commercial pilot who must team up with a suspected murderer after an emergency landing in hostile territory, with Mike Colter, Yoson An, Tony Goldwyn and Daniella Pineda in supporting roles.

Brodie Torrance, a Scottish former RAF pilot, captains Trailblazer Airlines Flight 119 from Singapore to Honolulu by way of Tokyo. Among the fourteen passengers is Louis Gaspare, a fugitive wanted for homicide who is being extradited to Canada in the custody of an RCMP officer. Told by a superior not to change course over the South China Sea despite a severe storm, Brodie flies on until lightning knocks out the avionics, and turbulence kills a flight attendant and the officer. Brodie and his co-pilot, Samuel Dele, manage to put the aircraft down on a road on Jolo, a remote island in the southern Philippines controlled by rebels. In New York, the airline's crisis manager, David Scarsdale, learns that local authorities will need a full day to respond and hires a team of private mercenaries to go in.

Brodie heads into the jungle with Louis, a former French Foreign Legionnaire. At a deserted warehouse he reaches the airline and his daughter by phone before killing a rebel who attacks him, and Louis dispatches the others; the pair learn that the militants kidnap foreigners for ransom. By the time they return, the rebel leader Datu Junmar has seized the passengers and crew, executing a couple who tried to run. Brodie and Louis capture two looters, force them to reveal where the base is, and leave a note for rescuers. They break into the camp and get the hostages onto a bus, but when more rebels close in, Brodie stays behind as a diversion and is about to be executed when the mercenaries arrive. Everyone retreats to the plane; while the pilots restart the aircraft, Louis and the mercenaries hold off the attackers. Louis stays behind and disappears into the jungle with a bag of ransom money, and Junmar is killed by the landing gear as the plane takes off. Brodie lands the crippled plane on nearby Siasi and calls his daughter to say he is coming home.

Shot in Puerto Rico after passing from Lionsgate to Solstice Studios and back, Plane was released by Lionsgate on January 13, 2023. It grossed $74.5 million worldwide and received generally favourable reviews, with 78% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62.

overview: Tom doles out truths about post-marriage intimacy, his problematic pet pug and why men are to blame for most of life's inconveniences.
title: Tom Papa: What a Day!
plot: Tom doles out truths about post-marriage intimacy, his problematic pet pug and why men are to blame for most of life's inconveniences.

overview: SG-1 searches for an ancient weapon which could help them defeat the Ori, and discover it may be in the Ori's own home galaxy. As the Ori prepare to send ships through to the Milky Way to attack Earth, SG-1 travels to the Ori galaxy aboard the Odyssey. The International Oversight committee have their own plans and SG-1 finds themselves in a distant galaxy fighting two powerful enemies.
tagline: The lines have been drawn. The battle has been waged. Only one thing can save us...
title: Stargate: The Ark of Truth
plot:
Stargate: The Ark of Truth is an action-adventure film that delves into complex themes of power, free will, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. At its core, the movie explores the idea of a powerful artifact known as the Ark of Truth, which has the ability to reveal hidden truths and manipulate reality.

The main theme of Stargate: The Ark of Truth revolves around the concept of free will versus determinism. The characters are faced with an existential crisis when they realize that their actions may be predetermined by the Ark's influence, raising questions about the nature of choice and agency in a world where fate seems to be at play.

The film also touches on the theme of power and its corrupting influence. As the characters grapple with the implications of the Ark's power, they must confront the darker aspects of human nature and the dangers of unchecked ambition. The movie suggests that true wisdom lies not in wielding power, but in understanding one's place within a larger cosmic context.

Furthermore, Stargate: The Ark of Truth explores the idea of sacrifice and redemption. The characters are forced to make difficult choices that require them to put the greater good above personal interests, highlighting the importance of selflessness and putting others before oneself.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together with a sense of urgency and tension, creating a narrative that is both thought-provoking and action-packed.

overview: Record-shattering Korean girl band BLACKPINK tell their story —  and detail the hard fought journey of the dreams and trials behind their meteoric rise.
tagline: The rise of a global phenomena.
title: BLACKPINK: Light Up the Sky
plot:
BLACKPINK: Light Up the Sky is a 2020 documentary film directed by Chris Moon and produced by RadicalMedia. The movie follows the lives of South Korean girl group BLACKPINK, consisting of Rosé, Jennie, Lisa, and Jisoo.

The main themes of BLACKPINK: Light Up the Sky include:

1. Female Empowerment: The film showcases the journey of four young women who have become one of the most successful K-pop groups in the world. It highlights their struggles, hard work, and dedication to their craft, serving as an inspiration to young girls around the globe.

2. Identity and Cultural Heritage: As a group that blends Korean pop culture with international influences, BLACKPINK explores themes of identity and cultural heritage. The film delves into the group's experiences navigating different cultures and languages while maintaining their unique sound and style.

3. Friendship and Camaraderie: Throughout the documentary, the bond between the members is palpable. The film captures intimate moments, behind-the-scenes footage, and heartfelt conversations that reveal the deep friendship and trust among Rosé, Jennie, Lisa, and Jisoo.

4. Perseverance and Resilience: BLACKPINK has faced numerous challenges throughout their career, from intense training sessions to grueling tour schedules. The documentary showcases the group's unwavering dedication to their craft and their ability to overcome obstacles.

5. Self-Discovery and Growth: As the members of BLACKPINK navigate their careers and personal lives, they also undergo significant personal growth. The film explores their individual struggles, passions, and aspirations, offering a glimpse into their evolving identities outside of the group.

Overall, BLACKPINK: Light Up the Sky is a heartwarming and inspiring documentary that celebrates the power of female friendship, cultural exchange, and artistic expression.

overview: After discovering a betrayal, Carlinhos takes a fun stranger to accompany him on Christmas. But Graça proves to be a madwoman capable of bringing the traditional family home down.
title: Christmas Full of Grace
plot:
Christmas Full of Grace (Portuguese: Um Natal Cheio de Graça) is a 2022 Brazilian Christmas romantic comedy directed by Pedro Antonio and written by Carolina García and Fil Braz. It stars Sérgio Malheiros as Carlinhos, Gessica Kayane as Graça and Vera Fischer as Lady Sofia, the matriarch of Carlinhos's wealthy family, with a supporting cast that includes Monique Alfradique, Leticia Isnard, Heitor Martínez and Diogo Defante. It was filmed in the Leblon neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro between November and December 2021.

Carlinhos plans to propose to his girlfriend Bebela on Christmas Eve, just before the two are due to attend his family's traditional holiday dinner at his grandmother's mansion. Moments before, he discovers that she has been cheating on him with another woman. Heartbroken, he rushes out of their apartment and runs into Graça, an outspoken, free-spirited stranger who offers to pose as his girlfriend so that he will not have to explain the breakup to his family.

Carlinhos reluctantly accepts the plan, but quickly realizes it was a mistake, as the uninhibited Graça shakes up the formal dinner in Lady Sofia's mansion. As the holidays go on, he learns that Graça lost her father, who used to work as Santa Claus, and that since his death she has spent every Christmas with a different family to avoid being alone. The more time they spend together, the closer Carlinhos and Graça become. When Bebela suddenly reappears and Graça's secret is exposed by Carlinhos's cousin, the fake relationship falls apart, and Carlinhos must decide whether he can trust his feelings before the New Year arrives.

The film follows the familiar fake-relationship formula of holiday romantic comedies, mixing family chaos, humor and the theme of finding belonging during Christmas.

Christmas Full of Grace premiered on Netflix on November 30, 2022. Among its memorable moments are a visit to a Christmas festival where Graça runs into one of the families she once spent the holidays with, and a reconciliation at a New Year's Eve party.

overview: An urgent phone call pulls a Yale Law student back to his Ohio hometown, where he reflects on three generations of family history and his own future.
tagline: Inspired by a true story three generations in the making.
title: Hillbilly Elegy
plot:
Hillbilly Elegy is a 2020 American biographical drama directed by Ron Howard from a screenplay by Vanessa Taylor, based on JD Vance's 2016 memoir, who later became the 50th vice president of the United States. It stars Amy Adams as Vance's mother, Bev, and Glenn Close as his grandmother, Mamaw, with Gabriel Basso as the adult JD, Owen Asztalos as young JD, Haley Bennett as his sister Lindsay, Freida Pinto as his girlfriend Usha, and Bo Hopkins in his final film role as Papaw.

The story moves between two periods. In 2011, JD is a student at Yale Law School, working several jobs to pay his way and hoping to land a summer internship, when his sister calls to say that their mother has overdosed on heroin. He drives back to his hometown of Middletown, Ohio, to deal with the crisis, while trying to make it back in time for a crucial job interview.

Through flashbacks, the film recalls JD's childhood in the late 1990s, as the son of a family with roots in Appalachian Kentucky. His mother, Bev, struggles with addiction and violent mood swings, which bring a series of boyfriends, the loss of her job for stealing pills at work and terrifying outbursts. JD, falling into bad company as a teenager, finds stability when his tough, foul-mouthed grandmother Mamaw takes him in and pushes him to work hard at school and make something of his life. Encouraged by her, he goes on to join the Marine Corps and later college. In the present, JD struggles to find his mother a place in rehab and must decide how much of himself he can give to his family without sacrificing the future he has worked so hard to build.

The film explores poverty, addiction and family loyalty in working-class America, centering on the bond between three generations.

Given a limited theatrical release on November 11, 2020, before streaming on Netflix from November 24, Hillbilly Elegy was poorly received, with 24 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 38. Close received Academy Award, Golden Globe and SAG nominations, and the film was nominated for Best Makeup and Hairstyling, but it also earned three Golden Raspberry nominations.

overview: Rachel Watson, devastated by her recent divorce, spends her daily commute fantasizing about the seemingly perfect couple who live in a house that her train passes every day, until one morning she sees something shocking happen there and becomes entangled in the mystery that unfolds.
tagline: What you see can hurt you.
title: The Girl on the Train
plot:
The Girl on the Train is a 2016 American psychological thriller directed by Tate Taylor from a screenplay by Erin Cressida Wilson, adapted from Paula Hawkins's 2015 novel of the same name. Emily Blunt plays Rachel Watson, an alcoholic divorcée who becomes caught up in a missing-person case, alongside Rebecca Ferguson as Anna, Haley Bennett as Megan Hipwell, Justin Theroux as Tom, Luke Evans as Scott, with Allison Janney, Édgar Ramírez and Lisa Kudrow.

Having lost her job and her marriage, Rachel rides the commuter train into New York City every day aimlessly, fixating on the house of her ex-husband Tom and his new wife Anna, and that of their neighbours Scott and Megan. Megan had worked as the nanny to Tom and Anna's baby before quitting. Rachel's marriage collapsed after depression over her infertility drove her to drink, and she believes she once humiliated Tom at a barbecue thrown by his boss, costing him his job. She still harasses the couple when drunk. One day she sees Megan kissing a man who is not her husband; she sets off to confront her, then wakes up hours later in bed, covered in blood. When Megan is reported missing, Riley questions Rachel, who was seen nearby.

Posing as Megan's friend, Rachel tells Scott of the affair and identifies the man as Megan's psychiatrist, Abdic. Rachel books a session with Abdic herself and learns that Megan, as a very young mother, had lost a baby who drowned in the bath. Megan's body is then found; she was pregnant, but neither Scott nor Abdic was the father. A furious Scott attacks Rachel for lying to him, though CCTV clears him of the murder. On the train Rachel meets Martha, the wife of Tom's former boss, who tells her that at the barbecue she had merely been ill and gone to lie down, and that Tom was fired for sexually harassing colleagues. Rachel realises Tom has fed her false memories of her blackouts and hurt her during them. Anna finds a hidden phone that belonged to Megan, and a now sober Rachel recalls seeing Megan with Tom on the day she vanished, and Tom hitting Rachel when she confronted them. When the women confront him, Tom knocks Rachel out and tries to kill her, but she stabs him in the neck with a corkscrew and Anna finishes him off. The two tell Riley he died in self-defence.

Released by Universal Pictures, the film grossed $173.2 million worldwide on a $45 million budget. Critics praised Blunt but found the story melodramatic; it scored 44% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: While Sergeant John Tyree is home on two weeks leave from Germany, he meets Savannah after he dives into the ocean to retrieve Savannah's purse that had fallen off a pier. John eventually falls in love with Savannah, who promises to write to him until he returns from overseas.
tagline: Love brought them together. Will fate tear them apart?
title: Dear John
plot:
Dear John is a 2010 American romantic drama film directed by Lasse Hallström and starring Channing Tatum and Amanda Seyfried.

The movie follows the story of John Tyree, a U.S. Army soldier who falls in love with Savannah Lynn Curtis, a college student, while on leave during his deployment to Iraq. The two share a whirlwind romance, but their relationship is put to the test when John is deployed again, and Savannah must navigate her feelings for him from afar.

The main themes of Dear John include:

1. Love vs. Duty: The film explores the conflict between following one's heart and fulfilling one's duty. John is torn between his love for Savannah and his commitment to serving his country.
2. Long-distance relationships: The movie highlights the challenges of maintaining a relationship when physical distance separates the partners. John and Savannah must navigate the difficulties of communication, trust, and intimacy despite being apart.
3. Sacrifice and loyalty: As John prepares to deploy again, he is forced to confront the reality of his situation and make sacrifices for the sake of his country. This theme is echoed in Savannah's own struggles with her feelings for John and her desire to support him.
4. Coming-of-age: The film can also be seen as a coming-of-age story for both John and Savannah, as they navigate their first loves, independence, and adulthood.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $215 million worldwide. Despite its flaws, Dear John remains a romantic drama that explores the complexities of love, duty, and sacrifice in the face of adversity.

overview: The Guardians of Arcadia reunite to battle the nefarious Arcane Order, who've reawakened the primordial Titans.
tagline: They will rise.
title: Trollhunters: Rise of the Titans
plot:
Trollhunters: Rise of the Titans is a 2021 American computer-animated fantasy action film directed by Johane Matte, Francisco Ruiz Velasco and Andrew Schmidt, and written by Guillermo del Toro, Marc Guggenheim and Dan and Kevin Hageman. It is the finale of del Toro's Tales of Arcadia franchise, which includes the series Trollhunters, 3Below and Wizards, and brings together the heroes of all three shows. The voice cast includes Emile Hirsch, Lexi Medrano, Charlie Saxton, Kelsey Grammer, Alfred Molina, Steven Yeun, Nick Frost, Colin O'Donoghue, Diego Luna, Tatiana Maslany and Nick Offerman.

A year after the events of Wizards, the master wizard Douxie and Nari, a former member of the villainous Arcane Order, lure the Order's Belloc and Skrael onto a subway train, where they are joined by the former Trollhunter Jim Lake Jr., his girlfriend Claire and his best friend Toby. The battle goes badly: Jim is wounded, the train runs out of control, and Nari is captured by the Order after swapping bodies with Douxie in an attempt to deceive them.

Regrouping in a rebuilt Camelot, the heroes learn from Blinky that the Arcane Order intends to awaken the Titans, giant ancient beings, and have them converge on Arcadia Oaks, the center of the universe, to destroy and remake the world. Before her connection is broken, Nari passes Jim a cryptic message about a ninth configuration and an artifact called the Krohnisfere. Failing to prevent the ritual that breaks the Genesis Seals, the heroes split into teams that travel across the world, from Hong Kong to Brazil and Greenland, to stop the rising Titans. As allies fall and the final Titan approaches Arcadia, Jim must uncover the meaning of Nari's words and rally his friends for a battle on which the fate of everything depends.

The film emphasizes friendship, sacrifice and destiny, offering a conclusion that ties together the many characters and storylines of the franchise.

Rise of the Titans was released on Netflix on July 21, 2021. It received positive reviews, with an 88 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics; Den of Geek praised its stakes, visual effects, imagination and humor, while noting that few characters other than Jim receive full development.

overview: Dragon Hunters is a fantastic tale telling the adventures of two dragon hunters: the world has become a vast conglomerate of islands of varying size and shape. This babbling universe is mainly peopled with ruthless rogues, surly peasants and illiterate, petty lords Their main concerns revolve around two fundamental rules : Eat and don't get eaten.
tagline: Dragon hunting isn't a fairy tale
title: Dragon Hunters
plot:
Dragon Hunters (French: Chasseurs de dragons) is a 2008 animated fantasy adventure directed by Arthur Qwak and Guillaume Ivernel, written by Frédéric Engel-Lenoir, with music by Klaus Badelt. Produced by Futurikon with LuxAnimation, Mac Guff Ligne and Trixter, it features the French voices of Vincent Lindon, Patrick Timsit and Marie Drion, and in the English version Forest Whitaker, Rob Paulsen and Mary Mouser. It is set in the same creative universe as the Dragon Hunters television series.

The story takes place in a world that has broken into countless floating islands of all shapes and sizes, drifting through the sky. This dizzying universe is populated by rogues, peasants and petty lords, all struggling to survive in a land overrun by ravenous creatures known as dragons, which come in many bizarre forms and wreak havoc wherever they go.

Lian-Chu and Gwizdo are two dragon hunters who are far from the best in their profession. Lian-Chu is a huge, gentle giant with a heart of gold, while Gwizdo is a scrawny, greedy schemer with a talent for scams. Their shared dream is to retire to a farm where they can raise sheep in peace. Meanwhile, in a fortress a few islands away, the fearful Lord Arnold lives in dread of the World Gobbler, a monstrous dragon that awakens every twenty seasons to spread destruction, and that no one has ever defeated or survived to describe. His young niece Zoe, who idolizes heroes from storybooks, decides to take matters into her own hands. Convinced that Lian-Chu and Gwizdo are the champions of her dreams, she recruits them, and the unlikely trio set off on a perilous journey to the end of the world to confront the beast.

The film combines comedy and adventure with a story about friendship, courage and the gap between legend and reality.

Dragon Hunters was released in France on March 26, 2008, and performed modestly internationally, grossing about 12.2 million dollars worldwide, with strong results in Brazil. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 67 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics.

overview: After being wrongfully expelled from Harvard University, American Matt Buckner flees to his sister's home in England. Once there, he is befriended by her charming and dangerous brother-in-law, Pete Dunham, and introduced to the underworld of British football hooliganism. Matt learns to stand his ground through a friendship that develops against the backdrop of this secret and often violent world. 'Green Street Hooligans' is a story of loyalty, trust and the sometimes brutal consequences of living close to the edge.
tagline: Just think of someone you hate.
title: Green Street Hooligans
plot:
Green Street Hooligans is a 2005 British sports drama film directed by Lexi Alexander and written by Paul Anderson. The movie follows the story of Danny Meehan, a young Englishman who gets caught up in the world of professional football hooliganism.

The main themes of Green Street Hooligans include:

1. **The struggle for identity**: Danny Meehan is a troubled teenager trying to find his place in the world. His involvement with the Green Street gang helps him discover his sense of belonging and purpose.
2. **The allure and danger of hooliganism**: The film portrays the thrill and excitement of being part of a group, but also highlights the violence, aggression, and lawlessness associated with football hooliganism.
3. **Friendship and loyalty**: Danny forms strong bonds with his fellow gang members, particularly Luke, who becomes like a brother to him. These relationships are tested as they navigate the dangers of their lifestyle.
4. **The consequences of violence**: The movie shows how violence can escalate quickly, leading to tragic consequences for those involved. This theme serves as a warning about the destructive nature of hooliganism.
5. **Coming of age and self-discovery**: Through his experiences, Danny learns valuable lessons about himself, his values, and what he wants to achieve in life.

The film features a talented young cast, including Elijah Wood, Charlie Hunnam, and Claire Forlani. The movie received generally positive reviews for its gritty portrayal of football hooliganism and its exploration of themes relevant to young men's lives.

Overall, Green Street Hooligans is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the complexities of male friendships, loyalty, and the consequences of violence.

overview: A young undercover FBI agent infiltrates a gang of thieves who share a common interest in extreme sports. A remake of the 1991 film, "Point Break".
tagline: The only law that matters is gravity
title: Point Break
plot:
Point Break is a 2015 action thriller directed and shot by Ericson Core and written by Kurt Wimmer, a remake of the 1991 film of the same name that starred Patrick Swayze and Keanu Reeves. An American, German and Chinese co-production, it stars Luke Bracey as Johnny Utah, a former extreme athlete turned FBI recruit, Édgar Ramírez as Bodhi, the charismatic leader of a group of thrill-seeking criminals, Teresa Palmer as Samsara, Ray Winstone as FBI agent Angelo Pappas and Delroy Lindo.

Utah, a motocross star, gives up extreme sports after his best friend dies during a stunt. Seven years later, as a candidate to become an FBI agent, he studies a series of spectacular crimes, including a diamond heist from a skyscraper in Mumbai with an escape by parachute and a raid in Mexico in which stolen cash is scattered over the countryside. He concludes that the robberies were carried out by the same team, which is attempting to complete the Ozaki 8, a series of eight extreme ordeals meant to honor the forces of nature.

Predicting that the group will attempt the next ordeal on a giant wave in France, Utah goes undercover with Pappas. After nearly drowning, he is rescued by Bodhi and welcomed into his circle, where he meets Samsara and is drawn into a world of daring feats, including wingsuit flying through Alpine cliffs and extreme snowboarding down a steep mountain. As Utah grows closer to the group and begins to share their philosophy, he becomes torn between loyalty to his new friends and his duty as an agent, while the gang's actions grow increasingly dangerous and deadly. Utah must ultimately stop Bodhi before the final ordeal.

The film puts its emphasis on real extreme sports stunts shot in locations around the world, presenting the robberies as acts of eco-activism.

Released in China on December 4, 2015, and in the United States on December 25 by Warner Bros., Point Break grossed about 134 million dollars against a 105 million dollar budget. Critics considered it inferior to the original, giving it 11 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 34.

overview: When Emily Woodrow and her friends happen on a treasure chest full of gold coins, they fail to to heed the warnings of a wise old psychic who had foretold that they would encounter trouble with a very nasty and protective Leprechaun.
tagline: Evil has a whole new rap!
title: Leprechaun: Back 2 tha Hood
plot:
Leprechaun: Back to the Hood is a 2003 American horror-comedy film directed by Rob Spera and starring Curtis Armstrong, J.C. Brandy, and Eddie Griffin.

The main themes of Leprechaun: Back to the Hood revolve around the struggle for power, revenge, and redemption in an urban setting. The movie follows the story of a group of teenagers who unwittingly unleash the vengeful spirit of the Leprechaun, played by Warwick Davis, on their neighborhood.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the Leprechaun's primary motivation is to reclaim his stolen gold and exact revenge on those who wronged him. However, as he navigates the urban jungle, he begins to realize that there are more complex issues at play, such as poverty, racism, and social inequality.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with their own personal demons and confront the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood. The movie explores themes of identity, community, and the struggle for survival in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, the Leprechaun's quest for revenge becomes a metaphor for the cyclical nature of violence and the need for redemption and forgiveness. The film's ending suggests that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for change and a chance to start anew.

Overall, Leprechaun: Back to the Hood offers a unique blend of horror-comedy and social commentary, making it a fascinating and thought-provoking watch.

overview: Catherine Clare reluctantly trades life in 1980 Manhattan for a remote home in the tiny hamlet of Chosen, New York, after her husband George lands a job teaching art history at a small Hudson Valley college. Even as she does her best to transform the old dairy farm into a place where young daughter Franny will be happy, Catherine increasingly finds herself isolated and alone. She soon comes to sense a sinister darkness lurking both in the walls of the ramshackle property—and in her marriage to George.
tagline: Mistrust your senses.
title: Things Heard & Seen
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "Things Heard & Seen" released in 2021 by Likely Story. 

However, I found that there is a movie titled "Things Heard & Seen" released in 2022, directed by Shari Springer Berman and Robert Pulcini, not Likely Story.

The movie "Things Heard & Seen" (2022) is a psychological thriller starring Amanda Seyfried as Catherine, a young woman who moves to the countryside with her husband, but discovers that their new home has a dark history. 

As for the main themes of the movie, it explores several ideas such as:

1. The power of secrets and hidden histories: The movie delves into the idea that the past can be both fascinating and terrifying, and how secrets can shape our present.
2. Isolation and loneliness: Catherine's move to the countryside is meant to bring her closer to nature and her husband, but she finds herself increasingly isolated and alone, highlighting the difficulties of building a new life in a remote area.
3. The blurring of reality and fantasy: As Catherine becomes more entrenched in the history of their home, she begins to question what is real and what is just her imagination, leading to a sense of disorientation and unease.

These themes are woven throughout the movie, creating a complex and suspenseful narrative that keeps the viewer engaged until the very end.

overview: London, 1956. Genius actor and film director Laurence Olivier is about to begin the shooting of his upcoming movie, premiered in 1957 as The Prince and the Showgirl, starring Marilyn Monroe. Young Colin Clark, who dreams on having a career in movie business, manages to get a job on the set as third assistant director.
tagline: She's worth all the trouble
title: My Week with Marilyn
plot:
"My Week with Marilyn" is a 2011 British comedy-drama film directed by Simon Curtis, starring Michelle Williams as Marilyn Monroe and Kenneth Branagh as Colin Chilvers. The movie is based on the 2000 biography "Not So Pretty Foolish Heart" by Kenneth Anger.

The main themes of "My Week with Marilyn" include:

1. **Mental Health**: The film explores Marilyn's struggles with mental health, including her depression and anxiety. Her fragile state is exacerbated by the pressures of fame, relationships, and the Hollywood system.
2. **Identity Crisis**: Marilyn's character grapples with her identity, torn between her persona as a movie star and her desire for authenticity and connection. This theme is reflected in her complicated relationships with those around her.
3. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Despite being surrounded by people, Marilyn feels deeply lonely and isolated. Her inability to form genuine connections with others is a recurring theme throughout the film.
4. **The Objectification of Women**: The movie critiques the way women are objectified in society, particularly in the entertainment industry. Marilyn's character is both a symbol of femininity and a victim of the patriarchal system that exploits her for male pleasure.
5. **The Illusion of Hollywood Glamour**: "My Week with Marilyn" offers a behind-the-scenes look at the glamour and superficiality of old Hollywood. The film highlights the artificial nature of the movie industry, where people are reduced to their public personas.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a nuanced portrayal of Marilyn Monroe's life, both on and off screen.

overview: After breaking up with his longtime stage partner, a famous but jaded Vegas magician fights for relevance when a new, "hip" street magician appears on the scene.
tagline: Abracatastic!
title: The Incredible Burt Wonderstone
plot:
The Incredible Burt Wonderstone is a 2013 American comedy film directed by Don Scardino and starring Steve Carell, Ryan Reynolds, and Mark Ruffalo. 

At its core, the movie explores themes of identity, friendship, and the blurred lines between reality and illusion. The story revolves around Burt Wonderstone (played by Steve Carell), a successful magician who has lost his edge after being upstaged by a young and charismatic rival, Anton Marvel (played by James Marsden). As Burt navigates this crisis of confidence, he must confront the fragility of his own identity and the true nature of his craft.

Throughout the film, the main characters grapple with the tension between authenticity and artifice, as they struggle to maintain their illusions in a world that is increasingly skeptical of magic. The movie also delves into the complexities of male friendship, particularly the complicated dynamic between Burt and his rival Anton, who represents both a threat and an opportunity for growth.

Ultimately, The Incredible Burt Wonderstone is a film about finding one's true self and learning to let go of the need for control and perfection. It's a story that balances humor with heart, using the world of magic as a metaphor for the human experience.

overview: A young man who was sentenced to 7 years in prison for robbing a post office ends up spending 30 years in solitary confinement. During this time, his own personality is supplanted by his alter ego, Charles Bronson.
tagline: The Man. The Myth. The Celebrity.
title: Bronson
plot:
Bronson is a 2008 British biographical prison film and black comedy directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, who co-wrote it with Brock Norman Brock. Tom Hardy stars as Michael Peterson, the man who took the name Charles Bronson in 1987 and came to be regarded as Britain's most violent prisoner, responsible for around a dozen hostage-takings behind bars. Matt King, James Lance, Kelly Adams and Amanda Burton co-star.

Peterson recounts his own life with mocking, self-deprecating humour, sometimes speaking straight to the camera in prison clothes and sometimes performing it as a stage act before a theatre audience. In 1974, aged 22, he robs a post office and receives seven years, but his violence inside keeps lengthening the sentence. Moved to a psychiatric hospital, he is sedated with drugs he says sap his strength, and in 1978 he tries to win a transfer back to prison by attempting to strangle a fellow inmate, a self-confessed paedophile, stopping short of murder. He points out that, for all his years in confinement, he has never killed anyone. He claims that a rooftop protest in 1982, which caused enormous damage, led the authorities to declare him sane and release him in 1987.

Free again, he visits his parents and his predatory Uncle Jack, who reunites him with a former inmate who arranges bare-knuckle fights and gives him the ring name Charles Bronson, after the American actor. On New Year's Day 1988 he steals a ring to propose to a woman who tells him he was only a fling, and after sixty-nine days of freedom he is back in jail. In 1993 he takes a prison librarian hostage, greases his naked body for the coming brawl with the guards, and is warned by the governor that he will die inside. In 1999 an art teacher sees promise in his drawings and Bronson briefly becomes a model prisoner, but when the art class is to close he seizes the teacher, paints himself black and arranges his captive as a living copy of René Magritte's The Son of Man before summoning the guards for another beating. Closing text notes that he has spent some thirty years in solitary confinement with no release date.

Hardy spoke with the real Bronson by phone before meeting him, and Bronson praised his portrayal. Filming took place in and around Nottingham. The film grossed about $2.3 million and drew positive reviews for Hardy's performance, holding 75% on Rotten Tomatoes and 71 on Metacritic, though some critics objected to its violence.

overview: A disgraced doctor and his family are held hostage at their home by criminals on the run, when a robbery-gone-awry requires them to seek immediate medical attention.
title: Survive the Night
plot:
Survive the Night, formerly titled The Long Night, is a 2020 American action thriller directed by Matt Eskandari. Chad Michael Murray plays Rich Clark, a disgraced doctor, and Bruce Willis plays his father Frank, with Shea Buckner and Tyler Jon Olson as the criminal brothers Jamie and Matthias Granger and Lydia Hull as Jan Clark.

The story begins with a robbery that goes badly wrong. Jamie impulsively tries to rob a garage, but the owner resists; Jamie shoots a hostage, and Matthias takes a bullet in the leg. The two get away, but Matthias urgently needs medical help, so they force their way into the home of Rich, a physician whose career is in ruins, and take him and his family hostage, demanding that he remove the bullet. Frank, Rich's father, discovers that his wife has been killed.

Rich manages to extract the bullet, but Frank seizes the moment, grabs the scalpel and slashes Jamie, who stabs him with a kitchen knife; wounded, Frank escapes into the darkness. Rich then threatens to sever Matthias's artery, but Jamie shoots Rich in the shoulder. Matthias is left helpless, because Rich has not closed the wound and has only clamped it to stop the bleeding. Frank creeps back to the house, finds his wife's body and sees his injured son through a window; the two meet in the garage, where Rich talks his father through treating his own wound, while the brothers weigh what to do next.

At dawn Jamie sets out to hunt down and kill the family. Jan and Riley are hiding together in an outbuilding, and father and son resolve to strike back: Jamie is stunned by Rich in the garage, and Frank lures him away from the house with the car. Jamie returns, however, and catches Rich from behind as he reunites with Jan, knocking him out. When Rich comes to, Jamie forces him to finish the operation, but Matthias dies on the table. Frank slips back inside and frees Jan, who stops Jamie from shooting Rich, fires at him and misses, and runs from the house with Jamie in pursuit. Rich grabs a gun, follows them and shoots Jamie dead, and the surviving family members are reunited on the porch.

The film was shot in Columbus, Georgia, in only ten days and released in the United States on May 22, 2020. Reviews were poor: it holds 13% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 26, indicating generally unfavourable reviews.

overview: A man will become a criminal to save his family.  Director: Shawn Welling  Writer: Derek H. Potts  Stars: Tom Vera, Tom Sizemore, Lee Majors |
tagline: A man will become a criminal to save his family.
title: Narco Sub
plot: A former U.S. Navy Seal is forced to become the international criminal he once fought against when a powerful and violent drug cartel kidnaps his wife and daughter.

overview: John Quincy Archibald is a father and husband whose son is diagnosed with an enlarged heart and then finds out he cannot receive a transplant because HMO insurance will not cover it. Therefore, he decides to take a hospital full of patients hostage until the hospital puts his son's name on the donor's list.
tagline: Give a father no options and you leave him no choice.
title: John Q
plot:
John Q is a 2002 American drama film directed by Nick Cassavetes and starring Denzel Washington. The movie revolves around the life of John Quincy Archibald, a father who will do anything to save his ailing son.

The main themes of John Q include:

1. **Patriotism and Self-Sacrifice**: John Q is a classic tale of patriotism and self-sacrifice. Denzel Washington's character, John Quincy Archibald, is willing to risk everything to save his son, demonstrating the depth of his love and devotion.

2. **Healthcare System Critique**: The film critiques the US healthcare system, highlighting its flaws and inefficiencies. John Q's desperate attempt to get his son the necessary treatment exposes the system's shortcomings and raises questions about access to quality care.

3. **Family and Love**: The movie showcases the unbreakable bond between a father and son. John Q's actions are motivated by his love for his child, and he will stop at nothing to ensure his son receives the medical attention he needs.

4. **Social Inequality and Class Struggle**: The film touches on social inequality and class struggle, as John Q navigates the complexities of the healthcare system, which often favors those with more resources.

5. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Throughout the movie, John Q undergoes a transformation from a desperate father to a selfless hero. His actions lead to redemption and personal growth, both for himself and those around him.

The film's themes are thought-provoking and timely, making John Q a powerful and emotional cinematic experience.

overview: Recounts the story of fledgling writer Samuel Liston and his experiences with Floyd Deveraux, the enigmatic, middle-aged father of two who enlists Samuel to write his biography.
tagline: A 'cerebral' comedy.
title: Big Gold Brick
plot:
Big Gold Brick is a 2022 American black comedy with surreal and fantasy elements, written and directed by Brian Petsos in his feature directorial debut. It stars Emory Cohen as the struggling writer Samuel Liston and Andy Garcia as Floyd Deveraux, with Megan Fox as Floyd's second wife and attorney Jacqueline, Lucy Hale as his daughter Lily, Leonidas Castrounis as his son Edward, Oscar Isaac as Anselm, Shiloh Fernandez as Roy and Frederick Schmidt as Percy. Justin Hori composed the score; the film runs 132 minutes.

The story is framed as Samuel's account of how he met Floyd, a memoir that later becomes a literary sensation. At his lowest point, a despondent Samuel leaves his apartment, rides a bus out of town and wanders the streets until he is struck by a Cadillac driven by Floyd, an enigmatic, middle-aged father of two who was eating ice cream at the wheel. Mortified at having badly injured him, Floyd visits him in the hospital and offers a deal: free room and board in his large suburban home and 500 dollars in cash a week if Samuel will write his biography. Samuel moves in with the eccentric Deveraux family, which includes Jacqueline, who at one point attempts to seduce him, the tween Edward, a death metal fan with disturbing interests, and the teenage Lily, a former violin prodigy who walked away from her career by smashing her instrument at a recital. As he listens to Floyd's tall tales, Samuel is plagued by vivid nightmares and hallucinations, including a talking Santa doll in his room, and the line between reality and delusion blurs, especially after the menacing, inhaler-using Anselm draws him and Floyd into violent trouble.

Principal photography began in Toronto in May 2019. Samuel Goldwyn Films acquired distribution rights in June 2021 and released the film in theaters and on digital platforms on 25 February 2022. Critical reception was largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes reported a 21 percent approval rating from 34 reviews, with a consensus faulting its quirkiness, visual tricks and crowded narrative for hiding a lack of purpose, and Metacritic gave it 30 out of 100. Glenn Kenny of RogerEbert.com dismissed it as bloated, strained and unfunny, arguing that Petsos echoes Richard Kelly, Wes Anderson, David Lynch and the Coen brothers without doing anything useful with those influences. Time's review was kinder, singling out Garcia's suave, eccentric performance as the film's main asset.

overview: A recently widowed detective still grieving over his wife's death discovers a shocking connection between himself and the suspects in a serial killing spree linked to the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
tagline: Four victims. Four painful secrets.
title: Horsemen
plot:
Horsemen is a 2009 American psychological thriller directed by Jonas Åkerlund, written by David Callaham and produced by Michael Bay. It stars Dennis Quaid as Aidan Breslin, a detective and forensic dentistry expert, and Zhang Ziyi as Kristen, the adopted daughter of one of the victims, with Lou Taylor Pucci, Clifton Collins Jr., Barry Shabaka Henley, Neal McDonough and Peter Stormare. The film was shot over eight weeks in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

Breslin is a widower who has become emotionally distant from his two sons, Alex and Sean, since his wife's death. Because of his expertise in dental forensics, he is called to a strange crime scene containing human teeth and the painted words "come and see". Soon after, a woman named Mrs. Spitz is found suspended from a hook contraption in her bedroom, the same message written on the walls, and the autopsy reveals that she was pregnant and that the fetus has been removed. Breslin concludes that four attackers were involved and that they filmed the murder.

As more victims are found in similarly staged scenes, a tattoo parlor owner who built four of the hook devices offers a lead, and a remark from his son Sean leads Breslin to the Bible. He realizes that the killings are modeled on the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse from the Book of Revelation, with each crime representing War, Famine, Pestilence or Death. Kristen unexpectedly confesses to the murder of her adoptive mother, revealing a disturbing history of abuse in the Spitz household. As the remaining killers carry out their ritual and Breslin struggles to uncover who is behind the group, the investigation leads him closer to his own home and family than he could have imagined.

The film combines a serial killer mystery with themes of parental neglect, abuse and alienated youth, presented with heavily stylized visuals and graphic violence.

Horsemen received a limited release in the United States on March 6, 2009, before arriving on home video in July. It was poorly received, with 17 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews; Variety's Jordan Mintzer found it predictable and full of clichés such as overstylized torture, whiplash editing and crude neon lighting.

overview: A pregnant woman, who is taking care of her son with development problems, is at her breaking point when a caregiver from the Philippines steps into her life. Diana suspects that she’s using voodoo against her after the quick improvements of her son.
tagline: No one will save her from his child
title: Mother
plot:
Mother (Spanish: Madre) is a 2016 Chilean psychological horror thriller written and directed by Aaron Burns, an actor and visual effects supervisor who had worked with Eli Roth on The Green Inferno and Knock Knock; it was his second feature as director after Blacktino. Produced by Miguel Asensio Llamas and Nicolás López as the first feature from Purgatorio, a horror label within Sobras International Pictures dedicated to Latin American folklore, it stars Daniela Ramírez, Cristóbal Tapia Montt, Aida Jabolin, Matías Bassi, Nicolás Durán, Ignacia Allamand, Cristián Carvajal and Igal Furman. The dialogue is in Spanish, and Antonio Quercia photographed the film, with music by Manuel Riveiro.

Diana Prieto (Ramírez), a well-off housewife in Santiago, is pregnant with her second child while struggling to care for her first, Martin (Bassi), a boy of about ten with severe autism who can be unpredictably violent and must be restrained at night so he does not hurt himself. Her husband Tomás (Tapia Montt) is often away on business trips to Japan, and every nanny they hire quits within days. When Martin has a violent outburst in a supermarket, a Filipina employee, Luz (Jabolin), calms him almost instantly. Diana hires her, and Luz explains that her own son David (Durán) was once like Martin and is now cured. Under her care Martin improves dramatically, but Diana grows uneasy: Luz speaks to the boy only in her own language, takes him off his medication without permission, and strange homemade charms begin turning up around the house. Using an instant translation app, Diana becomes convinced that Luz is turning her son against her through voodoo, and as she suffers nausea, rashes and hallucinations, she begins to fear that the nanny is poisoning her too, in a game that may prove deadly.

The film premiered at AFI Fest in 2016 and screened at South by Southwest in March 2017, where Netflix acquired its worldwide streaming rights. Released in Chilean theaters on 27 April 2017, it had the best opening of the year for a Chilean film, with about 20,000 admissions in its first week, before streaming on Netflix. Reviewing it at SXSW, Dennis Harvey of Variety called it a flat, derivative blend of the "nanny from hell" thriller and Rosemary's Baby, criticizing its lack of suspense, pedestrian shock imagery, Ramírez's unsympathetic characterization and an unsatisfying ending.

overview: When odd reports are received through official channels stating that the President of the United States is being held captive on a secret international moon base called Vegan and that he has been replaced on Earth by a clone, the US Marshall Service immediately sends their 'best' man, Dix, on the mission.
tagline: The most outer spaced-out comedy ever!
title: 2001: A Space Travesty
plot:
2001: A Space Travesty is a 2000 satirical science fiction comedy film directed by Allan A. Goldstein. Leslie Nielsen stars as Marshal Richard "Dick" Dix, a bumbling special agent, with Ophélie Winter, Peter Egan, Ezio Greggio, Alexandra Kamp and Verona Pooth in supporting roles. Despite its title, the film parodies 2001: A Space Odyssey in only a few sequences, aiming its spoofs at a wide range of science fiction films and at American politics of the era. It was filmed in Canada as an international co-production.

Dix, a special agent, ends a terrorist hostage situation at a fast-food restaurant in his own chaotic fashion, to the annoyance of the police chief. At headquarters, his superior introduces him to Cassandra Menage, who explains that the President of the United States, a thinly veiled caricature of Bill Clinton who is never named, has been kidnapped and replaced by a clone. Dix is sent by space shuttle to Vegan, a base on the Moon where the cloning is believed to have taken place, causing mayhem throughout the journey.

On arrival, Dix is greeted at security by Lieutenant Bradford Shitzu and is soon confronted by strange incidents involving the aliens who live in the colony. He shares quarters with Captain Valentino DiPasquale, played by Greggio, and sets out to question the main suspect, Dr. Griffin Pratt, who gives him a tour of his cloning facility. Along the way he meets the alluring scientist Dr. Uschi Künstler and attends a party where the suspects are gathered. Stumbling from one misunderstanding to another, and accompanied by a constant stream of sight gags, slapstick and sexual innuendo, Dix tries to uncover the conspiracy behind the cloning, locate the real president and bring him safely back to Earth, while thwarting a plot that threatens the leadership of the free world.

The film received poor reviews. The website Need Coffee acknowledged Nielsen's deadpan comic style but recommended the film only to viewers in the mood for silly, puerile humor, while Jason James of The Nut Gallery gave it one star out of five. It was one of a number of broad spoof comedies that Nielsen headlined in the years following the success of The Naked Gun films, trading on his deadpan persona.

overview: U.S Marshal Mike Donovan has dark memories of the death of his first love. He keeps peace between the Americans and the natives who had temporarily adopted and taken care of him. The evil actions of a white sorcerer lead him to confront the villain in the Sacred Mountains, and, through shamanic rituals conquer his fears and uncover a suppressed memory he would much rather deny.
tagline: The devil you know.
title: Renegade
plot:
Blueberry (French: Blueberry: L'expérience secrète), released in some regions as Renegade, is a 2004 French psychedelic Western directed by Jan Kounen. It is loosely adapted from the Franco-Belgian comic series Blueberry, written by Jean-Michel Charlier and drawn by Jean Giraud, better known as Moebius, although it departs considerably from its source. Vincent Cassel stars as Mike Blueberry, with Juliette Lewis, Michael Madsen, Temuera Morrison, Djimon Hounsou, Eddie Izzard, Tchéky Karyo and Ernest Borgnine. Although a French production, it was filmed in English to suit its setting in the American West of the 1870s.

Mike Blueberry, a marshal in a frontier town, is haunted by fragmented memories of a traumatic event in his youth: the death of the young woman he loved and a violent confrontation with a man named Wallace Blount, which left the young Mike badly injured. Rescued and nursed back to health by a Native American tribe, who taught him their ways and gave him the name Broken Nose, he has since devoted himself to keeping the peace between white settlers and the Native Americans who once adopted him.

That fragile peace is threatened when Blount, a ruthless outlaw with an interest in occult powers, returns to the region. Blount is searching for a legendary treasure hidden in the sacred mountains of the Native Americans, and his actions, along with the greed of other prospectors, threaten to provoke bloodshed between the settlers and the tribe. Blueberry must confront his old enemy in the mountains, and with the help of a shaman, he undergoes a ritual involving a hallucinogenic brew that takes him on a visionary inner journey. Through the experience, he must face his fears and uncover a buried memory of the past that he would much rather deny, leading to a spiritual and physical confrontation with Blount.

The film is noted for its lengthy psychedelic sequences, created with computer-generated imagery and inspired by Kounen's interest in Amazonian shamanism. It was not a critical success in the English-speaking world, receiving a 22 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes from nine reviews. Jamie Russell of the BBC described it as two parts bonkers to one part boring, while other critics found it disappointing for fans of the original comics.

overview: Following a ghost invasion of Manhattan, paranormal enthusiasts Erin Gilbert and Abby Yates, nuclear engineer Jillian Holtzmann, and subway worker Patty Tolan band together to stop the otherworldly threat.
tagline: Who You Gonna Call?
title: Ghostbusters
plot:
Ghostbusters (2016) is a supernatural comedy film directed by Paul Feig, starring Melissa McCarthy, Kristen Wiig, Kate McKinnon, Leslie Jones, Chris Hemsworth, and Bill Murray.

The movie begins with Erin Gilbert (Kristen Wiig), a paranormal researcher who has written a book about ghosts. She meets Abby Yates (Melissa McCarthy), another ghost hunter, at a bar where they share a drink and discuss their shared interest in the supernatural. The two women meet again at a coffee shop, where they discover that they are long-lost friends from college.

As they reconnect, Erin reveals to Abby that she has been researching ghosts for years, but her research was initially met with skepticism by her academic peers. However, after discovering a mysterious entity known as "Rowan," which is connected to an ancient Sumerian deity, Erin and Abby decide to team up and start their own ghost-hunting business.

The two women recruit two other experts: Jillian Holtzmann (Kate McKinnon), a quirky engineer who creates gadgets for the Ghostbusters, and Patty Tolan (Leslie Jones), a street-smart New Yorker with a talent for tracking down supernatural entities. Together, they form a team known as the "Ghostbusters."

The Ghostbusters soon discover that Rowan is connected to an ancient Sumerian deity named Gozer, who was worshipped by a cult in New York City. The cult, led by a charismatic leader named Vinz Clortho (Neil Casey), plans to bring about the apocalypse and resurrect Gozer.

As the Ghostbusters delve deeper into the mystery, they realize that Rowan is not just a simple ghost but a powerful entity with supernatural abilities. They also discover that Erin's past is connected to the cult, which makes her a target for Vinz Clortho.

The team faces numerous challenges as they try to stop the cult and prevent Gozer from being resurrected. Along the way, they encounter various supernatural entities, including ghosts, demons, and otherworldly creatures.

As the stakes grow higher, the Ghostbusters realize that they need to work together to defeat Vinz Clortho and his minions. In a thrilling climax, the team faces off against Vinz Clortho in an epic battle of wits and supernatural powers.

In the end, the Ghostbusters succeed in defeating Gozer and banishing him back to the underworld. The movie concludes with Erin and Abby reflecting on their newfound friendship and the challenges they faced as women in a male-dominated field.

Ghostbusters (2016) is a fun and action-packed film that pays homage to the original 1984 classic while introducing new characters and plot twists. The movie features impressive visual effects, witty humor, and a talented cast of comedic actresses who bring their characters to life with charm and wit.

overview: Two children wake up in the middle of the night to find their father is missing, and all the windows and doors in their home have vanished.
tagline: In this house...
title: Skinamarink
plot:
Skinamarink is a 2022 Canadian experimental horror film written and directed by Kyle Edward Ball in his feature debut. It stars Lucas Paul as four-year-old Kevin and Dali Rose Tetreault as his six-year-old sister Kaylee, with Ross Paul and Jaime Hill as their father and mother. Ball, who had run a YouTube channel recreating nightmares described by viewers, developed the film from his short Heck (2020) and shot it on digital video in his childhood home in Edmonton on a budget of about $15,000.

In 1995, Kevin is injured in what Kaylee says was a sleepwalking accident and is brought home from the hospital. In the middle of the night, the two children wake to find that their father has vanished and that the windows, doors and other objects in the house are gradually disappearing. They settle downstairs in front of the television, watching old cartoons, but the house stays dark: they hear unexplained thumps, find a chair upside down on the ceiling, and discover that the downstairs toilet has disappeared. Kevin wonders whether their father "went with mom," but Kaylee does not want to talk about their mother.

A voice calls Kaylee upstairs, where she sees her father, who tells her to look under the bed, and then her mother, who says that they love the children and tells her to close her eyes before vanishing.
