Unbeknownst to Hal, Carol is actually the daughter of Thomas Wayne, a wealthy businessman with connections to the intergalactic police force known as the Green Lantern Corps.

Hal's life takes a dramatic turn when he is recruited by Abin Sur (voiced by Phil LaMarr), a Green Lantern who has been sent to Earth to find and train a new recruit. Hal is chosen for his bravery, intelligence, and sense of justice, making him an ideal candidate to become the next Green Lantern.

Abin Sur takes Hal to the planet Oa, where he meets other members of the Green Lantern Corps, including Kilowog (voiced by Michael Ironside), a tough but fair instructor who trains new recruits in the ways of the Corps. Hal is given a power ring that allows him to create energy constructs and project energy beams.

As Hal begins his training, he faces various challenges, including battling the villainous Sinestro (voiced by Kevin Kilner), a former Green Lantern turned dictator who seeks to overthrow Abin Sur and take control of the Corps for himself. Hal also meets Ch'p (voiced by Justin Long), a small, insectoid alien who becomes his sidekick.

Throughout the film, Hal struggles with the weight of responsibility that comes with being a Green Lantern. He must balance his desire for adventure and recognition with the need to protect the innocent and uphold justice. With the help of Abin Sur and Kilowog, Hal learns to harness his powers and become a true hero.

In the end, Hal faces off against Sinestro in an epic battle that tests his skills and courage. With the help of his friends and allies, Hal emerges victorious, having proven himself as a worthy Green Lantern. The film concludes with Hal returning to Earth, ready to face new challenges and defend the universe from threats both internal and external.

Overall, Green Lantern: First Flight is an exciting and action-packed origin story that introduces audiences to the iconic character of Hal Jordan and the world of the Green Lantern Corps.

overview: A team of explorers discover a clue to the origins of mankind on Earth, leading them on a journey to the darkest corners of the universe. There, they must fight a terrifying battle to save the future of the human race.
tagline: The Search for Our Beginning Could Lead to Our End.
title: Prometheus
plot:
Prometheus is a 2012 science fiction film directed by Ridley Scott, produced by 20th Century Fox, and distributed by 20th Century Studios. The movie takes place in the year 2093 and serves as a prequel to the Alien franchise.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a group of humans who are searching for answers about the origins of humanity. They discover an ancient alien artifact on Earth, which leads them to a spaceship called the Prometheus. The crew of the Prometheus is led by Captain Janek (played by Guy Pearce) and includes scientists like Dr. Elizabeth Shaw (played by Noomi Rapace), Dr. Charlie Holloway (played by Logan Marshall-Green), and Dr. Peter Weyland (played by Michael Fassbender).

The crew of the Prometheus sets out on a mission to find the origins of humanity, which they believe is connected to an ancient alien species known as the Engineers. They travel through space and eventually arrive at a distant planet called LV-223, where they discover a massive structure that appears to be some sort of temple.

As the crew explores the temple, they begin to uncover clues about the origins of humanity and the purpose of their mission. However, they soon realize that they are not alone on the planet, and that something is hunting them. The crew discovers that the Engineers were responsible for creating life on Earth, but also created a deadly creature known as the Xenomorph.

As the crew delves deeper into the temple, they begin to experience strange occurrences and equipment malfunctions. It becomes clear that the planet's atmosphere is toxic, and that the crew is being hunted by the Xenomorph. The crew tries to escape, but it's too late, and many of them are killed by the creature.

In the end, only a few members of the crew manage to survive, including Dr. Shaw and her partner, Charlie Holloway. They discover that the Engineers had created the Xenomorph as a failsafe to prevent humanity from becoming too powerful. The movie ends with Dr. Shaw and Charlie Holloway escaping the planet in a shuttle, but not before they realize that the true purpose of their mission was not what they expected.

Throughout the movie, there are themes of creation, responsibility, and the dangers of playing god. The film also explores the idea of humanity's place in the universe and our relationship with technology. Overall, Prometheus is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that sets the stage for the Alien franchise.

overview: Eddie, a struggling animal trainer and single dad suddenly finds himself the personal wrangler for a large and lovable St. Bernard whose fabulous movie "audition" catapults the dog to stardom. However, a trio of unscrupulous ne'er-do-wells have plans to kidnap the famous dog and hold him for ransom.
title: Beethoven's Big Break
plot:
Beethoven's Big Break, also known as Beethoven: The Reel Story, is a 2008 American comedy film and the sixth installment in the Beethoven series, effectively rebooting the franchise by disregarding the storylines of the previous five films. It stars Jonathan Silverman as Eddie Thornton, Jennifer Finnigan as Lisa Waters, Moisés Arias as Eddie's son Billy, Eddie Griffin as the director Stanley Mitchell, Rhea Perlman as the producer Patricia Benji and Stephen Tobolowsky as Sal DeMarco, with Oscar Nunez and Joey Fatone as Sal's henchmen and dog trainer Cesar Millan as himself. A dog named Cujo plays the title role.

Eddie Thornton is the assistant to Sal DeMarco, an untalented and egotistical animal show host, and both have been hired to train the animals for a film called Frizzy, the Bichon Frise. When the canine star, Frizzy, is kidnapped and held for ransom, Sal blames Eddie, who is promptly fired by Patricia. She and Stanley refuse to pay the ransom and instead hold auditions to find a new Frizzy, but none of the candidates is right. Unknown to them, the kidnapping was orchestrated by Sal himself with his henchmen, Tick and Bones.

Meanwhile, Billy is walking around town when a huge stray dog begins following him. He takes the dog home and, noticing how it responds to Ludwig van Beethoven's Fifth Symphony, names it Beethoven. Eddie comes home to find his house wrecked by the enormous animal. When Eddie goes to the studio with Billy to collect his pet lizard, Pete, Beethoven bursts onto the set and chases the lizard in a chaotic scene that delights the filmmakers. Beethoven and Eddie are hired on the spot, and Sal is fired. Charged with getting Beethoven to perform stunts, Eddie soon finds the dog untrainable: Beethoven crashes through scenes and makes a sloppy mess, but Stanley thinks the results are even funnier and keeps them in the film. Lisa, the movie's screenwriter, starts spending more time with Beethoven and with Eddie. Seeking revenge for his dismissal, Sal orders his henchmen to kidnap Beethoven, but Eddie, Billy and Lisa track the dog to Sal's show stage and rescue him. Sal and his accomplices are arrested, and Eddie and Lisa begin a relationship.

The film was released direct-to-DVD by Universal Studios Home Entertainment on December 30, 2008. Common Sense Media rated it three out of five stars, and Kevin Carr of 7M Pictures said its slapstick humor would make it a sure-fire hit with young children.

original_title: 劇場版 FAIRY TAIL 鳳凰の巫女
overview: The film revolves around a mysterious girl named Éclair who appears before Fairy Tail, the world's most notorious wizard's guild. She lost all of her memories, except for the imperative that she must deliver two Phoenix Stones somewhere. The stones may spell the collapse of the magical world, and Natsu, Lucy, and the rest of the Fairy Tail guild are caught up in the intrigue.
title: Fairy Tail: Phoenix Priestess
plot:
Fairy Tail the Movie: Phoenix Priestess (Japanese: 劇場版 FAIRY TAIL 鳳凰の巫女) is a 2012 Japanese animated fantasy action comedy film, the first based on Hiro Mashima's manga Fairy Tail. It was directed by Masaya Fujimori from a screenplay by Masashi Sogo, with Mashima serving as story planner. Tetsuya Kakihara, Aya Hirano, Rie Kugimiya, Yuichi Nakamura and others reprise their roles from the anime series, and Aya Endō voices the title character Éclair, with Mika Kanai as her bird-like companion Momon.

After Natsu Dragneel and his team from the Fairy Tail guild defeat a gang of bandits in the port town of Negura but fail to stop their leader escaping, Lucy Heartfilia meets Éclair, an amnesiac priestess from the Fire Village who distrusts magic and carries one half of her village's Phoenix Stone. Éclair lets the team accompany her to deliver the stone to the wizard Kalard in the monster-filled Boundary Forest. Meanwhile, Duke Cream, the vain ruler of the neighboring country of Veronica, who holds the stone's other half, sends Dist and his Carbuncle guild to capture her. In the forest, a holographic message from the long-dead Kalard reveals that he was Éclair's father and had devised a spell to neutralize the stone's cursed magic. Éclair bonds with Lucy over the loss of their fathers.

Returning to Magnolia, the team finds the guildhall destroyed by Carbuncle and Éclair taken. Learning that Cream intends to unite the stone halves to summon a phoenix and gain immortality, Natsu leads a rescue to Veronica. Éclair regains her memories as Cream prepares to sacrifice her, and Momon dies saving her. The summoned phoenix appears as a giant monster, Dist tries to seize its power for himself and is fought by Natsu, and the creature begins absorbing the wizards' magic for a devastating attack. Lucy learns that Éclair is more than four centuries old, having drunk the phoenix's blood to survive the destruction of her village, the site of present-day Veronica. Using an arrow made by Kalard, Natsu and Erza destroy the stone inside the phoenix, which kills both it and Éclair, whose spirit rises to rejoin Momon. Later, as the guildhall is rebuilt, Lucy glimpses a young Éclair's spirit among the townspeople.

The film opened in 73 Japanese theaters on August 18, 2012, ranking ninth with the weekend's highest per-screen average, and was released in North America on home video in December 2013. It received positive reviews, with critics praising the development of Lucy and Éclair.

overview: When they take some friends on an extreme sport adventure, the last thing Jared and Sam expect to see below the shark-infested waters is a legendary pirate ship rumored to contain millions of dollars in gold. But their good fortune is short-lived, as a ruthless gang of criminals gets word of what they have uncovered.
tagline: Treasure has its price.
title: Into the Blue
plot:
Into the Blue is a 2005 thriller film directed by John Stockwell. The movie follows two brothers, Miller and Jake, who embark on a deep-sea diving adventure to find a lost shipwreck in the Caribbean. As they delve deeper into the ocean, they encounter a group of divers who are also searching for the wreck.

The main theme of Into the Blue revolves around the dangers of obsession and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The characters' relentless pursuit of the treasure serves as a metaphor for the destructive nature of greed and the importance of respecting the power of nature.

Throughout the film, the characters are forced to confront their own personal demons and the true cost of their actions. As they navigate the treacherous underwater world, they must also contend with their own mortality and the fragility of human life.

The movie also explores the theme of brotherly love and loyalty, as Miller's obsession with finding the treasure puts a strain on his relationship with Jake. The film ultimately becomes a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of prioritizing human relationships over material gain.

Overall, Into the Blue is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions in the natural world.

overview: In the year 3000, man is no match for the Psychlos, a greedy, manipulative race of aliens on a quest for ultimate profit. Led by the powerful Terl, the Psychlos are stripping Earth clean of its natural resources, using the broken remnants of humanity as slaves. What is left of the human race has descended into a near primitive state. After being captured, it is up to Tyler to save mankind.
tagline: Take Back The Planet
title: Battlefield Earth
plot:
Battlefield Earth, directed by Roger Christian and based on the novel by L. Ron Hubbard, is a science fiction film that explores complex themes that are both thought-provoking and visually stunning.

At its core, Battlefield Earth is a story about the struggle for freedom and the dangers of totalitarianism. The film takes place in a distant future where humans are enslaved by an alien species known as the Psychlos, who have taken over the planet. The main character, Jonnie Goodboy Tyler, played by John Travolta, is a human who is captured by the Psychlos and forced to work on their home planet.

Through Jonnie's journey, the film delves into themes of oppression, rebellion, and the power of individual resistance. The Psychlos' rigid social hierarchy and strict control over every aspect of human life serve as a commentary on the dangers of authoritarian regimes and the importance of individual freedom.

The movie also explores the concept of empathy and understanding between different cultures. As Jonnie navigates his new surroundings and forms relationships with various Psychlo characters, he begins to see the world from their perspective, challenging his own biases and assumptions. This theme is particularly relevant in today's society, where cultural exchange and understanding are more important than ever.

Furthermore, Battlefield Earth touches on the idea of environmentalism and the consequences of exploiting natural resources without regard for the long-term effects. The Psychlos' reckless use of technology and their disregard for the planet's ecosystem serve as a warning about the dangers of unchecked industrialization and the importance of living in harmony with nature.

Overall, Battlefield Earth is a visually stunning film that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative and characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and a staple of science fiction cinema.

overview: The story of the Podolsk cadets’ heroic stand outside Moscow in October 1941. Cadets were sent to the Ilyinsky line, fighting alongside units from the Soviet 43rd Army to hold back the German advance until reinforcements arrived. Hopelessly outnumbered, young men laid down their lives in a battle lasting almost two weeks to obstruct the far superior German forces advancing towards Moscow. Around 3,500 cadets and their commanding officers were sent to hold up the last line of defense outside Moscow. Most of them remained there for eternity.
tagline: They fought for Moscow
title: The Last Frontier
plot:
The Last Frontier, also released as The Final Stand (Russian: Podolskie kursanty, literally "Podolsk Cadets"), is a 2020 Russian Second World War film directed by Vadim Shmelyov, who co-wrote the screenplay with Igor Ugolnikov, Viacheslav Fetisov and Vadim Zadorozhny. It dramatizes the stand of the Podolsk military school cadets during the Battle of Moscow in October 1941. The cast includes Aleksey Bardukov as Lieutenant Afanasy Aleshkin, Sergei Bezrukov as Captain Ivan Starchak, Evgeniy Dyatlov, Lyubov Konstantinova, Artem Gubin and Ekaterina Rednikova.

The film opens with a lengthy portrait of life at the artillery and infantry schools in Podolsk, following the officer cadets from field exercises to the barracks as they form friendships and court young women; two close friends are rivals for the affections of the same girl. In October 1941, with the cadets on the verge of completing their training and receiving their commissions, the Wehrmacht breaks through the front and a German tank column advances on Moscow. Regular army units are stretched too thin to stop it, and the cadets, many of them still boys, are abruptly ordered to the Ilyinsky defensive line, their senior officer reminding them that their fathers and brothers are already dying to hold back the enemy.

At the front, the cadets become the main barrier between the Germans and the capital. In long and brutal battles against overwhelming forces, the inexperienced recruits quickly lose their naivety and learn the realities of war at great personal cost. Holding their ground, they sacrifice their lives to fulfill their mission and buy precious days for reinforcements to arrive.

The film was shot from August to November 2018 at the VoenFilm complex in Medyn, where a village, pillboxes, a river and a stretch of the Warsaw Highway were built, with historical consultants recreating details down to the numbers of tanks and aircraft; Bezrukov's character carries a Thompson submachine gun because one was found in excavations at the Ilyinsky line. It had a budget of 450 million rubles, including 60 million from the Ministry of Culture, and received support from the Ministry of Defense and other state bodies. Central Partnership released it in Russia on November 4, 2020. Russian media reviews were generally positive, while KinoKultura's Ian Garner found it competently made and well acted but a repetition of familiar patriotic war-film tropes.

overview: After dominating the boxing world, Adonis Creed has been thriving in both his career and family life. When a childhood friend and former boxing prodigy, Damien Anderson, resurfaces after serving a long sentence in prison, he is eager to prove that he deserves his shot in the ring. The face-off between former friends is more than just a fight. To settle the score, Adonis must put his future on the line to battle Damien - a fighter who has nothing to lose.
tagline: You can't run from your past.
title: Creed III
plot:
Creed III is a 2023 American sports drama film directed by Michael B. Jordan in his directorial debut, the sequel to Creed II (2018) and the ninth film in the Rocky franchise. Written by Keenan Coogler and Zach Baylin from a story they developed with Ryan Coogler, it stars Jordan as retired boxing champion Adonis Creed and Jonathan Majors as his childhood friend Damian "Dame" Anderson, with Tessa Thompson, Wood Harris, Florian Munteanu and Phylicia Rashad.

In 2002, teenage Donnie sneaks out with his friend Dame, a Golden Gloves champion, to watch him win an underground fight in Los Angeles. On the way home, Donnie impulsively attacks a man named Leon outside a liquor store; Dame is arrested while Donnie flees, and the two lose contact. In the present, Donnie has retired from the ring and lives with his wife Bianca and their hearing-impaired daughter Amara, runs a gym with Tony "Little Duke" Evers and promotes the heavyweight champion Felix Chavez. Dame, newly released from prison, asks Donnie to help him resume his career. Donnie takes him on as Chavez's sparring partner, though his aggression alarms the others.

When Chavez's scheduled opponent, Viktor Drago, is attacked at a party, Donnie nominates Dame as the replacement. In his first professional bout, Dame wins the title with dirty tactics, exploiting a shoulder injury he inflicted on Chavez in sparring. Donnie's adoptive mother, Mary-Anne, then reveals the letters Dame wrote him from prison, which she hid, and a photo shows Dame with the inmate who attacked Drago. Confronted, Dame admits he manipulated Donnie and accuses him of abandoning him. After Mary-Anne's death, Donnie tells Bianca the truth about that night: Leon was the abusive caretaker of their group home, and Dame pulled a gun to save Donnie from Leon's friends. Publicly taunted, Donnie comes out of retirement and, after training with Duke and Drago, faces Dame at Dodger Stadium. In a grueling fight, he rises from a knockdown in the final round to knock Dame out and win back the title. Afterward the two men reconcile, each accepting that the past was not the other's fault, and Donnie shadowboxes with Amara in the empty stadium.

Released by MGM in the United States on March 3, 2023, Creed III opened at number one and grossed $276.1 million worldwide on a $75 million budget, the highest-grossing Creed film. Critics praised Jordan's direction and Majors's performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 89% approval and Metacritic a score of 73.

overview: A bird raised by mice begins to question where she belongs and sets off on a daring journey of self-discovery.
title: Robin Robin
plot:
Robin Robin is a 2021 British stop-motion animated musical short film directed by Dan Ojari and Mikey Please, who wrote the screenplay with Sam Morrison. Produced by Aardman Animations as its first collaboration with Netflix, the half-hour Christmas special was announced in November 2019 and stars the voices of Bronte Carmichael, Richard E. Grant, Gillian Anderson and Adeel Akhtar. Its puppets were needle-felted rather than made of plasticine. The film premiered at the BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2021 and was released worldwide on Netflix on 24 November 2021.

A bird's egg rolls into the path of a family of mice, and the robin that hatches from it is raised by them as one of their own. Robin (Carmichael) grows up believing she is a mouse and never learns to fly, but her clumsy enthusiasm keeps ruining the family's careful raids on the "Who-Man" houses for crumbs. When she spoils yet another outing, she begins to doubt that she really belongs, and although Dad Mouse (Akhtar) stands up for her, she feels guilty. Setting out on her own at night, she tries to break into another human house and meets a thieving Magpie (Grant), and the pair narrowly escape the house's malicious Cat (Anderson).

The Magpie takes Robin to his hideout, shows her the wonderful things he has collected, and tells her about the shiny star on top of the Christmas tree that supposedly brings people their wonderful things. The two resolve to steal the star. The heist goes well until Robin makes noise once again and hides in a shed, drawing the Cat's attention; she manages to drive the Cat off with fire, but blows up the whole shed in the process. Afterwards Robin wishes only to be a proper mouse. The next day her mouse family comes looking for her, but just as they are about to be reunited the Cat reappears. In the showdown Robin defeats the Cat and, at last, learns to fly. In the end Robin, the Magpie and the mice go crumb-hunting together: Robin distracts the humans, the Magpie wedges the door with a spoon, and the mice clear the dinner table.

Amira Macey-Michael, Tom Pegler, Endeavour Clutterbuck and Megan Harris voice Robin's mouse siblings. The score was composed by Ben Please and Beth Porter of the Bookshop Band and performed by the Bristol Ensemble, with lyrics by the directors. Robin Robin was well received by critics and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film, as well as at the British Academy Children's Awards and the NAACP Image Awards.

overview: Marcello, a small and gentle dog groomer, finds himself involved in a dangerous relationship of subjugation with Simone, a former violent boxer who terrorizes the entire neighborhood. In an effort to reaffirm his dignity, Marcello will submit to an unexpected act of vengeance.
title: Dogman
plot:
Dogman is a 2018 Italian drama film directed by Matteo Garrone, not RAI. The movie tells the story of Marcello, a struggling dog catcher who forms an unlikely friendship with his canine companion, Dogman.

The main themes of Dogman revolve around the struggles of working-class life, loneliness, and the human condition. The film explores the complexities of Marcello's character, who is both brutal and vulnerable, as he navigates the harsh realities of his job and personal relationships.

Through Marcello's story, Garrone sheds light on the darker aspects of Italian society, including corruption, violence, and social inequality. However, the film also offers a poignant portrayal of human connection and empathy, highlighting the transformative power of friendship and companionship.

The title "Dogman" itself is a metaphor for the struggles of everyday life, where individuals are often reduced to their most basic roles or personas, much like the dog that Marcello befriends. The film's narrative is both a commentary on the human condition and an exploration of the complexities of relationships, ultimately revealing the resilience and dignity of its characters in the face of adversity.

overview: Beneath Anna Poliatova's striking beauty lies a secret that will unleash her indelible strength and skill to become one of the world's most feared government assassins.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
Québec Crédit d'Impôt Cinéma et Télévison
tagline: Never make the weapon the target
title: Anna
plot:
Anna is a 2019 action thriller written, produced and directed by Luc Besson. Sasha Luss stars as Anna Poliatova, a fashion model who is secretly a trained assassin, alongside Helen Mirren as her handler Olga, Luke Evans as the KGB officer Alex Tchenkov and Cillian Murphy as the CIA agent Leonard Miller, with Alexander Petrov and Lera Abova in supporting roles.

In 1990, Anna is a young Russian woman desperate to escape an abusive relationship. Alex, a KGB agent, learns of her situation and recruits her. After a year of training she is told that she must serve four more years under the senior handler Olga, after which she will be released to start her life again. When the Soviet Union collapses, however, Vassiliev, the head of the renamed intelligence service, refuses to honour the deal, believing that the only way out of the agency is death. Anna is placed in Paris under cover as a model, carrying out assassinations between photo shoots, and with Olga's approval begins a relationship with another model, Maude, to deflect suspicion.

When the CIA discovers who she is, Anna agrees to become a double agent under Miller in return for asylum and a new life in Hawaii. Miller orders her to kill Vassiliev, hoping his successor will improve relations with the United States. Anna kills him over a game of chess and fights her way out of the Lubyanka building. She then meets Alex and Miller together, returning the secrets she has stolen from each but warning that copies will be released if she is harmed. Both men accept, and Miller agrees to let her disappear. Olga, watching the meeting, follows Anna and apparently shoots her dead for treason, and her body is swiftly taken away before Miller can confirm anything. The victim was in fact a double: the real Anna escapes through the sewers, removing a wig from her shaved head. It is revealed that Olga had discovered the CIA plot earlier and the two women agreed to let it go ahead because Olga wanted Vassiliev's job. Moving into Vassiliev's old office, Olga watches a farewell video in which Anna thanks her but warns that she has kept proof of Olga's role in the killing, and Olga deletes Anna's file from the agency's records.

Produced by EuropaCorp, the film was shot in Belgrade, Paris, Moscow, Milan and Guadeloupe and released in the United States by Summit Entertainment in June 2019. It grossed $32.8 million worldwide, and reviews were largely negative, with 34% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 40.

overview: A famous horror writer finds inspiration for her next book after she and her husband take in a young couple.
title: Shirley
plot:
Shirley is a 2020 biographical drama film that tells the story of Shirley MacLaine's life, focusing on her early years and her struggles with mental health. The movie delves into the complexities of MacLaine's psyche, exploring themes of trauma, identity, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

At its core, Shirley is a deeply personal and introspective film that grapples with the darker aspects of human experience. It sheds light on the often-overlooked struggles of women in the entertainment industry, particularly those who have been marginalized or silenced throughout history.

The film also touches on the theme of performance and the masks we wear to navigate the world. MacLaine's character is a masterful example of this, as she navigates the complexities of her own identity through her various roles and personas. This theme is woven throughout the narrative, highlighting the tension between authenticity and artifice.

Furthermore, Shirley explores the idea of female empowerment and the struggle for women to find their place in a patriarchal society. MacLaine's character is a product of this era, navigating the constraints placed upon her as a woman in Hollywood while also forging her own path and asserting her independence.

Ultimately, Shirley is a powerful and poignant film that offers a nuanced exploration of the human experience. It is a testament to the enduring power of storytelling and the importance of shedding light on the often-overlooked stories of women who have shaped our culture.

overview: In this classic story of love and devotion set against the backdrop of the American Civil War, a wounded Confederate soldier named W.P. Inman deserts his unit and travels across the South, aiming to return to his young wife, Ada, who he left behind to tend their farm. As Inman makes his perilous journey home, Ada struggles to keep their home intact with the assistance of Ruby, a mysterious drifter sent to help her by a kindly neighbor.
tagline: Find the strength. Find the courage. No matter what it takes... find the way home.
title: Cold Mountain
plot:
Cold Mountain is a poignant and powerful tale that delves into the human spirit's capacity for resilience, hope, and redemption. Set against the backdrop of the American Civil War, the film follows W.P. Inman, a wounded Confederate soldier who deserts his unit to return to his beloved home in Cold Mountain, North Carolina.

As Inman navigates the treacherous terrain of war-torn America, he encounters various characters who challenge his perceptions and force him to confront the harsh realities of his past. The film's narrative is marked by a sense of longing and yearning, as Inman searches for a sense of belonging and connection in a world torn apart by conflict.

One of the primary themes of Cold Mountain is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Inman's journey is a metaphor for the search for one's true purpose and meaning in life. As he encounters various characters who embody different aspects of himself, he begins to uncover fragments of his own identity and reconcile with his past.

The film also explores the theme of love and relationships, particularly the complex bond between Inman and Ruby Thewes, a strong-willed and independent woman who becomes his unlikely companion on his journey. Through their interactions, the film highlights the transformative power of human connection and the ways in which love can heal even the deepest wounds.

Furthermore, Cold Mountain is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war and the devastating impact it has on individuals and communities. The film's portrayal of the brutal realities of war serves as a stark reminder of the need for compassion, empathy, and understanding in the face of conflict.

Ultimately, Cold Mountain is a movie about the human spirit's capacity to persevere in the face of adversity, to find hope and redemption even in the darkest of times. The film's narrative is marked by a sense of hope and renewal, as Inman and Ruby navigate the challenges of their journey and discover new paths forward.

overview: After a spectacular crash-landing on an uncharted planet, brash astronaut Leo Davidson finds himself trapped in a savage world where talking apes dominate the human race. Desperate to find a way home, Leo must evade the invincible gorilla army led by Ruthless General Thade.
tagline: You'll be sorry you were ever born human.
title: Planet of the Apes
plot:
Planet of the Apes is a 2001 American science fiction adventure film from director Tim Burton, written by William Broyles Jr., Lawrence Konner and Mark Rosenthal. Loosely based on Pierre Boulle's 1963 novel, it remakes the 1968 film. Mark Wahlberg plays the astronaut Leo Davidson, with Tim Roth as General Thade, Helena Bonham Carter as Ari, Michael Clarke Duncan as Colonel Attar, Paul Giamatti as Limbo, Estella Warren as Daena and Kris Kristofferson.

In 2029, Leo works with apes trained for spaceflight aboard the space station Oberon. When an electromagnetic storm nears the station, his favourite chimpanzee, Pericles, is sent into it in a probe pod and vanishes. Leo follows in another pod without permission and crash-lands in the year 5021 on Ashlar, a planet where intelligent apes rule and keep humans as slaves. Ari, a chimpanzee who opposes this cruelty, buys Leo and a young woman, Daena, as servants in the house of her father, Senator Sandar. Leo breaks free and liberates other humans, taking the orangutan slave dealer Limbo prisoner to keep him quiet, while the ruthless chimpanzee General Thade and his gorilla deputy Attar lead an army in pursuit.

Leo reaches Calima, the forbidden temple of Semos, the first ape, whom the apes worship and expect to return one day. It proves to be the ancient wreck of the Oberon: Leo realises that the storm hurled him forward in time while the station, searching for him, crashed on the planet thousands of years earlier. Its logs show that the apes aboard, led by Semos, mutinied after the crash; the survivors of both species are the ancestors of the planet's people. As the apes attack the gathered humans, Leo uses the ship's remaining fuel to strike their first wave. The fighting halts when Pericles' pod descends from the sky, having also been carried through time; the apes take him for Semos and lay down their arms. Thade follows Leo into the wreck and grabs his gun, but Leo traps him on the pilot's deck. Leaving Pericles with Ari, Leo flies the pod back through the storm. Crashing in Washington, D.C., he finds the Lincoln Memorial now honours Thade, and the police and reporters who surround him are apes.

Released by 20th Century Fox on July 27, 2001, the film grossed $362.2 million worldwide, the ninth-highest total of the year. Reviews were mixed: critics faulted the screenplay and twist ending but praised Rick Baker's makeup, the visuals and the score, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: As World War II rages, the elite Sixth Ranger Battalion is given a mission of heroic proportions: push 30 miles behind enemy lines and liberate over 500 American prisoners of war.
tagline: The most daring rescue mission of our time is a story that has never been told
title: The Great Raid
plot:
The Great Raid is a powerful and emotional war drama that delves into the themes of sacrifice, camaraderie, and the human cost of conflict. The film tells the true story of the 1945 Bataan Death March, where American prisoners of war were forced to march over 60 miles through treacherous terrain, resulting in the deaths of thousands.

At its core, The Great Raid is a story about the bonds of friendship and loyalty that form between men who are forced to rely on each other for survival. As the characters navigate the brutal conditions of the Bataan Death March, they must confront their own mortality and the true meaning of sacrifice. Through their struggles, the film highlights the importance of human connection in the face of adversity.

The Great Raid also explores the theme of redemption, as the characters grapple with the moral implications of their experiences during the war. The film's portrayal of the Bataan Death March is unflinching and unsparing, yet it also offers a message of hope and resilience in the face of overwhelming oppression.

One of the most striking aspects of The Great Raid is its exploration of the psychological toll of war on the human psyche. The characters are forced to confront their deepest fears and anxieties, and the film's portrayal of their emotional struggles is both haunting and deeply moving.

Overall, The Great Raid is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores some of the most fundamental themes of the human experience. Through its gripping story and memorable characters, the film offers a powerful tribute to the men who suffered during the Bataan Death March, and serves as a reminder of the enduring power of human connection in the face of adversity.

overview: Ray Kinsella is an Iowa farmer who hears a mysterious voice telling him to turn his cornfield into a baseball diamond. He does, but the voice's directions don't stop -- even after the spirits of deceased ballplayers turn up to play.
tagline: If you believe the impossible, the incredible can come true.
title: Field of Dreams
plot:
Field of Dreams is a 1989 American sports fantasy drama film written and directed by Phil Alden Robinson, based on W. P. Kinsella's 1982 novel Shoeless Joe. Kevin Costner stars as Ray Kinsella, an Iowa farmer who builds a baseball diamond in his cornfield that draws the ghosts of baseball legends, including Shoeless Joe Jackson (Ray Liotta) and the Chicago Black Sox. Amy Madigan plays his wife Annie, with James Earl Jones and Burt Lancaster, in his final film role.

Ray lives on a corn farm in Dyersville, Iowa, with Annie and their daughter Karin, haunted by his broken relationship with his late father, John, a devoted baseball fan. One evening he hears a voice whispering "If you build it, he will come" and envisions a ballfield. Despite the financial risk, he plows under part of his crop to build it. Shoeless Joe appears, soon joined by other banned Black Sox players, though Annie's brother Mark, who cannot see them, warns that the family is going bankrupt. The voice next urges Ray to "ease his pain," which he takes to mean Terence Mann, a reclusive 1960s author. Ray drives to Boston and takes Mann to a game at Fenway Park, where both hear the voice say "go the distance" and see statistics for Moonlight Graham, who played one game for the New York Giants in 1922 without ever batting.

In Chisholm, Minnesota, they learn that Graham became a beloved doctor and died years earlier. Ray slips back to 1972 to meet the elderly Graham, who declines his invitation. On the way home, they pick up a young hitchhiker who turns out to be Archie Graham. Ray confesses that he stopped playing catch with his father at 14 and mocked his hero, Joe, and never reconciled with him before his death. At the farm, Graham finally gets to bat, but when Mark demands that Ray sell, a scuffle knocks Karin off the bleachers. Graham steps off the field to save her from choking, becoming old Doc Graham again, and leaves without regret. Mark suddenly sees the players and urges Ray to keep the farm, as Karin and Mann predict that people will come to watch. Mann is invited into the corn, and the catcher removes his mask, revealing Ray's father as a young man. Ray asks his father to play catch as a line of cars approaches the field.

Released by Universal Pictures on April 21, 1989, the film grossed $84.5 million on a $15 million budget, received positive reviews and was nominated for three Academy Awards, including Best Picture. In 2017, it was selected for the National Film Registry.

overview: As her friends prep for a Life Day holiday celebration, Rey journeys with BB-8 on a quest to gain a deeper knowledge of the Force at a mysterious Jedi Temple. There, she embarks on a cross-timeline adventure through beloved moments in Star Wars history, coming into contact with iconic heroes and villains from all eras of the saga. But will she make it back in time for the Life Day feast?
tagline: To: Luke. From: Your father.
title: LEGO Star Wars Holiday Special
plot:
The LEGO Star Wars Holiday Special is a heartwarming and humorous celebration of the Star Wars universe, focusing on the character of Chewbacca and his family during the Wookiee holiday, Life Day. The special explores themes of family, tradition, and cultural identity.

At its core, the story revolves around Chewbacca's desire to connect with his family and understand the significance of Life Day, a celebration that holds great importance for the Wookiees. As he navigates this unfamiliar holiday, Chewbacca learns valuable lessons about the importance of embracing his heritage and finding common ground with those around him.

The special also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation, as Chewbacca struggles to balance his duties as Han Solo's co-pilot with his desire to connect with his family. This internal conflict serves as a poignant reminder that even in a galaxy filled with adventure and excitement, it's the simple moments of connection and community that truly bring meaning to our lives.

Throughout the special, the LEGO Star Wars universe is infused with its signature blend of humor, wit, and lighthearted charm, making for an entertaining and engaging viewing experience. Ultimately, the LEGO Star Wars Holiday Special is a feel-good story that celebrates the power of family, tradition, and self-discovery in a way that's both nostalgic and accessible to audiences of all ages.

overview: After Washington DC detective Alex Cross is told that a family member has been murdered, he vows to track down the killer. He soon discovers that she was not his first victim and that things are not what they seem.
tagline: Don't Ever Cross Alex Cross
title: Alex Cross
plot:
Alex Cross is a 2012 American action thriller directed by Rob Cohen, starring Tyler Perry as the title character, a psychologist and police detective, and Matthew Fox as a professional killer nicknamed Picasso. The screenplay by Marc Moss and Kerry Williamson is based on James Patterson's 2006 novel Cross. The third film in the Alex Cross series, it was conceived as a reboot, and unlike its predecessors it was released by Summit Entertainment rather than Paramount.

Dr. Alex Cross works as a detective for the Detroit Police Department alongside his childhood friend Thomas Kane and their colleague Monica Ashe, who are secretly romantically involved. At home, Cross lives a happy family life with his mother, his pregnant wife Maria and their two children. When a businesswoman is tortured and murdered, Cross deduces that the killer is a lone professional, possibly a former special forces operative, who leaves behind a charcoal drawing of his victim, earning him the nickname Picasso.

Linking the victim to two other businessmen, the team predicts Picasso's next target and manages to prevent the assassination in a gunfight, though the killer escapes after being wounded. Cross believes Picasso is too focused on his targets to come after the detectives, but he is wrong. Picasso strikes back at the team personally, murdering people close to them in revenge, and Cross is left devastated. Driven by grief and rage, Cross and Kane set out to hunt down the assassin by any means necessary, a pursuit that pushes Cross to the limits of his principles and forces him to think like the man he is chasing to discover who is ultimately behind the killings.

The film recasts the character as a younger, more physical action hero, torn between his family life, a possible move to an FBI job in Washington and his obsession with the case.

Released on October 19, 2012, Alex Cross opened in fifth place and grossed about 34.6 million dollars worldwide on a 35 million dollar budget. Critics panned it, giving it 11 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus blamed Cohen's direction and a tasteless, lazily written script, and a Metacritic score of 30.

overview: A widower suspects that his seemingly perfect adolescent daughter is a heartless killer.
title: The Bad Seed
plot:
The Bad Seed is a 2018 American horror drama television film directed by Rob Lowe for Lifetime, a remake of the 1956 film, based on William March's 1954 novel and Maxwell Anderson's play of the same year. Lowe, who also executive produced, stars as David Grossman, a widowed father, with Mckenna Grace as his daughter, Emma, Sarah Dugdale, Cara Buono, Marci T. House, Lorne Cardinal and Chris Shields, and a special appearance by Patty McCormack, who played the murderous child, Rhoda, in the original film. It aired on Lifetime on 9 September 2018.

Nine-year-old Emma, a polite, seemingly perfect girl, tells her father that she hopes to win her school's citizenship medal. When a cat drowns in the backyard, she shows no emotion. To her disappointment, the medal goes to her classmate Milo Curtis. At the school celebration, Emma voices contempt for Milo, then apologizes when her father scolds her. But she secretly lures Milo to a cliff, takes his medal and pushes him to his death, before slipping back to the party. When David asks her about the tragedy, she remains cheerful and shows no empathy; his sister, Angela, a psychiatrist, suggests that Emma is in shock.

David hires a babysitter, Chloe, but Emma discovers her stealing her father's pills and blackmails her. At Milo's funeral, his mother asks David for photographs from the ceremony, and as he looks through them he notices how many show Emma scowling at Milo. When Emma's teacher and an investigator visit to discuss what happened on the day of the celebration, Emma eavesdrops, and David begins to suspect the terrible truth about his daughter. As the people around Emma who threaten to expose her begin to die, David confronts the possibility that his child is a psychopath, and he is forced to decide how far he is willing to go to stop her.

The film drew attention for Grace's chilling performance and for McCormack's return to the story that made her famous, playing a psychiatrist. Reviews were mixed, with critics finding it a competent update of the classic tale. A sequel, The Bad Seed Returns, followed in 2022, with Grace reprising her role.

overview: Lurk what's waiting for the Monster High ghouls when they bring their killer fashion to the howlways of the spooktacular Haunted High! When the ghouls of Monster High follow Spectra Vondergeist one day, they discover a creeperiffic Ghost World with an all-spirit school. But their scary-cute student bodies are hardly welcome with the very strict Principal Revenant, and she punishes Spectra with frightful detention chains that prevent her from re-joining Monster High. Now, it's up to the imperfectly perfect friends to take on ghostly forms in order to save one of their own from disappearing forever!
title: Monster High: Haunted
plot:
Monster High: Haunted is a 2015 American computer-animated fantasy film based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll franchise. Directed by William Lau and produced by Mattel Playground Productions, with animation by Nerd Corps Entertainment, it was released on DVD and Blu-ray by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment and introduced a new line of ghost characters and dolls. The voice cast includes Erin Fitzgerald as Spectra Vondergeist and Sue Swan as Draculaura, alongside Celeste Henderson, Haviland Stillwell, Karen Strassman, Laura Bailey, America Young and Cam Clarke.

At Monster High, the school for the children of famous monsters in the town of New Salem, the ghostly student blogger Spectra Vondergeist is desperate for a juicy story, while Draculaura becomes convinced she is being haunted. Spectra reveals a secret she has never shared: close by lies a hidden spirit world with its own all-ghost school, Haunted High, which she once attended. Hoping to find help and perhaps a scoop, since there has not been a haunting in ages, not since the legend of the Red Lady, she heads there and fails to return. Led by Clawdeen Wolf, Draculaura, Rochelle Goyle, Twyla and Sirena Von Boo set out after her, entering a realm where non-ghost monsters are feared as "solids." Twyla, daughter of the Boogie Man, devises a way to disguise the friends as ghosts so they can slip into the school. There they find a student body crushed by the strict Principal Revenant, who rules with the help of her Hall Moanitors and punishes pupils with detention chains that would keep Spectra trapped forever. Befriended by Haunted High students such as River Styxx, Vandala Doubloons, the painter Portergeist and Kiyomi Haunterly, the ghouls work to expose Revenant's scheme and her hateful rumors, unravel the mystery of the Red Lady and free their friend.

The film was released on home video in the United States on 24 March 2015. Common Sense Media's Renee Longstreet called it an engaging, mildly suspenseful story that stands on its own beyond selling toys, praising its humor, bright style and message about the harm of gossip and rumors while noting the familiar skimpy costumes. A DVD Talk family review described it as fun and not scary, recommending it for children aged seven to ten.

overview: Through unlocked genetic memories that allow him to relive the adventures of his ancestor in 15th century Spain, Callum Lynch discovers he's a descendant of the secret 'Assassins' society. After gaining incredible knowledge and skills, he is now poised to take on the oppressive Knights Templar in the present day.
tagline: Your destiny is in your blood.
title: Assassin's Creed
plot:
Assassin's Creed is a 2016 science fiction action film directed by Justin Kurzel, based on Ubisoft's video game series. It stars Michael Fassbender in a dual role as Callum Lynch and his ancestor Aguilar de Nerha, with Marion Cotillard as the scientist Sofia Rikkin, Jeremy Irons as her father Alan Rikkin, Brendan Gleeson as Cal's father Joseph, Charlotte Rampling and Michael K. Williams. Set in the same universe as the games, it tells an original story that moves between modern times and 15th-century Spain.

In 1492 Andalusia, during the Granada War, Aguilar is inducted into the Assassin Brotherhood and charged with protecting Prince Ahmed of Granada from the Templar Order. In 1986, the young Cal finds his mother murdered by his father, an Assassin, and flees as Templar gunmen arrive. Thirty years later, Cal is sentenced to death for murder, but Abstergo Industries, the modern front of the Templars, fakes his execution and brings him to its research facility in Madrid.

The Templars are searching for the Apple of Eden, an ancient artifact that holds the genetic code for free will, which they believe can be used to eliminate violence by controlling humanity. Because Cal descends from Aguilar, the last known keeper of the Apple, Sofia places him in the Animus, a machine that lets him relive his ancestor's genetic memories. In the past, Aguilar and his partner María fight to rescue Ahmed from the Templar Grand Master Tomas de Torquemada, who wants the Apple. In the present, Cal begins to experience hallucinations and to absorb Aguilar's skills, meets other Assassin descendants held at the facility and confronts the truth about his mother's death. Torn between the Templars' promises and his heritage, Cal must decide where his loyalty lies as Abstergo closes in on the Apple.

The film translates the games' central ideas, such as the Animus, the Leap of Faith and the conflict between Assassins and Templars, into large-scale action sequences.

Released in December 2016, Assassin's Creed grossed 240.9 million dollars worldwide against a 125 million dollar budget, reportedly losing money for New Regency. It received negative reviews, with 19 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a joylessly overplotted slog, and a Metacritic score of 36.

overview: When a group of misfits is hired by an unknown third party to burglarize a desolate house and acquire one rare VHS tape, they discover more found footage than they had bargained for.
tagline: This collection is killer.
title: V/H/S
plot:
V/H/S is a 2012 found-footage horror anthology film written and directed by Adam Wingard, David Bruckner, Ti West, Richard Shepard, and Glenn McQuaid. The film's main themes revolve around the exploitation of young women, the consequences of curiosity, and the blurred lines between reality and fiction.

The film is presented as a collection of five short films, each with its own unique style and tone, which are linked together by a framing device featuring a group of friends who discover a mysterious VHS tape in an abandoned house. As they watch the tapes, they become increasingly enthralled and disturbed by the content, which appears to be footage from various sources, including a creepy home movie, a disturbing documentary, and a surreal, avant-garde film.

Throughout the film, the themes of exploitation and objectification are repeatedly explored, particularly in relation to young women. The films within the anthology often feature female characters who are subjected to violence, humiliation, or degradation, highlighting the darker aspects of human nature.

The theme of curiosity is also a dominant one, as the protagonists become increasingly drawn into the world of the VHS tapes, despite the risks and consequences. This can be seen in their willingness to watch the footage, even when they know it's disturbing or potentially deadly.

Finally, the film explores the idea that reality and fiction are not always distinct, and that the lines between them can become blurred. The VHS tapes themselves seem to be a kind of portal into another world, one that is both fascinating and terrifying.

Overall, V/H/S is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges its viewers to confront their own fears and anxieties about the nature of reality and human behavior.

original_title: Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day
overview: Alexander's day begins with gum stuck in his hair, followed by more calamities. Though he finds little sympathy from his family and begins to wonder if bad things only happen to him, his mom, dad, brother, and sister all find themselves living through their own terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day.
tagline: One day can change everything.
title: Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day
plot:
Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day is a heartwarming film that explores the complexities of family dynamics, sibling relationships, and the challenges of growing up. The movie delves into the emotional struggles of its protagonist, Alexander, as he navigates a day filled with mishaps and misfortunes.

At its core, the film is a poignant portrayal of the imperfections and quirks that make families unique. It highlights the importance of love, acceptance, and understanding in the face of adversity. Through Alexander's experiences, the movie shows how even the most trying days can be transformed into opportunities for growth, connection, and laughter.

The film also touches on themes of sibling rivalry, teasing, and the challenges of navigating different personalities within a family. However, it does so in a way that is relatable and endearing, rather than confrontational or preachy. Ultimately, Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day is a film about finding joy and humor in the everyday moments, even when things don't go according to plan.

The movie's tone is lighthearted and humorous, with a touch of satire that pokes fun at the absurdities of family life. The characters are well-developed and memorable, particularly Alexander, who is both frustrating and lovable at the same time. Overall, the film is a delightful and entertaining exploration of what it means to be a part of a loving but imperfect family.

overview: A foul-mouthed cat and its gang cross paths with humans.
tagline: Stop behaving like a human!
title: Bad Cat
plot:
Bad Cat is a 2016 animated film that revolves around the story of a stray cat named Tufan and his adventures with a group of misfit animals in Istanbul. The movie explores several themes, primarily focusing on redemption, friendship, and the struggle for survival.

At its core, Bad Cat is a tale about Tufan's journey from being an outcast to finding acceptance among his peers. As he navigates the complexities of his new friendships, Tufan learns valuable lessons about loyalty, trust, and the importance of having someone by your side. Through his experiences, the film highlights the transformative power of relationships in helping individuals overcome their past mistakes and find a sense of belonging.

The movie also delves into the theme of redemption, as Tufan seeks to make amends for past wrongdoings and prove himself to those around him. This narrative thread is woven throughout the story, adding depth and complexity to the characters' motivations and actions.

Furthermore, Bad Cat touches on the idea of community and the struggle for survival in a harsh environment. The film's setting, Istanbul, serves as a backdrop for exploring the city's vibrant culture and the resilience of its inhabitants. The movie showcases how even in the face of adversity, individuals can come together to support one another and find ways to thrive.

Overall, Bad Cat is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of redemption, friendship, and survival with humor, wit, and a touch of Turkish culture.

overview: Phil and Claire Foster fear that their mild-mannered relationship may be falling into a stale rut. During their weekly date night, their dinner reservation leads to their being mistaken for a couple of thieves—and now a number of unsavoury characters want Phil and Claire killed.
tagline: One ordinary couple. One little white lie.
title: Date Night
plot:
Date Night is a 2010 American action comedy film directed by Shawn Levy. The movie follows the story of a married couple, Phil and Claire Foster, played by Steve Carell and Tina Fey, who are celebrating their fifth wedding anniversary with a romantic dinner date.

However, things take a turn when they get caught up in a mistaken identity situation, where they become embroiled in a complex web of espionage and crime. As they navigate this unexpected adventure, Phil and Claire must confront their own relationship issues and learn to work together as a team.

The main theme of Date Night is the exploration of marriage and relationships under pressure. The film takes a lighthearted approach to this serious topic, using humor and action to highlight the challenges that couples face in their daily lives. Through Phil and Claire's journey, the movie shows how even the most mundane situations can become extraordinary when we least expect them to.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and how it relates to our relationships with others. As Phil and Claire navigate their mistaken identities, they are forced to confront their own sense of self and how it intersects with their relationship with each other. This theme is woven throughout the movie, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, Date Night is a fun and entertaining film that uses humor and action to explore the ups and downs of marriage and relationships.

overview: A love story between two savants with Asperger's syndrome, a kind of autism, whose conditions sabotage their budding relationship.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG II
title: Mozart and the Whale
plot:
Mozart and the Whale is a 2005 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Mark Herman. The movie tells the story of two socially awkward individuals, Eliza (played by Katie Holmes) and Desmond Doyle (played by John Krasinski), who meet at a support group for people with autism.

The main theme of Mozart and the Whale revolves around the idea of acceptance, understanding, and the power of human connection. The film explores how Eliza and Desmond's lives are forever changed when they discover that they share a love for Mozart's music, which becomes a common ground between them. Through their shared passion, they begin to break down their defenses and form a deep bond.

The movie also delves into themes of loneliness, isolation, and the struggles of those with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Desmond's character, in particular, is portrayed as someone who has been misunderstood and mistreated by society due to his condition. The film sheds light on the complexities of ASD and challenges stereotypes surrounding individuals with autism.

Furthermore, Mozart and the Whale touches on the idea of finding one's identity and sense of belonging. Eliza and Desmond both struggle to find their place in the world, but through their relationship, they discover a sense of purpose and acceptance that they had been missing.

Overall, Mozart and the Whale is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the beauty of human connection and the importance of understanding and accepting individuals with autism.

overview: The Japanese government sets up a special task force to fight the giant creatures suddenly appearing across the country. Soon, the squad unexpectedly meets a giant silver humanoid who starts appearing every time a space monster attacks!
tagline: Have you become so fond of humans, Ultraman?
title: Shin Ultraman
plot:
Shin Ultraman (シン・ウルトラマン) is a 2022 Japanese superhero film by director Shinji Higuchi, with Hideaki Anno as writer, co-producer and co-editor. Reimagining the 1966 television series Ultraman as the franchise's 37th film, it was produced by Toho Studios and Cine Bazar. Takumi Saitoh plays Shinji Kaminaga, with Masami Nagasawa as Hiroko Asami and Hidetoshi Nishijima, Daiki Arioka, Akari Hayami and Tetsushi Tanaka in supporting roles.

After a series of kaiju attacks, Japan creates the S-Class Species Suppression Protocol (SSSP) to deal with the monsters. During a battle with the creature Neronga, a silver giant descends from the sky and destroys it, while SSSP member Kaminaga is hurt trying to rescue a lost child. Hiroko Asami, an analyst transferred from the Public Security Intelligence Agency, is paired with Kaminaga, who seems to have recovered but behaves oddly, and she names the giant "Ultraman" in a report. Unknown to the team, Kaminaga is Ultraman, and he defeats the kaiju Gabora before it can reach a nuclear waste site.

The alien Zarab offers Japan a treaty but really intends to provoke nations into destroying one another; he abducts Kaminaga, impersonates Ultraman in attacks and leaks footage of Kaminaga's transformation, sparking a global manhunt. Asami rescues Kaminaga, who uses his Beta Capsule to save her in turn and unmask Zarab before defeating him. Another alien, Mefilas, turns Asami into a mind-controlled giant, then restores her as a show of goodwill and offers the government a giant version of the device, the Beta Box, in exchange for total obedience. With the SSSP's help, Ultraman seizes the Box and fights Mefilas, who withdraws on seeing Ultraman's superior, Zōffy, watching.

Zōffy reveals that the real Kaminaga was killed by debris when Ultraman first landed, and that Ultraman took his identity out of admiration for his sacrifice. Judging humanity a danger, Zōffy unleashes the ultimate weapon Zetton to wipe it out. Ultraman is beaten at first, but SSSP physicist Akihisa Taki uses data Kaminaga left behind to devise a plan, and Ultraman traps Zetton in a black hole. Rescued by Zōffy, Ultraman gives up his own life to revive Kaminaga, and Zōffy comes to respect humanity's determination.

Released in Japan on May 13, 2022, it grossed $34 million worldwide, the most successful Ultraman film. Critics praised its direction, effects and action, though some criticised the screenplay's structure; it holds 94% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: In this animated retelling of the story from the Bible's Book of Genesis, Joseph's gift of dream interpretation and his brilliantly colored coat inspires jealousy in his brothers.
title: Joseph: King of Dreams
plot:
Joseph: King of Dreams is a 2000 American animated musical fantasy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie is loosely based on the biblical story of Joseph, as told in the book of Genesis.

The film begins with a young boy named Joseph (voiced by Jake Gyllenhaal), who has a vivid dream that he will become a great leader and ruler over Egypt. However, his father Jacob (voiced by Patrick Stewart) is skeptical of the dream and dismisses it as mere fantasy.

As Joseph grows up, he becomes a skilled musician and storyteller, but his brothers, Reuben (John Kassir), Simeon (Corey Burton), Levi (Clancy Brown), Judah (Tom Kane), and Benjamin (Jason Alexander), are jealous of the attention and favoritism shown to him by their father. They plot against Joseph, selling him into slavery in Egypt.

In Egypt, Joseph is sold to Potiphar (Vincent Cassel), a high-ranking official in Pharaoh's court. Despite being mistreated and imprisoned, Joseph proves himself to be a loyal and hardworking servant. When Potiphar's wife accuses Joseph of trying to seduce her, he is falsely accused and sentenced to death.

However, Joseph's faith and integrity are eventually revealed when he interprets the dreams of Pharaoh (John Mahoney), who has been plagued by recurring nightmares. Joseph correctly predicts that Pharaoh will die and be succeeded by a great leader from his own family.

Pharaoh takes Joseph as his advisor and promotes him to a high-ranking position. As time passes, Joseph becomes a trusted counselor and helps Pharaoh prepare for the impending famine that will devastate Egypt.

When the famine hits, Joseph's brothers come to Egypt seeking food and forgiveness. However, they are met with hostility by their brother, who has become a powerful leader. In a dramatic confrontation, Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers and forgives them for their past betrayal.

The film ends with Joseph becoming Pharaoh, ruling over Egypt with wisdom and justice. He also reunites with his family, including his wife Asenath (Suzanne Pleshette) and his children. The movie concludes with a grand musical number, "Any Dream Will Do," in which Joseph reflects on the fulfillment of his dreams and the realization of his destiny.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a blend of traditional and computer-generated imagery. The music is catchy and memorable, featuring a range of styles from pop to rock to Middle Eastern influences. Overall, Joseph: King of Dreams is a heartwarming and entertaining animated film that brings an old story to life in a fresh and exciting way.

overview: Russian inmate Boyka, now severely hobbled by the knee injury suffered at the end of Undisputed 2. No longer the feared prison fighter he was, he has declined so far that he is now good only for cleaning toilets. But when a new prison fight tournament begins - an international affair, matching the best fighters from prisons around the globe, enticing them with the promise of freedom for the winner - Boyka must reclaim his dignity and fight for his position in the tournament.
tagline: One deadly tournament. Last fight for freedom.
title: Undisputed III: Redemption
plot:
Undisputed III: Redemption is a 2010 American martial arts action film directed by Isaac Florentine, the sequel to Undisputed II: Last Man Standing and the third installment in the Undisputed franchise. Scott Adkins reprises his role as the Russian prison fighter Yuri Boyka, with Mykel Shannon Jenkins as Turbo, Mark Ivanir as Gaga, Hristo Shopov as Warden Kuss and Marko Zaror as the Colombian fighter Dolor. It was released direct-to-video in 2010.

Years after his defeat by George "Iceman" Chambers, Boyka has been reduced to working as a janitor in a Russian prison, his knee badly damaged. When he hears about the Prison Spetz Competition, an international tournament between prison fighters that offers the winner a chance at freedom, he trains in secret to rehabilitate his knee, shaves off his long hair and beard, and challenges the reigning Russian champion, defeating him to win the right to represent his country.

At the brutal Gorgon prison in Georgia, Boyka joins fighters from around the world under the cruel Warden Kuss. The prisoners are forced to labor in a quarry, while the Colombian favorite, Raul "Dolor" Quiñones, receives special treatment and performance-enhancing drugs. Boyka initially clashes with the brash American fighter Turbo, but the two gradually develop mutual respect and begin training together. Boyka discovers that the tournament is rigged for profit in Dolor's favor, organized by a syndicate that includes the mobster Gaga and his associate Farnatti. As the competition proceeds and Boyka and Turbo advance alongside Dolor and the Brazilian Rodrigo Silva, they learn that defeated fighters are taken away and executed. When the organizers decide to eliminate the remaining fighters, Boyka and Turbo must not only fight for their lives in the ring but also find a way to escape, leading to Boyka's climactic final bout against Dolor despite his injuries.

Undisputed III received positive reviews from martial-arts fans and critics, who praised its elaborate fight choreography, Adkins's acrobatic performance and Florentine's direction, and it is often regarded as one of the best direct-to-video action films of its era. Its success led to a further sequel, Boyka: Undisputed, in 2016.

overview: A young drug-addled writer approaching the bottom of his descent submits to two months of agonizing detox at a treatment center in Minnesota.
tagline: I'm fine.
title: A Million Little Pieces
plot:
A Million Little Pieces is a 2018 American drama film directed by Sam Taylor-Johnson, not 2019, and produced by The Picture Company.

The movie revolves around the life of Steve Harmon (played by Jake Lacy), a high school student who finds himself in a difficult situation after being arrested for stabbing his friend. As he navigates through the complexities of his life, Steve struggles with feelings of guilt, anger, and self-discovery.

One of the main themes of A Million Little Pieces is the exploration of mental health and the consequences of trauma. The film delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the destructive power of unchecked emotions and the importance of seeking help when needed.

The movie also touches on the theme of redemption and personal growth, as Steve grapples with his past mistakes and tries to find a way to make amends. Through his experiences, he learns valuable lessons about forgiveness, empathy, and the importance of human connection.

Furthermore, A Million Little Pieces explores the complexities of family dynamics and the struggles that come with navigating difficult relationships. The film highlights the need for understanding, support, and acceptance in overcoming adversity.

Overall, A Million Little Pieces is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of the human experience, exploring themes of mental health, redemption, and personal growth.

overview: In the Texas bayous, a local homicide detective teams up with a cop from New York City to investigate a series of unsolved murders.
tagline: No one is safe.
title: Texas Killing Fields
plot:
Texas Killing Fields is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of obsession. The film's narrative revolves around two detectives, Brian Heigh (Sam Worthington) and Mike Souza (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), who are tasked with investigating a series of gruesome murders in Texas.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession, particularly the all-consuming nature of desire that can lead individuals to commit heinous acts. The character of Debra (Jessica Alba), a young woman whose disappearance sets off the chain of events, is a prime example of this theme. Her disappearance serves as a catalyst for the detectives' investigation, but it also highlights the darker aspects of human psychology.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The character of Detective Heigh, in particular, struggles with his own demons, which are slowly revealed throughout the movie. His obsession with solving the case becomes an all-consuming force that threatens to destroy him.

Furthermore, Texas Killing Fields critiques the notion of a "perfect" family and the facade that often hides dark secrets. The film's portrayal of the seemingly idyllic suburban community is juxtaposed with the gruesome reality of the murders, highlighting the tension between appearance and reality.

Overall, Texas Killing Fields is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of obsession, trauma, and the destructive power of secrets.

overview: On a post-apocalyptic Earth, a robot, built to protect the life of his dying creator's beloved dog, learns about life, love, friendship, and what it means to be human.
tagline: Take an unforgettable journey.
title: Finch
plot:
Finch is a post-apocalyptic drama film directed by Miguel Sapochnik, written by Jeremy Penner, and produced by Amblin Entertainment. The movie stars Tom Hanks as the titular character, a scientist who embarks on a perilous journey to save humanity from extinction.

The story begins in 2035, where we see a world ravaged by a deadly virus that has wiped out most of humanity. We are introduced to Finch (Tom Hanks), an elderly scientist who is working on a top-secret project to preserve human knowledge and culture before the world ends. He is accompanied by his loyal dog, Goody (played by a CGI-generated canine).

Finch's mission is to upload human consciousness into a robotic body, allowing people to live on in a digital realm. However, Finch soon realizes that he has only 30 days left to complete his task before the virus takes over and destroys what's left of humanity.

As Finch navigates the desolate landscape, he encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile creatures, and malfunctioning robots. Despite these challenges, Finch remains determined to fulfill his mission and ensure that human knowledge is preserved for future generations.

Throughout his journey, Finch forms a bond with Goody, who becomes more than just a companion – she's a symbol of hope and companionship in a world devoid of humanity. As they face numerous dangers together, Finch begins to question the morality of his mission and the true meaning of life.

As the days tick by, Finch's physical body begins to deteriorate, and he must find ways to sustain himself in the harsh environment. He also encounters other survivors, including a young girl named Zoe (played by Ayelet Zurer), who becomes a source of inspiration for Finch.

The film's climax revolves around Finch's final upload of human consciousness into the robotic body. As he completes his task, Finch is forced to confront the reality of his own mortality and the fate of humanity. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Finch's uploaded consciousness existing in a digital realm, surrounded by the knowledge and culture he worked so tirelessly to preserve.

Throughout the film, Tom Hanks delivers a powerful performance as Finch, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both flawed and endearing. The movie's themes of hope, resilience, and the human condition are timely and thought-provoking, making Finch a compelling watch for audiences.

Overall, Finch is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human existence in the face of catastrophic loss. With its stunning visuals, engaging storyline, and outstanding performances, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and drama.

overview: Doug Harris is a loveable but socially awkward groom-to-be with a problem: he has no best man.  With less than two weeks to go until he marries the girl of his dreams, Doug is referred to Jimmy Callahan, owner and CEO of Best Man, Inc., a company that provides flattering best men for socially challenged guys in need.  What ensues is a hilarious wedding charade as they try to pull off the big con, and an unexpected budding bromance between Doug and his fake best man Jimmy.
tagline: He's the best man... money can buy.
title: The Wedding Ringer
plot:
The Wedding Ringer is a 2015 American buddy comedy film directed by Jeremy Garelick in his directorial debut and co-written by Garelick and Jay Lavender. Kevin Hart stars as Jimmy Callahan, who runs a business supplying best men, with Josh Gad as Doug Harris, Kaley Cuoco as his fiancée, Gretchen, Affion Crockett, Olivia Thirlby, Jorge Garcia and Ken Howard. Produced by Adam Fields, Will Packer Productions and Miramax and distributed by Screen Gems, it was released on 16 January 2015.

Doug, a socially awkward but successful tax attorney, is engaged to the beautiful Gretchen Palmer, but with the wedding approaching, he realizes that he has no friends to serve as his best man or groomsmen. He turns to Jimmy, whose company, The Best Man, Inc., provides fake best men for grooms who lack friends of their own, complete with invented histories. Doug needs not only a best man but seven groomsmen to match Gretchen's bridesmaids, a package known as the "Golden Tux" that Jimmy has never attempted. Jimmy agrees to take on the job for $50,000.

Jimmy assumes the identity of "Bic," supposedly a military priest stationed in El Salvador, and assembles a misfit group of groomsmen, among them an escaped convict, a man who can dislocate his shoulder and another who can speak sentences backwards, all given fake identities. At a family brunch, Doug nearly blows his cover, until Jimmy accidentally sets Gretchen's grandmother on fire. To win over Gretchen's skeptical father, Ed, Jimmy and Doug's groomsmen are drawn into a muddy football game against Ed's old college teammates, and Doug's bachelor party turns into a wild night. As the wedding approaches, Doug and Jimmy develop a genuine friendship, while Doug begins to wonder whether Gretchen truly loves him, and Jimmy must decide whether the relationship has become more than just a job.

The Wedding Ringer received generally negative reviews, with critics finding its humor crude and its story predictable, though Hart and Gad's chemistry drew some praise. It was a box-office success, grossing more than $79 million worldwide against a budget of $23 million.

overview: After five disparate high school students meet in detention, they realize they have more in common than they think and form a band that becomes a champion for students sidelined by the high school elite.
tagline: Poets, geniuses, revolutionaries.
title: Lemonade Mouth
plot:
Lemonade Mouth is a 2011 American musical comedy-drama film that revolves around the story of four high school students who form a band and use their music as a way to express themselves and fight against the injustices they face in their school.

The main theme of Lemonade Mouth is the struggle for individuality and self-expression, particularly among teenagers who feel like outsiders or misfits. The film explores how these characters find solace and empowerment through music, which becomes a powerful tool for them to express their emotions, tell their stories, and challenge the status quo.

At its core, Lemonade Mouth is a story about embracing one's true self and finding the courage to speak out against injustice. The film celebrates the power of music as a means of social commentary and activism, highlighting how art can be a powerful tool for change.
