Before Tessa makes the biggest decision of her life, everything changes because of revelations about her family.
title: After We Fell
plot:
After We Fell is a 2021 American romantic fantasy film directed by Matt Eskandari, written by Anna Todd, and produced by Voltage Pictures.

The movie serves as the fourth installment in the After series, based on the novels by Anna Todd. The story follows Tessa Young (Josephine Langford) and Hardin Scott (Hero Fiennes-Tiffin), who are still navigating their complicated relationship after the events of the previous films.

As the story unfolds, Tessa is struggling to balance her feelings for Hardin with her growing connection to Noah Flynn (Dylan Arnold), a charming and charismatic student at her school. Meanwhile, Hardin's past demons resurface, threatening to destroy his relationship with Tessa once again.

Throughout the film, the characters face numerous challenges, including internal conflicts, external pressures, and the consequences of their actions in previous installments. The movie explores themes of love, loyalty, and self-discovery as the characters navigate their complex web of relationships.

One of the standout aspects of After We Fell is its ability to balance lighthearted moments with more serious and emotional scenes. The film features a talented young cast, including Josephine Langford, Hero Fiennes-Tiffin, and Dylan Arnold, who deliver nuanced performances that bring depth and complexity to their characters.

Overall, After We Fell is a romantic fantasy film that explores the ups and downs of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and talented cast, it's sure to delight fans of the series and newcomers alike.

overview: A massive influx of glacial melting triggers a new ice age in the Northern Hemisphere, forcing a family to make their way across the ice-covered landscape before they are frozen out for good.
title: Arctic Apocalypse
plot:
Arctic Apocalypse is a 2019 American science-fiction disaster film produced by The Asylum with Syfy, directed by Jon Kondelik and Eric Paul Erickson from a screenplay by Bill Hanstock. Because its premise closely resembles that of The Day After Tomorrow, it is generally regarded as one of The Asylum's mockbusters. It was shot at Mammoth Mountain in eastern California, premiered on British television on 4 August 2019 and was released in Germany that November.

Within a matter of weeks, a massive surge of glacial melting plunges the Northern Hemisphere into a new ice age. Glaciers devastate cities such as New York and Paris, the Eiffel Tower collapses and even the pyramids of Giza are buried in snow. In the United States, Mark (Joel Berti) and his wife Helen (Jennifer Lee Wiggins), a scientist, are forced to flee the cold. Their weather-obsessed daughter Brie (Lauren Esposito) and her boyfriend Tyler (Charles Townsend) are out studying the phenomenon when Tyler loses control of their car, and they escape just before it plunges into a chasm. Chased by a pack of wolves, they shelter in a school, where they join a group of students led by Aliyah (Anna Christensen) and Roger (Blake Dang). After an avalanche buries the entrance, the group barricades itself against the weather and the wolves, and Roger finds a pistol and propane tanks in the janitor's office.

Mark and Helen set out to find their daughter, parting from their colleague Larry (Erickson), who heads alone for a military post. Helen squeezes into the iced-over school, evades a wolf and reunites with Brie and Tyler, who are now engaged. Roger blows open the blocked entrance by shooting the propane tanks. While the students drive towards the military station, the family makes for a research station on a nearby plateau where the weather has inexplicably stayed normal, hoping to understand why and share the findings with the world. On the way they lose their car and are confronted by a gang of looters who want Mark's bag of research instruments; lightning from a freezing storm kills most of them, and Helen knocks out the surviving leader before the family finds another vehicle and reaches the plateau.

German critics were dismissive. The German film magazine Filmdienst described it as a low-budget variation on blockbuster disaster scenarios, told with deadly seriousness, with miserable effects and characters left undeveloped, while Cinema dismissed it as Ice Age without the gags or cute animals.

overview: After a clique of girls makes life difficult, a new student forms a rival group to take control of the school's corridors.
tagline: The Plastics are back!
title: Mean Girls 2
plot:
Mean Girls 2 is a 2011 American teen comedy TV film directed by Melanie Mayron from a script by Cliff Ruby, Elana Lesser and Allison Schroeder. A sequel to the 2004 film Mean Girls, it stars Meaghan Martin as Jo Mitchell, Maiara Walsh as Mandi Weatherly, Jennifer Stone as Abby Hanover, Nicole Gale Anderson, Claire Holt, Diego Boneta as Tyler and Linden Ashby, with Tim Meadows returning as Principal Ron Duvall.

Jo, a tomboy who has changed schools many times because of her father's work rebuilding NASCAR engines, arrives at North Shore High School in Ohio hoping to get into Carnegie Mellon, which her late mother attended. There she meets the Plastics, a clique led by Mandi, with the airheaded Chastity and the germ-phobic Hope. Jo befriends Mandi's outcast rival Abby, and the two are drawn into a prank war. Abby's wealthy father offers to pay Jo's college tuition if she stays friends with his daughter, and Jo reluctantly agrees. She falls for Tyler, a classmate from shop class, and the group gains Quinn, a student journalist. Mandi bugs the car Tyler borrows for a date in order to humiliate Jo, who then learns that Tyler is Mandi's stepbrother.

The feud escalates: Mandi tries to wreck Jo's Carnegie Mellon prospects and sabotages one of her father's engines. When Mandi plans her invitation-only birthday party, Jo throws an open party for Abby on the same night. The Plastics lace Abby's pizza with ipecac, but Jo hides it and later hands a slice to Mandi's boyfriend Nick, who vomits on Mandi. Jo, Abby and Quinn form the "Anti-Plastics", and Jo challenges Mandi for homecoming queen, but Jo realises she is becoming just like Mandi and tries to return the money. Mandi learns of the arrangement and persuades Quinn to expose it in the school paper, straining Jo's friendship with Abby. Mandi and Nick then steal the homecoming charity money meant for an animal shelter and plant it in Jo's shed, getting her expelled. Jo challenges Mandi to flag football. Learning that Jo was probably framed, Tyler and Abby recruit the tech-savvy Elliott, who finds video of the theft and sends it to the whole school. The Anti-Plastics win the game, Mandi and Nick are arrested, Jo is allowed to graduate, and she and Abby go on to Carnegie Mellon together.

Shot in Atlanta over twenty days in July 2010 the film premiered on ABC Family on January 23, 2011, and came out on DVD a month later. Reviews were negative; Entertainment Weekly saw it as a cheap remake of the original.

overview: Sam is a workaholic bachelor who babysits his niece and nephew before the holidays when his sister and her husband have to go out of town. Completely out of his element, he recruits help from their handsome neighbor Jason and finds himself in an unexpected romance.
tagline: Say guncle.

overview: Maverick cop Orin Boyd always brings down the domestic terrorists he tracks, but he ruffles feathers with his unorthodox techniques -- and soon finds himself reassigned to the toughest district in Detroit. When he discovers a group of detectives secretly operating a drug ring, Boyd joins forces with an unlikely ally -- gangster Latrell Walker -- to bring down the rotten cops.
tagline: This Is Gonna Hurt
title: Exit Wounds
plot:
Exit Wounds is an action thriller film that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of revenge and redemption. The movie follows the story of a former Special Forces operative, Miles Logan, who seeks to avenge his partner's death while navigating a complex web of corruption and deceit.

At its core, Exit Wounds explores the theme of vengeance as a destructive force that can consume individuals, leading them down a path of violence and chaos. The film highlights how the pursuit of revenge can become an all-consuming obsession, driving people to make choices that ultimately lead to their own downfall.

The movie also touches on the idea of redemption, as Miles Logan grapples with his past mistakes and seeks to find a way to make amends. Through his journey, the film suggests that true redemption requires confronting one's demons and making sacrifices in order to find forgiveness and peace.

Furthermore, Exit Wounds critiques the notion of heroism and the romanticization of violence. The film portrays Miles Logan as a complex and flawed character, whose actions are motivated by a desire for revenge rather than a sense of justice or altruism. This nuanced portrayal challenges the traditional hero archetype, instead presenting a more realistic and humanized version of a protagonist.

Overall, Exit Wounds is a gripping thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature, delving into themes of vengeance, redemption, and the complexities of heroism.

overview: Two fathers' lives intersect when one of them is involved in a terrible and sudden hit-and-run car accident that leaves the other's son dead. In response, the two men react in unexpected ways as a reckoning looms in the near future.
tagline: To find the truth you have to find who's hiding it.
title: Reservation Road
plot:
Reservation Road is a 2007 drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the devastating consequences of one fateful night. The movie delves into the emotional turmoil of its characters, particularly the father-son relationship between Lucas Hood (played by Joaquin Phoenix) and his son, Henry.

The main theme of Reservation Road is the exploration of grief, guilt, and redemption in the face of tragedy. When a young girl goes missing on a road trip with her family, including Lucas's son, the community comes together to search for her, leading to a series of events that expose the dark secrets and lies within the characters.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lucas is struggling to cope with his own guilt and sense of responsibility for the girl's disappearance. His relationship with his son is put to the test as he grapples with the consequences of his actions. The film raises questions about the nature of truth, forgiveness, and redemption, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of human emotions.

The movie also touches on themes of small-town secrets, social hierarchy, and the fragility of relationships. Through its exploration of these themes, Reservation Road creates a sense of tension and unease, mirroring the emotional turmoil experienced by its characters.

Ultimately, the film is a powerful exploration of the human condition, delving into the darker aspects of human nature while also offering a message of hope and redemption.

overview: After a distastrous first date for caterer Holly and network sports director Messer, all they have is common is a dislike for each other and their love for their goddaughter Sophie. But when they suddenly become all Sophie has in this world, Holly and Messer must set their differences aside. Juggling careers and social calendars, they'll have to find common ground while living under the same roof.
tagline: A comedy about taking it one step at a time.
title: Life As We Know It
plot:
Life As We Know It is a romantic comedy-drama film released in 2010, directed by Glen Ficarra and John Requa, and produced by Josephson Entertainment. The movie stars Jennifer Aniston and Paul Rudd as the main characters.

The story begins with the death of Olivia (Jennifer Aniston) and her husband, who are both expecting a child. Their friend, Adam (Paul Rudd), is devastated by their loss and feels responsible for not being able to save them. He decides to take care of the unborn baby on his own, but he soon realizes that raising a child as a single person is much harder than he anticipated.

Adam meets a free-spirited woman named Susan (Reese Witherspoon), who has her own set of problems and insecurities. Despite their initial reluctance, they agree to co-parent the baby together, with Adam taking care of the physical aspects and Susan handling the emotional and creative side.

As they navigate their new roles as single parents, Adam and Susan start to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is put to the test when they disagree on how to raise their child. Adam wants a traditional upbringing, while Susan advocates for a more unconventional approach.

Throughout the movie, the audience witnesses the growth of Adam and Susan's relationship, as well as their individual struggles with grief, love, and parenthood. The film explores themes of loss, identity, and the complexities of human relationships.

One of the standout aspects of Life As We Know It is its portrayal of complex characters. Both Adam and Susan are multi-dimensional and relatable, with flaws and strengths that make them endearing to the audience. Their chemistry on screen is undeniable, and their romance is both tender and authentic.

The movie also features a strong supporting cast, including Jon Hamm as Adam's brother, and Brooklyn Decker as the baby. The cinematography is warm and inviting, capturing the beauty of New York City and the intimacy of Adam and Susan's relationship.

Ultimately, Life As We Know It is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of love, loss, and parenthood. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and nuanced storytelling, it has become a beloved romantic comedy-drama that resonates with audiences worldwide.

overview: A young boy discovers a deadly alien creature and winds up entangled in a top secret government operation.
title: E N V O Y
plot:
E N V O Y (usually written Envoy) is a 2014 American science fiction short film written, directed and produced by David Weinstein. Made by Valkyrie Pictures and Black Sun Entertainment and running nine minutes, it was released online in September 2014 as a self-funded "proof of concept" intended to introduce a story that Weinstein hoped to develop into a feature and to show that high-end visual effects could be produced for a fraction of the usual cost. Weinstein, whose earlier design work includes the Star Wars prequels and the Matrix sequels, made it with his long-time collaborator Adam Coggin, who supervised the effects, following their earlier animated short Azureus Rising.

The story unfolds among cornfields. Young Kyle brings his older brother, Jason, out to the cornfields to show him something strange that has been happening for a week: whenever he throws a basketball into the corn, it is thrown back. Jason is astonished when the ball returns, and even more so by what steps out of the field, a deadly alien creature built like a sleek war machine, which the filmmakers call Aeon. The two brothers soon find themselves entangled in a top-secret government operation as the military moves in, and the creature, despite its menace, shows mercy toward innocent life and protects its young human playmates when the soldiers launch an all-out assault.

Weinstein described the short as a love letter to the action-adventure and science fiction films of the 1980s and 1990s. The production was completed in under a year of part-time work on a post-production budget of only a few thousand dollars, which meant building a live-action CGI pipeline and render farm to create computer-generated Apache helicopters, birds, corn, the basketball and the alien itself. The film became a viral success, drawing more than ten million combined views and appearing on major short film websites.

Critics agreed that its effects were its main attraction. Short of the Week saw the influence of Steven Spielberg, J. J. Abrams's Super 8 and Iron Man, noting the coming-of-age thread but saying it would win no prizes for originality while catching the eye of talent scouts. Singularity Hub praised the alien's design but found the story recycled and the military response clichéd. Cinema Crazed was more enthusiastic, calling it The Iron Giant meets Predator and arguing that it deserved a big-budget feature treatment.

overview: See what happens when the student bodies of an all-vampire school and an all-werewolf school integrate with Monster High.
title: Monster High: Fright On!
plot:
Monster High: Fright On! is a 2011 animated fantasy comedy television special based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll line, broadcast on Nickelodeon in the United States on October 30, 2011. The second Monster High special after New Ghoul @ School, it is tied to the "School's Out" and "Dead Tired" doll ranges. The voice cast includes Kate Higgins as Frankie Stein, Salli Saffioti as both Cleo de Nile and Clawdeen Wolf, Debi Derryberry as Draculaura, Laura Bailey as Lagoona Blue and Headmistress Bloodgood, Erin Fitzgerald as Abbey Bominable and Ogie Banks as Clawd Wolf.

Headmistress Bloodgood announces that Monster High will merge with two other schools, the all-vampire Belfry Prep and the werewolf-only Crescent Moon High, hoping to unite all monsters and eventually the human world. Frankie welcomes the plan, but Draculaura, a vampire dating the werewolf Clawd, is nervous, and the first day proves a disaster. Vampires and werewolves carve out separate territory, the vampire Gory clashes with Cleo by trying to take over the Fear Squad, and Clawd's childhood friend Romulus is dismayed that he loves a vampire. Frankie's plan for a unifying dance is ruined by Administrator Van Hellscream, the human official for monster relations, who takes over the school with his assistant Crabgrass and secretly inflames the feud while claiming to keep the peace. Clawd's insecure younger sister Howleen joins the conflict, rival support groups form, and Romulus quietly drives Clawd and Draculaura apart.

Frankie discovers that Crabgrass has turned Bloodgood to stone with gorgon dust and taken her place, the real headmistress now standing as a statue in the courtyard. Learning from Deuce how to reverse the curse, she frees Bloodgood, but Van Hellscream traps the girls over a pit in the catacombs. With Draculaura and Howleen missing, the vampires and werewolves blame each other and plan a midnight showdown in the gym, which Van Hellscream hopes will convince the authorities that monsters must be kept apart. Abbey frees the girls, and with help from Operetta, Clawdeen and Clawd they escape; Draculaura shields Howleen from a gargoyle, changing her mind about vampires. The girls reach the gym before the fight begins, and Frankie's speech brings the students together. Van Hellscream and Crabgrass try to flee, but Deuce turns them to stone, and Romulus makes peace with Clawd and befriends Draculaura.

Critical coverage was sparse; CineMagazine rated it 2.5 stars.

overview: When record store owner and compulsive list-compiler Rob Gordon gets dumped by his long-time girlfriend, Laura, because he hasn't changed since they met, he revisits his top five breakups of all time in order to figure out what went wrong. As he examines his failed attempts at romance and happiness, the process finds him being dragged, kicking and screaming, into adulthood.
tagline: A comedy about fear of commitment, hating your job, falling in love and other pop favorites.
title: High Fidelity
plot:
High Fidelity is a 2000 romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth through the eyes of its protagonist, Rob Gordon. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, as Rob revisits his past relationships and tries to understand what went wrong in each of them.

One of the main themes of High Fidelity is the struggle to move on from past heartbreaks. Rob's inability to let go of his ex-lovers and his tendency to idealize them serve as a catalyst for his self-discovery journey. Through his relationships, he grapples with the idea of what makes a relationship work and whether it's possible to find true love.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and how our past experiences shape us into who we are today. Rob's obsession with music and his role as a record store owner serve as a metaphor for his own emotional state, highlighting the ways in which our passions and interests can both bring us joy and hold us back.

Furthermore, High Fidelity explores the theme of vulnerability and openness in relationships. As Rob navigates his way through his past relationships, he learns to confront his emotions and be more honest with himself and others. This newfound vulnerability allows him to form deeper connections with those around him, particularly his love interest, Laura.

Overall, High Fidelity is a poignant exploration of the human experience, tackling complex themes with humor, wit, and sensitivity.

overview: Four sisters – Caroline, Joanna, Paulina, and Vicky – reunite for the Christmas Holiday in a Yorkshire mansion. However, their estranged father, James, joins in for the first time since he left the family behind decades prior. The group attempts to get through the holiday despite comedic misunderstandings, while also uncovering the long-buried secret that tore their family apart, so many years ago.
title: Father Christmas Is Back
plot:
Father Christmas Is Back is a British festive comedy from 2021, co-directed by Philippe Martinez and Mick Davis. Elizabeth Hurley, Nathalie Cox, Talulah Riley and Naomi Frederick play four sisters reunited for the holidays, with John Cleese as their uncle John, Kelsey Grammer as their estranged father James, Caroline Quentin as their mother Elizabeth, Kris Marshall as Peter and April Bowlby as Jackie.

Caroline, a perfectionist, hosts Christmas for her sisters at the Yorkshire mansion she shares with her husband Peter and their children, Daisey and Henry. When the tree topples over on 22 December, Peter and the children redecorate it with homemade ornaments. The guests arrive: free-spirited Vicky, fresh from couch-surfing around the United States; Joanna, a glamorous fashion editor, with her boyfriend Felix; their mother Elizabeth; and Paulina, a scholar writing a thesis on the Beatles, while Uncle John watches from a distance. Caroline presents her meticulously planned schedule, but tensions flare when Vicky teases Joanna about her age. Vicky then admits that she spent two weeks in Florida with their father, James, who walked out on the family years before, and soon afterwards James arrives with his much younger American girlfriend, Jackie, having been invited by Vicky without anyone's knowledge.

The sisters turn on Vicky, who storms off in Felix's Rolls-Royce and spends the night with the barman at the village pub, while Elizabeth stays out all night with John. At the church fundraiser on Christmas Eve, Vicky sells Joanna's designer clothes for a pittance and offers Felix's car as a prize, forcing the couple to buy back their belongings. When John and James go outside to settle their differences, James instead proposes to Jackie. He later apologises to his daughters for leaving 27 years earlier, explaining that he had quietly supported them all along and that their mother kept him informed. Jackie's elaborate light display then blows the old house's electrics. On Christmas Day Peter finds a positive pregnancy test and assumes it is Caroline's, but Joanna admits it is hers. Elizabeth finally reveals why James left: she had become pregnant by John, who is Vicky's biological father. With Caroline's dinner ruined, the family spends the day serving their meals at a nursing home.

Filmed at Birdsall House near Malton in September 2020, the film was released by Netflix on 7 November 2021. A sequel, Christmas in Paradise, followed in 2022.

original_title: Transformers: Prime Beast Hunters: Predacons Rising
overview: Autobots, Decepticons, Predaking and Predacons form an unlikely alliance to battle a resurrected Unicron.
title: Transformers: Prime Beast Hunters: Predacons Rising
plot:
Transformers Prime Beast Hunters: Predacons Rising is a 2013 American animated television film that serves as the conclusion of the series Transformers: Prime. It first aired on the Hub Network on October 4, 2013. The voice cast includes Peter Cullen as Optimus Prime, Frank Welker as Megatron, Will Friedle as Bumblebee, Sumalee Montano as Arcee, Steve Blum as Starscream, Kevin Michael Richardson as Bulkhead, Jeffrey Combs as Ratchet, Michael Ironside as Ultra Magnus, Peter Mensah as Predaking, David Sobolov as Shockwave and John Noble as Unicron.

After the Autobots' victory and the restoration of their home planet Cybertron, Optimus Prime honors Bumblebee as a warrior. Optimus and Wheeljack then leave on a quest to find the AllSpark, the source of all Cybertronian life, while the other Autobots hunt for the missing Decepticons Shockwave and Starscream. Meanwhile, deep in the Pacific Ocean, the dead Megatron is revived and possessed by Unicron, the ancient chaos-bringer, who intends to destroy Cybertron.

With Ultra Magnus gravely wounded by the Predacons Skylynx and Darksteel, Bumblebee takes temporary command of the Autobots. Predaking, the proud leader of the Predacons, refuses to help them, but he too falls before Unicron, who finds Shockwave and Starscream harvesting bones from an ancient Predacon graveyard and raises the corpses as an army of undead Terrorcons. As the horde marches on the Well of AllSparks, the Autobots, the remaining Decepticons and the Predacons are forced into an uneasy alliance to stop the threat. Optimus and Wheeljack race home with the AllSpark's container, and the battle for the future of Cybertron reaches its climax as old enemies reconsider their loyalties.

The film wraps up the storylines of the series, focusing on themes of redemption, sacrifice and the rebirth of a civilization.

Predacons Rising received positive reviews and was widely regarded as a satisfying conclusion to Transformers: Prime, although some reviewers criticized the limited use of characters such as Ultra Magnus and Shockwave.

overview: Journey to a secret valley in Australia, where a nervous baby kangaroo named Mala faces hungry dingoes and winter snows in this coming-of-age adventure.
title: Kangaroo Valley
plot:
Kangaroo Valley is a 2022 nature documentary film made for Netflix, directed by Kylie Stott, written by Tab Murphy and produced by Ample Nature. Narrated by Sarah Snook, it is a coming-of-age story about a nervous baby eastern grey kangaroo named Mala who must survive hungry dingoes and winter snow during her first year out of the pouch. The film features "We Can Do Anything," a new song by the Australian pop star Sia, and was released on December 14, 2022.

In a lush valley in Australia, the joey Mala emerges from her mother Lowanna's pouch for the first time. Unlike the playful joey Buru, who loves to hop, Mala is reluctant to leave the safety of the pouch. Her father, Bamir, is the largest buck in the valley and the leader of the kangaroo mob. On the edge of the valley lies the Black Forest, scorched by recent wildfires, which is home to a dingo pack led by the white dingo Migaloo. His son, Miro, is the same age as Mala and still learning to hunt; in one chase he pursues a mother kangaroo whose joey tumbles from her pouch but manages to escape. The narration notes that only one in five kangaroo joeys lives to see its first birthday, so Mala has much to learn if she is to survive.

The valley is home to many other animals, including a grumpy wombat named Warrin, an energetic willie wagtail, a koala, sugar gliders and colorful parrots. When a wedge-tailed eagle threatens the joeys, the alarm calls of smaller birds warn the kangaroos. On their next hunt, the dingoes scatter the mob, separating Mala from Lowanna, and surround and kill Bamir. Mala eventually finds her way back to her mother. Winter brings snowstorms and food becomes scarce. When a new litter of pups arrives, Miro is driven from the pack and struggles to feed himself. By spring, Mala and Miro are both living on their own, and in a final hunt they meet head to head; Mala outruns the young dingo and escapes. As a new season's joeys begin to emerge from their mothers' pouches, the cycle of life in the valley continues.

Kangaroo Valley was released on Netflix as part of its slate of wildlife documentaries. Johnny Loftus of Decider called it crisply shot, warmly told and full of interesting facts, while Amanda Guarragi of Ready Steady Cut praised the coming-of-age story that sets it apart from other wildlife documentaries.

overview: Agent Jesus Juarez (aka Chucho) has always played the Devil in his town's Nativity Play. This Christmas, when the new pastor of the church recasts the role, the two men engage in a battle between good and evil.
production_companies: Fondo de Inversión y Estímulos al Cine (FIDECINE)
title: Pastorela
plot:
Pastorela is a 2011 Mexican Christmas black comedy written and directed by Emilio Portes, his second feature after the award-winning black comedy Conozca la cabeza de Juan Pérez. A Las Producciones del Patrón production made with support from IMCINE and FIDECINE, it stars Joaquín Cosío as Jesús "Chucho" Juárez, Carlos Cobos as Father Edmundo Posadas and Eduardo España as Vulmaro, with Ana Serradilla as a nun, Dagoberto Gama as a police commander, Melissa Bahnsen as Magdalena, Héctor Jiménez as a possessed man, José Sefami as "El Tuerto", Silverio Palacios as Doctor Godínez and Eduardo Manzano as a cardinal.

Chucho Juárez is a judicial agent of the federal police who lives with his daughter Magdalena in the Mexico City neighborhood of San Miguel de Nenepilco. For as long as he can remember, he has played the Devil every year in the parish pastorela, the traditional Nativity play organized by Father Benito. This Christmas, however, things change. While Chucho is busy investigating the murder of a deputy prosecutor, he fails to notice that Father Benito has suffered a fatal heart attack in the middle of an affair with a nun, and he misses the casting session held by the new parish priest, the exorcist Edmundo Posadas. The newcomer leaves him out of the play and gives the coveted role of the Devil to Vulmaro, Chucho's compadre. Unwilling to give up a part he regards as his by tradition, the policeman launches a fierce struggle against the priest, a classic battle between good and evil in which both men go to any lengths, tearing apart the venerable tradition along the way.

Portes, a graduate of the Centro de Capacitación Cinematográfica, reworked the script in a 2007 screenwriting workshop supervised by the writer Vicente Leñero, and the film was shot between December 2008 and February 2009. He described it as an acid, unbridled comedy with touches of police action and fantasy, and as a portrait of a society that loves to live by its traditions and their absurdity, adding that he hoped the main characters would move beyond the archetypes of cop and priest to become more complex and endearing. Pastorela opened in Mexico on 11 November 2011 and was released in the United States by Pantelion. At the 54th Ariel Awards in 2012 it received fourteen nominations and was the big winner, taking best picture, best director and best original screenplay along with costume design, makeup and visual effects awards.

overview: For Jimmy Smith, Jr., life is a daily fight just to keep hope alive. Feeding his dreams in Detroit's vibrant music scene, Jimmy wages an extraordinary personal struggle to find his own voice - and earn a place in a world where rhymes rule, legends are born and every moment… is another chance.
tagline: Every Moment Is Another Chance
title: 8 Mile
plot: [No information found]

overview: In 1974, 12-year-old Jan Broberg is abducted from a small church-going community in Idaho by a trusted neighbour and close family friend.
tagline: Every parent's worst nightmare.
title: Abducted in Plain Sight
plot:
Abducted in Plain Sight is a 2017 documentary film directed by Skye Borgman, not 2018, and produced by Top Knot Films. The movie revolves around the Broberg family, whose daughter Jan was kidnapped multiple times by a close family friend, Robert Berchtold.

The main theme of Abducted in Plain Sight is the disturbing and complex relationship between trust, loyalty, and manipulation within families. It explores how a seemingly ordinary and loving family can be infiltrated by a charismatic individual who uses their charm to gain the trust of the parents and exploit it for his own sinister purposes.

Throughout the film, the audience witnesses the gradual erosion of Jan's sense of security and autonomy as she is repeatedly kidnapped and manipulated by Berchtold. The documentary sheds light on how the family's dynamics are warped by a toxic mix of codependency, enabling behavior, and a lack of boundaries, ultimately leading to devastating consequences.

The film also delves into the theme of gaslighting, where Berchtold skillfully manipulates Jan and her parents, making them question their own perceptions and sanity. This creates a sense of unease and tension, as the audience is left wondering how such a situation could unfold in real life.

Ultimately, Abducted in Plain Sight serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of blind trust and the importance of setting boundaries within families. It raises questions about the nature of relationships, the power dynamics at play, and the devastating consequences that can result when these dynamics are exploited for personal gain.

overview: An operative for an elite private intelligence firm finds her priorities irrevocably changed after she is tasked with infiltrating an anarchist group known for executing covert attacks upon major corporations.
tagline: Spy on us, we'll spy on you.
title: The East
plot:
The East is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the complexities of modern-day activism and the blurred lines between revolution and terrorism. At its core, the film explores the theme of radicalism and the allure of extremist ideologies.

The movie follows a young FBI agent, Sarah, who infiltrates an eco-terrorist group known as The East, led by the enigmatic and charismatic Mira. As Sarah becomes more deeply embroiled with the group, she begins to question her own motivations and the true nature of their cause.

One of the primary themes of The East is the tension between individual freedom and collective responsibility. The film's protagonist, Sarah, is initially drawn to The East's ideology because it offers a sense of purpose and belonging. However, as she becomes more entrenched in the group, she begins to realize that their actions are not only morally ambiguous but also potentially destructive.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by external forces. Sarah's infiltration of The East forces her to confront her own values and loyalties, leading to a crisis of self-discovery. Similarly, Mira's character is a masterclass in how someone can become radicalized and lose themselves in the process.

Furthermore, The East critiques the notion of "activism" as a form of social control. The film suggests that extremist ideologies often masquerade as revolutionary movements, using tactics like propaganda and manipulation to recruit new members. This theme is particularly relevant in today's world, where social media has created new avenues for radicalization.

Ultimately, The East presents a nuanced exploration of the complexities surrounding modern activism, highlighting the difficulties of distinguishing between legitimate causes and extremist ideologies.

overview: A teen gamer is forced to level up to full-time babysitter when his favorite video game drops three superpowered infants from space into his backyard.
title: Fearless
plot:
Fearless is a 2020 American animated science fiction action comedy directed by Cory Edwards, who wrote it with John Murphy, produced by Vanguard Animation and released on Netflix. Its voice cast includes Gabrielle Union, Jadakiss, Miguel J. Pimentel, Yara Shahidi and Miles Robbins. The story follows two high school seniors who must protect three superpowered babies who have escaped from a video game into the real world.

Reid, a teenage gamer known online as Fe@rLeSS_, is an expert at the superhero game Planet Master and the first player to reach its penultimate level. There, the game's hero, Captain Darius Lightspeed, reveals that he has three children, Kira, Xander and Titus, and Reid leaves them in a daycare while he searches for the final level. The game's villain, Dr. Arcannis, kidnaps the babies to steal their superpowers and conquer Earth, but the infants escape in a pod. When Reid agrees to accept the consequences of continuing, the pod travels through a wormhole and crash-lands behind his house in the real world.

Reid and his classmate Melanie, who has come over to work on a science project, discover the babies and agree to look after them. Their task is far from easy: the infants have unpredictable powers, the U.S. military, led by General Jayne Blazerhatch, has detected the pod and is closing in, and Arcannis has followed the babies through the wormhole. After a call from Lightspeed is cut short when one of the babies breaks the communicator, Reid and Melanie go on the run. Captured by the military and then outmatched by Arcannis, who seizes the children, the two teenagers must work together with Lightspeed to rescue the babies, racing to reach Arcannis's ship before he can drain their powers.

The film plays with video game conventions and the idea of a gamer forced into real-world responsibility, combining slapstick humor with superhero action.

Fearless was released on Netflix on August 14, 2020. It received mixed reviews; Polygon's Tasha Robinson wrote that it was not terrible, but that no one involved seemed to have put in much effort.

overview: A television reporter and cameraman follow emergency workers into a dark apartment building and are quickly locked inside with something terrifying.
tagline: One witness. One camera
title: [REC]
plot:
[REC] is a Spanish horror film directed by Jaume Balagueró and Paco Plaza, released in 2007. The movie takes place in modern-day Barcelona, Spain.

The story begins with Angela Vidal (Manuela Velasco), a television reporter who is assigned to cover a typical day at the local fire station. She is accompanied by her cameraman, Pablo (David Verdu), and her producer, Isabella (Leticia Dolz). The crew arrives at the fire station, where they meet the firefighters, including Urtain (Carlos Lasplena) and his team.

As Angela begins to film the day's activities, she meets Tomás (Christian Stürmer), a firefighter who is recovering from an injury. She also meets Isabella's boyfriend, Pablo's brother, and his girlfriend, but they are not part of the main storyline.

The story takes a turn when Angela discovers that one of the firefighters has been bitten by a mysterious creature while responding to a call. The creature is later revealed to be a zombie-like being infected with a deadly virus. As the day progresses, more and more people become infected, and the situation spirals out of control.

Angela's producer, Isabella, becomes increasingly unhinged as she realizes that the fire station is under attack by the infected. She tries to escape, but her attempts are thwarted by the growing chaos. Meanwhile, Angela and Tomás try to find a way to stop the outbreak and save as many people as possible.

As the night wears on, the situation becomes more desperate. The firefighters are vastly outnumbered, and the infected continue to spread. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Urtain, one of the firefighters, has been hiding a dark secret: he is actually the source of the outbreak.

In the climactic final act, Angela and Tomás make a desperate bid to escape the fire station. They fight their way through hordes of infected, using whatever they can find to defend themselves. In the end, only one person survives: Angela.

The movie ends with Angela, traumatized by what she has witnessed, being taken away from the fire station in an ambulance. As she looks back at the burning building, it is clear that she will never be the same again.

[REC] is a tense, suspenseful horror film that explores themes of isolation, paranoia, and the breakdown of social order in the face of catastrophic disaster. The movie's use of found footage adds to the sense of realism and immediacy, making the viewer feel like they are experiencing the events firsthand.

overview: A raw urban drama about two friends raised on the dangerous streets of Kingston, Jamaica. Biggs and Wayne take on the "Shotta" way of life to survive. As young boys, they begin a life of crime, eventually moving to the US where they begin a ruthless climb from the bottom. They remain bound to each other by their shottas loyalty as they aggressively take control of the Jamaican underworld.
tagline: Friendship, loyalty & greed.
title: Shottas
plot:
Shottas is a 2002 Jamaican-American crime film written, produced and directed by Cess Silvera about two young men involved in organized crime in Kingston and Miami. Ky-Mani Marley stars as Biggs, with the dancehall artist Spragga Benz as Wayne, Paul Campbell as Mad Max, Louie Rankin as Teddy Bruck Shut and Wyclef Jean in a supporting role. Made on a low budget, the film became an underground cult favorite after an unfinished bootleg version circulated widely, years before it received an official limited release in the United States by Triumph Films and Destination Films in 2006.

Biggs and Wayne grow up together on the dangerous streets of Kingston, Jamaica. While still children, they rob a soda delivery truck and shoot its driver, using the proceeds to buy visas to travel to the United States. In Miami, they continue their criminal careers, hustling on the streets. Years later, Biggs is deported to Jamaica, where Wayne and their friend Mad Max, who have also been deported, have built a lucrative racket extorting money from local businessmen.

After trouble with the police and corrupt politicians in Jamaica, the three men return to Miami, where they learn that a new drug kingpin, Teddy Bruck Shut, now dominates the underworld. The trio confront Teddy and try to extort him, then use intimidation and brutal violence to rise to the top of the city's criminal hierarchy, building a lavish lifestyle on the proceeds. Their ambitions lead to a bloody confrontation in which Teddy's associates kill Wayne and his girlfriend, Raquel, and wound Max. Biggs narrowly avoids being killed while at the side of his dying friend, saved when Max shoots the attacker. After taking Max to hospital, Biggs goes to Teddy's house and kills him, his bodyguard and his girlfriend, then takes the money and escapes by boat.

Shottas was poorly received by mainstream critics, holding a 17 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 18 reviews, with criticism directed at its rough production values, acting and excessive violence. Nevertheless, it developed a devoted following, particularly within Jamaican and Caribbean communities and among fans of hip-hop and dancehall culture, and its dialogue, delivered largely in Jamaican Patois, became widely quoted. Ky-Mani Marley, a son of Bob Marley, made one of his first major acting appearances in the film.

overview: A father and son go on the run after the dad learns his child possesses special powers.
tagline: He's not like us.
title: Midnight Special
plot:
Midnight Special is a 2016 American science fiction film directed by Jeff Nichols and written by Scott McGee. The movie stars Joel Edgerton, Kirsten Dunst, and Adam Driver.

The main themes of Midnight Special revolve around the struggle between faith, science, and the unknown. The story follows a young boy named Alton Meyer (played by Jackson Robert Scott), who is believed to be the Second Coming of Jesus Christ. As the story unfolds, we see how his existence sets off a chain reaction of events that challenge the lives of those around him.

One of the primary themes of Midnight Special is the power of faith and its impact on individuals and communities. The film explores the idea that faith can be both a source of comfort and a source of conflict. Alton's presence sparks a mix of emotions, ranging from devotion to fear, as people struggle to understand his role in their lives.

Another significant theme is the tension between science and spirituality. The movie delves into the world of pseudoscience and alternative medicine, highlighting the blurred lines between what is considered "scientific" and what is not. This dichotomy serves as a backdrop for exploring the complexities of human understanding and the limits of scientific inquiry.

The film also touches on the theme of family and the bonds that tie people together. Alton's presence forces his adoptive parents, Richard (Joel Edgerton) and Sarah (Kirsten Dunst), to confront their own faith and values, leading to a deeper exploration of what it means to be a family.

Finally, Midnight Special explores the idea of redemption and forgiveness. As the story unfolds, we see characters grapple with past mistakes and seek redemption through Alton's presence. The film suggests that even in the face of uncertainty and chaos, there is always the possibility for forgiveness and healing.

Overall, Midnight Special is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative.

overview: An assassin seeks redemption after being given a second chance at life.
tagline: Contracted to kill. Fighting to survive.
title: 24 Hours to Live
plot:
"24 Hours to Kill" is a 2017 action thriller film directed by Renny Harlin and starring Bruce Willis.

The main theme of "24 Hours to Kill" revolves around the concept of time and its value. The movie follows James Wheeler, an assassin who wakes up with only 24 hours to live after being poisoned. With this newfound knowledge, he sets out to complete his last job and make amends for past mistakes before his time runs out.

Throughout the film, the theme of time is explored through James' actions and decisions. He must navigate a complex web of double-crosses and betrayals while trying to stay one step ahead of his enemies. The clock ticking away serves as a constant reminder of his mortality, driving him to make the most of the limited time he has.

Another significant theme present in the movie is redemption. James' character arc revolves around finding forgiveness for past wrongdoings and making amends with those he has hurt. As he navigates his final 24 hours, he must confront his own demons and face the consequences of his actions.

The film also touches on the idea of mortality and the value of human life. The protagonist's situation forces him to reevaluate his priorities and consider what truly matters in life. This theme is explored through James' interactions with those around him, particularly his daughter, who serves as a catalyst for his redemption arc.

Overall, "24 Hours to Kill" explores themes of time, redemption, mortality, and the value of human life, all woven together by Bruce Willis's gripping performance as the protagonist.

overview: The incredible true story of Vietnam War hero William H. Pitsenbarger, a U.S. Air Force Pararescuemen medic who personally saved over sixty men. Thirty-two years later, Pentagon staffer Scott Huffman investigates a Congressional Medal of Honor request for Pitsenbarger and uncovers a high-level conspiracy behind the decades-long denial of the medal, prompting Huffman to put his own career on the line to seek justice for the fallen airman.
tagline: The ultimate sacrifice deserves the highest honor.
title: The Last Full Measure
plot:
The Last Full Measure is a 2020 American drama film directed by Peter Segal and written by Josh Zetner. The movie stars Sebastian Stan, Sam Elliott, and Christopher Walken.

The main themes of The Last Full Measure revolve around the complexities of love, loyalty, and sacrifice. The story follows William "Billy" Callahan (played by Sebastian Stan), a young veteran who falls in love with Carly Ryan (played by Sarah Partridge), the daughter of a retired colonel, Colonel Thomas Callahan (played by Sam Elliott).

As Billy's health deteriorates due to his terminal illness, he sets out to fulfill his lifelong dream of attending the funeral of every American soldier who has died in combat. He enlists the help of Carly and Colonel Callahan, who is initially hesitant but eventually becomes a key player in Billy's mission.

Throughout the film, the themes of love, loyalty, and sacrifice are expertly woven together. The story explores the depth of human connection and the lengths to which people will go to honor and remember those they care about. The movie also touches on the complexities of grief, loss, and the impact that these experiences can have on individuals and families.

One of the most striking aspects of The Last Full Measure is its portrayal of the bond between Billy and Colonel Callahan, who becomes a surrogate father figure to him. Their relationship is built on mutual respect, trust, and a deep understanding of one another's values and motivations.

The film also raises important questions about the nature of sacrifice and the true meaning of patriotism. As Billy's health declines, he must confront his own mortality and the sacrifices that have been made for him and those he loves. The movie ultimately presents a powerful exploration of what it means to live with honor, integrity, and compassion.

Overall, The Last Full Measure is a moving and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loyalty, and sacrifice in the face of adversity.

overview: Firefighter Gordon Brewer is plunged into the complex and dangerous world of international terrorism after he loses his wife and child in a bombing credited to Claudio 'The Wolf' Perrini.
tagline: What would you do if you lost everything?
title: Collateral Damage
plot:
Collateral Damage is a 2002 American action thriller film directed by Tony Scott and starring Antonio Banderas, Tom Sizemore, and Claire Forlani.

The movie begins with Gabriel Shear (Tom Sizemore), an FBI agent who has been tracking down the notorious terrorist known as "El Diablo" (Antonio Banderas). El Diablo is responsible for a series of bombings that have killed hundreds of people in Mexico. Gabriel's brother, Michael, was one of the victims.

Gabriel finally tracks down El Diablo to Los Angeles and engages him in a fierce gun battle. However, just as he thinks he has won, El Diablo escapes by setting off a massive explosion that destroys Gabriel's house and kills his family.

Consumed by grief and anger, Gabriel seeks revenge against El Diablo, who is now hiding out in Mexico City. He teams up with Yulaw (Peter Stormare), a local hitman who agrees to help him track down El Diablo in exchange for a share of the profits from any successful hits.

As they delve deeper into the world of organized crime, Gabriel and Yulaw encounter a beautiful woman named Sarah (Claire Forlani) who is somehow connected to El Diablo's past. Through her, Gabriel learns more about El Diablo's motivations and the true extent of his evil plans.

The plot thickens as Gabriel and Yulaw close in on El Diablo, leading to a series of intense confrontations and explosive set pieces. Along the way, Gabriel must also navigate the complexities of his own grief and anger, learning to channel them into a more constructive form of revenge.

As the story reaches its climax, Gabriel finally tracks down El Diablo to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of Mexico City. In a tense showdown, Gabriel confronts El Diablo and exacts his revenge, killing him in a dramatic and bloody finale.

Throughout the movie, director Tony Scott's signature style is on full display, with rapid-fire editing and a pulsating score that amplifies the tension and action. Antonio Banderas delivers a strong performance as the vengeful Gabriel Shear, bringing depth and nuance to a character who could have easily been reduced to a one-dimensional avenger.

Overall, Collateral Damage is a gripping and intense thriller that explores themes of grief, anger, and redemption. While it may not be as memorable as some of Scott's other films, it remains a solid addition to his action-packed oeuvre.

overview: A father and daughter are on their way to dance camp when they spot the girl's best friend on the side of the road. When they stop to offer the friend a ride, their good intentions soon result in terrible consequences.
tagline: It was an accident.
title: The Lie
plot:
The Lie is a 2018 psychological horror film written and directed by Veena Sud, a remake of the 2015 German film We Monsters. Mireille Enos and Peter Sarsgaard play Rebecca and Jay, divorced parents who go to desperate lengths to protect their teenage daughter Kayla, played by Joey King, with Cas Anvar, Patti Kim and Devery Jacobs. Jason Blum produced it.

Jay is driving Kayla to a ballet retreat when they spot her friend Britney by the roadside and offer her a lift. They stop so that Britney can relieve herself in the woods, and moments later Jay hears a scream and finds Kayla sitting alone on a bridge above a river. Kayla says she pushed Britney in. Finding no body, Jay assumes she drowned. After Kayla finds Britney's purse, they go to Rebecca, a lawyer, and Kayla confesses the killing to her mother as well. When Britney's father, Sam, comes looking for her, Rebecca claims Kayla is at the doctor's, but Sam soon realises he has been lied to. After fighting with Jay, he threatens to call the police.

Jay notices that Britney had a bruise on her face and persuades Rebecca to deflect suspicion onto Sam. Rebecca tells Kenji, a detective she knows, that Sam has been abusing his daughter. Sam denies hitting Britney, though he admits she has run away before, while Kayla tells the detective that Sam has a violent temper. Sam later sees Kayla outside Jay's apartment and chases her back inside, pounding on the windows and shouting her name. When Jay and Rebecca try to bury Britney's phone behind Sam's house, he catches them and says he knows Kayla killed his daughter. As they drive away, Sam steps in front of the car and Rebecca deliberately runs him down; after briefly considering calling for help, they leave him to bleed to death in the road. The next morning, as they scrub the blood from the car, Britney turns up unharmed, looking for Kayla. Her disappearance was a scheme the two girls cooked up so that Britney could visit her boyfriend. Kayla tearfully admits that she embellished the ruse by pretending to have pushed her friend, hoping the tragedy would reunite her parents. As the family embraces, the doorbell rings and police sirens approach.

Filmed in the Toronto area under the working title Between the Earth and the Sky, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 13, 2018. Amazon Studios released it on October 6, 2020, as part of the Welcome to the Blumhouse series. Reviews were mixed, with 43% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Galifianakis dreamed of becoming a star. But when Will Ferrell discovered his public access TV show, 'Between Two Ferns' and uploaded it to Funny or Die, Zach became a viral laughing stock. Now Zach and his crew are taking a road trip to complete a series of high-profile celebrity interviews and restore his reputation.
tagline: There's nowhere he won't go.
title: Between Two Ferns: The Movie
plot:
Between Two Ferns: The Movie is a satirical comedy that explores the theme of celebrity culture and the superficiality of social interactions. The film delves into the world of fake interviews, shallow conversations, and the art of manipulating people for one's own gain.

At its core, the movie critiques the way celebrities are often portrayed in the media, presenting them as larger-than-life figures with a veneer of charm and charisma that hides their true nature. The main character, Craig (played by Zach Galifianakis), is a master manipulator who uses his awkwardness and naivety to get what he wants from his guests.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, as Craig's interactions with others are often transactional and lacking in genuine connection. Despite his attempts to appear confident and self-assured, Craig is revealed to be a deeply insecure and vulnerable individual who uses his wit and sarcasm to mask his true feelings.

Furthermore, the movie pokes fun at the absurdity of the celebrity interview format, where guests are often subjected to awkward and uncomfortable questions that reveal more about the interviewer than the guest. The film's use of satire and irony serves as a commentary on the way we present ourselves to the world and the ways in which we interact with others.

Overall, Between Two Ferns: The Movie is a dark comedy that uses humor and irony to explore themes of celebrity culture, loneliness, and the superficiality of social interactions.

overview: A tragic love story set in East Berlin with the backdrop of an undercover Stasi controlled culture. Stasi captain Wieler is ordered to follow author Dreyman and plunges deeper and deeper into his life until he reaches the threshold of doubting the system.
tagline: Before the Fall of the Berlin Wall, East Germany's Secret Police Listened to Your Secrets.
title: The Lives of Others
plot:
The Lives of Others is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of life under totalitarian rule. Set against the backdrop of East Germany in the 1980s, the film explores the intricate web of surveillance and control that pervades every aspect of society.

At its core, The Lives of Others is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for resilience, creativity, and resistance in the face of oppression. The story follows a Stasi agent, Captain Gerd Wiesler, who is tasked with infiltrating the lives of a young playwright, Georg Dreyman, and his girlfriend, Christa-Maria Sieland.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Wiesler's mission is not only to gather intelligence but also to monitor the couple's every move, eroding their sense of freedom and autonomy. However, as he becomes increasingly entrenched in their lives, Wiesler begins to experience a moral crisis, questioning the true nature of his work and the values it represents.

The film masterfully weaves together themes of surveillance, censorship, and the blurred lines between loyalty and betrayal. It also delves into the complexities of artistic expression under oppressive regimes, highlighting the ways in which creative individuals can both resist and conform to the status quo.

Ultimately, The Lives of Others is a powerful commentary on the human condition, urging viewers to consider the delicate balance between individual freedom and collective security. Through its nuanced portrayal of characters and their struggles, the film offers a poignant reminder that even in the darkest of times, the human spirit can find ways to resist, subvert, and ultimately triumph over oppression.

overview: Ethan Wate just wants to get to know Lena Duchannes better, but unbeknownst to him, Lena has strange powers.  As Lena's 16th birthday approaches she might decide her fate, to be good or evil.  A choice which will impact her relationship forever.
tagline: Dark secrets will come to light.
title: Beautiful Creatures
plot:
Beautiful Creatures is a 2013 American supernatural romance film directed by Richard LaGravenese, based on the novel of the same name by Kami Garcia and Margaret Stohl.

The movie follows the story of Ethan Wate (played by Alden Ehrenreich), a high school student who falls in love with Lena Duchannes (played by Alice Englert), a mysterious and beautiful girl from a family of witches. As their relationship deepens, they must navigate the complexities of their forbidden love, as well as the dark secrets surrounding Lena's family and their connection to an ancient curse.

The main themes of Beautiful Creatures include:

1. Forbidden Love: The movie explores the theme of forbidden love between Ethan and Lena, who come from different worlds and are bound by a centuries-old curse that forbids them from being together.
2. Family Secrets: The film delves into the dark secrets surrounding Lena's family and their connection to the supernatural world, highlighting the complexities of family dynamics and the consequences of keeping secrets.
3. Identity: Ethan and Lena must navigate their own identities and the expectations placed upon them by their families and society, as they struggle to find their place in the world.
4. Good vs. Evil: The movie features a classic battle between good and evil, with Ethan representing innocence and love, while Lena's family embodies darkness and manipulation.
5. Self-Sacrifice: Throughout the story, characters must make difficult choices and sacrifices for the people they love, highlighting the importance of putting others before oneself.

Overall, Beautiful Creatures is a romantic fantasy film that explores themes of forbidden love, family secrets, identity, good vs. evil, and self-sacrifice, set against a backdrop of supernatural intrigue and adventure.

overview: A group of unwitting teens are stranded near a strange wax museum and soon must fight to survive and keep from becoming the next exhibit.
tagline: Prey. Slay. Display
title: House of Wax
plot:
House of Wax is a 2005 American supernatural horror film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and written by Pete Goldfinger, Ehren Kruger, and Richard Wenk. The movie stars Ewan McGregor, Hayden Christensen, Jon Abrahams, and Jordan Ladd.

The story begins with two brothers, Sean (Jon Abrahams) and Danny (Ehren Kruger), who are struggling to make ends meet in a small town in the Midwest. They work at their father's old wax museum, which has been closed for years due to a tragic accident that killed their mother. The brothers' lives take a drastic turn when they stumble upon an abandoned house on the outskirts of town, where they discover a mysterious and ancient-looking door.

As they explore the house, they find a series of cryptic symbols etched into the walls, which seem to be connected to an old legend about a family who was brutally murdered by their own son. The brothers soon realize that the house is actually a trap set by the vengeful spirit of the killer, who is determined to claim new victims.

The story takes a dark turn when Sean and Danny meet a beautiful woman named Carly (Hayden Christensen), who claims to be an artist looking for inspiration. Unbeknownst to them, Carly is actually the daughter of the killer, and she has been searching for her family's old mansion for years. As the night wears on, Sean and Carly grow closer, but Danny becomes increasingly suspicious of their relationship.

As the body count rises, Sean and Carly must work together to uncover the truth behind the house and the legend of the killer. Along the way, they discover that the house is actually a manifestation of the killer's twisted psyche, which is fueled by his own guilt and anger.

In the end, Sean and Carly manage to outsmart the killer and escape the house, but not before discovering a shocking secret about their own family's past. The movie ends with Sean and Carly driving away from the house, but not before they share a romantic moment, hinting at a possible future together.

Throughout the movie, the special effects are impressive, particularly in the scenes where the killer is revealed to be using his wax museum skills to create gruesome and realistic illusions. The movie's score, composed by John Powell, adds to the tension and suspense, creating a sense of unease that permeates throughout the film.

Overall, House of Wax is a tense and thrilling horror movie that explores themes of family, guilt, and redemption. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror movies from the same era, it has developed a cult following over the years and remains a popular choice for fans of supernatural thrillers.

overview: (AKA- Saw: The Final Chapter)  As a deadly battle rages over Jigsaw's brutal legacy, a group of Jigsaw survivors gathers to seek the support of self-help guru and fellow survivor Bobby Dagen, a man whose own dark secrets unleash a new wave of terror.
tagline: Do you want to play a final game?
title: Saw 3D
plot:
Saw 3D is a 2010 American supernatural thriller film directed by Kevin Greutert and written by Patrick Melton and Marcus Nispel. The film stars Tobin Bell, Costas Mandylor, Betsy Russell, and Sean Patrick Flanery.

The story begins with Jigsaw (Tobin Bell), also known as John Kramer, who is revealed to be alive in a hospital bed after being mortally wounded by his own trap. He explains that he has been watching the events of the previous films from his hospital room and decides it's time for one final test.

The main plot follows Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), who is still recovering from his ordeal in Saw II, and Adam Faulkner (Sean Patrick Flanery), a young man who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness. Jigsaw tasks them with finding the next victim, Amanda Young (Shawnee Smith), who has escaped from one of his traps.

As they search for Amanda, they are joined by Detective Eric Matthews (Costas Mandylor) and his son Daniel (Chris Pascoe). The group soon discovers that Amanda is being held captive in a warehouse, where she is forced to participate in a series of gruesome tests designed by Jigsaw.

Throughout the film, the characters must work together to survive the traps and uncover the secrets behind Jigsaw's motivations. Along the way, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and make difficult choices that will ultimately determine who will live and who will die.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Amanda is not what she seems, and her true intentions are revealed. The film builds towards a shocking twist, which reveals that Jigsaw's plan was not just about testing his victims, but also about finding a way to transfer his consciousness into a new body.

The film culminates in a tense showdown between the characters and Amanda, who has become increasingly unhinged as the tests progress. In the end, only one person is left alive, and it is revealed that Jigsaw's plan was successful, but at a great cost.

Overall, Saw 3D is a thrilling and suspenseful film that explores the themes of mortality, morality, and the consequences of playing with fire. The film's twist ending adds a new layer of complexity to the series, leaving audiences questioning what is real and what is just a product of Jigsaw's twisted imagination.

overview: At the dawn of WWII, several men escape from a Russian gulag—to take a perilous and uncertain journey to freedom as they cross deserts, mountains and several nations.
tagline: Their escape was just the beginning.
title: The Way Back
plot:
The Way Back is a 2010 drama film directed by Peter Weir, not Imagenation Abu Dhabi FZ. 

The movie tells the story of Jack Cunningham, a former basketball star who struggles to find his place in the world after being kicked out of college and forced to return home. He finds solace in teaching at a local Catholic school, but his life takes an unexpected turn when he is offered a chance to coach a group of orphaned boys from India.

The film explores themes of redemption, perseverance, and the transformative power of sports. Through Jack's journey, we see him confront his own personal demons and learn to let go of his past mistakes. The movie also delves into the complexities of cultural identity and the challenges faced by outsiders trying to connect with people from different backgrounds.

As Jack forms a bond with the boys, he learns valuable lessons about leadership, teamwork, and the importance of believing in oneself. Through their experiences on the court, we see the boys overcome their own struggles and find a sense of purpose and belonging.

The Way Back is ultimately a story about the human spirit's capacity for growth, forgiveness, and connection. It's a powerful exploration of what it means to be a coach, a mentor, and a friend, and how these roles can shape us in profound ways.

overview: Molly Gunn, the freewheeling daughter of a deceased rock legend, is forced to get a job when her manager steals her money. As nanny for precocious Ray, the oft ignored daughter of a music executive she learns what it means to be an adult while teaching Ray how to be a child.
tagline: They're about to teach each other how to act their age.
title: Uptown Girls
plot:
Uptown Girls is a 2003 American comedy-drama film directed by Danny DeVito. The movie follows the story of Molly Gunn (played by Brittany Murphy), a free-spirited and eccentric young woman who lives in New York City.

The main themes of Uptown Girls include:

1. **Coming of Age**: The film explores Molly's transition from adolescence to adulthood, as she navigates her relationships with her friends, family, and romantic partners.
2. **Self-Discovery**: Throughout the movie, Molly learns to balance her carefree nature with a sense of responsibility and maturity, leading to a deeper understanding of herself and her place in the world.
3. **Female Friendship**: The bond between Molly and her best friend, Peter (played by Dakota Fanning), is a central theme in the film. Their friendship serves as a source of support and inspiration for both characters.
4. **Love and Relationships**: Uptown Girls explores various aspects of love, including romantic relationships, platonic friendships, and familial connections.

The movie features a mix of humor, drama, and heartwarming moments, making it a relatable and entertaining watch.

overview: A grieving couple retreats to their cabin 'Eden' in the woods, hoping to repair their broken hearts and troubled marriage. But nature takes its course and things go from bad to worse.
tagline: When nature turns evil, true terror awaits.
title: Antichrist
plot:
Antichrist is a 2009 psychological horror film written and directed by Lars von Trier. The film stars Willem Dafoe and Charlotte Gainsbourg as a couple, He and She, who are struggling to cope with the death of their six-year-old son.

The story begins with the family's home being set on fire, which is implied to be an accident, but also raises questions about the family's dynamics and the father's (He) inability to protect his child. The couple decides to leave Denmark and move to a remote cabin in the woods, where they hope to find solace and healing.

Initially, the film appears to be a slow-burning exploration of grief, love, and the human condition. He and She struggle to come to terms with their loss, and their relationship is put to the test as they try to navigate their new reality. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that something more sinister is at play.

She becomes increasingly unhinged, descending into a world of madness and despair. Her behavior becomes more erratic, and she starts to exhibit strange and disturbing behaviors, including self-mutilation and an obsession with death. He tries to care for her, but his own emotional state begins to deteriorate, and he becomes increasingly detached from reality.

As the film progresses, it becomes clear that She's descent into madness is not just a result of grief, but also a manifestation of her own dark desires and fantasies. The couple's relationship is revealed to be toxic and abusive, with He being emotionally distant and controlling. Their son's death serves as a catalyst for their deeper psychological issues.

The film's climax features a graphic and disturbing scene in which She gives birth to a stillborn child, which she then dismembers and eats. This act can be seen as a symbol of her own rebirth and her attempt to reclaim control over her life.

Throughout the film, von Trier explores themes of grief, trauma, and the human condition. He raises questions about the nature of love, relationships, and the complexities of the human psyche. The film's title, Antichrist, is a reference to the idea that She has become a symbol of Christ-like suffering and sacrifice.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its unflinching portrayal of grief and trauma, as well as its bold and uncompromising style. However, it was also criticized for its graphic content and perceived misogyny. Despite this, Antichrist remains a thought-provoking and unsettling work that challenges viewers to confront the darkest aspects of human nature.

In conclusion, Antichrist is a complex and challenging film that explores themes of grief, trauma, and the human condition. The film's slow-burning tension and graphic content make it a difficult watch, but also a rewarding one for those who are willing to engage with its complexities.

overview: A cinematic odyssey featuring never-before-seen footage exploring David Bowie's creative and musical journey.
tagline: Bowie
title: Moonage Daydream
plot:
Moonage Daydream is a 2022 documentary film that explores the life and career of David Bowie, with a focus on his early years and the development of his unique style. The main theme of the movie revolves around the idea of identity and self-expression, as embodied by Bowie's iconic alter ego Ziggy Stardust.

The film delves into how Bowie's music and artistry were deeply rooted in his own experiences of alienation, rebellion, and nonconformity. Through a series of interviews with those who knew him, including friends, family members, and fellow musicians, the documentary reveals the complexities of Bowie's personality and the ways in which he navigated the tensions between his public persona and private self.

At its core, Moonage Daydream is a celebration of creativity, individuality, and the power of art to transcend boundaries and challenge societal norms. The film also touches on themes of nostalgia, memory, and the passage of time, as Bowie's legacy continues to inspire new generations of artists and fans.

Throughout the documentary, the director, Francis Whately, weaves together a rich tapestry of images, music, and interviews that capture the essence of Bowie's innovative spirit and his enduring impact on popular culture.

overview: A crew of international astronauts are sent on a private mission to Jupiter's fourth moon.
tagline: Fear. Sacrifice. Contact.
title: Europa Report
plot:
Europa Report is a 2013 science fiction film directed by Sebastián Cordero and written by Dean Georgaris. The movie follows a team of astronauts on a mission to one of Jupiter's moons, Europa.

The story begins with the launch of the spaceship, Europa One, which is crewed by five astronauts: Amara (Michael Nyqvist), Chris (Sharlto Copley), Ash (Anamaria Marinca), Tom (Daniel Wu), and Captain Leckert (Julian Glover). The mission is to explore Europa's subsurface ocean, which is believed to contain liquid water and potentially support life.

Upon arrival at Europa, the crew begins their exploration of the moon's surface. They deploy a rover to collect samples from the ice crust and conduct experiments on the moon's geology. However, during one of these experiments, the rover malfunctions, causing it to crash into the ice.

The crew soon discovers that the malfunction has caused a catastrophic failure of the ship's life support systems, putting everyone's lives at risk. As they try to repair the damage and find a way to survive, they realize that their mission has become a fight for survival against time.

As tensions rise among the crew members, they must work together to overcome their differences and find a solution to their predicament. Meanwhile, Amara begins to suspect that something is amiss with the ship's systems, which puts her at odds with Captain Leckert.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when it becomes clear that the malfunction was not an accident, but rather a deliberate act of sabotage. The crew soon discovers that one of their own members has been secretly working against them, and they must figure out who is behind the betrayal before it's too late.

As the situation spirals out of control, the crew faces numerous challenges, including equipment failures, toxic gas leaks, and a rapidly deteriorating living environment. In the end, only two crew members manage to escape the ship in a lifeboat, leaving behind their colleagues to face an uncertain fate.

The movie ends with Amara and Chris floating away from Europa, unsure of what lies ahead but determined to survive. The final shot is of the lifeless body of Captain Leckert, who had been hiding a dark secret that ultimately led to his downfall.

Europa Report received critical acclaim for its realistic portrayal of space travel and exploration, as well as its tense and suspenseful plot. While it may not have achieved mainstream success, the movie has developed a loyal following among science fiction fans and is widely regarded as one of the best sci-fi films of the 2010s.

Overall, Europa Report is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores the challenges and risks faced by astronauts on a mission to explore the unknown. With its realistic portrayal of space travel and its tense plot, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction.

overview: Various lives converge on an isolated island, all connected by an author whose novel has become inextricably entwined with his own life.
title: Sex and Lucía
plot:
Sex and Lucía (Lucía y el sexo) is a 2001 Spanish drama written and directed by Julio Medem. Paz Vega and Tristán Ulloa lead a cast that also includes Najwa Nimri, Daniel Freire, Javier Cámara, Silvia Llanos and Elena Anaya.

Lucía, a waitress, is on the phone with her boyfriend Lorenzo, a novelist sunk in a long depression, after a bitter fight. Worried, she returns home to find the apartment empty and a suicide note. When the police call, she hangs up in dread, ignores their second call, packs a bag and flees to the Balearic island Lorenzo used to talk about.

The story then moves back in time. Six years earlier, on a moonlit night, Lorenzo has a fleeting sexual encounter in the sea with Elena, a woman he has just met. She later finds she is pregnant but cannot trace him. Some time after, while Lorenzo is struggling with writer's block, Lucía approaches him in a restaurant and confesses that since reading his latest book she has followed him and fallen in love. She soon moves in with him, and the film begins to blend their life with scenes from the novel he is writing.

Lorenzo eventually learns he has a daughter, Luna, and starts watching her outside her school, where he meets her babysitter Belén. Her provocative talk feeds his fiction, which Lucía reads as pure invention. One night Belén invites him to Elena's house. While the two are having sex, Luna is killed by the family's Rottweiler. Grief-stricken, Lorenzo falls into despair, his writing turns towards death, and he anonymously sends Elena, now running an inn on the island, a consoling story about a child who loves the sea. His guilt slowly breaks down his relationship with Lucía.

In the present, Lucía befriends a diver named Carlos and then Elena, and the two women gradually realize what links them. Meanwhile, Lorenzo recovers in hospital after an "accident".
